abstract: This is a human-written perspective paper on artificial intelligence (AI). We are all in a global AI experiment that has exciting prospects and questionable ethics. abstract: Background Ocean acidification (OA) represents a growing threat to marine biodiversity, particularly affecting the sensitive early life stages of invertebrates. While the physiological impacts of OA are widely recognized, its specific effects on organogenesis and the molecular regulation of defensive traits in cephalopods remain poorly understood. abstract: In the context of digital transformation reshaping the higher education ecosystem, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into learning and research activities has emerged as a key driver for enhancing academic effectiveness. Although AI tools are increasingly used to support students’ academic tasks, there remains limited understanding of the factors that shape university students’ satisfaction and AI usage behavior, particularly in the Vietnamese higher education context. abstract: Marine pathogenic microorganisms are crucial to ecological health and fishery aquaculture. abstract: Abstract In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. abstract: Artificial intelligence is used to describe, organise and interpret cultural heritage collections, yet discussion often focuses on what systems can produce rather than on the knowledge embodied in their data. This contribution approaches that problem through underwater archaeology, where the material traces of a shipwreck are encountered through historical documents, nautical charts, acoustic surveys, photographs, oral testimony and family memories. abstract: Abstract This study aims to assess the relationship between personality traits and cyber security behaviors using a hybrid approach augmenting Covariance-based Structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) with Machine Learning (ML). abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), secure and energy-efficient data aggregation has been challenging due to limited energy supply, dynamic nature of the network, and presence of malicious nodes. Within this group, members of the Lithophyllum prototypum complex are repeatedly associated with high coral settlement responses, but the mechanisms underlying this effect remain incompletely understood. abstract: One of the major challenges in forecasting is the rapid intensification (RI) of tropical cyclones, wherein cyclone intensity can increase rapidly under dynamic and changing atmospheric and oceanic conditions. This paper explores how a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI)-physics model can be used to enhance tropical cyclone RI forecasting. abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is increasingly central to improving the quality of geography education. This study developed a model intended for enhancing geography education quality based on AI-GIS integration and empirically examined future geography teachers’ readiness to adopt these technologies, drawing on a survey of 100 bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in geography at al-Farabi Kazakh National University (27 items across three blocks: socio-intellectual characteristics, experience and integration, and professional/eth

title: Salud financiera y gestión estratégica en empresas inmobiliarias: Una revisión de enfoques y tendencias
abstract: La volatilidad del mercado, las nuevas regulaciones y las demandas de sostenibilidad, convierten la salud financiera en un factor clave para la permanencia y la competitividad de las empresas inmobiliarias. Sin embargo, la literatura actual presenta enfoques dispersos y una escasa integración entre los indicadores financieros tradicionales y las variables estratégicas a largo plazo. Este estudio analiza la evolución de la investigación sobre estos temas mediante una revisión bibliométrica y sistemática. abstract: The entry into force of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) creates a practical implementation problem for fisheries governance. abstract: Introduction Air pollution has become a critical global health and environmental concern due to rapid urbanisation and industrialisation. Making accurate prediction of air quality has became crucial for effective prevention and control. Machine learning offers a robust approach by capturing complex pollutant interactions, enabling precise and timely air pollution prediction. They are also sensitive indicators that allow gauging environmental change. abstract: El presente artículo analiza la relación entre la ciberseguridad y la inteligencia artificial (IA) en México desde una perspectiva comparada con Estados Unidos de América, China e Israel. abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting marine biodiversity, particularly for monitoring elusive or endangered species. However, traditional eDNA sampling protocols often rely on small water volumes (≤2 L), which can limit detection sensitivity, especially in vast and dynamic marine environments. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness of large-volume eDNA enrichment (5–50 L) for improving the detection probability of endangered marine species, using metabarcoding and quantitative PCR (qPCR) designed for Balaenoptera brydei (Bryde’s Whale). abstract: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. abstract: Live fuel moisture content (LFMC) influences vegetation flammability, but field measurements are too sparse to describe its variation over large areas. abstract: Seabirds face myriad threats on land and at sea resulting in widespread population declines. Predictive species distribution models (SDMs) provide a powerful tool to estimate numbers of birds exposed to risks, and to attribute them to source populations. abstract: Loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) are highly migratory marine reptiles whose seasonal habitat shifts can alter their exposure to fisheries, vessel traffic, and plastic pollution. abstract: Abstract In recent years, climate extremes such as floods have created significant environmental and economic hazards for Australia. Deep learning methods have been promising for predicting extreme climate events; however, large flooding events present a critical challenge due to factors such as model calibration and missing data. abstract: Abstract Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has caused extensive damage to forests, particularly in eastern and southern regions with sustained combat, where field shelterbelts have often been used as cover and subsequently heavily destroyed. abstract: La ingeniería y la ciencia han acompañado el progreso humano desde las primeras aldeas hasta la actual sociedad del conocimiento. title: Preserving clinical method in artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis: a cognitive-safety framework against premature diagnostic closure
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can support differential diagnosis, but final-answer accuracy does not by itself establish diagnostic safety. This narrative review examines how AI exposure may alter hypothesis generation and proposes AI-associated differential diagnosis narrowing as a testable process-level construct of the clinician-AI system. The construct describes reduced differential breadth, flexibility, or counterfactual exploration after AI exposure; it is not a validated syndrome and does not imply causation. title: Filosofía e inteligencia artificial en la era del aceleracionismo extremo
abstract: El artículo aborda cómo en la era del aceleracionismo extremo, con la tecnología de la inteligencia artificial teniendo un rol protagónico debido a su carácter omniabarcador, la filosofía parece quedar obsoleta. title: DTAM: A multimodal deep learning model for traffic-related content detection from social media
abstract: Traffic incidents reported on social media, especially Twitter, can provide valuable real-time information for managing urban transportation. However, detecting traffic-related tweets is difficult because people often use informal, short, and noisy language. This study introduces DTAM (Deep Twitter Analysis Model), a multimodal deep learning model that automatically identifies traffic-related tweets with high accuracy. title: ¿Cuál es la voz de la IA?, y pensándolo bien, ¿qué daño nos hace?
abstract: This text analyzes the differences between a text written by a human and one produced by AI. Based on concrete experiences, the author demonstrates that texts produced by AI supplant what she calls the “voice” of a human author, since they produce impersonal, aseptic, and complacent versions of the content a human wishes to create. title: Construction method of temporal deep learning model for aging assessment of power hard composite insulators
abstract: Abstract Hard composite insulators are essential for reliable power transmission, but aging caused by environmental and electrical stresses increases leakage current and failure risks. Existing assessment methods face challenges in prediction accuracy, adaptability, and temporal feature analysis. This research proposes a novel ModABi-LSTMO framework that integrates DWT-based feature extraction, BiLSTM temporal learning, and ModAO optimization for accurate and intelligent aging assessment of power hard composite insulators. abstract: It is complicated to comprehend the shear strength behavior of steel fiber-reinforced concrete (FRC) because of various parameters that are involved. title: Alteration in coastal land utilization and prospective modeling for Parepare Bay, Indonesia
abstract: Coastal zones, marked by dynamic natural processes and human activities, require a profound understanding of land use and land cover (LULC) change. abstract: El presente artículo propone una aproximación al análisis de la educación y la responsabilidad social según el papa Francisco desde la complejidad. abstract: Gill histopathology is widely used in fish toxicology, but lesion scores and targeted measurements capture only part of the structural information in routine sections. abstract: Adapting object detection models to underwater environment presents significant challenges due to underwater light attenuation and limited data availability. abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence (AI), ship path planning (SPP) has emerged as a core technique for autonomous ships to guarantee navigation safety and enhance energy efficiency. abstract: To proactively react to unknown uncertainties caused by a rapidly changing climate, we propose to adopt diverse, adaptive, and robust engineering (DARE): Earth’s ecosystems naturally thrive in spite of unknown uncertainties by incorporating diversity, adaptability, and robustness in their “designs”. Therefore, we propose a strategy aligned with nature’s own approach to dealing with uncertainties that does not rely on predictions about the future. abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. abstract: Despite years of research, the processes controlling warm-rain formation remain uncertain. abstract: Efficient detection and precise classification of oil spills in marine environments remain challenging, mainly due to the oil spill class imbalance within Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) datasets, which reduces deep learning model performance and often leads to false negatives. title: Hydroclimate Variability at Lake Tana, Ethiopia, Over the Past 6,000 Years: A Critical Synthesis of Geochemical and Isotopic Records
abstract: Lake Tana, the source of the Blue Nile in the northwestern Ethiopian highlands, is a climatically sensitive archive at the northern margin of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). Its sediments record changes in the balance between Atlantic/Congo Basin moisture and Indian Ocean/Red Sea moisture, making it a key site for understanding Afro-Asian monsoon dynamics. abstract: Despite the accumulation of vast amounts of ocean observation data and diverse instrumentation, a critical gap persists in modern oceanography: instruments and their generated heterogeneous datasets are routinely treated as isolated entities, lacking a systematic knowledge graph to map the overarching observation technology ecosystem. This systemic disconnection creates a severe semantic gap between raw instrument specifications and the geophysical parameters they measure, ultimately hindering automated cross-platform interoperability and intelligent data discovery. abstract: Nitrogen pollution is a major environmental challenge in groundwater systems, and identifying nitrogen metabolic potential is essential for understanding its development and transformation. However, functional characterization relies on metagenomic data, while conventional water-quality monitoring does not directly quantify pathway-specific N-cycle gene abundance. abstract: Abstract Satellite-derived soil moisture products provide valuable large-scale information but often exhibit reduced accuracy in heterogeneous watersheds with limited monitoring data. This study evaluated whether a strategically designed monitoring network combined with machine learning could refine Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture estimates in the Vacacaí River basin (11,177 km²), southern Brazil. abstract: Groundwater drought events in temperate maritime regions have historically occurred relatively rarely and subsequently received limited research attention despite their significant potential socio-economic and ecological implications. Accordingly, understanding of groundwater drought processes and their hydrological controls remains limited in these regions. abstract: Abstract The contamination of aquatic environments by antibiotics has become a major environmental concern due to their persistence and contribution to antimicrobial resistance. In this study, activated carbon derived from babassu endocarp (BAC) was evaluated for the removal of amoxicillin (AMX) from aqueous solutions under ultrasonic irradiation. abstract: ABSTRACT Tomatoes are very perishable climacteric fruits that require a considerable amount of moisture, soften, and get spoiled by microbes after harvest, causing loss of quality and food. Thus, a sustainable approach is needed to preserve the nutritional quality and microbial safety of the products over a longer period. abstract: Abstract Self-powered wearable systems require energy harvesters that are mechanically compliant, comfortable, and environmentally sustainable. abstract: Tropical coastal seascapes are valuable ecological systems providing essential services such as shoreline protection, carbon sequestration, and fisheries support. Understanding seascape change requires attention to both spatial scale and habitat composition, yet these aspects are often overlooked in coastal management. title: A Hybrid GeoAI–Remote Sensing Framework for Urban Flood Susceptibility Prediction in Coastal Megacities: A Case Study of Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: Urban flooding poses a persistent and escalating threat to coastal megacities, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions where climate variability and unregulated land use intensify vulnerability. This study develops a hybrid GeoAI–Remote Sensing framework for urban flood susceptibility prediction in Lagos, Nigeria. abstract: Background Understanding the spatial distribution of ichthyoplankton is fundamental for identifying spawning habitats, evaluating recruitment processes, and monitoring changes in marine fish populations. However, previous studies in Korean waters have largely focused on individual coastal regions, limiting nationwide comparisons of assemblage structure. abstract: Extensive research has focused on improving animal nutritional composition through feed formulations and culture environment optimization. However, the application of machine learning (ML) modeling for nutritional enhancement remains underexplored. title: Seasonal cycles dominate the multiscale co-variability of dimethyl sulfide and precipitation
abstract: Dimethyl sulfide (DMS) is a major natural source of marine cloud condensation nuclei (CCN), yet whether its variability leaves a detectable imprint on precipitation remains unclear. Using a new dataset of two decades of daily global DMS fields reconstructed from satellite observations, we found DMS–precipitation co-variability across extensive but regionally patchy ocean sectors. abstract: The growing operational requirements in deep-sea conditions have shown the shortcomings of traditional underwater anechoic coatings in terms of high-pressure resistance, broadband coverage and high-performance sound absorption. To overcome these issues, this study presents a unique underwater cavity-free sound-absorbing metamaterial containing acoustic black hole (ABH) effects. title: Long-term chlorophyll-a dynamics reveal abrupt baseline shifts in coastal waters of the northwestern Arabian Gulf
abstract: Long-term chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) records combined with environmental observations provide a framework for detecting gradual trends and abrupt baseline shifts in coastal ecosystems. Using in situ water-quality observations collected from 13 coastal monitoring stations between 2001 and 2024, we compared Chl-a dynamics between sites inside Kuwait Bay and gulf sites in the adjacent northwestern Arabian Gulf. abstract: Abstract Despite recent progress in underwater monocular depth estimation, the field still faces numerous complex challenges. The performance of existing methods remains constrained by factors such as light attenuation, scattering effects, and color distortion inherent in underwater environments. title: Enhanced burn severity mapping using machine learning and sentinel-2 spectral indices in tropical montane forests of Tanzania
abstract: Forest fires pose a significant threat to ecosystems, biodiversity, and human settlements, necessitating accurate and timely detection of burned areas for post-fire management. Remote sensing-based techniques coupled with google earth cloud computing platform, has emerged a best technique for spatial and temporal monitoring of the impact of forest fires. title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
abstract: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP).

abstract: The marine power system is the core for propulsion, generating electricity and supporting operation of main equipment. Its operation and maintenance is therefore particularly important. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine energy harvesting technologies demand composite materials capable of withstanding harsh and variable marine environments. In this study, we developed and evaluated a potentially bio-based composite system by combining a bio-derived epoxy resin with flax fiber reinforcement for marine applications. abstract: Oceanic fracture zones, the inactive traces of former transform faults, are often considered tectonically inactive once relative plate motion across them ceases. abstract: The integrated warm-wet conditions across China, represented by the Warm-Wet Index (WWI), exhibit pronounced interdecadal variability during 1960–2022. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper evaluates the effect of in utero exposure to the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami on birth outcomes in Indonesia. abstract: Abstract Short-term rentals (STR) are forming a growing part of the accommodation offer to international and domestic tourists. To resolve these issues, this study proposes the High-Resolution Algal Bloom Delineation Network (HABD-Net), a lightweight semantic segmentation framework, combining a ConvNeXt-based Algal Bloom Enhancement Module and an Index-Guided Self-Attention mechanism to improve multi-scale feature representation to incorporate a weak RGB-derived color–spatial prior. title: IA educativa y formación de agentes de cambio inclusivo en estudiantes de Pedagogía SEA-UV
abstract: La formación inicial de profesionales de la educación requiere experiencias que articulen inclusión, análisis de Barreras para el Aprendizaje y la Participación (BAP) y uso crítico de inteligencia artificial (IA), particularmente en modalidades abiertas. El objetivo fue analizar los resultados observados en dimensiones vinculadas con la competencia de agente de cambio educativo inclusivo en estudiantes de Pedagogía del Sistema de Enseñanza Abierta de la Universidad Veracruzana. title: Hematological Profile of Healthy White-Bellied Sea Eagles (Haliaeetus leucogaster) Undergoing Rehabilitation at Bali Wildlife Rescue Centre
abstract: Background: Haliaeetus leucogaster, or the white-bellied sea eagle, is one of the largest raptors in Indonesia and plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance. Hematological evaluation is essential for assessing health and release suitability after rehabilitation; however, reference data for this species, especially from Indonesia, remain limited. Purpose: This study aimed to support clinical assessments and conservation strategies by, providing descriptive hematological data for H. leucogaster undergoing rehabilitation at the Bali Wildlife Rescue Centre, Indonesia. title: Algorithmic Trust And Ai Literacy In Shaping Economic Decision-Making: The Role Of Perceived Autonomy As A Mediating Variable
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in economic activities continues to increase, but it poses a risk of dependency if not accompanied by rational trust and adequate literacy. This study aims to analyze the relationship between algorithmic trust and AI literacy on economic decision-making, both directly and through perceived autonomy as a mediating variable. The research method uses a quantitative explanatory approach through a survey of 200 AI user respondents in Indonesia. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling. title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Fisheries Management and Intelligent Aquatic Water Resource Monitoring
abstract: Digital twins are increasingly proposed as a means of linking aquatic observations, predictive models and management decisions. Their relevance to sustainability nevertheless depends on more than the speed or accuracy of an artificial intelligence model. This critical narrative review examines the evidence connecting digital-twin architectures with capture fisheries, aquaculture and freshwater and coastal water-quality monitoring. title: Bacterial responses to Engineered Oxygen Supply (EOS) in a fjord-like estuary are limited despite widespread plume transport
abstract: Coastal deoxygenation is increasing globally, prompting growing interest in Engineered Oxygen Supply (EOS) as a remediation tool. While EOS can improve dissolved oxygen (DO), assessing whether this translates into broader ecological benefits remains challenging. Bacterial communities are potential indicators because they respond rapidly to environmental change and regulate key biogeochemical processes. title: Turing-like tests for language and vision demonstrate a narrowing gap between humans and AI
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we systematically benchmark AI's ability to imitate humans in three language tasks (image captioning, word association and conversation) and three vision tasks (colour estimation, object detection and attention prediction), collecting data from n = 636 humans and 37 AI agents. abstract: ABSTRACT Sulphur hexafluoride has become a priority substance for greenhouse gas mitigation in electric systems. An ideal substitute should simultaneously satisfy requirements for dielectric strength, boiling point, global warming potential and chemical stability; however, these metrics are deeply coupled and mutually constraining at the molecular level. abstract: John Millington Synge’s The Playboy of the Western World and Riders to the Sea present rural Irish life through complex interactions among domestic space, sound, family relationships, and individual identity. This study, titled “Acoustic Space and Existential Identity: A Study of Domesticity and Filial Conflicts in John Millington Synge’s The Playboy of the Western World and Riders to the Sea,” examines how acoustic space and soundscape shape domestic experiences, existential identity, and filial conflicts in the two plays. title: Integrating ensemble learning with empirical rock-physics equations for sonic-log reconstruction and geomechanical property estimation: a case study from the Williston basin
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of geomechanical properties is important for reliable hydrocarbon reservoir exploration and development, but conventional well logging and core analysis can be costly, time-consuming, and limited by incomplete sonic-log coverage. This study develops a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates ensemble machine learning with empirical rock-physics relationships to predict geomechanical properties from readily available conventional well logs. title: Skillful subseasonal-to-seasonal ensemble forecasting with a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic model
abstract: Accurate subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction is critical for disaster mitigation under accelerating climate change, yet remains challenging due to complex multi-sphere interactions and intrinsic atmospheric uncertainty. Here we present TianXing-S2S, a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic deep learning model for global S2S ensemble forecasting. TianXing-S2S first encodes diverse multi-sphere predictors into a compact latent space, then employs a diffusion model to generate daily ensemble forecasts. title: AI Models empowering teaching in higher education: current applications, practical dilemmas and pathways for improvement
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence continues to iterate, mainstream models such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Copilot are entering the teaching spaces of universities, and teaching processes, teacher–student relations and assessment practices are changing with them. Drawing on a literature review and case analysis, this paper maps the deployment landscape and application picture of mainstream AI models in higher education teaching and assesses both the effects that have already emerged and the problems that have been exposed. title: Ways to search for novel antibiotics
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health threat, leading to dissemination of untreatable infections. In addition, the pace of antibiotic discovery to combat resistant pathogens has slowed down significantly in the 21st century. The majority of clinically relevant antibiotics are compounds that were initially isolated from soil bacteria (actinomycetes) during the Golden Era of antibiotic discovery (1940s–1960s) or their synthetic derivatives. title: AI-assisted performance prediction and optimization of CMOS and GDI logic circuits at 45 nm
abstract: An artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted optimization framework is presented for low-power digital circuit design using gate diffusion input (GDI) logic in 45 nm complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Core combinational and sequential building blocks, including logic gates, adders, multiplexers, and flip-flops, are implemented at the transistor level using Cadence Virtuoso and compared against conventional CMOS realizations. title: INTEGRATED SEISMIC ASSESSMENT AND SAFETY IMPROVEMENT OF THE KAPCHAGAY HPP DAM, KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: The Kapchagay Hydropower Plant (HPP), one of the largest hydraulic structures in Kazakhstan, is located in a seismically active region. This study was conducted in 2000 after an abnormal drop in the water level in the Kapchagay Reservoir was discovered during its operation. A comprehensive investigation was conducted to identify the causes of water losses and assess the operational and seismic safety of the facility. title: Global offshore wind development (2015–2025): multiscale structural evolution based on object-level sar mapping
abstract: Offshore wind is an important renewable infrastructure supporting the global energy transition, making accurate offshore wind turbine (OWT) mapping essential for understanding infrastructure expansion and informing marine spatial management. Existing long-term approaches often extend single-period detections over time based on structural-stability assumptions, but accumulated identification errors and regional imaging differences limit consistent object-level representation across years and regions. title: Integrating support vector machine predictions with finite element analysis for linear buckling optimization of composite plates under variable design parameters
abstract: The buckling behavior of composite plates plays a critical role in the design of lightweight high strength, high stiffness structures used in aerospace, marine, and civil engineering applications. This study investigates the linear buckling performance of unstiffened and stiffened composite plates made of carbon fiber composite, graphite composite, and Kevlar composite materials. title: Stability and composition of large sulfuric acid–methanesulfonic acid–base molecular clusters
abstract: Abstract. Sulfuric acid (SA) together with base molecules such as ammonia (AM), methylamine (MA) and dimethylamine (DMA) is known to play a central role in atmospheric new particle formation (NPF). NPF occurs through gas-to-particle conversion via the formation and growth of molecular clusters. While previous studies have demonstrated that mixtures of bases can strongly enhance nucleation rates, the influence of multiple acidic species for larger cluster stability and growth remains less explored. title: The influence of moisture ingression on mechanical and vibrational properties of basalt, glass, and hybrid fiber-epoxy composites
abstract: Basalt fiber, a natural and eco-friendly reinforcement, has demonstrated superior properties compared with conventional synthetic fibers. This study investigates the effect of ageing on the mechanical and vibrational properties of Basalt/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, and Basalt-Glass/Epoxy hybrid composites. Laminates were fabricated using vacuum bagging, ensuring uniform fiber-matrix volume fractions, and then exposed to ageing in seawater, tap water, and distilled water for a duration of 80 days. title: Making blue carbon governable in China: standardisation, local experimentation and policy implications
abstract: China’s dual-carbon agenda has elevated blue carbon from a broad ecological aspiration to an actionable policy domain requiring accounting standards, measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), and institutional implementation pathways. This article examines how blue carbon policies are made operational in China, focusing on the institutional and technical devices through which marine carbon sinks are rendered calculable, verifiable and governable. title: Los riesgos de la IA dialógica en la educación superior: afectaciones cognitivas y en la capacidad de lecto-escritura
abstract: Dialogic Artificial Intelligence (DAI) or communicative AI within Large Language Models (LLMs) is rapidly expanding across higher education and academic workflows in both teaching and research. The adoption of DAI is being driven by the pressure to enhance productivity and automate academic practices. This paper discusses the primary risks that the intensive use of DAI poses to human cognitive capacities, information biases, and the erosion of literacy, critical thinking, argumentation, and academic discourse skills. title: A Review of Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Text Classification Models
abstract: A basic premise of standard machine learning is that the training set and the test set come from the same distribution, but this premise is often broken in practice. Text classification is one of the most fundamental tasks in natural language processing (NLP). The poor robustness of its models to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become an important research topic. This study reviews the latest research on OOD generalization in text classification. title: State space model for new generation network alternative to transformers: a survey
abstract: Abstract In the post-deep learning era, the Transformer architecture has demonstrated its powerful performance in pre-trained large models and various downstream tasks. However, the enormous computational demands of Transformers have deterred many researchers. To reduce the complexity of attention models, numerous efforts have been made to design more efficient methods. title: Narrativas algorítmicas y cultura digital universitaria: usos de ChatGPT, TikTok y herramientas de IA generativa en el sur de México
abstract: This article examines how university students in southern Mexico articulate academic uses of ChatGPT, TikTok, and other generative artificial intelligence tools. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design combined a nonprobability survey of 412 students from five states, 102 digital diary entries, and 96 excerpts from 32 semi-structured interviews. title: Real-time in-water fish biomass estimation from stereo bounding-box geometry without dense depth maps
abstract: In biomass estimation of in-water fish, a primary challenge is accurately estimating depth to reconstruct the physical dimensions of detected specimens. Conventional stereo methods struggle in underwater environments due to light reflections, homogeneous backgrounds, and optical artifacts, often failing to produce reliable disparity maps. This study presents StereoGeoBox, a practical alternative that estimates depth solely from the geometric correspondence of stereo bounding boxes detected by YOLO11. title: An AI-driven model for risk stratification and prototype intervention mapping in motoric cognitive risk syndrome and subjective cognitive decline
abstract: As Alzheimer's disease and other dementias continue their global rise, there is a compelling need for early identification of pre-clinical cognitive decline. Motoric Cognitive Risk Syndrome and Subjective Cognitive Decline represent crucial transition phases to facilitate targeted intervention, and existing unimodal approaches are neither sensitive nor sufficiently multimodal for appropriate risk classification and individualized intervention mapping (prototype). title: Digital technology, agricultural resilience, and food security: a mini review
abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly deployed to strengthen food security under climate stress, resource constraints, and geopolitical disruption. This review synthesizes two largely separate bodies of scholarship: an international literature on digital agriculture and the four classical dimensions of food security, and a rapidly expanding Chinese literature on the digital economy and agricultural economic resilience. abstract: Sea export operations depend heavily on human resources because freight forwarding personnel coordinate documentation, customs procedures, container handling, shipping schedules, and communication among stakeholders. Human-related failures may result in documentation errors, shipment delays, additional costs, regulatory penalties, and service disruptions. title: Rethinking e-business through AI: comparative insights and actionable solutions
abstract: Purpose The incremental adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has been emphasized in much academic research and still remains incomplete with regards to the context-based acceptance and utilization. Prior studies mainly focused on technological acceptance and organizational growth but most of the time they overlook the constraints between economy-wise or country-wise differentiation in AI adaptation. abstract: Today, satellite image analysis and mapping systems play a significant role in urban planning, energy management, potential assessment, and sustainable development studies. In addition to the difficulty and high cost of fieldwork, the analysis of observations delays potential assessment and detection efforts. To overcome this delay and high cost, the use of satellite imagery is among the most important methods that facilitate these processes. title: A multi-stage hybrid optimization framework based on Crocodile Optimization and Beetle Antennae Search for high-precision air quality analytics
abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization continue to impair global air pollution, making accurate air quality forecasting critical for effective environmental management. The main aim of this paper is to create a hybrid intelligent system that combines improved feature selection optimization to accurately predict applications. A collection of computerized weather stations with the main chemicals, such as CO and hydrogen, is used in the structure. abstract: Accurately predicting battery life is vital for next-generation energy storage. Zinc-silver batteries (ZSBs) offer high power and energy density but suffer from short cycle life due to parasitic oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) that cause irreversible swelling. title: Image-Based Asymmetric Feature Fusion Using EfficientNet-B0 and MobileNetV3Large for Multi-Class Fish Disease Classification
abstract: This study proposes an asymmetric hybrid feature-fusion network that combines EfficientNet-B0 and MobileNetV3Large in parallel for multi-class classification of eight fish disease categories. The approach is designed to exploit the complementary feature-learning capabilities of both lightweight convolutional neural network architectures while maintaining computational efficiency for potential diagnostic applications. abstract: Fisheries and aquaculture influence marine carbon cycling, but biological carbon-retention does not necessarily constitute atmospheric carbon dioxide removal. This critical narrative review reassesses carbon sink fisheries, a concept developed in Chinese fisheries research, through an ecological-economic-social framework. abstract: ABSTRACT As urban sound environments grow more complex, environmental monitoring increasingly demands not just sound‐level measurement but also source attribution. Current source recognition techniques can identify which sources are present in a mixture, but cannot measure each source's energy contribution, making accountability impossible. abstract: Sustainable development has become a global priority, with individuals, businesses, and governments working toward the Sustainable Development Goals to address environmental challenges, particularly climate change. abstract: The U.S. Copyright Office has released its report Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability. This paper explores the copyrightability of AI-generated and AI-assisted works in the United States, focusing on that report and on the jurisprudence of human authorship. abstract: This article presents the results of a theoretical-conceptual study based on a critical analysis of the relevant philosophical literature. title: El docente ante los desafíos del siglo XXI
abstract: Teacher in the 21st century faces significant challenges due to technological evolution, pedagogical changes, and social transformations. Education is a constantly evolving process, and with the arrival of the 21st century, the challenges that arise in teacher training are becoming increasingly complex and varied. title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
abstract: The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is expected to increase the instability of renewable energy resources, particularly during periods of simultaneous low wind and solar power generation, known as renewable energy droughts. title: Multiple lineages in freshwater mytiloid bivalves: polyphyly of Sinomytilus and establishment of a new genus from China (Bivalvia, Modiolidae)
abstract: The systematics of freshwater mytiloid bivalves has long been confounded by morphological convergence, particularly among East Asian taxa traditionally assigned to Sinomytilus . In this study, an integrative revision of Chinese Sinomytilus sensu lato was conducted, combining shell morphology, anatomical observations, multi-locus phylogenetic analyses, mitogenome-based phylogeny, and molecular dating. title: Modelado numérico y clasificación del riesgo ecológico por transporte de contaminantes en cuerpos de aguas superficiales
abstract: This paper examines water pollution and its health risks. The primary goal is to identify ecological risk zones using a hybrid approach that combines numerical solutions and machine learning. The two-dimensional advection-diffusion equation is used to model pollutant dispersion, creating a dataset for training a supervised classification model. The results demonstrate high accuracy, surpassing 95%, in predicting risk zones (low, medium, or high). It is concluded that this method is an effective tool for water quality management thus having the potential to adapt to real conditions.

abstract: The concept of fiduciary duty has long been framed around safeguarding a company's assets and finances. title: Small Modular Electrochemical Containers for Decarbonization of AI Data Centers
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems that are efficient, compact, modular, and compatible with space-constrained data centers. abstract: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on massive pretraining based on the Transformer architecture and show significant emergent effects in general tasks. title: Climate change perceptions and livelihood vulnerability of small-scale fishing communities along the Banadir Coast, Somalia
abstract: Small-scale fishing communities along Somalia’s Banadir coast face compounding climate-related pressures, yet remain almost entirely absent from the peer-reviewed literature on climate change perceptions and livelihood vulnerability. This study addresses that gap through a cross-sectional survey of 125 artisanal fishers at two Mogadishu landing sites, Abdiaziz and Hamarweyne. abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites offer high specific strength, high stiffness, and good corrosion resistance, which makes them suitable for aerospace, automotive, marine, and wind-energy structures. Their interlaminar fracture behavior is harder to pin down because delamination testing is slow and costly and the response shifts with loading mode. abstract: One of the main challenges of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in initial teacher education relates to its incorporation as a tool to support problem-solving and the design of learning experiences without neglecting critical reflection or the ethical responsibility of future teachers. The proposed study analyzed the perceptions of elementary education students regarding the use of GenAI in a problem-based learning experience conducted in a Geometry and Measurement course. title: Decompression Theory and Models for Diving Operations: A Review of Principles, Algorithms, and Applications
abstract: Decompression sickness (DCS) has been a persistent safety concern in diving operations since its recognition among 19th-century caisson workers. This review consolidates the theoretical foundations and historical development of decompression theory, from Dalton’s and Henry’s laws to representative algorithms used in contemporary diving practice. abstract: Parasites integrate environmental conditions across trophic levels and may therefore provide sensitive, mechanistically interpretable signals of ecosystem change. This narrative synthesis evaluates the potential of parasites and parasite communities as environmental bioindicators and climate-sensitive sentinels, with particular emphasis on arid ecosystems and Saudi Arabia. abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. abstract: The Tourism 5.0 paradigm is emerging as a pivotal response to the limits of a purely efficiency-oriented digitalisation, by placing people and sustainability back at the centre of innovation to create a holistic and responsible tourism ecosystem. abstract: Technical, social, avant-garde, global, and cognitive pressures are driving the adoption of new technologies characterized by constant updates and automation most notably generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and autonomous agents. abstract: Mitochondria are central regulators of cellular metabolism, integrating energy production, redox balance, and signaling pathways that shape aging trajectories. abstract: Flexible tactile sensors represent pivotal physical interfaces for human-machine interaction and embodied intelligence. However, the inherent trade-offs between sensitivity and sensing range, multimodal crosstalk, and long-term biosafety remain critical bottlenecks hindering practical implementation. abstract: Understanding long-term land-cover dynamics in the uMngeni catchment is critical for safeguarding ecosystem integrity and sustaining biodiversity under increasing anthropogenic and climatic pressures. However, spatially explicit assessments of these transformations remain limited, particularly under future climate change. This study analysed land-cover changes from 1991 to 2021 using Landsat (5, 7, and 8) imagery and random forest classification. abstract: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) creates escalation risks under U.S.–China competition because rapid technological change, strategic secrecy, and private control of advanced systems complicate effective oversight. This paper evaluates which governance model can best reduce these risks through a qualitative comparative case-study approach supported by legal analysis. abstract: Overlapping source signatures and nonlinear hydrochemical relationships complicate nitrate source apportionment at the watershed scale. This letter presents an integrated framework linking hydrochemical source identification, quantitative apportionment, and data-driven prediction, with nitrate isotopes providing complementary constraints on sources and transformations. abstract: The rise of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is transforming reading, writing, and learning practices in higher education, which presents ethical challenges related to authorship, transparency, and critical digital literacy. In the field of initial teacher education, it is necessary to move beyond an instrumental use of these technologies and promote ethical and pedagogical reflection on their implications. title: Climate‐Driven Straightening of Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclone Trajectories
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) trajectory shifts remain a critical uncertainty in climate risk assessment. However, due to the absence of effective quantification methods for TC trajectories, our understanding of the overall characteristics of their trajectory shifts and the underlying impact mechanisms remains quite limited. title: Developing scenario-based, near-term iterative forecasts to inform water management
abstract: Near-term, iterative ecosystem forecasts with scenarios representing alternate management decisions have high potential for providing valuable insights on how decisions may impact future ecological conditions. Scenario-based forecasts may be particularly useful for informing the decision-making around freshwater ecosystems managed for multiple objectives. We applied a near-term, iterative forecasting system at Lake Alexandrina, Australia, which is located at the nexus of one of the world’s largest catchments and a protected coastal wetland. title: Integrated Prediction and Analysis of Soil Erosion and Soil Organic Carbon Loss in the Dayekou Watershed, Qilian Mountains
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil erosion poses a critical threat to ecological security in mountain watersheds worldwide. Predicting its dynamics and associated soil organic carbon (SOC) loss remains an ongoing challenge during the 21st century due to complex interactions among climate, land use, and topography. This study developed an integrated modeling framework by combining Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks, Cellular Automata‐Markov (CA‐Markov), and the InVEST Sediment Delivery Ratio module to predict soil erosion and SOC loss in the Dayekou Watershed in northwest China's Qilian Mountains. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and health implications of air pollution in Nigeria
abstract: Air pollution is a major environmental and public health challenge in Nigeria, driven by urbanization, industrialization, transportation, biomass combustion, gas flaring, waste burning, and increasing energy demand. However, evidence on its sources, spatial and temporal patterns, health effects, and emerging monitoring approaches remains fragmented. This study conducted a systematic review of evidence on air pollution in Nigeria using the PRISMA 2020 framework. title: Digital Transformation Policies for Sustainable Tourism: A Comparative Policy Analysis of the European Union and Albania
abstract: This study analyzes how digital transformation and environmental sustainability are articulated as a common policy agenda known as the “twin transition” in the tourism sector, comparing the European Union (EU) as a mature regulatory and financing framework with Albania as an EU candidate country undergoing rapid but uneven digitalization. abstract: Solar flares are violent energy-release events in the solar atmosphere, accompanied by intense electromagnetic radiation and energetic particles that threaten satellites, radio communications, and power infrastructure, making accurate flare prediction essential for space weather early warning. This paper proposes a deep learning model integrating ConvNeXtV2 with a Transformer–Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to forecast whether a solar active region will produce a ≥ C-class or ≥ M-class flare within the next 24 h. title: CaMa‐PyTorch (v1.0): A New Catchment‐Based Macro‐Scale Floodplain Model Written in PyTorch
abstract: Abstract Accurate simulation of river discharge underpins hydrological research, climate‐impact assessment, and flood forecasting. CaMa‐Flood, a widely used global river‐routing model, applies physically based principles to represent water transport through river networks. However, its legacy Fortran implementation restricts compatibility with modern AI frameworks and prevents efficient GPU utilization. title: Six species in the Tapinoma nigerrimum complex (Hymenoptera: Formicidae): Tapinoma elongatum sp. nov. – an endemite of southwest Iberia
abstract: A new species of the Tapinoma nigerrimum complex, T. elongatum sp. nov ., is described from SW Spain. Applying a protocol of Numeric Morphology-based Alpha-Taxonomy considering 16 standardised characters recorded by high-resolution stereomicroscopy, the new species can be safely separated from the related species Tapinoma nigerrimum (Nylander, 1846), T. magnum Mayr, 1861, T. ibericum Santschi, 1925, T. darioi Seifert et al., 2017 and T. hispanicum Seifert et al., 2024 by more elongated funiculus segments, scape and mesosoma. abstract: Expedition scientists on the JOIDES Resolution ( JR ) during the Ocean Drilling Program (ODP), Integrated Ocean Drilling Program, and International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) carried out visual descriptions of hundreds of kilometers of cores to characterize the sequences drilled for subsequent subsampling and analysis. title: Urban Expansion, Thermal Transformation, and Ecological Stress in Chennai, India: A Multi-Temporal and Predictive Analysis Integrating Landsat and VIIRS
abstract: Rapid urban growth transforms land cover and alters surface thermal conditions, especially in fast-changing tropical coastal cities. This study examines the spatial and temporal relationships among land-use/land-cover (LULC) transformation, land surface temperature (LST), relative thermal stress, and nighttime illumination in Chennai, India. title: Application of radar remote sensing for cyclone damage mapping in Bangladesh: a coherence-based approach
abstract: Abstract. Rapid and reliable assessment of cyclone-induced damage remains a major challenge in coastal regions where cloud cover and accessibility limit conventional approaches. This study presents a coherence-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for identifying as well as quantifying cyclone-induced surface changes in coastal districts in Bangladesh. Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 data were analyzed using interferometric coherence to capture spatial and temporal variations associated with five major cyclones: Amphan (2020), Sitrang (2022), Mocha (2023), Hamoon (2023), and Remal (2024). title: Liquid hydrogen storage for transport applications: A cross-sector review of technologies, thermal management and deployment readiness
abstract: Hydrogen, particularly low carbon or clean hydrogen, is widely recognised as a promising clean fuel with strong potential for decarbonising the transport sector. Among various hydrogen carriers, liquid hydrogen offers exceptionally high gravimetric energy density, making it a potentially viable candidate for energy-intensive transport modes such as aviation, high-utilisation heavy-duty trucking, and selected marine applications where energy demands and range requirements exceed the capabilities of batteries and compressed hydrogen. title: Research Priorities for a Circular Economy for Plastic Sustainability in the Caribbean
abstract: Abstract Caribbean countries bear a disproportionate burden of marine plastic pollution because of their small landmass, high population density, and insufficient waste management infrastructure. Many Caribbean nations depend on informal, unmanaged landfills, underscoring an urgent need for more resilient, sustainable systems. title: Transitioning from Paper to Electronic Trade Documents: The Need for Reliable Physical Assurance
abstract: The transition from paper-based to electronic trade documents (eTDs) represents a critical step in modernising global supply chains; however, the absence of reliable mechanisms to verify the physical movement of goods vis-a-vis the eTD workflow remains a significant challenge. This study proposes the PROGRESS framework, an integrated digital trade architecture that combines AI-driven document verification with real-time physical tracking to ensure end-to-end assurance of consignments. title: Retroalimentación con IA generativa en la evaluación inclusiva: Marco de mediación docente basado en el diseño universal para el aprendizaje
abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into educational feedback offers opportunities to expand personalisation and accessibility, but it also raises risks of bias, opacity and the erosion of teacher mediation. The objective of this theoretical-conceptual article was to propose a framework to guide the use of generative AI in feedback from the standpoint of inclusive assessment and Universal Design for Learning (UDL). title: An Introduction to Methods to Quantify Carbon Dynamics in Rangeland Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Rangeland ecosystems store substantial terrestrial carbon and contribute to climate mitigation, yet their spatial heterogeneity, dynamic disturbance regimes, and multiple carbon pools make accurate quantification challenging. This introduction outlines and compares methodological approaches for measuring aboveground biomass, soil organic carbon, and fire-derived pyrogenic carbon across rangelands, with emphasis on how sampling design, sensor platforms, modeling frameworks, and accounting tools scale across ecological gradients. title: Microplastics and bisphenol A in the edible mussel Perna perna from southeastern Brazil: occurrence and dietary exposure assessment
abstract: Abstract Edible bivalves are an important route of human exposure to environmental contaminants because they are consumed whole and accumulate particulate and chemical hazards from coastal waters. This study assessed microplastics (MPs) and bisphenol A (BPA) in the brown mussel Perna perna from Espírito Santo Bay, southeastern Brazil, and estimated dietary exposure under average- and high-consumption scenarios. abstract: To what extent do machine-learning (ML) models predict self-reported Big Five personality traits? title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study
abstract: Introduction Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment. abstract: Abstract This viewpoint article argues that South African teacher education requires a distinctly decolonial agenda for generative artificial intelligence (AI), developed in critical dialogue with scholarship from Aotearoa New Zealand and wider international contexts. abstract: Maritime traffic risk shows significant spatial and temporal differences among vessel activities, navigation conditions, and environments. title: Contrasting microbial assembly and iron–sulfur–carbon cycling in the abandoned and present Yellow River estuaries
abstract: Large river deltas are important coastal carbon sinks, yet how changes in sediment supply are associated with subsurface microbial communities and biogeochemical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated meter-long sediment cores from the abandoned (YRM1) and present (YRM2) Yellow River estuaries, representing contrasting settings associated with the historical river diversion. abstract: Background Candida auris infections pose a severe global public health threat. abstract: One of the core technologies for water transportation safety is the intelligent anti-collision technology for vessels. Although significant progress has been made in the research of intelligent anti-collision for vessels, the problem of multi-vessel adaptive anti-collision in complex waters has not been fully explored. title: West Nile virus in Greece: One Health surveillance for early warning
abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) has emerged as a significant public health threat in Greece since 2010. Central Macedonia was the epicentre of the 2010 and 2022 outbreaks, whereas Attica, Eastern Macedonia and Thrace, and Thessaly predominated in other seasons. abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. title: Contrasting Seasonal Chlorophyll-a Dynamics in Tibetan Plateau Lakes Driven by Climate-Dependent Thermal and Mixing Processes
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP) hosts the world’s largest and highest-altitude plateau lake system, whose ecosystems are highly sensitive to climate change. Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), as a key indicator of phytoplankton biomass and lake trophic status, exhibits pronounced changes in response to long-term climatic and environmental changes. title: An improved CNN-Transformer network for seismic denoising with local–global feature modeling
abstract: In seismic exploration, field data are always affected by noise, reducing the quality of subsequent analysis. Striking a balance between signal preservation and noise attenuation effectively is a major challenge. This study adopts a dual-branch framework with convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformer architecture that integrates blind-spot convolution (BS-Conv) for local detail capture, rank-augmented linear attention (RALA) for global feature extraction, and the gated CNN block (GCB) for adaptive feature selection to achieve high-fidelity signal reconstruction and noise suppression.

abstract: Deep learning (DL) compilers rely on cost models and auto-tuning to optimize tensor programs for target hardware. abstract: ABSTRACT The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. abstract: The identification of individuals from their vocalisations offers a non-invasive approach to population monitoring, but only if individual vocal signatures are distinct and stay stable over time. abstract: Abstract. The global depletion of groundwater poses a significant challenge to water security. abstract: Ecological risk assessment (ERA) is moving toward greater ecological realism, where population-level responses across focal species are evaluated. abstract: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO 2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). abstract: Sentiment analysis has become increasingly important for interpreting customer-generated content across social media and digital technologies. abstract: Invasive plant-derived biochar offers a promising strategy for converting invasive biomass into valuable soil amendments. abstract: Batam City, designated a National Strategic Area and Free Trade Zone, has undergone rapid urbanization, industrialization, and infrastructure development that drive land use change. abstract: ABSTRACT Soil moisture monitoring is pivotal to precision agricultural irrigation. Conventional soil moisture sensors rely on external power supplies and suffer from poor environmental compatibility. Many conventional low-light image enhancement methods are typically designed for uniformly dark inputs and tend to over-brighten or distort normally exposed regions in mixed-illumination scene. abstract: Introduction Assessing residual contamination in coastal wetland soils after oil-well retirement requires comparisons with both active oil-well sites and natural reference wetlands. abstract: Oral biofilms are spatially ordered microbial communities whose pathogenic behavior is shaped by more than taxonomic composition. Their development reflects the combined effects of adhesin-receptor recognition, interspecies coaggregation, matrix formation, metabolite exchange, local physicochemical gradients and host-derived selection. abstract: Vegetation net primary production (NPP) is integral to the global carbon cycle, especially in the alpine ecosystems of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. However, hydropower construction can profoundly disrupt ecosystem health and carbon sequestration capacity, particularly along the Yarlung Zangbo River. Therefore, there is an urgent need to understand the impacts of hydropower construction on riparian vegetation NPP through precise, engineering-scale assessments of long-term changes. abstract: Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. title: Beyond total arsenic: rethinking seafood-related arsenic risk assessments
abstract: Seafood is an important component of human nutrition worldwide but also represents a major dietary pathway of arsenic (As) exposure. Assessing seafood-related health risks remains challenging because As toxicity depends strongly on chemical speciation rather than total concentration alone. Although seafood often contains high total arsenic (tAs), most occurs as organic compounds such as arsenobetaine, generally regarded as low in toxicity and rapidly excreted in humans. abstract: Abstract. Europe is a global leader in mitigating methane emissions through comprehensive policies, including the EU Methane Strategy and commitments under the Global Methane Pledge. National bottom-up inventories are widely regarded as high quality; however, atmospheric observations remain essential for independent verification and tracking emission reductions. abstract: Background Heavy metal contamination is a global concern due to its persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity to ecosystems and human health. The Galápagos Archipelago, with its high endemism and limited industrial activity, provides a unique setting where natural and anthropogenic sources may interact. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the presence, distribution, sources, and effects of heavy metals in environmental matrices and wildlife in the Galápagos. abstract: Pasture eaten (t DM/ha) is known to be a primary driver of profitability in New Zealand pastoral dairy farm systems. However, locally relevant estimates of achievable home-grown feed eaten (the “pasture potential”) are difficult to derive at industry scale. abstract: Hospital-trained deep learning models for echocardiographic wall motion abnormality detection achieve strong performance under standard clinical acquisition conditions but often degrade substantially when deployed on autonomous robotic acquisition systems. abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization and intensifying heat extremes are accelerating building energy demand and associated carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities. abstract: Cianjur Regency was often hit by landslides. In 2022, this regency was affected by landslide, leading to several civilian deaths, injuries, along with damaged houses and infrastructure. abstract: Annelids inhabit marine, freshwater, and terrestrial ecosystems and are important models for studying animal evolution, regeneration, and host-microbe interactions, yet their rapidly growing omics resources remain dispersed across repositories and publications. title: Projected Global Mortality and Economic Burden from Wildfire Smoke under Climate Change
abstract: Abstract Climate change is intensifying the frequency and severity of wildfires, amplifying landscape fire-sourced smoke (LFS), and its global health effects. However, future global LFS-attributable deaths and their associated attributable death costs remain poorly quantified. abstract: Societal Impact Statement Pollen allergies are a primary cause of seasonal allergic rhinitis, which affects over 500 million people globally, damaging quality of life and incurring significant costs in medical treatment and reduced work productivity. Many countries monitor pollen to inform allergy sufferers about seasonal pollen levels. In Norway, airborne pollen has been monitored for 45 years. abstract: Urban street-flooding is a growing concern in coastal cities, where intense rainfall and aging drainage systems often combine to disrupt daily life. This study introduces a value-at-risk (VaR) framework for anticipating resident-reported street-flooding complaints in New York City from antecedent rainfall. It draws on 15 years of publicly available 311 and weather-station data, with more than 75% of complaints occurred within two days of measurable rain. This finding motivates a rainfall-based approach to understanding complaint activity in three boroughs: Manhattan, Queens, and Staten Island.

abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) plays a central role in biological carbon pump (BCP) and global carbon cycling, but NPP estimates in high-latitude regions remain highly uncertain despite their disproportional contribution to the global carbon sink. abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the cost and efficiency of hydrogen production via water splitting is a long‐standing research challenge in support of carbon neutrality goals. abstract: Sharks and rays are an important yet heterogeneous component of India’s marine fisheries, contributing to food supply, household income, processing, trade and associated services, while many species have life-history characteristics that make them sensitive to sustained fishing mortality. abstract: Technology has become part of almost every daily task, and the way it interacts with the natural world is tangled. abstract: Abstract Urban heat exposure is unevenly distributed within cities, often disproportionately affecting socially and environmentally vulnerable populations. abstract: To improve the detection accuracy of SAR ship targets under complex background clutter, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 detection method for SAR ship detection tasks. abstract: Tourism ecological security (TES) is essential for sustaining destination resilience, ecological quality, and long-term tourism development. The digital economy (DE) plays a crucial role in improving TES by enabling smart monitoring, efficient resource allocation, and precision governance. Conversely, enhanced TES creates green demand and application scenarios for digital technologies, thereby facilitating DE upgrading. abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient that constrains productivity across many terrestrial ecosystems. Soil microorganisms regulate P transformation through distinct functional strategies, yet how these strategies vary with land use and environmental conditions across chronically P-impoverished landscapes remains poorly understood. They play a critical role in flood risk assessment, infrastructure design, and urban drainage planning. abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire-weather activity globally, yet the extent to which ecosystem structure modulates fire-weather regimes in complex mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. title: Beyond Consumption Smoothing: Investment-Focused Microfinance and Household Economic Progression in Rural South Africa
abstract: While extensive research exists on microfinance as a tool for smoothing consumption at the household level in poor communities, studies on the progression beyond consumption to household economic development are just beginning to emerge. This paper addresses the limited knowledge by examining how investment-focused microfinance loans enable poor households to transition from consumption smoothing to household economic development within rural communities. abstract: Numerous global initiatives and policy frameworks, including blue carbon strategies, biodiversity targets, and ecosystem restoration commitments, highlight the need to conserve and restore seagrasses, yet losses continue to accelerate across many regions. abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted health service utilisation worldwide. Its long-term effect remains uncertain, especially after the major adjustment of China’s COVID-19 control policies at the end of 2022. Evidence is also limited on whether recovery differed between hospitals and township health centres (THCs). The research aimed to evaluate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and its ending on health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province from 2014 to 2024. abstract: Incorporating the perspectives of local fishing communities and their ecological knowledge (LEK) can enhance policymaking and improve wildlife and economic management strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the local ecological knowledge of fishermen at Beni Haroun Dam regarding the Great Cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo) a species legally protected under Algerian law, and to reveal their conservation attitudes toward this species. abstract: La atención sanitaria basada en valor (ASBV) incentiva un modelo asistencial que se centra en la participación de las personas trabajadoras, los profesionales de la salud laboral y los proveedores con el fin de alcanzar el mejor resultado de salud al menor coste posible. abstract: Data-driven maritime accident analysis based on mainstream accident databases is approaching a high performance ceiling, calling for further breakthroughs from both data quality and modelling perspectives. abstract: This study examined the effects of the Media Literacy and Education course on the media use patterns of social studies pre-service teachers. Conducted within qualitative research framework, the study employed case study design and involved 33 teacher candidates enrolled at a state university in the Black Sea Region of Türkiye. abstract: Global water scarcity, influenced by climate change, population increase, and the exhaustion of freshwater resources, requires wastewater recycling. This article emphasizes the importance of wastewater within a circular and climate-resilient economy that functions as a source of clean water, fertilizers, and energy. abstract: "Schrödinger's Cat" is a quantum mechanics thought experiment in which a cat in a sealed box is considered both alive and dead until the box is opened and its true state observed. In species threat assessments, the reverse paradox can apply. We present the case of the Erect-crested penguin (Eudyptes sclateri), one of four extant penguin species currently listed as "Endangered" on the IUCN Red List - a classification based largely on limited and inconsistent observations from the 1970s. abstract: Accidental epiphytes — terrestrial plants that opportunistically establish in trees — occur across climatic regions, but the conditions that allow them to colonise arboreal habitats remain poorly understood. abstract: Reliable projections of temperature and precipitation underpin water and agricultural planning in arid Central Asia, yet most Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) assessments for the region are domain-averaged and do not resolve the contrasting physical-geographical zones of Uzbekistan. Conventional mesophilic enzymes lose much of their activity under the high-salinity, alkaline and thermally stressful conditions that define industrial biomass processing- a gap that microorganisms from naturally halo-alkaline ecosystems are well positioned to fill. title: Environmental Gradients and Turnover Shape Aquatic Invertebrate Communities in High‐Andean Ecosystems of Northern Chile
abstract: ABSTRACT The high Andean salars of northern Chile are unique ecosystems characterised by their high altitude (up to > 4000 m above sea level), high salinity and marked geographical isolation. Despite their ecological importance and increasing exposure to anthropogenic pressures such as lithium extraction, the diversity and composition of their aquatic invertebrate communities remain poorly documented. title: A Multiagent Reinforcement Learning-based Energy-Efficient Routing Algorithm for Submerged Optical Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Abstract The benefits of a rapid communication rate, ultrawide bandwidth, and reduced delay have made Submerged Optical Wireless Sensor Networks (SOWSNs) a popular topic of study. However, offering a low-consumption and dependable routing in SOWSNs is difficult because of the restricted power resources and highly fluctuating topologies induced by the water stream velocity. An Energy Efficient Routing Algorithm using Multiagent Reinforcement Learning (EERA-MRL) for SOWSNs has been presented as a solution to this problem. title: Cover and Content
Multi-modal deep reinforcement learning for traffic-aware adaptive routing in IoT logistics systems
abstract: The growth of IoT-enabled logistics has created rich real-time sensor streams that can support smarter delivery prediction, SLA monitoring, and adaptive routing. This paper presents MARLIN, an end-to-end traffic-aware logistics framework that learns directly from raw multi-modal data, including traffic sequences, LiDAR, camera inputs, IoT telemetry, and weather signals. MARLIN combines reconstruction-based modality encoders, hierarchical cross-attention fusion with learnable gating, an SLA-aware prediction head, and a graph-based Soft Actor-Critic routing agent. title: Climate change adaptation in Mexico: A literature review of progress, evidence gaps, and research priorities
abstract: Adaptation to climate change is key to reducing the vulnerability of human and natural systems. Over the past decades, research on climate change adaptation in Mexico has increased considerably. Previous reviews have focused on specific aspects of climate adaptation in Mexico; however, no study has systematically synthesized adaptation research across sectors, climate risks, responses, adaptation stages, and geographic regions within a common analytical framework.
