A novel nested NPR metamaterial with enhanced load-bearing capacity, energy absorption, and shape recovery performance
abstract: Abstract Traditional negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) structures rely on a limited number of local plastic hinges for energy absorption under compression, leading to limited plastic deformation zones, low plateau stress, and poor load-bearing capability. These limitations restrict their application in scenarios requiring both high energy absorption and load-bearing capability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a nested NPR structure without increasing the total mass. title: Dual opposing regulatory axes of EnvZ/OmpR control biofilm-mediated tolerance and OmpF-dependent resistance to β-lactams in Phytobacter diazotrophicus
abstract: Background Phytobacter diazotrophicus ( P. diazotrophicus ) is an infrequent opportunistic pathogen. Its biofilm-forming potential and the regulatory function of the EnvZ/OmpR two-component system linking biofilm formation and β-lactam resistance have yet to be elucidated. Herein, we confirmed biofilm production in P. diazotrophicus and generated envZ / ompR knockout mutants to dissect the dual regulatory roles of this two-component system. title: A multivariate causal chain detection methodology assessed on the ENSO modulation of the Northeastern Brazil precipitation
abstract: Abstract This study presents a novel data-driven methodology for extraction causal chains from high-dimensional climate datasets, with a particular focus on detecting and visualizing the pathways that link climate anomalies across geographically distant regions. The proposed framework is designed to be computationally efficient while maintaining high interpretability, making it suitable for large-scale analytical applications in climate science. title: Injecting visual semantics into sparse radar: A sensor enhancement framework for robust 3D detection
abstract: Abstract Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is highly valuable for all-weather autonomous driving perception due to its excellent environmental robustness and range-velocity measuring capability. However, it inherently suffers from severe point cloud sparsity, high noise, and insufficient semantic information, which makes it challenging to distinguish static targets from background clutter. Existing methods heavily rely on multi-sensor fusion or dense geometric distillation, which easily introduce geometric priors that are difficult to support by sparse radar observations. title: Multi-sensor remote sensing framework for water quality monitoring and hydroclimatic controls in small high-Andean lakes of the Central Andes
abstract: This study presents an integrated multi-satellite assessment of water quality in small high-Andean lakes (SHAL) and a reservoir in the Central Andes. Sentinel-2 MSI and Landsat 8 and 9 OLI imagery were used to evaluate multiple atmospheric correction methods and develop a framework for monitoring remote mountain lakes. Water quality and trophic state were investigated in seven SHAL and one reservoir within the Misicuni and Chocaya watersheds, Bolivia. title: Contrasting invasion risks of Pomacea canaliculata and Pontederia crassipes under future climate change in the middle and lower reaches of Yangtze River
abstract: The invasion and spread of alien aquatic organisms pose an increasing threat to ecosystem stability and functioning, biodiversity conservation, and socioeconomic development under ongoing climate change. However, limited attention has been given to the compound ecological risks of multi-species invasions driven by the combined effects of climate factors, topography, water quality, vegetation, and other environmental variables under future climate scenarios. title: A New Higher‐Level Taxonomy of Monothalamous Foraminifera
abstract: Monothalamous foraminifera are a highly diverse, paraphyletic assemblage of single-chambered lineages characterized by an organic or agglutinated test or lacking any external covering. Traditional morphology-based taxonomy divides them into the organic-walled Allogromiida and agglutinated Astrorhizida. Molecular systematics showed that this division is not justified as different wall types occur within the same lineages. title: Variation of total organic carbon concentrations in rainwater in Hanoi City, Vietnam
abstract: Organic carbon in precipitation represents an important pathway linking atmospheric processes with terrestrial and aquatic carbon cycling, yet data from rapidly urbanizing tropical and subtropical cities remain scarce. This study investigated total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations in 264 rainwater samples collected from 21 wards across Hanoi, Vietnam, between May 2023 and December 2025. TOC concentrations ranged from 0.41 to 17.72 mgC.L-1, with an average of 3.75±2.94 mgC.L-1, exceeding mean values previously reported for Asia and global continental regions. title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of mangrove cover based on Sentinel-2 imagery and Random Forest in Ketapang District, South Lampung, Indonesia

title: Numerical investigation of energy absorption behaviour of additively manufactured functionally graded lattice structures for automotive crash box applications
abstract: In the quest to improve crash safety in automotive structures, lightweight energy absorbing lattice architectures have gained considerable attention. This study presents a combined numerical and experimental investigation of additively manufactured uniform and functionally graded (FG) lattice structures for automotive crash-box applications. Four lattice topologies Body-Centered Cubic (BCC), Body-Centered Cubic with vertical stiffeners (BCCz), Octet Truss, and Re-entrant Auxetic are evaluated under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. title: Ecosystem Health Assessment of Hulun Lake Using an eDNA Metabarcoding‐Based Phytoplankton Index of Biotic Integrity
abstract: ABSTRACT Hulun Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in China, is currently experiencing significant water quality deterioration. Therefore, water quality assessment is of paramount importance, as it not only provides critical insights into the current pollution status of lakes but also offers a scientific basis for effective lake management and ecological restoration. title: Gaussian process reconstruction and seasonal change in tidal non-linearity in a monsoon-influenced estuary
abstract: Abstract Shallow estuaries distort the incoming tide as it propagates into shallowing water. How strong that distortion becomes controls the speed at which water levels rise, the direction of net sediment transport and the landward limit of salt intrusion. This study quantifies that distortion at Bang Pakong, a monsoon-influenced estuary on the inner Gulf of Thailand, using 353{,}644 water-level readings recorded at about ten-minute intervals between May 2019 and June 2026. title: Engineering mechanics of bio-inspired architected cementitious materials (ACM) and composites (ACC) enabled by digital fabrication
abstract: Concrete is inherently weak and brittle under tension, making it susceptible to cracking under mechanical and environmental loading. Recent advances in digital fabrication enable control over spatial arrangements of cementitious materials across meso-to-macro length scales, shifting cementitious design from passively formed microstructures to intentionally engineered architecture. title: Comprehensive assessment of ICESat-2/ATLAS geolocation performance and temporal stability during 2019–2025 over Eastern Xinjiang, China
abstract: Spaceborne photon-counting laser altimetry provides high-density along-track photon observations for a wide range of Earth surface applications. Although the geolocation accuracy of ICESat-2/ATLAS has been extensively evaluated, previous studies have generally focused on individual accuracy components or relatively limited observation periods, leaving its overall geolocation performance and temporal stability insufficiently characterized. abstract: Study region A high-altitude plateau city Kunming, the provincial capital of Yunnan in Southwest China. Study focus Urban atmospheric heavy metals (HMs) derived from natural and human sources are efficiently scavenged by wet deposition and subsequently delivered to terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, posing potential ecological and human health risks. title: The Role of Risk Assessment in Environmental Impact Assessment: A Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental impact assessment (EIA) is the core link in environmental decision‐making. However, traditional EIA often lacks structured methods for handling uncertainties and low‐probability high‐consequence risks. Risk assessment (RA) addresses this gap by enhancing the scientific basis of evaluation, supporting more defensible permitting and policy decisions, and improving transparency and public trust. title: Identification of potential pathogenic genes for lung adenocarcinoma induced by 6PPD-quinone through network toxicology and SHAP analysis
abstract: Background Lung cancer continues to maintain a high mortality rate, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being its most common type. As an emerging environmental pollutant, 6PPD-quinone is attracting increasing attention. Through network toxicology, we constructed a prognostic model and validated it with molecular docking and dynamics simulations, revealing its underlying molecular mechanisms. title: Conditioned media derived from HepG2 cells treated with phosphoeleganin synthetic-derived compound PE/2 improve cytokine balance and metabolic response in 3T3-L1 adipocytes
abstract: Background The liver–adipose axis regulates insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism, and its dysregulation contributes to metabolic disorders. PE/2, a semisynthetic derivative of the marine natural product phosphoeleganin, reduces IL-6 expression and secretion, enhancing insulin sensitivity in liver cells (HepG2). However, its role in liver–adipose communication is unclear. Methods To clarify the impact of PE/2 on liver–adipose tissue crosstalk, the conditioned media approach was used. title: Supporting post-bushfire biodiversity through citizen science tourism: recovery, regeneration, and reflections
abstract: The Australian 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires had profound ecological and socio-economic impacts on Kangaroo Island, threatening iconic species including koalas, Kangaroo Island dunnarts, and glossy black cockatoos, and disrupting local tourism. In response, and co-designed with multiple stakeholders, Passport to Recovery (P2R) was developed as a tourist-focused, place-based citizen science program to quickly integrate multiple biodiversity monitoring projects into a single, cohesive experience. title: Directional GPS‐IR Observations Using a Linearly Polarized Double‐Ridged Horn Antenna
abstract: ABSTRACT Most GPS interferometric reflectometry (GPS‐IR) studies use geodetic RHCP antennas with near‐hemispherical coverage and select the reflection zone through elevation and azimuth masks during processing. Direction‐ and polarization‐selective antennas are established in GNSS reflectometry, and tilted or linearly polarized antennas have also been used for SNR‐based retrieval, but a fixed‐beam horn antenna has not been evaluated for this purpose. title: SCRT ‐ DETR : A Lightweight Structural Degradation‐Aware Detector With Spatial‐Frequency Enhancement for Robust Pipeline Defect Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Regular monitoring of pipeline defects is crucial for the safe operation of municipal environmental infrastructure. However, tiny structural degradation, topological discontinuities, low‐light interference, and the slender morphology of defects pose significant challenges for accurate detection. In complex pipeline environments, existing detectors generally suffer from insufficient structural‐frequency perception and morphology‐insensitive localization. title: Modeling of Average Global Climate Change by 2200
abstract: According to a predictive global climate model described and used in a recent study (April 2025), future climate change is relatively insensitive to various greenhouse gas (GHG) emission scenarios, despite their significant differences. The author concluded that it is likely necessary to move even closer to pre-industrial CO₂ concentrations to truly reverse the current trend. This work aims to verify this hypothesis using a "280 ppm" scenario and to reproduce the 2025 study with a more powerful tool. title: Evaluating mangrove establishment trajectories and carbon recovery potential using a spatial age-based framework
abstract: Abstract Mangrove restoration is a vital nature-based solution for climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation. However, large-scale mangrove restoration success is predominantly evaluated using area-based metrics, which fail to capture the complex temporal trajectories of forest structural and functional recovery. Stand age directly determines structural heterogeneity and carbon stocks, making it a key indicator for monitoring recovery trajectories and estimating carbon stocks. title: Enhanced Aquaculture by Water Quality Assessment Using Discriminant Analysis Algorithm
abstract: Water quality is essential for sustainable aquaculture, but its variability makes assessment difficult. This study compares linear and quadratic discriminant analysis for classifying aquaculture water conditions using a public dataset of 4,300 observations with 14 physicochemical and biological parameters. Data preprocessing included outlier removal and feature standardization, followed by a stratified train-test split without hyperparameter tuning. title: A Review of Clustering Algorithms: Evolution, Comparison, and Challenges from Traditional Clustering to Deep Clustering
abstract: Against the background of big data, clustering algorithms, as a core task of unsupervised learning, have been widely applied, and the related theories and technologies have continued to iterate and develop. Existing reviews mostly focus on the classification and comparison of traditional clustering algorithms, while insufficient attention has been paid to the evolutionary relationship between traditional clustering and deep clustering. title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. title: Environmental controls of mangrove propagule and seedling establishment: salinity, hypoxia, sulfide, sediment instability, and early root function
abstract: Mangrove propagules and seedlings encounter interacting environmental constraints before secure anchorage and functional root systems develop. This narrative review synthesizes hydrological, physiological, biogeochemical, and sediment evidence to organize establishment into propagule delivery, retention, rooting, seedling persistence, and progression toward sapling recruitment. Tidal connectivity, elevation, hydroperiod, and drainage influence both propagule movement and root-zone conditions. title: Utilizing calcite‐bound phosphate to reconstruct historical phosphorus loading to marl lake ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing historical phosphorus (P) concentrations in lakes has been a long‐standing problem for paleolimnology. The most commonly applied method is the use of diatom‐inferred total P models, but there are well‐documented limitations to these approaches. Authigenic calcite co‐precipitated with P is a promising geochemical indicator of ambient P conditions in the water column through time. title: Science Needs for a Terrestrial Biosphere Tipping Point Early Warning System
abstract: Abstract Tipping points in the Earth system have the potential to cause major detrimental impacts to the biosphere and societies. Their inherent nonlinearity implies that even relatively small additional increases in external forcing might result in disproportionately large adjustments to components of the Earth system. In some cases, tipping points may lead to alternative states that would be difficult to return from. title: Forecasting Annual Capture Fisheries Production in Somalia Using ARIMA Models
abstract: The study aims to forecast the production of Somalia's capture fisheries for the five years that follow, from 2024 to 2028, using the Box-Jenkins method and employing in-sample data spanning 50 years, from 1974 to 2023. Among the alternative models, ARIMA (1,1,1) was determined by the study to be the most suitable. The study obtained the data from World Bank development indicators (WDI) for the period between 1975 and 2023. journal: Journal of Ocean and Coastal Economics

title: Building resilience of water infrastructure to cascading cross-border climate risks: a case study of Malawi’s drinking water infrastructure
abstract: Background Malawi’s water security depends on the Lake Malawi-Shire River system, which receives approximately 60% of its inflows from transboundary catchments in Tanzania and Mozambique. This dependence creates cascading cross-border climate risks that threaten downstream water infrastructure. The system exhibits threshold behavior at 474.1 m above sea level (asl), below which hydrological drought conditions emerge and outflows to the Shire River cease. abstract: O presente trabalho avaliou a eficiência do aprendizado profundo para a classificação de uso e cobertura da terra utilizando imagens de altíssima resolução espacial do bairro Conjunto Paulo VI, em Belo Horizonte (MG). title: Wetl-SAM2YNet: A foundation model driven framework for fine-scale wetland mapping
abstract: Fine-scale wetland mapping is challenged by fragmented patch shapes, spectral confusion between wet and dry surfaces, and the scarcity of annotated high-resolution training samples. This study proposes Wetl-SAM2YNet, a framework based on Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2, a vision foundation model), designed for community level wetland classification in arid regions. title: Monitoring seasonal and long-term forest canopy dynamics using Sentinel-2 imagery and Random Forest on the Google Earth Engine platform
abstract: Understanding forest canopy dynamics is critical for assessing the condition, resilience, and conservation priorities of protected landscapes. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal and seasonal variation in mapped forest canopy density within the Orchha Wildlife Sanctuary, Madhya Pradesh, India, using multi-seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery and a Google Earth Engine (GEE)-based Random Forest (RF) classification framework. title: Solid-state Volvariella volvacea-fermented rice milling by-product as a potential sustainable alternative protein source to soybean meal in juvenile milkfish (Chanos chanos) diet
abstract: The present study evaluated solid-state Volvariella volvacea- fermented rice bran (VFRB) as a potentially sustainable alternative protein source to soybean meal (SBM) in diets for juvenile milkfish ( Chanos chanos ). A 60-day feeding trial was conducted following a completely randomized design with five dietary treatments in triplicate: a full SBM-based control and diets in which SBM was replaced with VFRB, at 25, 50, 75, and 100% by weight. title: Review article: Climate hazards in African cities – knowledge gaps and research needs
abstract: Abstract. This study presents a semi-systematic synthesis of scientific literature published between 2015 and 2025 on climate risk in African cities. From an initial set of 1,832 records identified through broad climate- and urban-related keywords, 273 articles were selected through title and abstract screening. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study combines quantitative mapping of geographic coverage, climate hazards, methodologies, and keyword networks with expert review and AI-assisted synthesis of research gaps. title: Ecotourism: A Key Strategy For Realizing Golden Indonesia 2045: Penelitian
abstract: The Golden Indonesia 2045 initiative aims to transform Indonesia into a globally competitive, inclusive, and sustainable developed nation by the centenary of its independence. However, challenges such as environmental degradation, climate change, and interregional economic inequality demand a reorientation of the national development paradigm from extractive modalities to a green economy. This article aims to analyze ecotourism as a key strategy in supporting the achievement of the four main pillars of the Golden Indonesia 2045 Vision. abstract: Background Elite swimmers increasingly face calendars requiring multiple performance peaks within a single season, a scenario for which traditional single-target periodization models may be insufficient. Methods This longitudinal collective case study followed five elite female middle- and long-distance freestyle swimmers across a 52-week macrocycle preparing for two national championships. title: An efficient hybrid weld seam detection network based on knowledge distillation and model pruning
abstract: Abstract Accurate weld type recognition and stable keypoint localization are essential for automated weld seam inspection, yet real-time deployment is still challenged by the high computational cost of dense prediction models and visual disturbances such as arc glare and spatter. This paper presents LDCNet, a lightweight compression framework for DenseNet-CenterNet. title: Bridging Geomythology and Geospatial Analysis for Flood Risk Assessment in Tamil Nadu
abstract: ABSTRACT The need for more holistic and context‐aware approaches to flood‐risk assessment has become increasingly urgent with extreme climate change events faced globally. Modern models overlook the long‐term environmental knowledge incorporated in ancient literature, myths, and cultural memory as they rely primarily on hydrological and geospatial datasets. To address this gap, this study integrates geomythology with GIS‐based flood‐susceptibility analysis using openly available data on land cover, rainfall, elevation, slope, and topographic wetness index (TWI). title: Short-Term Reservoir Inflow Prediction Using Weather Forecast Data and ExtraTrees Regressor for Hydroelectric Power Plant Operations
abstract: Reliable short-term inflow forecasting is critical for optimizing hydroelectric power plant (HPP) operations, where water availability is directly influenced by dynamic and often extreme weather patterns. Inaccurate inflow estimations can result in either uncontrolled water spills or reservoir levels dropping below operational thresholds, both leading to reduced energy efficiency and potential operational risks. title: Data Driven Model Development to Predict Soil Temperature and Freeze-Thaw Cycles in Pavement Foundation Systems
abstract: Abstract Road infrastructure is central to economic development of the United States. However, particularly in cold climates, the soil temperature and annual freeze-thaw cycles significantly impact road conditions, therefore it is important to accurately predict the number of freeze-thaw cycles and their duration. While prior data-driven studies have predicted soil temperature at daily or monthly timesteps, none have combined sub-daily temperature prediction with direct estimation of freeze-thaw cycle count and duration in a form deployable by practicing engineers. title: Cross-DATA: Cross-Data Attention Distillation for Lightweight Sound Classification with Limited Data
abstract: Using the UrbanSound8K dataset as a representative case, this study investigates how lightweight acoustic models can be trained with limited labeled data in resource-constrained environments. Because conventional knowledge distillation confines knowledge transfer to a single target dataset, it leaves the rich prior knowledge in external audio sources largely unused. title: Cell-associated viral community composition and its functional potential in a dimictic lake on the Canadian shield
abstract: The Turkey Lake Watershed (TLW), located in Northern Ontario, forms a cascading lake system that drains into Lake Superior. Historically, the TLW has served as a key research site for studies on acid rain and climate change. Despite its long-standing ecological importance, investigations into its microbial communities remain limited, and to date, no studies have explicitly examined the viral component of this watershed. title: Drivers of Ecosystem Metabolism in an Anthropogenically Modified Delta
abstract: Abstract Estuaries are under threat globally from a wide range of stressors, with rates of ecosystem metabolism – respiration (R), gross primary production (GPP), and net ecosystem metabolism (NEM) – representing a way for resource managers to quantify their impacts. In this study, we assessed how natural and anthropogenic stressors have altered metabolism within the extensively modified Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (“Delta”) in California, USA. title: Physicochemically Motivated Decomposition for Long-Sequence Urban O3 Forecasting: A Cross-Method Comparison
abstract: Surface ozone (O3) forms via nonlinear chemistry and is highly non-stationary, complicating 168-h forecasts. Many models omit key physical drivers, mix time scales, and degrade quickly with lead time. We propose a decomposition-ensemble framework that fuses surface observations with NWP predictors (e.g., solar radiation, PBL height). title: LARVA-Net: A Bio-Inspired Recursive Attention Model for IoT-Based Microclimate Prediction in Black Soldier Fly Insectariums
abstract: Microclimate prediction is critical for optimizing larval growth and productivity in Black Soldier Fly (BSF) insectariums, where temperature and humidity exhibit nonlinear and time-varying dynamics. Conventional models such as Vector Autoregression (VAR) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) often struggle to balance accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability in IoT-based environments. title: ViT‐A‐LSTM‐DE Framework With Dense Fusion Encoder for Superior Algal Bloom Risk Assessment and Monitoring
abstract: The occurrence of algal blooms poses serious environmental, economic, and health risks, requiring reliable and timely forecasting systems. This research introduces a multimodel framework named modified vision transformer-based adaptive long short term memory with dynamic encoder for accurate detection and prediction of algal bloom. A modified vision transformer is employed to extract the fine-grained spatial features from satellite images while an adaptive long short-term memory with dynamic encoder captures temporal dependencies and contextual variations in time-series data. title: A multi-attention mechanism-improved ResNet18 approach for lithology identification and classification
abstract: Lithology identification is vital for improving geological exploration accuracy, optimizing petroleum exploration schemes, and ensuring construction engineering safety. Traditional identification methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and heavy dependence on domain expertise. title: Analysis of Clean Water Demand in Telawang District, East Kotawaringin Regency
abstract: Access to clean water is a fundamental community need that requires careful planning based on population growth and the capacity of existing water supply infrastructure. Telawang District, East Kotawaringin Regency, continues to face limitations in clean water services, as the existing non-PDAM water supply system serving the Ibu Kota Kecamatan (IKK, district administrative center) has a production capacity of only 10 L/s and serves 394 household connections, equivalent to approximately 1,576 people or 9.6% of the total population of 16,397. title: Collaborative Prediction Algorithm for Investment and Financing Network System Based on Improved Hypergraph Convolution and Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: After more than 20 years of rapid development, the Chinese financial market is experiencing a decrease in user traffic dividends. The overall industry growth rate is slowing down, yet the market’s potential demand remains substantial. The industry is transitioning from a phase focused on incremental growth to one that equally emphasizes incremental and existing stock growth, accelerating the exploration of new development models. This paper proposes the CPA-FHA, a collaborative prediction algorithm for investment and financing networks based on improved hypergraph convolution and ant colony al

title: Listening to the City: Evaluating BirdNET Reliability and Bias in Urban Bird Community Assessments
abstract: ABSTRACT BirdNET is increasingly used for passive acoustic monitoring (PAM), yet its reliability in urban environments that have high levels of anthropogenic noise remains poorly understood. We evaluated BirdNET's performance in two Italian cities, Turin and Florence, by analysing over 4300 10‐min audio recordings (approximately 723 h of audio in total) and manually validating up to 500 detections per species. title: C-MixNet: Regime-aware clustering and MDN-augmented LUBE for uncertainty-aware wind power forecasting
abstract: Wind power forecasting under uncertainty remains a critical challenge due to non-stationary patterns, regime shifts, and fluctuating dynamics across time. Existing interval-based methods often struggle to generalize across heterogeneous operating conditions, resulting in inconsistent coverage and suboptimal reliability. This paper presents C-MixNet, a hybrid framework that integrates regime-aware clustering, Mixture Density Network (MDN), and Lower Upper Bound Estimation (LUBE) for robust Prediction Interval (PI) generation. title: Three challenges for legacy phosphorus in different catchment compartments
abstract: The loading of soils with P that exceeds crop requirements may have involved chemical fertilizer and manure P additions with certain P forms. Both the P source nature and in-situ conversion processes alter resulting P forms present in soils (Stutter et al., 2015). Forms include orthophosphate inorganic P as well as diverse P compounds where P or PO43− joins C-based molecules (so-called organically complexed P), necessitating hydrolysis and desorption to liberate plant available P into solution. title: Deep operator network prediction of velocity profiles in combined wave-current bottom boundary layers
abstract: Accurate prediction of the velocity profiles in combined wave-current bottom boundary layers is essential for offshore engineering applications. While our previous work in Yin et al. (2026) proposed data-driven methods to model the spatiotemporally varying velocity profiles, it relied on empirical mathematical expressions for both the wave and current parts. This study introduces an advanced framework that utilizes the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) architecture to learn the operators mapping the flow parameters to the velocity profiles. title: Phytochemical-based quality control of cayenne pepper using spectroscopic monitoring of lycopene content and antioxidant capacity
abstract: Abstract Quality control in cayenne pepper fruit is important for maintaining product consistency. The research aimed to evaluate lycopene content and antioxidant capacity as the main indicators of cayenne pepper quality. Visible-near infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy is an emerging technology that can predict lycopene content and antioxidant capacity non-destructively, accurately, and quickly. Spectral data (381–1065 nm) were analyzed using support vector machine regression to develop the calibration model. title: Projected Climate‐Induced Range Dynamics of Alburnoides Species in Anatolia Using an Ensemble Species Distribution Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems harbour a substantial proportion of global biodiversity yet face intense pressure from multiple stressors. Historical models indicate that Türkiye has served as a crucial hub of fish diversification since the Late Miocene, although projections suggest that freshwater biodiversity faces escalating threats. This study investigates the past, present and future distribution dynamics of 14 species belonging to the Alburnoides genus in Türkiye using an ensemble species distribution modelling (SDM) approach. title: An Adaptive Multimodal Meta-Fusion Framework for Alzheimer's Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia Classification using EEG, MRI, and Cognitive Biomarkers
abstract: A single-modality approach to neurodegenerative disease classification is often limited by heterogeneous clinical manifestations, modality-specific feature distributions, and incomplete data availability. This study proposes an Adaptive Multimodal Meta-Fusion (AMMF) framework integrating cognitive-demographic, structural MRI, and EEG biomarkers for classification of the Alzheimer's disease (AD), Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD), and Cognitively Normal (CN) participants. title: A Transferable Individual‐Based Framework for Quantifying Demographic Structure and Spatial Organization in Colonial Species Using UAV Imagery
abstract: ABSTRACT Remote sensing of colonial wildlife has largely focused on estimating population size, providing limited insight into internal demographic structure and spatial organization. We present a transferable, individual‐based framework that integrates morphology‐informed classification and spatial metrics to extract demographic composition and social spacing from high‐resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. title: Multi-dataset cross-domain knowledge distillation for unified medical image segmentation, classification, and detection
abstract: We propose a unified cross-domain transfer learning framework that leverages knowledge from multiple heterogeneous medical imaging datasets to improve performance across segmentation, classification, and object detection tasks. Our approach employs a multi-dataset teacher–student paradigm, in which multiple source and target teachers are first trained on individual datasets and subsequently fused into a single joint teacher that aggregates domain-invariant representations learned across sources. title: Toward evidence-based fish welfare regulation: policy lessons from Chile, Norway, and Scotland
abstract: Aquaculture has become a major contributor to global food production, but its rapid expansion and intensification have increased concerns regarding the welfare of farmed fish. Although advances in welfare science have generated animal-based measures, operational welfare indicators, and increasingly sophisticated monitoring technologies, their incorporation into regulatory frameworks remains uneven. This review examines the evolution of fish welfare regulation and compares the regulatory approaches of Chile, Norway, and Scotland, three major salmon-producing jurisdictions representing distinct

title: An Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) calculation and compliance screening tool: Development, verification, and benchmark comparison
abstract: The Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI), mandatory under MARPOL Annex VI since January 2023, requires existing ships to demonstrate a design-efficiency level that a large share of the conventionally configured fleet cannot meet without intervention. The tools available to evaluate and plan for compliance, however, are limited: certification grade calculators are proprietary and opaque, while academic treatments tend to embed the computation within one-off scenario studies rather than provide a reusable, openly described instrument. title: COLLABORATIVE INNOVATION MODELS FOR APPLICATION-ORIENTED MARITIME UNDERGRADUATE COLLEGES UNDER THE BACKGROUND OF BUILDING A MARITIME POWER
abstract: Building a maritime power is a talent problem before it is a technology problem, and application-oriented maritime undergraduate colleges sit where the two meet. Their inherited teaching models, though, were designed for a shipping industry that no longer exists, and the distance between what they produce and what the blue economy needs has widened under digital transformation. This paper asks what collaborative innovation actually looks like inside such institutions, and whether the multi-stakeholder arrangements now promoted in Chinese policy close that distance. title: A cross-domain fault diagnosis method for high-speed train axlebox bearings based on time-frequency mapping and adversarial networks
abstract: Abstract The health condition of axlebox bearings in high-speed trains is directly associated with operational safety. However, variations in rotational speed, load, and operating environment induce pronounced domain shift in vibration signals, which undermines the generalization capability of intelligent diagnosis models trained under a single operating condition.To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross condition bearing diagnosis method integrating a CNN BiLSTM hybrid network and multi constraint domain adaptation for cross condition diagnosis of high speed train axle box bearings.

title: Shared-first risk-aware open-set domain adaptation for catalogue-absent structural state identification
abstract: Abstract Bridge structural health monitoring (SHM) models are normally trained with a fixed catalogue of structural states, yet the bridge continues to change after the model is deployed. Traffic, support restraint, ageing, and local cracking can produce target responses for which no source label exists. In that situation, closed-set domain adaptation is risky because alignment may pull an unfamiliar response into a known class. title: Amplicon sequencing reveals host-associated lineages of Cystobasidiomycetes (Basidiomycota, Pucciniomycotina) in Arthoniales (Ascomycota, Arthoniomycetes), but no association with thallus architecture
abstract: Lichen-associated Cystobasidiomycetes have been reported from a wide range of lichens worldwide. Previous studies proposed that lichen-associated Cystobasidiomycetes may be involved in the development of the thallus cortex, suggesting also a contribution to the construction of thallus architecture within the Parmeliaceae . However, Parmeliaceae do not include species with ecorticate thalli. title: Environment-Specific Guidance Improves Forecast Skill for Isolated Convection Initiation over South China
abstract: Abstract Is convection initiation (CI) harder to forecast in some large-scale environments? Using 8,607 radar-detected isolated CI events over South China during 2018–2023 and ERA5 fields, we identify two recurrent pre-CI environments: a thermal environment with broad warm-moist support and a dynamic environment with more organized flow. Across 200 forecast models, dynamic cases generally have lower skill than thermal cases. title: Environment-adaptive Acoustic–Optical sensing for fish abundance estimation in complex aquaculture waters
abstract: Abstract Reliable fish abundance estimation is essential for the operation and management of aquaculture systems, but remains challenging under turbidity, bubble interference, target occlusion, and acoustic reverberation. This study develops an Acoustic–Optical fusion sensing framework for robust fish monitoring in complex aquaculture waters. An environment-aware geometric fusion network, termed EAGF-Net, is proposed to integrate optical appearance information with sonar-derived geometric features. title: Deciphering water salinization mechanisms of arid lake-groundwater systems in Inner Mongolia, China: An integration of multi-isotopic models
abstract: Study region Three representative arid lake-groundwater systems in Inner Mongolia, China: Daihai Lake (DL), Ulansuhai Lake (UL), and the Bahannao Lake Group (BL). Study focus Salinization severely threatens water security of arid lake-groundwater systems, yet the coupled mechanisms linking salinity sources, geochemical transformations and groundwater salt transport have not been well understood. abstract: Background Complete blood count (CBC) and biochemical parameters (liver function, renal function, Blood glucose, and lipid profile) are the most routinely used tests in clinical laboratory practice, and serve as critical evidence for disease diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the distribution patterns of age- and sex-related differences in CBC and biochemical indicators, identify the age-related inflection points of these indicators, and analyze their correlation patterns across different sexes and age groups. title: Segmentation of flexible intermediate bulk container lifting lug for electrolytic aluminum plant based on improved U-Net
abstract: This paper addresses the automation of flexible intermediate bulk container (FIBC) lifting loop segmentation in aluminum electrolysis plants by proposing an improved semantic segmentation approach based on an enhanced U-Net architecture. Traditional manual operations are inefficient and pose safety risks, while factors such as dust and uneven lighting in complex industrial environments challenge existing vision algorithms. title: Phase‐Shift‐Assisted Wind‐Driven Triboelectric Nanogenerator With a Ternary Contact Structure for Low‐Ripple Output and Corrosion‐Related Applications
abstract: The wind energy frictional nano‐generator (W‐TENG) can efficiently collect low‐frequency, random mechanical energy from the wind for self‐powered systems, such as smart farms; however, the practical output signal has severe pulse and fluctuation issues. This article introduces a phase‐shift‐assisted wind‐driven W‐TENG with a ternary contact structure. title: Urban sentinels: quantifying marginal effects of impervious cover on Brachionus–Keratella dominance
abstract: Abstract Urbanization, often quantified as impervious cover, alters catchment hydrology and limnological conditions, yet sensitive bioindicators and quantitative metrics for small urban freshwater ecosystems remain limited. We evaluated whether rotifers with widespread distribution ( Brachionus and Keratella ) can serve as indicators of urbanization across 18 ponds in Berlin along an impervious-cover gradient. title: Swarm-optimized heterogeneous ensemble with quantile regression for small-sample long-tailed distribution prediction
abstract: Predicting maintenance costs for industrial equipment faces the dual challenges of small sample sizes and long-tailed data distributions. Existing methods struggle to ensure both point prediction accuracy and reliable intervals for the tail. abstract: Wind turbine maintenance decisions are frequently made under uncertainty, yet conventional degradation models often provide deterministic predictions that ignore the tail risks associated with unexpected component failure. We propose a stochastic operator residual learning framework with conformal calibration for risk-aware wind turbine maintenance. title: Probabilistic constraints on the zero emissions commitment
abstract: Estimates of the zero emissions commitment (ZEC) rely on multi-model ensembles that sample structural differences between models but cannot assign probabilities to outcomes. Here we present, to our knowledge, the first observationally constrained perturbed parameter ensemble (PPE) assessment of ZEC with a process-based Earth system model, using ~340 members of the University of Victoria Earth System Climate Model across ten emission-rate and carbon-budget combinations following and extending the flat10MIP protocol. title: Transformación Digital en la educación superior: impacto en el rendimiento académico
abstract: El análisis y tratamiento de datos en las Instituciones de Educación Superior supone un reto importante para el correcto funcionamiento administrativo y académico. title: Developing an Eco-Nationalism-Based Village Regulatory Model for SDG Achievement and Sustainable Local Economic Development in Madura, Indonesia
abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the use of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study aims to develop an eco-nationalism-based village regulatory model that integrates environmental protection, sustainable local economic development, and SDG implementation within village governance. title: The Role of Blue Economy in Attracting Foreign Direct Investment and Enhancing Gulf Cooperation Council Fiscal Balance
abstract: Objectives This study examines the role of selected blue economy logistics indicators in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) and enhancing fiscal balance in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Because consistent sector-level FDI data are unavailable, maritime trade and container port throughput are used as measurable proxies for the maritime-logistics component of the blue economy. title: Physics-Frequency-Guided Bidirectional Mamba Network for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Bearing Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Rolling bearing fault diagnosis is critical for the reliable operation of rotating machinery. However, vibration signals collected under varying sampling rates, devices, and operating conditions often exhibit domain shifts, and only limited labeled samples are available in the target domain. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-scale physics-frequency bidirectional Mamba network (MS-PFMamba) for cross-sampling-rate, cross-device, and few-shot bearing fault diagnosis. abstract: ABSTRACT The shipping industry plays a vital role in global trade and also exerts significant environmental and social pressures due to high fuel consumption, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and intensive port activities. Implementing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices offers a strategic pathway to enhance sustainability performance in this sector; however, it remains difficult to determine which managerial and operational actions can most effectively drive improvements in ESG performance. title: Reconstructing Glacier Dynamics in Complex Terrain with ICESat-2 and Gaussian Process Interpolation
abstract: Abstract. We apply Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to ICESat-2 along-track height change data to generate spatially continuous glacier height change fields across two glaciated regions with complex topography and dynamic behaviour: Larsen-B (Antarctic Peninsula) and central Southern Svalbard. title: Peak-valley resource demand forecasting for enhanced data reliability
abstract: Accurate load demand forecasting serves as the fundamental prerequisite for data reliability analysis in multi-user heterogeneous load access scenarios. In such environments, the volume of data flows generated by industrial, residential, and commercial loads exhibits complex temporal variation patterns characterized by distinct periodicity and volatility. title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. title: Effects of illumination conditions and phenological stages on tree species classification using UAV RGB imagery
abstract: Accurate tree species information is essential for biodiversity assessment, forest ecosystem monitoring, and adaptive forest management. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery offers a cost-effective and flexible means of repeatedly acquiring very-high-resolution canopy information; however, the image characteristics used to distinguish tree species can vary with vegetation phenology and natural illumination. title: FSF-RTDETR: a frequency–spatial feature fusion network for eggplant fruit disease and pest detection in complex agricultural scenes
abstract: Detecting fruit diseases and pests in complex agricultural scenes remains challenging due to large target-scale variation, weak lesion features, leaf and branch occlusion, and severe background interference. To address these problems, this study focuses on eggplant fruit disease and pest detection and proposes FSF-RTDETR, a frequency–spatial fusion model. title: Research on Warehouse Path Planning for Logistics Robots Based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
abstract: How to efficiently and reasonably carry out path planning has always been a hot spot of research in the field of warehouse logistics robots. We propose a logistics robot warehouse path planning strategy based on the Improved Whale Optimisation Algorithm (IWOA). The whale optimisation algorithm’s convergence speed is slow, making it easy to fall into the limitations of the local optimum. title: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery gearboxes based on low-rank adaptive convolutional network
abstract: Traditional fault diagnosis methods face challenges in extracting temporal features from measured signals and achieving noise-resistant robustness in practical measurement scenarios. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight compound fault diagnosis model (TLCN) based on a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) convolutional network. title: Financial data analytics without identification: a structured review of a fragmenting field
abstract: We review 224 studies of financial data analytics published between 2020 and 2026 and document a mismatch between the questions the field asks and the designs it uses to answer them. Roughly three in ten titles in the corpus assert a causal relationship — analytics capability improving financial performance, digital inclusion reducing unemployment, ESG orientation raising firm value — while not one names a difference-in-differences, instrumental-variable, regression-discontinuity, or event-study design. abstract: This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Spartina anglica extract (SAE) in a human keratinocyte model of inflammation. HaCaT cells were stimulated with tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) to induce inflammatory responses. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay to determine non-cytotoxic concentrations. abstract: Avian schistosomes (AS) are trematodes of significant medical importance as the causative agents of cercarial dermatitis, a re-emerging waterborne human disease. Their monitoring has traditionally relied on examination of snail hosts; however, this approach is time-consuming, requires taxonomic expertise and often underestimates their diversity due to low prevalence of infection. Although environmental DNA (eDNA)-based methods have shown promise in detecting AS, most studies have employed species-specific assays that restrict the discovery of novel genetic lineages. title: Concentration‐Dependent Growth, Survival and Tissue Responses of Asian Seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) Fingerlings Following Short‐Term Dietary Exposure to Polyethylene Microplastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are emerging aquatic pollutants that may impair fish health through ingestion and tissue‐level toxicity. This study evaluated whether short‐term dietary exposure to fluorescently labeled polyethylene microplastics (PE‐MPs) produced concentration‐dependent changes in growth, survival, intestinal morphology, and skeletal‐muscle integrity in Asian seabass fingerlings. abstract: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. abstract: Abstract Population assignment methods enable biodiversity managers to identify the population origins of individuals or samples, which can help to determine the population‐specific impacts of human activities. abstract: Wind turbines operating in complex terrain are exposed to terrain-induced aerodynamic disturbances, such as strong vertical wind shear, wind veer, turbulence and flow deviation, which increase asymmetric rotor loading and can degrade operational reliability. The quantitative link between such disturbances, the operational response recorded by the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, and the parameterisation of Wind Sector Management (WSM) strategies remains insufficiently documented for real turbines. title: Tension–Tension Fatigue Damage Evolution and Failure Mechanism of Carbon/Glass Hybrid Fiber Composite Rods for Mooring Cables
abstract: ABSTRACT Fatigue failures of major structural cables threaten engineering infrastructure. Fiber‐reinforced polymer (FRP) composites are promising alternatives to steel cables, while hybrid composites can overcome the limitations of single‐fiber systems and promote applications in super‐long‐span and high‐tonnage cables. abstract: South Sulawesi possesses abundant renewable energy potential, particularly from hydro, wind, solar, and biomass resources. However, rapid population growth and increasing energy consumption across sectors create challenges in ensuring sustainable energy supply and planning. This study aims to project the mid-term renewable energy supply and demand in South Sulawesi using the Long-range Energy Alternatives Planning (LEAP) model. More critically, each individual’s spectral baseline level and fatigue-change pattern differ, so simply lengthening the window still leaves models struggling to predict across individuals from observed spectral features. title: Input-data perturbation in groundwater level prediction: a controlled experiment on accuracy–reliability trade-offs among data augmentation and Bayesian-type uncertainty estimation methods
abstract: Groundwater is a major water resource for irrigation and domestic use, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where freshwater is scarce and the total amount of rainfall is limited. Hence, monitoring both quality and quantity parameters of this source is necessary for optimal water resources management, environmental studies, and ecosystem modeling, as well as ecological planning. title: NAA-GAN: Noise-Aware Cross-Attention for Robust Blind Image Watermarking
abstract: Robust blind image watermarking remains challenging because embedded watermark information must remain recoverable after image processing while preserving the visual quality of the watermarked image. This paper proposes NAA-GAN, a generative adversarial watermarking framework that conditions the encoder on a six-dimensional descriptor of the anticipated distortion category. abstract: Abstract Freshwater scarcity is a major global challenge driven by population growth, industrialization, climate change, and declining freshwater resources. This review systematically and critically evaluates recent advances in nanofluid‐assisted solar still desalination, focusing on freshwater productivity, thermal performance, energy and exergy efficiency, stability, economic feasibility, and environmental sustainability. title: A physics-based hybrid model for reliable gas turbine power prediction under extreme weather conditions
abstract: Accurate prediction of gas turbine maximum power output is critical for electricity market bidding and grid stability in renewable-integrated power systems. Physics-based models cannot adequately capture performance degradation caused by equipment aging, while data-driven models, particularly tree-based ensembles, exhibit poor extrapolation beyond training ranges, posing a critical limitation under increasingly extreme weather conditions. title: ASC-MAPPO: attention-based communication and safety-constrained multi-agent proximal policy optimization for cooperative path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance of connected autonomous vehicles
abstract: Fleets of connected autonomous vehicles have to solve two problems at once: they must agree on who goes first, and each of them must stay clear of traffic that nobody controls. This paper presents ASC-MAPPO, an attention- and safety-constrained variant of multi-agent proximal policy optimization designed for exactly that coupling. title: Digital twin-driven congestion-aware route planning for intelligent transportation systems
abstract: With the rapid advancement of autonomous driving and navigation technologies, an increasing number of vehicles rely on real-time routing services such as Google Maps and Waze. However, these services frequently fail to improve aggregate traffic conditions, as rerouting drivers based on existing congestion amplifies herding behavior and produces new secondary bottlenecks. abstract: L'incorporation de la technologie IoT dans les réseaux d'approvisionnement en eau offre la possibilité d'améliorer la surveillance, le contrôle et l'efficacité opérationnelle, représentant ainsi une révolution dans la gestion des infrastructures urbaines. title: Captioning daily activity images in early childhood education: benchmark and algorithm
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Early childhood education (ECE) produces large volumes of daily activity images that document classroom routines, play, peer interaction, and teacher-guided activities. Converting such multimedia records into educationally meaningful captions remains difficult because ECE scenes contain fine-grained activity areas, visually ambiguous teaching toys, and professional terminology that are underrepresented in generic captioning datasets. title: FARABI: fuzzy-assisted routing for adaptive blockage-resilient 6G IoV
abstract: High-frequency millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) communications are promising for 6G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) services but remain vulnerable to dynamic vehicular mobility, bursty heterogeneous traffic, and heavy-tailed physical blockage. Conventional routing approaches often rely on memoryless channel models, non-differentiable soft-computing heuristics, or centralized optimization that may not adequately capture blockage persistence and tail-latency risks. abstract: The object of this study is the concept of a “route”, which requires reconsideration. A conventional route is represented by a polyline consisting of waypoints and verified in ECDIS; this is sufficient for a navigator but not for an automatic control system that must execute the route. The article proposes a formalization of the digital route of a Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) as an extension of the standard IEC 61174 route format (RTZ) by adding turn arcs with wheel-over points, corridors and safety zones, a speed profile, and time stamps. title: Valorization of yak bone collagen byproducts: computational screening and experimental validation of anti-aging peptides targeting MMP-1
abstract: Abstract Valorization of yak collagen byproducts offers a sustainable route to food-derived bioactive peptides. To prioritize candidate peptides from yak collagen-derived sequences, we developed AgeAttnMLP, an ESM-2-based screening model that achieved an AUC of 0.891 under conventional five-fold cross-validation and 0.879 under an additional cluster-aware grouped evaluation. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Groundwater quality degradation in arid and semi-arid regions requires assessment approaches capable of identifying critical parameter exceedances while minimizing the masking effects commonly observed in aggregated water quality indices. Conventional entropy-weighted water quality indices (EWQI) may underestimate groundwater deterioration because they primarily rely on data variability and may not adequately represent persistent guideline exceedances. abstract: Background Automated dietary assessment increasingly struggles to evaluate industrial food processing levels, revealing a systemic gap between the visual presentation of meals and their underlying ultra-processed food composition. abstract: Abstract Absolute angular position measurement is critical for automated systems, yet conventional optical and magnetic encoders often suffer from complex alignment, vulnerability to dirty environments, or high cost. This paper proposes a proof-of-concept angular measurement scheme that converts rotational displacement into monotonic distance variations via a helical reference surface, measured by a single-point Time-of-Flight (ToF) distance sensor. title: Multiclass Classification and Spatial Clustering of Disaster Tweets for Humanitarian Awareness
abstract: Background: Social media is a critical channel of real-time information channel during natural disasters, but the informal and fragmented nature of tweets makes automatic classification difficult. Named entity recognition (NER) can capture contextual cues, such as affected locations. abstract: Camera‐based computer vision remains the dominant approach to facial expression recognition (FER), but its performance depends on controlled conditions, including stable lighting, unobstructed views, and fixed camera angles, while continuous recording raises privacy concerns. abstract: The customer experience of e-commerce logistics depends on the time limit for order fulfillment, and the late delivery risk should therefore be identified at the time of placing an order. abstract: Summary Seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI) are important tools for investigating subsurface structures and properties. Open-source seismic modeling and inversion tools enable researchers to test new methods, reproduce published results, and use waveform data to characterize the subsurface. abstract: Vegetation-growing concrete supports plant growth through interconnected pores, but root-secreted organic acids progressively degrade its cementitious matrix, threatening long-term durability. abstract: There are still a huge demand for safe and sustainable modes of transport which has led to the creation of autonomous self-balancing bicycles. abstract: The Red List Index (RLI) is a key indicator for global biodiversity targets, but its application to freshwater fishes has been limited by infrequent reassessment and sparse monitoring data. abstract: Abstract The selection of an effective hydrogen vehicle technology is a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) problem with conflicting evaluation criteria and uncertainty in experts’ judgments. abstract: ABSTRACT The Kingston Hydrological Basin (KHB) in Jamaica faces serious challenges in water security due to increased urbanisation, limited water resources and inadequate sewage treatment facilities. abstract: This study examines the real-world operational applications of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) technologies in smart ports and their implications for port management and digital transformation strategies. abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-Light Detection and Ranging (UAV-LiDAR) is preferred for large-scale forest inventories due to its consistent, repeatable monitoring. abstract: Pantai Papuma merupakan destinasi wisata pesisir unggulan di Kabupaten Jember, Jawa Timur, yang menghadapi tekanan lingkungan seiring meningkatnya jumlah kunjungan wisatawan. abstract: This article examines the effectiveness of maritime security regulations and policies implemented by the Indonesian Maritime Security Agency (Bakamla) in the West Zone in relation to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16, which promotes peace, justice, and strong institutions. As a strategic and vulnerable area to transboundary threats, the West Zone requires robust maritime surveillance to safeguard national sovereignty and stability. title: Kaiser window-based S-transform for vibration signal denoising in rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Vibration signal analysis is widely used for bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, but the presence of strong background noise often masks fault-related features, reducing diagnostic accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a noise removal method based on the Kaiser window S-transform (KST), in which the signal is windowed over time using a variable Kaiser window. abstract: Weather forecasting in complex terrain remains challenging due to mountainous topography, which generates high spatial variability, local atmospheric circulations, and rapidly evolving convective systems. This paper focuses on the optimization of the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) to enhance convection-permitting numerical weather prediction in complex terrain. abstract: Selecting a colour palette that suits its design context (application domain, audience, and accessibility profile) affects usability, engagement, and accessibility, yet remains a difficult computational problem. Vision–language models (VLMs) have improved performance on this task but share three limitations: deterministic outputs cannot represent the variance inherent in a design brief, single-scalar training fixes the harmony–accessibility trade-off at training time, and post-hoc context filtering leaves the generator itself context-blind. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates whether local institutional quality is associated with firm-level innovation from an economic geography perspective. Focusing on Italian manufacturing firms, we examine whether cross-province differences in institutional quality are related to firms’ patenting activity and whether this relationship varies by firm size. title: Fine-Grained Plant Species Classification Using Contextual Metadata
abstract: Fine-grained plant species classification is difficult because closely related species can exhibit highly similar morphological characteristics, limiting the effectiveness of image-only recognition. This study developed an Enhanced Multimodal Swin Transformer that combines visual features from PlantCLEF images with contextual metadata describing taxonomic hierarchy, geographical distribution, seasonal occurrence, and ecological characteristics. title: Genotype x environment interaction for stomata traits in a rice recombinant inbred population
abstract: Drought is a major abiotic constraint limiting global rice ( Oryza sativa L.) production. While stomatal traits are linked to drought adaptation, their environmental stability and breeding utility are poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding hydrocarbon charge in structurally complex rift basins requires constraining the temporal and spatial relationships among source‐rock maturation, hydrocarbon generation and expulsion, migration pathways, trap development, reservoir architecture and fault behaviour. abstract: Model comparisons in urban air-quality forecasting can be sensitive to choices in data preparation and evaluation. abstract: Tree height-diameter (H-D) models were originally developed to address the difficulty associated with measuring tree height in the field. abstract: Abstract The application of data analysis methodologies to the construction sector—specifically, to the design of concrete structures—can offer significant advantages in terms of structural performance, economic efficiency, and environmental impact. This study evaluates, through a series of fully executable case studies of reinforced concrete columns, the most efficient alternative from both an economic and environmental perspective. abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analysis (SIA) of eye lenses can provide a retrospective view of resource use over a fish's life. abstract: Abstract Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. abstract: Abstract Many sectors rely upon weather information, yet raw numerical weather prediction (NWP) output alone is rarely sufficient to support real‐world decisions. abstract: Accurate estimation of in situ stress from conventional well logs is challenging when stress measurements are available for only a few wells and blind wells differ in pressure regime, logged interval, or curve baseline. abstract: Turkish abstractive text summarization remains underexplored despite the language’s agglutinative morphology, which poses distinct challenges for subword tokenization. abstract: Detecting and tracking vehicles ahead during driving is a critical technology for ensuring driving safety and enhancing the driving experience. However, traditional detection and tracking models often suffer from high computational intensity and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles have become a dominant framework for evaluating corporate sustainability. However, despite the widespread adoption of ESG, issues such as greenwashing, inconsistent accountability, persistent social and environmental injustices, and low trust remain unresolved. abstract: Wheat is a vital staple crop worldwide. abstract: Introduction Phragmites australis (common reed) is a globally distributed and highly productive emergent macrophyte with important ecological functions in wetland ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. abstract: The southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), a critical component of the “Asian Water Tower”, hosts a large concentration of maritime temperate glaciers that are highly sensitive to climate change. However, persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and supraglacial debris complicate consistent long-term glacier mapping, while the use of static glacier boundaries may introduce temporal mismatches in altimetry-based glacier mass-change estimates. abstract: Abstract Discovering meaningful feature (molecule) combinations to define simple, accurate, and easily interpretable decision rules for disease classification and prediction can improve the study of disease diagnosis and prognosis. abstract: Cool, shallow lakes have historically been treated as simplified limnologic systems that readily mix vertically during open water. abstract: Abstract. Groundwater is one of the most important freshwater resources for ecosystems and mankind. abstract: Abstract Plant height is one of the key economic traits in spring oat ( Avena sativa L.) and a major determinant of lodging, and consequently, yield potential. Understanding the genetic basis of the variation in plant height can significantly benefit plant improvement efforts. Although plant height is straightforward to measure, it can be intense when conducted across numerous plots and environments. title: Liability for rogue behaviors of agentic AI
abstract: This article addresses liability for harm caused by rogue behaviors in agentic AI systems (AAI), such as specification gaming and deliberate deception. These harms stem from inherent AI vices - intrinsic, inevitable, and unpredictable rogue behaviors of AAI which cannot be fully eliminated with the current state of technological development. Current regulatory frameworks mainly focus on risk prevention but fail to address how liability should be allocated when harms do occur. title: Database-Pipeline Interactions Shape Taxonomic Inference in 16S rRNA Bacterial Community Profiling
abstract: Abstract High-throughput sequencing has transformed microbiome study by enabling cost-efficient, high-resolution profiling of microbial communities using 16S rRNA gene amplicons. Despite its widespread adoption, taxonomic inference remains highly dependent on the choice of reference database and bioinformatic pipeline. title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Assisted Secondary Amine‐Phosphonate Tandem Sites on Mesoporous Nano‐Silica for Uranyl Carbonate Capture From Alkaline Wastewater
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective capture of uranium from alkaline radioactive wastewater remains highly challenging because uranyl carbonate complexes, particularly [UO 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ] 4− , possess remarkable thermodynamic stability and electrostatic repulsion from negatively charged adsorbent surfaces. Herein, we report a secondary‐sphere activation strategy by constructing secondary amine‐phosphonate tandem sites within mesoporous nano‐silica channels (GP@SiO 2 ‐APTES) for efficient uranyl carbonate capture. title: A data-driven method coupling multiple physical constraints for correcting structural errors in groundwater contaminant transport models
abstract: Abstract. Model structural errors are pervasive in groundwater contaminant transport modeling under complex environmental conditions, hindering accurate prediction of contamination transport. Data-driven methods (DDMs) coupled with physical constraints provide an effective approach for correcting structural errors and improving prediction. title: Bendlet-Based Medical Image Fusion Using Modified Spatial Frequency and Contrast Visibility
abstract: Multimodal medical image fusion combines complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities into a single image to support clearer visualization and more informed clinical interpretation. Conventional fusion methods may introduce blurring, reduce contrast, or lose important edge and texture information, particularly when curved anatomical boundaries are not represented effectively. title: Effects of adding quercetin to soybean meal-based feed on the growth, antioxidant capacity, and gut and liver health of juvenile turbot
abstract: Introduction The antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties of quercetin and their regulatory mechanisms had been extensively studied in aquatic animals. However, limited information was available regarding the effects of quercetin in farmed fish fed diets with high soybean meal inclusion. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of adding quercetin to soybean meal-based feed on the growth, antioxidant capacity, and gut and liver health of juvenile turbot. abstract: Abstract Achieving an effective balance between global exploration and local exploitation remains a fundamental challenge in metaheuristic optimization, often leading to premature convergence or slow convergence on complex engineering problems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel hybrid optimization algorithm, termed Multiverse–Giza Pyramid Construction Optimization (MV-GPCO), which integrates the complementary search mechanisms of the Multiverse Optimization (MVO) and Giza Pyramid Construction (GPC) algorithms within a unified optimization framework. title: The microbial aerial thread: co-restoring source and sink across dryland-urban gradients
abstract: Dryland ecosystems serve as major sources of atmospheric bioaerosols through aeolian transport of dust-associated microorganisms. These microbial communities are dispersed across vast distances, connecting dryland soils and vegetation to distant recipient ecosystems, particularly urban areas. This review synthesizes current understanding of microbial ecology in arid soils, microbial dispersal through dust, and interactions with urban ecosystems. title: Selective multimodal representation and visitor appraisal in educational heritage: evidence from Chinese academies
abstract: Introduction Research on heritage experience has examined material settings, cultural meanings, and visitor appraisal through psychological measures and digital visitor records. Their relationships within the same multimodal records remain less clear. Methods This study examines these relationships in educational heritage using 2,855 Ctrip reviews, 4,531 valid sentences, and 6,975 visitor-uploaded images from four Chinese academies, including 829 reviews with matched text and images. title: Validation of a lateral flow assay for the qualitative detection of okadaic acid-group toxins in shellfish
abstract: BACKGROUND: Okadaic acid (OA)-group toxins, including OA, dinophysistoxin-1 (DTX1), DTX2, and their acyl esters, cause diarrhetic shellfish poisoning. Regulatory monitoring commonly relies on LC-MS/MS, which is accurate but resource-intensive, creating a need for validated rapid screening methods. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the Sensoreal DSP Alert™ lateral flow assay (LFA) for qualitative determination of OA-group toxins in bivalve mollusks through single-laboratory validation based on AOAC International and Interstate Shellfish Sanitation Conference guidance. title: Soil health and One Health implications in the anthropocene: a perspective on microbiome engineering
abstract: Abstract Background Climate change and Anthropocene pressures accelerate soil degradation, threatening agricultural productivity, ecosystems, and human health. Within the One Health framework, soils are critical living systems. However, while physical and chemical dimensions of soil health are well studied, the biological dimension—particularly microbiome functional diversity—remains heavily underutilized in climate-resilient agriculture. title: Whole genome sequencing and tuberculosis surveillance and control: a critical view from resources limited settings
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly presented as a transformative tool for tuberculosis (TB) surveillance, drug-resistance detection, and precision treatment (1,2). Its scientific value is not in dispute. As countries work toward the milestones of the WHO End TB Strategy (3), however, an important question for resource-limited settings is not whether genomic tools work, but where they should sit among competing priorities. abstract: In 2014, the report A World That Counts, commissioned by the United Nations Secretary-General, argued that better access to high-quality data would improve public decision-making to address major global challenges more effectively (Independent Expert Advisory Group on a Data Revolution for Sustainable Development [IEAG], 2014). title: A lightweight YOLO based framework for real-time seat belt detection in intelligent traffic surveillance
abstract: Abstract Road accidents remain a major cause of fatalities worldwide, and proper seat belt usage significantly reduces the risk of severe injuries and death. Ensuring compliance through automated traffic surveillance systems is therefore essential; however, reliable real-time detection remains challenging due to illumination variations, occlusions, windshield reflections, and low contrast between seat belts and vehicle interiors. title: Operating-Condition-Aware Fault Diagnosis of Variable-Speed Aviation Piston Pumps Using Interpretable Multi-Domain Features
abstract: In variable-speed aviation piston pumps, changes in rotational speed, flow demand, and load can shift fault-related spectral content and make fixed-frequency features sensitive to operating condition. This study evaluates an operating-condition-aware and physically interpretable diagnostic procedure using open experimental data from a nine-piston swashplate-type aviation piston pump.
