title: Quantifying Geodiversity in the State of Rio de Janeiro Using a Spatial Grid-Based Approach
abstract: Abstract This article presents a quantitative geodiversity assessment of Rio de Janeiro State using spatial analysis methods applying hexagonal grids and cartographic processing at multiple resolutions. Geodiversity is the variability, relationships, and assemblages of geological, geomorphological, pedological, and hydrological components and processes. title: Functional genomic analysis of Vreelandella zhaodongensis BS253: a new isolate from hypersaline lakes from Brazilian Pantanal
abstract: Abstract Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. In this study, we report the complete genome sequencing and functional characterization of isolate BS253, isolated in a hypersaline alkaline lake from Brazil’s Pantanal region. title: EDGRU: edge-guided dual graph reasoning U-Net with spatial graph attention for infrared small target detection
abstract: Abstract Detecting infrared small targets continues to be difficult because of indistinct object contours, intense background interference, and restricted multi-scale feature extraction. To tackle such problems, this work introduces EDGRU, an edge-oriented dual graph reasoning U-Net which simultaneously utilizes edge information and dual graph logic, and spatial graph attention for robust feature representation. title: Attribution and projection of 2020 summer-like hot-wet compound extremes in East Asia using large-ensemble regional climate simulations
abstract: A hot June followed by exceptionally wet July-August conditions in 2020 caused widespread disruption across East Asia; however, the anthropogenic contributions to such hot–wet compound extremes (HWCEs) and their future risk remain insufficiently understood. Using large-ensemble regional climate simulations from the Weather@Home framework, we quantify anthropogenic influences on the likelihood of 2020-like HWCEs across three subregional hotspots, the Korean Peninsula (KP), southern Japan (JS), and the southern Yangtze River Basin (YS), and assess changes in their future risk at global warming l

In this paper, we propose an iterative learning–based nonlinear sliding mode control (IL‐NSMC) scheme for a single‐link flexible manipulator (SLFM). title: Development of oleaster-enriched functional bread using mechanically aerated frozen dough: Nutritional enhancement, rheological properties, and process optimization
abstract: Background: Oleaster (Elaeagnus angustifolia L.) fruit is a promising plant ingredient for functional bakery products because its incorporation can enhance the nutritional profile of cereal-based foods. However, using oleaster fruit powder in mechanically aerated frozen dough is technologically challenging because the gas-cell structure forms before freezing and, in the absence of yeast fermentation, cannot be restored after thawing. title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. title: Site Selection Method for UAV Full-Domain Inspection Nests under Multi-factor Constraints: A Case Study of Guang'an City
abstract: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used for automated urban inspection, and the spatial layout of UAV nests directly affects inspection costs. To achieve efficient and stable city-scale UAV nest network construction, this study takes Guang'an City as an example. Based on multi-source data including terrain relief, temperature, and wind speed, a multi-factor environmental suitability evaluation system is established. title: Gobernanza humanista de la inteligencia artificial en la gestión universitaria
abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en las universidades plantea desafíos que van más allá de la adopción de nuevas herramientas y que involucran las capacidades de dirección, control y aprendizaje institucional. abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. title: Potential Carbon Loss from Soil Subsidence of Rewetted Tropical Agricultural Peatlands in West Kalimantan, Indonesia

abstract: Despite the rapid advances in anomaly detection, many existing methods assume that normal data are homogeneous and can be modeled by a single one‐class boundary. abstract: This systematic survey and position paper examines cross-modal retrieval as a pivotal paradigm in multilingual information access, particularly in the context of Indian regional languages characterized by rich linguistic diversity, complex orthographies, and extensive code-mixing. Despite significant progress in natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, the integration of translation, semantic optimization, and multimodal alignment for Indic languages remains underexplored. abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s ‘Dual Carbon’ goals and the strategic opportunity to develop new quality productive forces (NQPF), coordinated development between NQPF and the high-quality development of the construction industry (HQDCI) has emerged as an important pathway toward regional sustainability. abstract: Abstract Numerical analysis of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) combines aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, structural, mooring, and control models. abstract: Human threats to freshwater ecosystems overall compromise water security, and identifying these threats is essential to set up the required strategies in managing water resources. The article focuses on Spain as the region of study since this country maintains a long-lasting conflict between the use of water resources and the impacts on freshwater ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Mechanistic models, expressed as simulations that can be run and visualised, are a powerful way to understand biological and other systems. Building them, however, requires formulating mathematical or rule‐based descriptions and translating them into working code, skills that many ecologists and other disciplinary researchers do not have. title: Informing the public about earthquakes in Canada: exploring the application of a new geocommunication model
abstract: Canadian geoscience initiatives include the research of natural hazards, their potential impacts on people, infrastructure, and the environment, and how these impacts might be mitigated. Engagement activities and educational resources are often an important component of such endeavours. Earthquake-related programs, in particular, are the focus of the work presented here. abstract: Indonesia's pioneer ships burn subsidised fuel, yet their requests are often based on nominal daily figures from ship specifications rather than measured consumption. This study estimates the fuel demand and speed-related saving potential of KM. Bung Tomo, a 1,257 GT passenger ship serving pioneer route R-16 (836 nautical miles, 10-day round voyage) from Kalianget, Indonesia. abstract: Documents related to reservoir flood control scheduling are typically unstructured, posing significant challenges to effective management. abstract: This article presents a statistical forecasting framework for wind speed using two well-known classical forecasting models, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and the exponential smoothing state space (ETS) models with the naïve model as a benchmark for comparison. abstract: Rapid urbanization and inadequate municipal waste management in sub-Saharan Africa have exacerbated severe environmental and public health crises, prominently characterized by the operation of uncontrolled open dumpsites. In Ibadan, Nigeria, major disposal facilities such as La Awotan dumpsite rely heavily on open dumping and unmitigated burning. abstract: The early-stage deployment of green methanol-powered inland vessels faces a fundamental infrastructure dilemma: limited vessel cruising range increases the need for en-route bunkering, whereas spatially dispersed demand makes dense construction of fixed bunkering stations economically burdensome. title: From genome to phenotype: advances, challenges and One Health perspectives in the genomic prediction of antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has substantially improved the detection and surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) by enabling the rapid identification of acquired resistance genes, resistance-associated point mutations, and mobile genetic elements. abstract: Urban land increase is often conflated with spatial redistribution when entropy is interpreted as a direct measure of growth. abstract: Didimacar bajelaopsis sp. nov . is described from Kuwait in the northern Arabian Gulf using morphological and mitochondrial DNA barcode evidence. abstract: Abstract Identifying the coupling mechanisms that operate in the two directions, upward and downward, between Earth's lower atmosphere and geospace (ionosphere, magnetosphere, and beyond) is currently one of the greatest scientific challenges to be addressed by the atmosphere and space science communities. abstract: As AI systems and their underlying technologies continue to advance at extraordinary speed, eminent scientists are warning of risks, including extreme risks. While high-profile governmental and intergovernmental initiatives such as AI summits, OECD and UN initiatives have raised hopes, substantial gaps remain between the severity of potential harms and the capacity of these initiatives to address them. abstract: Abstract We examine stress and strength across the deep subduction plate boundary at ∼60 km depth offshore northeastern Japan, near the downdip seismic limit of the megathrust. abstract: ABSTRACT Identity‐based Recommendation (IDR) plays a crucial role in modern personalized recommendation systems by leveraging users' identity information and historical interactions to model long‐term user preferences. title: Professional practices, collective dynamics, and psychosocial aspects of sailors on a French warship
abstract: Background Warship crews live and work for extended periods in confined spaces, separated from their families and exposed to high operational demands. While psychosocial risks in naval and maritime work are increasingly documented, little is known about how sailors collectively organize, regulate, and adapt their daily activity aboard combat vessels. abstract: This study assesses land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and Trees Outside Forests (TOF) in Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh, within the semi-arid Bundelkhand landscape. abstract: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. abstract: Malaria is an infectious disease that continues to be a significant worldwide health issue, with Indonesia positioned second in Southeast Asia for the highest incidence rate in 2023. The evolution of resistance to antimalarial medications is a key concern in malaria control, highlighting the need for new treatment agents. abstract: A reliable assessment of large-amplitude roll phenomena such as parametric roll requires an accurate characterization of roll damping. Global inland freshwater aquaculture has rapidly expanded, intensifying greenhouse gas emissions and sustainability challenges. abstract: Metabolic health is basis for all health, influencing energy regulation to disease prevention to hormonal balance. abstract: Antarctic soil ecosystems harbor unique microbial communities that survive under prolonged low temperatures, high UV radiation, desiccation, oligotrophic conditions and other environmental stresses. abstract: The reliable determination of constitutive model parameters from in-situ cone penetration tests with pore pressure measurement (CPTu) remains a challenging inverse problem in geotechnical engineering, complicated by large deformations, complex stress changes, and the inherent non-uniqueness of the inverse mapping. abstract: The study examined quality of work-life as a predictor of lecturers’ job engagement in Colleges of Education in South East, Nigeria. abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. To explore this problem, this study proposes a hybrid framework including text mining, sentiment analysis, and opinion evolution modeling based on fuzzy theory. abstract: Abstract Infrared (IR) spectroscopy has lost relevance in modern natural product structural elucidation workflows but holds many advantages that can be leveraged with contemporary tools and technologies. With the aim of showing the applicability of the technique for dereplication and structural elucidation of natural products, we have assembled an IR spectral library of diverse natural product structures and chemotypes. abstract: Abstract Landslide susceptibility maps (LSMs) depict the spatial probability of landslide occurrence, typically using data-driven models based on past event distributions. However, these models often overlook temporal changes, assuming that past patterns reliably predict future events. In a rapidly changing world, influenced by factors such as climate change and urbanization, this assumption may lead to inconsistencies in LSMs over time, reducing their predictive accuracy. abstract: Understanding the variation characteristics of impact pressure induced by dam-break waves is essential for a deeper understanding of the impact pressure mechanisms on structures and for enhancing their impact resistance. abstract: The present review is a systematic literature review-cum-bibliometric analysis of quick commerce (Q-commerce), the retail model that promises to deliver everyday goods within minutes. abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, 3D printing technology has emerged as a promising approach for the fabrication of flexible sensors, owing to its advantages of low cost, high design flexibility, and simplified construction processes. abstract: The Russia–Ukraine conflict has disrupted global commodity markets, particularly crude oil, natural gas, wheat, and corn, leading to increased price volatility and affecting exchange rate dynamics. This study aims to analyze the Granger-causal relationship between global commodity prices and the USD/IDR exchange rate using the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). abstract: Biomachining is a non-traditional, innovative method of material removal where microorganisms and the culture medium in which they are produced are used to remove materials, especially metals. This process provides a sustainable approach when compared to physical and chemical machining by reducing the consumption of energy, as well as reducing toxic waste. abstract: Abstract Quantitative extraction of animal visual information often relies on annotated data collected for specific species and recording environments, limiting rapid transfer across biological systems. abstract: Abstract Urban wetland parks serve as vital infrastructure for climate resilience, yet a critical epistemological gap remains between their objective thermodynamic performance and the subjective thermal well-being of visitors. abstract: Cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis often has to adapt to a new operating condition with only a few labelled target samples. This setting creates two coupled problems. abstract: Soil contamination indices based on a single heavy metal (HM) fail to satisfy the interests of regulatory authorities, landowners and researchers who are more interested in a comprehensive index by aggregating such measures, facilitating evaluation of the effectiveness of remedial actions. abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) is a potent, short-lived greenhouse gas. Although methane remains in the atmosphere for approximately 12 years, its 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) is approximately 27–30 times greater than that of CO 2 (IPCC AR6), making rapid mitigation a critical near-term climate strategy. abstract: Accurate assessment of solar energy potential is a core input for renewable energy planning in high-altitude regions such as Eastern Anatolia, where ground measurement stations are sparse. Compared with traditional manual inspections, UAV remote sensing provides advantages of non-contact operation, wide coverage, rapid acquisition, and high spatial resolution. title: Development of Real Time Bus Tracking and Monitoring System Using GPS Visualization for UTHM Students
abstract: The rapid growth of university populations has increased the demand for efficient and reliable campus transportation services. Conventional campus bus systems generally operate using fixed schedules without providing passengers with real-time information regarding bus location, estimated arrival time, or passenger occupancy. This limitation often results in extended waiting times, ineffective travel planning, and inefficient transportation management. title: Interacting climatic, environmental, biologic and socio‐economic drivers of the global dengue expansion
abstract: Dengue is the most rapidly expanding mosquito-borne viral disease worldwide. The worst year on record was 2024, with over 100 countries reporting 14.4 million cases and over 11,000 deaths. Since then, and up to August 2026, another 7.4 million cases and over 5000 deaths have been reported. The region of the Americas was impacted the most, followed by South-East Asia and the Western Pacific. Both the spread of dengue viruses (DENV) and their primary vectors, Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, are driven by several factors. title: dSPACE-based Real-Time Position Control of an Elastic Cable Winch System using Fuzzy PD Controller
abstract: This study presents real-time vertical position tracking of an elastic cable winch system using a fuzzy logic-based PD (FLC-PD) controller. The dynamic model of the system was used with a two-degree-of-freedom reduced form derived from a four-degree-of-freedom structure in the previous work; drum angle and load position were taken as state variables. abstract: We discuss a novel approach to Premodern Japanese Language Pedagogy (PJLP) with potential applications in other languages and fields. Drawing inspiration from grassroots initiatives such as the DIY and Maker movements, this paper advocates for an approach to AI in Education that fosters instructional and student agency over the pedagogical process. abstract: Study region The Indus River Basin (IRB) is a major transboundary river basin in South Asia. title: Differential colorimetric pH measuring microfluidic manifold with embedded sensors and actuators for textile dyeing industry
abstract: Abstract This work presents a fully integrated microfluidic opto-electro-mechanical platform demonstrating a proof-of-concept for real-time colorimetric pH sensing in intensely colored textile solutions. The system features acrylic manifold with dual spectral sensors, an embedded magnetic mini-stirrer for rapid mixing, custom bidirectional syringe pumps, and automated fluid routing. abstract: ABSTRACT Metschnikowia bicuspidata , the causative agent of milky disease in the Chinese mitten crab ( Eriocheir sinensis ), is an important aquatic pathogenic yeast in freshwater aquaculture. However, the developmental characteristics and molecular regulation of its biofilm formation remain poorly understood. abstract: Background: Mine haul road conditions directly influence haul truck speed, cycle time, and operational productivity. At Sector 7 of PT Asmin Bara Bronang, overburden haulage had not met the production target, and several road segments did not satisfy the geometric design criteria specified in Ministerial Decree No. 1827 K/30/MEM/2018. title: Remote sensing and the EU nature restoration Regulation: monitoring biodiversity indicators for integrated forest management
abstract: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear. This review synthesises current evidence on the use of RS for monitoring forest biodiversity indicators defined in the NRR and identifies methodological gaps and operational priorities. abstract: ABSTRACT The growing participation of variable renewable sources in the Brazilian electricity system makes it necessary to understand how their different spatial and seasonal patterns can contribute to the stability of energy supply. In this context, the study evaluated the seasonal dynamics and spatiotemporal complementarity among hydropower, wind and solar resources in Northeast Brazil (NEB), between 1999 and 2022, with a focus on long‐term strategic planning. title: Physics‐Constrained Decomposition of Accumulated Fatigue‐Life Deviations After Static Residual‐Stress Correction in Welded Compact‐Tension Specimens
abstract: ABSTRACT Welding residual stress alters crack‐tip driving forces, complicating fatigue crack‐growth life assessment. Static corrections may leave systematic life deviations that are difficult to interpret. This study develops a physics‐constrained framework for diagnosing and decomposing these deviations in welded compact‐tension specimens. Two as‐welded specimens are assessed against a low‐residual‐stress reference from two post‐weld heat‐treated specimens. abstract: As climate change disrupts the pattern of rainfall and the onset of the seasons, local and traditional knowledge has drawn renewed attention as a resource for adaptation. This study compares the knowledge of rain, seasons and natural omens recorded in Sangam literature with the traditional understanding of climate in the agrarian communities of Erode District, Tamil Nadu. title: Natural Compounds in Cancer Chemoprevention: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Cancer remains a significant global health challenge, with increasing incidence rates despite advancements in treatment modalities. Chemoprevention, utilising natural or synthetic agents to hinder, delay, or reverse carcinogenesis, has emerged as a promising approach to reduce cancer risk alongside conventional therapies. abstract: Pitting corrosion is one of the most prevalent and detrimental forms of localized corrosion in stainless steels exposed to chloride-containing environments. Its initiation and propagation are governed by the combined effects of alloy composition, environmental conditions, and experimental parameters. abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid entropy-based model that combines the Theil and Hoover indices to quantify navigational disorder as a meso-scale indicator for comparative screening of navigational order and relative collision-risk exposure in maritime traffic systems. title: System dynamics evidence of sub-additive carbon reduction from combined mitigation strategies in multi-echelon logistics networks
abstract: The transition of multi-echelon logistics networks toward carbon neutrality is constrained by the inability of traditional static models to capture complex emission dynamics and time-delayed effects. To bridge this critical gap, this study develops a comprehensive system dynamics framework that captures non-linear feedback mechanisms, nonlinear interactions and temporal delays across transportation, inventory, and ware-housing operations. title: Modeling and Simulation of Reactive Power Compensation Using a Synchronous Motor with Excitation Control in MATLAB/Simulink
abstract: This study investigates reactive power compensation using a synchronous motor in a three-phase electrical power system without conventional capacitor banks through MATLAB/Simulink-based modeling and simulation. The proposed system consists of inductive loads and a 15 kVA synchronous motor operating as a dynamic reactive power compensator via excitation current control. title: Hybrid ARIMA–TCN–Self‐Attention Control With Superb Fairy‐Wren Optimization for Adaptive BLDC Motor Speed Regulation in Electric Vehicles
abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained significant attention in recent years and are rapidly emerging as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel‐based transportation due to their efficiency and environmental benefits. The primary objectives in EV development are to maximize energy utilization and extend driving range both of which depend heavily on enhancing motor performance. title: Spatiotemporal Characteristics and Driving Factors of Snow Drought on the Mongolian Plateau
abstract: Abstract Snow drought exerts widespread impacts on ecosystems and water resources. However, its spatiotemporal variability and key drivers in cold and arid regions remain poorly quantified. In this study, we used the ERA5-Land reanalysis to construct a snow water equivalent index to characterize snow drought. title: First report of Daptrius chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara) for the Greater Antilles
abstract: Abstract We report the first Greater Antillean record of Daptrius chimachima (Yellow-headed Caracara), a bird observed between 24 and 31 March 2023 at the Grand Hotel Excelsior Port Royal in Port Royal, Jamaica. Given that this observation was made nearly 800 km from the species’ core range, the observed bird may have arrived via ship assistance, or it may have island-hopped northward through the Lesser Antilles. title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. abstract: This Guest Editor’s Introduction of the Special Issue on Africana Digital Technologies introduces the urgency of expansion for this subfield of the discipline of Black Studies and some key interventions in the humanities and social sciences.

abstract: Introduction As AI evolves into agent-based forms, AI threat perception has become a defining workplace concern. Informed by Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Protection Motivation Theory, this cross-sectional study investigates how AI threat perception relates to post-adoptive AI agent engagement via dual paths of AI self-efficacy and defensive motivation. abstract: ABSTRACT Generative AI and large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, have transformed many working practices, including scientific writing. Previous large‐scale studies have identified shifts in the use of certain stylistic markers, such as the word delve , in disciplines like biomedicine, engineering and computer science, yet comparable evidence from the humanities remains scarce. abstract: The shift toward sustainable materials has fuelled the exploration of renewable carbon approaches to bioplastics, combining biomass valorization, the use of carbon dioxide (CO2), and polymer architecture. This review focuses on the valorization of second-, third-, and fourth-generation biomass, such as lignocellulosic residues, algal systems and industrial waste streams, in the context of integrated biorefinery systems. abstract: Abstract Gridded precipitation products are widely used to assess long-term rainfall and snowfall change, yet their trend reliability remains uncertain. The Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) was selected as a cross-sectional survey approach, data were collected from 184 respondents between March and May 2025 through both online and printed questionnaires. title: First record of Prostoma clepsinoides Dugès, 1828 (Nemertea, Eumonostilifera) from Hachijo-jima Island, Japan
abstract: Prostoma clepsinoides Dugès, 1828 is reported from Hachijo-jima Island, Tokyo, Japan, based on a mitochondrial COI barcode sequence from one freshwater specimen. The specimen was collected from a spring-fed stream and grouped with published sequences currently assigned to P. clepsinoides . To our knowledge, this is the first published record of Prostoma from Hachijo-jima Island. No morphological voucher specimen was retained because the entire specimen was used for DNA extraction.

title: Evaluating seasonal forecasts in Austria using agrometeorological indicators
abstract: Abstract Farmers rely on weather information to guide crop management; however, outcomes often remain uncertain until harvest. This pilot study evaluated downscaled medium- to seasonal-range forecasts for Austria (2018–2022), focusing on air temperature, precipitation, and six crop-independent agrometeorological indicators (stress and suitability metrics). title: Advances in Wound Healing and Skin Regeneration: From Biology to Molecular Mechanisms
abstract: Introduction: Wound healing is a highly ordered and regulated physiological process for restoring the integrity of the skin after injury. Chronic wounds, such as diabetic ulcers and burns, still represent a significant clinical problem because of compromised cell reactions and disordered molecular signalling. This review aims to familiarise the readers with aspects of skin biology, wound healing processes, and basic cellular and molecular regulators of tissue repair and regeneration. abstract: ABSTRACT Mercury (Hg) bioaccumulates in aquatic organisms and biomagnifies through food webs, potentially reaching concentrations that affect fish, wildlife and human health. Because Hg concentrations generally increase with trophic position, ontogenetic shifts towards piscivory can increase dietary Hg exposure as fish begin consuming prey with higher Hg concentrations than lower‐trophic invertebrates. abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate sensors based on solid‐contact ion‐selective electrodes (SC‐ISEs) are a promising technology for low‐cost, continuous ion sensing. However, implementing stable, printable solid‐state reference electrodes that match the scalability of SC‐ISE remains a key challenge. title: A Semantic and Lexical Analysis of LLM-Generated Responses in Comparison with Stack Overflow Answers
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become indispensable tools in programming education and professional software development. However, their output quality remains poorly characterized, particularly in terms of the semantic and linguistic quality of the explanatory text. Traditional evaluation metrics such as ROUGE primarily rely on lexical overlap and therefore only partially reflect the semantic adequacy of code explanations. abstract: Abstract Clean water is essential for life, ecosystems, and economic development. As water treatment technologies advance and sewage systems grow more complex, wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are essential for protecting public health and water resources. However, constructing these plants—particularly in developing countries—remains economically and technically challenging. abstract: Serang script, an Arabic-derived writing system used for Bugis and Makassar, reflects the historical interaction of Islam, local languages, and manuscript culture in South Sulawesi. title: Reconfiguración de la identidad docente en la era de la Inteligencia Artificial generativa
abstract: Este estudio analiza la forma en la que el profesorado percibe la integración de la inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) en el ámbito educativo y de qué manera esta tecnología influye en la reconfiguración de su identidad profesional. A partir de un cuestionario aplicado a 328 docentes de diferentes etapas educativas, se examinan sus percepciones, niveles de uso, competencias tecnológicas y principales desafíos asociados a la implementación de la IAG en el aula. abstract: The psychological fallout of natural disasters is rarely a direct function of the event's physical severity. Instead, it emerges from a complex interplay between hazard characteristics, localized spatial conditions, institutional efficacy, and the psychosocial resources accessible to affected populations. This paper seeks to construct an integrative conceptual model that elucidates how geographical determinants shape psychological vulnerability to natural disasters within the Libyan context. abstract: Introduction Cyber hygiene is often assumed to enhance individuals' ability to evaluate the veracity of online information, with potential implications for decision-making, social trust, and resilience to misinformation. title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of the Jeju Genome Project cohort in Korea
abstract: The Jeju Genome Project (JGP) is a genomic and phenotypic cohort established to provide a comprehensive resource for precision medicine on Jeju Island, South Korea. JGP integrates whole-genome sequencing (WGS), customized genotyping arrays, and detailed clinical and lifestyle phenotyping to characterize population-specific genetic architecture, disease determinants, and risk profiles among participants recruited on Jeju Island. title: Metabeams with intrinsic tension-rotation and tension-shear-rotation couplings for tailoring auxeticity
abstract: Abstract Negative Poisson's ratios commonly arise from internal rotational mechanisms. However, conventional honeycombs generally remain non-auxetic because their ligaments behave as classical beams with largely decoupled axial, shear, and rotational responses. Here, antichiral and chiral metabeams containing periodically embedded rotating bodies are introduced to encode element-level tension-rotation coupling (TRC) and tension-shear-rotation coupling (TSRC), respectively. Using these metabeams as structural building blocks, two complementary classes of mechanical metastructures are developed.

The seriousness of NOx emission can be realized by the fact that its prolonged exposure can cause lung cancer in human beings. abstract: Facility layout plays a critical role in determining production efficiency, productivity, and the smoothness of material flow in manufacturing systems. abstract: Drought is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon influenced by both precipitation variability and temperature-driven processes, particularly under evolving hydro-climatic conditions. A comprehensive assessment of long-term drought dynamics across Türkiye is presented using multi-timescale Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) based on data from 21 representative cities across seven geographical regions. title: Distinct climate responses to regional aerosol reductions: an overview of the regional aerosol model intercomparison project
abstract: Abstract Changes in emissions of anthropogenic aerosols and their precursors made strong contributions to trends in global and regional climate over the historical era. abstract: Big Data analysis has fundamentally reshaped American presidential campaigns. title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. abstract: Global biodiversity loss is accelerating, with approximately one million species facing extinction and ecosystem degradation that compromises the welfare of over three billion people. While there is growing awareness and global consensus on biodiversity protection, nation-state governance alone cannot be counted on to address transborder species protection. abstract: Satluj and Beas, Indus basin Himalayan glaciers fed rivers, have seen astronomic magnitude of human interference due to agricultural intensification, population pressure, urbanization and industries which subsequently deteriorates the water quality of the river systems. abstract: Abstract. Over the last ten years, open-access earth observation satellite data volumes have grown exponentially. Through use of this data, geohazard remote sensing scientists' abilities to impact policy and reduce societal vulnerability to geohazards has become increasingly tangible. However, much of this open-access data is acquired, stored, and disseminated by the Global North, whilst most disasters take place in the Global South. title: Autobiography of Carlos Vega
abstract: I do not believe my biography is particularly interesting, but I hope that it may at least be entertaining, and that anyone reading it may find in it at least one sentence that proves inspiring, especially those researchers who are just beginning their scientific careers. It is only fair to acknowledge that life is an adventure, and that we never quite know what lies ahead.

abstract: Accurate prediction of tensile strength retention (TSR) of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites exposed to elevated temperatures is essential for assessing their thermal reliability. However, existing ML approaches for TSR prediction have mainly focused on classical algorithms, while recent tabular foundation models and adaptive ensemble strategies remain unexplored. abstract: Este artículo presenta el diseño y la evaluación psicométrica inicial de la CREEAI-6, una escala breve de seis ítems para evaluar creencias sobre capacidades específicas de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en el contexto argentino. abstract: ABSTRACT Spices are widely consumed in Morocco and may constitute a significant dietary source of toxic metals such as lead (Pb). This study assessed Pb contamination and associated health risks in six commonly consumed spices (turmeric, black pepper, paprika, cumin, ginger, and cinnamon) collected from Moroccan markets ( n = 200). abstract: Bayesian inference and scientific computing often call for cataloguing all modes of a multimodal black-box objective, not just its global optimum. abstract: Indoor person-following robots routinely lose sight of their target at corners, doorways, and in crowds, and most local planners then stall at the last seen position. title: On the ethics of utilizing prediction markets for forecasting hydrological catastrophe
abstract: As peer-to-peer prediction markets increasingly allow real-money wagering on environmental events, public scientific agencies are being drawn into the role of financial “settlement oracles,” the designated sources of truth against which contracts resolve. abstract: Objectives: Digital technologies increasingly shape communication, organization, and decision-making in everyday life. abstract: This study is a quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-correlational research design that determined the level of visitor awareness and self-reported ecotourism practices at Bauang Bakawan Eco-Tourism Park, La Union. abstract: Selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitors (coxibs) offer reduced gastrointestinal toxicity compared to traditional non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), yet their safety remains controversial as evidenced by several market withdrawals due to severe cardiovascular and hepatic risks. title: Data visualisation as an ‘emotional repository’
abstract: Understanding the role of emotions in engagements with data visualisations (graphs, charts, maps) is important given their increasing circulation in everyday life and their influence on how people make sense of social and political issues. This paper builds on sociological perspectives on emotions and advances existing research on the interplay between data visualisation and emotions by proposing the concept of ‘emotional repository’ to describe data visualisations. title: Integrative Lipidomics Reveals Schizochytrium Oil-Induced Muscle Lipid Remodeling Associated with Meat Quality, Oxidative Stability, and Flavor in Hu Lambs
abstract: Intensive grain feeding in lamb meat production can promote excessive n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) deposition, which may compromise meat quality and flavor. This study investigated the response of Hu lamb meat to dietary docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-rich Schizochytrium oil (SO), with particular attention paid to meat quality, antioxidant status, muscle lipids, and flavor. SO supplementation significantly enhanced meat lightness, activities of antioxidant enzymes, expression of antioxidant genes, DHA content, and the n-3/n-6 PUFA ratio. title: Resilience of standalone microgrids: indicators, enhancement strategies, and challenges—an integrative review
abstract: Microgrids have emerged as a promising solution for improving energy access, enhancing local energy independence, and strengthening resilience against environmental, technical, and operational disturbances. Resilience refers to the ability of a system to withstand, adapt to, and recover from disruptive events while maintaining reliable operation. Unlike grid-connected systems, standalone or islanded microgrids must operate autonomously during disturbances, making resilience a critical design and operational consideration. title: Land cover change and dry-season thermal patterns across the urbanizing areas in southeastern Vietnam
abstract: Industrial urbanization is altering land cover and surface thermal conditions in southeastern Vietnam, but comparisons among secondary urban areas remain limited. This study compares impervious-surface expansion, vegetation indices, and February land surface temperature (LST) in selected urban areas of Binh Duong, Tay Ninh, and Binh Phuoc from 1999–2024. Eight Landsat scenes acquired in February between 1999 and 2024 were selected, comprising four Landsat 5 Thematic Mapper scenes and four Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager and Thermal Infrared Sensor scenes. abstract: This study empirically investigates how safety culture, customer relationship management (CRM), and quality management jointly drive organizational effectiveness within Thailand’s maritime transport sector. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) theoretical framework, the research examines these vital intangible capabilities as synergistic drivers of sustained competitive advantage. title: Study on Curing Kinetics of Low‐Viscosity Epoxy Grout Under Frontal Water Condition
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐viscosity epoxy grout (LER) is susceptible to interference from frontal water during application, but the quantitative relationship between LER curing and frontal‐water conditions remains unclear. This study introduces the frontal water‐to‐grout ratio ( x ) as a quantitative parameter and examines LER curing under different frontal water conditions. title: Short-term forecasting from GRACE data via dynamic mode decomposition with sequential update
abstract: Dynamical systems theory is often used for short-term forecasting of hydrologic processes, because it preserves physical interpretability while remaining computationally efficient. One of its tools, dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), provides a modal representation of high-dimensional systems capable of capturing dominant spatiotemporal dynamics in observed data. We investigate the ability of xDMD, a DMD variant that allows for inhomogeneous dynamics, to predict short-term anomalies in basin-averaged total water storage across 15 major river basins worldwide. title: Performance optimization of an IoT ‐enabled vibratory double‐slope solar still with carbon aerogel‐impregnated carbon fiber felt and phase change material
abstract: Abstract Freshwater scarcity and the low productivity of conventional solar stills create a need for improved desalination systems that enhance freshwater production while enabling continuous monitoring. To address this limitation, an IoT‐enabled vibratory double‐slope solar still integrating carbon aerogel‐impregnated carbon fiber felt (CA‐CFF), phase change material (PCM), and vibration‐assisted heat transfer was developed and experimentally investigated. title: Fire Regime in Wasur National Park, Indonesia: Climatic Influences and Indigenous Burning Practices
abstract: This study examines the fire regime and its driving factors in Wasur National Park, Indonesia. This study employs a MODIS hotspot time-series analysis to examine the relationship between hotspot detections and climatic variables, supported by in-depth interviews with key informants from Kanume, an indigenous people living in Wasur NP. The findings reveal that the monsoonal climate, with its distinct dry and wet seasons, is strongly associated with annual variations in hotspot detection. title: Modeling soil volumetric water content based on climatic factors in the Tripoli region (Libya) using multiple linear regression
abstract: Climate scientists have been interested in the causes of the significant rise in temperatures, resulting in cold and heat waves, and consequently, periods of drought and flooding in various parts of the world. Our current study highlights the impact of climatic factors on soil moisture in the city of Tripoli, Libya. While many climatic variables affect volumetric water content of the soil, statistical analysis revealed a high degree of correlation between these factors, exceeding VIF values. title: Bayesian Model Averaging for Identifying the Robust Determinants of Finland's Production‐Based Ecological Footprint
abstract: ABSTRACT This study employs Bayesian regression and Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) to analyze the determinants of the production‐based ecological footprint (EF) of Finland during 1990–2022. Using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo estimation and enumeration of the 256‐model space with the Bayesian Adaptive Sampling algorithm, the analysis accounts for parameter uncertainty and nonlinearity among the predictors (GDP and its square, renewable energy, foreign direct investment, urbanization, nuclear energy, and innovation), together with an FDI × urbanization interaction. title: Design and trial implementation of a continental-scale, kilometre-resolution hourly precipitation analysis for Australia using satellite, radar and gauges
abstract: Abstract. High-resolution precipitation information is essential for hydrometeorological applications such as extreme weather monitoring, flood forecasting, and disaster risk management. Despite substantial advances in satellite, radar, and gauge observations, producing kilometre-resolution sub-daily precipitation analyses over continental domains remains challenging due to heterogeneous data availability, scale mismatches, and computational constraints. title: Transforming the global food system for environmental sustainability and food security
abstract: The global food system simultaneously drives and is threatened by intersecting planetary crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and desertification, and pollution and waste. Food production and consumption generate approximately one-third of anthropogenic greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, account for 39% of global deforestation, and impose external costs estimated at US$15 to US$20 trillion annually. title: Accounting for otherness in social enterprise: The case of a taxation service
abstract: The study aimed to account for the influence of otherness on a social enterprise's provision of tax services to clients in the Northern Territory of Australia. It collected quantitative data from client interviews conducted before the social enterprise provided taxation services. The collected useable quantitative data from 265 clients comprised 11 variables, grouped according to Role Set Theory into legal, social, and economic status roles. title: Bridging smart specialization and climate adaptation: evidence from the partnerships for regional innovation process in Attica
abstract: Introduction European regions are under increasing pressure to align climate adaptation with innovation-led development. This paper examines how climate adaptation priorities can be translated into a place-based innovation agenda through the Partnerships for Regional Innovation (PRI) process in Attica, Greece. title: Valorization of Natural Textile Waste Through Composting: Current Trends in Biodegradation Techniques, Chemistry, and Quality Evaluation
abstract: Textile composting is receiving increased attention as a sustainable solution to deal with textile waste that is landfilled. In this comprehensive review, three major areas of textile composting are discussed: stages of composting, chemistry of biodegradation, and scientific approaches in evaluating the quality of compost. The review paper is based on a comprehensive analysis of the extant literature mainly published in the last decade. title: Extracting Agricultural Experts' Experiential Knowledge from Non-Standardized Text with Quantity and Operation Scope Constraints
abstract: Expert advice on crop management is often written informally, and in such text a number can easily be assigned the wrong role or attached to the wrong operation, material, or measurement basis. We propose QS-IE, a knowledge extraction method constrained by quantity and operation scope. Its unit of extraction is a complete quantitative fact. title: Beyond climate migration: the right to remain and the right to development as complementary frameworks for climate mobility governance in Africa
abstract: Introduction Legal and policy responses to climate mobility remain overwhelmingly oriented toward displacement, relocation and cross-border protection, overlooking the right of people to remain in their homes under conditions of dignity and security. In Africa, where climate mobility is substantially governance-determined, this migration-centered orientation leaves both displaced and immobile populations inadequately protected, and overlooks the potential of the right to development to govern the terms of relocation where movement proves unavoidable. title: Vector-borne disease, deep-time ecology, and one palaeopathology
abstract: Rather than ‘novel’ zoonoses, some of our most serious threats are ‘old foes’ in particular ecological and social settings. The recent outbreak of disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo is precisely an example of this – the ‘old foes’ of malnutrition and malaria reappearing in new ways. It is important to understand how infectious diseases appear and disappear over time. title: A preliminary assessment of the field diet and trophic position of the two-spotted cricket Gryllus bimaculatus using DNA metabarcoding and stable isotope analysis
abstract: Although Gryllus bimaculatus is widely used as a laboratory model organism, its ecology under natural conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we provide a preliminary assessment of the field diet and trophic ecology of wild G. bimaculatus using stable isotope analysis and gut-content DNA metabarcoding. Stable isotope analysis provided a preliminary estimate of the trophic position of G. bimaculatus , suggesting that it occupies an intermediate position between herbivores and carnivores. title: Manufacturing and Scale-up Roadmap for Metamaterials
abstract: Abstract Metamaterials provide exceptional properties arising from their well-defined engineered structures in which periodic features ranging from the nanoscale to the macroscale are manufactured to yield the desired characteristics. Recent advances in manufacturing techniques have dramatically expanded the design space and potential applications of metamaterials. abstract: Abstract The interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between the repair material and the existing concrete substrate is generally regarded as the weakest link in a structural repair system, where interfacial damage often initiates and adversely affects the overall performance of the structure. This study investigates the interfacial bonding performance of ordinary concrete (NC) substrates repaired with nano-SiO 2 (NS) modified ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC). title: Calibration guidelines and a runoff-isotope module for lake proxy system modeling (PRYSM v2.0)
abstract: Abstract. Lake sediments preserve information about past air temperature and precipitation, providing critical, real-world targets to validate climate models. However, these paleoclimate data encode information about multiple climate signals as well as lake dynamics, which makes comparison of paleoclimate data and model output challenging. Proxy system models (PSMs), or forward models that translate climate variables into proxy data, are tools for mechanistically interpreting paleoclimate data. title: Dynamic event-triggered fractional-order super-twisting control for practical fixed-time quadrotor tracking under DoS attacks
abstract: Denial-of-service (DoS) attacks interrupt controller-to-actuator communication in quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), preventing timely control updates and degrading trajectory-tracking accuracy. External disturbances and limited communication bandwidth further complicate precise tracking under such attacks. abstract: Este estudio integra modelación hidrodinámica bidimensional con análisis multivariante para interpretar las inundaciones pluviales urbanas en el Centro Histórico de Querétaro, México. A diferencia de los enfoques basados en índices compuestos, se busca identificar y jerarquizar las variables hidráulicas, hidrometeorológicas y morfométricas que explican la respuesta de la escorrentía superficial concentrada en elementos urbanos como vialidades y callejones. title: An agronomy-oriented framework for multiscale maize phenotyping from 3D point clouds
abstract: Accurate stem and leaf segmentation and phenotypic trait extraction from maize 3D point clouds are essential for understanding plant architectural responses to stress and their relationships with agronomic performance. This study established a full-season single‑plant maize 3D point cloud dataset under three planting densities (D1, 90000 plants ha⁻¹; D2, 110000 plants ha⁻¹; and D3, 130000 plants ha⁻¹) and three irrigation levels (I1, 100% ETc; I2, 65% ETc; and I3, 40% ETc). abstract: Nanomaterials have been present for centuries as colloidal materials in historical objects such as Lycurgus Cup, medieval church windows and weapons made of Damascus steel. However, it was until Turkevich designed a controlled synthesis method for metallic nanomaterials (MNMs), specifically gold nanoparticles. abstract: Abstract. Fast and accurate calculation of atmospheric transmittance is essential for infrared atmospheric remote sensing and satellite data assimilation. title: Environmental levels of PBDEs in Brazilian industrial cities: Sources, seasonal variability, and human exposure implications
abstract: Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) are prioritised chemicals regulated under the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants. PBDE data are, however, developing for outdoor air, soil, surface water and sediment in Brazil. This study therefore targeted eight commonly reported PBDE congeners in air (using passive air sampler-polyurethane foam) and soil in Sorocaba (a major industrial city) as well as adjacent cities (Votorantim and Itu) in Brazil. abstract: ABSTRACT This article introduces a strictly convergent—in the sense of Semi‐Global Uniform Ultimate Boundedness (SGUUB)—model‐free adaptive control (MFAC) strategy for unidentified discrete‐time nonlinear systems. abstract: The urgency of this study lies in integrating Papuan ethnoscience contexts with PISA 2025 scientific literacy competencies to promote culturally relevant science education in the Indonesia–Papua New Guinea border region. Scientific literacy achievement of Indonesian students remains low, and the gap widens in Papua’s RI–PNG border region where instruction is rarely anchored in students’ lived experience. abstract: In this study, wastewater tainted with dyes presents a significant environmental problem that calls for effective and reusable photocatalysts to remove pollutants under visible light. The purpose of this work is to create and describe a BiO₃–SnO₂ heterojunction nanocomposite for the photocatalytic degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) and Methyl Orange (MO). abstract: ABSTRACT Growing industrial demand for sustainable materials has drawn attention to naturally derived reinforcements for thermoplastic composites. Continuous basalt fiber (CBF), made from volcanic rock, is attracting interest in composite additive manufacturing because of its high strength, corrosion resistance, and high‐temperature performance, which suit it to aerospace, construction, defense, and automotive applications. title: Dual activities of lysis and capsule degradation enable the bacteriophage protein Lys33795 to effectively disrupt Streptococcus suis biofilms
abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is an encapsulated zoonotic pathogen that can form recalcitrant biofilms. Bacteriophage-derived endolysins and depolymerases represent promising antibiofilm agents, but currently, no report has described protein which displays both of lytic and capsule degradation activities simultaneously. Here, we mined the porcine gut virome and identified Lys33795, a dual-activity antibacterial protein that degrades both capsule and peptidoglycan of S. suis. title: Climatic extremes and their social implications in 17th century Transylvania: An historical climate reconstruction
abstract: The 17 th century was a period of significant climatic and social challenges in Europe, marked by the transition to the Maunder Minimum, as part of the Little Ice Age; marked by low solar activity, many negative thermal anomalies, long and harsh winters, rainy years, numerous extreme weather phenomena, famines, epidemics, etc. Taking these aspects into account, the present study aims to reconstruct, based on written historical sources, the climatic variability in the Principality of Transylvania during the 17 th century. title: Human health risk assessment and integrated contamination analysis of Cd, Cu and Cr in urban soils of Annaba City, Northeast Algeria
abstract: Urban soils represent significant sinks for heavy metals and may constitute potential risks to human health, particularly within rapidly urbanizing and industrialized settings. abstract: ABSTRACT As the thermal demands of automotive radiators and electronic cooling systems continue to grow, it is imperative to develop advanced heat transfer fluids that possess better thermophysical properties. The present work focuses on the hydrodynamic and thermal behavior of a tri‐hybrid nanofluid formulated with ethylene glycol as the base fluid over a Riga plate, which is modeled using the Sutterby non‐Newtonian fluid framework. title: Port efficiency beyond the terminal: weather exposure, cargo-origin concentration and logistics vulnerability
abstract: Ports connect maritime services with inland freight networks, so their efficiency may reflect not only terminal-side capacity and operations but also the external conditions under which cargo flows are generated and routed. This paper investigates the association of weather exposure and cargo-origin concentration with heterogeneity in port-efficiency outcomes. title: Predictors of Cardiovascular Events in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Two-year Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Aim: Patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (HD) for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) have a high risk of cardiovascular (CV) events. This study aimed to identify predictors of CV events in these patients, focusing on the prognostic significance of plasma docosapentaenoic acid (DPA). Patients and Methods: This prospective study enrolled 255 patients on maintenance HD between May 2019 and May 2020. title: SubSAM-detect: Segment anything model-driven intelligent Hazard annotation and multi-scale defect detection for substation satellite inspection imagery
abstract: Automated hazard detection in high-resolution satellite imagery of electrical substations presents significant challenges, including complex background clutter, high intra-class defect variability, and the prohibitive cost of pixel-level annotation. Existing methods are limited by their reliance on extensive manual labeling and their inability to generalize across diverse substation configurations and equipment types. title: Coping with Climate Change in Southeastern Europe: The Case-Studies of Greece and Bulgaria and Their Growing Cooperation with Israel
abstract: The article analyzes the main challenges posed by climate change in Greece and Bulgaria and examines the policies adopted by both countries to address its effects through climate adaptation measures. In this context, the article highlights the importance of technological innovation in climate adaptation policies and explores the emerging cooperation between Greece and Israel, as well as between Bulgaria and Israel, in the fields of environmental protection and climate adaptation.

abstract: Dynamic electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring has become an indispensable tool in clinical diagnosis and non-invasive monitoring. However, its front-end sensing component, ECG electrodes, still have issues such as long-term stability and dynamic artifacts, which limit its application in high-reliability scenarios. Therefore, developing highly biocompatible ECG electrodes, reducing or stabilizing contact impedance, and eliminating relative sliding during movement are of utmost importance. title: Expanding the geographic and host range of moss-nostocacean symbioses in central Europe
abstract: Since their re-discovery, Moss-cyanobacterial symbioses are of increasing interest, especially Nostoc-feather moss symbioses. Efforts to document Nostoc-feather moss symbioses have historically been centered in Scandinavia and the North American Boreal forest zone. title: Sub-chronic toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in Danio rerio: evidence from hematological, biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological biomarkers
abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) have emerged as widespread aquatic contaminants with the potential to induce multiple toxic effects in fish. This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics and sub-chronic toxicity of PS-MPs in Danio rerio over 20 days. SEM revealed irregular and aggregated PS-MPs with micrometre-scale dimensions (approximately 1–200 µm), while DLS showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 1,115.5 nm with a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.569. Acute toxicity analysis determined the LC 50 value of PS-MPs to be 89.1 μg/L, and morphogenetic abnormalities were also observed.

title: PRECOG-Edge: A predictive–cognitive system from reactive scheduling to adaptive coordination in edge environments
abstract: Efficient decentralized task scheduling remains a fundamental challenge in dynamic and heterogeneous edge computing environments, particularly for latency-sensitive and distributed applications. Existing approaches typically address reactive scheduling, resource prediction, or intelligent reasoning in isolation, limiting adaptability and robustness in real-world deployments. This paper presents PRECOG-Edge, a decentralized predictive–cognitive scheduling system that advances edge scheduling from reactive decision-making to predictive, cognitive, and autonomous multi-agent coordination. title: Sample preservation by freezing: impact on sulfite quantification in cooked shrimp
abstract: Sulfites are widely used in shrimp processing to prevent melanosis, yet the effect of freezing on sulfite stability during sample preservation for regulatory monitoring remains unexplored. This study assessed whether frozen storage at −18 °C significantly affects sulfite quantification in cooked shrimp, aiming to validate frozen samples as a reliable alternative to refrigerated samples in official control workflows. title: Technical Evaluation of the Smart Water Jug-Plastic Bottle Disposal System
abstract: This study evaluated the technical performance and behavioral impact of the Smart Water Jug–Plastic Bottle Disposal System (SWJ – PBDS) as a strategy at Ocampo National High School – Senior High School (ONHS-SHS). The research addressed the escalating issue of plastic waste, focusing on reducing plastic bottle consumption through innovative smart sensor technology. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining descriptive and quasi-experimental designs. The descriptive component details the system’s characteristics via surveys, gathering data on user experiences and operational aspects

abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging natural hazards, caused by prolonged shortages of precipitation and changes in temperature that reduce water availability. Reliable assessment of drought conditions across space is essential for sustainable water resource management and effective climate adaptation. abstract: Hydroxyapatite (HA) is a widely used biomaterial due to its excellent biocompatibility, bioactivity, and osteoconductivity. abstract: This study aims to design, fabricate, and validate an axial-mode helical antenna for enhancing 5G cellular signals at 2.3 GHz, specifically to address signal attenuation in suburban areas caused by base station distance, vegetation attenuation, and propagation obstacles. abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. abstract: The assessment of human thermal stress under changing climatic conditions has gained increasing attention in recent decades, particularly in densely populated regions. abstract: Literary interpretation changes as readers encounter new passages, answer interpretive questions, and revisit earlier material in light of later context. abstract: Soil biogeochemical cycles regulate nutrient availability, soil organic matter dynamics, greenhouse-gas exchange, and crop productivity, but their functioning is increasingly modified by climate change. abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics in effluents are difficult to remove, as conventional and even advanced treatment technologies often show limited efficiency. abstract: This research investigated the influence of data integration digitalization on the performance of Container Freight Stations (CFSs) in Kenya. The motivation for this study arises from the ongoing operational difficulties encountered by Kenyan CFSs, including congestion and elevated operational expenses, despite their essential function in alleviating port congestion. abstract: Past climate change has repeatedly reshaped Earth's biomes, yet how their expansion and contraction influence biodiversity patterns through time remains unclear. abstract: Ball-balancing on a robotic manipulator is a challenging control problem due to its nonlinear dynamics, underactuation, instability, and stringent safety requirements. abstract: Topological light fields, with their robust properties, offer transformative potential across photonics. title: Integrating passive acoustic monitoring and point counts to assess occupancy of secretive marsh birds in Tennessee
abstract: Abstract Monitoring of wildlife populations is fundamental for evidence‐based conservation yet remains particularly challenging for cryptic species. Secretive marsh birds (hereafter marsh birds) are notoriously difficult to monitor because of their shy, unobtrusive nature and dense vegetation preferences. Existing approaches, such as call‐broadcast point count surveys, can result in low detection probabilities and increased uncertainty in population assessments. title: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhanced expert system framework for supply chain risk management: a healthcare industry application
abstract: Traditional expert systems struggle to manage high-stakes healthcare supply chain risks, such as drug shortages and counterfeiting, since knowledge bases require manual updating. This paper proposes a framework combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), fuzzy inference, and Dempster-Shafer evidential reasoning to extract and structure risk knowledge from unstructured documents. abstract: Seed dispersal is a key life-history process shaping plant fitness, population dynamics, community assembly, and species distributions. Global environmental change can modify dispersal by altering environmental conditions, landscape connectivity, dispersal vectors, and the selective pressures acting on plant populations. abstract: ABSTRACT Logistics performance is critical to economic competitiveness and resilient supply networks, particularly in emerging economies facing technological, infrastructural, workforce, environmental, and institutional constraints. abstract: This article examines South Korea’s evolving grand strategy as a geopolitical swing state under intensifying US–China competition. abstract: Abstract The shallow water table (SWT) in urban areas of cities located in arid areas emerges as a challenge threatening the existing infrastructure. It is essential to explore practical solutions to mitigate SWT rise in unconfined aquifers, where waterlogging and drainage/dewatering dynamics have not yet been adequately studied. abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization in tropical cities is intensifying surface urban heat island (SUHI) effects, posing significant challenges for sustainable urban planning. abstract: Abstract During routine nest monitoring on Bonaire, we documented two unprecedented nestling mortalities of Amazona barbadensis (Yellow-shouldered Amazon) consistent with assumed predation by a terrestrial crab, Gecarcinus ruricola. The first incident involved a chick approximately two weeks old that exhibited conspicuous limb lesions and a ruptured crop. abstract: Wildlife crimes seriously threaten biodiversity and public health security. Identifying the species of wild animals and their products involved in such cases is the key to handling them. This study aimed to establish a wildlife DNA identification system based on a local alignment algorithm, thereby providing reliable technical support for public security organizations with high-precision and high-efficiency species identification techniques. abstract: The American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a widely distributed Neotropical species for which detailed osteological descriptions of the skull and mandible remain scarce. This study provides an integrative characterization of the cranial and mandibular complex using gross anatomy, descriptive cranial morphometry, radiography, and three-dimensional (3D) scanning. abstract: Rainfall-induced landslide clusters are widespread hazards in the hilly regions of southeastern China. In August 2018, an intense rainfall event triggered numerous landslides in Luhe County, Guangdong Province. Based on a detailed landslide inventory, this study analyses the geometric and kinematic characteristics of landslides and investigates their spatial patterns. abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) enables simultaneous acquisition of spectral and spatial information and has been widely adopted across science and engineering. abstract: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a discharge preparation service (DPS) for patients after heart valve replacement surgery. In Tunisia, population-level data on its prevalence and determinants remain limited. Our study aimed to estimate the prevalence of depression in the Tunisian population and identify associated socio-demographic and clinical factors. abstract: This study aims to compare the impacts of demand- and supply-side policies within the input-output (IO) model framework. abstract: Biological invasions are a major driver of biodiversity loss, and tracking non-native species introductions is essential for biodiversity monitoring and policy assessment. First records, defined as the earliest documented evidence of a species occurring in the wild outside its native range, provide a standardized metric to quantify introduction dynamics across regions and taxonomic groups. title: Online education and digital learning paradigms in India: An exhaustive review of the literature
abstract: The purpose of this study is to give an overview of the evolution of digital learning paradigms, its implementation in Indian institutions and the challenges and opportunities which it provides. The review also seeks to identify gaps in the current research that can be used to direct future empirical and theoretical research. abstract: Vegetable oils play a strategic role in global food systems. abstract: ABSTRACT Ensuring high‐precision trajectory tracking for wheeled mobile robots operating under complex constraints and uncertainties remains a critical challenge. abstract: Liberia has long depended on foreign assistance or aid to complement its domestic resources to deliver on its evolving complex development priorities and needs. The decline in foreign aid poses major challenges which can be surmounted through effective domestic resource mobilization strategy and fiscal probity. abstract: Conventional active vibration control methodologies predominantly focus on achieving performance improvement relative to open-loop systems, rather than exploring the inherent performance boundaries imposed by physical constraints, system structures, and actuation/sensing limitations. abstract: The field of forensic linguistics has become progressively relevant, especially in multilingual societies like in the Philippines. However, the literature remains insufficient and disintegrated. There is a need for a systematic synthesis of these existing studies in the Philippines and see what the current landscape of research looks like for future opportunities and directions. title: The redox code of Leishmania : An introduction and critical review of its metabolic strategies
abstract: Leishmania parasites use specialized survival mechanisms to endure and grow in unfavorable intracellular settings. A strong redox metabolism is essential for immune evasion and long-term intracellular survival. In contrast to higher eukaryotes, Leishmania uses a distinct thiol-based antioxidant system centered on trypanothione, which is not found in mammalian hosts. abstract: Financial settlement breaks remain a persistent operational risk. abstract: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ), a pathological hallmark implicated in disease onset and progression. abstract: To restore a stream to a more natural condition and still minimize flooding and erosion, the optimal longitudinal bed slope and meander sinuosity are needed. abstract: The integration of digital economy and agricultural industry (IDEAI) is a crucial pathway for promoting rural revitalization and building a strong agricultural sector. abstract: Melanoma cells respond to therapy not only through selection of pre-existing resistant clones, but also by rapidly engaging reversible adaptive programs that preserve viability under treatment. These programs connect signaling rewiring, metabolic plasticity, inflammatory responses, cell-state transitions and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. abstract: Rising demand for sustainable energy, together with growing concern over the environmental impact of fossil fuels, has focused attention on alternative biofuels. Waste cooking oil (WCO) is an attractive, low-cost feedstock for biodiesel that simultaneously addresses a waste-disposal problem and reduces reliance on virgin vegetable oils. abstract: Abstract Uncertainties of hydraulic parameters in representing land-surface characteristics of revegetating riparian zones remains a critical limitation in hydrodynamic flood modelling, particularly when riparian revegetation is implemented as a nature-based solution (NbS) for downstream flood mitigation. abstract: Abstract The Congolese Copperbelt is a major source of copper and cobalt for the global energy transition, but mineral processing creates substantial and poorly documented local air-pollution risks. This study presents a multi-pollutant, multi-directional, and seasonally resolved assessment of ambient air quality around one hydrometallurgical plant in Kakanda and one pyrometallurgical plant in Lubumbashi. abstract: Public services planned around averages can conceal structurally underserved residents in dispersed rural territories. This study develops a municipal digital twin simulator for testing drone-assisted emergency access in a Spanish municipality of nineteen settlements covering 406.71 km². abstract: Animal venoms constitute a rich source of bioactive peptides targeting membrane receptors, including G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ligand-gated ion channels. title: Equity dimensions of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards: Long-term spatial population projections for New York City consistent with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. abstract: Electrical distribution failures in industrial facilities threaten workers, equipment and continuity of production. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread pollutants in freshwater aquaculture systems, entering through the degradation of pond linings and nets, contaminated aquafeeds, agricultural runoff and atmospheric deposition.
