title: Movement characteristics of persistent extreme precipitation events over China during the warm season using high spatiotemporal resolution data
abstract: Abstract Moving persistent extreme precipitation events (PEPEs) can cause severe disasters along their tracks. However, a PEPE typically consists of multiple rain cells that evolve and move differently from one another, rendering the conventional single-center tracking method incapable of capturing their respective characteristics. Here we use a multi-rain cell tracking method to characterize the movement of PEPEs during the warm season (May to September) over China, utilizing high-resolution precipitation data at half‑hourly temporal and 0.1° spatial resolutions for the period 1998–2024. abstract: The unique microenvironment created by photovoltaic (PV) power stations may progressively reshape ecosystem species composition through sustained effects on aboveground vegetation and soil seed banks. We investigated aboveground vegetation and soil seed banks across three PV power stations with different operational durations (5, 10, and 15 years) in desert steppe ecosystems to assess how PV-induced microhabitats filter vegetation and seed bank assemblages. abstract: The spread of AI-generated deepfakes has produced a form of cybercrime that targets human biometric identity and injures victims' honor, property, and psychological security. abstract: This paper evaluates the deployment and potential nuclear fuel requirements of Small Modular Reactors (SMR) for supplying the electricity demand associated with data center expansion. abstract: This introduction explores the challenges of integrated sustainable waste management (ISWM) when managing ever-increasing volumes of garbage in fast growing cities. abstract: This paper proposes an Adaptive Security-Margin Tracing for Hosting Capacity (ASMT-HC) method for photovoltaic (PV) integration in radial distribution networks (DNs). abstract: BACKGROUND: The Neotropical armored catfish genus Harttia is an exceptional model for studying sex chromosome evolution, as it harbors the highest diversity of multiple sex chromosome systems known among fishes. abstract: ABSTRACT Urban parks in rapidly developing cities face increasing heavy metal contamination, yet seasonal dynamics remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation technology offers a groundbreaking approach to water treatment. However, the relentless pursuit of high energy efficiency has encountered a bottleneck in vapor generation, necessitating consideration of vapor diffusion. To tackle these limitations, this work establishes a comprehensive liquid‐liquid‐vapor transport kinetics framework, which couples water transport, vapor generation, vapor diffusion, and thermal management. title: Auditing platform metrics for communication research: a cross-platform case study of TikTok and Instagram engagement
abstract: Introduction Social media metrics are increasingly used in communication research to study public engagement, content visibility and platform dynamics. Cross-platform comparisons, however, can mislead when metrics are treated as equivalent without prior validation. This article examines this problem through a methodological case study of TikTok and Instagram engagement associated with UAE and Dubai tourism content. title: The 2009–2010 Ouazzane seismic sequence: evidence for a possible active horsetail-like termination of the Jebha Fault, Rif belt, Northern Morocco
abstract: The western-central Rif is characterized by diffuse seismicity, including a pronounced earthquake sequence occurring in 2009–2010 near Ouazzane, southwest of the Jebha Fault. The structural significance of this sequence and its relationship to the regional fault system remain poorly constrained. We analyzed the regional earthquake catalogue, performed double-difference hypocentral relocation and GardnerKnopoff declustering, and integrated regional focal mechanisms with mapped geological structures to investigate the spatial organization and seismotectonic significance of the Ouazzane sequence.

title: Transforming Contingency Plans into BPMN-Based Disaster Management Workflows: A Design Science Research Study in Agam Regency
abstract: This study addresses the operational bottlenecks in regional disaster management caused by static, narrative-based Contingency Plans. It aims to bridge the semantic gap between legal bureaucratic prose and machine-readable BPMN workflow specifications to facilitate modern e-Government integration in Agam Regency. We applied a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to systematically extract and transform passive policy texts into structured Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) workflows. title: Ecosistemas Pedagógicos influidos por la Inteligencia Artificial: Transformaciones, Desafíos y Oportunidades para la Educación Superior
abstract: La inteligencia artificial está cambiando la forma en que las instituciones, profesores y estudiantes, aprenden, comparan y comparten conocimiento de manera transformadora. abstract: ABSTRACT Heterointerface engineering with a built‐in electric field enables tailoring of surface electronic structures, bridging electronic modulation with reaction kinetics for efficient energy conversion. title: Translational plausibility of honey-derived antimicrobial biomaterials against biofilm-associated infections
abstract: Chronic biofilm-associated infections drive antimicrobial resistance (AMR) via prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy that is often ineffective. Honeys from Apis mellifera and stingless bees (Meliponini) exhibit antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity via complementary mechanisms: osmotic stress, low pH, hydrogen peroxide, methylglyoxal, bee defensin-1, and phenolic and organic compounds. title: Sex-associated differences in initial resection location, margin status, and re-excision in extremity leiomyosarcoma: a retrospective tertiary-center cohort study
abstract: Background Sex-associated differences in early surgical care may occur within individual sarcoma entities. We examined recorded tumor characteristics, initial resection location, margin status, and re-excision in extremity leiomyosarcoma. Methods This exploratory retrospective study included 79 patients with initial resection during 2000–2015 who ultimately received treatment at a tertiary sarcoma center. title: Isolation and characterization of novel Klebsiella phages from Benin and their antibiofilm activities on multidrug resistant and hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strains
abstract: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae represents a growing clinical threat, particularly where multidrug resistance limits treatment options. This study aims to characterize Klebsiella phages isolated in Benin and evaluate their efficacy in reducing bacterial cell growth, biofilm inhibition and biofilm disruption. To achieve this objective, we isolated Klebsiella phages by enriching samples of hospital effluent, pig droppings, and stool, using clinical multidrug resistant and hypervirulent K. pneumoniae strains as hosts. title: PRECISION BROODING OF BROILER CHICKS: A REVIEW OF THERMAL PHYSIOLOGY, SENSING, AND A FRAMEWORK FOR EMBEDDED CONTROL
abstract: In broiler pens, temperature, humidity and air quality are all controlled by a single factor: ventilation. Yet much of the control research has focused on temperature alone. This review treats the first four weeks of broiler production as an engineering problem. It translates experimental evidence on chick responses into measurable design specifications and derives the heat, moisture and gas balances that limit what a ventilation system can achieve. title: Research on Intelligent Agent Technology Empowering ICT Skilled Talent Cultivation for Smart Shipping
abstract: Addressing the urgent demand for high-skilled Information and Communications Technology (ICT) talent driven by the agile and digital-smart transformation of smart shipping, this paper explores the mechanisms, architecture, and paths of AI Agent technology and multi-agent matrices in empowering ICT skilled talent cultivation for smart shipping. abstract: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss is increasingly recognized as a grand challenge requiring new forms of innovation, coordination, and knowledge integration across organizational and institutional boundaries. abstract: Text-to-video retrieval answers user queries through searches based on concepts and embeddings. However, due to limitations in the size of the concept bank and the amount of training data, answering queries in the wild is not always effective because of the out-of-vocabulary problem. Furthermore, neither concept-based nor embedding-based search can perform reasoning to consolidate search results for complex queries that include logical and spatial constraints. title: Framing the unknowable: The role of language and frame multiplicity in early‐stage startup pitches
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Early‐stage startup pitches must make largely unknowable futures plausible. As such, they bear a rhetorical burden. This study theorizes how multiple frames jointly shape this burden and, consequently, affect investor evaluations. Specifically, it considers how future growth frames interact with concreteness and novelty frames. title: Change-aware contrastive learning framework for dynamic multi-objective optimization
abstract: Dynamic multi-objective optimization problems pose significant challenges due to frequent environmental changes, insufficient exploitation of historical knowledge, and limited generalization capability of predictive models. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Change-aware Dynamic Contrastive Learning framework (CDCL) for dynamic multi-objective optimization. abstract: Cet article analyse les représentations, les usages et les non-usages des intelligences artificielles génératives (IAG) chez des élèves du secondaire en France. abstract: Efficient extracellular secretion remains a major bottleneck in microbial cell factories, motivating the search for chassis organisms with native high-throughput transport capacity. Klebsiella quasipneumoniae (Kqp), a recently delineated member of the Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex, encodes diverse secretion-related systems, including RND-type efflux pumps, type II and type VI secretion systems (T2SS/T6SS), outer membrane vesicle (OMV) pathways, and capsular polysaccharide (CPS) export machinery. title: THE ROLE OF EDUCATION IN ENHANCING CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS AND DIGITAL SAFETY AMONG ADOLESCENT GIRLS AGED 13–19
abstract: Education plays a vital role in empowering adolescent girls to understand and respond effectively to cyber threats in an increasingly digital society. This study examines the implementation of cybersecurity education in schools, girls’ perceptions of online safety, and the role of educators in promoting cybersecurity awareness. The study adopts a descriptive research design in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh, using purposive sampling to select 90 female students and 90 teachers. title: Resource allocation efficiency and population alignment of community health centers: a home-based healthcare perspective
abstract: Background Faced with the dual pressures of a global aging population and strained health resources, community health service centers serve as a hub connecting hospitals with home-based healthcare. title: Creep behavior and particle breakage of carbonaceous mudstone coarse-grained soil: experimental study and discrete element modeling
abstract: Carbonaceous mudstone coarse-grained soil is commonly used as embankment fill in southwestern China. It exhibits significant creep characteristics, and its long-term deformation is closely related to particle breakage. In this paper, large-scale confined creep tests, sieving tests, and single-particle compression tests were carried out, combined with a discrete element model considering stress corrosion effects, to investigate the creep characteristics, particle strength evolution, and mesoscopic breakage mechanisms of carbonaceous mudstone subgrade fill under different gradations. abstract: Este artículo analiza, desde una perspectiva sociojurídica, la fe pública notarial en su tránsito hacia la digitalización en Ecuador, en un contexto de tensiones culturales, institucionales y tecnológicas que condicionan la implementación de los actos notariales digitales. title: Transcriptomic reprogramming and displacement of mastitis-associated Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by lactic acid bacteria
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is one of the main etiological agents of acute mastitis during lactation, and its ability to persist in biofilms can compromise conventional antimicrobial treatments. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) have emerged as promising probiotic candidates for mastitis management, but the molecular mechanisms underlying their interaction with S. aureus remain poorly understood. title: Numerical Investigation of the Effects of Equivalence Ratio and EGR on Combustion Characteristics in an n-Heptane Fueled HCCI Engine
abstract: Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition (HCCI) combustion offers low nitrogen oxides and soot emissions with high thermal efficiency, but direct control of combustion phasing is lacking. In this study, the effects of fuel-air equivalence ratio and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) on the combustion characteristics of an n-heptane fueled HCCI engine were investigated using a single-zone chemical kinetic model implemented in Chemkin. title: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. Inspired by nature's enzymatic proton transfer systems, we report a bioinspired terephthalate‐modified NiFe‐catalyst (NiFe‐TPA) for efficient BDOR in a flow‐cell electrolyzer. title: Development and validation of a cell death gene signature for overall survival in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
abstract: Kidney renal clear carcinoma (KIRC) is a common genitourinary malignancy with high morbidity and mortality rates despite multimodal therapies. Programmed cell death (PCD) is an active death process that occurs not only in the normal development of individuals but also in abnormal physiological states or diseases. title: Microbial processes for sustainable metal recovery and surface engineering
abstract: Microbial manufacturing is emerging as a complementary method to traditional metal processing using microorganisms and their metabolites as functional agents for selective dissolution, recovery, surface modification, and protective mineral formation. This review critically evaluates microbial manufacturing with a focused emphasis on sustainable metal recovery and surface modification and finishing, integrating mechanisms, quantitative performance, process intensification, scale-up, and techno-economic and life-cycle considerations. title: Exploring rainfall thresholds for shallow landslides using effective half-life precipitation indices and cluster analysis: a case study in Santos and Guarujá, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Santos and Guarujá have a long history of shallow landslides, with rupture surfaces generally reaching depths of up to 3 m. The slopes are underlain by gneissic and migmatitic bedrocks, where failures occur in immature residual soils, often at the soil–saprolite interface and exacerbated by anthropogenic interventions. title: Career Anxiety Among Students: Bibliometric Analysis of Scholarly Papers Published from 2016 to 2025
abstract: Career anxiety amongst students has emerged as a rather topical issue in the realm of psychology and education; however, at present, there is no comprehensive bibliometric analysis that would allow tracing the evolution of knowledge in this field. The purpose of this paper is to present the results of the bibliometric analysis of 525 peer-reviewed scientific papers on career anxiety amongst students, published freely in electronic form during 2016 – 2025. title: Vertical accuracy of ASTER, SRTM, and NASADEM digital surface models across Malawi’s diverse topography
abstract: Digital Surface Models (DSMs) are widely used as important sources of topographic information for earth science and environmental applications. The accuracy of DSMs has direct impacts on several environmental calculations and processes. Therefore, it is imperative to select the most suitable DSM based on the aim and accuracy requirements of each application. However, the use of an appropriate DSM has always been a challenge. title: A versatile on-axis visualization system for the macromolecular crystallography beamline BM07 at the ESRF
abstract: We describe the design of a new dual-magnification on-axis microscope adapted for actinic illumination on beamline BM07 at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). The instrument combines two cameras equipped with 50 mm and 150 mm focal-length imaging optics, providing low- and high-magnification views of the sample environment, respectively. abstract: Introduction Methotrexate (MTX) is a potent antineoplastic agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by nephrotoxicity, which may result in treatment interruption. abstract: This article presents and examines a writing process model developed to support students’ purposeful interaction with a chatbot acting as a group member in text production. title: Effects of waveguide tube geometry and surrounding medium conditions on acoustic emission signal attenuation
abstract: Deep-seated deformation in landslides is typically concealed and exhibits a time lag; reliably obtaining information on internal deformation through acoustic emission (AE) technology remains a key challenge in landslide early warning. Metal waveguides can reduce the impact of strong soil attenuation on AE signal acquisition; however, the mechanisms of propagation attenuation within the metal waveguides themselves remain unclear. abstract: La gamificación educativa y el aprendizaje distribuido contaban con fundamentos teóricos y evidencia independiente, pero su integración en plataformas adaptativas mediante acceso lúdico condicionado al desempeño académico permanecía insuficientemente articulada. title: The edible energy return on investment in dairy-bred beef finishing in Ireland
abstract: Food production—including beef production—in the industrialised world relies heavily on fossil fuels. title: Salinity Stress Elicits Genotype‐Dependent Responses of Turf and Forage Performance and Seasonal Dormancy Across Multiple Harvests in Orchardgrass ( Dactylis glomerata L.)
abstract: ABSTRACT Limited water availability coupled with increasing soil salinity poses a major challenge to sustainable turfgrass growth and performance. Dactylis glomerata L. (orchardgrass) is a widely distributed cool‐season perennial grass traditionally valued for forage production, with increasing interest in its potential as an alternative low‐input turf‐type species for water‐ and salt‐limited environments. abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. abstract: The nutcracker optimization algorithm (NOA) is a novel swarm intelligence algorithm, inspired by the different natural behaviors of nutcrackers during two periods. Compared with many classical algorithms, NOA performs competitively on various test suites and optimization problems. NOA still suffers from local-optimum entrapment, an imbalance between exploration and exploitation, and insufficient convergence accuracy. abstract: Critical and valuable elements are increasingly sought from dilute waste streams, but successful microalgal recovery depends on more than dissolved concentration. This narrative Mini Review examines how pH, redox conditions, ligand complexation, ionic competition, and phycosphere chemistry control elemental speciation and accessibility, and how these constraints interact with biosorption, membrane transport, intracellular homeostasis, sequestration, and stress responses. abstract: As ações do vento figuram entre as principais causas de danos estruturais em estufas agrícolas, tornando essencial a compreensão de seus efeitos sobre o comportamento estrutural e dos elementos de vedação dessas construções. abstract: Energetic materials store energy through chemical potential intrinsic to chemical bonds, making them unique energy carriers that are irreplaceable for aerospace exploration, advanced weapon systems, and resource exploitation and other fields. title: EDUCATIONAL ROBOTICS AND SMART LEARNING IN PRIMARY SCHOOLS OF KAZAKHSTAN: A SCIENTIFIC-METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR QUALITY EDUCATION, INNOVATION AND DIGITAL INCLUSION
abstract: Educational robotics has become one of the fastest-growing directions in smart learning. However, primary schools in emerging economies still lack a scientifically grounded methodological framework that links classroom practice to the national goals of quality education, innovation, and digital inclusion. This study examines how educational robotics can be taught to pupils in Grades 1–4 within a smart-learning environment in Kazakhstan, and whether the country's smart-learning infrastructure and public education investment are associated with long-run human capital outcomes. title: Türkiye in Africa: strategic realignment through soft power, security, and south–south partnerships
abstract: Objectives This study aims to analyze Türkiye’s strategic engagement in Africa, focusing on its evolving foreign policy approach through soft power, security cooperation, and South–South partnerships. It seeks to understand how Türkiye positions itself as an influential actor in Africa and the implications of this engagement for regional and global geopolitics. abstract: ABSTRACT The sharp decline in light yield ( LY ) of X‐ray scintillators under extreme high temperatures remains a key bottleneck for their application in high‐temperature radiation imaging. title: An advanced hybrid aquila optimizer with DE–QOB–elite strategies for precise PEMFC parameter extraction
abstract: The Aquila Optimizer (AO) is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm widely applied to solve complex nonlinear problems. title: Developing AI-Integrated Speaking Assessment via Yoodli for Vocational Tourism Students: A Borg and Gall Study
abstract: This study addressed the lack of contextualized, efficient, and objective speaking assessments oriented toward sustainable tourism. At SMK Negeri 1 Medan, speaking activities were not sufficiently oriented toward sustainable tourism, while conventional teacher-led assessment was constrained by limited time, potential scoring subjectivity, and delayed individualized feedback. title: Climate-sensitive patterns of premature cardiovascular mortality in a subtropical city
abstract: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. title: Beyond Star Trek: Latin American science fiction and the ELSI of emerging technologies
abstract: Science fiction has been recognized as a place of anticipatory governance, with audiovisual productions such as Star Trek serving as prominent references in ELSI’s research on genetics, biotechnology, and human enhancement. Latin American science fiction has developed parallel and largely unrecognized imaginaries involving genetics, computing, and biotechnology from structurally distinct social positions rooted in inequality, colonial erasure, and the historically expendable body. title: Microwall‐Integrated Terahertz Metasurfaces for Spatially Guided Label‐Free Sensing of Micrometer‐Scale Plastic Particles
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastic pollution is a critical environmental problem owing to its effects on ecosystems and human health. Therefore, technologies capable of accurately detecting micrometer‐scale polymer particles and converting their presence into measurable device‐level signals are indispensable for mitigating their impact. This study proposes a microwall‐integrated terahertz metasurface structure for spatially guided, label‐free sensing of micrometer‐scale plastic particles. title: CALIBRATING TURBIDITY AS A SUSPENDED-SEDIMENT SURROGATE IN A BACKWATER-AFFECTED TROPICAL DISTRIBUTARY
abstract: Turbidity is the most widely used surrogate for suspended-sediment concentration, yet its calibration is sensitive to particle size, sediment composition and hydraulic regime, and the assumption of a stable reach-wide relation is rarely tested in backwater-affected channels. This study evaluates the turbidity–suspended-solids relationship along a 5,000 m reach of the Erowha River, a distributary of the Forcados system in Delta State, Nigeria, during the wet season, when backwater from the receiving channel governs local hydraulics. title: Effects of Industrial Structure and Industrial Scale on SO2 Emission Intensity: Evidence from the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Industrial transformation and regional economic integration have reshaped the spatial distribution and cross-regional spillover patterns of industrial air pollution. Using a spatial panel model and data from 118 prefecture-level units in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YEB) during 2011–2020, this study examines the direct and spatial spillover effects of industrial structure adjustment and industrial scale expansion on industrial SO2 emission intensity. title: Unyielding Resilience of the Schengen Area: Adapting to Crises in a Transforming World
abstract: Abstract The Schengen area has recently experienced many crises. Despite occasional references to its potential end, it has proven its resilience. Whilst researchers explore Schengen's borders and databases, few studies have focused on the discourse on Schengen per se. This article fills this gap by examining discursive shifts in the perception of Schengen's resilience during recent crises, especially since 2015 (refugee crisis, COVID‐19, Russian invasion of Ukraine). title: Wet-year precipitation anomalies and geohazard economic losses in China: A province-year sensitivity and climate-exposure assessment
abstract: : Wet years can become economically costly when hydroclimatic anomalies coincide with geohazard-prone terrain and exposed socioeconomic systems. title: Natural forests are key for bryophyte conservation, while active land-use reveals homogenous communities with low richness, new records, and habitat indicators in the Eastern Amazon
abstract: Abstract The implementation of strategies that integrate land use with biodiversity conservation has never been more urgent in the Brazilian Amazon. Here, we compared the effects of land-use types characterized by family farming and low-intensity management systems on the community structure of bryophytes and their lineages (liverworts and mosses) in the Eastern Amazon. We evaluated bryophyte communities across natural forest and three active land-use types: managed forest, agroforestry, and açaí monoculture. title: Unpacking Age‐Structure Transition: A Geographical Perspective
abstract: Abstract This study analyses the age structure of the population and its recent evolution from a geographical perspective. This is achieved through an original method that enables highly sensitive identification of similarities among local age profiles. The results of the analysis reveal three distinct geographies of age structure in Türkiye: (1) child‐dominant profiles, (2) the transition belt where adults dominate and (3) areas where seniors are overrepresented. title: El Futuro de la Arquitectura Actual, en la Era de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA)
abstract: La Inteligencia Artificial (IA) generativa se ha convertido en una herramienta que ha revolucionado la industria creativa, incluida la arquitectura, al ofrecer nuevas posibilidades para la generación de arte, diseño y contenido con la menor intervención humana. En este contexto, el presente artículo analiza la integración de la IA generativa en la arquitectura actual con los retos que plantea en torno a la autoría, originalidad, valor artístico, propiedad intelectual y autenticidad. title: Catching needles in haystacks: a structured search framework to optimise counter-poaching patrols
abstract: Counter-poaching patrols are a primary tool for protecting wildlife in threatened landscapes, yet detection rates of active poaching incursions are typically low and patrol planning frameworks that have been operationalised and performance-assessed remain rare. We describe a structured search framework applied over a decade of counter-poaching operations in the Kenyir Core Area, Malaysia, 1,200 km² of mountainous tropical forest critical to Malayan tiger recovery. abstract: Introduction: The antibacterial activity of metal-based nanoparticles (MBNPs) varies considerably even among materials with the same elemental composition. abstract: Landslide-dammed lakes are produced by mass-movement processes and may remain apparently stable before rapid breach or collapse. This study examines the Matai’an Creek landslide-dammed lake in eastern Taiwan to diagnose why recognized hazard signals did not translate into timely structural action. title: Structural and Electrochemical Characterization of Na2CO3/ γ- Al2O3 Electrodes for Supercapacitor
abstract: The development of electrode materials with suitable structural and surface properties is crucial for improving electrochemical energy storage systems. Gamma alumina (𝛾-Al2O3) has attracted considerable interest in electrochemical research due to its unique structural and surface properties. However, its charge-storage capacity is still limited, highlighting the need for structural and compositional modifications to improve its electrochemical performance. title: Rationale and design of RECOVER – a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry
abstract: Background: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. title: Fibrocalcific phenotypes in calcific aortic valve disease: imaging characterization, treatment timing, and efficacy assessment
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease involves two structural processes, fibrous matrix remodeling and mineral deposition, that contribute unequally between patients, so leaflets of similar hemodynamic severity need not share the same tissue composition. title: Spatio-temporal analysis and forecasting of land use/land cover change in East Medinipur district, India using CA-Markov model
abstract: Land Use/Land Cover (LU/LC) serve as essential indicators of global environmental changes. This study examined the LU/LC change in the East Medinipur district of West Bengal, India, using remote sensing data and the CA-Markov modeling approach. Through GIS tools and satellite imagery, the study maps, monitors, and analyzes LU/LC changes over a 20-year period (2001–2021), utilizing data from Landsat 4–5 and Landsat 8. title: Anomalous durability of the cement at the combined effect of high initial curing temperatures and sulfate attack
abstract: An experimental program was conducted to evaluate the effect of initial curing temperature on cement grout under sulfate attack by wet-dry cycling. Cement grout with a water-to-cement ratio of 1.0 were initially cured at 20°C, 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C and then subjected to 30 wet–dry cycles in 5% Na 2 SO 4 solution. title: Exploring traditional rice germplasm in Sri Lanka: Morphological diversity, stress adaptation, nutritional value, and future breeding potential
abstract: Sri Lankan traditional rice varieties represent a valuable genetic resource characterized by substantial diversity in morphological, agronomic, adaptive, and nutritional traits. This study synthesizes the key variations observed among traditional germplasm with emphasis on vegetative growth, yield performance, stress tolerance, and nutritional quality to highlight their potential for sustainable rice improvement. title: A resilient-sustainable assessment framework for prioritization of generation expansion projects
abstract: Renewable-integrated generation expansion requires project prioritization that recognizes interdependent resilient-sustainable drivers under disruption. Existing approaches treat effective criteria as independent or retain fixed importance structures, limiting their ability to connect causal interdependence, disruption severity, vulnerability, and final project priority. abstract: Abstract Background Quorum sensing (QS) in bioluminescent bacteria underpins bacterial cell-to-cell communication, but the global evolution of this field has not been comprehensively evaluated scientometrically. This study maps QS research in bioluminescent bacteria to assess its developmental trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration networks, and emerging frontiers. title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a novel optimization methodology to determine optimal graphene platelet (GPL) distribution patterns and GPL volume fraction (GVF) in axially functionally graded GPL-reinforced (AFG-GPLs) composite curved beams. Existing studies are limited to predefined distribution patterns, restricting GPL-efficient structural design. title: Parameter Optimization of an LCC ‐S MCR ‐ WPT System Based on an Improved Multi‐Objective Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm
abstract: Magnetically Coupled Resonant Wireless Power Transfer (MCR‐WPT) shows great potential, but the coordinated optimization of efficiency and output power remains a critical issue in practical applications. To improve the overall transmission performance of MCR‐WPT systems, this paper proposes a parameter configuration method based on the Improved Multi‐Objective Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (IMOAHA). title: Assessing Land Use and Land Cover Change in the Jamanxim River Region (Brazilian Amazon) from 2015 to 2025 Using CBERS-4/PAN Imagery
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) changes in the Amazon are among the main drivers of biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and the intensification of climate change. This study aimed to analyze the multitemporal dynamics of LULC around the Jamanxim River, Pará, Brazilian Amazon, between 2015 and 2025, using high-resolution imagery from the CBERS-4/PAN satellite. title: Evaluation of satellite-based rainfall estimates and their performance across Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Precipitation plays a crucial role in Ethiopia’s rain-fed agriculture, ecosystems, and water resources; yet it exhibits, high spatial and temporal variability. However, the sparse gauge network makes accurate monitoring difficult. This paper evaluates widely used satellite precipitation products (SPPs), CHIRPS_v2, CHIRPS_v3, IMERG, GSMaP, PERSIANN, and AgERA5 (agrometeorological indicators derived from ERA5 reanalysis) against daily rain gauge observations from 95 Ethiopian stations between 2001 and 2024. title: Behind the organizational chart: The emergence of “gurus” in advice networks
abstract: Explaining the endogenous emergence of “gurus” – high-status professionals who are referred to for advice but are unlikely to seek it themselves – in organizations requires an integrated approach. This approach must consider the interplay of individual attributes (e.g., skills and status), structural factors (e.g., informal networks), and organizational contexts (e.g., knowledge-sharing infrastructure and internal competitiveness) from a dynamic perspective. abstract: Introduction Livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (LA-MRSA) of Sequence Type (ST) 398 is widespread in European pig farming, yet molecular evidence linking specific farm strains to finished pork products remains limited. title: Sustainable development of high-speed railway to green railway construction in China: practice, countermeasure and prospects
abstract: Purpose This study reviews green high-speed railway (HSR) development in China from a full-life-cycle perspective, focusing on key environmental practices, challenges and future priorities. Design/methodology/approach A structured review of peer-reviewed studies, policy documents, industry standards and railway-sector reports is conducted across six dimensions: land use and biodiversity, embodied carbon, operational energy and emissions, noise and vibration, water and soil environment, and solid-waste management. abstract: This study addresses countering unintentional IT insider activity, understood as actions by operators of automated systems that violate official job regulations as a result of behavioural deviation. This problem is reduced to an optimization problem, for which the authors have previously proposed an analytical model and a hybrid method for solving it. title: ‘I'm Not Smoking; I'm Just Vaping’: Deciphering the Reasons for and Against Vaping and Intention to Quit Among Young Consumers
abstract: Abstract Vaping has become a defining feature of youth culture and a fast‐expanding consumer practice, yet little is known about how young people rationalize their continued use despite awareness of health risks and social controversy. Drawing on behavioral reasoning theory (BRT) and insights from social identity theory (SIT), this study examines how young consumers construct, compare and prioritize reasons for and against vaping under conditions of uncertainty, thereby deciphering their intention to quit. title: Integration of Green Economy and Social Entrepreneurship for Sustainable Regional Development: Evidence from Community Empowerment Programs in North Sumatra
abstract: This study examines how the integration of green economy practices and social entrepreneurship shapes sustainable regional development through community empowerment programs in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Employing a mixed methods sequential explanatory design, the study combines quantitative survey analysis using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with qualitative in-depth interviews to explain how ecological efficiency and socially driven innovation jointly strengthen household economic capacity and regional resilience. title: Sustainable laser-assisted processes for semiconductor manufacturing: a comprehensive review
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is essential for modern electronics, yet conventional fabrication relies heavily on high energy consumption and chemically intensive processes. As sustainability becomes imperative, alternative technologies that lower energy use and carbon footprints are urgently needed. This paper reviews the role of sustainable laser-based processes as potential green solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. title: Changing waters: from waterscape to landscape and back again
abstract: Across Sweden, around 2,400 lake-lowering and drainage projects since the early nineteenth century converted wetlands and lakes into fields, fixing a particular vision of progress into ditches, land deeds, and sediment. This article reviews 82 archival, scientific, and policy sources to ask what was done, why, and when, and to trace how these interventions continue to shape contemporary restoration politics. title: Effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis in the Horqin Sandy land
abstract: Background Continuous cropping is a major constraint that limits the sustainable cultivation of medicinal plants. However, the effects of continuous cropping on yield, medicinal quality, and the rhizosphere soil microecological environment of Atractylodes chinensis , particularly in the Horqin Sandy Land, remain unclear. title: TCLNet: A Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection
abstract: Infrared object detection plays an important role in low-light and complex-environment perception. However, infrared images often exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio, weak target-background contrast, and limited texture information, which can degrade detection performance in small-target and cluttered-background scenarios while making it difficult to balance detection accuracy and model complexity. title: The effects of national security assessments in public procurement on competition, sustainability, innovation, and critical technology procurement
abstract: By strategically leveraging public procurement, governments can harness market competition to drive business innovation and sustainable development. It remains unclear, however, how this premise is affected by heightened security awareness due to increasing geopolitical tensions. Focusing on European Union (EU) member states, we examine how security-oriented practices in public procurement affect tender outcomes. abstract: Wound and device-associated infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilms limit host immunity and antibiotic efficacy, promoting chronicity and resistance. abstract: La expansión de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) favorece atribuciones cognitivas que requieren una clarificación ontológica. abstract: Abstract This paper examines how human nouns are distributed across gender values in Bantu languages. In Bantu studies, one gender value is widely described as the “human” gender, and it is generally expected that human nouns are predominantly assigned to it with some notable exceptions. abstract: Adverse conditions and work at height affect the safety and efficiency of radio frequency (RF) scanning at telecommunication towers. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa permite resolver muchas tareas escolares sin que el estudiante posea la habilidad evaluada, lo que compromete la validez de la evaluación. abstract: ABSTRACT The Moran effect traditionally refers to the synchronization of population dynamics driven by shared environmental forcing rather than direct interactions among populations. abstract: Abstract High Arctic tundra vegetation is highly fragmented, reflecting micro-topographical heterogeneity that governs local patterns of snow accumulation and soil moisture, and thus the distribution of plant communities. abstract: The early period of life is crucial for the development of species-specific traits and, as such, for a correct understanding of the evolutionary constraints and adults’ adaptations. abstract: Irreversible vision loss, affecting millions of people worldwide, most often ends in the death of retinal neurons that the human eye cannot replace. abstract: Climate risk assessments used by the financial sector are often based on empirical data from recent decades that do not span the full range of possible futures. We argue that the financial sector needs to embrace risk analysis for all plausible scenarios, not just for median outcomes.

abstract: Background Stagnant government health expenditure (GHE) and declining development assistance for health (DAH) threaten universal health coverage (UHC) for women in low-income countries (LICs) and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). abstract: The development of therapeutic resistance in solid tumors is not merely an incidental response, but a relentless recapitulation of Darwinian evolution under profound pharmacological pressure. Consequently, traditional reactive clinical paradigms are increasingly demonstrating insurmountable limitations. This review highlights the critical paradigm shift from late-stage containment towards "evolutionary interception", a proactive approach that predicts and pre-emptively blockades resistance trajectories during therapeutic windows of minimal clonal complexity. title: Inteligencia Artificial y Diseño Universal para el Aprendizaje para fortalecer la resolución de problemas y la participación inclusiva en la enseñanza de la Matemática en Educación Básica y Bachillerato
abstract: La integración de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación matemática abre nuevas perspectivas para la personalización del aprendizaje, el feedback y el acompañamiento en la resolución de problemas, pero su contribución a una educación verdaderamente inclusiva necesita una pedagogía que contemple esa diversidad del alumnado. Este trabajo tuvo como finalidad revisar y analizar, de forma sistemática, la evidencia científica sobre la IA y el Diseño Universal para el Aprendizaje (DUA) en la enseñanza de las Matemáticas en Educación Básica y Bachillerato, centrándose en la resolución de prob

title: Gravitational redshift as a template for correlated dephasing in quantum processors
abstract: Quantum processors encode computational information in relative phases and are therefore sensitive to spatially and temporally correlated dephasing. We formulate gravitational redshift as a physically constrained template for such noise. title: From cultivation to clinical translation: a critical review of ginger phytochemistry, antimicrobial mechanisms, bioavailability, and standardization
abstract: Ginger ( Zingiber officinale Roscoe ) is simultaneously a food, traditional medicine, and source of chemically diverse phenolic and volatile constituents. Its antimicrobial promise is supported by numerous in vitro studies, yet translation remains constrained by inconsistent botanical identification, extraction-dependent composition, non-comparable susceptibility assays, limited pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic integration, and a scarcity of controlled clinical evidence. abstract: Hava kargo operasyonları, yük çeşitliliği, hacim farklılığı ve uçak tipine göre sürekli değişen gereksinimler nedeniyle standardizasyonun sınırlı, hata toleransının düşük olduğu karmaşık faaliyetlerden oluşmaktadır. abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to explore how hybrid work models can be integrated into production management processes and how such integration can enhance organisational resilience in the context of emergency management. Additionally, the study seeks to address a gap in the literature at the intersection of hybrid work, business continuity and crisis preparedness. In this study, a hybrid methodology combining bibliometric analysis and theoretical literature review was applied. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effects of 5% n-butanol and green-synthesized MgO nanoparticles on the engine performance, combustion, emission, and tribological characteristics of dual-biodiesel-based fuel blends. MgO nanoparticles were synthesized using guava leaf extract and characterized by SEM, TEM, FTIR, and XRD, confirming a flake-like morphology with particle sizes below 50 nm. title: Impact of Project-Based Learning on Student Engagement in Science Classroom
abstract: This research explores how learning science through Project-Based Learning (PBL) can increase student engagement by influencing student interest and academic performance in the 7th-grade classroom. While elementary students often enjoy science because it is very hands-on, middle school introduces a more structured instruction, which can reduce student motivation and lead to a decrease in engagement. abstract: Spices have played an important role in culinary traditions, medical practices, and exchange networks for millennia, yet their identification in the archaeological record remains difficult owing to the limited modern comparative micro-morphological reference data. To address this issue, this study documents the micro-morphological characteristics of 14 spice species (including seeds, bark, rhizomes, and fruits) belonging to 7 plant families and 12 genera commonly used in Southeast Asia, including seeds, barks, rhizomes, and fruits. abstract: Introduction Global plastic production continues to increase, resulting in widespread environmental contamination with plastic waste that gradually breaks down into small particles. Micro- and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) have recently attracted considerable attention. abstract: This study evaluated whether data from the space‑borne Environmental Mapping and Analysis Programme Hyperspectral Imager (EnMAP HSI) can derive continuum-removed absorption features comparable to those from an Analytical Spectral Device (ASD) field spectroscopy for characterizing grass canopy nitrogen (N), acid detergent fibre (ADF), and acid detergent lignin (ADL) in senescent sour and sweet veld types. abstract: El pensamiento lógico-matemático es una competencia fundamental en la formación universitaria, particularmente en Administración; sin embargo, la modalidad abierta, con menor interacción presencial, plantea retos para su fortalecimiento, en un contexto donde el uso creciente de inteligencia artificial (IA) modifica cómo los estudiantes abordan estos contenidos. title: InSAR observations from multiple tracks reveal rainfall modulation of post-failure reactivation of the Xiongwadashan landslide
abstract: Large mountain landslides may remain active after major movement, yet the migration of dominant deformation zones, internal post-failure partitioning, and rainfall modulation remain insufficiently understood. We investigate the Xiongwadashan (XW) landslide on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau using Sentinel-1 LOS observations from selected pre- and post-event periods between 2017 and 2025, terrain-constrained three-dimensional displacement estimates for 2022–2024, CHIRPS rainfall data, and field observations. abstract: ABSTRAK Revitalisasi nilai-nilai Pancasila di tingkat desa menjadi tantangan penting seiring dengan menurunnya kohesi sosial dan partisipasi masyarakat akibat perubahan sosial. Di Desa Pesu, Kabupaten Magetan, perempuan memiliki potensi sebagai agen pembangunan melalui berbagai kegiatan kemasyarakatan, namun perannya belum dioptimalkan untuk mendukung implementasi nilai-nilai Pancasila maupun pencapaian Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). abstract: In online higher education, discontinuities in student performance and socialization function as early signs of academic delay or dropout. This article presents an institutional pilot that integrated generative AI (TECgpt/Skill Studio) as technopedagogical support for an academic status assessment tool (VEA), used to detect at-risk trajectories in an online degree program. abstract: Moist tropical forest extent monitoring and mapping are at the center of ecosystem preservation in the 21st century. Satellite remote sensing has proven to be essential for assessing forest loss in wide and remote areas at a continental scale. Nevertheless, yearly assessments using optical images tend to face challenges in African moist tropical forests, where the semi-persistent cloud coverage prevents short-term and small-scale events from being correctly detected. abstract: This article examines the paradigmatic features of toponyms used in fairy-tale texts and explores their role in the semantic and structural organization of fictional narratives. Toponyms in fairy tales are not merely geographical markers; they can also convey cultural, historical, symbolic, and emotional meanings. The study focuses on the relationships established among different types of place names within fairy-tale discourse and considers how these relationships contribute to the development of the fictional world. abstract: Abstract Most biosignature methods are biased by what we know about life on Earth. However, an agnostic approach would be more beneficial when looking for life on other planets. Molecular Assembly (MA) is an experimental agnostic biosignature method that could help to look for unknown life. To date, there has been no experimental test employing MA with an instrument type that is spaceflight ready. abstract: Background Anxiety related to medical and dental procedures is common in childhood. Brief, portable interventions that combine immersive virtual reality (VR), mindfulness, and nature exposure may help children practice self-regulation, but the feasibility, acceptability, and tolerability of Operation Calm require evaluation before clinical efficacy testing. abstract: In the digital era, the development of digital agriculture (DA) serves as an effective pathway to achieve high-quality agricultural development (HQAD). Although both DA and HQAD are current research hotspots, the interaction and coordination mechanisms between them still urgently require exploration. abstract: Background and Aim: Hedysarum gmelinii Ledeb. contains bioactive phenolic compounds, including prenylated chalcones, but its biological properties, particularly its ovicidal activity against veterinary parasites, remain insufficiently characterized. abstract: The search for renewable energy sources highlights the use of microalgae, unicellular and photosynthetic organisms. Microalgae are used in wastewater treatment due to their ability to remove compounds and nutrients. Research on skin and lung fibrosis has accumulated extensive experience in antifibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic approaches. abstract: ABSTRACT Electroreduction of nitrite provides a route to couple aqueous nitrite remediation with ammonia synthesis, but high selectivity requires coordinated nitrite deoxygenation and surface‐hydrogen delivery. abstract: Abstract The article examines major changes to EU legislation introduced under the Digital Omnibus VII focusing on the first three proposals advanced under the agenda: the Data Omnibus, AI Omnibus and the European Business Wallet. abstract: En el ámbito de la formación por competencias, la necesidad de evaluar el impacto de las innovaciones pedagógicas ha impulsado el uso de enfoques de inferencia y de descubrimiento causal, que permiten ir más allá de las relaciones descriptivas para identificar mecanismos subyacentes en los procesos de aprendizaje. abstract: This paper focuses on students’ potential vulnerability to trust in individuals who might act as facilitators of human trafficking or trafficking-adjacent fraud. abstract: La introducción de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación superior requiere habilidades digitales que relacionen conocer informático, criterio docente y ética. abstract: En un contexto donde la economía de la experiencia exige a los museos transitar de la provisión de servicios a la escenificación de eventos memorables, este estudio busca superar la dicotomía entre "museo físico" y "museo virtual". abstract: This research is driven by the widespread adoption of digital payment systems among university students, which potentially encourages spontaneous shopping behavior. abstract: Multi-omics approaches have revealed a cross-species functional emergence phenomenon leading to emergent suppression of Fusarium wilt. abstract: This study examines the opportunities and challenges facing Turkish hotel equipment exporters in the Saudi Arabian market through the lens of the cultural economy and Institutional Theory. abstract: Plant populations are embedded in complex social, cultural, and political contexts, yet plant conservation has traditionally been framed as a predominantly ecological and technical challenge. abstract: Abstract Soil microorganisms are key drivers of ecosystem functions supporting biodiversity, food production, and climate regulation. While most studies have primarily focused on low‐viscosity ethers or highly fluorinated solvents for LT performance, their practical applications remain limited by inadequate stability and environmental and safety concerns. In this work, a low‐cost, highly safe electrolyte for LT applications was designed based on sodium‐ion pouch cells. abstract: PM2.5-bound heavy metals are of concern because of their persistence, toxicity, and inhalation-related carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic effects. This study distinguishes three types of news values for science news on social media, including general, social media-specific, and research-specific news values. title: Wheat responses to salt stress through regulatory systems and trait-based adaptation
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic stress that limits wheat productivity and threatens global food security. This review provides a trait-oriented and integrative synthesis of wheat responses to salt stress by linking physiological mechanisms, phenotyping approaches, and genomic-assisted breeding strategies. abstract: Introduction Migrant populations are exposed to multiple psychosocial stressors throughout the migration process, increasing their risk for common mental health conditions. abstract: This study examines whether and through what channels China's cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) comprehensive pilot zones (CPZs) raise the quality, rather than merely the volume, of city-level exports. abstract: Abstract This article draws on the cross-disciplinary literature on risk, uncertainty and precaution to address a central dilemma put forward against precautionary principles. According to this dilemma, weak versions of precautionary principles, which hold that policymakers can justifiably adopt precautionary measures even when they lack certainty of impending harm, fail to justify adopting any precautionary measures. abstract: Virtual reality (VR) provides options to achieve higher levels of engagement, personalization, and service delivery in the industry of business events. However, to adopt it, it is necessary to meet the technology requirements, because its value for different stakeholders is perceived differently in the context of organizations and institutions. abstract: The Collared Forest Falcon ( Micrastur semitorquatus ) is a falconid species distributed across the Americas, including Ecuador. Despite its broad geographic range, information regarding its breeding ecology remains limited in many regions. Nesting of this species has been previously reported in caves, human settlements and various tree species. However, conventional (de)multiplexing schemes based on interferometry and Dove prisms are often quite bulky. abstract: Introduction Olive ( Olea europaea L.) cultivation is expanding beyond its traditional Mediterranean production regions; however, information on cultivar performance, phenotypic diversity, and molecular relationships under temperate Himalayan conditions remains limited. This study aimed to characterize olive germplasm using integrated morpho-pomological and simple sequence repeat (SSR) approaches. title: More than taste or nutrition: How perceived naturalness shapes acceptance of meat alternatives
abstract: Consumer adoption of plant-based meat alternatives can be an effective strategy to reduce some harmful repercussions associated with meat consumption. However, people still show reluctance to shift towards more sustainable protein options. In this study, we investigated consumer acceptance of three meat alternatives, namely plant-based chicken, tofu, and chickpeas, through the lens of three product characteristics: sensory similarity to meat (i.e. how much the stimuli was expected to be similar to meat in texture, taste, smell, and preparation), perceived nutritional equivalence to meat, and p

abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has arisen as a paramount worldwide public health challenge of the twenty-first century, with Klebsiella pneumoniae identified as a key priority pathogen by the World Health Organization. This opportunistic Gram-negative bacterium causes several healthcare-associated and community-acquired illnesses, such as pneumonia, urinary tract infections, bloodstream infections, liver abscesses, and sepsis. These affirmative-action students frequently face significant cultural and academic transition barriers when learning abstract scientific concepts through unfamiliar metropolitan (Jakarta-centric) analogies. abstract: Abstract Rain-on-snow (ROS) events have significant hydro-geomorphological consequences. While these events have been widely studied, their meteorological capacity to thermodynamically alter or melt snow when unconstrained by snow amount, hereafter referred to as snowmelt potential (SMP), remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to its long-term trends. abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are regarded as attractive candidates for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their further development remains constrained by sluggish ion/electron transport and limited structural stability of cathode materials. To overcome these limitations, we designed an acetate‐intercalated NiMn layered double hydroxide cathode (Ac‐NiMn‐LDH) using a template‐guided assembly route. abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon‐free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy‐intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. title: Eco-anxiety and perception of environmental threats: case study of Czech adolescents
abstract: Introduction Eco-anxiety is an increasingly important psychological response to the climate crisis, particularly among adolescents, whose developmental stage is characterised by identity formation, emotional change, and future-oriented thinking. This study explored how adolescents experience and interpret eco-anxiety. Methods This qualitative case study employed semi-structured interviews with five Czech adolescents aged 15–19 years who reported concerns about climate change. abstract: This paper proposes a Hierarchical System Theoretic Process Analysis (HSTPA), a hazard analysis method for a system consisting of many components with complex functions. HSTPA is an extension of the System Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), which is used in the early stages of system development to analyse hazard factors arising from interactions between components. abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic and electrocatalytic upgrading of lignocellulosic biomass into value‐added chemicals offers a sustainable route to carbon neutrality. 5‑hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key intermediate because its selective oxidation yields 2,5‑furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a renewable monomer for biodegradable polyesters. abstract: PURPOSE: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. abstract: Compound disruptions in high-end equipment manufacturing can simultaneously fragment operations and maintenance (O&M) resource networks and constrain critical resource flows. Using natural disasters and trade sanctions as representative compound risks of topology-based network fragmentation and capacity-constrained flow bottlenecks, this study addresses a recovery problem in which network reconfiguration changes the feasible space of downstream resource scheduling, while scheduling outcomes feed back through system-level evaluation to influence upstream reconfiguration. abstract: Abstract Digital agriculture is one of the levers that will enable food systems to adapt and remain resilient in the face of climate change. However, in addition to being generally slow to take off, its adoption is not geographically uniform. While studies at the producer level have investigated the rationale for this disparity, we argue that it could be that different countries and markets are prepared to absorb digital technologies into their value chains. title: La aplicación de los derechos digitales en Ecuador: privacidad y seguridad en entornos digitales
abstract: La digitalización de la vida cotidiana ha transformado la manera en que las personas se comunican, trabajan y acceden a servicios, generando nuevos riesgos para la privacidad. Es así que el estudio se planteó como objetivo central analizar la aplicación de los derechos digitales en Ecuador, con énfasis en la protección de la privacidad y la seguridad en entornos digitales. abstract: Access to finance is vital for improving food security, particularly in developing nations where agricultural production is crucial. Despite several financial interventions targeted at increasing agricultural production, smallholder farmers continue to lack access to reasonable, timely, and sufficient financing, limiting their ability to invest in improved technology and inputs, lowering productivity and food supply. abstract: Rapid growth in electricity demand is accelerating the construction of transmission infrastructure across mountainous areas. Improper disposal of drilling rock powder (DRP) generated during transmission-tower foundation construction can disturb fragile mountain ecosystems and increase handling costs. This study examines the reuse of sieved DRP as an equal-mass substitute for Portland cement in cementitious grout. Since 2021, business incubators have been formally integrated into Algerian higher education institutions, yet existing research remains largely confined to single-institution, descriptive assessments. abstract: Nerve injuries, including peripheral nerve injury (PNI) and central nervous system injury, remain challenging due to the limitations of conventional approaches in recreating the complex neural microenvironment and practical constraints such as donor-site morbidity and immune-related risks. abstract: Rapid urban development increasingly requires deep excavations near existing structures, where soft soils often induce significant wall and ground movements. This study presents the design and experimental evaluation of a 1 kVA voltage stabilizer based on a capacitor bridge cascade model (CBCM) for improved household voltage regulation. abstract: El diseño de evaluaciones constituye una tarea central en el ámbito educativo. abstract: Introduction: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a three-dimensional structural spinal deformity, with well-documented biomechanical consequences but comparatively underexplored psychosocial and functional dimensions. title: A chromosome-level reference genome of the largest cervid species - the European moose ( Alces alces ; Linnaeus, 1758)
abstract: We describe a chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly from a male European moose (Alces alces alces). The assembly comprises two pseudo-haplotypes of 3,148 Mb and 3,112 Mb, with sex chromosomes in haplotype one, and 33 autosomes in each haplotype (68 in total). Assembly completeness is high (BUSCO 98.3% and 95.7%), with 21,496 and 20,498 annotated protein-coding genes for haplotypes one and two, respectively. abstract: Tradisi penanaman kepala kerbau dalam berbagai ritus adat di Indonesia—seperti syukuran laut, pembangunan infrastruktur, dan bersih desa—sering menimbulkan ketegangan teologis ketika berhadapan dengan nilai-nilai monoteisme Islam. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui studi kepustakaan dan observasi budaya, penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana simbolisme animistik bertahan, dinegosiasikan, dan mengalami transformasi semantik

title: The importance of the regional context for the development of local smart tourism destinations
abstract: This study examines how regional characteristics inﬂuence the development of local Smart Tourism Destinations (STDs) in its territory, highlighting that, beyond city level initiatives, regional contexts play a key role by shaping the enabling conditions for smart transformation. Despite this relevance, the extent to which regional strategies aﬀect the development of local STDs remains largely unexplored in the existing literature, resulting in a gap that this research aims to address. abstract: Salinity stress represents a significant environmental challenge that affects plant growth, resulting in adverse impacts on crop productivity and overall yield. abstract: Abstract With the rapid urbanization in China, millions of people have moved from rural regions to cities as migrant workers, where many of them face various discrimination and ill treatment. Meanwhile, the increasing number of migrants in cities might render indigenous urban residents the future numerical minority. This study presents a multiple Martian-year climatology of atmospheric water ice clouds on Mars, from observations by the Planetary Fourier Spectrometer Short Wavelength Channel (PFS/SWC) onboard Mars Express. Participatory governance, multi-criteria decision analysis and climate-investment planning are rarely combined in a single, transparent workflow. abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of integrating sustainable environmental education through a digital waste incentive system on students ecological literacy, covering cognitive, affective, and behavioral dimensions. The study was designed as a quasi-experiment using a non-equivalent control group pretest-posttest design with a delayed posttest. title: Exclusive quark and gluon dijet production as probes of GPDs at collider energies
abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

abstract: ABSTRACT Crimped filaments are important for thermal insulation, flexible actuation, and smart textiles; whereas mechanically textured monocomponent fibers often exhibit limited structural stability and durability. abstract: This study evaluates the combined effects of projected climate and land-use/land-cover (LULC) change on streamflow and sediment yield in the Teji Catchment, Ethiopia. The analysis covered historical and future periods from the 1980s to the 2060s, with the 1980s, 2000s, and 2020s representing the historical period. The 2040s and 2060s represent projected scenarios. abstract: Medicinal plant infusions constitute an important source of dietary polyphenols; however, their biological activity depends not only on their phytochemical composition but also on the metabolic transformations that occur after gastrointestinal digestion. This study comparatively evaluated eight ethnofloristic medicinal plants traditionally consumed in the Huasteca Potosina (Mexico) through an integrated phytochemical, biological and computational pharmacokinetic approach to prioritize bioactive resources for functional food and nutraceutical applications. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the fatigue behavior of Flat–Joggle–Flat (FJF) adhesive joints with different bonding techniques. abstract: Plastic waste is a difficult environmental problem to address, and school cafeterias, which often use single-use plastics, contribute to this problem. However, many schools have not yet implemented sustainable practices, and students are often limited to theoretical learning that rarely links scientific concepts to real-world environmental issues. abstract: The Mahaweli River takes in the largest volume of water amounting to one seventh of Sri Lanka’s total runoff and has a catchment area that covers 15 % of the land in the country. A number of multipurpose reservoirs have been stored in the Upper Mahaweli River Catchment (UMRC) mainly to generate hydropower, which contributes to about 40-50% of the total hydropower production in the country. title: On the Maturation of Chinese Characters and the Mechanism behind the Contention of Hundred Schools of Thought
abstract: Academic circles hold diverse views on the causes of the “Contention of a Hundred Schools of Thought.” This paper proposes that the maturity, practical application and diffusion of Chinese characters during the Spring and Autumn Period substantially enhanced administrative governance and economic development, bringing the prefecture-county system to dominance. Populations whose intellectual horizons had long been confined to parochial local contexts, metaphorically “frogs at the bottom of a well,” achieved free circulation of information and talent across the Chinese-character cultural sphere.

abstract: Kim Stanley Robinson’s The Ministry for the Future (2020) explores how ecological repair might acquire economic value within institutions shaped by fossil capitalism. Drawing on ecological Marxism and critiques of neoliberal temporality, this article examines the interdependence of reproductive value and relational time in the novel. It argues that the carbon coin attempts to reorient valuation toward the maintenance and reproduction of socio-ecological life while remaining vulnerable to re-financialization and constrained by the limited mandates of central banks. title: Comparative analysis of central nervous system persistence of morbilliviruses across host species reveals shared features with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a rare but always fatal neurological complication of measles, associated with persistent measles virus (MeV) infection of the central nervous system (CNS). MeV is detected in the brains of deceased SSPE patients as hypermutated viral genomes, which often contain premature stop codons in the matrix (M) gene and encode a hyperfusogenic fusion (F) protein. title: Integrating GIS, multi-criteria decision analysis and google earth engine for national-scale groundwater potential assessment in Zimbabwe
abstract: Abstract Reliable groundwater assessment remains a major challenge in data-scarce regions underlain by crystalline basement aquifers, where limited hydrogeological information restricts sustainable water resource planning. This study developed and validated a national geospatial framework for groundwater potential assessment in Zimbabwe by integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), and Google Earth Engine (GEE). title: When foresight meets action research: A methodological approach to wicked problems
abstract: Responding to recent calls from action research (AR) scholars to move beyond business-centric and immediate concerns, this paper investigates how integrating foresight with AR can enhance engagement with wicked problems. These are complex societal and intertemporal challenges that require both short-term and long-term perspectives. Methodologically, we explore how foresight can facilitate more radical cognitive shifts from AR scholars and participants, enabling them to transcend present-oriented, organization-centered issues and engage more effectively with the complexities of wicked problems.

title: Can AI make reading more engaging? A motivational framework for AI-assisted reading assessment in EFL/ESL classrooms: a practitioner case study
abstract: Background Sustaining reading motivation in EFL and ESL settings remains a persistent pedagogical challenge. Textbook-based comprehension tasks—with predictable content, pre-printed answer keys, and limited interactivity—can produce passive compliance rather than engagement. The maturation of large-language-model (LLM) tools now makes it feasible for individual practitioners to generate demographically responsive, proficiency-calibrated reading materials at low time cost. title: Omega-3 fatty acids in aromatase inhibitor-associated dyslipidemia: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and future perspectives
abstract: Aromatase inhibitors (AIs), including anastrozole, letrozole, and exemestane, are widely used as adjuvant endocrine therapy for postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. However, prolonged estrogen deprivation induced by AI therapy may adversely affect lipid homeostasis and has been associated with alterations in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), potentially contributing to long-term cardiovascular risk. The mechanisms underlying these abnormalities appear to involve estrogen-dependent

title: Peran Mediasi Efisiensi Biaya dalam Hubungan Cost Reduction dan Financial Distress pada Perusahaan Sektor Kesehatan
abstract: Penelitian ini menguji peran efisiensi biaya sebagai variabel mediasi dalam hubungan antara cost reduction dan financial distress pada perusahaan sektor kesehatan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2021-2024. Sampel dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling terhadap 24 perusahaan, menghasilkan 96 observasi data panel; setelah koreksi autokorelasi Cochrane-Orcutt dan pembersihan data pencilan, diperoleh 68 observasi valid untuk diregresi. journal: Jurnal BANSI - Jurnal Bisnis Manajemen Akutansi

title: Shear Capacity Analysis of Reinforced Concrete Beams with Glass Fibers: Experimental Study and Validation of SAP2000
abstract: Reinforced concrete is the main material in construction in Indonesia, but it has weaknesses in tensile strength and susceptibility to shear failure. This study aims to evaluate the effect of the addition of glass fiber with doses of 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% on the compressive strength, shear capacity, and crack pattern of reinforced concrete blocks. The research method was carried out through laboratory tests on cylindrical and beam test objects, as well as numerical modeling using SAP2000 compared with the provisions of SNI 1726:2019 and SNI 2847:2019. title: Characterization and pollution assessment of surface water in the Ziz Basin, southeastern Morocco
abstract: Surface-water resources in arid and semi-arid regions are increasingly vulnerable to climatic variability and anthropogenic pressures, including urban expansion, wastewater discharge, agricultural activities, and inadequate waste management. In southeastern Morocco, the Ziz Basin is an important water-resource system, particularly because it is connected with the Hassan Addakhil Dam. Understanding the spatial distribution of water quality and identifying the main pollution sources are essential for protecting these resources and supporting sustainable water management.
