title: Beyond the specimen: rethinking ornithological collecting in a changing world
abstract: Natural history collections underpin a wide range of ornithological research, yet the context in which they operate is rapidly changing. Advances in genomics, digitization and analytical approaches are transforming what can be learned from specimens, while accelerating environmental change is increasing the need for temporally explicit, integrative data. These developments necessitate a reassessment of how and why birds are collected. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of eco-tourism competitiveness in countries along the belt and road
abstract: The ecological environment serves as a pivotal factor in ensuring the sustainable development of the tourism industry, which, in turn, acts as a crucial link in stimulating economic growth and fostering deeper understanding and trust among countries and regions along the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Consequently, an increasing number of nations are prioritizing eco-tourism development to bolster international tourism collaboration and partnerships. title: Active duty service members' experiences navigating musculoskeletal health throughout their military careers: a qualitative interview study
abstract: Introduction Musculoskeletal injury (MSK-I) and pain (MSK-P) pose a substantial burden to Active Duty Service Members (ADSM) and are a leading cause of medical encounters and lost duty days. Evidence indicates that barriers exist to musculoskeletal (MSK) health care-seeking, which can result in exacerbation of MSK conditions (e.g., MSK-I, MSK-P), chronic pain, and greater healthcare costs. title: An integrated experimental and numeric approach to investigate the structural dynamics of the Segesta Temple, Sicily
abstract: Abstract The Temple of Segesta, one of the oldest and best-preserved Doric temples in the Mediterranean, offers a unique case for studying the dynamic behavior of ancient masonry structures in a moderate seismic zone. This paper presents the stages leading to its dynamic characterization. title: Extracellular vesicles of pathogenic fungi: biogenesis, immune regulation and therapeutic potential
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) encapsulate a variety of biologically active molecules, such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, and have been recognized as crucial mediators of intercellular communication. The production of EVs has been observed across numerous fungal species. Upon infection by pathogenic microorganisms, EVs contribute to the regulation of various pathophysiological processes and are instrumental in the activation and modulation of host immune responses through the transport of molecules derived from either the pathogen or the host. title: Bacteria from extreme environments as candidate bioinoculants for drought tolerance in legumes: a critical appraisal of mechanisms and evidence
abstract: Drought is one of the major constraints limiting legume productivity, impairing plant growth, biological nitrogen fixation, and seed nutritional quality. The increasing frequency and intensity of water scarcity have intensified the search for sustainable strategies to improve crop resilience. Bacteria isolated from extreme environments have been proposed as candidate bioinoculants because adaptations to desiccation, salinity, or extreme temperatures may provide traits relevant to plant performance under water deficit. However, most of these isolates are extremotolerant rather than extremophili

title: Forest-residue-derived constituents for low-carbon cementitious materials: evidence boundaries, quantitative trade-offs, and cold-region service qualification
abstract: Forest-residue-derived constituents are increasingly being considered for low-carbon cementitious materials, but their functions differ substantially and should not be treated as a single waste-substitution category. Wood ash may serve as a screened supplementary cementitious material or mineral filler, wood-derived biochar mainly modifies hydration and pore-water behavior at low dosage, and wood fiber acts primarily as crack-control reinforcement. title: Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of the mechanisms of Citrobacter freundii–induced ‘‘water bubble disease’’ in Macrobrachium rosenbergii
abstract: The frequent outbreaks of “water bubble disease” in recent years have emerged as a major bottleneck hindering the healthy and sustainable development of the Macrobrachium rosenbergii farming industry. This study aimed to confirm the pathogenicity of Citrobacter freundii in M. rosenbergii through bacterial isolation, identification, challenge tests, and histopathological examination. title: Wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series: insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of a high earth-rockfill dam
abstract: Long-term deformation of high earth-rockfill dams reflects post-construction consolidation, creep, reservoir loading, and cyclic operation. Separating these superimposed components is essential for gaining process-level insights into spatial patterns and differential responses. This study investigates the Pubugou Dam, a 186 m high earth-rockfill dam in Southwest China, using ascending and descending Sentinel-1 observations from 2017–2023. title: Late Quaternary range dynamics of Pinus remota and Pinus cembroides (Pinaceae): contrasting climatic stability and habitat persistence
abstract: The fragmented distribution of many desert and montane species in North America has frequently been interpreted as a legacy of Late Quaternary climatic fluctuations. Among pinyon pines, Pinus remota exhibits a markedly discontinuous distribution in northeastern Mexico and southern Texas, raising the question of whether this pattern represents the remnant of a formerly broader range. abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) induces secondary brain injury characterized by neuroinflammation, blood–brain barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Quercetin (QR), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has shown neuroprotective potential; however, the molecular signatures associated with its effects in acute ICH remain incompletely defined. title: Flexible active-matrix dual-band electrochromic display based on a Gires-Tournois resonator for human and robotic vision
abstract: Reflective displays have attracted considerable attention owing to their ultralow-power operation and compatibility with flexible and wearable platforms 1 . Although dynamic optical modulation has been demonstrated in reflective displays, including electrophoretic displays (EPDs), their operation remains confined to the visible spectral range. title: Eco‐Design as a Strategic Lever for the Circular Economy: Insights From Industrial Case Studies
abstract: ABSTRACT The transition to a circular economy (CE) necessitates redesigning products and processes to minimise environmental impacts throughout their entire lifecycle. Eco‐design represents a key enabler of this transformation; yet, its concrete interplay with CE remains underexplored, especially empirically and across diverse organisational contexts. This study investigates how eco‐design practices contribute to CE actions through a qualitative multiple‐case study of nine manufacturing companies, selected to capture variation in sector, size, and sustainability orientation. title: Transcriptomic analysis of Listeria innocua response to a green food sanitizer: presumable viable but nonculturable state induction
abstract: Viable but nonculturable (VBNC) state physiologically enables numerous bacteria such as Listeria to survive adverse conditions while evading conventional microbiological detection. Molecular mechanisms underlying this phenomenon are still poorly understood. Using RNA-seq, this study investigated transcriptomic profiles of L. innocua in VBNC state induced by a green sanitizer formulation based on a natural polyphenol gallic acid amended with hydrogen peroxide and lactic acid. title: Amorphous Co 2 O 3 /Crystalline Cu Interface Enables Ultra‐Rapid Nitrite Conversion for Integrated Cascade Electroreduction of Nitrate to Ammonia
abstract: ABSTRACT Given serious nitrate (NO 3 − ) pollution and the energy‐intensive nature of traditional ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis, the electrocatalytic NO 3 − reduction reaction (NO 3 − RR) offers a green route for NH 3 production. Copper (Cu)‐based catalysts, although kinetically favorable for NO 3 − ‐to‐NO 2 − conversion, still suffer from sluggish *NO 2 reduction, resulting in poor NH 3 selectivity. title: Monitoring changes in the prevalence of the Beijing lineage of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Ecuador: 2018 and 2023
abstract: Background The Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing sublineage (Lineage 2) is a major global health concern due to its association with increased transmissibility, hypervirulence, and multidrug resistance (MDR). Although it is dominant in East Asia, its prevalence in South America is generally low, except in some locations in Peru and Colombia, where local prevalences reach up to 16.4 and 15.6%, respectively. title: Restricciones alimentarias, deficiencias nutricionales y manifestaciones gastrointestinales en pacientes con síndrome de ehlers-danlos hipermóvil: revisión sistemática y síntesis de la evidencia clínica
abstract: Introducción y objetivo. El síndrome de Ehlers-Danlos hipermóvil (hEDS) y los trastornos del espectro de hipermovilidad (HSD) se asocian con síntomas gastrointestinales que pueden modificar la ingesta alimentaria. title: New anatomical features of radiodont oral cones from the Fezouata Biota (Early Ordovician, Morocco)
abstract: Radiodont mouthparts (oral cones) are rare in the fossil record compared to the frontal appendages and cephalic carapaces of these iconic early Palaeozoic animals. Therefore, the study of oral cones has primarily been based on their associations with other body parts, from both taxonomic and ecological perspectives. In the Fezouata Biota (Early Ordovician, Morocco), the oral cones are extremely rare; only one fragmented piece has been figured to date, with four plates. title: Successful Experiences of Virtual Enterprises in Social E-Commerce: The Cases of Facebook–Instagram and Amazon
abstract: This study clarifies the fundamental distinctions between traditional e-commerce, social media marketing, and social e-commerce, establishing a conceptual framework that explains their convergence and divergence in theory and practice. It examines international experiences where social e-commerce has been successfully implemented, highlighting Facebook and Amazon as representative models of virtual enterprises operating in this domain. title: The Long‐Term Trend of the Equatorial Electrojet Over Indian Sector
abstract: Abstract The upper‐atmosphere cooling trend is well documented, while the long‐term trend of the ionospheric electrodynamics remains poorly understood. Using two geomagnetic observation data sets over Indian sector, we analyze the long‐term trend of the monthly‐median equatorial electrojet (EEJ) in 1967–2015 after removing the solar activity and seasonal signals. title: Influence of rock block shape and mass on runout and lateral spreading: evidence from controlled field tests
abstract: Rock block shape and mass influence rockfall mobility, but their combined effects on runout and lateral spreading are not well quantified. We conducted 144 controlled field tests using elongated, cubic, spherical, and flaky blocks in six mass groups (6.5–55 kg; n = 6 per shape–mass combination). Blocks were released from rest on a 30-m-high, 35° slope and traveled onto a 20-m-long horizontal platform. abstract: ABSTRACT Toddy , a naturally fermented traditional beverage, is increasingly recognized not only as a cultural staple but also as a reservoir of diverse bioactive metabolites. However, the molecular mechanisms by which these compounds interact with host proteins involved in inflammation remain unclear. Earlier studies largely focused on metabolite profiling or basic in vitro assays, leaving a gap in structure‐based validation, molecular dynamics analysis, and pharmacokinetic assessment. title: Case Report: Neonatal COL1A1-related osteogenesis imperfecta recognized after multiple fractures in an infant admitted for jaundice
abstract: Background Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare inherited skeletal fragility disorder characterized by impaired bone strength and increased susceptibility to fractures. Most genetically confirmed cases are associated with pathogenic variants affecting type I collagen, particularly COL1A1 and COL1A2. Severe neonatal OI may present with multiple fractures, skeletal deformities, and respiratory complications; however, early diagnosis remains challenging because classical clinical manifestations may be absent during the neonatal period. title: Fascioliasis in Kenya: a review
abstract: Fascioliasis is a disease of major public health, veterinary health and socio-economic importance in Kenya. The disease is classified as a Neglected Tropical Disease by the World Health Organisation with Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica being the leading causative agents of fascioliasis in the world. The primary definitive hosts of Fasciola parasites are domestic ruminants with humans being accidentally infected and mud snails of genera Radix spp. and Galba spp. serving as the intermediate hosts. title: First record of the subfamily Eucerotinae (Hymenoptera, Ichneumonidae) from the mainland Afrotropics, with a description of a new species
abstract: The ichneumonid subfamily Eucerotinae has been thought to be almost absent from the tropics, with the only known Afrotropical species found in Madagascar. We report the subfamily as present in the mainland Afrotropics and describe a new species, Euceros ibex Hopkins, Nascimento & Santos, sp. nov ., from Uganda and Cameroon. The subfamily was likely not observed in the mainland Afrotropics before because of low abundances and insufficient sampling. title: Biostimulant-associated shifts in soil biochemical functioning and microbial community structure under field conditions: an exploratory field-scale assessment
abstract: The increasing adoption of agricultural biostimulants necessitates a clearer understanding of their ec ological impacts beyond plant performance, particularly regarding soil biochemical functioning and microbial community dynamics under field conditions. This study presents a field-scale exploratory assessment of a commercially available biostimulant applied within a maize ( Zea mays L.) production system in the Mopani region of Limpopo, South Africa. title: Design of the Pesut Mahakam Mascot as a Conservation Education Media in the Central Mahakam Area
abstract: The Mahakam Irrawaddy dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris), locally known as the pesut Mahakam, is a threatened aquatic mammal inhabiting the Mahakam River ecosystem in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. Its survival is increasingly threatened by habitat degradation and various human activities, while public awareness of its conservation needs remains limited despite ongoing protection efforts. This study aimed to design a pesut Mahakam mascot as a visual communication medium to support conservation education and public engagement in the Central Mahakam region. title: Literacidad digital y nociones de derechos de autor ante la IA generativa
abstract: El presente artículo analiza la relación entre el nivel de literacidad digital y la percepción jurídica de derechos de autor en estudiantes universitarios de nuevo ingreso ante el uso de IA generativa. Bajo un enfoque mixto de alcance descriptivo-correlacional, se aplicó un cuestionario a 88 alumnos y entrevistas semiestructuradas a expertos en derecho, creatividad y comunicación audiovisual. Germ-free (GF) fish models are powerful tools to reveal the functions of intestinal microbiota and special strains. title: Preparation and application of functional hydroxyethyl cellulose hydrogels containing β-cyclodextrin complexes for cosmetic materials
abstract: To address the formulation challenges associated with cosmetic active ingredients, including degradation, oxidation, and potential skin irritation, functional supramolecular inclusion complexes were prepared by a coprecipitation method using arbutin, niacinamide, and benzoic acid as guest molecules and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) as the host. title: Photonic crystal nanocavity refractive-index biosensor for multiple biological samples: A numerical study
abstract: Abstract This numerical study presents a two-dimensional photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity biosensor based on a silicon slab for the refractive-index (RI) sensing of multiple biological samples, namely blood samples associated with tuberculosis, malaria, and dengue, and hemoglobin concentrations relevant to anemia assessment. title: ADAPTACIÓN SOCIAL DEL ESTUDIANTE DE NUEVO INGRESO A UN NIVEL UNIVERSITARIO: EVENTO CULTURAL
abstract: La adaptación social de los estudiantes de nuevo ingreso a un nivel universitario es un momento crucial en el avance académico y personal. Este proceso de adaptarse a nuevas dinámicas académicas, sociales y emocionales influye significativamente en el rendimiento académico y bienestar general. Es por eso que resulta importante comprender a los estudiantes que navegan por estos cambios y es fundamental para que puedan desarrollar estrategias que ayuden a su integración y éxito en el entorno universitario. title: Gestión estratégica de la transformación digital y competitividad internacional de empresas exportadoras
abstract: La transformación digital es constituida como una capacidad estratégica para fortalecer la competitividad empresarial en los mercados internacionales. La finalidad fue que se determine la relación en cuanto a gestión estratégica de la transformación digital y la competitividad internacional de las empresas exportadoras de Arequipa afiliadas a la Cámara de Comercio e Industria de Arequipa. title: Two new species of Poeciloneta Kulczyński, 1894 (Araneae, Linyphiidae) from Xizang, China
abstract: Two new species of the genus Poeciloneta Kulczyński, 1894 are described from Xizang Autonomous Region: P. duinanensis sp. nov . (♂♀) and P. jidingensis sp. nov . (♂♀). Detailed descriptions, along with photographs of genital characters and somatic features, and a distribution map, are provided. title: Quantitative Comparison of Writing Styles Among Indonesian Women Novelists: A Corpus Linguistics Approach
abstract: Using the KORTARA Korpus Nusantara application, this study employed a quantitative corpus linguistics approach to examine the lexical density and average sentence length in nine novels by Indonesian women authors. title: Distinct Role of NH 3 in Enhancing Atmospheric Nitrous Acid Formation: Evidence From an Autumn Field Campaign in Beijing
abstract: Abstract Nitrous acid (HONO) is a key precursor of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), which plays a central role in atmospheric oxidation and aerosol formation. However, the mechanisms responsible for frequently elevated HONO levels, particularly the role of ammonia (NH 3 ) under complex atmospheric pollution conditions, remain under debate. title: Immune-driven remodeling in calcific aortic valve disease: mechanisms and immunotherapeutic opportunities
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent degenerative valvular disorder in the aging population, for which no pharmacological therapy has proven effective in halting or reversing disease progression. Over the past decade, CAVD has been increasingly recognized not as a passive degenerative process of calcium deposition, but as an active, inflammation-driven disease characterized by osteogenic remodeling. title: A Short Evidence‐Based, Belief‐Focused Educational Video Improves Back Pain Beliefs but Not Lifting Behaviour in Healthy Office Workers: An Exploratory Randomised Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Unhelpful beliefs about low back pain are associated with altered movement behaviour during lifting. abstract: La adquisición continua de variables del suelo mediante dispositivos del Internet de las Cosas (IoT) genera datos cuya utilidad depende de su adecuada gestión, visualización e interpretación. Este artículo presenta el diseño e implementación de una plataforma web como capa de servicios de un sistema IoT de monitoreo edáfico para agricultura de precisión. title: Comparative Analysis of Groundwater Recharge Dynamics in Granular (Soil) and Fractured Aquifers Using Water Level Fluctuation Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Groundwater recharge estimation is fundamental for the sustainable management of water resources, especially in complex hydrogeological systems comprising granular and fractured aquifers. This study investigates recharge dynamics in two sub-basins through the monitoring of Water Table Fluctuation (WTF) in seven wells: five dug wells (DW) located in the granular aquifer (soil) and two tube wells (TW) in the fractured aquifer. abstract: La contratación integral por precio fijo en Ecuador traslada al contratista gran parte de los riesgos financieros y restringe los reajustes y los contratos complementarios, por lo que la calidad de los estudios previos determina la prevención de contingencias económicas. title: Body dimension perception: a study among students of the military police officer training course
abstract: Introduction Analyzing body size perception among Military Police Officers is important for their work. Thus, the aim of the study was to analyze body dimension perception among students of the Military Police Officer Training Course (MPOC). Methods MPOC students were evaluated for body dimension perception and variables such as anthropometric measures and body composition, mood state, and physical activity time. title: Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) in heat stroke: molecular mechanisms from gut dysbiosis to multi-organ injury
abstract: Heat stroke, a life-threatening condition characterized by core hyperthermia (≥40 °C), central nervous system dysfunction, and multi-organ failure with mortality rates of 20–70%, is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory and hemodynamic disorder rather than a purely thermoregulatory collapse. Among the emerging mediators of its pathophysiology, trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO)—a gut microbiota-derived metabolite generated from dietary choline, L-carnitine, and betaine—has attracted growing attention as a molecular link between heat-induced gut dysbiosis and multi-organ injury. abstract: ABSTRACT This study focuses on the development of nanofibrous mats incorporated with essential oils (EOs) for application as active food packaging materials. Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and polystyrene (PS) were employed as hydrophilic and hydrophobic polymer matrices, respectively. abstract: Abstract Enhanced weathering, adding crushed silicate minerals to soils, is being explored as a way to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide, but its effects on soil organic carbon remain uncertain. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. In a 55-week soil microcosm experiment, adding olivine alone reduces total soil organic carbon. abstract: Though military fiction should hold a significant place in literature, contemporary novels about recent wars are often categorised as popular fiction and are not extensively studied in British literature for a reading of trauma narratives. Works produced by veteran authors that draw attention to the psychological state of the soldiers are often sidelined. title: Spatiotemporal control of drug release on implant surfaces for simultaneous infection inhibition and osseointegration
abstract: Permanent orthopedic and dental implants fail through two mechanistically linked yet temporally distinct pathways: early bacterial colonization that matures into biofilm-protected infection, and insufficient long-term bone anchorage. title: Extraction of rotor unbalance characteristics from non-stationary vibration signals during speed fluctuations
abstract: Abstract Speed fluctuations introduce pronounced non-stationarity into rotor vibration signals, which makes the accurate extraction of rotational-frequency, amplitude, and phase characteristics considerably more difficult than under steady-speed conditions. To address this problem, a rotor-unbalance characteristic-extraction method is developed for speed-fluctuation conditions. abstract: Heterotopic bones that are within the cardiac skeleton are termed ossa cordis. This is the first confirmed ossa cordis in nyala (Tragelaphus angasii). Three distinct bones (two dextrum and one sinistrum) were discovered, a novel finding in any species. title: From epidemiology to molecular pathology: current research status and future prospects on the role of toxic metal exposure in the development and progression of bladder cancer
abstract: Bladder cancer remains a prevalent and lethal urinary malignancy, characterized by high recurrence rates and persistently poor prognosis for muscle-invasive disease. This clinical reality underscores the urgent need to identify modifiable risk factors. Epidemiological evidence from case-control and prospective cohort studies has established dose-dependent associations with arsenic and consistent tissue-specific accumulation of cadmium and chromium, while lead remains conditional on metabolic status. abstract: La incorporación de inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) en la educación superior plantea oportunidades para apoyar la planeación, la creación de materiales y el diseño de actividades, pero también riesgos relacionados con la integridad académica, la privacidad, la dependencia tecnológica y la calidad de la información. title: BRANDS OF UKRAINIAN CITIES
abstract: Amid growing global and regional compe­tition among cities, territorial branding is becoming particularly important as a tool for shaping their unique identities. A cityʼs brand not only serves as a means of visual differentiation but also becomes a strategic resource that ensures the territoryʼs recognition, attractiveness, and competitiveness. Clinical manifestations vary from asymptomatic carrier states to severe transfusion-dependent anemia. Current routine diagnostic methods in China, gap polymerase chain reaction (gap-PCR) and reverse dot blot hybridization (RDB), detect only 24 common variants, leading to frequent genotype-phenotype mismatches and undiagnosed cases. abstract: Groundwater depletion in the Sana’a Basin, Yemen, has intensified due to over-abstraction, rapid urbanization, and limited natural recharge. abstract: Abstract North-eastern Türkiye is highly endemic for human cystic (CE) and alveolar echinococcosis (AE), but the contribution of free-roaming dogs to transmission remains poorly understood. abstract: Teachers’ classroom assessment (CA) practices can significantly impact student learning, motivation, and socio-emotional well-being. This paper presents the process and outcomes of an effort to build a framework of CA principles to facilitate K-12 teacher practices that will lead to improved student learning, motivation and belonging called, ‘A Guiding Framework for Effective, Equitable Classroom Assessment for Teacher Practice and Student Success’. abstract: Regional early warning governance has become increasingly important as multidimensional threats such as social conflict, environmental crises, and regional instability develop beyond the traditional scope of disaster management. abstract: Background Donor human milk (DHM) is a critical alternative for vulnerable infants when maternal milk is unavailable, but its clinical utilisation in South Africa is constrained by limited understanding of how maternal knowledge, perceived safety, cultural meanings and social contexts shape local acceptance. abstract: Cancer-testis antigens (CTAs) are attractive targets for tumour immunotherapy due to their restricted expression in human malignancies and broad population-level prevalence. abstract: Saudi Arabias giga-project programmes create unusually demanding supply networks: complex project interfaces, geographically dispersed production, specialist imports, simultaneous demands for capacity and strict performance expectations. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is now among the foremost threats to global health, and the pipeline of new antibiotics has not kept pace with it. A structural driver of resistance is often overlooked: the dominant “single molecule–single target” paradigm of antibiotic design imposes a well-defined selective pressure that bacteria can escape through a single mutation or acquired gene. abstract: BACKGROUND: Chinese cabbage is one of the most widely consumed vegetables in China. abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. abstract: Childhood obesity has become a major global public health concern. It is an early-onset systemic immunometabolic disorder closely associated with multi-organ complications, including insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease (CVD). abstract: Using the 2020 and 2024 multiregional input-output tables at constant prices, we examine China’s position in the electrical and optical equipment (E&E) value chain and its exposure to hypothetical decoupling. abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the geographic distribution of mosquito-borne viruses (MBVs), increasing the risk of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus transmission in regions that have historically experienced limited exposure. abstract: Cerebral ischemia frequently triggers persistent learning and memory dysfunction, which is closely associated with structural and functional impairments of memory-related brain regions including the hippocampus, amygdala and cerebral cortex. abstract: The contemporary era is defined by an illusive condition where boundaries between factual reality and fiction blur due to massive disinformation and rapid technology. This technocentrism triggers a crisis of values, dehumanization, and directional disorientation in Indonesian church institutions and theological higher education. abstract: Planned adaptation projects channel climate finance to rural communities, yet the pathways connecting intervention design to household participation are often assumed rather than examined. This study assessed the effect of polypropylene (PP) fiber reinforcement on the wetting–drying (W–D) durability of clayey sand stabilized with 0.25% xanthan gum (XG). title: The effect of urban density on stock returns: evidence from satellite imagery and firms in the United States
abstract: Abstract We study how the urban density of the areas where firms are located impacts their stock returns. Using high-resolution satellite images and image segmentation algorithms, we develop measures of building density for the most populated metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) in the US. We find that firms in urban areas with a higher potential for density increase are perceived as less risky in the stock market because they can feasibly sustain their growth, leading to lower stock returns. abstract: La sentencia Bosco del Tribunal Supremo español (2025) reconoció el derecho de acceso al código fuente de una aplicación administrativa que determina el cumplimiento de los requisitos para percibir una prestación social, consolidando así la transparencia algorítmica como manifestación del principio constitucional de transparencia. abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems harbour nearly half of all known fish species yet rank among the most threatened on the planet, with biological invasion operating as one of the primary functional destabilizers in systems where dam cascades have already dismantled natural biogeographical barriers. abstract: ABSTRACT The rare event of an extremely bright explosion of a classical nova in 1901 gave birth to GK Per (Nova 1901). abstract: Success of a genome-wide association study (GWAS) depends on the density of variants available for analysis; these variants are sometimes rare and ancestry-specific. abstract: Purpose China is an indispensable and dynamic member of the global community. abstract: Introduction Indigenous cultures across Turtle Island have long promoted wellness through language, ceremony, storytelling, movement, community connection, and relationships with the natural world. These cultural practices may serve as important pathways for healing and health promotion. abstract: ABSTRACT Curtailing environmental hazards from CO 2 emissions remains challenging for developing economies, especially for countries with high population growth and fossil‐energy dependence. abstract: ABSTRACT The North‐East region of India is a host to a variety of underutilized plant species, including Litsea cubeba . It is a fruit widely utilized as a spice and flavor enhancer. abstract: Abstract Under the background of global warming, drought risk has intensified. Clarifying the changing patterns and response relationships of different drought types is vital for risk management and climate change adaptation. Using multi‐model data from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase VI (CMIP6) and an improved three‐dimensional clustering algorithm, this study identified meteorological and Agricultural drought (AD) events in Asia. title: Intelligent Hybrid Selection of Secure and Energy-Efficient Lightweight Encryption Algorithms for Sustainable Internet of Things
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has increased the demand for secure and resource-efficient confidentiality mechanisms in constrained environments. Selecting an appropriate lightweight cipher is challenging because its implementation involves trade-offs among hardware resources, computational performance, memory, and energy requirements. abstract: Accessibility to urban green spaces is recognized to have wide-ranging benefits for population health. Yet, the ways in which green space accessibility is quantified remain limited, with popular approaches based on measuring the spatial distribution of opportunities with respects to population locations. title: Spatial organisation of microplastics in road runoff across an urban network
abstract: Road runoff is a major pathway by which microplastics are transported from urban surfaces to aquatic ecosystems, yet the spatial scales over which measurements represent road networks remain unresolved. This constrains source attribution, monitoring design and urban emission inventories. abstract: The effect of hydrolysate and eluate recirculation on the solubilization and recovery of carbon and nutrients from waste activated sludge during microwave-alkali treatment was systematically investigated. The results showed that the recirculation strategy significantly enhanced the accumulation of sCOD, PO 4 3- -P, and TAN in both hydrolysate and eluate, with concentrations increasing by up to 4–9 times depending on recirculation conditions. abstract: This scoping review collects empirical studies exploring the conceptualization, perception, and decision-making of Generation Z regarding marriage in Asia. This study examined literature related to meaning-making as marriage constructs, readiness standards that introduce individual decision trajectories, and sociocultural factors such as socioeconomic context, gender norms, family systems of support or control, and language use in social media. abstract: Mismanagement of the animal by-products (ABPs) pig slurry, poultry manure and rendered by-products poses serious environmental problems. The need to reduce environmental impacts such as eutrophication caused by livestock farming has prompted European Union (EU) policymakers to introduce policies and strategies for more sustainable management of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) and to improve the recirculation of P in agricultural systems. abstract: Abstract Europe finds itself adrift in a world of rising geopolitical uncertainty. Russia has brought interstate war back to Europe. American democracy and hegemony and the ‘liberal international order’ appear to be in steep decline. The world as Europeans and Americans have known it for 80 years may be gone forever. abstract: This study examines the effects of monetary and non-monetary rewards on employee motivation and performance within the Directorate General of Taxes in Indonesia, with particular attention to the mediating role of employee motivation. Unlike studies that treat rewards as a single construct, this study analyzes monetary and non-monetary rewards as distinct variables. title: Cover crop rotations improve soil health in commercial tropical vegetable systems, but responses depend on soil type
abstract: Sustainable vegetable production requires healthy soils. While the effects of cover cropping as a conservation practice on mid- and long-term soil health improvement in temperate row crops are well studied, the short-term recovery of soil health in tropical vegetable systems is less documented. We evaluated the effects of shifting from a vegetable–fallow rotation to a vegetable–cover crop rotation of legumes or legume-grass in commercial farms of two municipalities on the semi-arid southern coast of Puerto Rico: Guánica (a loamy Typic Calciargids) and Santa Isabel (a clayey Typic Haplusterts).

title: Gradual Institutional Change in Food Security Governance: The Case of Majene Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Local food security is usually assessed through availability and distribution, yet the institutions that govern it are seldom examined as products of change over time. Earlier research on Majene Regency, West Sulawesi, identified a dormant Food Security Council as the main coordination bottleneck, but its synchronic design could not explain how that condition arose. abstract: ABSTRACT Firms increasingly commit to sustainability, yet ecological degradation and social exclusion continue to intensify. This has prompted interest in regenerative approaches that restore rather than preserve socio‐ecological systems, although evidence on their organisational consequences remains scarce. abstract: Underutilized and climate-resilient roots and tubers are foundational to Andean food systems, but their persistence depends not only on genetic resources and breeding, but also on seed circulation, farmer preferences, diets, markets, governance, livelihoods, and cultural transmission. This study developed a sustainability-monitoring framework for Peru’s Agrobiodiversity Zones (ZABD)—collectively governed territories dedicated to the in situ conservation and use of native agrobiodiversity—and obtained participatory evidence related to the content and face validity of its indicator set. abstract: La escritura argumentativa permite formular una posición, seleccionar evidencia, considerar alternativas y participar responsablemente en debates académicos y públicos. abstract: Sustainable forest management is critical for promoting multiple ecosystem services (ESs), yet the thresholds of site condition and stand structure on the comprehensive benefit of multiple ESs remain unclear across forest types at regional scales. abstract: Breast milk is the optimal nutritional intake for infants. abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to be a major global disease, directly impacting endemic regions and indirectly affecting FMD-free regions. abstract: En la formación inicial docente, la alfabetización académica constituye un proceso fundamental para la apropiación de los discursos y prácticas de lectura y escritura propios del campo educativo. abstract: Introduction Emotional resilience is a key psychological resource for maintaining well-being and adaptation in the workplace and is closely associated with perceived emotional intelligence. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between perceived emotional intelligence and resilience and to explore their associations with sociodemographic and occupational variables. abstract: Esta voz presenta un análisis de la democracia deliberativa. En primer lugar, se expone el origen de la democracia deliberativa como área de estudio y su panorama actual. title: Effectiveness of Dithane M-45 in Suppressing Fungal Disease Improving The Growth and Yield of Red Bell Pepper (Capsicum Annuum L.)
abstract: Red bell pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) production can be constrained by fungal diseases, making effective disease management important for maintaining plant growth and yield. This study examined the response of red bell pepper to Dithane M-45 under field conditions in Tikala Subdistrict, North Toraja Regency, from July to September 2023. A completely randomized design (CRD) was used to evaluate six concentrations: 0 (control), 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 g/L, with three replicates per treatment and four plants per experimental unit. title: Industrial Extrusion Processing and Structure Development of Biodegradable Films for Food Packaging Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Biodegradable films have emerged as sustainable alternatives to conventional plastics for food packaging, but their industrial implementation requires balancing functional performance, processability, structure development and end‐of‐life behavior. This review critically examines biodegradable films, focusing on functional requirements, material selection and industrial processing technologies, particularly extrusion‐based processes and multilayer structures. title: Synergistic dual-phase network in rigid-flexible PU/LAGP composite electrolytes for fast-ion-conducting solid-state lithium batteries
abstract: Introduction The practical implementation of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is severely hindered by the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness. Additionally, “ion-trapping” effects give rise to sluggish interfacial lithium-ion transport, further restricting battery performance. Developing composite solid electrolytes that simultaneously resolve these two bottlenecks remains a critical challenge. title: Structural characteristics and regulatory mechanisms of the ocular surface microbiota and their relationship with ocular surface health
abstract: This review delineates the spatial distribution of ocular surface microbiota (OSM) and its dynamic interplay with ocular health. Culture-independent surveys employing 16S rRNA and metagenomic sequencing reveal an ultra-low-biomass ecosystem characterized by restricted α-diversity. Firmicutes , Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria are the dominant phyla. Corynebacterium , coagulase-negative staphylococci, Propionibacterium and Streptococcus show high prevalence and temporal stability. These four genera form a conserved core. title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. title: Only Your Mind Sets the Limits: Socio‐Cognitive Pathways between Growth Mindset and Reading Achievement Across Nordic and Chinese Educational Systems
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mindset theory has increasingly shifted from asking whether growth mindsets predict achievement to asking how, for whom, and under what conditions beliefs about intelligence become motivationally consequential. AIMS: This study contributes to that theoretical shift by examining mindset as a distal belief embedded within a broader social-cognitive system of achievement motivation. title: Pollution Characteristics and Health Risk Assessment of Potentially Toxic Elements in the Black Soil Region of Southern Jilin Province, China
abstract: Abstract To investigate the spatial distribution, pollution status, sources, and health risks of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in the topsoil of three counties/cities (Shuangliao City, Lishu County, and Gongzhuling City) in southern Jilin Province, 138 topsoil samples (0–20 cm depth) were collected and analyzed for eight elements (As, Cd, Cr, Pb, Hg, Cu, Ni, and Zn). Spatial distribution patterns were examined using Kriging interpolation. Pollution levels were assessed via the single-factor pollution index, Nemerow comprehensive pollution index, and potential ecological risk index. Source

title: Urban-rural gap in mathematics achievement: problem comprehension and linguistic barriers
abstract: Learning inequalities between students from urban and rural institutions are accentuated when the language of instruction differs from the mother tongue. This research analyzed the gaps in mathematical problem solving and the associated linguistic factors, through an explanatory cross-sectional study with 395 secondary school students from public institutions in Ayacucho, Peru. A confirmatory factor analysis and a hierarchical regression by ordinary least squares with robust standard errors were applied. title: Designing ecological corridors for connectivity in fragmented protected areas: a transferable framework to guide conservation policy
abstract: Habitat fragmentation in the South Chilean biodiversity hotspot threatens endemic species and ecosystem functionality, requiring a shift from isolated protected areas to integrated connectivity networks under Chile's SBAP Law (No. 21,600). This study develops a replicable framework to parameterize landscape resistance through a multispecies hybrid approach, integrating habitat suitability modeling for six focal species, systematized expert knowledge, and weighted uncertainty metrics. title: Genealogías invisibles. Dibujar las redes de la arquitectura moderna (1923–1966)
abstract: Dibujar una genealogía implica decidir qué relaciones forman parte de la historia que representa. Este artículo parte de esa premisa para reconstruir la arquitectura moderna entre 1923 y 1966 a partir de las relaciones profesionales documentadas entre arquitectos y arquitectas. La investigación utiliza el dibujo como método. Cada conexión que se incorpora permite seguir nuevas trayectorias y observar la posición que estas adquieren dentro de una red común. title: Administrative Decentralization
abstract: The legitimacy of the administrative state has been challenged since it was first created. These challenges to the legitimacy of the administrative state in theory have transformed into a crisis in reality. The second Trump Administration dismantled several administrative agencies and disrupted many other agencies in its first year in office. In the year before the second Trump Administration, the Supreme Court overturned Chevron U.S.A. Inc. v. title: Overcoming insect pest challenges for sustainable rice production in the Americas
abstract: Rice production in the Americas has expanded to meet a rising demand, but insect pests continue to threaten yields, grain quality, and farmer incomes. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the major insect pests affecting rice systems across the Americas and evaluates the performance, trade-offs, and complementarities of existing and emerging controls. It describes regional pest complexes, such as rice water weevil in the United States, Hoja Blanca vectors and stem borers in tropical areas, and late-season stink bugs across the continent. title: Mechanism Research Progress of Acupuncture Regulating Vagus Nerve-Cholinergic Anti-inflammatory Pathway in the Prevention and Treatment of Endometriosis-Related Pain
abstract: Endometriosis (EM)-related pain involves multiple links including local inflammatory microenvironment, neurogenic inflammation, peripheral and central sensitization, and autonomic nervous imbalance. Current hormone therapy and surgical treatment cannot achieve sufficient pain relief and are prone to recurrence. This paper reviews the role of the vagus nerve-mediated cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAIP) in EM pain and the mechanistic evidence that acupuncture regulates this pathway. title: Climatic thresholds and temporal decoupling drive reproductive phenology in Neotropical cloud forests: a 36‐year analysis
abstract: Reproductive phenology influences ecosystem functioning and climate sensitivity in tropical montane cloud forests, but phase‑specific climatic thresholds and the temporal coupling between flowering and fruiting remain poorly quantified over decadal scales. We analyzed a 36‑year monthly record (1983–2018) from a Venezuelan cloud forest (15 focal species) and NASA/POWER hydroclimatic data, integrating random forest models, regression‑tree threshold analysis, climate‑window sensitivity analyses, scale‑dependent coherence, species‑level trend analyses, and temporal models that account for seasonal

title: L’innovation locale et sa contribution au développement durable : pour une taxonomie du système local de transition
abstract: L’article examine l’innovation locale en l’opposant au modèle schumpétérien, centré sur le marché, qui aborde les territoires uniquement dans le cadre de la compétition mondiale. Envisager l’innovation au service du développement durable du territoire implique de l’intégrer dans la politique de transition écologique. L’article propose de dépasser la notion de système local d’innovation pour envisager celle de système local de transition, dont les composantes seront développées. title: Bacterial Cellulose: A Sustainable Platform for Fabricating Advanced Carbon Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The global shift toward sustainable energy storage solutions has highlighted bacterial cellulose (BC) as a renewable, biodegradable biopolymer for fabricating advanced carbon nanostructures. This review examines the microbial synthesis, optimization, thermochemical conversion, and applications of BC‐derived carbon materials in next‐generation electrochemical energy storage (EES) devices, with comprehensive coverage of both battery and supercapacitor applications (2014–2025). title: A gradual and general method to understand why Functional Programming is important
abstract: En el contexto actual, la programación sigue enseñándose predominantemente bajo un punto de vista imperativo, en el que los programas son concebidos como series de instrucciones ejecutables por computadoras. Sin embargo, la Programación Funcional (PF) propone una visión más amplia, que incluye a la anterior, pero la expande: los programas son descripciones computables. Incorporar esta visión en la formación de programadores requiere un enfoque pedagógico que no imponga la abstracción prematuramente, sino que la construya de forma progresiva. title: The 2025 Santorini earthquake sequence unveils the tail of the magnitude-frequency distribution
abstract: Abstract We present a statistical analysis of the intense earthquake swarm near Santorini, Greece, in 2025. A change-point analysis of the b -value of the Gutenberg–Richter frequency-magnitude distribution indicates that, despite obvious spatiotemporal changes in seismicity characteristics during the crisis, there was no significant change of b with time. title: Sub-aerial biofilms on urban stone surfaces: community structure and microbial co-occurrence networks
abstract: Sub-aerial biofilms (SABs) play a key role in the biodeterioration of stone cultural heritage, yet their microbial composition may vary depending on the colonized lithic substrate. The aim of this study was to analyze the taxonomic composition of SABs in relation to the type of stone substrate. The material consisted of ten SAB samples, including eight collected from a historic cemetery in Kraków and two from retaining walls within the city. title: Social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India: A qualitative evidence synthesis
abstract: Background and objectives There is a high prevalence of social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India. This review was conducted to explore the phenomenon of social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India. Methods We searched PubMed, SCOPUS, CINAHL and Google Scholar with an appropriately designed search strategy to identify qualitative or mixed methods studies that explored the phenomenon of social isolation and loneliness among elders in India with restrictions of English language papers published between 2015-2025. title: Decentralized authentication in VANETs using blockchain and edge computing
abstract: Vehicular Ad hoc Networks are highly dynamic wireless networks that enable communication between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. They enhance road safety by supporting driver-assistance services and advanced transportation applications, such as automated driving and intelligent transportation systems. These networks are characterized by dynamic topology, intermittent connectivity, and limited resources. title: The land use challenge in the United Kingdom: Finding space for food production and biodiversity
abstract: The nations of the United Kingdom have set ambitious policy targets for land-based activities and outputs including around food production, climate change and biodiversity. As land area is constrained these targets risk not being met without coordinated policy. Maximising the public and private benefits from the land requires understanding the trade-offs and synergies between different activities, and the comparative advantage of different areas in producing different outputs. title: Estrategias SEO en emprendimientos sostenibles de Argentina, México y Perú
abstract: Purpose: The sustainable work that a business undertakes in creating a product or service should be visible to all its audiences, as it is a differentiating factor in today's highly competitive market. In this sense, this study seeks to determine whether sustainable businesses use SEO tools to position themselves in their markets, as well as to identify gaps in opportunities and areas for improvement. abstract: Plant vascular tissues consist of multiple cell types that together coordinate long-distance transport, signaling, and perform diverse metabolic functions. While extensive research uncovered key regulators of vascular patterning and function, the dissection of individual vascular cell types has been hindered by their inaccessibility in planta and the interdependence among the cell types. title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI
abstract: Abstract The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an “immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said.” Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion MRI and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. title: Autonomous paths for the localisation of foreign public buildings in the modern Jiangnan region, China, based on a mixed method
abstract: Between 1840 and 1949, the Jiangnan region, represented by Jiangsu Province and Shanghai, experienced the proliferation of foreign-influenced architecture. The eclectic integration of architectural forms produced a postcolonial paradox, increasingly blurring the distinction between Western colonial influence and indigenous cultural subjectivity. This paper examines modern foreign public buildings in Jiangnan through a mixed method, integrating literature analysis, entropy weight method, and case study analysis to investigate autonomous paths for the localisation of foreign architecture. abstract: Este artículo consolida y actualiza una literatura hasta ahora dispersa sobre optimización de minas a cielo abierto, integrando en un solo marco de referencia más de 90 publicaciones producidas entre 1965 y 2026 —desde el algoritmo de Lerchs-Grossmann hasta los enfoques contemporáneos de planificación integrada—, conectando por primera vez la teoría de grafos, modelos económicos, diseño computacional y la gobernanza ASG en una trayectoria conceptual unificada. title: Does the Belt and Road Initiative reduce poverty? Evaluating grain trade openness as an intermediate policy outcome
abstract: Introduction Eradicating poverty remains a core objective of global sustainable development. While the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) provides a novel paradigm for inclusive growth, existing evaluations predominantly focus on macroeconomic aggregates, often overlooking the micro-level transmission mechanisms within the agricultural sector. Methods Leveraging the BRI as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies a two-way fixed effects difference-in-differences (TWFE-DID) model to a panel of 131 countries from 2000 to 2023. title: Nonlinear thermo-viscoelastic characterisation and modelling of adhesively bonded joints in CFRP-strengthened steel
abstract: Adhesively bonded carbon fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) plates are widely used to strengthen ageing steel members, but the long-term performance of such retrofits is governed by the adhesive layer’s thermo-viscoelastic behaviour. This paper presents an experimental–numerical framework for the nonlinear thermo-viscoelastic characterisation of a structural adhesive and for evaluating the effects of sustained loading on the CFRP-strengthened steel beams. title: Hegemonic decline and grand strategy: A variegated framework
abstract: Abstract How do hegemons respond to relative decline? The existing literature suggests that declining hegemons either cling to the status quo through preventive war and other expansionist measures or retrench. This article argues that hegemonic decline produces incentives for both forms of action. More specifically, I provide a variegated framework that distinguishes between mild and acute decline as two distinct situations through which declining hegemons may pass. title: A GIS ‐Based Method to Prioritize Railway Links for Climate Resilience Planning Based on Operational Exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional climate risk assessments typically consider hazard, exposure, and vulnerability dimensions, but often restrict exposure to spatial hazard intersections, neglecting the operational intensity of infrastructure. This study proposes a geographic information systems (GIS)‐based framework that uses operational exposure derived from freight and passenger flows as the primary metric for network prioritization. title: Linking Biodiversity Risk Management to Supply Chain Financing: Strategic Financing Transformation Under Physical Climate Risk
abstract: ABSTRACT Using panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2011 to 2024, this study examines the association between biodiversity risk management (BRM) and trade credit provision (TCP). Our results show that BRM positively impacts corporate TCP. Heterogeneity analyses show that the positive effect is statistically significant among non‐heavily‐polluting firms, high‐tech firms, firms in more competitive markets, and firms facing less stringent environmental regulation. title: Evaluating the impact of homoeopathy in managing the morbidity associated with grade III and IV lower limb lymphoedema in adults with lymphatic filariasis
abstract: Introduction Lymphatic filariasis is a major public health burden, particularly in endemic regions, with millions suffering from chronic lymphoedema and hydrocele. While mass drug administration aims to restrict transmission, effective morbidity management remains a significant challenge. Homoeopathy has reported potential in managing lymphoedema, yet evidence in cases of grade III and IV lymphoedema is limited. abstract: Abstract Practical parameter identifiability in ODE-based epidemiological models is a known issue, yet one that merits further study. It is essentially ubiquitous owing to noise and errors in real data. In this study, to avoid uncertainty stemming from data of unknown quality, simulated data with added noise are used to investigate practical identifiability in two distinct epidemiological models. title: Educación de jóvenes y adultos en Ecuador: Equidad educativa, inclusión y desarrollo humano
abstract: La educación de personas jóvenes y adultas con escolaridad inconclusa constituye una dimensión del derecho al aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida y un componente potencial de las políticas de equidad en Ecuador; este artículo examina críticamente su relevancia para la inclusión social y el desarrollo humano, con especial atención a las modalidades de alfabetización, educación general básica y bachillerato; se desarrolló una revisión documental crítica de fuentes normativas, publicaciones institucionales y literatura científica, seleccionadas por su pertinencia temática, trazabilidad y capacidad

abstract: The gut microbiota contributes to host homeostasis through metabolic, immunological, neural, and barrier-related pathways, and its role in the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases has received increasing attention. Patients with Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis often exhibit alterations in gut microbial composition, microbial metabolic function, and peripheral inflammatory phenotypes. title: GIS-based inventory and utility assessment of spring resources in the Kashmir Himalaya
abstract: Introduction Mountain springs are the primary source of drinking water and support the livelihoods of many people in the Indian Himalayan Region. These springs face pressure from human activities, land-use changes, and climate change. Detailed records of springs in the Kashmir Himalaya are scarce, making planning and conservation difficult. title: Cortisol measurements, biochemical and hematological parameters as biomarkers of Cunero cattle welfare during pre-slaughter handling in the Apurimac Region of Peru
abstract: Introduction For Cunero cattle, hematological parameters and biochemical biomarkers may serve as potential indicators of pre-slaughter stress, though their functional utility requires further validation. These measurements are essential for evaluating animal welfare when they fall within physiological ranges. Methods Blood samples were collected from the coccygeal vein of 100 Cunero cattle (50 females and 50 males) after they were transported from the Apurimac highlands to the municipal slaughterhouse in Abancay. title: On microlocal artifacts arising in tomography modeled by a class of generalized Radon transforms
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we provide a unified framework for understanding how and why artifacts arise in limited data tomography, using precise microlocal analysis of the underlying generalized Radon transforms (gRT). Our insights facilitate a more accurate assessment of reconstructions and eventually enable practical artifact reduction strategies in real-world imaging applications. title: Islet extracellular matrix remodelling in type 2 diabetes: implications for β-cell failure and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterised by progressive insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, ultimately resulting in impaired glucose homeostasis. While metabolic and genetic factors are central to disease development, increasing evidence indicates that disruption of the pancreatic islet extracellular matrix (ECM) may be an important contributor to β-cell failure. title: Micro/nanoplastics–metal(loid) co-exposure in rice: evidence, mechanisms, and food-safety implications
abstract: Micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) and metal(loid)s frequently co-occur in rice agroecosystems, where legacy metal(loid) contamination and continuing plastic inputs may jointly threaten soil quality and rice safety. Co-exposure complicates risk assessment because rice responses cannot always be predicted from MNP-only or metal(loid)-only treatments. To address this, the review integrates mechanistic findings into a mixture- and context-dependent synthesis linking MNP traits and metal(loid) identity/speciation to soil–rhizosphere processes, plant uptake/partitioning, and grain food-safety outcomes. title: The Qianlong XXXV event: a potential benchmark for extreme geomagnetic storms based on historical Chinese auroral archives
abstract: Modern technological society is highly vulnerable to extreme geomagnetic storms, yet the terrestrial upper limit of such events remains poorly constrained because continuous instrumental geomagnetic records cover only a relatively short historical period. To extend this baseline, we quantitatively reconstruct the geomagnetic superstorm of September 1770 (termed Qianlong XXXV storm) using systematically documented auroral observations preserved in Chinese regional chronicles. title: Saindhava Lavana in Visha Chikitsa: An Integrative Review of Ayurveda Concepts and Contemporary Scientific Evidence

title: Time-dependent pharmacokinetic changes and renal SGLT2 expression alterations of dapagliflozin under high-altitude hypoxia in diabetic rats
abstract: Objective This study investigated the time-dependent effects of high-altitude hypoxia on the pharmacokinetics (PK), renal sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) expression, and glycemic response to dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rats. Methods T2DM was induced in male Wistar rats via high-fat diet and low-dose streptozotocin. title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and in vitro validation reveal the molecular mechanisms of bisphenol A-induced MASLD
abstract: Background Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Methods This study combined network toxicology and molecular docking to explore BPA-induced hepatotoxicity targets and pathways in MASLD. title: Recent Advances in Covalent Triazine Frameworks for Solar‐Driven Photocatalysis: Intrinsic Advantages, Modification Strategies, and Photocatalytic Applications
abstract: Photocatalysis, a highly attractive technology, can harness abundant and clean solar energy to produce chemical fuels and degrade hazardous pollutants into harmless molecules, offering a promising pathway to tackle both energy crises and environmental pollution. Owing to their distinctive π‐conjugated structure, nitrogen‐rich triazine motifs, high specific surface area, and good chemical and thermal stability, covalent triazine frameworks (CTFs) have emerged as an important class of porous organic semiconductors with widespread photocatalytic applications. title: Differential DNA methylation profiling of spermatogenesis-associated genes in patients with idiopathic hypospermatogenesis: a hospital-based case-control study
abstract: Hypospermatogenesis is a histopathological subtype of non-obstructive azoospermia and is characterized by a decrease in the total number of germ cells within the seminiferous tubule as a result of spermatogenic failure. Germ cell epigenetic reprograming during development shows that the methylation status of testicular DNA is highly distinct in which hypomethylated foci predominates. title: Historiography and Time: In Search of a Lost Poem in Ian McEwan’s What We Can Know
abstract: Tracing the delineations of historiography, time, and post-historical perspectives in the contemporary period, this paper examines the intertwining of the narrator's and the historian's roles, the use and abuse of extratextual materials to prove historicity and to deconstruct its time through narrative techniques in Ian McEwan’s What We Can Know (2025). abstract: En los últimos años, distintos municipios argentinos han incorporado chatbots y asistentes virtuales como canal de atención ciudadana y de acceso a trámites de asistencia social, siguiendo el modelo pionero de Boti, del Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. title: Land use transitions drive ecosystem service supply–demand balance: spatiotemporal assessment and risk zoning in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section)
abstract: Growing human interference with natural ecosystems has positioned land use transition as a dominant force shaping the supply–demand equilibrium of ecosystem services (ESs). Focusing on the ecologically vulnerable Three Gorges Reservoir Area (Hubei section), this study examined how land use changes from 2000 to 2020 influenced water yield (WY), carbon storage (CS), food production (FP), and soil retention (SR). title: A striking new subgenus and species of Asian horned toads (Anura, Megophryidae, Megophryinae) from Xizang, China
abstract: Motuo County, located in the eastern Himalayas and within the lower section of the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, is characterized by steep elevational gradients and complex topography, supporting high levels of biodiversity and endemism that remain insufficiently explored. Moench] biomass production is a promising component of the bioeconomy that combines high productivity with the potential use of local resources and by-products from bioenergy processes. abstract: Based on morphological comparisons and molecular phylogenetic analyses, a new species of the genus Leptobrachella from Mayanghe National Nature Reserve, Guizhou Province, China, is described, Leptobrachella mayanghe sp. nov . Phylogenetic analyses of mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI gene sequences supported the new species as an independent lineage. title: Comparative phytolith profiles of the weed grasses Echinochloa colona and Echinochloa crus-galli (Poaceae): implications for species taxonomy
abstract: Introduction Taxonomic delimitation of closely related Echinochloa species is frequently complicated by morphological plasticity and overlapping vegetative characters, necessitating complementary diagnostic approaches. This study aimed to evaluate whether integrated phytolith characteristics can provide reliable discriminatory features for distinguishing Echinochloa colona and E. crus-galli . title: “We are just blind there”: institutional invisibility of female genital schistosomiasis in South Africa
abstract: Introduction Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS) remains severely overlooked within neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), disproportionately affecting women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Despite its high prevalence and association with adverse reproductive health outcomes and increased HIV susceptibility, FGS receives minimal attention in research, policy, and clinical practice. Understanding how FGS is or isn’t prioritised within policy implementation is critical for addressing this gap. title: El papel de las inversiones europeas: aprendizajes nacionales
abstract: Las inversiones de la Unión Europea han desempeñado un papel decisivo en la modernización económica de España desde su adhesión, pero su contribución efectiva a la convergencia territorial, la transformación productiva y el crecimiento potencial sigue siendo objeto de debate. abstract: Esta contribución enfoca el uso de una metodología mixta, en concreto la combinación de experimentos lingüísticos y entrevistas metalingüísticas. title: Simultaneous Bayesian quantification and decomposition of structural, parameter, and forcing uncertainty in hydrologic models: A blended model approach

This study proposes a unified Bayesian framework that jointly quantifies and temporally decomposes these three uncertainty sources in streamflow prediction. The blended model structure of Mai et al. abstract: ABSTRACT This work reports a novel strategy for fabricating stable and highly efficient shortwave infrared (SWIR) light emitters by incorporating lead sulfide (PbS) quantum dots (QDs) into a cesium lead bromide (CsPbBr 3 ) nanocrystal (NC) matrix. The CsPbBr 3 matrix effectively reduces surface trap states of PbS QDs and significantly enhances their quantum yield. title: A comparative legal analysis of migratory bird conservation along the African–Eurasian flyway
abstract: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African-Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. Making Sense of Relaxation in Digital Space: A Netnographic Study on Relaxation Music Commentary on YouTube
abstract: Relaxation music is increasingly integrated into everyday life in digital spaces, particularly to facilitate sleep, calm the mind, and create a comfortable atmosphere. This study aims to explore how users describe and interpret their experiences of relaxation while listening to music and relaxation soundscapes on YouTube, how interactions among users contribute to shaping and expanding these meanings, and the contexts and purposes underlying their use of relaxation music. title: Exploring the relationship between cultural landscapes and psychological well-being through indigenous environmental design in rural China
abstract: Introduction Indigenous environmental design in rural China is increasingly affected by modernization, tourism development, and ecological change. However, empirical evidence concerning the relationship between cultural landscape fidelity and residents’ psychological well-being remains limited. title: Evaluation of dragon fruit (Hylocereus spp.) cultivated in the medium lowland agroecosystems based on yield traits and biochemical contents
abstract: Fruit crops are highly susceptible to climate change and global warming, posing a significant threat to fruit production. Recognizing dragon fruit as a potential candidate for climate-smart horticulture, this study assessed its adaptability to medium-lowland agroecosystems based on morphological, yield, and biochemical performance. title: A new species of alpine grasshopper of the genus Podismopsis Zubovski, 1900 (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Gomphocerinae) from Central Europe
abstract: Podismopsis kristini sp. nov . (Orthoptera, Acrididae, Gomphocerinae) is described from the Tatras in Slovakia, representing the seventh European species of the genus Podismopsis Zubovski, 1900, and the first record of the genus from the Western Carpathians. The new species inhabits cold, wind-exposed alpine grasslands at 1,820–1,920 m a.s.l. in the upper part of the Žiar Valley in the Western Tatras and is known only from the type locality. abstract: This mini review examines the potential roles of proton signaling in the peripheral and central nervous systems and its proposed regulation by keratan sulfate (KS). Protons are central to bioenergetics and rapid chemical signaling, linking metabolism to membrane excitability and receptor activity across tissues. Nanoscale-to-microscale pH transients may add a further layer of intercellular communication in the nervous system through proton-sensitive ion channels and receptors. abstract: Given the decisive role of financial systems in economic growth, investment, and resource allocation, the comparative assessment of financial development levels is considered a key indicator in analyzing countries’ development processes. This study aims to analyze the financial development performance of CIVETS countries for the 2000–2020 period using the integrated MAXC-CRISUS-RAWEC-Borda Count model. abstract: Objectives CBT101 is a creatine prodrug under development for disorders driven by impaired neuronal energy homeostasis, with initial development focused on creatine transporter deficiency and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. This first-in-human study aimed to assess the safety and tolerability of single and repeated ascending intranasal doses of CBT101 in healthy male volunteers and explored neurophysiological evidence of central pharmacodynamic activity using quantitative EEG (qEEG) and event-related potentials (ERPs). title: Unexpected fault reactivation during underground gas storage in depleted reservoirs: defining operational pressure bandwidths
abstract: Introduction Underground gas storage and emerging subsurface storage applications for CO 2 , H 2 , and N 2 increasingly rely on depleted, faulted reservoirs. In such settings, pressure recovery and cyclic operations may bring faults close to reactivation even when reservoir pressure remains below the initial value and within the range previously experienced during primary production. title: Acute study of the glycemic, insulinemic and triglyceride responses on white bread with peanuts and cashews in different forms (whole nut, nut butter and nut milk)
abstract: Frequent nut consumption is associated with reduced cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and mortality, particularly in individuals with diabetes, highlighting their potential health benefits. This study investigated the acute postprandial glycemic, insulinemic, and triglyceride responses to white bread consumed with peanuts and cashews in three forms: whole nuts, nut butter, and nut milk. title: Quantitative risk assessment of BSE transmission if insects are reared on residual streams containing animal proteins
abstract: Insect production can play an important role in the bioconversion of residual streams from agri-food production into valuable nutrients for feed and food and as such advance the transition from a linear to a circular food production system. However, under current EU legislation, insect rearing on residual streams containing animal proteins is not allowed because of the risk of animal disease transmission including bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE). abstract: Biomaterial-associated infections remain a major obstacle in regenerative medicine, wound healing, and implantology. While conventional anti-infective materials have mainly focused on preventing bacterial adhesion or delivering antimicrobial agents, infection control alone is often not enough to restore tissue function. abstract: Abstract Northern Thailand experiences severe PM₂.₅ pollution during the dry season from biomass burning, yet the response to incremental emission reductions remains poorly quantified. abstract: Urbanization at a rapid pace is estimated to contribute about 1.5 billion people to urban areas by 2030, leading to increasing concerns regarding the provision of safe water and sanitation facilities and changes in land-use patterns and land-cover. In India, urbanization is mainly city-centric and results from migrations from the rural hinterland, with an increase in urban growth of about 250% over the last two decades. abstract: Perianal infectious wounds form a contaminated, moist, mechanically disturbed repair niche that differs from standard cutaneous wounds. This critical narrative review evaluates whether natural-product pharmacology and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated miRNA biology can be linked credibly in this setting.
