title: Digital marketing and purchase intention among generation X consumers: an empirical study in the automotive sector
abstract: Purpose This study examines the influence of digital marketing levers – email, mobile, social media, and content marketing – on the purchase intention of Tunisian Generation X consumers in the automotive sector. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted, collecting data from 367 Tunisian Generation X consumers to assess the impact of digital marketing levers on purchase intention. title: An energy-efficient approach to sludge drying: Simulation and optimization of a heat pump assisted low-temperature belt dryer
abstract: Sludge drying is the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting stage in the sludge treatment and disposal process. The thermal drying technologies currently employed generally exhibit high energy consumption, which increases the overall cost and energy demand of sludge management. To solve this problem, this study designed a novel heat pump-assisted low-temperature belt dryer with a center-return air configuration to enhance drying uniformity and efficiency. title: Evaluation of health and economic impacts of atmospheric PM₂.₅ in Tabriz, Iran, using BenMAP-CE and AirQ+
abstract: Air pollution poses a major threat to public health and carries the highest burden of environmentally related diseases. This study evaluated mortality associated with long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ and the corresponding economic burden in Tabriz city. The analysis was conducted using the BenMAP-CE and AirQ⁺ software. We evaluated five scenarios concerning the annual average PM₂.₅ concentration: increases to 35 and 25 µg/m³, decreases to 15 and 10 µg/m³, and a reduction to the theoretical minimum risk level of 2.4 µg/m³. title: Functional peptide therapeutics for veterinary osteoarthritis: mechanisms, delivery systems, and translational priorities
abstract: Introduction Veterinary osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic whole-joint disorder that causes pain, gait impairment, reduced activity, and diminished quality of life in companion and performance animals. Current multimodal management includes weight control, rehabilitation, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, prostaglandin E2 EP4 receptor antagonists, anti-nerve growth factor monoclonal antibodies, intra-articular therapies, and nutraceuticals. title: Catalyzing Halal Industry Development in a Non-Muslim Society: The Role of Indonesian Muslim Diaspora in South Korea
abstract: The rapid expansion of the global halal industry has created opportunities for halal ecosystem development in non-Muslim societies. In South Korea, however, halal industry growth faces challenges related to limited infrastructure, fragmented certification systems, and social stigma toward Islam and halal practices. This study examines the role of the Indonesian Muslim diaspora in catalyzing halal industry development in South Korea. abstract: ABSTRACT Most cyanobacterial genomes are rich in the GCGATCGC octamer, also known as Highly Iterated Palindrome 1 (HIP1). Despite its description over three decades ago, the biological function of this highly abundant sequence is only beginning to be elucidated. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la administración tributaria ha trastocado la gestión del riesgo tributario y ha brindado a los órganos de control del gasto público herramientas de predicción masiva y de análisis de datos. abstract: Lesotho has enacted the Lesotho Inclusive Education Policy (LIEP) to guide the conduct of inclusive education. However, the extent of the implementation of the policy on inclusive schooling in the rural communities of Lesotho is yet to be ascertained. Two research questions were raised and answered in this qualitative study. The study adopted the bioecological system theory as a theoretical lens. abstract: Dryland pastoral systems are increasingly affected by the interrelation between socioenvironmental variability and change with land degradation. In Mexico, goat pastoralism (CaprinoCultura) represents a key social-ecological system (SES) that sustains rural livelihoods under highly constrained conditions. abstract: Despite growing interest in virtual reality (VR) in heritage tourism contexts, empirical evidence on its value beyond single-use applications across the customer journey remains limited. This research examines the effectiveness of VR across the visit and post-visit stages of the tourism customer journey and their interrelated effects across successive stages. title: Integrating heat stress tolerance indices based on grain yield for the selection of resilient wheat genotypes
abstract: Wheat productivity is threatened by terminal heat stress, which hampers yields 6-10% per 1 °C above optimal temperatures during grain filling. Although heat stress tolerance indices offer objective selection criteria, their individual effectiveness varies with genetic background and environment. This study evaluated 230 diverse bread wheat genotypes across six environments (three locations × two seasons, 2021-23) under timely- and late-sown conditions to identify heat-tolerant germplasm using an integrated multivariate framework. title: Rethinking intraspecific diagnostics in Lymantria dispar: from traditional taxonomy to population genomics
abstract: The spongy moth, Lymantria dispar , provides a compelling example of how advances in genomic methods can reshape the practical interpretation of intraspecific taxonomy. Historically, geographic forms of this species were differentiated on the basis of morphology, geographic range, and female flight capability; subsequently, a three-subspecies framework comprising L. d. dispar, L. d. asiatica , and L. d. japonica became widely adopted. title: If you think twice, you might not forget: inhibition and memory-maintenance trade-offs in Russian single vs. Hausa bipartite negation
abstract: Several approaches have attempted to explain the skewed distribution across languages and regions of bipartite compared to single negation, the latter unequivocally the most common, but still often subject to diachronic change. It is a paradox that double negation arises, among other things, to strengthen negation semantically or define its scope, while at the same time, this fortification may lead to its demise. Several grammaticalization pathways result in double, discontinuous negation typologies negating single events or constituents, but such constructions seem to be inherently unstable.

abstract: The study focuses on investigating the asymmetry and moon cycle effects of the Vietnam stock index (VN-Index) return series by estimating extended GARCH models. The data used are the daily closing prices of the VN-Index traded on the Vietnam stock market on the HoSE from 2000 to 2024, with a total of 1129 trading days. title: Comparing Indonesian Patent Law Enforcement with Malaysia, Singapore, and Germany System
abstract: Patent enforcement is a critical element in ensuring legal certainty, enhancing innovation, and strengthening a technology-based investment climate. However, patent enforcement practices in Indonesia continue to face significant structural and institutional challenges. This article identifies three principal issues: the limited institutional capacity of the Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DGIP), prolonged patent dispute resolution processes, and the lack of adequate technical expertise within judicial proceedings. title: Precision Fermentation for Next Generation Food Ingredients: Technological Foundations, Food Applications, Sustainability, and Regulatory Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Precision fermentation has emerged as one of the most transformative approaches in contemporary food biotechnology, enabling the targeted production of high‐value food ingredients through engineered microorganisms. abstract: ABSTRACT Sleep is an essential yet costly biological process, leaving animals vulnerable to predation and constraining their use of space and time. Optimal sleeping sites therefore represent valuable, potentially contested resources, yet they remain largely overlooked in primate community ecology. title: Loneliness in women’s experiences in a wartime context
abstract: In the context of a full-scale war, the relevance of research into women’s loneliness takes on a new significance, shaped by profound personal and psychological changes within society, the consequences of which have implications for both the resilience of the social environment and Ukraine’s overall safety. The aim of the study was to identify the levels, forms, types and nature of women’s experiences of loneliness across different age groups during wartime, and to establish whether this state represents a need, an involuntary consequence or an adaptive necessity. abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrasound‐induced luminescence (UL) converts mechanical energy into optical signals and has significant potential applications in multi‐parameter sensing, bioimaging, and nondestructive evaluation. abstract: Abstract While the Vicsek model is widely used to understand active systems, the explicit relationship between structural evolution and the order transition remains an open question. Here we investigate this relationship in the original Vicsek system. abstract: ABSTRACT Low cost, bio‐based, and biodegradable macromolecular thermoplastic starch (TPS) is widely blended with poly(butylene adipate co‐terephthalate) (PBAT) to reduce material cost in agricultural films and food packaging. However, this approach often leads to a significant deterioration in overall performance, especially at higher TPS loading. abstract: ABSTRACT Electrostatic complexation of oppositely charged biomacromolecules produces a spectrum of condensed phases, from liquid coacervates to ordered solids. title: From sustainable tourism attitudes to green purchasing behavior: the mediating role of moral intention among Generation Z
abstract: Introduction Although Generation Z (Gen Z) is widely regarded as the most environmentally engaged cohort in the tourism market, favorable sustainability attitudes do not reliably translate into green purchasing behavior. title: Psychometric properties of the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS): An item response theory and classical test theory analysis
abstract: Over the past two decades, social networking services have become a pervasive and integral part of young adults’ lives. In this context, the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) was developed to assess problematic social media use (PSMU). title: Public traceability of university co-creation and collaborative governance for sustainability. A documentary audit of Ecuadorian higher education
abstract: Introduction This study examines the public visibility and documentary traceability of university co-creation and collaborative governance for sustainability, based on documentary evidence available on the institutional portals of a set of universities in Ecuador. It explores how publicly available records represent forms of territorial articulation that extend beyond traditional university extension models. abstract: Introduction Climate change impacts are not gender-neutral, yet standard reporting relies on aggregate household indicators that obscure intra-household power dynamics and diverse individual vulnerabilities. This review assesses gender-differentiated climate resilience in rural farming households and evaluates the extent to which empirical evidence aligns with the gender-responsive, participatory and transparent mandates of the Paris Agreement. abstract: This paper presents an integrated techno-economic synthesis for selecting pole-mounted off-grid photovoltaic configurations, consolidating six experimental and analytical studies into a unified multicriteria decision framework. The analysis is grounded in a one-year high-resolution outdoor experimentation (Aug. 25, 2025 – Aug. 24, 2026) at the QEERI Outdoor Test Facility in Doha, Qatar, complemented by validated analytical models addressing environmental and structural constraints. title: Integrating a soil temperature module into AquaCrop improves simulation of crop growth and yield under straw mulching
abstract: Introduction Straw mulching is a core practice in conservation agriculture, improving the soil hydrothermal environment, enhancing water-use efficiency, and increasing crop yield, and is widely regarded as an environmentally friendly and sustainable mulching technique. However, most existing crop models simplify or neglect mulch-induced regulation of soil temperature and water processes, thereby limiting their capacity for system-level assessment of crop growth and water dynamics under mulched conditions. abstract: The vadose zone plays a vital role in sustaining society and ecosystems on the Earth. The complexity of vadose zones, coupled with expensive and laborious field investigations pose a formidable challenge in their characterization, and hence they are neglected in hydrogeologic studies. This study demonstrates a novel scientific framework for the grid-scale hydraulic characterization of vadose zones using the laser diffraction (LD) technique and grain-size analysis (GSA) models. title: A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security research
abstract: Abstract Background Climate change has become a global concern, influencing water resources, food security, public health, and societal progress worldwide. Floods, droughts, and irregular monsoons, as manifestations of climate change, adversely affect crops, farmers' livelihoods, and food security. A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security (CCFS) research can indicate progress and emerging research directions on adaptation and risk-management practices, supporting farmers, policymakers, and investors in decision-making. abstract: Assessing metal(loid) distribution in agricultural systems is critical for environmental monitoring and food safety. This study investigated nutrients and trace metal(loid)s in soil profiles (0–30 cm depth) under oolong tea plant cultivation for varying periods (0.5, 3, 6, and 10 years) and their corresponding harvested tea leaves. abstract: Este estudio examina las conductas disruptivas en niños de 6 a 8 años de la Unidad Educativa Abdón Calderón, ubicada en Guayaquil, Guayas, Ecuador, y su influencia en el rendimiento académico. title: Sensory regimes of gentrification: urban transformation, embodied experience, and neoliberal spatial production in Cihangir
abstract: Gentrification has predominantly been examined through economic restructuring, demographic change, and spatial reorganization, while its sensory and embodied dimensions remain underexplored in urban sociology. This study reconceptualizes gentrification as a multi-layered urban transformation regime operating not only through material and economic change but also through the reconfiguration of sensory urban experience. title: Cuidar con máquinas: Tensiones y significados del tecnocuidado en la era digital
abstract: Este artículo analiza cómo profesionales de la medicina, la sociología y la informática conceptualizan el tecnocuidado a partir de entrevistas en profundidad. Se identifican tres ejes clave: la relación humano-máquina, la desinstitucionalización del cuidado y las tensiones entre vigilancia, autonomía y privacidad. abstract: Non-ribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPS) are multi-modular enzymes that produce secondary metabolites. The diverse and functionally important biosurfactants derived from various microbes have numerous applications across multiple industries. Probiotic-derived biosurfactants, especially those from bacteria classified as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS), are emerging as eco-friendly alternatives to synthetic surfactants. title: Microfluidic fabrication of lipid-coated PLGA nanoparticles co-delivering CuS and curcumin for combined chemo-photothermal therapy
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, with chemotherapy serving as a primary treatment modality. However, its clinical efficacy is often compromised by systemic toxicity, poor drug solubility, and non-specific targeting. To address these limitations, we report the fabrication of lipid-coated poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) co-delivering curcumin (Cur) and copper sulfide (CuS) for combined chemo-photothermal therapy using a microfluidic swirl mixer. title: Dopamine release in the medullary reticular formation is related to locomotor velocity
abstract: Dopamine is classically recognized for modulating locomotion through basal ganglia circuits. However, it also modulates motor circuits in the brainstem and spinal cord. The medullary reticular formation (MRF) integrates supraspinal motor commands and relays them to the spinal cord, yet the role of dopamine in this region is poorly understood. title: A community-level view of Wolbachia DNA positivity across mosquito assemblages in eastern China
abstract: Wolbachia is a widespread mosquito-associated endosymbiont with important implications for vector biology and microbial ecology. However, field studies often examine Wolbachia within individual mosquito species, which can obscure how host community structure shapes the microbial signal observed at a sampling site. Here, we analyzed Wolbachia DNA positivity in a taxonomically curated collection of 2,434 mosquitoes from Huai'an, Lu'an, and Xuzhou in eastern China. abstract: This quantitative correlational study sought to ascertain whether and to what degree Royal University of Law and Economics (RULE) student-directed learning experiences among undergraduate studnets in Cambodia were associated with their satisfaction and engagement. Constructivism and situated learning theory served as the study’s guiding principles. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a free‐final‐time sensitivity‐based pseudospectral constrained guidance algorithm for terminal‐speed maximization under control input constraints. abstract: Meat quality and carcass traits are amongst the reasons why native chickens are popular amongst consumers and it is important that these traits are not lost when improving their growth performance through crossbreeding with fast growing breeds. abstract: ABSTRACT Subtropical forests, particularly the Araucaria Forest, host tree species of both temperate and tropical origins that exhibit contrasting ecological strategies, which may shift across ontogenetic stages. abstract: Abstract Ramadi District, the capital of Al-Anbar Governorate in western Iraq, faces a severe shortage and unbalanced distribution of sports facilities—a challenge common to many post-conflict and rapidly urbanizing cities in developing countries. This study aimed to analyze the spatial distribution of existing sports facilities and identify optimal locations for new ones using an integrated GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making approach. title: Climate shocks, disability, and mathematics learning in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Climate shocks already disrupt schooling in sub-Saharan Africa. Children with disabilities, for their part, face deep barriers to enrolment, retention and achievement across the region. A smaller body of work suggests that climate shocks in early childhood may also raise the number of children who become disabled. abstract: ABSTRACT Rising multidrug resistance demands novel antimicrobials. Lantibiotics are ribosomally synthesized peptides with unique post‐translational modifications (including lanthionine) that confer potent bactericidal activity against Gram‐positive species. Their membrane‐disruptive and cellular inhibitory mechanisms make them promising candidates for next‐generation antibiotics to combat escalating antibiotic resistance. abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). abstract: Citrus production across growing regions is increasingly exposed to rising atmospheric CO 2 , higher temperatures, and greater variability in water availability, with Mediterranean orchards facing particularly pronounced climatic pressures. These climatic drivers affect citrus performance through interconnected changes in photosynthesis, root functioning, flowering, salinity responses, redox regulation, and source–sink relationships, with consequences for productivity and fruit quality. abstract: Phaeocollybia is a globally distributed agaricoid genus and remains poorly studied in China. In this study, field surveys were conducted, and specimens of Phaeocollybia were collected in Yunnan Province and the Xizang Autonomous Region of southwestern China from 2024 to 2025. abstract: Introduction Understanding the foundations of public trust in law enforcement is critical for effective governance, particularly in non-Western contexts. While procedural justice theory has received growing empirical attention in China, existing studies have produced mixed findings and largely neglected the combined influence of interactional experiences, neighborhood environmental conditions, and institutionally embedded factors on police legitimacy perceptions. abstract: We study statistical properties of atmospheric particulate matter fluctuations using six years of daily PM2.5 concentration data from fifty-four Indian cities. abstract: Crops aimed at nourishing an exponentially increasing population are frequently vulnerable to a diversity of adverse ecological conditions. Due to climate change, extreme events including flooding, droughts, heat, and frost are expected to further upsurge in the future. abstract: Multidrug-resistant and carbapenem-resistant Serratia marcescens ( S. marcescens ) infections are increasingly difficult to treat because of intrinsic and acquired antimicrobial-resistance mechanisms, limited therapeutic options, and the organism’s capacity to persist within biofilms. Phage therapy has therefore emerged as a potential precision antimicrobial strategy against refractory S. marcescens infections. abstract: Abstract The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising technologies for sustainable power generation, offering high electrical efficiency, fuel flexibility and minimal pollutant emissions. Environmental performance of SOFC systems is influenced by operational efficiency, upstream fuel generation, manufacturing, system integration, and end‐of‐life management. abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. abstract: Formal participation in village budget planning does not necessarily ensure equitable influence over budget priorities. This study examines weaknesses in the budget planning process in Nagari Salayo, Solok Regency, West Sumatra, and identifies opportunities to integrate social equity. abstract: Mesoscopic fluctuations reveal stochastic dynamics of molecules in both inanimate and living matter. abstract: This article interrogates the Chinese state’s pursuit of ontological security (OS) through the Sinicisation of history, conceptualised as narrative self-grasping. abstract: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. abstract: Abstract Salinity is a major abiotic stressor limiting crop production globally. abstract: Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand experience high infertility rates yet low use of assisted reproductive technology services. This qualitative study explored healthcare professionals’ experiences of delivering fertility care to Pacific patients. abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. abstract: Schistosomiasis is major neglected tropical disease of humans that is caused by trematodes in the genus Schistosoma. abstract: Freight transport is central to economic vitality, yet a major source of congestion, emissions, and social externalities. title: Unpacking Modern Slavery in Business Research: Conceptualization and Operationalization
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the tragic humanitarian impact of modern slavery, modern slavery research is underdeveloped and advancing slowly. Theoretical studies abound, while there are few quantitative studies with large‐scale empirical evidence to test theory. We review the literature to better understand how modern slavery has been defined and measured. We find a wide discrepancy among conceptual definitions of modern slavery. Only a few studies operationalize (measure) modern slavery. To aid conceptual clarity, we develop a tentative business‐related definition of modern slavery based on our review.

abstract: Soil salinization threatens global agricultural sustainability and may elevate soil-borne disease risk through coordinated changes in soil conditions and the rhizosphere microbiome, yet long-term field evidence remains limited. Here, a 19-year controlled field experiment with an artificial salinity gradient (non-saline, moderate, and severe) was conducted to characterise salinity-associated responses of soil physicochemical properties, wheat crown rot (WCR), and the rhizosphere microbiome. abstract: Background and Aims Wildfires can cause substantial changes in vegetation condition and ecosystem structure, making rapid and reliable post-fire assessment essential for environmental management. This study evaluated vegetation change, burn severity, and short-term post-fire response following the 2025 Palisades Fire in California, USA. abstract: Introduction The presence of lead ions in water bodies represents a persistent environmental problem due to their toxicity, mobility, and bioaccumulation capacity, which demands the development of efficient and sustainable treatment alternatives. title: Linking rain-on-snow events to river floods in the Tianshan Mountains
abstract: Rain-on-snow (ROS) events are widely recognized as an important cryosphere–hydrology coupling mechanism, yet when and where ROS events translate into river floods remains poorly constrained, particularly in arid high-mountain regions. abstract: Background Malnutrition and inadequate oral intake are common during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), yet little is known about how patients perceive and experience nutrition management during transplant-unit hospitalization. Objective To explore Chinese HSCT patients' perceptions and experiences of nutrition management during transplant-unit hospitalization. title: From electrode swelling to structural integration: a quantitative electro-chemo-mechanical framework for electric-vehicle batteries
abstract: Electro-chemo-mechanical coupling is well established in electric-vehicle batteries, yet its translation from electrode behavior to pack- and vehicle-level performance remains difficult. This mini-review organizes the evidence around five transferable descriptors: electrode/cell swelling, contact or stack pressure, stiffness and strength, mechanical-abuse tolerance, and inactive structural mass or volume. abstract: Introduction Developing functional foods with high bioactivity often compromises sensory characteristics, making optimization essential. Methods This study evaluated the functional composition, antioxidant activity, vitamin content, microbiological safety, sensory acceptability, and phenolic bioaccessibility during simulated gastrointestinal digestion of a pumpkin–apple–honey–walnut appetizer enriched with 1%–5% of rosehip extract or powder. title: On the satellite constellation launching techniques and their implications for spacecraft structural design
abstract: The rise in the deployment of low Earth orbit satellite constellations has reshaped the space utilization landscape, driving unprecedented demand for multi-satellite launches. This trend arises from the growing need for low-latency global connectivity, high resolution observation and more accurate navigation services. In this context, this article provides a critical review of current and emerging strategies for large-scale deployment of satellites, with a particular focus on their implications for spacecraft configuration and structural design. abstract: Objetivo: Determinar la prevalencia de sarcopenia oculta en pacientes con diabetes mellitus tipo 2 (DM2) y obesidad, y evaluar el rendimiento diagnóstico del índice de masa corporal (IMC) para su detección. title: Innate immunity and antibiotic activity in resistant bacterial infections in immunocompromised hosts
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is particularly difficult to manage in immunocompromised hosts, in whom impaired bacterial containment and clearance can coexist with restricted treatment options, altered drug exposure, and anatomically complex infection sites. Susceptibility testing and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) assessment guide antibiotic treatment, while host defenses help determine whether injured bacteria are cleared. title: Guiding Lights of Literacy: The Role of Leadership and Policy in Educational Journey Among Elementary Schools of Benguet
abstract: This study investigates the role of leadership and policy in sustaining literacy excellence among elementary schools in Benguet Province, Philippines. Literacy is recognized as a cornerstone of lifelong learning, equity, and national development, yet challenges remain in translating national policies into effective school-level practices. title: How personality traits and cultural value orientation moderate the pathway from musical emotional expression to group cohesion in choral rehearsal
abstract: Introduction Choral singing is widely valued for building cohesion in community, educational, and well-being settings, yet the route by which emotional expression during rehearsal becomes group cohesion remains poorly specified, and most work still centers on individual feeling rather than on group-level interaction. Grounded in emotional contagion and social identity theory, this study proposes and tests a dual-moderated mediation model. abstract: Exposure to environmental stressors such as heat and air pollution is rising in urban areas, placing soft mobility users (e.g., pedestrians, cyclists, and scooter riders) at particular risk—a challenge that will only intensify with climate change. abstract: BACKGROUND: Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. title: Dialogue Act Script: A Structured Framework for Generating Multilingual and Multicultural Dialogues
abstract: Non-English dialogue datasets are scarce, and models are often trained or evaluated on translations of English-language dialogues, an approach which can introduce artifacts that reduce their naturalness and cultural appropriateness. abstract: Abstract. Sugarcane (Saccharum spp.), an economically important crop in the food and bioenergy industries, has historically played a central role in the economy of Cuba, shaping its agricultural landscape and international relations. Although production has declined in recent decades, sugarcane remains a strategic crop, with its byproducts contributing to national energy and industrial outputs. abstract: After more than two decades of implementing the Special Autonomy policy, Papua continues to lag behind other regions in Indonesia in terms of development. The complex legal, political, and human rights context, combined with the region's diverse social, economic, cultural, environmental, and natural resource characteristics, poses significant challenges to the implementation of current approaches. abstract: Introduction To improve health for all demographics in our society, we need a diverse biomedical research workforce in which those affected by health disparities are in positions of power to prioritize and solve preventable differences in health outcomes across various populations. abstract: Introduction Standard environmental risk assessment frameworks, such as the OECD 236 Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity (FET) test, rely heavily on macroscopic morphological endpoints that may fail to detect subtle, sublethal molecular disruptions before phenotypic damage becomes apparent. Mechanism-based biomarkers capable of ultra-early toxicity prediction are therefore needed. abstract: ABSTRACT Nanotechnology has evolved from empirical traditional material practices to a highly advanced field based on the controlled design and manipulation of matter at the nanoscale. abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon carbide (SiC) and its composite variants are gaining significant traction in the semiconductor and aerospace sectors, owing to their outstanding mechanical strength, large bandgap, excellent thermal resilience, and strong resistance to radiation. However, these same properties make SiC extremely difficult to process using conventional machining techniques, which often result in low material removal efficiency, severe subsurface damage, and excessive tool wear. abstract: Owl pellets provide a valuable, non-invasive tool for documenting small mammal assemblages, particularly in areas lacking systematic faunal surveys. Fourteen phenolic compounds were quantified by HPLC, while total phenolic content (TPC), FRAP, and DPPH radical-scavenging assays were used to assess antioxidant-related properties. abstract: In West Africa, legume trees are widely used by agro-pastoralists to enhance livestock productivity, yet their potential to mitigate enteric methane (eCH₄) remains insufficiently documented. abstract: Abstract. The Liang–Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF) framework has been increasingly used to identify causality in Earth–system dynamics in recent years. abstract: The current research aimed to develop and validate a novel measurement scale, the Motivation for Cognitive Activities Questionnaire (MCAQ), specifically designed to assess individuals’ motivation to engage in everyday cognitive activities. abstract: Riverine flooding poses a significant risk to residential properties worldwide, with climate change exacerbating its frequency and intensity. Although flood-resilient retrofitting (FRR) is increasingly recognized as a mitigation measure for reducing flood damage, its implementation remains low. While existing research has identified numerous FRR implementation barriers, these are often fragmented and lack theoretical integration. title: Impacts of shrub coverage for arctic ecosystem carbon uptake and storage
abstract: Abstract. Although shrubs employ distinct water- and carbon-use strategies compared to trees and are increasingly expanding across warming tundra and grassland, they remain insufficiently represented in global land surface models. Here, we incorporated two shrub types, deciduous and evergreen, into the nutrient-enabled terrestrial biosphere model QUINCY, which features a state-of-the-art treatment of soil nutrient dynamics and carbon exchange. title: Fire and Carbon Dynamics: A Global Review of Knowledge and Gaps Across Biomes
abstract: Abstract Purpose of review Fire is a major driver of terrestrial carbon (C) cycling, rapidly releasing carbon accumulated over decades to millennia and reshaping ecosystem structure and function across biomes. As climate change intensifies fire regimes, understanding fire-induced changes in C stocks and fluxes is increasingly urgent. abstract: This study examined data collection and processing methods and sustainable supply chain management among logistics operators in Lagos State, Nigeria. Specifically, it identified and ranked data collection and processing methods, ranked the economic, environmental, social and operational dimensions of sustainable supply chain management, and assessed whether data collection and processing methods significantly predicted sustainable supply chain management. abstract: Abstract Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the larval stage (metacestode) of Echinococcus multilocularis, is an emerging zoonotic disease with limited treatment options, highlighting the need for new therapeutic targets. Like other helminths, E. multilocularis relies on anaerobic metabolism via malate dismutation, a poorly characterized pathway. abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. title: Drought modulates soil hydraulic, biological, and physicochemical responses to one-off tillage in a long-term cover-cropped Mediterranean vineyard
abstract: Sustainable soil management is a crucial factor to maintain soil health and long-term functionality in vineyards. In Mediterranean climates, cover crops have become a sustainable alternative to conventional tillage due to their positive effects on soil structure, water retention, and biological activity. abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and serious games have demonstrated growing potential in physical therapy, exergaming, and the promotion of physical activity across diverse patient populations. abstract: Dermal bone, the earliest known form of bone, develops without a cartilage precursor and persists in extant fish species. abstract: Abstract Despite revolutionary advances in immunotherapy and targeted therapies, tumor recurrence driven by minimal residual disease (MRD) and drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells remains a critical challenge in oncology. MRD, a reservoir of residual cancer cells undetectable by conventional imaging but identifiable via sensitive molecular techniques like next-generation sequencing and ctDNA analysis, serves as a prognostic biomarker for relapse across hematologic and solid malignancies. abstract: BACKGROUND: Speech and orofacial functions (breathing, swallowing, and chewing) both develop within the stomatognathic system and share common anatomical structures and motor control mechanisms. abstract: Purpose This review paper critically synthesizes contemporary scholarship on dark tourism, integrating conceptual foundations, visitor motivations, management practices, ethical dilemmas, sustainability challenges, and emerging research directions. abstract: Introduction This study explores, from a phenomenological perspective, how cryptocurrency investors experience emotional, cognitive, and social processes in an uncertain environment and how these experiences influence decision-making, risk management, and identity perception. Methods This qualitative phenomenological study involved semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 19 participants selected through criterion sampling. title: Genome-wide association study and candidate gene prioritization for stem architectural traits in Tartary buckwheat
abstract: Stem architecture is a key determinant of lodging resistance, yield potential, and mechanical harvestability in Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ), yet the genetic basis of stem-related traits remains poorly understood. abstract: This conceptual analysis argues that aesthetic values in AI-mediated visual culture are socially constructed and shaped by power relations rather than being universally shared or psychologically neutral. Visual content is now produced, circulated, and evaluated within socio-technical systems governed by platform infrastructures, algorithmic recommendation mechanisms, and data-driven optimization logic. title: Green public facilities and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective
abstract: Background This study conceptualizes green public facilities as green-space resources embedded in urban public-resource allocation and examines the relationship between their spatial distribution and residents’ health from a socio-spatial perspective. Methods Data on 6,871 respondents from the 2021 Chinese General Social Survey were linked to green public facility and public transport point-of-interest data and statistical indicators for 82 districts/counties. title: Media and Digital Imperialism
abstract: This text introduces the Special Issue “Imperialism, Information, Communication, and Culture in the Phase of Digitalisation”. It argues that digitalisation reconfigures, rather than replaces, the foundations of imperialism. It briefly revisits the historical emergence of imperialism, examines how digital platforms reconfigure media imperialism, and summarises theoretical approaches to the relationship between imperialism and digital technologies. Finally, it presents the contributions gathered in the Special Issue.

title: A four-decadal (1981–2024) quality-assured ground-based soybean phenology dataset from Northeast China: a FAIR-compliant resource for climate impact and agricultural adaptation studies
abstract: Although satellite remote sensing has been widely used to monitor land surface phenology, long-term, high-quality ground-based observations are essential for validating and calibrating these products, particularly for understanding agricultural ecosystem responses to climate change. However, such ground-truth datasets remain scarce, limiting the full potential of Earth system data applications. Here we present a comprehensive ground-based soybean phenology dataset for Northeast China, a region critical to national food security. title: Mental Health Literacy, Positive Mental Health, and Help-Seeking Intention Among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Correlational Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mental health literacy (MHL) is considered an important resource for promoting mental health, facilitating the recognition of mental health problems, reducing stigma, and encouraging appropriate help-seeking behaviours. Among undergraduate nursing students, MHL may also be associated with positive mental health and a greater willingness to seek professional support when needed. This study aimed to examine the associations between mental health literacy, positive mental health, and help-seeking intention among undergraduate nursing students. Methods: A correlational study

title: Assessing changes in electrical resistivity signals in simulated mass and single graves over 18 months after burial
abstract: Abstract Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) has been increasingly explored as a non‐destructive technique for searching for unmarked graves. However, its effectiveness remains uncertain as measured resistivity responses are influenced by burial type, time after burial, soil properties and environmental conditions. Previous studies have reported both positive and negative resistivity anomalies associated with graves, highlighting the need for further controlled investigations. title: Distinct Molecular Relationships and Partial Pathway Convergence of Anserine and RRR-α-Tocopherol in Human Diabetic Kidney Disease
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) involves interacting metabolic, inflammatory, vascular, and fibrotic disturbances. This study investigated the molecular relationships of anserine and RRR-α-tocopherol with human DKD using a disease-centered computational framework in which compound-target evidence was established independently before integration with kidney transcriptomic data. title: Early career challenges of physical education teachers
abstract: Introduction Early career physical education teachers face challenges similar to those of other novice teachers, in addition to field-specific difficulties. Their professional adjustment depends on the interaction between personal psychological and pedagogical resources and the workplace demands. Successfully navigating this process and ensuring adequate socio-institutional support are essential for career development and sustained professional practice. title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes
abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. abstract: How protein sequences evolve to maintain functional conformational dynamics under thermal stress remains an important question in molecular evolution. Thermophilic enzymes are often considered to achieve stability primarily through enhanced structural rigidity, yet thermal adaptation may also involve the preservation or reorganization of correlated motions across the protein scaffold. title: An Examination of the "Addiction and Addiction Prevention" Course Using Activity-Based Teaching Methods: A Qualitative Study
abstract: This study aimed to examine prospective educators’ experiences, perspectives, and perceived competencies regarding activity-based instructional practices implemented throughout an undergraduate "Addiction and Addiction Prevention” course. The study employed a qualitative descriptive design utilizing inductive thematic analysis. The study group comprised a complete cohort of 55 undergraduate students (100% participation rate) enrolled in the course and meeting predefined inclusion criteria at a public university in Turkey during the 2025–2026 academic year. title: Indonesia’s Palm Oil Trilemma: Reconciling Biodiesel Expansion, Export Competitiveness, and Supply Resilience under Climate and Governance Constraints
abstract: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative literature review examines the resulting policy trilemma using peer-reviewed research published during 2020-2026 and the IPOSS fourth-quarter 2026 industry outlook as a contextual, explicitly prospective source. title: Institutional dynamics of circular and climate-adaptive water governance in Bengaluru
abstract: Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change threaten global urban water security, with projections indicating that over 1 billion urban residents will face water short ages. In many Global South cities, water crises are infrastructural as well as institutional challenges rather than merely hydrological ones, yet city-level analyses of these institutional barriers remain scarce. title: Acoustical Materials from Conventional to Cutting-Edge Innovations─An Overview
abstract: Abstract With rapid urbanization and industrial expansion, noise pollution has escalated into a pervasive environmental and public health crisis. Thus, an imperative need arises for both advanced sound mitigation strategies and, especially, a fundamental shift toward sustainability to meet pressing worldwide environmental policies. title: Solenostemma argel Dead Leaves as an Eco‐Friendly and Low‐Cost Adsorbent for Effective Removal of Methylene Blue From Aqueous Media: Adsorption Performance and Mechanism
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable, low‐cost adsorbents derived from agricultural waste are needed for the removal of toxic dyes from contaminated water. Solenostemma argel dead leaves (SAL) were evaluated as a biosorbent for methylene blue (MB) removal from contaminated water. SAL was characterized by x‐ray diffraction (XRD), N 2 adsorption–desorption (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species
abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds—including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules—that may modulate gut microbiota–host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.

title: Wildfire severity reshapes soil organic carbon fractions and stabilization pathways in a subalpine forest
abstract: Introduction Wildfire disturbance is a major driver of soil carbon cycling in subalpine forests, yet differential responses of soil organic carbon fractions to fire severity remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated a subalpine forest in northwestern Sichuan, China, 6 years after wildfire. Four fire-severity classes were established: unburned control (UB), low-severity fire (LSF), moderate-severity fire (MSF), and high-severity fire (HSF). abstract: Most rock art research has been influenced by David Lewis-Williams. In addition, his recognition of the impact of ‘critical, radical thought’ on our practice. title: Recent Advances in LDH‐Based Sorbents for Wastewater Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorption is an efficient and environmentally benign technique for wastewater treatment. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are low‐cost materials with high adsorption capacities for a wide array of pollutants. This review comprehensively summarizes recent studies on the adsorption of dyes, metal ions, inorganic anions, and organic contaminants using LDH‐based materials. abstract: Schrenk’s spruce ( Picea schrenkiana ) is a dominant coniferous tree species in the Western Tian Shan forests and plays an important ecological role in maintaining mountain forest ecosystems in Kyrgyzstan. In recent years, the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve has seen a significant increase in diseased and declining spruce trees, raising concerns about forest health and ecosystem stability. abstract: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar la eficacia de la aplicación profesional de barniz de fluoruro de sodio al 5 % en la prevención de caries dental y en la reducción de la hipersensibilidad dentinaria en comparación con un placebo. abstract: Abstract Far-right political shifts have been linked to increased racism, raising concerns about their impact on minority access to public services. This study investigates whether far-right electoral victories encourage discrimination by street-level bureaucrats, who are expected to act impartially. title: Factors influencing elderly people’s intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research
abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. abstract: India is among the most entomophagically diverse countries in the world. Despite this biological resource, India has not converted its edible arthropod tradition into a regulated protein sector. abstract: Peer learning and dialogic pedagogy are well established in Higher Education research but remain underutilized in MBA education, where transmissive and expert-centered formats continue to dominate. This article examines the World Café method as a structured dialogic peer-learning architecture within an MBA sustainability and responsible leadership module at a UK business school. abstract: Grounded in Vygotsky's cultural-historical paradigm, this article presents a theoretical analysis of the role of thematic social role-play in preschool psychological development, positioning it not merely as a recreational activity but as the leading activity driving psychological maturation. abstract: Accurate quantification of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture is critical for establishing credible baselines, identifying emission hotspots, and prioritizing mitigation strategies. In Kenya, most agricultural emission estimates have relied on nationally aggregated activity data and Tier 1 emission factors, which limit the representation of spatial heterogeneity and management effects. abstract: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited investment in new capacity since 2018. abstract: Background Weed management in transplanted rice requires effective herbicide delivery while improving input-use efficiency and reducing reliance on conventional application practices. This study developed and evaluated a biodegradable gelatin capsule-based herbicide delivery system, subsequently protected through a design patent, as an alternative approach for herbicide application. abstract: Cableless power transmission—the transfer of electrical energy through free space rather than a conductor—now spans commodity near-field chargers, standardized electric-vehicle (EV) charging, kilometre-scale microwave and laser beaming, and in-orbit tests of space-based solar power. OBJECTIVES: To develop the first Inter-American Consensus on HCM, in order to standardize the care of these patients tailored to the regional context. abstract: Abstract In this review, we synthesize evidence to argue that climate change and conflict are mutually reinforcing. We first examine conflict as a barrier to mitigation, focusing on four faultlines that slow climate action: (a) ideological polarization, (b) “elite versus ordinary people” narratives, (c) intranational, place‐based conflicts, and (d) international disputes. abstract: Obesity and its associated diseases represent one of the most urgent public health crises of our time, affecting billions worldwide. Current pharmacological agents, such as GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, have demonstrated high clinical efficacy in diabetes and weight management. However, the required lifelong medication is often limited by high economic costs and severe side effects, including gastrointestinal complications. abstract: Introduction Climate change poses significant challenges to open-field production of okra ( Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) This study evaluated the effects of light-emitting diode (LED) spectral quality on reproductive development, fruit characteristics, yield, mineral composition, antioxidant activity, and total phenolic content of okra. abstract: Recurrent pulmonary infection (RPI) refers to the frequent and repeated episodes of lower respiratory tract infections. title: Stabilizing perovskite solar cells for space applications
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offer transformative potential for space photovoltaics with exceptional specific power (up to 50,000 W/kg without encapsulation), tunable bandgaps for high-efficiency tandems (> 35% for perovskite/Si, > 31% for all-perovskite), intrinsic radiation self-healing and low-temperature solution processing. These attributes enable dramatic reductions in launch mass and cost for satellite constellations, space stations, orbital computing centers, space solar power station (SSPS) and deep-space probes. However, the extreme space environment: high-temperature illumination (

title: Rethinking avian influenza control: a systems-oriented One Health perspective for family poultry
abstract: Early detection and control of high- and low-pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI, LPAI) in family poultry flocks remain challenging in settings where mortality from enzootic diseases such as Newcastle disease (ND) and infectious bursal disease (IBD) is persistently high. High background mortality obscures recognition of unusual disease events and delays reporting. In addition to epidemiological constraints, rebuilding trust among family poultry producers, particularly those affected by uncompensated culling during previous HPAI outbreaks, is essential for effective control. Locally grounded, p
institutions: Chattogram Veterinary and Animal Sciences University

title: Ecological dynamics of gut bacteriophages in food animal production systems: Mechanisms of microbiome modulation and implications for livestock health and production
abstract: Gut bacteriophages (phages) are the most diverse and abundant component of the enteric virome in food-producing animals, and act as core modulators of intestinal microbial community structure and function, with important implications for livestock health and production performance. Predominantly colonizing the intestinal mucus layer, phages mediate dynamic interactions with bacterial hosts and shape gut microecological homeostasis. title: Sustainable desulfurization through coupled extraction-catalytic oxidation strategy: Mechanisms, materials, and process intensification
abstract: In response to the imperative for sustainable energy and environmental protection, ultra-deep desulfurization of fuels poses a critical challenge. Conventional hydrodesulfurization and emerging non-hydrogenation techniques face limitations in efficiency, economic viability, and ecological sustainability, particularly for refractory sulfur species. Among alternatives, extractive catalytic oxidative desulfurization (ECODS) has emerged as a prominent approach by integrating catalytic oxidation and liquid-phase extraction under mild conditions. It employs green solvents such as ionic liquids and d

title: Cover crop management influences soil properties and grapevine performance across three growing seasons in a subtropical vineyard
abstract: Cover crop management can modify soil conditions and grapevine performance, but these responses may depend on the vegetation-management strategy and growing season. This study evaluated the effects of different cover crop management systems on soil, physiological, yield, and fruit technological variables of Vitis vinifera L. cv. Viognier cultivated in Campo Largo, Paraná, Brazil, for three growing seasons (2023–2026; 2023/24, 2024/25, and 2025/26). The treatments were: T1, spontaneous vegetation (white clover in winter and Cynodon spp in summer) with herbicide application in the vine row; T2,

title: Reflexões sobre o conceito de preservação na Arquivologia Brasileira: uma análise a partir da legislação federal e da produção científica
abstract: This study addresses the concept of preservation in the field of Archival Science, starting from federal legislation and academic production on the subject. It comparatively analyzes the presence and uses of the term "preservation" in Brazilian archival legislation and academic production, seeking to identify continuities, shifts, and changes in how the topic is formulated over time. The research adopts a qualitative approach, of a basic nature, with a deductive method, articulating documentary and bibliographic research. Empirically, it involves the collection and analysis of legal provisions

title: The Institutionalization of REIT Sustainability Reporting: Cross‐Country Evidence From ESG Disclosure Regimes and Building Sustainability Policies
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the institutionalization and textual evolution of sustainability reporting among listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, and Japan between 2020 and 2025. Reporting is framed as the joint product of two institutional layers: capital‐market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure regimes and building‐level sustainability policies. For the full listed universe (641 REIT‐year observations), the analysis combines transition modeling with binomial logit estimation. To analyze the text of
journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: Advances in photothermal-driven tumor immunomodulation and synergistic therapy
abstract: Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a local treatment that uses photothermal conversion agents (PTAs) to absorb light and produce heat in tumor tissue. The direct result is tumor ablation. At the same time, heat-damaged tumor cells may undergo immunogenic cell death (ICD). This process is often accompanied by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), followed by dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation. Because of this immune effect, PTT has been explored as a partner for immunotherapy. It may be useful in tumors where antigen presentation is weak or where the immune mic

title: Senior Executive Pay and Corporate Sustainability Performance: The Roles of Green Innovation, Governance and State Ownership in China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between senior executive pay and corporate sustainability performance using 14,524 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms over the period 2019–2023. This period provides consistent data availability and encompasses China's transition towards the 2020 dual‐carbon policy. Drawing on agency, managerial power, stakeholder and resource dependence theories, we investigate nonlinear effects, green innovation as a mediating mechanism, and governance and ownership as boundary conditions. journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: “Discovering World Englishes has lessened my burden in English language education”
abstract: Abstract The growth of World Englishes (WE) in Applied Linguistics has provided important contributions to English language education and teacher professional development. Critical frameworks in WE have raised awareness and inspired knowledge creation about linguistic diversity in contexts where local teachers have been marginalized for being non-native speakers of English. Contributing to the understanding of English use and English language education dynamics in the expanding circle, this study reports the findings of a qualitative study examining how a group of ten in-service Colombian Engl

title: Forest endophytes as a biological resource insights into their role in sustainable agriculture and agroforestry
abstract: Abstract Forest ecosystems are the hidden reservoir of beneficial microorganisms, particularly for endophytes, that colonize plant tissue internally without causing any disease symptoms and play a key role in plant health and ecosystem sustainability. Forest-derived endophytic bacteria and fungi are crucial in nutrient cycling, stress resistance and growth promotion via phosphorus solubilization, nitrogen fixation and synthesis of phytohormones. Those microbes allow plants to survive in low-nutrient and stressful environments. This review offers insights into the diversity, abundance, distribu

title: Transients and Stellar Activity as Revealed by Ultraviolet Diagnostic Tracers
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) observations offer unique insights into transient and variable astrophysical phenomena, from the Sun and nearby stars to supernovae and star-forming galaxies. Here, we summarise and review the diagnostic power of the UV spectrum for probing the physical conditions, dynamics and energetics of these events. We trace the historical development of UV astronomy from early satellite missions to the current landscape shaped by the Hubble Space Telescope, the GALaxy Evolution eXplorer, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and AstroSat /UVIT. Particular emphasis is placed on res

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Climate Change-Related Health Issues in Africa
abstract: While climate change disproportionately impacts African public health, AI predictive modeling remains heavily constrained. Using a Synthetic Knowledge Synthesis approach and VOSviewer, we conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature, comparing Global and African corpora. Network analysis reveals stark divergences: global research emphasizes complex, predictive models for planetary health, whereas African research focuses on localized, reactive solutions for immediate infectious disease triage. Severe structural barriers in Africa, including compute deficits, data silos, and e
institutions: Zdravstveni dom dr. Adolfa Drolca Maribor

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods are increasingly applied to accelerate structural design, estimate operating parameters and states, and support adaptive control and scheduling. This review develops a task-oriented framework organized around three interconnected domains: structural design and optimization, parameter and state estimation, and control and optimization. Supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid or physics-i

title: FASST: A Compact Stateless Atmosphere Model for Long-Term Ocean Coupling
abstract: Coupled climate simulations are computationally expensive, largely because of the atmosphere. We introduce FASST, a coupled climate model that retains the prognostic POP2 ocean while replacing the atmosphere and sea ice with lightweight U-Net emulators. The atmospheric emulator is diagnostic, predicting surface fluxes from the evolving ocean-ice state every $6$ simulated hours, while the sea-ice emulator advances the ice state monthly. For $140$ years of unforced integration, FASST maintains a stable global-mean climate without SST restoring, with post-transient global-mean SST of $291.30 \pm

title: Graph Neural Networks for Astrophysics and Cosmology
abstract: Physics seldom makes breakthroughs when we consider objects only in isolation. Instead we model and measure how objects sit among their neighbours, spatial, temporal, or otherwise: a galaxy in its environment, a halo in its history, a photon hit in a detector. Graphs are ideally suited for encoding exactly these relations, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) learn the geometric functions that respect them. This review presents the use of GNNs for astrophysics and cosmology, and argues that GNNs often suit physics and physical data better than any alternative: they fit the native geometry of the d

title: Conditional Diffusion Generation of DVL and Inertial Signals for Underwater Navigation
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) navigate without satellite positioning and rely on Doppler velocity log (DVL) and inertial sensors for motion estimation. Deep learning methods for processing these sensors require training data covering the motion the AUV encounters, commonly obtained through costly sea trials. To overcome this limitation, we present a conditional diffusion framework that generates synthetic DVL and inertial signals to replace real recordings in training. title: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is often proposed as a low-cost complement to multibeam surveys of ports, but its accuracy is seldom measured on an area the model has never seen. We test SDB in the turbid, shallow and tidal waters of the Abu Dhabi coast against 285,619 multibeam soundings from twelve surveys at six port areas, reduced to Lowest Astronomical Tide. The Stumpf ratio, the Lyzenga transform, a monotonic gradient-boosted tree model (LightGBM) and a U-Net ensemble were trained on 72 Sentinel-2 images and tested in transfer to an unseen site and with local control (about 20% of a s

title: Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
abstract: Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $η(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on sp

title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
abstract: We developed a machine learning (ML) surrogate trained on instantaneous large eddy simulation (LES) data filtered using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to predict mean flow fields in natural rivers with complex geometries. The surrogate enables efficient prediction of mean flow fields downstream of marine hydrokinetic (MHK) turbine arrays at a fraction of the computational cost of high fidelity simulations, facilitating turbine layout optimization in natural waterways where bathymetry, turbulence, and turbine interactions influence the available energy resource. We demonstrate the capabi

title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra
abstract: Machine-learning models for spectroscopy usually treat a spectrum as a fixed-grid intensity vector, leaving the physical coordinate implicit in the array index. Such models are tied to a single sampling grid, spectral range and resolution, which limits their use when measurement conditions change. Here we represent each spectral point as a pair of intensity and wavenumber and compute Transformer positional encodings from the wavenumber itself. On Raman spectra of three bacterial species and their synthetic mixtures, this representation remained robust to noise, sparser sampling and partial spe

title: Latent space configuration for neural network finetuning, fast ranking, and embedding dimensionality reduction
abstract: Finding K most similar elements for a query in a large gallery of neural network (NN) embeddings is essential in various areas of computer science and industrial applications of artificial intelligence. This paper proposes search algorithms for structured latent spaces (LS) of NNs which allow to speed up top K item retrieval owing to O(1) complexity small candidate gallery subset search. ArcFace-pretrained IResNet50 models are finetuned using Latent Space Configuration (LSC) methodology to obtain new distribution of embeddings with desired geometric properties. Applying the proposed algorithms

title: Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion
abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence is widely assumed to scale with effort: more researchers, papers and investment should accelerate discovery. Theories of technological growth instead locate the difficulty of discovery in the space of ideas. Here we show that neither scale nor space is enough: breakthroughs depend on diverse attention, which collective concentration can deplete. Across 36 years of computer science, we analyze 7.2 million papers, 73,089 peer reviews and 3.7 million researchers and their topic shifts. title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation
abstract: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. title: HypoNet Nankai PS: rapid hypocenter determination for the Nankai Trough using physics-informed neural networks with three-dimensional P- and S-wave velocity models
abstract: Rapid and accurate hypocenter determination based on three-dimensional (3D) seismic velocity models is essential for seismic monitoring in subduction zones, yet it remains computationally demanding. HypoNet Nankai, a hypocenter determination package that uses physics-informed neural network (PINN) travel-time inference for a realistic 3D P-wave velocity model of the Nankai Trough subduction zone, was designed to address this problem, but supported only P-wave arrival times. Here, we present HypoNet Nankai PS, which extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times. We first constructed
institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: YingLan: A Multimodal Ocean Foundation Model for Unified Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Observations
abstract: Multimodal ocean modeling remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity in data structures, physical semantics, and spatiotemporal characteristics across satellite imagery, gridded oceanographic fields, and buoy observations. Existing approaches largely focus on task-specific ocean modeling, while learning transferable representations from heterogeneous observations remains an open problem. title: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment
abstract: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. Supporting experiments examine acoustic feature selection, statistical pooling and Transformer patch configurations. The two-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved a mean macro-F1 of \tex

title: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones
abstract: Rapid intensification (RI) is one of the most dangerous and unpredictable phases of tropical cyclones, and its environmental and structural drivers are difficult to identify and separate in observations. Here we introduce CausalVisionRI, a causal-prior-constrained deep-learning system for 24-h RI warning in the western North Pacific. It integrates infrared remote sensing imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and an observationally discovered causal graph into a unified model. The graph and eight sign-verified effects on 24-h intensity change provide an auditable causal prior for training. D

title: Manifold-Informed Neural Networks for Low-Label ECG Electrolyte Inference
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) supervise on the residual of a known differential operator. Many high-stakes inference problems admit no such operator: clinical signals, behavioral measurements, materials properties. We introduce the Manifold-Informed Neural Network (MINN), a PINN-parallel paradigm that replaces the physics operator residual with a manifold operator residual: a discrete Poisson equation $\mathbf{L}_G \mathbf{H} = s_ϕ(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{m})$ on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph in the learned latent space, with a learned, task-aware source. title: A fully convolutional neural network to classify UXOs using multicomponent electromagnetic induction data
abstract: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance relies on electromagnetic induction (EMI) methods to detect and classify buried and submerged metallic objects, but the standard classification workflow requires physics-based inversion and manual expert review. We present a fully convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies UXO directly from multicomponent time-domain EMI data, bypassing the inversion step entirely. The CNN uses a segmentation-like architecture that preserves the spatial dimensions of the input and outputs a high-resolution classification map suitable for generating a diglist. Two CNN

title: Physical-Variable-Informed Deep Learning for Robust Diagnosis in Industrial Fluid Transport Systems
abstract: Industrial fluid transport systems are monitored through heterogeneous sensing streams, but robust fault diagnosis remains difficult because response signals vary with operating conditions and differ from physical variables in sampling rate, observation duration and data granularity. To address these challenges, we propose a physical-variable-informed deep learning framework (PhyNet) for robust fault diagnosis under real-world sampling heterogeneity. institutions: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Will AI kill us all---or just make mathematicians obsolete?
abstract: AI's recent advances have fueled predictions of human intellectual obsolescence and fears for the future of mathematics. I argue that, impressive as these achievements are, they do not establish AI's capacity to invent new concepts and theories or sustain autonomous recursive self-improvement. Human intelligence also involves judgment, imagination, and embodied experience that standard measures fail to capture. title: Dynamical Batching: How Class-Cycling Training Shapes the Internal Structure of Neural Networks
abstract: We investigate whether cyclically varying the class composition of training batches can modify both the performance and the internal organization of neural networks. Motivated by nonequilibrium systems, in which cycling between related sub-goals can make switching between their solutions increasingly efficient, we introduce Dynamical Batching (DB), a sampling protocol that periodically emphasizes each class while leaving the loss and the optimizer unchanged, and compare it with Uniform Batching (UB), in which every mini-batch has equal class proportions. title: GeoPrompt: Geometry-Conditioned Prompt Learning for Underwater Open-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary instance segmentation (OVIS) provides a promising solution for marine perception by recognizing and segmenting categories beyond predefined label spaces. Existing OVIS methods usually rely on vision-language alignment, where visual region features are matched with textual category embeddings to recognize both seen and unseen classes. However, this alignment assumption becomes fragile in underwater environments.
