institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence

title: AudiPsy: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning over Spoken Counseling Conversations for Depression Assessment
abstract: Depression assessment from counseling speech requires integrating textual and acoustic psychological evidence across turns, yet existing end-to-end classification approaches lack explicit multimodal evidence interpretation and context-aware reasoning. We propose AudiPsy, an evidence-grounded omni-LLM for depression assessment over spoken counseling conversations. AudiPsy employs an Observation-Assessment-Summary (OAS) paradigm to integrate dialogue transcripts, textual and acoustic emotions, and textual-acoustic emotion incongruence into structured reasoning. OAS incrementally organizes multim
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Cross-Spectral Feature Fusion for Multispectral Document Binarization
abstract: Historical document binarization remains challenging when faded ink, bleed-through, and background degradation exhibit wavelength-dependent behavior across visible and near-infrared observations. This study investigates whether adaptive cross-spectral feature fusion and targeted structural guidance can improve multispectral document binarization beyond fixed fusion and generic attention mechanisms. Four registered SMADI bands at 500, 600, 700, and 1000 nm are processed using a multi-branch conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). Visible, NIR, and structural feature streams are fused

title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
abstract: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic. FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training,

title: DiffAuction: An Auction-Driven Framework for Generative Image Advertising
abstract: Diffusion models enable multiple advertisers to compete for exposure within a shared generated image. Yet existing approaches are computationally costly when generating images under varying target-share configurations, and it remains unclear how the resulting outcomes should be evaluated and priced. To address these gaps, we propose DiffAuction, a framework integrating controllable generation, click-intent evaluation, and auction design. First, our training-free Residual Share Calibration (RSC) decomposes joint-attention updates into product-specific residuals and rescales them according to ta

title: ShadAR: Real-time Prompting On-demand Visual Augmentation in Augmented Reality
abstract: Augmented Reality can reshape our visual perception (e.g., simulating color blindness) yet such effects are typically pre-programmed by experts, making visual augmentation static and inflexible. We introduce ShadAR, an AR system that allows users to describe expected visual augmentations (e.g., "Blur all people") for changing their vision in real time. ShadAR can graphically manipulate AR passthrough real-time via shader injection. title: Principal Component Analysis for Multivariate Extremes
abstract: Outline: While previous chapters focused on modeling multivariate extremes, we now turn to dimension reduction methods. This chapter explores ways to reduce the dimensionality of the data while preserving key information relevant to the analysis of multivariate extreme values.

title: Self-thresholding angular-radial models of extremal dependence
abstract: Assessing compound risks requires a model for routine and extreme joint behaviour together, and a principled answer to where the joint tail begins. We propose the self-thresholding angular-radial (STAR) model: after marginal standardization, the radius given the angle follows a spliced distribution, with a flexible body below an angle-dependent threshold curve and a generalized Pareto tail above it. institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

title: SHAM-Bench: A Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks
abstract: Span-level hallucination detection pinpoints unsupported content in LLM outputs, enabling actionable feedback and targeted mitigation. Existing evaluations for span-level hallucination detection methods are fragmented across tasks, annotation formats, and metrics, and most span-level datasets cover only a single NLG domain, making it difficult to assess whether a detection method actually generalizes across tasks and domains. In this paper, we introduce SHAM-Bench (Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks), a unified benchmark for span-level hallucination detection spanning six

title: Recovering Plausible Transmission Outage Scenarios
abstract: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower lev

title: MAGIC: Margin-gated Contrastive Debiasing with Evidence Restoration for VLM Test-time Robustness Scaling
abstract: This paper studies the problem of test-time robustness scaling for large vision-language models (LVLMs), which aims to mitigate language bias during inference. Existing approaches typically adopt test-time scaling techniques such as contrastive decoding to improve inference performance. Despite the progress, the performance of these approaches is far from satisfactory due to intentional evidence removal during perturbations and redundant inference cost. Towards this end, we propose a novel approach named Margin-gated Contrastive Debiasing with Evidence Restoration (MAGIC). The core of our MAGI
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

title: Effect-Size Estimation and Confounding-Aware Permutations for PERMANOVA
abstract: Motivation: PERMANOVA is widely used to test associations between covariates and high-dimensional data with arbitrary distributions, such as ecology, metabolomics, or microbial community profiling. In these contexts, its effect size measure (R2) is generally used to indicate how much the high-dimensional measurement covaries with respect to a separate, univariate measure. However, as we show, this conventional effect size is inflated under the null, resulting in values that do not accurately reflect the conventional expectation of "variance explained." Furthermore, standard permutation schemes

title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use
abstract: Large language models operationalize an intuitive, view of meaning as use. We argue that it faces a rule-following challenge. Using Kripke's interpretation of Wittgenstein, we argue that finite histories of use do not determine a unique rule for future extension. This reframes the debate about OOD generalization but also about NLP evaluation; benchmarks that measure performance on fixed use cases or local robustness, we argue, do not by themselves establish semantic competence. To evaluate whether models preserve rules and concepts under principled domain extension, we propose to evaluate two

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG ev

title: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos
abstract: Generating reusable driving environments requires both controllable future observations and an explicit representation that supports rendering from different viewpoints, yet existing methods still recover explicit scenes from generated RGB videos through optimization for each sequence. To overcome these limitations, we present Drive2Gauss, a feedforward framework that converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes. A Multimodal Video Generator predicts the three modalities from reference multiview images and future control signals. Furthermore, w

title: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
abstract: Negation remains a persistent challenge for language models across NLP tasks and modalities. We show that this weakness can undermine LLM safety guardrails through a structural vulnerability we term polarity blindness: the failure to recognize harmful intent after polarity-altering linguistic transformations. We study two forms of polarity inversion: grammatical negation and antonym replacement, and use synonym replacement as a polarity-preserving control. We further test whether an adversarial textual wrapper amplifies these failures. Using a 260-prompt benchmark across 10 state-of-the-art LL

title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive

title: OACap: Caption-Guided Active Observation for Detailed Video Captioning
abstract: Unlike question answering, where a query specifies a perceptual target, open-ended detailed captioning must determine what evidence to acquire and how to integrate it into a coherent global description. We propose Observation-Adaptive Video Captioner (OACap), a caption-centered agent that turns unsupported or missing information into targeted observation requests, uses spatiotemporal tools to acquire evidence, and iteratively verifies and revises the caption. OACap captions consistently improve performance across general video-understanding benchmarks using a fixed text-only reader. To better

title: A Hierarchical Space-Ground Collaborative Network: Architecture Design and Deployment
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) landscape demands a profound architectural evolution toward a unified, collaborative ecosystem that integrates satellite and terrestrial segments to provide ubiquitous global connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional independent management paradigms are increasingly challenged by the profound spatiotemporal nonstationarity of low-Earth orbit (LEO) channels and the volatile demands of massive heterogeneous services. To address these challenges, this study focuses on the architectural design of space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) and investigates elastic deployment
institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: From Gaze to Guidance: Interpreting and Adapting to Users’ Cognitive Needs with Multimodal Gaze-Aware AI Assistants
abstract: Current LLM assistants are powerful at answering questions, but they have limited access to the behavioral context that reveals when and where a user is struggling. We present a gaze-grounded multimodal LLM assistant that uses egocentric video with gaze overlays to identify likely points of difficulty and target follow-up retrospective assistance. We instantiate this vision in a controlled study (n=36) comparing the gaze-aware AI assistant to a text-only LLM assistant. The gaze-aware assistant was rated as more accurate and personalized in its assessments of users’ reading behavior, and users

title: Estimation and Inference for One-pass Streaming Function-on-Function Regression
abstract: In many applications, functional pairs are collected sequentially from a data stream. Existing function-on-function regression methods are primarily designed for batch data, and bootstrap inference has become one of the most popular approaches. However, this procedure may be infeasible when observations cannot be stored. In this paper, we propose a one-pass functional SGD estimator that updates upon each observation's arrival without data storage, and a weighted rolling validation rule is provided for step size selection for implementation. Further, an online multiplier bootstrap is developed
institutions: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 found
institutions: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

title: Safety Offset Learning: When Benign Fine-Tuning Misaligns LLMs
abstract: Safety risks from fine-tuning are commonly characterized by the harmfulness of the training data:harmful fine-tuning is considered dangerous, while benign fine-tuning is often assumed to preservealignment. We argue that this view misses a more fundamental factor-the behavioral transition inducedby supervision. Harmful fine-tuning and safety-degrading benign fine-tuning can both be understoodas learning the same refusal-to-compliance transition, but on different data distributions. We studywhether such a transition learned on benign inputs can generalize to harmful requests. We constructbenign

title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts
abstract: Learning an unfamiliar visual category requires more than adapting a classifier: the model must connect its visual evidence to a useful semantic name. A pre-trained vision-language model can retain discriminative image features while providing a weak textual anchor for the target concept. We address this imbalance through context-grounded semantic anchoring. Our framework, SynerNet, learns concept-specific name embeddings, exposes them to compatible linguistic contexts, and conditions their representations on visual evidence. Difficulty-aware processing and adaptive objective weighting coordin

title: Mean estimation in spatial functional data
abstract: Functional mean estimation exhibits a sparse-to-dense phase transition as the number of measurements per curve increases. For spatially indexed functional data, however, dependence between nearby curves and increasing spatial sampling density fundamentally alter this transition. We investigate this phenomenon under a unified framework allowing both increasing-domain and infill asymptotics, with irregular temporal observations. Our analysis identifies two distinct sources of estimation error: an observation-level component governed by the total number of measurements and a curve-level component
institutions: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

title: ActionRoPE: Action as Coordinates for Spatially Consistent Control in Planar-Camera Game World Models
abstract: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world. This formulation is poorly matched to a broad class of planar-camera worlds, such as top-down and isometric games. In these worlds, player motion induces a geometrically well-defined planar camera displacement. We observe that the key to spatially consistent control in such worlds is to represent the effect of each action directly in world coo

title: Vehicle-State-Aware Confidence Estimation for Direct Wind Sensing on a Multirotor
abstract: Direct wind sensing from a multi-rotor UAV enables localized atmospheric measurements, but the reliability of the anemometer depends on vehicle motion. This work presents a vehicle-state-aware confidence method that uses horizontal and vertical vehicle speed to quantify the acquisition of each wind observation. The resulting confidence score is used to adapt measurement influence to a two-dimensional vector estimator. Experiments were conducted during horizontal translation, vertical motion, and held-out autonomous waypoint flight. The proposed two-feature formulation achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.

title: Lychee: Certified Screening of Inverted Lists for High-Recall Vector Search
abstract: Nearest-neighbor search over embedding vectors matches faces against watchlists, transactions against known fraud patterns, and medical images against confirmed cases, where a missed neighbor is a missed threat, fraud, or diagnosis. Because an approximate index cannot report which queries lost a true neighbor, these applications require recall of 0.999 to 0.9999, at a cost far below that of exact search over billions of vectors. Inverted-file indexes reach high recall by probing more lists, but they read and score every probed vector at full precision, so that throughput falls in inverse propo

title: DeclineCraft: A RAG Abstention Benchmark for Jointly Measuring Combined Retrieval and Parametric Knowledge
abstract: Reliable retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires recognizing when neither retrieved documents nor parametric knowledge supports an answer. We introduce DeclineCraft, a dynamic abstention benchmark whose unanswerable questions target Minecraft feature additions after a corpus cut-off, with audits of possible parametric exposure. Later cut-offs support evaluation of future models. Across 27 LLMs, we measure Correct Abstention Rate (CAR; how often models acknowledge insufficient knowledge on unanswerable questions), Answerable Attempt Rate and Answer Accuracy. We find that (1) single-shot r

title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: To prepare for future outbreaks, researchers need to know what studies have been done and what data they use. Mapping a large literature by hand is slow, while large language models alone can misstate or conflate sources. We present EpiLens, a lightweight, open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to every paper in a corpus and links outputs to source passages. We build a corpus of 2,297 papers from the sources of a multi-pathogen parameter study and evaluate EpiLens's paper-classification workflow against 214 manually labelled

title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process. We therefore ask whether ordinary reasoning failures and adversarially induced failures can be characterized using the same internal coordinates. Towards this end, we in this paper study a white-box diagnostic framework CauTrace to disclose the root-cause of why LLM fails from three fundamental inspections: Functional States, Propagation of Representation, Temporal-State Coordination and Reasoning Trajectory. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
abstract: Repository-level coding benchmarks largely assume that tasks and environments remain unchanged throughout execution. In software development, code, dependencies, runtime state, and requirements can change while an agent is still working. We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents under such mid-execution changes. From the same saved history and workspace, a Clean continuation proceeds without intervention, while a matched Shifted continuation receives a task-relevant update. Success requires completing the current task, preserving still-valid work, and satisfying the appl
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: TRACE: Training-aware Robustness and Challenge Evaluation for Text-Vision Embedding Models
abstract: Existing benchmarks for text-vision embedding models report aggregate scores that obscure whether performance comes from general capabilities, task-specific adaptation, or robustness to challenging tasks. We introduce TRACE, a Training-aware Robustness and Challenge Evaluation framework that reorganizes 168 tasks from various sources of datasets into three categories: General, Adaptability, and Challenge. Through controlled experiments on two text-vision embedding models, we show that combining general and adaptation data improves Adaptability performance by 7.67 and 7.09 points, respectively,
institutions: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology

title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a

title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries. We consider multi-turn grounded conversational scenarios where a user query is either ill-formed or ambiguous in the context of the prior dialog or, more interestingly, it may be well-formed but when posed against retrieved documents there are multiple relevant interpretations. The task is to recognize both such cases and then generate an appropriate clarification request to the user. We present ClariEdge, a new dataset of approximately 3,900 examples that include such ambiguous

title: Music of the Deep: An acoustic blueprint of sperm whale codas
abstract: Sperm-whale codas are usually described by the number and timing of their clicks. Earlier acoustic studies showed that individual clicks and longer coda sequences contain additional organization. We ask how that organization compares with music, whose smaller sounds also form larger units and ordered sequences. We compare codas with performed violin music, drum grooves, and sung melodies. Their sequences resemble music in some measures of predictability, yet codas show a different relationship between the smaller sounds within a unit and the order of units across a sequence. This combination w

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
abstract: Engineers who audit a declared specification of an engineered system need to know which physical constraints it respects, which it violates, which field was altered and how to correct it. NeSySpec is an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic audit framework, built on Logic Tensor Networks, that answers these questions in one pipeline. title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. There are three contributions: (1) We collected sixteen VPR database-query datasets based on existing data from S

title: Mostly Reading: What Open-Book Scores Measure in Document-Level LoRA Adapters
abstract: Single-document LoRA adapters have been proposed as units of knowledge to be merged and retrieved; yet open-book scoring, with the document in the prompt, can credit a document's own adapter (its specialist) for reading that document as readily as for holding it. Training one adapter for each of 150 Wikipedia articles on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, we find that open-book scores mostly measure a reading behaviour every adapter shares: a random adapter trained on another document recovers 82 % of the specialist's open-book advantage over the base model but only 2 % of its advantage on a cloze probe t

title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200–600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) str

title: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
abstract: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft gam

title: Virtual Placebo: a scoping review of control conditions in randomized controlled trials of psychological immersive virtual reality interventions
abstract: Research on immersive virtual reality (IVR) as a therapeutic tool is growing rapidly, with randomized controlled trials (RCTs) now commonplace. Yet the control conditions in many of these studies that claim strong specific IVR effects vary from usual care to active immersive experiences, making it difficult to draw clinically meaningful conclusions. We conducted a scoping review of recent literature on psychological IVR interventions to assess the main forms of control conditions used and their relations to study outcomes. In this paper, we make the case that most of the recent RCTs studying t

title: CulturalRiddles: A Multicultural Benchmark of Riddles
abstract: As LLMs expand their language coverage, evaluating how well they understand and represent diverse cultures becomes increasingly important. However, many benchmarks remain English-centric, with limited cultural coverage and a focus on factual knowledge over its application in real-world cultural contexts. We propose CulturalRiddles, a benchmark of original, culturally grounded riddles created entirely by humans through a participatory community effort, spanning 62 cultures (45 countries, 51 languages). These riddles are deeply rooted in their respective cultures and require abductive and compos

title: Conducting Reliable Keyword Estimation with Unreliable ASR in Police Audio Data
abstract: Extracting insights from large audio data sets using human transcription is expensive and time-consuming. Off-the-shelf Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems offer an easy-to-use scalable alternative, but systematic transcription errors, especially in domain-specific settings, can bias downstream analyses and lead to unreliable conclusions. We investigate whether imperfect ASR transcripts can still be used to obtain statistically valid keyword frequency estimates by combining model outputs with a small set of human-labeled examples, following Prediction Powered Inference and Design-based

title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents
abstract: In finance, the answer that matters is usually the current one: prices, rates, and disclosures hold only as of a given day, so retrieving up-to-date facts is a core capability of a financial agent. Yet most financial benchmarks overlook timeliness. They fix each answer at annotation time, so the gold goes stale as markets move and, once leaked into training data, rewards recall rather than search and analysis. We introduce LiveSearch, a live benchmark that stores each question as executable verifier code: a typed program of calls to a professional financial data service, followed by a declarat

title: AGR: Agentic Generative Retrieval with Tool-Augmented Search
abstract: Large-scale search and recommendation systems derive much of their retrieval quality from rich, heterogeneous features, yet existing generative retrieval (GR) methods struggle to exploit such feature ecosystems efficiently. Static feature injection either encodes all available signals or places them according to predetermined schemes, increasing serving cost and introducing irrelevant or conflicting evidence. More fundamentally, existing methods cannot adaptively determine when a feature is needed, which feature to select, or where it should influence hierarchical Semantic ID (SID) generation.

title: An Open Reliability Atlas of Sensitivity and Failure Modes in the Pulse Physiology Engine
abstract: Pulse is an actively maintained open-source adult-physiology simulator, yet its maintainers report no formal sensitivity analysis of its operational inputs. We present the first open reliability atlas across its critical-care envelope: Morris elementary-effects sampling of seven inputs, four severity scenarios, male and female bodies (1,280 simulations). Sensitivity is skewed: three inputs carry a median 93% of each output's total. A four-flag classifier reveals failure modes: two operator-actionable, one sex-stratified. Tidal-volume oscillation (20.6% of runs) is consistent with patient-venti
institutions: Centre Hospitalier Régional et Universitaire de Nancy

title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. title: Quantifying the Threat: A Bayesian Probabilistic Framework for Heavy Metal Health Risks among Children in the Densu Basin, Ghana
abstract: Groundwater in Ghana's Densu River Basin remains a key domestic water source, but multi-metal contamination threatens children's health. Previous deterministic hazard index assessments provide limited treatment of uncertainty, co-exposure, and spatial variability. This study applies a Bayesian probabilistic framework for non-carcinogenic risk assessment using 94 groundwater samples and measurements of Fe, Mn, Ni, Pb, Cd, and As. A Bayesian regression model propagates parameter uncertainty and accounts for contaminant co-occurrence. Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo is used for posterior inferen
institutions: Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Spherical Brownian Diffusion for Language Modeling
abstract: Continuous diffusion language models involve two coupled design choices: how to corrupt continuous token representations and how to invert that corruption at generation time. Recent work has explored language generation on the unit sphere through geodesic and von Mises--Fisher (vMF) paths, raising the question of which forward process to use on this geometry and how much that choice matters relative to inference. title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability
abstract: Linear hyperspectral unmixing aims at retrieving pure material spectra present in an observed scene and their associated abundance fractions in each pixel. In most practical situations, hyperspectral images are affected by spectral variability (SV) also known as intra-class variability, which is caused by different physical phenomena including atmospheric effects, intrinsic variability of the pure materials and illumination or topographic changes. title: On-the-fly Estimation of Quantum-Corrected Thermodynamics in LAMMPS
abstract: We present a native implementation of the Two/Three-Phase Thermodynamics (xPT, $x \in \{2,3\}$) method within the LAMMPS molecular dynamics framework, termed FixXPT. xPT is an approach for obtaining absolute, quantum-corrected thermodynamics (entropy, enthalpy, free energy, heat capacity, diffusivity) from the density of states function, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function of an equilibrium trajectory. title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents interact with Web services to perform tasks on users' behalf. Errors during these interactions can disrupt execution and prevent task completion, motivating external intervention. However, agents may self-recover through continued execution, raising the question of when to intervene and when to wait for self-recovery. We present an empirical study of errors and self-recovery in LLM agents. We construct ReInBench, a dataset containing 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and Web tasks. Our study examines how often and how quickly agents self-recover, how self
institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: FATE-5: Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for Continuous Big Five Personality Control
abstract: Controlling personality in large language models is important for building conversational agents that can be customized to different users and interaction settings. However, existing personality control methods often face a tradeoff between strong trait expression and natural dialogue generation. We introduce FATE-5, Faithful Alignment of Trait Expression for the Big Five, a two-stage framework that separates personality encoding from naturalness alignment. FATE-5 first learns continuous soft prompt representations of Big Five profiles using dialogue supervision and an auxiliary survey objecti

title: NumTrace: Auditing the Number Provenance of Financial Analyst Agents
abstract: A numerical claim generated by a financial analyst agent can match a number in a company filing but refer to the wrong entity, concept, period, unit or scope. A check based on reference answers can mark such an answer as wrong but does not explain why it fails. In this paper, we present NumTrace, a new benchmark that audits the provenance of each numerical claim made by financial analyst agents: its source and financial semantics. title: SoftBART-CORM Models for Density Regression
abstract: Flexible modelling of the conditional distribution of a response given predictors is important in many applications where nonlinear effects, heteroskedasticity, and multimodality may be present. We introduce the SoftBART-CoRM, a predictor-dependent infinite mixture model that combines the interpretable component structure of Compound Random Measures (CoRMs) with SoftBART priors on both mixture weights and component-specific parameters. title: Finite-Size CV-QKD for Satellite Quantum Communication under a Hybrid Noise Model
abstract: Satellite-based continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is fundamentally constrained by finite communication windows, channel attenuation, and statistical fluctuations arising from a limited number of exchanged quantum states. This work develops a finite-size CV-QKD framework for satellite quantum communication under a hybrid noise model that jointly incorporates satellite geometry, atmospheric and propagation losses, quantum Poissonian noise coexisting with classical additive white Gaussian noise, detector imperfections, and composable finite-key security under collective attack

title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: ER-Chord: Spatially Consistent One-Step Image Editing via Equal-Energy Reliability Redistribution
abstract: One-step generative models enable fast text-guided image editing, yet they often introduce unintended changes to regions that should remain unchanged. Temporal aggregation stabilizes editing fields across noise levels, but leaves their spatial allocation insensitive to local variations in reliability. Consequently, temporal stability alone does not ensure spatially consistent editing. To address this lim- itation, we propose ER-Chord, a training-free and inversion-free framework for reliability-guided spatial redistribution. title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
abstract: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. title: $N \to Δ$ Transition Form Factors in the Thermal AdS/QCD Soft-Wall Model with Modified Propagators
abstract: We investigate electromagnetic (EM) and axial vector (AV) form factors of the nucleon-Delta baryon transition within the thermal AdS/QCD soft-wall model. While the vector bulk-to-boundary propagator admits a well-behaved analytical solution, the transverse axial vector equation of motion involves the vacuum expectation value of the bifundamental scalar (generating chiral symmetry breaking). title: Target-Aware Curation of Hallucination Stress Tests for Large Language Models
abstract: Hallucination stress tests can yield similar average scores across language models even when different prompts elicit hallucinations in each model. We develop a procedure that iteratively edits source-grounded seed prompts to expose hallucinations in a target model. An LLM editor revises each prompt in response to the target's answer and a judge's category-specific score and explanation. In the main setting, the target also receives feedback on its previous response. title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
abstract: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
abstract: Synthetic rewrites, where a language model rewrites a natural document e.g. into a target style, are now a standard ingredient of pretraining corpora. However, critical aspects of their use remain poorly understood, such as how much compute should be spent rewriting training data and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform the rewriter. title: QUBO-Based Conformer Selection with Quantum-Classical Hybrid Optimization for Multiconformer Ligand Modeling
abstract: A ligand can adopt multiple conformations within the same binding site, and these conformations can interact differently with the surrounding protein. Multiconformer modeling must therefore determine which candidate conformations to retain and what occupancies to assign to them. An established automated approach uses mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) with hard occupancy and conformer-count limits for this selection. title: Mass Spectra of Doubly Heavy Strange baryons $Ω_{QQ^{'}}$ and their Decay properties
abstract: This study investigates baryons $Ω_{cc}$, $Ω_{bc}$ and $Ω_{bb}$ composed of two heavy quarks and one strange light quark, focusing on their radial and excited state mass spectra. We employ the Hyper Central Constituent Quark Model (hCQM), incorporating higher-order corrections, including second-order mass corrections with explicit consideration of spin-dependent interactions. title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. title: Nuclear fission: from fundamentals to frontiers
abstract: Nuclear fission, the division of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter fragments, is a process of fundamental importance to nuclear physics, energy production, and the origin of the elements. This chapter, part of the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, provides a pedagogical introduction to a broad array of topics in fission physics, progressing from the macroscopic liquid-drop model and microscopic shell corrections through fission dynamics, observables, modern theoretical frameworks, and experimental techniques ranging from traditional double-energy methods to inverse kinematics at radioactive-i

title: SITO: Sifting a Commercial Text-Safety API for Missed Harm and False Flags in English, Ukrainian and Surzhyk
abstract: Platforms that host young users screen messages with commercial text-safety APIs, but independent evidence on how often such systems miss harm or flag harmless text is scarce, especially outside English, and the documentation of the one studied here leaves its false-positive rate unquantified. We evaluated one such API, Tuteliq Detect as deployed under the release identifier tuteliq-detect-v5.20261011 (not the separately published v6 model), on six harm categories: authorised push-payment fraud, money-mule recruitment, social engineering, romance scams, gambling harm and bullying. title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
abstract: A model behind an API can be identified from its one-word answers to everyday questions such as "Name a sound" or "Name a poet". A model's profile records how often it gives each answer to each question. We attribute new answers to the model most likely to have given them. On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance. Profiles built through OpenRouter identified all ten models served by DeepInfra under blinded labels. A system prompt lowers accuracy by 6 to 16 points. We applied the method to 96 endpoints of 13 open models on OpenRouter

title: Me, Myself, and My Voice: Exploring Cultural and Linguistic Identity in AAC AI-generated Voices
abstract: Voice is a central element of identity. We recognize people by their voice, and we uniquely express who we are with it. For people who rely on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, such as speech-generating devices (SGD), the device’s voice becomes an identity marker others associate with them. Yet, it is hard to find a voice that truly aligns with one’s identity both linguistically and culturally. Although modern AI-generated voices can reproduce diverse accents and speaking styles, AAC users still lack accessible ways to articulate how they want an identity-aligned voice

title: Transverse momentum dependent parton distributions at small $x$
abstract: Transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions provide a three-dimensional description of the momentum structure of hadrons. They are probed in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at the LHC and RHIC, and are a central part of the physics program of the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). While TMD factorization is well established at moderate Bjorken $x$, the small-$x$ regime requires a different treatment, since large logarithms of $1/x$ must be resummed and non-linear effects due to high gluon densities become important. title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. title: Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model
abstract: Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) provide a unified description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse spatial structure of the nucleon. We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. A central new result is the explicit analytic expression for the axial-vector-diquark contribution to the helicity-flip GPD $E^{q}$. title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
abstract: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task performance. Video editing provides a useful testbed for this question, combining multimodal perception, long-horizon planning, and tool use with delayed outcome feedback. title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
abstract: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. abstract: We extend the full-kinematic background-field construction developed for gluon transverse-momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMDPDFs) in Mukherjee et al. [Phys. Rev. D 109, 034035 (2024)] to quark TMDPDFs, providing a common framework for their large- and small-$x$ dynamics. We compute the leading-power quark TMD beam function at next-to-leading order using the background-field method. title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space.

title: Surface Conditioning for Zero-Shot Multivariate Correction in a Marine Biogeochemistry Emulator
abstract: Bias correction in process-based models usually means iterative data assimilation with explicit covariance modelling. We propose a lightweight alternative based on a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry (BGC), showing that the conditioning pathway of its autoencoder can serve as an observation injection point. The decoder is conditioned on surface variables via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), originally designed to incorporate physical boundary forcings. title: Robust Active Learning for More Efficient and Reliable Paths to Optimal Design
abstract: Simulation-driven design optimization requires active learning strategies that efficiently combine models with different computational costs and levels of fidelity. We introduce Multifidelity Cost-Aware Screening (MF-CAS), which enables the joint selection of sampling location and fidelity using a surrogate that provides decomposed uncertainty intervals rather than a complete predictive probability distribution. title: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation
abstract: Behavior Cloning has demonstrated promising generalization capabilities for robotic manipulation in terrestrial environments. However, marine visual distortions and dynamic currents create a severe domain shift that remains a key bottleneck in adapting generalist architectures to underwater field manipulation. To address this, 1616 episodes of underwater manipulation data were collected in calm and turbulent waters and were used to train 14 generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models (DynamicVLA) with varying proprioception observation configurations. title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis
abstract: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) characterizes the local frequency content of time-varying signals by evaluating the discrete Fourier transform over a sliding analysis window. The STFT is governed by a fundamental resolution trade-off: a short window localizes rapid transients in time at the cost of frequency resolution, whereas a long window resolves closely spaced harmonics at the expense of temporal resolution. title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
abstract: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged. For a Gaussian variational autoencoder (VAE) with constant input skip $0\leqα<1$, a model without a skip can be written in skip form by multiplying its decoder output by $b=1-α$ and its noise variance by $b^2$. The distribution of observations and latent variables and its exact generative scores stay the same, while reconstruction mean squared error (MSE) is multiplied by $b^2$. Separate training can produce different generators because optimization depends on the parameter coordinates.

title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. title: Evaluation of Radon Content in Soil Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Radon measurements of the air in the soil in a 40 m deep borehole were combined with meteorological data and evaluated using artificial intelligence. The purpose of the study is to analyze the factors influencing radon levels. Neural networks were employed for this purpose. After training the neural networks, a high coefficient of determination was achieved both in the training and in the forecast (test) phase if weekly or monthly averages are used. abstract: The proliferation of invasive smooth cordgrass (Spartina alterniflora) within the Bay of Brest poses a severe ecological threat to coastal wetlands, disrupting sedimentary dynamics and endangering high-value native taxa such as Limonium humile. Within the Armorique Regional Natural Park (PNRA), ecosystem preservation has traditionally relied on manual photo-interpretation a labor-intensive approach limited by estuarine morphological complexity and the critical need for early invasion detection. abstract: The article examines modern methods for predicting the remaining life of metallic ship structures with due consideration of fatigue, crack growth, corrosion wastage, and actual operating conditions. The analytical basis comprises eleven peer-reviewed publications issued in 2021–2026 and three regulatory and technical documents published by IMO and DNV. title: A physics-informed neural network framework for soil thermal conductivity estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of the bulk thermal conductivity of marine sediments is important for the design of offshore energy infrastructure, particularly subsea power cables where sediment thermal properties govern heat dissipation. Although purely data-driven models can provide high predictive accuracy, their predictions are not inherently constrained by established physical behaviour, particularly when applied beyond the conditions represented by the training data. title: Demo: RollingPol: Single-Shot Polarization Imaging for Underwater Sensing
abstract: Underwater optical sensing is severely degraded by backscattered light from suspended particles. While polarization-based image enhancement methods can suppress this backscattering effect, existing methods are either costly, or require sequential image captures that can't handle dynamic scenes. We address this challenge with RollingPol, a single-shot polarization imaging system that couples fast polarization modulation with the rolling-shutter readout of commodity cameras to encode multiple polarization states within a single exposure. abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) provides important all-weather images. These images help researchers observe the sea surface. However, separating the coast from the ocean in these images is hard. Near-shore areas face three main issues. The first issue is coherent speckle noise. The second issue is geometric distortion caused by the radar’s side-looking geometry. The third issue is feature aliasing caused by multiple scattering from coastal buildings. abstract: Dutch peatland drainage for intensive dairy farming purposes causes land subsidence and releases massive amounts of soil carbon as CO2, confronting policymakers with the challenge of sustaining dairy farming while fulfilling the reduction commitments of land subsidence and CO2 emissions under the Dutch Climate Act and the Paris Climate Agreement. abstract: Landslide hazard assessment and monitoring have traditionally relied on visual interpretation and heuristic classification methods, often limiting the spatial and temporal resolution of actionable insights. Recent advances in remote sensing technologies and machine learning offer new opportunities to automate and enhance the semantic understanding of landslide processes across diverse terrains. Challenges in preserving such coastal and submerged sites require creative approaches to engineering geology. abstract: In practical engineering, equipment parameters are difficult to obtain and measurement data is limited. This paper proposes a PINN-Modelica data-driven modeling method that couples a neural network with a Modelica model encapsulated as an FMU. abstract: In the context of digital transition in engineering geology, this study develops an AI-based framework to automate outlier detection in Cone Penetration Test (CPT) data, addressing the growing data volume and quality demands in offshore wind farm projects. CPT, widely used for seabed characterization, is prone to outliers due to equipment variability and harsh marine conditions, which compromise soil interpretation and design safety. abstract: Hydro-saline ground conditions are intensifying in arid coastal cities, accelerating infrastructure deterioration under rapid urban expansion. Large plastic items such as bottles and bags degrade in the environment, ultimately breaking down into microplastics (MPs). abstract: Side channels improve river resilience by increasing flow capacity and providing water buffer space. abstract: Visual quality evaluation of rural landscape is the basis for rational planning and development of rural cultural tourism resources, and the existing evaluation methods are mostly subjective and qualitative, with less research on objective and quantitative methods. abstract: Abstract The sustainable development of urban transportation systems requires a comprehensive understanding of cities’ unique compositions and evolution. title: The 2026 Rasuwa Disaster: A Transboundary Rock–Ice Avalanche, Himalayan Tsunami, and Cascading Hazards
abstract: The Himalaya is increasingly affected by high-mountain disasters driven by the interactions among cryospheric change since 1990, slope instability, thawing of glacial deposits and rock-mass permafrost, avalanches, and river systems. The 2026 Rasuwa disaster in the Nepal Himalaya highlights the destructive potential of these cascading processes, in which a massive rock–ice avalanche transformed into a devastating downstream flood and sediment-laden flow. title: A Novel Parametric Reduced-Order Modeling Method for Transient Prediction of Modelica-Based Brayton Cycles
abstract: Repeated transient simulations of Brayton cycles are often required during parameter studies, control assessment, and design iteration, whereas direct Modelica simulation under many conditions can remain inefficient despite its flexibility for system-level dynamic modeling. A parametric reduced-order modeling method is developed for fast transient prediction of Modelica-based Brayton cycles under unseen parameters and new operating conditions. title: Assessing the Potential for CO2 and Pollutant Emission Reduction via Redistribution of Port-Induced Road Traffic: A Case Study of the Port of Rotterdam
abstract: Abstract Public authorities face the challenge of air quality management in complex territories and need tools to disentangle the contributions of heterogeneous sources of emissions. Transportation is a major source of nitrogen oxides and accounts for about 30% of global carbon emissions. This becomes even more relevant in territories where transportation significantly serves other purposes than just people mobility. title: Risk Monitoring and Early Warning for Urban Critical Infrastructure: An Analytical Framework and Scenario Comparison
abstract: Risk monitoring and early warning for critical urban infrastructure face challenges such as infrastructure interdependence, data heterogeneity, cross-system risk propagation, and incomplete response chains. Existing research has yielded substantial results in areas such as urban lifeline monitoring, infrastructure interdependencies, digital twins, and intelligent early warning systems; however, the disparities in early warning capabilities across different application scenarios remain insufficiently explained. title: Typhoon track and temporal forecasting of wind and rain based on a multifactor coupling model and LSTM networks
abstract: This study proposes an integrated typhoon forecasting framework that sequentially combines a multi-factor physical model with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The physical component handles track projection via typhoon genesis indices, multi-layer steering flows, and β-drift corrections, and characterizes post-landfall wind decay through the Kaplan attenuation model; the LSTM network independently models temporal precipitation using features derived from physical outputs; and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) quantifies track prediction fidelity. abstract: Faults are critical structural units controlling regional tectonic frameworks and geomorphic evolution. Despite the increasing use of multi-source remote sensing data fusion for fault identification, conventional evaluation methods often overlook scale-dependent variations and their tectonic implications. abstract: Abstract Bremen, Germany’s smallest federal state, consists of the city of Bremen and, 57 km to the north, the city of Bremerhaven on the mouth of River Weser with one of Europe’s largest container terminals. Both the city of Bremen and Bremerhaven are integrated into three Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) corridors. With their strategic location and advanced multimodal infrastructure, Bremen and Bremerhaven serve as essential hubs for European freight transport. abstract: Sustainable tourism demands infrastructure that is not only physically adequate, but also environmentally friendly and digitally connected. This study compares sustainable tourism infrastructure and digital infrastructure in Indonesia with Thailand and Singapore, and examines the integration of the two. title: Site-Specific Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Analysis for the Akosombo Saddle Dam, Ghana
abstract: This study presents a site-specific probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) for the Akosombo Saddle Dam located in Akosombo, Ghana. The primary objective is to determine the Operation Basis Earthquake (OBE) and Safety Evaluation Earthquake (SEE) ground-motion spectral parameters to support the seismic performance assessment of the dam, following the provisions of International Commission on Large Dams (ICOLD) B148. title: Environmental and Socioeconomic Impacts of Disrupted Rail Freight from Asia and Europe: A Scenario Analysis
abstract: Abstract With modern, globalized value chains, disruptions to transportation systems may have large, far-reaching economic and environmental effects. In this work, we investigate a hypothetical scenario with a widespread disruption to intercontinental rail freight transport between Asia and Europe. In addition to the disruption, we examine mitigation scenarios where alternative transport routes are adopted. The environmental and socioeconomic effects of the disruption and mitigation scenarios indicate negative effects both in Asia and in Europe, with the greatest impacts occurring in Asia.

abstract: This study investigates the relationship between surficial geological units and the spatial distribution of liquefaction phenomena triggered by recent seismic events. Specifically, the earthquakes occurred in Christchurch (New Zealand, 2010–2011), Kaikoura (New Zealand, 2016), Damasi (Greece, 2021) and Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye, 2023) triggered extensive liquefaction in the river valleys of the Pinios, Orontes, Avon and Wairau Rivers, respectively. title: From Demographic Dividend to Industrial Transformation: A Forty-Year Review of Low-Cost Labor and the Development of China’s Electronics Assembly Industry
abstract: China’s electronics assembly industry is a pillar industry that enabled China to undertake international industrial relocation and integrate into global value chains. In the early days, it relied on abundant and cheap labor to form a global contract manufacturing advantage. With the arrival of the Lewis turning point, the increasing aging of the population and the improvement of the awareness of the rights and interests of migrant workers, the traditional low-cost employment model has encountered structural challenges, and industrial transformation is imminent. title: The Ethics and Identification of Combat Leadership: Navigating High-risk Research in a High-tension Global Landscape
abstract: Combat leadership defined as the ability to inspire and coordinate teams in high-pressure, high-importance, and high-threat environments is a critically important but under-discussed topic in leadership studies. While conventional military leadership is well-documented, specific data from active combat zones remains scarce. This research gap is primarily due to the ethical imperative that researchers ought not interfere with or compromise the safety of personnel in "in extremis" situations where lives are at immediate risk. title: Advanced Photovoltaic Technologies for Sustainable on Board Railways Services
abstract: Abstract The integration of photovoltaic (PV) technologies on railway rolling stock has gained increasing attention as part of the broader transition toward sustainable and energy-efficient transport systems. While conventional on-board PV installations have primarily targeted auxiliary loads rather than traction, recent advances in module efficiency, flexibility, and integration approaches open new perspectives for their application. title: Using Intelligent Transport System Monitoring Data to Assess Pavement Durability: Evidence from Lithuania
abstract: Abstract Intelligent transport systems (ITS) help manage road infrastructure using data, but their impact on pavement durability has not yet been fully researched. In Lithuania, three weigh-in-motion (WIM) monitoring points have been installed on national highways: A1 Vilnius–Kaunas–Klaipėda (80.815 km), A5 Kaunas–Marijampolė–Suvalkai (92.857 km) and A6 Kaunas–Zarasai–Daugavpils (26.431 km). These stations are primarily intended for monitoring rather than control purposes. title: Integrated Electrical Resistivity Imaging and Borehole Modelling for Delineation of Aged Hydrocarbon Contamination in the Niger Delta, Nigeria
abstract: Hydrocarbon contamination of shallow soils and groundwater is a persistent environmental and engineering-geological problem in the Niger Delta, where permeable deltaic sediments, shallow groundwater and prolonged residence times favour downward and lateral contaminant migration. Conventional borehole-based site characterization provides direct lithological and contamination evidence but is spatially limited and can be costly when dense sampling is required. title: Food Toxicology: Principles, Toxicological Mechanisms, Risk Assessment, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Food toxicology sits at the crossroads of toxicology, food science, biology, and public health. It focuses on the identification, source tracing, toxic action mechanisms, risk evaluation, and control strategies of all harmful toxic substances in food systems. These hazardous substances include both naturally occurring endogenous toxins and exogenous artificial pollutants generated in industrial production, agricultural cultivation, and food processing. abstract: The project Inform@Risk has been developing a landslide early warning system in the informal settlement Bello Oriente on the north-eastern slope of the city of Medellín, Colombia, the subsurface of which is made up entirely of the ultramafic ‘Medellín Dunite’. The geotechnical investigations carried out in the project to determine the requirements of that system included multiple mappings, drillings, and laboratory tests. title: Mechanical Performance and Technical Suitability of Carbonate Quarry Waste for Aggregate Production: The Süttő Travertine Case Study
abstract: Sustainable mining has become a strategic priority in the current context of increasing demand for raw materials and growing environmental constraints. In Hungary, with specific reference to the Süttő area selected as the study site, this research investigates the valorisation of extractive waste materials as a means to reduce environmental impact and promote circular economy principles. The study focuses on the potential reuse of quarrying waste derived from carbonate rock exploitation evaluating its suitability as aggregate for civil and building applications. title: Dynamic Rockfall Susceptibility Modelling in Czechia: Integrating Climatic Drivers and Temperature-Dependent Thresholds
abstract: Rockfalls are high-mobility, high-energy geohazards that affect steep slopes and are often triggered by climatic drivers such as intense rainfall, freeze-thaw cycles, and extreme temperature fluctuations. Here, we present an integrated framework combining data-driven and physically-based models to assess rockfall spatial distribution and runout trajectories within the Kokořínsko Protected Landscape Area in Czechia. title: Modelica-Based Parametric Analysis of Steady-State and Transient Thermal-Hydraulic Characteristics of PCHEs in S-CO2 Brayton Cycles
abstract: Printed circuit heat exchangers (PCHEs) are key components in supercritical carbon dioxide (S-CO2) Brayton cycles because of their compact structure and high heat transfer capability. However, existing studies have mainly focused on steady-state structural optimization or isolated component analysis, while the influence of geometric parameters on thermal-hydraulic responses under system-level transient disturbances remains insufficiently understood. In this study, a Modelica-based dynamic simulation framework is developed for the system-level analysis of recuperators in an S-CO2 Brayton cycle.

From Shipwreck to Digital Twin: Documenting the Neugrund Wreck (värskendatud versioon)
abstract: This article presents the creation and analysis of a high-resolution photogrammetric 3D model that forms the foundational component of a developing digital twin of an early 18th-century sailing shipwreck located near the Neugrund shoal in northwestern Estonian waters. The wreck, lying at a depth of 54–55 m, was documented during technical diving operations in 2025 using underwater photogrammetry. Approximately 4,500 images were processed to produce a high-resolution 3D model suitable for detailed archaeological analysis. title: MLP-Based Condition Assessment Method for Marine Propulsion Shafting Driven by Measured and Digital Twin Data Fusion
abstract: Marine propulsion shafting operates under complex, variable conditions, where stern bearing wear and pedestal settlement redistribute loads, migrate vibration energy, and distort the shaft orbit, threatening safe operation. To address insufficient fault samples, difficulty in measuring degradation states directly, and limited interpretability of purely data-driven models, we propose a multilayer perceptron (MLP) condition assessment method driven by measured and digital twin data fusion. A digital twin framework comprising geometric, physical, rule-based, and behavioral models was constructed.

title: Preliminary bathymetric and interannual thermal stability screening for ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) along the eastern coast of Sorsogon Province, Philippines
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) uses the temperature gradient between the warm surface and the cold deep water. Existing thermal resource screening studies rely only on short observational campaigns or multi-decadal climatologies that characterize seasonal conditions but not year-to-year continuity. This study screens the eastern coast of Sorsogon Province, Philippines, integrating a 20-year (2005–2024) CMEMS GLORYS12V1 reanalysis with GEBCO bathymetry, interpolated to 10–1000 m and analyzed across rainy, cool-dry, and hot-dry seasons. abstract: Abstract A revision of the submarine landslides occurring in the Ischia offshore has been carried out, considering theoretical approaches, modeling, and seismo-stratigraphic data, focusing on the Ischia Island example. Based on the literature data, marine hazards and tsunami assessment have been considered. Although sidescan sonar data demonstrating the hummocky facies in the northern Ischia offshore have not been published, morpho-bathymetric data from earlier studies have been reinterpreted. abstract: Abstract. The primary production and zooplankton life cycles in the Southern Ocean synchronize with seasonal sea ice melting, during which particulate organic carbon (POC) and nitrogen (PN), including ice algae, are supplied from sea ice into the water column. To understand carbon flow through food webs in this productive marginal ice zones, it is necessary to determine the quantity and quality of organic carbon and nitrogen in sea ice. abstract: Abstract. Understanding the dynamics of terrestrial water storage (TWS), and its components such as surface soil moisture (SSM) and groundwater, is important for the Brahmaputra River Basin, where water resources are expected to experience increasing demand and are highly vulnerable to extreme hydrological events and climate change. However, water storage dynamics are complex and difficult to capture by state-of-the-art large-scale hydrological models. title: Inter-hemispheric contrast in the sensitivity of polar amplification to sea-ice coverage conditions
abstract: Polar amplification of near-surface warming can have substantial global implications. However, large uncertainties remain regarding its future changes and the underlying mechanisms. Here we show substantial inter-hemispheric contrast in the climate state dependence of polar amplification by analyzing both future and distant past climates. Climate model simulations indicate that both the amplitude and seasonality of Arctic amplification greatly weaken in future sea ice-free climates. title: A Digital Twin-Assisted Multi-Module Revit/HBIM Information-Integration Framework for Preventive Conservation of Chaoshan Overseas-Chinese Residences
abstract: Historic overseas-Chinese residences in hot–humid coastal regions face interconnected challenges involving surface deterioration, environmental performance, continued use, and long-term sustainability. Existing digital conservation studies often address these issues separately, resulting in fragmented information, weak spatial associations, and discontinuities across survey, diagnosis, intervention, and reinspection. title: Enhancing the GEOS Land Analysis with the Assimilation of CYGNSS Soil Moisture Retrievals
abstract: Abstract Soil moisture (SM) retrievals from the NASA Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) are assimilated into the NASA Goddard Earth Observing System (GEOS) land data assimilation system from August 2018 to June 2024. The system uses a 24-member ensemble Kalman filter to integrate CYGNSS 6-hourly SM retrievals alongside, or in place of, established datasets from the Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT), the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, and the Soil Moisture Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission. title: A cost-effective data assimilation system for improving ROMS simulations in the Southwest Atlantic
abstract: This study presents for the first time the integration of the low-cost REMO Ocean Data Assimilation System (RODAS) into the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) for assimilating Sea Surface Temperature (SST) observations. RODAS is an Ensemble Optimal Interpolation (EnOI)-based data assimilation system originally developed for use with the HYCOM model. Here, it is adapted to ROMS and applied to the Southwest Atlantic, with a focus on evaluating its impact on short-term ocean hindcasts. title: Ise Bay Reanalysis (IBRA): a 12-year ecological hydrodynamic reanalysis dataset for Ise Bay, Japan
abstract: Abstract. Reanalysis datasets based on coupled ocean circulation and ecosystem models are essential tools for understanding coastal environmental variability and supporting water quality management. However, the development of such datasets for highly enclosed coastal systems remains limited, particularly those incorporating subsurface biogeochemical observations, such as dissolved oxygen (DO). This study presents the Ise Bay Reanalysis (IBRA), a 12-year (2011–2022), high-resolution reanalysis dataset of hydrodynamic and biogeochemical variables for Ise Bay, Japan. title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m−2 day−1 per decade (p < 0.05). title: Compound marine heatwaves and atmospheric boundary layer jets drive enhanced coastal precipitation
abstract: Heavy coastal precipitation is traditionally attributed to atmospheric dynamics, but the influence of co-occurring oceanic thermal extremes remains largely unexplored. Using satellite observations and reanalysis data from 1998 to 2023 over the South China Sea (SCS), we investigate the synergistic impacts of marine heatwaves (MHWs) and atmospheric boundary layer jets (BLJs). We reveal a compound effect: when MHWs and BLJs co-occur, regional coastal precipitation increases by 51.9% relative to climatology, more than doubling the 21.0% increase during pure BLJ events.
