title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
abstract: Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). title: From nominalizer to verbalizer, from state to event: denominal verbs in -euō in early ancient Greek
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the diachronic development of the Ancient Greek suffix - eu - from a nominal marker into a verbalizer, focusing on the transition of - euō verbs from stative to activity/eventive meanings. Building on Distributed Morphology and the Hale & Keyser/Harley framework of denominal verb formation, we argue that verbal - eu - emerged through the reanalysis of “deagentive” denominal verbs, i.e., verbs derived from agentive animate nouns. abstract: Kota Dumai, sebagai pusat ekonomi maritim vital di pesisir Riau, memiliki kerentanan tinggi terhadap kejadian hujan lebat yang dapat mengganggu aktivitas industri dan pelabuhan. title: The 2025 Record Low in Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Dual Forcing from La Niña and Southern Indian Ocean Warm Anomaly
abstract: Abstract In February-March 2025, the Arctic experienced record-low sea ice extent, despite a decadal slowdown in ice loss [1,2]. Although a weak La Niña was present, its influence alone is insufficient to explain this extreme event. Here, we demonstrate that this record low on an interannual scale was driven by the synergistic effects of La Niña and concurrent South Indian Ocean warm anomaly (SIOW). title: Reconstructing a long-term atmospheric circulation of Venus from sparse observations
abstract: The atmospheric superrotation of Venus exhibits pronounced long-term variability and meridional asymmetry, yet its underlying dynamics remain poorly understood because available observations are severely limited in both space and time. Here we apply an existing Venus data assimilation system to multiple 6-month periods spanning distinct superrotation regimes beyond previously investigated intensive observation campaigns. title: Constraining the vertical profiles of aerosol component and heating rate over east Asia through assimilating CALIOP observations
abstract: Abstract. The vertical distribution of distinct aerosol components fundamentally governs atmospheric shortwave heating rates and radiative effects. However, traditional data assimilation (DA) methods typically rely on total aerosol optical thickness (AOT) or extinction, which fails to constrain the specific aerosol composition and often leads to the misallocation of aerosol between scattering and absorbing species. title: Lead isotope evidence for Antarctic Ice Sheet changes in the Weddell Sea sector since the Last Glacial Maximum
abstract: The Weddell Sea influences global ocean circulation and sea level through modulating Antarctic Bottom Water formation and Antarctic Ice Sheet discharges, but the history of ice‐sheet dynamics in this region remains poorly constrained due to limited well‐dated geological records. To provide a new geochemical perspective on ice‐sheet dynamics since the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), this study presents paired authigenic and detrital Pb isotope records from sediment core PS1599‐3 recovered from the continental slope north of the Filchner Trough. title: Experimental and finite element analysis of tubular auxetic structures with varying cross-sectional geometries
abstract: Abstract Tubular auxetic metamaterials are attractive for lightweight protection and energy absorption because their deformation can be regulated through structural design. However, the effects of different cross-sectional configurations on the compressive behavior of tubular auxetic lattices remain insufficiently compared within a unified framework. In this study, two tubular auxetic lattice metamaterials with square and circular cross sections, denoted as XATL and XATLC, were designed using the same unit-cell arrangement. title: Wind-regime modulation of cloud, precipitation and sea surface heat budget: case studies over the central Great Barrier Reef
abstract: The Great Barrier Reef (GBR) is increasingly threatened by marine heatwaves and mass coral bleaching events, with local atmospheric conditions playing a critical role in modulating sea surface temperatures and heat stress. This study examines how synoptic-to-mesoscale meteorological processes shaped cloud formation, precipitation and the ocean surface heat budget across the central GBR during the 2021–22 austral summer. title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here we assess the seasonal-to-multi-year predictability of MHW frequency, cumulative intensity, and duration across 12 coral reef regions. title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. abstract: High-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipes are widely used for seawater transportation. abstract: Wind resource assessment increasingly depends on integrating heterogeneous reanalysis data, turbine information, geospatial operations, and persistent computational services. abstract: Abstract Traditional sound-absorbing materials face a trade-off between structural thickness and low-frequency sound absorption. abstract: Abstract Calco-carbonic reactive transport controls the dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid, a key process shaping the hydraulic and geochemical evolution of carbonate aquifers. abstract: Typhoon wind prediction is important for disaster prevention. ERA5 reanalysis provides spatially continuous wind fields but may smooth local structures, whereas FY-3E WindRAD, a dual-frequency scatterometer, observes ocean surface winds through C-band and Ku-band measurements with sparse coverage and temporal mismatch. abstract: Tropical cyclone genesis (TCG) in the Northwest Pacific is strongly influenced by the interaction of large-scale oceanic and atmospheric environmental fields. This study investigates the spatiotemporal characteristics of TCG from 1991 to 2020 and examines the modulation mechanisms of major environmental factors. Tropical cyclone records from the China Meteorological Administration best-track dataset are combined with NOAA ERSST.v5 sea-surface temperature data and ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis fields. abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) provides a low-cost approach for observing sea surface winds with dense spatial and temporal sampling. The growing availability of multi-system GNSS-R observations further improves sampling capability, but differences among missions, transmitted signals, and receiving platforms still limit consistent multi-source retrieval and fusion. abstract: Numerical models provide essential tools for evaluating dynamics and responses of aquatic resources under different management actions and environmental conditions. abstract: Phase-resolving Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) simulations resolve details of wave overtopping that empirical and data-driven predictors do not provide, but configuring, running and post-processing a numerical wave flume requires considerable expertise in computational fluid dynamics. abstract: Abstract East Asian winter monsoon (EAWM) is a powerful circulation system that profoundly influences both regional and global climate. While extensive studies have explored the factors driving the EAWM variation, recent studies reveal that the EAWM is not always an integrated system, exhibiting a notable decoupling tendency in recent decades. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract The Consortium for the Advancement of Marine Arctic Science (CAMAS) has been created in response to the need for improved capabilities in Earth system modeling, specifically focused on the Arctic marine system. Designed to enable collaborative research, CAMAS has so far carried out a series of 3 hybrid workshops from 2024 to 2026. abstract: Citizens, scientists, and governmental agencies are generating vast datasets on beach macrolitter, generally reported as litter item inventories. Despite this richness of information, most assessments of coastal environmental status rely on total item counts, underutilizing data on item size and type. abstract: Abstract. Sub-mesoscale eddies are oceanic features crucial for energy transfer processes, transport of heat and biogeochemical tracers, and for promoting diversity in marine ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Mountain precipitation varies systematically with elevation—a relationship known as the elevation dependence of precipitation. This dependence governs hydrological partitioning and ecosystem stability in high‐mountain regions worldwide. abstract: Abstract Climate monitoring is essential for agricultural planning and environmental management, especially in regions with a low density of meteorological stations, such as the state of Mato Grosso, Brazil. abstract: Abstract The 2013–14 UK winter storm series was characterised by an exceptional frequency and persistence of storm events, with impacts arising from cumulative hydro-meteorological forcing rather than the intensity of individual storms. abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies, prevalent across the global ocean, play a crucial role in the transport and mixing of climate‐sensitive tracers such as heat, salt, and nutrients. abstract: Abstract The Kerguelen Plateau in the Southern Indian Ocean sustains intense phytoplankton blooms through local iron enrichment. abstract: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) introduced a global sulfur cap in 2020, reducing the maximum sulfur content of marine fuel oil from 3.5% to 0.5%. This study evaluated changes in ship-related PM₂.₅ across coastal and inland areas of Kyushu, western Japan, using eight years (2016–2023) of PM₂.₅ chemical composition data from eight monitoring sites. abstract: As a critical energy-saving component in reverse osmosis desalination systems, turbine-type energy recovery devices require rigorous dynamic stability evaluation. title: Risk of biases in estimating storm surge extremes: a global study
abstract: Abstract Extreme sea levels (ESLs) threaten coastal zones, and global assessments suggest that future ESLs grow with rising mean sea level (MSL) as the main driver. Conventional practice assumes that present-day return levels are added to a given MSL trajectory into the future to obtain future return levels. Here, we test this additive assumption and show that it may under- or overestimate ESLs with consequences for coastal protection decisions. abstract: Urban heatwaves require methods capable of capturing seasonality, persistence, and extreme temperature events. A retrospective modeling framework was developed for Guayaquil using reanalysis-based air temperature, oceanic anomalies, and satellite-derived land surface temperature. abstract: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. title: Eutrophication and hydrodynamic confinement shape establishment patterns of the invasive Atlantic blue crab in a hypersaline coastal lagoon
abstract: Coastal lagoons are highly vulnerable to biological invasions due to their environmental heterogeneity, hydrodynamic confinement and increasing anthropogenic disturbance. Despite the rapid expansion of the invasive Atlantic blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) across Mediterranean transitional ecosystems, the processes shaping its establishment remain poorly understood. abstract: Aerosol influences on local thunderstorms are complex and often contradictory. Within aerosol-laden city environments, these interactions are further complicated by additional thermodynamic and kinematic effects related to the urban landscape. Observational studies are limited in their ability to distinguish the different influences of urban land cover and aerosols on thunderstorms, but numerical modeling can alleviate the problem by systematically accounting for each variable separately. abstract: Winter wave variability along the Atlantic coast of Europe is strongly influenced by large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns. Understanding how these large-scale modes translate into regional wave climate variability across timescales remains a key challenge for coastal hazard predictability. Here, we investigate the relationships between winter-mean significant wave height and sea-level pressure (SLP) indices, using ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2025). abstract: High-altitude wind energy offers a vast and comparatively stable renewable resource, yet its development in China lacks systematic assessment that integrates generation system characteristics. This study establishes a multi-scale evaluation framework for China’s 1000 m altitude wind resources by coupling 45 years of ERA5 (ECMWF Reanalysis v5) data for 1980–2024, four nested WRF (Weather Research and Forecasting) simulations at 27, 9, 3 and 1 km for 2000–2024, and a standardized airborne wind energy power curve. abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. abstract: Abstract The Saharan Air Layer (SAL) is a warm, dry, and stable air mass that carries millions of tons of dust annually, disrupting otherwise intense convection in the tropical North Atlantic Ocean. abstract: Abstract. The Pine Island Ice Shelf can be analysed within three distinct sectors: northern, southern, and central. Dynamics within the Northern Pine Island Ice Shelf (N-PIIS) remain less understood than those of the Central Pine Island Ice Shelf. Using satellite imagery, reanalysis datasets, and in situ observations, we examined changes in ice-front position, velocity, thickness, rift propagation, and polynya activity across the N-PIIS since 1973. abstract: Abstract Shallow circulations in the tropics are related to the sea surface temperature distribution, longwave cooling above the boundary layer, and shallow convection in both observations and models. To understand the influences sea surface temperature has on the shallow circulation strength, fixed sea surface temperature distributions are applied in experiments using an idealized general circulation model with uniform insolation and no rotation. abstract: This study presents a site-specific seismic-source probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment for Manzanillo, Colima, a coastal city in Mexico vulnerable to local tsunamis due to its proximity to the subduction zone along the Mesoamerican Trench. Historical records show that the region has been affected by significant tsunamis, most notably in 1932 and 1995. abstract: Abstract The interannual variability of the Southern Hemisphere polar vortex plays a key role in ozone depletion and recovery but this variability and its teleconnection patterns are less understood than in the Northern Hemisphere. abstract: Abstract Multiple observational records indicate a long‐term weakening of the zonal sea surface temperature (SST) gradient in the tropical Atlantic, characterized by enhanced warming in the east. abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) has been identified as a necessary complement to industrial decarbonization for climate change mitigation. abstract: ABSTRACT The proboscis monkey ( Nasalis larvatus ) is an endangered colobine endemic to Borneo, largely confined to mangrove, peat‐swamp, and riverine forest and capable of swimming across the rivers and tidal channels that structure its habitat. abstract: Abstract Summer 2024 observed a record‐low tropical cyclone (TC) landfall activity over China, with only two landfalls representing a 59.8% reduction from the 1979–2023 climatological mean. This study investigates the characteristics and underlying mechanisms of this extreme suppression, revealing distinct monthly variations driven by divergent genesis‐related factors. In June, no TCs formed, attributable to an anomalously strong and westward‐extended western Pacific subtropical high (WPSH) that suppressed monsoon trough‐associated convection. title: Field-informed obstruction-based representation of mangroves alters hydrodynamic partitioning and enhances modeled sediment retention in a tide-influenced estuary
Impacts of Tide–Surge Interaction on Sediment Dynamics During Typhoons
abstract: Extreme weather conditions dominate sediment transports and thus determine morpho-dynamic evolution in coastal zones. Tide–surge interactions during extreme weather conditions modulate surge, and thus impact storm tides and sediment dynamics, especially in macro-tidal turbid estuaries. In this study, the macro-tidal turbid Hangzhou Bay (HZB) is selected as an example. A three-dimensional numerical model combining tide, wave, surge, and sediment was established in HZB and validated using field data. abstract: Abstract Indonesia experiences rapidly evolving convection modulated by strong land–sea interactions across the Maritime Continent, requiring frequent observations for accurate numerical weather prediction (NWP). Sparse in situ observations, particularly over oceans, make geostationary infrared satellite observations an important source for assimilation in Indonesia's NWP system. title: Jet-streak forcing and deep moisture transport during the 7 March 2025 record rainfall in Bahía Blanca, Argentina
abstract: Bahía Blanca (38.7°S, 62.2°W) experienced an unprecedented rainfall event on 7 March 2025, officially documented by the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) as a historical record with an estimated return period exceeding 100 years. This study provides an observationally based diagnosis of the event, testing the hypothesis that record precipitation resulted from the coupling between upper-level jet-streak-associated divergence, deep ascent and exceptional moisture transport. abstract: Abstract The current study is concerned with the development and experimental validation of the numerical model for rotary friction welding (RFW) of AA6061 Aluminum alloy using the finite element method in Abaqus/Standard. The main objective is to present an efficient and predictive tool for the optimization of the RFW process to reduce the dependency on costly and time-consuming physical experimentation. title: Tectonic shortening via sediment compaction in the subduction trench: Southern Hikurangi margin, New Zealand
abstract: Horizontal compressive stress in subduction zones is accommodated by both brittle and ductile deformation, from the deep megathrust to the seafloor. Compaction of sediments is an important, but poorly understood, component of the overall strain budget. Combining seismic depth imaging, P-wave velocities, sediment physical properties, and age constraints, we characterize horizontal shortening in the southern Hikurangi trench (New Zealand) and assess its contribution to the accommodation of plate motion. title: Tibetan Plateau uplift increased western North Pacific tropical cyclone frequency
abstract: Nearly one-third of global tropical cyclones (TCs) form over the western North Pacific (WNP), with severe hazards impacting Southeast and East Asia. TC genesis over the WNP underwent substantial shifts during the Cenozoic, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Tibetan Plateau uplift was crucial in shaping the present-day WNP TC genesis pattern. abstract: Harmful algal bloom (HAB) research in Vietnam has developed substantially over the past three decades, evolving from bloom observations and morphology-based identification toward multidisciplinary studies integrating taxonomy, ecology, phycotoxins, molecular phylogenetics, remote sensing, modeling, and food-safety monitoring. International collaborative programs, particularly HABViet under the ENRECA/DANIDA framework, played an important role in strengthening national capacity in taxonomy, culture techniques, toxin research, monitoring, infrastructure, and postgraduate training. title: How Thunderstorms Are Changing in Mexico: Trends and Characteristics
abstract: ABSTRACT Thunderstorms are among the most hazardous and common meteorological phenomena in Mexico, yet comprehensive assessments of their long‐term trends and associated characteristics remain absent. This study investigates changes in thunderstorm days and their environments in Mexico during 1992–2024 using a multisource approach that integrates surface weather station records, proximity soundings based on reanalysis data, and gridded lightning observations. abstract: Microplastic investigations require a clear distinction between visually suspected particles and chemically confirmed polymers to ensure analytical accuracy and reliable environmental interpretation. This study critically re-examined the reported particle morphologies, size distributions, and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectral assignments in fish gastrointestinal (GI) preparations collected from Pasacao, Camarines Sur, Philippines. title: Spatiotemporal trends in heat stress across Bangladesh from 1981 to 2023 using ERA5 temperature, relative humidity, and Heat Index
abstract: Global climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of extreme temperature events, particularly in climate-vulnerable regions such as Bangladesh. Heat waves have become an increasingly important climate hazard in recent decades. This study examines the spatiotemporal patterns of temperature, relative humidity, and the Heat Index (HI) across Bangladesh using ERA5 data from 1981 to 2023. title: Sustainable high performance computing in the UK: a position paper on public investment, accountability, and the path to net zero
abstract: The UK invests significantly in High-Performance Computing (HPC), yet has no coherent national strategy that addresses sustainability, accountability, or long-term infrastructure planning. This paper proposes and promotes three key messages: first, that the return on public investment cannot be assessed without consistent public reporting on utilisation, research outputs, and cost-effectiveness for all publicly funded HPC systems; second, that publicly funded HPC systems should be subject to mandatory, standardised reporting on energy consumption, carbon emissions, with information on what hap

title: Subsurface Weakness Amplification and Progressive Capacity Loss in Piled Port Structures under Repeated Operational Loading
abstract: Piled port structures experience repeated operational loading that may degrade soil–pile interaction and reduce foundation capacity over time. This study investigates subsurface weakness amplification and progressive capacity loss using three-dimensional finite element modelling of coastal soil profiles and pile systems under cyclic loading. Parametric analyses evaluated soil stiffness and loading variations to quantify degradation mechanisms. title: Experimental wind tunnel dataset of wake and turbine measurements for wind farm control
abstract: Abstract. Open-access experimental datasets play a central role in validating and benchmarking numerical models used in wind energy and wind-farm control research. However, publicly available datasets providing time-resolved turbine loads, actuator commands, and inflow characterisation under controlled operation remain scarce. This paper presents a new open-access experimental dataset from wind-tunnel experiments featuring actuated, instrumented, scaled wind turbine models. title: INDITEK ‐2.0: A Bayesian inverse modelling framework for mechanistic evolutionary processes
abstract: Abstract Mechanistic eco‐evolutionary models are powerful tools for understanding how life diversified over geological timescales, yet estimating their parameters remains a key challenge. The high computational requirements of these models make probabilistic inversion methods unfeasible. We introduce INDITEK‐2.0, a novel Bayesian inverse modelling framework built upon the cost‐efficient and spatially explicit INDITEK diversification engine. title: The role of Tibetan Plateau heat source in shaping the interdecadal Eurasian dual high‑temperature mode
abstract: Based on multi‑source reanalysis and numerical simulations, this study investigates the interdecadal variability of summer near‑surface air temperature over Eurasia and the role of the Tibetan Plateau atmospheric heat source (TPQ 1 ). A pronounced dual high temperature mode is identified, characterized by two synchronous warming centers located in Eastern Europe and the region from the northern Tibetan Plateau to Lake Baikal. title: Disentangling climate change and urbanization effects on future tropical cyclone compound flood hazards
abstract: Tropical cyclone-induced compound flooding poses a growing challenge for low-lying coastal megacities, as climate change and continued urban development may further intensify these hazards. Yet most planning frameworks and hazard assessments remain anchored in historical extremes, failing to account for how future conditions may fundamentally reshape disaster potential. title: A snow-jet bridging mechanism driving the Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation dipole
abstract: The Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation sustains billions of people across the two continents, and its variability strongly affects water supply, irrigation, and drought-flood risks. While this variability has been linked to air-sea interactions, its connection with land-surface signals remains unclear. title: Effect of High-Aspect-Ratio Appendages on the Steady-State Balance of a Primary Wind-Powered Containership
abstract: Abstract Adding a Wind Propulsion System (WPS) to a merchant ship generates an added resistance due to the additional aerodynamic side force. It is called sail-induced resistance. A large sail-induced resistance reduces the net thrust provided by the WPS and also indicates that the ship is sailing with large leeway angle and rudder angle, the latter being detrimental to the ship’s manoeuvrability. title: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies rainfall in extreme compound rainfall-wave events in the NW Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract The concurrent occurrence of extreme rainfall and energetic wave conditions can generate compound coastal hazards with impacts exceeding those produced by either driver alone. Although recent studies have identified changes in rainfall-wave extremes along the northwestern Mediterranean coast, whether these changes can be attributed to anthropogenic climate remains unclear. title: A Radio Science Experiment for Dragonfly to Investigate Titan's Rotation and Interior Structure
abstract: Abstract NASA's mission Dragonfly to Titan is scheduled for launch in 2028 with arrival in 2034 to study Titan's prebiotic chemistry and habitability. We propose a radio science experiment for Dragonfly, in which radiometric tracking of the rotorcraft from the Deep Space Network, already baselined for communications and navigation, is used as a precision geodetic instrument to measure Titan's rotational state and tidal deformations, without any modification to the spacecraft. title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Future Projections of the 400 mm Isohyet in China Based on Self-Organizing Maps
abstract: The 400 mm isohyet is an important geographical boundary in China. Owing to climate change, the spatial position of this precipitation line is shifting, which has significant impacts on agricultural production, population distribution, and ecosystems in China. First, precipitation data from 1950 to 2022 were obtained from the fifth-generation ECMWF atmospheric reanalysis (ERA5). The 400 mm isohyet was extracted from the gridded precipitation field and then resampled using an improved uniform parameterization method. title: Climate Variability Along the Northern Coast of Senegal: Analysis of Trends, Anomalies and Breaks at the Stations of Thies, Louga and Saint-louis (1994-2024)
abstract: The northern coast of Senegal, located on the western edge of the Sahel, is characterized by high climate variability, the repercussions of which directly affect the region's socio-economic activities, particularly market gardening in the Niayes area. This study aims to analyze the variability of rainfall and temperatures at the Thies, Louga, and Saint-Louis weather stations over the period 1994-2024, through the study of temporal trends, interannual anomalies, and breaks in the climate series. title: Grid-spacing sensitivity of Rossby wave breaking to mesoscale diabatic processes
abstract: Abstract. Forecast busts – episodes of abnormally low forecast skill – remain a persistent challenge for numerical weather prediction despite steady improvements in forecasting skill. Previous studies have highlighted the roles of moist mesoscale processes and diabatically generated potential vorticity (PV) anomalies in triggering rapid error growth and downstream circulation misrepresentation, processes whose representation is highly sensitive to model grid spacing. title: Atmospheric pressure, temperature, and online search activity for epilepsy: A daily time‐series study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Meteorological conditions have been investigated as potential short-term correlates of epileptic seizures, but findings remain inconsistent. This study examined whether daily meteorological variation was associated with population-level online information-seeking for epilepsy. METHODS: A daily time-series study was conducted in Lombardy, Italy, from September 1, 2021, to September 2, 2026. title: Revealing the Microphysical Distribution Characteristics of Arctic Mixed‐Phase Clouds
abstract: Abstract As a typical cloud type in the Arctic, the microphysical characteristics of Arctic stratiform mixed‐phase clouds (MPCs) are essential for understanding interactions among Arctic clouds, aerosols, and radiation. This study uses 1‐year of shipborne observations from the Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) expedition in the Arctic Ocean. title: Contrasting distribution and biomass trends of two sympatric redfish (Sebastes) species off Southeast Greenland
abstract: Sustainable harvest of fish stocks requires regular monitoring of abundance and biomass in space and time. In Southeast Greenland, two Sebastes species, beaked redfish ( Sebastes mentella ) and golden redfish ( S. norvegicus ), coexist and have been harvested together. However, the species differ greatly in stock status as beaked redfish are depleted, while golden redfish have a surplus of exploitable biomass. title: Ultra‐Thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites—Material Overview and Aspirations
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultra‐thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites (µt‐TBDC) are emerging as a transformative alternative to conventional continuous‐fiber composites, offering the potential to overcome longstanding limitations in manufacturability, waste, and design flexibility. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of µt‐TBDCs, spanning manufacturing, forming, mechanical characterization, and multi‐scale modelling. title: Impact of geomagnetic storm intensity on thermospheric density and orbital decay of LEO satellites: a G1–G5 per-event analysis
abstract: Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites in February 2022. Prior multi-event analyses have characterized this response primarily through superposed epoch analyses (SEA). title: Calculation of range-height indicator (RHI) scan eddy dissipation rate (EDR) map based on Doppler Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) velocity data
abstract: An algorithm based on a structure function approach is developed to calculate the Eddy Dissipation Rate (EDR) map from range-height indicator (RHI) scans of short range Light Detection and Ranging (SRLs) at the Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA). With particular consideration on the temporal and spatial resolution of the Doppler velocity data from SRLs as compared with EDR maps from long-range Light Detection and Ranging (LIDARs) already in use at HKIA. The characteristics of such RHI EDR maps is studied in representative cases of building-induced turbulence and terrain-induced turbulence.

title: Geometry-Aware Structural-Demand Screening and Vulnerable-Region Identification for a Ship Hull Under Coupled Heave–Pitch Motions
abstract: This paper presents a geometry-aware structural-demand screening framework for a ship hull subjected to coupled heave–pitch motions in head seas. The work addresses the need to move beyond hydrodynamic susceptibility alone toward hull-resolved structural interpretation, particularly for large ships in which wave-induced motions produce concentrated bending, shear, stress and vulnerability patterns. title: Infrasound Newtonian Noise Estimation at the Einstein Telescope Candidate Site Sos Enattos
abstract: Abstract We investigate the seasonal variability of atmospheric infrasound and its contribution to Newtonian noise (NN) at the Sos Enattos site, a leading candidate location for the Einstein Telescope (ET). Infrasound data recorded at three stations, SOE0 (surface), SOE1 (−84 m) and SOE3 (−160 m), are analysed over multiple seasons to characterise both the temporal variability and the depth dependence of the acoustic field. title: Spatial heterogeneity of air temperature and precipitation trends: a multi-scale physiographic perspective from central Mozambique (1994–2023)
abstract: Abstract Central Mozambique encompasses coastal, inland, and high-elevation environments, yet long-term climate trend assessments based on meteorological station data remain limited. Spatial and temporal trends in mean air temperature and total precipitation were analyzed across ten locations over the period 1994–2023. Missing values were reconstructed using monthly scaling with NASA POWER data. title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. title: An experimentally calibrated MBD–DEM framework for ice fracture, fragmentation, and dispensing in a refrigerator ice maker
abstract: In the highly competitive home appliance market, the dispensing and crushing performance of built-in ice makers has become a critical quality attribute affecting both user satisfaction and product competitiveness. However, conventional product development processes still rely heavily on reactive trial-and-error approaches, which may lead to substantial economic losses during the later stages of mass production. title: Numerical study of hybrid Euler–Euler multiphase modeling in bottom-purged industrial-scale steel ladle
abstract: Abstract In steelmaking, inert gas injection is widely employed during ladle refining to enhance mixing and promote chemical reactions. Argon is injected through the bottom of the ladle, inducing a turbulent recirculating flow that improves heat and mass transfer. This agitation promotes molten metal homogenization, inclusion removal via the slag layer, alloy mixing, and slag-metal reactions. In this study, a numerical model based on a Hybrid RANS/LES turbulence approach was developed to simulate gas–liquid flow in an industrial 185-ton steel ladle. title: Investigation of multi-DOF WEC S-shaped buoy configurations in the nearshore region of East China
abstract: This study proposes a multi-DOF WEC employing S-shaped buoy profiles and a mechanically integrated PTO system tuned for site-specific nearshore wave conditions. The system uses heave and coupled surge/pitch motions, while the proposed PTO mechanism mechanically synthesizes the corresponding modal responses into a unified transmission path and represents their damping contributions through a single equivalent PTO damping coefficient. title: Improved Feed Additives and Grazing Management are Likely Suboptimal Strategies for Reducing the Carbon Costs of Beef
abstract: I analyze research thrusts meant to reduce the carbon costs of the most resource intensive food item, beef. Using numerical modeling and data, I analyze the two most vigorously promoted ideas: Improving feed additives for reducing methane emissions, and enhancing soil carbon sequestration via better managed grazing. I find that even with the realistically expected emission reductions of these research thrusts, beef emissions remain higher than those associated with producing alternatives (including pork, poultry, or dairy). title: How ENSO controls the propagation speed of seasonal onsets in Java–Bali: satellite rainfall evidence over two decades
abstract: Indonesia, as a tropical maritime continent, exhibits a seasonal rainfall pattern influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Variations in the Wet Season Onset (WSO) and Dry Season Onset (DSO) have broad implications for agriculture, water resources and disaster mitigation. This study aims to analyse the climatology and interannual variability of WSO and DSO over the Java–Bali region (104–116°E), using satellite-based rainfall data (1998–2024). title: Indo-Gangetic Plain experiences higher aerosol pollution than North China Plain despite lower emissions
abstract: Abstract We investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of aerosol pollution in the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) and the North China Plain (NCP), two of the world’s most populated regions, against their anthropogenic emissions. Utilizing CAMS EAC4 reanalysis, CAMS-GLOB-ANT emission inventories, and ERA5 meteorological data for the year 2019, we analyze the seasonally changing relationship between PM-forming emissions and ambient PM 2.5 concentrations. title: BEMT-based blade twist optimisation of a tiltrotor in hover using artificial bee colony algorithm
abstract: Abstract In this study, the aerodynamic effects of rotor blade twist geometry on the hover performance of the XV-15 tiltrotor were investigated. For this purpose, the twist distribution of the XV-15 tiltrotor was optimised under hover conditions using the artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm coupled with a Blade Element Momentum Theory (BEMT)-based numerical model validated against the NASA Ames experimental data. The blade twist was parameterised using a fifth-order continuous polynomial, whose coefficients were optimised to minimise the power coefficient while maintaining a constant thrust.

title: Direct Reuse of Uncured CFRP Prepreg Scraps for Structural Applications: Experimental Qualification and Numerical Validation of an Automotive Battery Case
abstract: ABSTRACT The high demand for fiber‐reinforced composite materials generates large quantities of uncured prepreg waste, still in pristine condition, usually landfilled or incinerated. Among the various established recycling routes, direct reuse of these scraps represents an attractive strategy to reduce both raw material consumption and manufacturing waste, while preserving the original constituents' properties, and avoiding energy‐intensive recovery processes or the use of hazardous chemicals, thus moving an energy demanding industry toward sustainability. title: Environmental and Operational Implications of Dynamic Positioning Failures in Offshore Operations: A Review of IMCA Reports from 2018 to 2024
abstract: Dynamic Positioning (DP) systems are widely used in offshore operations such as drilling, subsea construction, cable laying, offshore renewable energy support, and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) operations. As offshore activities become increasingly dependent on DP capability, failures in DP systems may result in operational disruption, safety concerns, and environmental exposure. Although advances in automation and redundancy have improved DP system reliability, the offshore industry continues to report DP incidents and undesired events. title: Influence of climate warming and land-cover change on aerobiological pollen season in Estonia
abstract: Abstract Pollen allergy is an increasing public health concern in Europe, as climate warming alters flowering phenology and airborne-pollen dynamics. This study analysed temporal and spatial changes in pollen seasons in Estonia using aerobiological monitoring data from Tartu, Tallinn, and Pärnu. Temporal changes were assessed by comparing two monitoring periods in Tartu (1990–1998 and 2012–2022), while spatial differences were evaluated across stations in contrasting climatic settings. title: Late Quaternary lake filling and drying in northern Australia's largest freshwater lake
abstract: ABSTRACT Lake Woods, Jurrkulu, is northern Australia's largest freshwater lake filled today in strong Indo–Australian summer monsoons (IASM) to maximum depths of ~5 m. On the western margins of the lake, two large arcuate ridges occur 20 to 40 m above the lake floor and inset within these are other mid‐elevation lake deposits, such as depositional ridges, which suggest past filling events much higher than the modern maximum. title: Disentangling atmospheric transport and mixing processes over mountains: overview of the preliminary field campaigns of the project DECIPHER
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the rationale, experimental design and preliminary outcomes of two field campaigns undertaken as part of the project DECIPHER at two mountain sites in the Italian Alps to investigate surface-layer processes and turbulent fluxes associated with slope-wind systems. The first campaign (23 July-29 October 2024) was concentrated at Col Margherita (2543 m above sea level (ASL) )and nearby Passo Valles. title: Parametric Study on Cyclic Behavior of Hexagonal Concrete-Filled Steel Tubular Columns
abstract: The seismic performance of columns plays a decisive role in the safety of steel–concrete composite structures. Although the seismic behavior of concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) columns has been extensively investigated. However, the cyclic behavior of hexagonal concrete-filled steel tubular (HCFST) columns equipped with continuously distributed Perfobond Rib (PBL) shear connectors along the column has not yet been comprehensively studied. title: Global patterns of treeline predictability and the gap between the forest and the treeline
abstract: The alpine treeline is the highest elevation at which trees can grow, which is assumed to be controlled by temperature and globally predictable. However, many upper forest limits (UFLs) do not reach this elevation, due natural factors and human disturbance. A large elevational distance between UFLs and the climatic treeline can indicate that human activities have removed mountain forest or prevented it from tracking treeline under climate warming. title: Hydrological control and distributed rainfall-runoff modeling of flood inflows from the Bt River to the Aghien Lagoon (Cte dIvoire) using the ATHYS software
abstract: Quantifying hydrological contributions from tributaries to lagoon systems represents a major challenge for understanding the functioning of coastal hydrosystems and for the sustainable management of water resources, particularly in tropical environments exposed to strong climatic and anthropogenic pressures.This study aims to assess flood contributions from the Bété River to Lagune Aghien, a strategic potential resource for the drinking water supply of Abidjan, through distributed rainfall-runoff modeling using the ATHYS model.The methodological approach relies on hydrometeorological time seri

title: From Fault Ruptures to Atmospheric Perturbations: Examining the 2016 Norcia Seismic Sequence

title: Analysis of the Contribution of Potato Production to the Local Socioeconomic Structure in Fena Fafan Subdistrict, South Buru Regency
abstract: Fena Fafan Subdistrict is the only region in South Buru Regency producing potatoes, situated at an elevation of 575 meters above sea level—an altitude ideal for optimal potato growth. This study aims to analyze the contribution of potato production to the local socio-economic structure. A descriptive quantitative method was used, utilizing secondary data from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) for the years 2020–2024. title: Experimental Exploration into Al 7075-T651 Machinability, Surface Quality, and MRR Using Avocado Cutting Fluid via Grey Optimization
abstract: This research aims to identify the optimal machining parameters for turning Aluminium Alloy 075-T651 using a tungsten carbide insert cutting tool and a flood coolant system, applying the Grey-based Taguchi method. Aluminium Alloy 075-T651 is commonly utilized in the automotive, marine, machine tools, and aerospace industries due to its excellent weight-to-strength ratio. A key focus of the study are the surface roughness and material removal rate, which is critical in machining. journal: International Journal of Mechanical Engineering and Applications

title: Integrated in vivo Anti-Inflammatory, Antioxidant-Related, and Preliminary Acute Oral Toxicity Responses to Gracilaria gracilis Extract
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress reinforce one another and are important targets in the development of marine-derived pharmacological candidates. This study evaluated the in vivo anti-inflammatory and antioxidant-related effects of an ethanol extract of BRIN-authenticated Gracilaria gracilis and included a separate preliminary single-dose oral toxicity assessment. Dried seaweed (300 g) was macerated with 96% ethanol in three 24-h cycles at a 1:3 (w/v) ratio, producing 24.5 g extract (8.17%, w/w). title: Performance assessment of urban drainage systems using a river–pipe–surface coupled modeling approach
abstract: Study Region: The HUA district represents a typical low-lying urbanized floodplain within a coastal megacity, where a high-density municipal pipe network directly intersects a dynamic river system, making it a regional model for studying compound waterlogging under the nonlinear interaction of localized precipitation and fluctuating downstream river boundaries. Study Focus: The research develops an integrated evaluation framework combining a river–pipe–land two-way dynamically coupled hydraulic model with a multi-level Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). title: A methodology for integrating Life Cycle Assessment into a Multidisciplinary Design Analysis and Optimization framework for sustainable launcher development
abstract: The increasing number of orbital and sub-orbital launches makes it necessary to investigate the environmental impacts of launch vehicles and to incorporate eco-design considerations into their development. In response to these emerging concerns, the European Space Agency has promoted the use of the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology as a standardization to support the mitigation of environmental impacts associated with present and future space missions. title: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1: implementation and computational evaluation
abstract: Abstract. Understanding the complete lifecycle of cloud hydrometeors is fundamental to advancing cloud microphysics, yet a formally documented and computationally efficient framework for tracking individual particles through complex processes like coalescence within parallelized cloud models has been lacking. title: Temperature-sensitivity of water stable isotopes in global precipitation: a groundwater noble gas-based, paleoclimate perspective
abstract: Water stable isotopes (δ2H and δ18O) are widely used to reconstruct past hydrological changes and paleoclimate variability. A key limitation, however, is that fossil isotope records reflect not only local temperature but also changes in circulation, moisture sources, and hydrological processes along air-mass trajectories. Although modern monthly and interannual δ2H–δ18O–temperature relationships have been proposed to calibrate paleoclimate reconstructions, their applicability to longer timescales, such as glacial–interglacial transitions, remains uncertain. title: Possible Reasons Why the Lp(a)HORIZON Lipoprotein(a)-Lowering Trial Failed to Demonstrate Improved Clinical Outcomes: Implications for Laboratory Medicine
abstract: The Lp(a)HORIZON trial aimed to determine whether lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] reduction using the drug pelacarsen could reduce cardiovascular (CV) risk in patients with both established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and an Lp(a) level ≥70 mg/dL (approximately 149 nmol/L), whose other CV risk factors were otherwise already treated optimally (1). On September 4, 2026, the topline results of the trial were announced stating that the trial failed to meet its primary endpoint of reducing the risk of CV events (2). journal: The Journal of Applied Laboratory Medicine

title: Seasonal Modulation of ENSO Teleconnections to Horn of Africa Rainfall
abstract: Abstract Rainfall over the Horn of Africa (HoA) exhibits pronounced interannual variability linked to the El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO). However, the seasonal evolution of ENSO‐driven rainfall anomalies is not adequately explained by the ENSO, particularly the Niño3.4 index. The results here show that nonlinear interactions between ENSO and both semiannual and annual migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone generate a combination mode (C‐Mode) that modulates the timing and amplitude of the HoA regional rainfall. title: Corrosion Hotspots Strongly Localize Crack Origins But Provide Conditional Timing Information
abstract: ABSTRACT Published specimen‐level data from 36 pre‐corroded structural‐steel fatigue specimens relevant to offshore applications were re‐analyzed to separate crack‐origin localization from crack‐initiation timing. Localization was available for 34 specimens and digital‐image‐correlation‐based timing for 21. Crack origins coincided with the global finite‐element hotspot in 20/34 specimens (58.8%) and with a global or near‐global hotspot in 31/34 (91.2%). journal: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures

title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
abstract: The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m−2 d−1) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m−2 d−1), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. title: Biases and predictability limits of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones in subseasonal prediction systems
abstract: Abstract Subseasonal prediction of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones (ETCs) is critical for anticipating associated weather extremes, yet biases and predictability limits of ETC activity in current forecast systems remain insufficiently quantified. Here, using hindcasts from ten state-of-the-art subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction systems within a Lagrangian tracking framework, we uncover a common and pervasive bias: the multi-model ensemble consistently predicts fewer and weaker cyclones at a one-month lead, underestimating frequency by 10-18% and intensity by approximately 13%,

title: Climate change effects on analogues of contrasting extratropical cyclones over the UK, Ireland and France
abstract: Abstract. Extreme extratropical cyclones present major socio-economic risks in the United Kingdom and are sensitive to anthropogenic climate change. Robust projections of the aggregate properties of extreme cyclones based on climate-model output have emerged in recent years. However, such projections average together cyclones with a range of contrasting dynamical characteristics potentially obscuring climate change effects on particular types of cyclones and the airstream structures within them. title: The impact of atmospheric rivers on the water level and hydrology in a lake in south-Central Chile
abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are major drivers of hydroclimatic extremes in mid-latitude regions, with important implications for water resource management and climate services. This study evaluates the hydroclimatic and hydrological response of Lake Villarrica in south-central Chile to AR landfalls during 2000–2024. ARs were identified using an ERA5-based catalog and classified as Zonal (ZARs) or Tilted Atmospheric Rivers (TARs) according to integrated vapor transport direction. title: Science and policy to manage nitrogen with cover crops—The Maryland experience
abstract: During the 1980s, research showed nitrogen-stimulated eutrophication was contributing to the Chesapeake Bay's deterioration, and cover crop research shifted from legumes to replace fertilizer, to winter cereals to reduce nitrogen (N) leaching. The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) adopted nutrient regulations and added technical and financial resources promoting N-capturing cover crops and N-use efficiency. Today, Maryland's "Clean the Bay" effort includes regulations and generous cost-sharing for planting and terminating cover crops. The MDA supports cover cropping on ∼180,000 ha annua

title: Assessment of Human Thermal Stress Dynamics and Regional Drivers Across the Arabian Peninsula During 1990–2022 From Observations
abstract: ABSTRACT Human thermal stress is intensifying in the Arabian Peninsula (AP); however, a lack of consensus in observational evidence continues to limit a quantitative understanding of trends and the relative influence of the meteorological drivers underlying regional variability. In this study, we used 33 years (1990–2022) of in situ meteorological observations from 75 stations across the AP to assess the variability and trend of human thermal stress, expressed through the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), together with an information flow analysis quantifying the directional information

title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. title: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
abstract: Abstract. Nuclear conflicts could ignite intense urban fires that inject considerable amounts of black carbon (BC) into the upper atmosphere, with the potential to disrupt global climate. While uncertainties in the total BC injection remain large, relatively few modeling studies and limited model diversity have explored the climatic response to low-to-moderate BC injections, leaving key aspects of their climate impact poorly understood. title: Experimental Study of Duct Cross-Sectional Area Reduction on Oscillating Water Column Performance Using Wave Period Variations
abstract: The development of renewable energy is a key approach to reducing fossil fuel dependence. This study examines the effect of modifying duct geometry into a convergent nozzle shape in an Oscillating Water Column (OWC) system. Experiments were conducted in a laboratory wave flume using sensors to measure wave height and pressure across nine wave period variations. Results show that reducing the cross-sectional area increases pressure by 57% and velocity by 44%, consistent with Bernoulli’s principle. title: Long-term climate variability and implications for groundwater recharge potential and saltwater intrusion vulnerability in the Cape Flats Aquifer, South Africa
abstract: The Cape Flats Aquifer (CFA) is a critical groundwater resource supporting urban, agricultural, and ecological needs in the Western Cape, South Africa. However, its sustainability is increasingly threatened by seasonal climate variability, which strongly influences groundwater recharge. This study examined seasonal rainfall and temperature variability and their potential implications for groundwater recharge and susceptibility to saltwater intrusion in the CFA. journal: Asian Journal of Water Environment and Pollution

title: Convection‐Permitting Simulations of Extreme Hourly Rainfall and Land‐Surface Impacts in the Middle‐Lower Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Abstract Extreme precipitation events frequently cause severe socioeconomic losses, making accurate forecasting critical. However, prediction of extreme precipitation remains challenging due to multi‐scale nonlinear interactions. Previous studies have largely attributed extreme rainfall to large‐scale circulation or mesoscale convective systems, the role of complex underlying surfaces remains insufficiently understood. title: Dynamic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves
abstract: This study investigates the seismic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves, considering dynamic soil–structure interaction (SSI). The analysis is conducted using the OpenFAST numerical framework, extended with an SSI model to represent the dynamic impedance of pile foundations. Additionally, the tool was adapted to account for the non-synchronous excitation at the different supports that arises from the arrival of obliquely incident planar waves or surface waves. title: An Investigation of the Characteristics of Indian Summer Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems Under Stratospheric Aerosol Geoengineering
abstract: Abstract Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems (LPSs) that govern the rainfall of the Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) contribute more than half of its rainfall and extreme rainfall events. In this study, we explore how LPS activity changes under greenhouse warming and Stratospheric Aerosol Intervention (SAI) using simulations from the fully coupled CESM2.1.3 climate model. title: Novel Filament‐Wound FRP Composite Tubes Integrated Grid Ribs and Multi‐Angle Winding Layer: Manufacturing, Interfacial Behavior and Proof‐of‐Concept Validation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial slip between concrete and fiber‐reinforced polymer (FRP) tubes remains a key concern in concrete‐filled FRP tube members. This study proposes a novel concrete‐filled FRP tube integrated with designable grid ribs and multi‐angle winding layers (GR‐CFFT). The internal grid ribs are intended to enhance rib–concrete mechanical interlocking, reduce interfacial slip, and improve the contribution of longitudinal reinforcement layers to flexural resistance. title: Quiet Time Ionosphere‐Thermosphere Predictability During Sudden Stratospheric Warmings in TIE‐GCM
abstract: Abstract We investigate the predictability of the ionosphere‐thermosphere (IT) region during sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs) by using subseasonal hindcasts in the Community Earth System Model, version 2 with the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (CESM2 [WACCM6]) to force the lower boundary of the TIE‐GCM. The extension of subseasonal hindcasts into the IT region enables the first comprehensive investigation of IT predictability during SSWs. title: A hybrid statistical–dynamical approach for seasonal prediction of the boreal winter stratosphere
abstract: Abstract The winter variability of the Northern Hemisphere Stratospheric Polar Vortex (SPV) is characterized by extreme events known as Sudden Stratospheric Warmings (SSWs). SSWs feature a rapid temperature increase and a reversal of the zonal winds in the SPV, exerting a downward impact on the troposphere. Yet, despite their importance, current seasonal prediction systems (SPSs) show limited skill in forecasting SPV variability and SSW occurrence. title: Spatial representativeness of total column ozone monitoring in Reykjavik, Iceland, and its regional significance in the North Atlantic region
abstract: Abstract In 2021, a double monochromator Brewer spectrophotometer was installed in Reykjavik, Iceland, complementing the long-term Dobson total column ozone (TCO) observations at this site. To assess the spatial representativeness of this TCO time series, the reanalyzed ERA5 TCO daily mean values in the area north of N 40° have been analyzed. A good agreement was found between the Brewer and ERA5 TCO, with almost no systematic bias and a RMSE of 7.7 DU (2.1%). title: How Does Terrain Relief of the Tibetan Plateau and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau Individually Modulate Summer Regional Hourly Extreme Precipitation in the Sichuan Basin, China?
abstract: Abstract The influence of terrain relief over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau on summer regional hourly extreme precipitation (RHEP) in the Sichuan Basin (SCB) under two dominant synoptic patterns remains poorly understood. Here, this study uses multi‐case Weather Research and Forecasting sensitivity experiments, in which the terrain relief of two plateaus is individually smoothed, to systematically investigate these modulation mechanisms. title: Hydrogen: Global budget, atmospheric measurements, climate impacts and sustainable aviation fuel
abstract: Hydrogen (H 2 ) has a key role in helping the world reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 by complementing other decarbonization pathways such as direct electrification, biofuels, synthetic fuels (e-fuels), carbon capture and storage (CCS), nuclear fission, wind energy, etc. The interest in the climate impact and behaviour of H 2 in the troposphere has been increasing as the research and infrastructure expands to support the clean energy transition. title: Black carbon aerosols intensified India’s 2015 mega heatwave and expanded heat stress exposure
abstract: Abstract Large-scale climatic drivers are known to amplify heatwave temperatures, whereas aerosols have complex regional temperature responses depending upon aerosol composition. With the help of recent observations and chemistry-coupled regional climate model simulations, we show that coincident aerosols—black carbon in particular—elevated the heatwave intensity of India’s deadly 2015 heatwave event. title: A new method for detecting aerosols: combining atmospheric detection LiDAR technology with intelligent driving technology
abstract: Abstract. The existing aerosol mobile detection system has problems such as over-reliance on labor power and difficulty in conducting continuous operations in toxic and polluted environments. This paper presents a new method for detecting aerosols. The method combines atmospheric detection LiDAR technology and intelligent driving technology. Through modular design (including control module, aerosol detection module, environment sensing and positioning module, and wire control chassis module), an intelligent cruise detection system for aerosols was built. title: Comprehensive assessment of historical surface air temperature simulations over iran using 51 CMIP6 models
abstract: Reducing uncertainty in regional surface air temperature (SAT) projections is essential for climate-resilient planning in countries such as Iran, where complex terrain and limited adaptive capacity heighten climate vulnerability. This study systematically evaluated 51 CMIP6 models, the conventional equally weighted multi-model ensemble (MME) and performance-based Weighted Multi-Model Ensemble (WMME) against CRU_TS4.08 observations for historical SAT over Iran during 1980–2014. title: Climate risk assessment in tropical wetlands through integrated hydroclimatic, land cover, and community knowledge
abstract: Abstract Climate-risk assessments in tropical wetlands increasingly combine hydroclimatic and land-cover data, but rarely integrate them with structured community evidence on experienced impacts and adaptation priorities. We address this gap in six communities around the Complejo Cenagoso de Zapatosa, a Ramsar site, and the Morales wetland in the Colombian Caribbean. We integrated hydroclimatic records and climate-extreme indices (1991-2020), land-cover change and runoff-potential analysis (1991-2020), flood-susceptibility modelling, and structured participatory evidence from 106 participants.

title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Stratosphere–troposphere exchange of ozone
abstract: Stratosphere-troposphere exchange (STE) of ozone is a significant source of tropospheric ozone, influencing air quality, atmospheric chemistry and climate forcing. This assessment synthesizes recent advances in understanding the magnitude, mechanisms, variability and future evolution of ozone transport across the tropopause, updating earlier reviews using observations, reanalyses and global chemistry-climate models. title: Analysis of technologies for biogas production through filtration and utilisation of wastewater in an urban environment

title: The Eco‐Digital Dimension in Children's and Young Adult Literature for Early Childhood and Primary Teacher Education: An Exploratory Inquiry
abstract: ABSTRACT Although ecological topics are gaining increasing relevance in children's and young adult literature, the intersection between environmental sustainability and digital media remains under‐researched. The two main research questions of this qualitative exploratory study are: how the eco‐digital dimension manifests within contemporary children's and young adult literature formats (RQ1), and how an eco‐digital webbook format can be integrated into initial teacher education for kindergarten and primary school (RQ2). title: Digital Nation: Can a State Exist Without Its Territory? Legal Challenge of Tuvalu and Other Endangered Islands
abstract: The article examines the transformation of the concept of statehood in the context of climate change and technological advancement, with particular emphasis on the case of Tuvalu. It addresses the question of whether a state that has lost its physical territory may continue to exist as a subject of international law. The analysis focuses on the legal concept of statehood, the criteria of statehood enshrined in the Montevideo Convention, and the challenges associated with their application to disappearing island states. title: A new method to derive water vapor supersaturation at cumulus cloud base from in situ measurements
abstract: Abstract. We quantify water vapor supersaturation (Sv) at warm cloud base by describing the ascent of a saturated (cloudy) air parcel as a reversible cloud-adiabatic process. In this framework, the parcel’s isobaric enthalpy is conserved along the ascent. title: Constitutive Expression Differences and Thermal Responses of Stress-Associated Transcripts in Pacific Abalone
abstract: We examined basal and exposure-associated transcript abundance in Pacific abalone. Pi3k, Akt, mTOR, Hsf1, Hsp70, and Hsp90 were compared across five anatomical samples and between heat-selected and common populations after identical two-week acclimation. Five transcripts were examined during adult exposure to 30 °C for up to 72 h and after a 15 min larval heat shock. title: More than meets the eye: artificial eyelashes as an unrecognized source of microplastics and heavy metals
abstract: Despite growing concern over microplastic pollution, leave-on cosmetic products such as artificial eyelashes remain largely unexplored as sources of microplastics and associated contaminants. Here, nine artificial eyelash products were characterized for polymer composition, heavy metal content, and fiber release under simulated environmental conditions. Three polymers were identified: PBT (55.56%), PET (33.33%), and PVC (11.11%). title: Influence of groundwater seasonality on suspended sediment dynamics, in a 20 km 2 Mediterranean mountainous catchment
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the interplay between groundwater and surface runoff in controlling suspended sediment dynamics within the Galabre catchment, a 20 km² Mediterranean mountainous catchment characterized by extensive badland areas. Using an End-Member Mixing Analyzing framework that accounts for event-specific variability in end-member chemistry, the study quantifies surface runoff and groundwater contributions during 86 flood events spanning three hydrological years. title: Methodological Approaches to Analyzing the Economic Impacts of Geoclimatic Risks in Russia
abstract: Global geoclimatic shifts pose substantial risks to the Russian economy, including infrastructure degradation, declining agricultural productivity, and structural challenges associated with the energy transition. The study is motivated by the need to critically evaluate existing climate-economic modeling approaches and assess their applicability to Russian conditions. The objective is to propose an ensemble framework capable of addressing structural uncertainty in climate-economic projections. Method . title: Cessation of Nearby Low‐Frequency Earthquake Activity Following the December 2024 M w 7.0 Mendocino Earthquake: The Likely Role of Pore Pressure Reductions
abstract: Abstract Earthquakes affect surrounding fault systems through multiple mechanisms. Here, we examine a rare cessation of activity in 27 families of low‐frequency earthquakes (LFEs) that likely reflect fault creep at the southern edge of Cascadia subduction, near the Mendocino triple junction. These sources usually exhibit nearly daily activity but were shut off for ∼7–25 days following the December 2024 moment magnitude ( M w ) 7.0 Mendocino fault earthquake. title: Heat extremes threaten cattle and outdoor workers across northern Australia’s extensive grazing systems
abstract: Australia is projected to warm throughout the 21st century, raising the risk of dangerous heat for livestock and the people who work with them, yet these changes have not been quantified for the extensive grazing systems of northern Australia. Here we employ a seven-model ensemble of regionally downscaled climate projections to quantify future changes in cattle heat load and the maximum safe metabolic rate for outdoor work under lower- and higher-emission pathways (Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) 1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0) at mid- and late-century. abstract: Shipbuilding is a complex project-based production environment in which maturity scores averaged across shipyards can obscure important organizational differences.This study assesses project management maturity in 32 Turkish shipyards using the Portfolio, Programme and Project Management Maturity Model (P3M3 ® ) version 2.1 Self-Assessment Tool and examines whether an aggregate result conceals distinct maturity configurations.One manager from each participating shipyard completed a Turkish questionnaire distributed through the Turkish Shipbuilders' Association (GİSBİR).The analysis covered 24

title: Global Multi‐Model Eddy Dissipation Rate Probability Density Functions for Clear‐Air Turbulence Under Climate Change
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric turbulence poses a major risk to aviation, and it is expected to intensify as a response to climate change. The probability density functions (PDFs) of dozens of different clear‐air turbulence (CAT) diagnostics have been found to shift to higher values in response to climate change, consistent with strengthened vertical wind shear at cruising altitudes. title: A Lower Bound on the Altitude of the Hiroshima Firestorm Plume From Ray Optics
abstract: Abstract Projections of nuclear winter are critically sensitive to the height of soot lofted by firestorms, yet direct observations of firestorm plumes are scarce. Here, a lower bound is established for the height of the Hiroshima firestorm plume 97 min after detonation. This bound is obtained via a ray‐optics calculation using the Enola Gay 's flight log, which gives the location and time when the plume was last visible. title: Projected weakening of Northern Hemisphere summertime high-latitude waveguide and teleconnection variability
abstract: Summertime high-latitude teleconnections shape persistent circulation anomalies and surface climate extremes across the Northern Hemisphere, yet their future evolution under anthropogenic warming remains poorly constrained. Using 31 CMIP6 models under SSP5-8.5, we examine projected changes in the high-latitude waveguide, teleconnection variability, and the resulting surface air temperature (SAT) response. title: Effect of sub-critical fluid shear flow on granular bed strength
abstract: Interactions between fluids and granular materials are prevalent on the Earth's surface. In the case of fluid flow over a sediment bed, the fluid imparts a shear stress to the granular materials. When the applied shear stress is above a critical value, the grains become entrained in the fluid flow. Prior experimental studies have shown that granular beds subjected to a sub-critical fluid flow can strengthen in the same direction as the sub-critical flow. abstract: Abstract. Spaceborne active CO2 IPDA lidar provides an active remote-sensing approach for XCO2 observations that differs from passive NIR/SWIR remote sensing. However, comparisons between DQ-1 ACDL and passive optical satellite XCO2 products remain limited. abstract: Abstract Glaciers produce abundant grains of reactive minerals that influence inorganic carbon cycling, yet the links between mineral weathering and CO 2 dynamics in glacier-fed streams (GFSs) remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified daily, gridded CO emissions in Central Asia (Xinjiang-China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan) for 2019–2024. abstract: The operational efficiency of water-lubricated rotary interfaces, i.e., fundamental load-bearing and sealing elements in fluid-energy systems, is severely bottlenecked by the inherently low load-carrying capacity of low-viscosity water films. abstract: Study region Southwest China (SWC). title: Cometary impacts an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth
abstract: Abstract An early period of cometary bombardment has long been speculated to provide an important source of prebiotic feedstock molecules, required for the origins of life on Earth. In support of this interpretation, comets boast a rich diversity of volatile organic molecules, with many thought to be limiting for prebiotic chemistry. title: Replica revolutions in rock art: from physical replicas to virtual reality libraries via contemporary art
abstract: Rock-art replicas generally are judged as more or less faithful substitutes for inaccessible originals. While previous studies have demonstrated the value of replicas for individual archaeological experiments, we reconceive them as persistent interdisciplinary research infrastructure. Drawing on reflections from original sites, we compare physical copies with virtual environments, developing criteria for evaluating replicas. title: Climate change impacts on the predicted performance of optimized building-integrated photovoltaics
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) are a promising strategy for enhancing building energy performance and reducing carbon emissions. However, most design optimization studies rely on historical climate datasets that may fail to capture the operating conditions buildings will experience under climate change. This study develops a computational framework for the multi-objective optimization of BIPV envelope systems using future climate projections from the CanESM5 model under the SSP3-7.0 scenario. abstract: Degree-day methods are essential for estimating building heating and cooling energy demands. We investigate the sensitivity of cooling and heating degree-day models, CDD26 and HDD18, at national and regional scales across mainland China. Non-observational datasets overestimate national heating demand while severely underestimating cooling demand. title: Asymptotic analysis of shallow water moment equations
abstract: The Shallow Water Moment Equations (SWME) are an extension of the Shallow Water Equations (SWE) for improved modelling of free-surface flows. In contrast to the SWE, the SWME incorporate vertical velocity profile information. The SWME framework approximates vertical velocity profiles using a polynomial expansion with Legendre polynomials and polynomial coefficients, also called moment variables. abstract: The article focuses on decarbonized hybrid energy systems based on solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) and gas turbines (GTs). The relevance of the work is driven by the global necessity to transition to low-carbon energy generation technologies. The main objective of the research is to conduct a thermodynamic analysis and optimize the parameters of the SOFC – GT hybrid system operating on two types of fuel: pure hydrogen and methane. abstract: In view of the problem of strong water sensitivity and susceptibility to dry and wet alternating damage of red clay, this study proposes to use plant-source enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) technology for eco-friendly stabilization. Through a series of tests such as ratio optimization, triaxial shear and dry and wet cycle, the mechanical properties and durability of cured red clay were quantitatively evaluated, and its microphysical curing mechanism was revealed in combination with SEM and EDS tests.
