title: Hydrodynamic Flood Modelling and GIS-Based Risk Mapping for Identifying Urbanization-Safe Zones in Hanwella, Sri Lanka
abstract: Urban expansion in flood-prone regions increases exposure to hydrological hazards and makes flood-informed land-use planning increasingly important. Hanwella, located in the Kelani River basin of Sri Lanka, is particularly vulnerable to flooding due to intense rainfall, river overflow, and growing urban pressure. This study develops a two-dimensional hydrodynamic flood modelling framework based on the shallow water equations and applies a Godunov-type finite volume method with the Harten–Lax–van Leer (HLL) Riemann solver to simulate water-level dynamics in the Hanwella region. title: An assessment of overbank flow-statistics within the context of environmental flow rules
abstract: Characterizing diversity in river flow regimes is crucial in informing river flow management guidelines for protecting freshwater ecosystems. In partly-confined reaches, river exhibit substantial lateral and vertical interaction when flow inundates its floodplain patches. A knowledge gap exists at the intersection of environmental flow assessment, overbank exceedance flow dynamics, and real-world policy application. title: Extreme event assessment and model diagnostic for attribution of the record-breaking July 2025 heat in Shandong, China
abstract: Abstract In July 2025, Shandong Province, China, experienced a record-breaking regional extreme heat event. Based on observational data from 77 meteorological stations (1961–2025), this study assessed the event’s extremity and systematically examines the feasibility of its attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models. The event reached a magnitude close to that of a 1-in-50-year event in the current climate, with 84.4% of stations recording high-temperature days (HTD, Tmax ≥ 35 °C) ranking among their top three historical values and 50.6% setting new records.

abstract: Rapid electricity demand growth, grid connection delays, and supply chain constraints create a serious risk of supply shortages and rising electricity costs in the next few years. This paper studies the strategy of adding colocated renewables and storage at existing power plants to take advantage of spare grid capacity. Using satellite imagery, we assess solar and wind potential near 3,890 U.S. fossil and renewable plants. abstract: At LNG terminals, electricity accounts for approximately 98% of the total energy consumption, with key power-consuming equipment in the transmission system contributing around 90% of the electricity demand. This study focuses on the gas and liquid transmission processes at LNG terminals and proposes a multi-period optimization model designed to maximize user satisfaction and minimize electricity operating cost. title: Numerical study of liquid-side mass transfer beneath a moving wavy boundary
abstract: This study investigates liquid-side scalar transport beneath propagating interfacial waves through numerical simulations of the Navier–Stokes and scalar transport equations in a moving reference frame. A wave-phase decomposition of the transport equations is employed to characterize near-surface scalar fluxes and to develop a physically based parameterization for the scalar transfer velocity. title: Developing a Climate Impact Indicator Framework for the UK Agri‐Food Sector: A Literature Review and Stakeholder Co‐Production Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Consistent monitoring and reporting of the impacts of weather in a changing climate is a key component in being able to attribute future risk and losses to weather variations. This allows the production of evidence required to facilitate mitigation, adaptation strategies and influence policy implementation. The agri‐food sector has always been impacted by weather and climate, but whilst data are consistently produced for metrics relating to the sector, there is no consistent reporting of how weather and climate are influencing these. title: Comparing surface albedo and land surface temperature of reflective roofs across five United States Cities
abstract: Abstract Rapid urban expansion and increasingly intense summer heat have heightened interest in reflective roofing as an urban heat-mitigation strategy. This study evaluates associations among roof type, surface albedo, and land surface temperature (LST) across five climatically distinct U.S. urban regions: Chicago, New York City (NYC), Las Vegas Valley (LVV), Los Angeles (LA), and Houston. abstract: Flowering-time divergence can contribute to ecological speciation, but causal genes and mutations remain largely unknown in wild plants. Here, we investigate flowering-time divergence between the wild rice species Oryza rufipogon and O. nivara. abstract: A morphotectonic analysis of the piggy-back basins of southern Limón, Costa Rica, is presented to evaluate their geomorphic evolution and relationship with active tectonic deformation. Seven basins were analyzed using geomorphic metrics derived from digital elevation models, including basin area, elevation, mean slope, local relief, and the normalized channel steepness index (ksn), complemented by drainage network analysis. title: Effect of Pipeline Burial Depth on Damage Response of Subsea Pipelines under Anchor Interaction in Soft Clay Seabed
abstract: Subsea pipelines are vulnerable to anchor-induced structural damage during ship mooring operations, particularly from raising and dragging interactions. This study quantified the effects of the pipeline burial depth on the structural damage response under these two loading scenarios in a soft clay seabed. abstract: Simulators are pivotal in advancing mobility technology, yet human adaptation in the context of these technologies remains underexplored. This study investigates the role of core executive functions (working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility) in adaptive performance within driving simulators based on a scoping review identifying a research gap and conducting a driving simulator study addressing it. title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
abstract: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. abstract: This study investigates the impact of mitigation strategies on pedestrian-level thermal conditions in four European cities with distinct climatic and morphological characteristics: Barcelona, Athens, Ljubljana, and Senigallia. Although reflective and vegetation-based interventions have been widely investigated, direct comparisons of their effects on both air temperature and pedestrian thermal comfort across contrasting urban environments under extreme conditions remain limited. abstract: Abstract This study investigates how aerosol perturbations influence precipitation formation in supercooled stratiform clouds with different supercooled liquid water content (SLWC). abstract: Abstract. Peatlands store vast amounts of carbon, yet their canopies are changing under northern warming. We assessed recent vegetation trajectories by analysing greening and browning across northern peatlands using a gap-filled, sensor-independent climate data record of leaf area index (LAI) for 2001–2023. title: A climatic-regional classification framework for exotic species plantation forestry in Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Plantation forestry underpins rural livelihoods, wood and energy security and landscape restoration in Ethiopia, yet the country lacks a forestry-specific climatic classification to support species deployment and plantation planning. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Topographical membrane surface patterns are a promising approach for increasing transmembrane flux and reducing foulant deposition. abstract: Abstract. title: Damage-mechanics-based prediction of natural fracture distribution in tight-sand gas reservoirs using 2d seismic data: Calibration and prediction
abstract: Prediction of natural fracture distribution in tight-sand gas reservoirs remains an industry challenge due to small fault throws. This study aims to develop a novel technique to address the aforementioned two bottlenecks. abstract: This paper reviews the suitability of carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP)–steel hybrid structures as load-bearing components of dynamic mechanical systems. The literature is evaluated against structural requirements, including load-carrying capacity, fatigue resistance and durability, and motion-related requirements, including inertial properties, vibration and damping. abstract: Abstract Reliable initialization of in situ $${K}_{0}$$ K 0 stresses and efficient stability analysis are fundamental to robust finite-element modeling of infinite slopes. Yet, existing modeling schemes either apply gravity loading with an indirect $${K}_{0}-\nu $$ K 0 - ν mapping that is not mechanics-consistent for sloping ground, or require large computational domains that are expensive for repeated analyses. abstract: Abstract Detachment of authigenic reservoir fines by breakage with consequent migration in rock, straining, and permeability decline has been widely reported for several technological and natural processes. abstract: Using data from the 2013–2017 China Migrants Dynamic Survey (CMDS), this study employs an IV-Probit model and a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach to examine the impact of air pollution on informal employment. abstract: Urea water solution is widely used in selective catalytic reduction systems to reduce nitrogen oxide emissions. abstract: Background: Grief is theorised to be characterised by wave-like reactions, yet little is known about how these reactions unfold between moments. abstract: Staphylococcus aureus infection is a major contributor to chronic non-healing wounds, where persistent bacterial colonization and biofilm formation impair tissue repair and sustain prolonged inflammation. abstract: The transition towards net-zero emissions requires integrated engineering solutions capable of simultaneously addressing renewable energy utilisation, industrial decarbonisation and sustainable fuel production. abstract: The increasing use of the adhesive bonding technology in various industries requires reliable models to predict the lifetime of bonded joints under cyclic loading and environmental conditions. Analyzing every cycle throughout the lifespan is computationally prohibitive. This work presents an enhanced cycle jump method to improve the efficiency of a multi-physics damage model for viscoelastic adhesives. abstract: Study region Ten major rivers spanning four drainage basins (Hai, Yellow, Huai, and Yangtze) across the alluvial plains of Henan Province, China. abstract: This study evaluates biophysical agricultural land suitability across the twenty districts of Erzurum, the fourth-largest province of Türkiye by surface area, by integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). abstract: Abstract FLOWS (FLOws of Water and Solutes in soils) is a dynamic physically-based model to simulate water flow and solute transport in the soil–plant–atmosphere system. title: Representing canopy interception in a distributed snow model to improve snow accumulation and melt timing
abstract: Seasonal snowmelt is a vital water resource for downstream populations and supports ecological processes in the mountainous Western United States. In subalpine forests, snow interception by tree canopies strongly influences snow accumulation, snow duration, and runoff timing. abstract: Background: Dromedary camel husbandry in Algeria is shifting toward sedentary confinement, yet the consequences for herd health and reproductive outcomes remain poorly documented. This study examined the associations of housing system, environmental constraints, and disease burden with dystocia in El Oued, Algeria. abstract: Este artigo mapeia e analisa a estrutura empresarial e a maturidade dos projetos brasileiros de lítio, terras raras e grafita. title: GOWC: an open tool for observing-conditions prediction and observation planning, tested against site monitors and an exposure-time calculator
abstract: GOWC (Global Observing-conditions Weather Catalogue) is an open web application that takes the user from a target to an exposure plan across 2,642 catalogued observatory sites. It computes seeing, airmass, extinction, precipitable water vapour, sky brightness and signal-to-noise from live Open-Meteo meteorology, including pressure-level profiles, and tests most of these outputs against an independent reference. abstract: We analyze scale-by-scale budgets of velocity and buoyancy second-order structure functions using Large Eddy Simulation of the BOMEX trade-wind cumulus layer. abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. abstract: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. abstract: The complete Wess-Zumino (WZ) action and stress-energy tensor (SET) of the conformal anomaly in both two and four dimensions is given. abstract: Space-based quantum information networks require simulation tools that capture orbital dynamics, probabilistic quantum operations, and classical coordination. We introduce QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for the design and performance evaluation of satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. title: The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf stabilized three adjacent ice sheets during the last glacial period
abstract: Global ice volume peaked between ~26,500 and 19,000 years ago and resulted in the Laurentide, Innuitian and Greenland ice sheets coalescing in Baffin Bay, a semi-enclosed basin between Greenland and Canada. However, the configuration of their marine terminating margins, which help establish the boundary conditions and sensitivity to processes that govern ice-sheet retreat, remains unclear. abstract: Deep-sea ferromanganese nodules (FNs) are important mineral resources, and their abundance is a key parameter for resource assessment. In this study, the association between FN abundance and seafloor topography near 113 geological sampling stations in the Pacific Clarion–Clipperton Fracture Zone is investigated. Results reveal that FNs are widely distributed on gentle slope terrain with gradients of ∼0.7°–4.6°, where FN abundance is 5–20 kg/m2. abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth's Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. abstract: The extent of the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets during Marine Isotope Stage 3 (MIS 3, 57-29 ka) is generally poorly constrained due to limited stratigraphic control, a lack of geological deposits, and inconclusive dates. For the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS), it is typically assumed that the ice extended beyond the present-day coast during MIS 3, although some data suggest a more limited ice extent. abstract: Coral reefs are in global decline due to climate change, shifting reef ecosystems from 24-hour net heterotrophy to autotrophy, altering carbon cycles and reducing resilience to stressors. Red Sea coral reefs experience some of the warmest waters globally, exceeding 30 °C and reaching up to 38 °C on reef flats during summer. abstract: AIM: Coral reefs support more than one-third of the global marine biodiversity, but global stressors have negatively impacted their health by disrupting fragile microbial partnerships, leading to widespread mass bleaching events. To address this issue, the use of beneficial microorganisms for coral (BMCs) has been shown to enhance coral resilience. abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification threatens marine calcifiers, but the independent effects of seawater pH and total alkalinity on shell formation remain poorly understood. abstract: Coastal geomorphological maps generated in a GIS context in Naples Bay and the Cilento area are presented here to establish a current geomorphological framework for these two sectors of the Eastern Tyrrhenian margin. While sedimentary processes have dominated the geological evolution of the Cilento area, volcanic processes have dominated Naples Bay. abstract: Previous studies show that two promising technologies can increase recruitment probability and survival: (i) helix recesses for entraining coral larvae and (ii) night-time feeding lights for improving subsequent survival. title: AIS-based noise models underestimate vessel noise exposure risk to marine mammals
abstract: Vessels are the dominant source of anthropogenic underwater noise, with well-documented effects on marine mammal behaviour and physiology that may ultimately compromise individual fitness. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) provides standardized, global, high-resolution positional information for most commercial and passenger vessels, making AIS-based noise models widely used to assess exposure risk. Brazil encompasses a wide diversity of coastal and marine ecosystems inhabited by three seahorse species ( Hippocampus reidi , H. erectus and Hippocampus patagonicus ), but available information has remained fragmented across scientific publications, museum collections, technical reports and monitoring programmes. abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to test whether four marine gastrotrich species shared between the North Sea and the Mediterranean Sea represent single, pan-European taxa or instead comprise hidden, genetically structured lineages. Using single-specimen whole-genome sequencing, multigene phylogenetics (18S, 28S, COI), and multiple species-delimitation methods, we analyzed populations of Xenotrichula intermedia , Halichaetonotus aculifer , H. atlanticus , and Turbanella bocqueti sampled from the North Sea and the Mediterranean Sea. abstract: The coral microbiome is believed to play a crucial role in sustaining corals and enabling adaptation to perturbations. A ubiquitous group of coral-associated bacteria, known as Endozoicomonas, are hypothesized to provide essential metabolites to corals, although detailed dynamics of the interactions between host and microbe are poorly understood. abstract: Marine ecosystems face multifaceted threats stemming from historical overexploitation and environmental degradation. Despite existing research, there are notable gaps in understanding the long-term dietary dynamics of marine organisms in the context of anthropogenic impacts. abstract: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. abstract: ABSTRACT In marine engineering structures, components made of 5A06 aluminum alloy are often subjected simultaneously to sustained tensile stress and corrosion in natural seawater; their initial surface condition may further influence the initiation and propagation of localized corrosion. abstract: The calanoid copepod Pseudodiaptomus marinus Sato, 1913, native to the Indo-Pacific region, has rapidly expanded its range in European waters since its first detection in the Adriatic Sea in 2007, raising questions about its introduction pathways and population dynamics. abstract: Efforts to protect marine and coastal environments in Åland, Finland, increasingly emphasise integrating local water ownership into formal governance. Although this transition is critical for survival, how planetary cues such as light interact with local ecological signals to prepare the genome for such rapid reprogramming remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. abstract: This study assessed the diversity, aboveground carbon stock, and economic value of mangrove forests along the coastal areas of Davao Oriental, Philippines. abstract: Lycengraulis grossidens is economically important for artisanal fisheries and prey of top predators in the Río de la Plata (RP) (SW Atlantic). abstract: Abstract Given the unprecedented climate-induced impacts on the marine environment, the conduct-oriented marine environmental protection obligation (MEPO) has become highly inadequate. abstract: The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on Earth. title: Ict-enabled Environmental Sustainability in Coastal Communities: Assessing Digital Governance and Blue Economy Development in Mombasa County, Kenya
abstract: Coastal communities face increasing environmental challenges; including habitat degradation, pollution, and climate-related shocks that threaten livelihoods built around the ocean economy. Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) are increasingly promoted as instruments of environmental governance, yet the extent to which digital governance capacity translates into sustainable blue economy outcomes in African coastal counties remains under-researched. This paper investigates the relationship between ICT-enabled digital governance and environmental sustainability in the context of blue

title: UCD-LFE: An Underwater Crack Detection Model for Hydraulic Structures in Complex Environments via Lightweight Design and Feature Enhancement
abstract: Underwater crack detection in hydraulic structures is difficult in complex underwater environments, where blur, uneven illumination, low contrast, and rough surface textures can weaken crack cues and introduce background interference, while multiple cracks further increase detection complexity. Practical inspection also requires compact models with low computational demand. To address these coupled challenges, this study develops UCD-LFE, an underwater crack detection model combining lightweight design with feature enhancement. title: Female-biased tolerance to delousing treatments in the sea louse Caligus rogercresseyi increases with compound lipophilicity
abstract: Sex-biased pesticide tolerance is increasingly recognized in arthropods, yet its implications for parasite management in aquaculture remain poorly understood. This study evaluated sex-specific antiparasitic tolerance in the sea louse Caligus rogercresseyi , a marine ectoparasite and a major challenge for salmon aquaculture. Here we analyzed 340 bioassays conducted between 2018 and 2026 across southern Chile, exposing male and female sea lice to four chemical actives plus one botanical formulation with differing modes of action and lipophilicity. title: Shifting baselines of tri-spine horseshoe crab habitats along a rapidly urbanized coast in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Coastal wetlands are being rapidly lost under urban expansion, yet many threatened marine invertebrates depend on these habitats during early life stages. The endangered tri-spine horseshoe crab Tachypleus tridentatus relies on suitable intertidal flats as juvenile nursery habitat, but conservation planning is hindered by weak historical baselines. Fujian Province was historically a major population center of this species in China, but its coastline has experienced intensive reclamation, port development and shoreline artificialization. title: From Osmotic Stress to Antibiotic Toxicity: Salinity as a Key Modulator of Enrofloxacin Effects in the Manila Clam ( Ruditapes philippinarum )
abstract: Antibiotic residues, particularly fluoroquinolones, increasingly co-occur with salinity fluctuations in coastal areas, yet their combined effects on marine bivalves remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the interactive impact of enrofloxacin (ENR; 5 and 500 ng/L) and salinity (30 and 40 PSU) on the marine bivalve Ruditapes philippinarum, using an integrative biomarker approach to assess metabolic, oxidative, and cellular responses. title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. title: Polar Seabed Observation Systems reveal winter diel rhythms and environmental drivers of euphausiids in Great Wall Bay, Antarctic Peninsula
abstract: The adaptive diel rhythm strategies of euphausiids during wintertime in the Southern Ocean surrounding the Antarctic continent remain poorly documented. To elucidate this knowledge gap, an in situ benthic observation campaign was conducted via the Polar Seabed Observation Systems (PSOS) in June 2023, targeting the Great Wall Bay (Antarctic Peninsula) to quantify winter diel activity patterns of euphausiids. title: Impact of real‐time digital dashboard on birth outcomes in high‐volume tertiary center: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the impact of implementing a real-time intrapartum digital monitoring dashboard on labor progression and birth outcomes in a high-resource high-volume tertiary care delivery ward. STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a university-affiliated medical center. We included all women admitted for an attempted vaginal delivery between January 2012 and December 2022. title: Comparison of Manila clam (Ruditapes philippinarum) diet between 2006 and 2024 in a changing coastal lagoon
abstract: Environmental changes are extensively reported in the literature, sometimes leading to long-term trends. This study focuses on Arcachon Bay, a coastal lagoon in SW France, which has been the scene of several environmental modifications over the past decades, including a severe decline of seagrass meadows and changes in its physicochemical features. title: When Armoring and Nourishment Are No Longer Enough: Managed Retreat and Coastal Adaptation in California
abstract: Coastal communities face a growing mismatch between shorelines that naturally move and development built as if they do not.California makes this tension especially visible.Homes, roads, rail lines, airports, wastewater facilities, public access, and other infrastructure occupy beaches, bluffs, bays, and low-lying shorelines that are already shaped by erosion, flooding,

title: Atmospheric forcing of an extreme Baltic Sea-level depression and post-minimum exchange in winter 2025/2026
abstract: Introduction During winter 2025/2026, the Baltic Sea experienced a pronounced basin-wide sea-level depression, with regional sea surface height (SSH) anomalies reaching approximately −60 cm or lower. We examine its atmospheric forcing, associated volume changes and subsequent hydrographic conditions. Methods We combine Copernicus Marine SSH, ERA5 atmospheric fields, Landsort/Landsort–Norra observations, modelled net transport across a Kattegat section, and CTD, Argo and glider measurements. title: Variation in the effectiveness of native microbial amendments for coastal dune restoration
abstract: Abstract Introduction Microbial amendments can improve restorations by increasing plant performance and decreasing soil erosion. Whole‐soil amendments collected from native ecosystems, in particular, can produce desirable outcomes; however, it is unclear if all native soil amendments produce equally positive effects. Instead, it is likely that donor locations differ in their microbial communities, which may change their efficacy for restoration. title: Developments in cartography and GIS in Albania – the contribution of Prof. Dr. Pal Nikolli
abstract: Prof. Dr. Pal Nikolli is a scholar whose academic and research work has contributed to the development of cartography and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in Albania, with a long and rich career in teaching and scientific research, which has significantly contributed to the development of these disciplines. He has combined theoretical knowledge with practical applications, helping to advance Albanian cartography and promote modern technologies in this field. title: Spatial Correspondence Between Vernacular Dwelling Typologies and Dialect Regionalization in the Jiaoliao Cross-Sea Cultural Area of China
abstract: Vernacular dwellings and dialects are material and linguistic carriers of regional culture. This study evaluates dialect regionalization as a reference for vernacular architectural research across the Jiaodong–Liaodong cross-sea region. Hierarchical clustering of 29 morphological variables identified five architectural types among 573 dwellings from 341 villages, independently of dialect information. title: Vulnerability of Small-Scale Fisheries to Potential Storm Surge in North Borneo Island, Malaysia
abstract: Abstract Small-scale fishers were crucial for providing fresh seafood and contributing to the protein intake of coastal communities. They typically used traditional fishing methods and ventured out to the sea in small boats, often working alone or with a few family members. Despite their vital contribution to the community, small-scale fishers faced numerous challenges and were highly exposed to the effects of climate change. title: Coral‐Like Nanomaterials for Plugging Shale Microfractures in Water‐Based Drilling Fluids
abstract: ABSTRACT Current plugging agents poorly adapt to shale micro/nano‐pores, leading to low plugging efficiency. Inspired by coral natural morphology, we fabricated a coral‐like multi‐branched nano‐silica plugging agent (SiO 2 ‐HNA) to fit shale micro/nano‐pores and fractures. Under the same experimental conditions, compared with conventional spherical nano‐SiO 2 , it exhibits superior filtration‐loss plugging and particle retention capacity, and a longer action duration, dense plugging and strong stability. title: Using climax thinking to understand psychological drivers of attitudes towards two coastal climate adaptations around the hypertidal Bay of Fundy
abstract: Abstract Coastal climate adaptations are changes that tackle the challenges arising from sea level rise. Adaptations such as risk information and changes to public infrastructure have been met with some degree of public opposition. Climax thinking is an emerging framework for exploring this resistance. In this study, we used climax thinking to explore public responses to two specific coastal climate adaptation strategies: public flood risk mapping and managed dyke realignment. title: Spatial lipidomics suggests fatty acid scavenging by an intranuclear parasite
abstract: Abstract Bacteria of the family Endozoicomonadaceae are widely associated with marine animals, yet their in situ metabolism remains mostly unknown. Genomic studies suggest that members of this family engage in extensive metabolic exchange with their hosts, ranging from nutrient provision in mutualistic sponge and coral symbioses to dependence on host metabolites like lipids in parasitic associations. title: Electrochemically driven vanadium-mediated phase-interface reconstruction for efficient and durable seawater oxidation
abstract: Abstract Efficient seawater oxidation requires rapid active-phase formation together with selective interfacial hydroxide/chloride ion (OH-/Cl-) regulation. Here, we report a cyclic-voltammetry activation strategy to electrochemically drive V-mediated phase-interface reconstruction in V-doped NiFe layered double hydroxide (V-NiFe LDH (EC)) for efficient and durable seawater oxidation. title: The Paralicella Paradox: Broadly Distributed Lineages Without Clear Geographic Partitioning in Paralicella tenuipes and the Paralicella caperesca Species Complex
abstract: ABSTRACT Abyssal environments (3000–6000 m ocean depth) are often presumed to promote broad genetic connectivity across ocean basins due to their vast spatial extent, apparent environmental homogeneity and few barriers to gene flow. While some deep‐sea taxa conform to this expectation, growing evidence shows that marked genetic structure can persist even in widely distributed species. title: TSUNAMI RISK IN PACITAN, INDONESIA: SPATIAL PATTERNS OF BUILDING VULNERABILITY IN AN EMERGING COASTAL TOURISM DESTINATION
abstract: Coastal tourism destinations along the southern coast of Java face significant exposure to tsunami hazards. This study models potential coastal inundation using the official deterministic worst-case scenario of an 11 m tsunami wave and evaluates tsunami-related building vulnerability in Watukarung, Indonesia, through the Papathoma Tsunami Vulnerability Assessment framework (PTVA-4). abstract: Background: FVKVEVLPQ from Arbacia lixula has previously been studied computationally in triple-negative breast cancer. This study explored its putative targets in breast cancer more broadly using network pharmacology and molecular docking. Methods: Peptide-associated targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction and SEA. Breast cancer-associated genes were obtained from DisGeNET and GeneCards. Navigating Blue Risk: Divergent Pathways in Tasmanian Aquaculture
abstract: The blue economy is commonly framed as a pathway to sustainability, promising the reconciliation of economic growth with environmental protection and social equity. In practice, however, industries seeking to operate blue face significant challenges translating high-level principles into practice. The study examines how the Tasmanian aquaculture sector (i.e., salmon, oyster, and seaweed industries) operationalise blue economy principles on the ground, and where gaps and burdens emerge. title: Low-Cost Drone-Based Monitoring of Coastal Erosion in California
abstract: Coastal erosion threatens infrastructure and communities along the California coast. This paper examines how the amount and location of coastal cliff erosion changed across survey periods along approximately 13 km of the Big Sur coastline using 27 publicly available USGS M3C2 point-cloud datasets covering 2017 to 2023. title: Comparative genomics reveals modular virulence repertoires and extensive horizontal gene transfer in Vibrio species associated with white syndrome of Porites cylindrica
abstract: Abstract Coral white syndrome (WS) is a widespread condition characterized by tissue loss and skeletal exposure, with multiple bacterial pathogens—particularly Vibrio species—implicated in its etiology. To investigate the genomic basis of potential virulence in Vibrio associated with WS of Porites cylindrica , we isolated 57 Vibrio strains from healthy and diseased coral tissues collected from reefs in Guam. title: RNA viruses as drivers of rapid diatom succession within a single bloom event
abstract: Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved. Here, using quantitative metatranscriptomics, we tracked temporal patterns of diatoms and associated viruses at near-daily resolution during the spring bloom in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea. title: ASSESSING THAILAND’S COMMUNITY CRAB BANKS THROUGH INTERNATIONAL CRITERIA FOR SUSTAINABLE MARINE CONSERVATION
abstract: This qualitative study evaluates Thailand’s Blue Swimming Crab Bank Expansion Project against five international criteria for sustainable community-based conservation: measurable ecological impact, community participation, scientific credibility, knowledge transfer, and policy alignment. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine biofouling poses significant challenges to maritime industries and threatens environmental sustainability and ecological security. Photocatalytic antimicrobial platform has emerged as promising antifouling strategy in marine applications. In this study, an S‐scheme heterostructure of g‐C 3 N 4 /LaFeO 3 nanosheets with Fe─N bonding is constructed to serve as a highly efficient and stable photocatalytic antimicrobial platform for marine use. title: A new approach for detecting phenological change using Time of Emergence ( ToE ) methodology
abstract: Abstract Many species are responding to environmental change by shifting the timings of phenological events such as migration or reproduction. These shifts are typically reported as rates of change, which do not indicate when such shifts transcend their original states, nor consider whether species experience novel environmental conditions or phenological mismatch with other species at their phenological events. At the GO/GaN interface, atomic interactions form configurations such as C–O–N–Ga (N‐polar van der Waals interactions) and C–O–Ga–N (Ga‐polar covalent interactions), which facilitate efficient photon absorption and charge migration into the graphene oxide shell. title: Beyond the maximum gradient: a consecutive-threshold criterion for nitracline detection in the Northwestern Indian Ocean
abstract: Depth of the nitracline is an important indicator of the vertical distribution and availability of nitrate in the upper ocean. While the conventional definition of the nitracline as the depth of maximum nitrate gradient (dN/dz) has been widely accepted, this study introduces a complementary consecutive-gradient criterion to detect the onset of a sustained nitrate gradient zone. title: Hydrophobic Microenvironment Engineering of Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Proteolysis‐Driven Marine Antifouling
abstract: ABSTRACT Peptide bond hydrolysis is essential to biology, yet the kinetic stability of amide bonds makes efficient and selective artificial proteolysis challenging. Here, we report a biomimetic Cu single‐atom nanozyme, Cu‐NC HSA, that integrates mixed d 9 ‐d 10 Cu‐N 4 active sites with a hydrogen‐substituted graphdiyne overlayer for selective protein hydrolysis. title: Exploring student biodiversity literacy in Indonesian coastal areas: implications for education for sustainable development
abstract: This study is driven by the degradation of Indonesia's coastal ecosystems, leading to a decline in biodiversity and increase disaster risk for coastal communities. Addressing this issue necessitates the engagement of multiple stakeholders, particularly educational institutions. This study aims to describe the profile of biodiversity literacy of high school students in coastal areas of Sumbawa Island, Indonesia, across cognitive, attitude, and behavioural dimensions and to discuss its relevance to Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). title: Information Visualization for Hainan Li Pottery: An Intangible Cultural Heritage Perspective
abstract: Hainan Li pottery is a traditional pottery-making practice of the Li ethnic group in Hainan and contains information related to craft history, daily life, and cultural memory. At present, its communication mainly relies on object display, textual explanation, cultural experience activities, and tourism promotion. However, existing approaches often focus on individual objects and lack systematic presentation of historical development, production procedures, vessel types, decorative motifs, and cultural relationships. title: A Comprehensive Repository of Morphological, Life‐History, Ecological, and Environmental Data for Sirenians and Marine Carnivorans Worldwide
abstract: Sirenians and marine carnivorans represent unique mammalian lineages that have transitioned from terrestrial to aquatic life. Although they serve as vital indicators of marine ecosystem health, nearly half of these species are threatened with extinction. However, a comprehensive database capturing both their biological traits and environmental variables has been lacking. title: Temperature‐Sensitive Juvenile Fitness Traits Show Correlated and Genetically Defined Variation in a Heatwave‐Affected Marine Fish
abstract: ABSTRACT Juvenile fish must balance energy allocation between somatic growth and lipid storage. This trade‐off is sensitive to environmental conditions, which can drive interannual differences in overwinter survival and recruitment. We examined individual variation in these strategies by rearing Gulf of Alaska (GOA) juvenile Pacific cod ( Gadus macrocephalus ) at four temperatures (0°C, 5°C, 9°C, and 16°C). title: Skin‐Protective Effects of Marinophyll, a Carotenoid From Marine Erythrobacter sp. SDW2
abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous studies have highlighted that marine organisms, such as microalgae and marine bacteria, exhibit significantly higher and more sustainable biosynthetic yields of unique carotenoids compared to terrestrial sources. These advantages in production efficiency have sparked significant interest in developing materials derived from marine origins. Marinophyll, natural carotenoids extracted from marine sources, have demonstrated potential in managing oxidative stress and inflammation linked to various skin conditions. abstract: This study evaluates sediment characteristics and coastal erosion vulnerability along the Batu Pahat coastline, focusing on Pantai Punggur, Pantai Perpat, and Pantai Parit Hailam in Johor, Malaysia. Eight sediment samples were analysed to determine specific gravity, moisture content, and bulk density, providing insights into the physical behaviour of coastal sediments that influence shoreline stability. title: DEVELOPMENT OF A CLASSIFICATION OF OIL SPILLS IN THE SOUTHEASTERN BALTIC BY POLLUTION AREA
abstract: The paper presents a classification of oil pollution in the southeastern part of the Baltic Sea, developed on the basis of an analysis of oil slick areas based on satellite radar images. Information processing was performed using the Pisces 2 geoinformation system, which provided high-precision georeference, automated area calculation and visualization of spatial data. abstract: The Indonesian government is actively working towards achieving comprehensive waste management through a range of strategies implemented across different regions. The decline in waste management can be attributed to the fast-paced rise in population, urbanization, and industrial consumption across various sectors. This research focuses on identifying the primary obstacles of waste management in Sleman Regency. title: Low genetic diversity in the cosmopolitan Asparagopsis taxiformis Lineage-2 (Florideophyceae, Rhodophyta)
abstract: The red alga Asparagopsis taxiformis (Rhodymeniophycidae) comprises six mitochondrial lineages (L1–L6) that are genetically distinct but morphologically indistinguishable. These cryptic lineages occur across tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide, but the phylogeographic structure of Korean populations remains poorly understood. title: Combined toxicity of chlorpyrifos and nanoplastics in the marine amphipod Parhyale hawaiensis: implications for chlorpyrifos risk assessment in Latin American coasts
abstract: Abstract Chlorpyrifos (CPF) is a widely used organophosphate insecticide, yet its ecological effects on Latin American marine species, both alone and in combination with other pollutants, remain poorly characterized. Here, we assessed the acute toxicity of CPF alone and in mixtures with low (100 µg L − 1 ) and high (1000 µg L − 1 ) concentrations of polyethylene nanoplastics (NPs) in the marine amphipod Parhyale hawaiensis . title: Mosques as Community-Based Vertical Evacuation Shelters in Tsunami-Prone Coastal Padang, Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia is among the most tsunami-prone countries in the world due to its location along active subduction zones. In coastal cities such as Padang, extremely short tsunami arrival times, high population exposure, and the limited distribution of purpose-built vertical evacuation shelters reveal a critical gap in socially embedded evacuation planning. This study examines the potential of mosques to serve as community-based vertical tsunami evacuation shelters in coastal Padang, focusing on spatial suitability, social legitimacy, and adaptive reuse within a local disaster risk reduction context

title: Outbreak of Mud Crab Reovirus ( MCRV ) in a Mud Crab ( Scylla serrata ) Fattening Facility in the Ashtamudi Backwaters, West Coast of India
abstract: The present study documents a confirmed outbreak of Mud Crab Reovirus (MCRV) in Scylla serrata from an open-water fattening facility in the Ashtamudi backwaters, Kerala, representing the first report of MCRV from the west coast of India. Mud crab farming has gained economic importance across Indian coastal states, but viral infections such as MCRV-related sleeping disease (SD) pose a critical threat to industry sustainability due to associated high mortalities. title: Updated dataset for “Jellyfish in Hong Kong: a citizen science dataset”
abstract: Abstract This work is an update and extension of the previously published article “Jellyfish in Hong Kong: a citizen science dataset”, by Terenzini et al. (2024). This Data Update consists of 516 jellyfish observations made by citizen scientists in Hong Kong during 2024 and 2025, who submitted photographs and videos to the Hong Kong Jellyfish Project website, iNaturalist project, and through social media. abstract: Background The pathological changes in neurodegenerative diseases are complicated and involve oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, protein misfolding, and synaptic loss. Marine algae contain a wide range of diverse natural compounds, such as polysaccharides, phenolics, terpenoids, and pigments, some of which may help preserve neurons by targeting oxidative pathways, dampening inflammatory responses, and preventing toxic protein aggregation. abstract: Marine bacteria remain insufficiently explored as potential plant bioinoculants. This study evaluated the plant growth-promoting potential of the euryhaline marine bacterium Cobetia amphilecti KMM 296 by comparing the effects of viable cells and cell-free culture supernatant on Glycine max. abstract: The mangrove forest ecosystem in Karawang Regency is undergoing rapid degradation, thereby threatening its ecological, social, and economic functions, as well as its role in coastal protection. This study aims to formulate a management strategy using a strategic management approach for mangrove ecosystem conservation and ecotourism development in Cilamaya Wetan District. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine algae present a promising foundation for developing sustainable bioplastics, distinguished by rapid growth, abundant carbohydrates, and minimal land and freshwater demands. This paper examines the utilization of marine algae‐derived starch and other polysaccharides in bioplastic manufacturing, encompassing algal characteristics, carbohydrate and polysaccharide recovery, bioplastic formulation and properties, and environmental implications. title: GIS-Based Mapping and Geodatabase Development for Expansive Soils: A Case Study of Selected Towns in the Wolaita Zone, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: Expansive soils cause costly damage to infrastructure through seasonal moisture-driven swelling and shrinkage, yet in many developing regions the geotechnical data needed to manage this hazard remains fragmented across paper records and individual project reports. This study addresses that gap by evaluating the engineering properties of expansive soils in three rapidly urbanizing towns in the Wolaita Zone of southern Ethiopia, namely Tebela, Wolaita Sodo, and Boditi, and consolidating the results into a spatially referenced ArcGIS geodatabase to support preliminary engineering design. abstract: Urban wetlands provide key services and support natural hydrological regulation; yet the values and flood-mitigation services they provide could be under-quantified in rapidly urbanizing coastal areas of Africa. title: Storage duration and water type determine the need for mercury chloride preservation of dissolved inorganic carbon
abstract: Abstract To quantify aquatic carbon budgets, it is important to accurately measure dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC). The standard approach requires the use of mercury chloride (HgCl 2 ) poison to preserve samples, but the real need and overall constraints of using such a toxic compound remain elusive. Here, we evaluate the need for filtration and mercury poisoning to maintain DIC stability in six contrasting water types across the freshwater–seawater continuum. title: Genetic diversity and differentiation of Egyptian vulture (Neophron percnopterus) populations in oceanic islands: implications for conservation
abstract: Abstract Genetic monitoring is central to the conservation of threatened species, particularly those with small and isolated populations, as reduced diversity can limit long-term survival and adaptive potential. Islands are ideal for examining these processes due to restricted gene flow and the enhanced effects of genetic drift and inbreeding. The Egyptian vulture ( Neophron percnopterus ), a long-lived species in global decline, serves as a model for examining how insularity shapes genetic diversity and structure. abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. abstract: Open dumping of municipal solid waste can expose surface water and groundwater to leachate, yet surface environmental constraints and subsurface conditions are often assessed separately. title: Topographic Organization of Abyssal Intraseasonal Variability in the Northern Philippine Basin
abstract: Abstract Deep intraseasonal variability (ISV) in weakly stratified marginal basins remains poorly understood, especially where complex bathymetry may modulate abyssal motions. Here we examine its structure and driving mechanisms in the northern Philippine Basin (NPB) using multi‐year, nearly full‐depth mooring observations at 128°E, 20.45°N. Velocities spanning the surface to 4,900 m reveal two dominant ISV bands near ∼83 and ∼113 days in the deep zonal flow, both intensifying toward the bottom with vertically coherent structures consistent with topographic Rossby wave (TRW)‐like motions. title: Seed Storage Conditions for Zostera muelleri Restoration: Effects of Temperature, Salinity and Sterilisation on Seed Contamination, Viability and Seedling Emergence
abstract: The decline of seagrass meadows is a continuing global concern, and seed‐based restoration provides a scalable approach to recovering lost and degraded meadows. Such approaches require large quantities of seed to be collected, processed, and often stored for months until deployment. Microbial contamination during storage reduces seed viability, germination and seedling development. abstract: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation is widely promoted for rice cultivation to reduce water use and enhance water productivity. title: Mapping uncertainty. Defining spatial accuracy of WWI historical sources in the Asiago Plateau (NE Italy)
abstract: During World War I (WWI), the landscapes of the Venetian Prealps were extensively transformed by the construction of defensive lines and field fortifications. Historical sources (aerial photographs, military cartography, ground photos, panoramic drawings, and written documents) preserve evidence and memory of these changes and enable the reconstruction of the spatial organization of past military systems through Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The digitization of such sources provides an effective means to locate military features that are no longer visible in the present-day landscape.

abstract: Wetlands are biodiversity hotspots and critical nature-based solutions for water purification, climate regulation, and flood and coastal risk reduction, yet they remain among the world’s most threatened ecosystems. This scoping review synthesized 2,482 China-focused studies published between 2001 and 2026 to examine how wetland plant biodiversity supports ecosystem services and informs governance and United Nations. title: Calcification patterns of a foundation species reveal resilience to environmental change in southern California over the twentieth century
abstract: Oceanographic changes due to carbon dioxide emissions have complex and varied impacts on marine calcifying taxa. Changes in calcification can unfold over decades or longer, requiring a longer-term understanding of biomineralization patterns than laboratory-based studies can provide. Here, we investigate the calcification history of the marine mussel Mytilus californianus to determine how this ecologically critical foundation species has responded to past and ongoing environmental changes in the southern end of its range within the California Current System (CCS) between 27.72° N and 34.47° N.

title: Salinity tolerance dynamics in selected crop species at germination stage under in vitro and in situ conditions in Patuakhali, Bangladesh
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic stress limiting crop productivity, predominantly in coastal regions. This study aimed to evaluate the salinity tolerance of selected crop species at the germination stage under both in vitro (petri dishes) and in situ (pot culture) conditions. The main research question was to identify crop species capable of tolerating different salinity levels and to assess their physiological and ionic responses for suitability in saline coastal regions of Bangladesh. title: Tracking highly Si-undersaturated, CO2-rich Ocean Island magmas from the surface to the depth of redox melting: a reverse approach to understand melting columns within mantle plumes
abstract: The generation and evolution of CO 2 -rich silicate melts within mantle plumes are critical to understanding intraplate magmatism. We employ a novel reverse experimental approach to track the compositional evolution of a primitive Cape Verde basanitic magma down the asthenospheric melting column at adiabatic temperatures (for a potential temperature T P = 1350°C). Melt evolution is reconstructed from 3 to 7 GPa, 1380–1420°C, i.e. from the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB) at ∼100 km to the redox melting front at ∼230 km. title: The costs and motivations of blue carbon ecosystem restoration in Australia
abstract: Restoration of blue carbon ecosystems (BCE), such as mangroves, seagrasses and saltmarshes has the potential to support climate mitigation, adaptation and biodiversity conservation. Yet, restoration efforts remain small-scale, costly and underfunded, while limited information on restoration costs, funding sources and barriers constrains coastal management decisions on restoration planning, investment and implementation. title: Spatial pattern analysis of built-up land use and zoning conformity using polygon-based statistics: a case study of Tegal city, Indonesia
abstract: Rapid urban expansion in coastal cities increasingly challenges the effectiveness of spatial planning enforcement. Tegal city, located on Java’s northern coast, is experiencing intensive built-up land development accompanied by growing spatial clustering. This study analyses polygon-level built-up land patterns using Ripley’s K-function to identify multi-scale clustering, Global Moran’s I to assess spatial autocorrelation, and Local Moran’s I (LISA) to detect local clusters. title: Historical geomorphology and structural glaciology of south-western Admiralty Bay, King George Island, Antarctica
abstract: This study presents a 1:8000 geomorphological and structural glaciological map of south-western Admiralty Bay, King George Island, based on a 1979 aerial survey. The map covers an area of 37.9 km2 and documents 16 462 structures and landforms. Large-scale landscape characteristics are determined by bedrock geology sculpted by overlying ice masses. The glaciers can be broadly separated into highly-crevassed tidewater glaciers, and less dynamic land-terminating glaciers. abstract: Most shallow-water methane seeps studied in the Svalbard-Barents Sea region fall within relatively warm and saline Atlantic water masses which have been hypothesized to impact epimegabenthic species composition and select against chemosymbiotrophic fauna. Seeps on the shelf off Svalbard's southernmost fjord Hornsund are subject to colder Arctic water masses, which theoretically could favor chemosymbiotrophic fauna, but were nonetheless devoid of chemosymbiotrophic siboglinids. abstract: Heat-killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strain L-137 (HK L-137) has shown bioactive properties associated with enhanced performance and immunomodulation in aquaculture species. abstract: Pengambengan Village, located in Jembrana Regency, is highly susceptible to tsunami disasters, necessitating the implementation of mitigation measures through the Tsunami Ready Program. This study aims to develop a tsunami hazard map and identify tsunami evacuation sites and route scenarios in Pengambengan Village to meet the Tsunami Ready indicators. The tsunami hazard map was generated by tsunami modeling based on a worst-case scenario on the Sumba Megathrust segment with Mw 8.5 using the COMCOT and QGIS software. title: Biocomposite Films Based on Biopolysaccharide and Hydrothermal Carbonised Pine Sawdust Waste: Properties, Performance, and Degradation Behaviour in Different Environments
abstract: Pine sawdust waste was converted by hydrothermal carbonisation into carbon-rich particles (HTC-WS) and incorporated into chitosan to produce a sustainable biocomposite film (Chit_HTC-WS). Chitosan-microcrystalline cellulose film (Chit_MCC) and neat chitosan (Chit) were also prepared for comparison. The films were characterised by structural, mechanical, thermal, surface, UV resistance, and degradation properties in freshwater, simulated seawater, and soil burial conditions. title: Measuring the margins: A combination-based indicator for boundary ecosystem assessment
abstract: Traditional richness- and abundance-based indices primarily quantify alpha diversity but do not directly represent spatial compositional distinctiveness. We developed a novel Combination Index (CI) that quantifies the rarity of species co-occurrence patterns using presence–absence data, without requiring abundance information, and is less directly dependent on species richness than conventional richness-based metrics. title: LC–MS/MS profiling, network pharmacology, and hERG liability docking of Haliclona caerulea metabolites as putative cardioprotective candidates
abstract: Introduction: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death worldwide; post-infarction injury involves oxidative stress and inflammation. Cardioprotective leads from marine sponges need early screening for cardiac ion-channel liability, because block of the human ether-à-go-go-related gene (hERG) channel prolongs the QT interval and may provoke fatal arrhythmia. title: X-VAD: Video Anomaly Detection with Kinematic Explanations
abstract: Anomaly scores alone do not describe unusual motion. X-VAD links scoring and reporting through 13 cell-level kinematic descriptors from SEA-RAFT optical flow. They describe speed, direction, flow deformation, and temporal change. Each vector is compared with normal training observations from the same cell. The four highest calibrated cell scores are averaged to obtain the frame score. No gradient-based training of an anomaly scorer is required. title: Characterization and Genome Analysis of a Novel Vibrio Alginolyticus Phage and Its Biocontrol Efficacy in Pearl Oyster Aquaculture
abstract: A novel lytic bacteriophage, designated vB_ValS-L9, infecting the potential pathogenic bacterium Vibrio alginolyticus L4, was isolated from a coastal aquaculture area in Beihai, China. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that vB_ValS-L9 possesses an icosa-hedral head (56.50 ± 4.19 nm in diameter) and a long tail (143.03 ± 5.32 nm in length), ex-hibiting a typical siphovirus-like morphology within the class Caudoviricetes. title: REE and Nd isotope geochemistry of Cretaceous carbonates from the Santos Basin, Brazil: Insights into hydrothermal processes and fluid origin
abstract: ABSTRACT The Brazilian pre-salt reservoirs of the Santos Basin are hosted in Aptian carbonates of the Barra Velha Formation, whose depositional environment and fluid history remain debated due to the lack of modern analogues. Here, we present geochemical and neodymium isotope data from a stratigraphic drill core transecting the upper 200 m of the Upper Barra Velha Formation. title: Fish and aquatic biodiversity of the Kura River under pollution, flow alteration and climate pressures
abstract: The Kura River supports a diverse aquatic community that includes fish, benthic organisms, mollusks, crustaceans, plankton and semi-aquatic mammals, while also sustaining fisheries, water supply and other ecosystem services. This study develops a five-author school research project into a structured academic synthesis of aquatic biodiversity and the pressures affecting river organisms. abstract: To achieve optimal measurement of the Earth's magnetic field at different latitudes when the attitude of the sensor changes, an omnidirectional sensor is necessary for marine magnetometers. A novel omnidirectional sensor consisting of primary and compensation coils is proposed to enhance omnidirectional performance. title: Collaborative Governance in Strengthening the Early Warning System (EWS) and the Impact of Floods on Communities in Special Areas of Jakarta
abstract: Background: Flooding remains a recurring hydrometeorological disaster in Jakarta, causing significant social, economic, and environmental impacts. Strengthening flood early warning systems (EWS) requires technological infrastructure and effective stakeholder collaboration. Objective: This study examines collaborative governance in strengthening flood EWS and proposes a collaborative model to mitigate flood impacts on communities. abstract: We monitored the mortality of the fan mussel Pinna nobilis (L.) in the Venice lagoon (North of Italy) during a period of one and half year (2023–2024) in two areas named Ottagono Alberoni (OA) and Coffa Val Grande (CV) reporting the disease condition for the period time 2024. title: Nutrient enrichment shapes depth-resolved bacterial community assembly in mangrove sediments
abstract: Abstract Microbial communities in mangrove sediments are critical for carbon and nutrient cycling; yet despite their importance, responses to eutrophication — a pervasive global threat to coastal ecosystems — remain poorly understood. Here, we tested whether nutrient enrichment restructures mangrove sediment bacterial communities more strongly in the subsurface than at the sediment surface. We assessed bacterial community responses to an in-situ slow-release NPK (Osmocote®) enrichment experiment in a temperate mangrove (Avicennia marina subsp. australasica) forest in Aotearoa New Zealand. title: Tsunami Vertical Evacuation Decision Making in High-Rise Buildings: Insights from an Immersive Virtual Reality Study in Chile
abstract: Abstract Tsunami vertical evacuation (TVE) is increasingly recognized as a critical life-saving strategy in coastal areas where rapid access to natural high ground is not feasible. While prior research has examined TVE infrastructure and urban-scale evacuation, limited attention has been given to evacuee decision making and wayfinding inside high-rise buildings. This article presents an immersive virtual reality (VR) system to evaluate indoor vertical evacuation behavior across 12 existing buildings in four Chilean coastal cities. In this study, we report its occurrence within the shells of two bivalve species, opportunistically collected in Mali Ston Bay, Adriatic Sea. abstract: Objective: This study aimed to develop and validate the model and examine its practicality and potential effectiveness in enhancing elementary school students’ cultural literacy. title: Climate innovation readiness in Southeast Asian cities: Integrating national context and urban implementation
abstract: Rapid urbanization, intensifying climate risks, and accelerating digital transformation are placing Southeast Asian cities at the center of global climate transitions. However, cities across the region exhibit uneven capacity to institutionalize and scale climate innovation. Existing climate-readiness frameworks, largely developed in European and North American contexts, insufficiently capture the governance asymmetries, infrastructural fragmentation, and uneven digital development characterizing Southeast Asia. title: Soil organic carbon and nitrogen responses to cover crops in Norfolk soil under long‐term contrasting tillage systems
abstract: Abstract Cover crops have garnered increased attention as a conservation strategy to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and nitrogen (N) while improving overall soil health in agricultural systems. However, their effect on SOC and N dynamics in sandy soils of the US southeastern (SE) Coastal Plain is poorly understood. This study evaluated the response of SOC and N pools to cover crops in a Norfolk loamy sand under long‐term (>40 years) conventional (CvT) and conservation (CnT) tillage systems and short‐term (5 years) winter cover cropping. abstract: Background: Biliary ascariasis is an important cause of biliary obstruction and related complications, particularly in endemic regions. It occurs when Ascaris lumbricoides migrates from the intestine into the biliary tree. Although imaging modalities such as ultrasonography may aid in diagnosis, Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) provides direct visualization of the biliary tract and offers both diagnostic confirmation and therapeutic removal of the parasite. title: Lives and livres : recovering invisible individuals from French East India Company records
abstract: Abstract The archival ledgers of the second French East India Company (1719–70) appear well suited to digital analysis, but a quantitative approach can have risks. From our experience on a multi-year digital humanities project that revisits these maritime trade records, we share pros and cons of using relational databases to analyse individuals, geography and identity. title: The metabolic regimes of lake ecosystems
abstract: Abstract This synthesis seeks to spark research on the metabolic regimes of lakes, ponds, and reservoirs. A metabolic regime is the generalized annual pattern of ecosystem metabolism—gross primary production and ecosystem respiration—that characterizes a set of ecosystems. Characterizing metabolic regimes has increased understanding of terrestrial, marine, and stream ecosystems, but has been underexplored for lakes, ponds, and reservoirs despite a growing abundance of metabolism data from these systems. abstract: The hydrological study of the basin located south of Mariel Bay in the province of Artemisa aims to identify flood-prone areas within the basin to prevent hazards to the territory's society and economy. abstract: Climate and weather-related hazards pose significant challenges to infrastructure project implementation in Leyte Province, Philippines, where typhoons, heavy rainfall, flooding, landslides, and coastal hazards can disrupt construction activities and affect project performance. This study aimed to identify, assess, and prioritize climate and weather-related risks affecting public infrastructure projects in Leyte Province and to determine their effects on project time, cost, quality, and safety. title: Temperature-gated active salt secretion enables stable photothermal evaporation
abstract: Abstract Photothermal evaporation offers a sustainable solution for brine and seawater desalination, yet its long-term operation is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation arising from diffusion-limited ion transport, especially under high evaporative flux. Here, inspired by the active salt secretion of the mangrove, we develop a temperature-responsive evaporator that actively regulates ion transport through temperature-gated channel dynamics for stable high-flux evaporation. abstract: Small-scale capture fisheries are important for utilizing small pelagic fish resources and sustaining coastal livelihoods. This study analyzes the effects of fishermen’s capabilities and operational effectiveness on small pelagic fish resource utilization and floating lift net performance in the Makassar Strait waters off Sabang Village, Balaesang District, Donggala Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. abstract: In this study, we utilize a controlled cellulose nanofiber (CNF) platform to investigate how synthesis parameters of delaminated 2D MXene components influence cellular response, photothermal behavior, and antimicrobial activity of the resulting composite materials. Six Ti3C2Tx MXenes were synthesized, delaminated, and then integrated into a cellulose nanofiber network under identical loading and vacuum-filtration conditions. title: The impact of updating World Meteorological Organization baselines on Australian climate change messaging
abstract: Baselines matter in our perception of which is the climate ‘normal’ and what benchmark we use to track climate changes. Use of recent baselines grounds expectations about historical and future climates in recent lived experience, but differences between even similar recent periods shape our perceptions and interpretations of climate information. abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to freshwater scarcity, yet it faces bottlenecks regarding salt accumulation, limited evaporation modes, and single functionality. Here, inspired by plant vascular tissues, we have developed a 3D core–shell Janus hydrogel evaporator to achieve the synergy of high‐efficiency freshwater production and stable hydrovoltaic energy harvesting. abstract: Abstract. title: AdhE Regulates the Adaptation Ability of Streptococcus mutans to Oxidative Stress and Heat Stress
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how S. mutans adapts to environmental stresses is key to deciphering its cariogenic virulence. Here, we report that alcohol‐acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (AdhE) modulates the stress adaptability in S. mutans by regulating a metabolic‐acetylation axis. abstract: Indonesia aimed to eliminate Tuberculosis (TB) by 2050, with efforts scheduled to begin in 2030. However, TB cases remained high in Kuningan Regency, necessitating urgent measures to address this issue. abstract: In the context of the renewable energy transition, Floating Offshore Wind Turbines are an effective technology for harnessing wind resources farther from the coast, where water depths preclude the use of fixed-bottom solutions. title: Climate‐modulated accumulation and erosion of sediments in the Rodderberg crater basin for the last 439 ka (East Eifel Volcanic Field, Germany)
abstract: ABSTRACT Glacial/interglacial climate cycles since marine isotope stage (MIS) 12 influenced the discontinuous and 73 m‐long sediment record from the volcanic crater of Rodderberg in the East Eifel Volcanic Field, Germany. abstract: ABSTRACT Access to clean drinking water is a critical component of public health and a major target of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 6). abstract: Abstract Microplastic particles (MPs) are ubiquitous in aquatic environments, with rivers playing a key role in transporting them from terrestrial sources to marine systems. abstract: Understanding how genome-wide divergence translates to barriers to gene flow is a central question in speciation research, particularly in marine environments where interconnected habitats frequently accommodate cryptic diversity. Using linked-read whole-genome data from the brown alga Ectocarpus, we investigated genome-wide reproductive isolation between two cryptic brown algal species E. siliculosus and E. crouaniorum across replicated hybrid zones in Europe and Chile. title: Selective Hg2+ Detection Using an Aza-BODIPY-Derived NIR Fluorescence Sensor: Environmental and Biological Applications
abstract: Abstract Mercury contamination in natural environments poses severe threats to ecosystems and human health, emphasizing the urgent need for reliable Hg2+ detection methods. In this work, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent aza-BODIPY derivative (BT) was synthesized as a potential fluorescence sensor. BT exhibited dual colorimetric and “turn-on” NIR fluorometric responses toward Hg2+ in H2O:EtOH (3:7 v/v), achieving a detection limit of 1.7 ppb. The sensor displayed high selectivity through rapid BT–Hg2+ complexation, with reversible sensing enabled by the addition of potassium iodide (KI).

abstract: Abstract Forest and land fires in Indonesia are frequently attributed to oil palm expansion and slash-and-burn land clearing, yet the social and institutional dynamics underlying fire occurrence remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the drivers of forest and land fires through case studies of two oil palm concessions in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, with particular attention to enclave areas within concession boundaries. title: The Impact of Land Use and Land Cover Changes on Runoff Volume for Hydropower
abstract: ABSTRACT This research investigates the complex relationship between land use and land cover (LULC) changes and runoff for hydropower. Remote sensing and Geographic Information System (GIS) approach were employed to conduct the analysis on LULC changes over the period of 21 years. abstract: Urban water bodies significantly contribute to mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, particularly during hot summer months. However, most studies have primarily focused on large water bodies, often overlooking the role and efficiency of smaller or medium-sized artificial ones. abstract: Abstract Magnetite and maghemite are the most common carrier minerals of paleomagnetic information in marine and terrestrial sediments. abstract: Pacific Island Countries (PICs) matter as geostrategic players in the Indo-Pacific maritime region for two main reasons: they are key players in global climate governance, and they offer good cases for studying small states in Area Studies. abstract: ABSTRACT Vibrio harveyi is a prominent bacterial pathogen of marine aquaculture. Vibrio harveyi has not previously been reported in starry flounder. abstract: Abstract The lateral line is a mechanosensory system that plays an important role in key fish behaviors such as navigation, prey detection, and schooling. abstract: Incidental bycatch of harbour porpoise ( Phocoena phocoena ) in set-net fisheries poses a threat to their populations. abstract: Mercury exposure during pregnancy remains a public health concern due to its potential impact on foetal neurodevelopment. title: Drivers of Spatial Change in Seagrass Carbon Stock Amid Shifting Species Dominance
abstract: Abstract Seagrass meadows are recognized for their significant role in blue carbon sequestration and storage. However, these ecosystems are being altered by climate change, and consequently so too are the ecosystem services they provide. Here, we evaluate drivers of spatial variation in carbon storage among seagrass meadows in the Lower Chesapeake Bay, which underwent a temperature-driven shift in species dominance from Zostera marina to Ruppia maritima in the last decade. abstract: La educación emocional en la actualidad es considerada un proceso clave en el desarrollo de habilidades socioemocionales y cognitivas que hacen posible el aprendizaje en cualquier área del conocimiento. abstract: ABSTRACT Local adaptation in species with high gene flow can be facilitated through different genomic mechanisms. For example, multiple studies have demonstrated that chromosomal inversions (CIs) are important for adaptive divergence in systems with high gene flow because they help protect locally adaptive alleles from recombination. Although much focus has been given to the importance of CIs in harboring adaptive alleles, there are other mechanisms that can facilitate genetic divergence. title: Mangrove Gastropod Research in Indonesia: A Scoping Review of Taxonomic Composition, Publication Trends, and Methodological Gaps (2015–2025)
abstract: To our knowledge, based on the databases searched, no scoping review specifically mapping publication trends, reported taxonomic composition, methodological approaches, and research gaps in Indonesian mangrove gastropod studies has been identified. This study aimed to summarize the temporal and geographic distribution of publications, identify the most frequently reported gastropod families and species, evaluate sampling and data analysis approaches, and identify research gaps to guide future studies. abstract: This preliminary study evaluated dietary inclusion of Sargassum spp. meal in feeds for prejuvenile Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) through method-specific feed characterization and a 67-day feeding trial. Two experimental diets containing 10% and 15% Sargassum spp. meal were compared with a commercial reference feed using 54 fish distributed among nine aquaria, with three independent aquaria per treatment and six fish per aquarium. abstract: Passenger terminals are not only service facilities for maritime travelers but also transport nodes that shape accessibility, mobility, and the functional relationship between ports and their surrounding areas. This study evaluates passenger-terminal facility performance and translates service-improvement priorities into implications for port-area development. abstract: Abstract Background Forests in the Baltic Sea region store carbon, harbour biodiversity, sustain rural livelihoods and supply wood for materials and heating. title: Immune Response of the Pacific Oyster Magallana gigas Following Shell Damage
abstract: Shell integrity is a key determinant of health in cultured bivalves; however, its damage may affect physiological and immune processes associated with repair. This study evaluated the effects of a single non-penetrating shell damage on cellular immune responses and immune-related gene expression in the mantle of the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas.
