title: Stage- and tissue-specific cadmium accumulation in Portunus trituberculatus during gonadal maturation
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in Portunus trituberculatus raises food safety concerns, yet its tissue-specific distribution during gonadal maturation remains poorly understood. Previous studies commonly combined hepatopancreas and gonads as “brown meat”, making it difficult to determine the relative contribution of individual tissues to Cd accumulation. title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. abstract: Abstract The Stokes drift generated by surface gravity waves has been widely investigated in both laboratory and field studies. However, key uncertainties remain, particularly regarding the modulating role possibly played by long-term oscillations induced by infragravity-like waves locally varying the mean depth. title: Retention forestry practices in India for biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, and sustainable forest management across diverse forest zones
abstract: Retention forestry is an ecologically informed forest management approach in which selected trees, deadwood, habitat patches, keystone species, old-growth individuals, riparian corridors, and microhabitats are deliberately retained during forest management interventions to maintain biodiversity, ecological continuity, and ecosystem services. title: Assessment of the stress response at harvest in European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax) in relation to water temperature and slaughter method
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of harvest and slaughter method, stunning procedure, and rearing water temperature on physiological stress response, loss of behavioral responses (LBR) and post − mortem muscle quality changes in European seabass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ). Physiological outcomes comprised plasma cortisol, glucose, lactate, and osmolality, while post-mortem outcomes were assessed by measuring muscle pH and rigor mortis temporal changes. abstract: SUMMARY Hypnea species are distributed across tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions. They exhibit high intraspecific morphological variation, which complicates species delimitation based solely on morphological characteristics. Recently, molecular analyses have enabled the validation of numerous species, the identification of cryptic species, and the description of new taxa. abstract: Na Península Ulu (PU), Ilha James Ross (IJR), localizada no Mar de Weddell, lado oriental da Península Antártica, é possível observar uma relação única de relevo-rocha-solo devido à configuração da paisagem, exemplificada por relevos em mesa e superfícies sedimentares erosivas como principais compartimentos geomorfológicos. title: Risk modelling of Human Machine Interactions in remotely operated ships using STPA and Bayesian Networks
abstract: Human-Machine Interactions (HMI) affect the safety of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS), particularly in remote operations where operators supervise vessels from a distance. As these interactions introduce risks inadequately captured by conventional methods, this study develops a methodology for quantifying HMI-related risks. title: Environmental triggers of resting spore germination in the chytrid parasite Staurastromyces oculus
abstract: Abstract Many parasites rely on a resting stage to endure across adverse environmental conditions or over periods of host scarcity. However, maturation conditions of the resting stage during dormancy and the proximate cues that trigger germination remain unknown for most parasite species, limiting our ability to predict when parasites reinitiate infection. title: Hidden population declines revealed by integrating long-term fisheries data with fishers’ knowledge
abstract: Abstract Technological creep, the gradual increase in fishing power due to technological innovation, can mask population declines and bias fisheries assessments, yet information on historical technology adoption is rarely available. Here, we integrate long-term fisheries statistics (1972–2022) with structured interviews with experienced fishers to reconstruct technological change in the Japanese pole-and-line skipjack tuna ( Katsuwonus pelamis ) fishery. abstract: Ecosystem monitoring frequently focuses on populations, but a community perspective better reflects food web ecology. We asked a common question among natural resource managers – how much sampling is needed to understand the community in my system? We identified two objectives: (1) provide a community perspective and (2) ensure computational effort does not become unwieldy. abstract: Seabird bycatch mitigation in longline fisheries has been a focus of sustainable fisheries research for decades. One strategy is to increase the sink rate of hooks to reduce the window of opportunity for seabirds to take baits and become hooked. However, this requires an understanding of the different forces on hooks and branchlines when setting gear. abstract: Understanding variation in body-size allometry and genetic diversity of the orange mud crab, Scylla olivacea, is important for effective fisheries management and conservation. This study evaluated length-weight relationships (LWRs) and mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) genetic diversity among S. olivacea samples collected once from four mangrove ecosystems (four localities; 28 individuals from each locality) along the east and west coasts of Peninsular Malaysia. The nutritional value and heavy metal concentration of the edible portions and by-products of two shrimp species that are consumed in Cameroon were evaluated in this study. abstract: Abstract Mesozoic calcareous nannofossils of the family Eoconusphaeraceae have traditionally been interpreted as nannoliths of uncertain biological affinity. However, their morphology, crystallographic organization, and occurrence in articulated coccospheres strongly suggest that they represent coccoliths produced by haptophyte algae. abstract: The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. abstract: Chinese hook snout carp ( Opsariichthys bidens ) deteriorates readily during postharvest transport, yet the interplay between muscle protein degradation, volatile flavor formation, and microbial metabolism under realistic transportation conditions remains poorly understood. This is the first study to systematically investigate the correlation between protein structural changes and microbial metabolism in Chinese hook snout carp during refrigerated transport simulating natural conditions at 4 °C, 16 °C, and 32 °C. abstract: Modern running tracks and football fields are covered with synthetic surfaces made of polyurethane and rubber blends with an admixture of various materials. We collected sand samples from the long jump sandpits of six elementary school and university sports facilities and examined microplastics (MPs) originating from synthetic surfaces. abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluated the effects of substituting fishmeal with Artemia biomass in aquaculture diets on growth performance and whole‐body composition of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Four dietary treatments were administered in triplicate to juvenile Nile tilapia (44 g) stocked in 1m 3 cages in a pond at 30 fish per cage for 84 days. abstract: Sourcing protein-based biomaterials directly from nature presents persistent challenges in scalability, processing, and batch-to-batch variability. abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhouse gas emissions from temporarily flooded upland croplands remain poorly characterized in the global greenhouse gas budget. We combined field measurements from 11 maize‐field sites temporarily flooded across the North China Plain with a global synthesis of 23 flooded upland cropland sites to quantify diffusive emissions. abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics are emerging contaminants in aquatic ecosystems, but their direct and maternally transmitted effects on host–parasite interactions remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Food web theory predicts that a top omnivore would not induce a trophic cascade through intermediate consumers and basal resources. abstract: Social relationships can shape the demands placed on animal communication, but different dimensions of social organization may affect signal repertoires in different ways. We investigated whether variation in social network structure covaried with whistle repertoire organization in wild common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ). abstract: Hot-water extraction offers a practical and food-compatible method for recovering soluble constituents from Halymenia durvillei , but extraction conditions may affect extract concentration and biomass-based recovery differently. This study evaluated the effects of biomass-to-water ratios (1:25 and 1:50, w/v), temperature (70 and 90°C), extraction times (1 and 2 h) and sequential extraction cycles on crude carbohydrate-rich extracts from sun-dried H. durvillei . abstract: Tourism urbanization prioritizes tourism consumption over traditional residential-focused development, reshaping land use patterns in destination areas. This research examines how tourism urbanization is associated with agricultural landscape change in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain from 1995 to 2020. abstract: Salicornia bigelovii is a promising oilseed crop known for its high yield potential and exceptional salt tolerance, ranking among the most salt-resistant vascular plants. abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. abstract: This study investigates the ecology of the extinct European Hippopotamus from the late Early–Middle Pleistocene ( c . 900–400 ka) sequence of the Megalopolis Basin, a glacial microrefugium for temperate taxa in southern Greece. Using stable carbon (δ 13 C) and oxygen (δ 18 O) isotope analyses and microwear analyses of Hippopotamus dental elements, we reconstruct dietary variability, past habitat conditions and hydrological or climatic changes at intra‐annual, multi‐annual and millennial scales. abstract: This study compares external morphology, claw handedness, and relative claw exaggeration in two sympatric fiddler crab species, Austruca annulipes and Austruca perplexa , collected from Ca Mau Province, Vietnam. A total of 206 adult males were measured across 19 morphometric traits, including carapace size, claw elements, and walking leg proportions. abstract: Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. abstract: We analyzed riverbed microbiota structure, gene expression, and fatty acid production across several sites along Little Miami River in Ohio, United States. abstract: Heavy metal contamination in agricultural soils and edible crops raises concerns about environmental quality and food safety in Bangladesh. This study investigated arsenic (As), lead (Pb), chromium (Cr), and cadmium (Cd) in 15 paired soil and edible crop samples from Nagarkanda Upazila, Faridpur. abstract: The Manila Amendments to the STCW Convention set compliance requirements for seafarers’ maritime communicative competence; however, higher-vocational Maritime English assessment still relies mainly on summative final-term evaluation, with high oral-assessment costs and delayed feedback. abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. abstract: Recurrent Ulva prolifera green-tide threatens ecosystems, and greenhouse-gas release during the decomposition of accumulated biomass can diminish the climate benefits of algal carbon fixation. abstract: This study explores a methodology for evaluating the component elements of health tourism destinations from the perspective of “therapeutic landscapes”. An index system for evaluating suitable areas of health tourism was established, and an empirical analysis was conducted using Hainan Island as a case study. abstract: The study was conducted due to rapid land use change driven by oil palm expansion in the Arowana Golden Red Conservation Area (AgrCA) in Riau Province, Indonesia. The study assessed the expansion of oil palm plantations and their influence on the environment of AgrCA. Using satellite imagery in 2017 and 2021, we found that oil palm plantations expanded from 2,234 ha (60.4% of the total area of AgrCA) in 2017 to 2,752 ha (74.4%) in 2021 by the conversion of swamps and swamp forests. title: Russia and Norway on Svalbard in Russian Media: Morphosyntax and the Construction of Arctic Actors
abstract: This study examines how the Russian mainstream newspaper Rossijskaja Gazeta represented Russia and Norway in the context of Svalbard during 2022–2025. Svalbard is a Norwegian Arctic Archipelago with a unique legal status that allows other countries, including Russia, to conduct economic activity there. title: Ecological pressures on the Kura River and sustainable pathways for pollution control, water conservation and biodiversity protection
abstract: The Kura River is a transboundary freshwater system linking upstream, middle-basin and downstream communities, agriculture, infrastructure and ecosystems across the South Caucasus. This study restructures and extends an original educational research project on the ecological problems of the Kura River while preserving its central themes, visual materials, tables and ten-question survey instrument. abstract: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. abstract: Intensive Litopenaeus vannamei culture generates organic loading that degrades pond water quality, yet nutrient status, phytoplankton composition, and Vibrio abundance are rarely examined together within a single production system. abstract: This study reports the heterologous production, purification, and characterization of the cytochrome Cyc2 TAG1 cluster 1 (Cyc2 TAG1_1 ) from Ghiorsea bivora TAG1 in the outer membrane of Escherichia coli BL21. title: An operational framework to develop and apply mid-range theory for conservation science
abstract: Conservation solutions often lack transferability between contexts, a weakness that stems from a lack of connection between general theories and context-specific research. To address this problem, we propose a methodology for developing middle-range theory in conservation science through the formalised application of an operational conceptual framework. title: Evaluating the Environmental and Biological Safety of Phosphonium-Based Porous Liquid Systems
abstract: Abstract Porous liquids have emerged as a promising class of advanced materials that combine permanent porosity with fluidity. They are often proposed as “green” alternatives in separations and catalysis, although their biological safety remains underexplored. abstract: Numerous studies have shown that oil-adjuvanted vaccines (OAV) can induce a variety of different side effects in Atlantic salmon including spinal deformities (SD). abstract: The genus Nostoc has long been known to be polyphyletic, and recent taxonomic work has segregated several Nostoc-like lineages into new genera, including Compactonostoc. Until now, C. shennongjiaensis was the only described species in the genus. abstract: The cement industry represents a significant source of atmospheric particulate emissions that may contribute to the deposition of trace metals in surrounding soils. This study evaluated the concentrations of zinc (Zn), manganese (Mn), and lead (Pb) in topsoil collected around a cement plant in Branis, Algeria. title: Earth as a wasted planet: An ecocritical study of anthropogenic waste in Kim Stanley Robinson’s 2312
abstract: The Earth has long served as a nurturing habitat for both living and non-living entities. However, humanity’s anthropocentric interventions have resulted in profound ecological degradation, thereby disrupting the ethical relationship between Anthropos and the Anthropocene. abstract: Abstract Biological invasions commonly occur in series, leading to new interactions between multiple invaders in novel habitats. abstract: To study the size-resolved organic aerosol composition in New York City, daily aerosol samples were collected using a Micro-Orifice Uniform Deposition Impactor (MOUDI) during the Summer 2023 New York City Metropolitan Measurements of Emissions and TransformationS (NYC-METS) campaign. title: The complete mitochondrial genome and phylogenetic analysis of the zebra turkeyfish Dendrochirus zebra (Cuvier, 1829) (Teleostei: Perciformes)
abstract: Dendrochirus zebra, a reef-dewelling scorpaenid, was sequenced for its complete mitochondrial genome (16,504 bp). abstract: The increasing pollution in aquatic systems with harmful substances and the persistent build up of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere have emerged as major environmental concerns, necessitating sustainable and efficient remediation strategies. abstract: Abstract Introduction Quarry restoration in Mediterranean regions such as Cyprus is expected to face more intensive problems than neighboring reference habitats due to effects of their recent disturbance, size, and isolation. Epigeic arthropod biodiversity can provide useful clues on restoration success. Objectives We assessed diversity of restored and reference areas at 10 quarry sites in Cyprus. title: Biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland
abstract: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of national gross domestic product. In this study, we assessed the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022. abstract: Indicator development for earth system governance involves choices that influence which issues are considered legitimate. This makes indicators inherently political, rather than merely technical tools that objectively inform policy decisions. This article proposes a framework of indicator politics and applies this to the development of inequality indicators under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Haryana. abstract: Abstract Trichochromones B–D (2–4), three new spirotetrahydrochromanone lactones, were isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1, together with the known trichochromone A (1). abstract: Ekosistem mangrove merupakan komunitas tumbuhan yang khas, hidup di wilayah pesisir dan muara sungai yang dipengaruhi oleh pasang surut. abstract: At a moment when climate change has become one of the most urgent cultural, political, and ethical crises of the Anthropocene, this paper argues that contemporary Anglophone theatre offers a powerful critical space for rethinking the damaged relationship between humanity and nature. It examines Bilodeau’s No More Harveys and Carleton’s The Turquoise Elephant through an ecocritical lens, focusing on pollution, the pastoral, wilderness, and apocalypse. abstract: Skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is one of Indonesia’s important fishery commodities with high economic value. abstract: Perkinsus olseni is a major pathogenic parasite that threatens shellfish aquaculture and can trigger mass mortality and considerable economic losses. Conventional culture-based assays and PCR-based detection protocols for P. olseni recommended by the World Organization for Animal Health (OIE) involve long assay durations and heavy dependence on sophisticated instruments, making them unsuitable for on-site rapid screening. abstract: This study focused on the tectonic setting and geothermal potential for selected areas within the Middle Benue Trough, North-Central Nigeria, using aeromagnetic data. title: Generative inference model reveals political and economic motivations for road construction in past societies
abstract: Abstract The construction of roads in past societies reflects a trade-off between a preference for straightness and the influence of slope gradient. This trade-off is, however, also conditioned by other factors, principally the political and economic motivations of a past society. abstract: Abstract Objective The intentional and accidental introduction of nonnative fishes has damaged freshwater ecosystems around the world. abstract: Freshwater food webs are increasingly exposed to eutrophication and warming, which can shift phytoplankton community composition and reduce the availability of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids to higher trophic levels. abstract: Erythropoietin (EPO) is the main hormonal regulator of erythropoiesis in vertebrates and also mediates non-hematopoietic functions. Despite extensive characterization in mammals, the cellular sources and targets of EPO signaling remain poorly defined in non-mammalian vertebrates. abstract: Anthropogenic activity threatens biodiversity through climate change, habitat fragmentation, and increasing frequency and scale of disturbance. However, the conus arteriosus and its valves, key components of the heart and blood circulation, have been underexplored in phylogenetic and ecomorphological contexts. title: Automated reconstruction of reproducible protein databases with RepDBmaker
abstract: RepDBmaker is a reproducible Snakemake pipeline designed for the automated construction of large-scale protein sequence databases. It enables the seamless downloading of sequences from different public databases and the integration of user-specified proteomes. The pipeline also performs standardized taxonomic annotations to all compiled sequences and contamination screening in eukaryotic proteomes. title: Trends in climate variables and their associations with crop yields in Fogera and Pawe districts, northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Understanding climate variability and its relationship with crop productivity is important for developing appropriate adaptation strategies in rainfed agricultural systems. This study assessed temporal trends and variability in rainfall and temperature and examined their associations with crop yields in Fogera and Pawe districts of northwestern Ethiopia. abstract: Abstract In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), specifically SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), this study examines the impacts of extreme climate change on grain production in the key agricultural region of northwest China. abstract: By snapping their claws, snapping shrimp create cavitation bubbles that release supersonic pressure waves when they collapse. Shock waves such as these are dangerous to animals because they can cause blast-induced neurotrauma by transferring kinetic energy to neural tissues. Previously, we discovered that helmet-like orbital hoods protect snapping shrimp from blast-induced neurotrauma by damping the shock waves they generate and use as weapons. title: Microtubules coordinate cellularization in a coenocytic relative of animals
abstract: Cellularization is the coordinated division of a multinucleate cell into many cells, a common life cycle transition across eukaryotes. In the best-studied model of this process, Drosophila melanogaster , cellularization requires actin and microtubule networks, as well as membrane vesicle delivery to drive the synchronous invagination of plasma membrane furrows. To identify unifying principles, we investigate cellularization in the ichthyosporean Sphaeroforma arctica , a close relative of animals with a multinucleate life cycle stage. abstract: Natural predation where rarity meets rarity raises an important conservation paradox: when one threatened species feeds on another and conservation decisions can be challenging. Here we present a natural history observation of such an interaction. During a camera-trapping survey in Singalila National Park, West Bengal, India, we documented a rare predation event involving an Asiatic Black Bear Ursus thibetanus and a Red Panda Ailurus fulgens. abstract: The present research study focuses on how food can be interpreted as a sort of indentured resistance in Khal Torabully's selected poems. The idea of Gastrocolonial is used as analysis of the various manifestations of food memories, spices, and markets as symbols of cultural continuity for Indian indentured laborers. We investigated sediments from a typical highly urbanized river basin—the Qinhuai River Basin, China—during normal flow (March 2025) and high flow (June 2025). title: Effect of shade and surface material on thermal conditions in California schoolyards
abstract: Schoolyards represent a critical asset for mitigating climate-related heat exposure among children. Young children in elementary school are a group particularly vulnerable to rising temperatures, heat waves, and prolonged exposure to high thermal stress. Such pupils are more susceptible to heat due to their physiological characteristics and the amount of time they spend outdoors during school hours. title: Temporal variability of mineral dust composition on an alpine snowpack in the Tateyama Mountains, Japan
abstract: Mineral dust is one of the major light-absorbing impurities in snow and ice, and affects snowpack and glacier melting. However, the origin and composition of mineral dust deposited on snow surfaces, and how these vary over time and space, remain poorly understood. This study examined the temporal and spatial variability in the composition of mineral dust in an alpine snowpack in the Tateyama Mountains, Japan and evaluated the relative contributions of long-range-transported and locally derived dust to dust deposition on the snow surface. abstract: The match/mismatch hypothesis (MMH) predicts that consumers that are asynchronous with a key ephemeral resource will have reduced fitness. However, by diet-switching to an alternative resource with which it is synchronous, a consumer may be able to buffer the negative fitness consequences of asynchrony. abstract: Abstract: The accelerating processes of global population growth and urbanization have led to increased use of transportation systems. This intensifies urban mobility and poses various environmental sustainability challenges. In this context, sustainable urban mobility has become increasingly significant. It enhances the quality of urban life, reduces carbon emissions, improves the efficiency of transportation systems, transforms cities into smart destinations, and strengthens their positions within tourism destinations. Engaged research practices, such as co-production and participatory action research, may be useful in addressing these complex questions and pushing adaptation research towards more transformative ends. abstract: Mycotoxins in cereals, particularly maize, represent a major threat to food safety and agricultural sustainability, a challenge expected to intensify under climate change. In this context, the development of environmentally friendly and sustainable mitigation strategies is urgently needed. abstract: Cavity-filling calcite is among the most widespread secondary phases in the Deccan Traps, and its position late in the amygdale paragenesis, after zeolites and silica phases, is long established. abstract: The issue of repatriating colonial cultural objects from the Netherlands to Indonesia has gained momentum as part of efforts toward historical reconciliation, postcolonial justice, and complex cultural diplomacy. abstract: ABSTRACT Phthalates pose significant risks to aquatic ecosystems, though their effects on nontarget organisms have been reported, with little information on Hydra. abstract: ABSTRACT A key bottleneck in the development of octopus aquaculture is the absence of formulated feeds that are readily consumed and fulfil their nutritional requirements. Until efficacious formulated feeds are developed, sustainably‐sourced natural seafood diets provide a potential viable alternative for octopus aquaculture. Long-term monitoring of life stages and traits is commonly used to assess population viability. However, comprehensive monitoring is challenging for inconspicuous orchids in spatially discrete subpopulations. title: A Persistent Warm West in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh: Spatial Contrasts Are Recoverable Where Multi-Decadal Trends Are Not
abstract: The Bangladesh Sundarbans is the largest continuous mangrove forest in the world, and the satellite thermal record over it is now long enough to invite decadal analysis. We ask a prior question: which parts of that thermal signal can the archive actually resolve? Using 25 years of MODIS April composites, we find the western third of the forest persistently warmer than the eastern third, by 0.654°C on average (95% confidence interval +0.428 to +0.880°C, paired p = 3.6 × 10 -6 ) and in 23 of the 25 individual years. title: Harnessing Wastewater-Based Epidemiology for One Health surveillance of enteric viruses
abstract: Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE) is an approach that is widely used to monitor the occurrence and distribution of pathogens shed by human populations through wastewater. This review critically evaluates the application of WBE of enteric viruses within a One Health paradigm. It highlights how enteric viruses from human and animal sources end up in wastewater and aquatic environments, and how their presence can be used to predict the occurrence of diseases in human and animal populations. abstract: ABSTRACT Countries have differing priorities in the process of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Examining how these priorities are reflected in national strategies facilitates the interpretation of future actions. The literature on SDGs achievement in Türkiye has largely been limited to municipalities, universities, and sectoral institutions. abstract: The Rosebud Sioux Tribe of southern South Dakota provides a case of study of the challenges Native American tribes in the Great Plains region face in developing sustainable water supplies that are resilient to both droughts and long-term climate change. The Rosebud Indian Reservation has a semiarid climate with water supplies that are particularly vulnerable to natural climate variation and a drying climate. abstract: Human–elephant conflict (HEC) in the Southern Western Ghats has significant socio-economic and ecological impacts, highlighting the need for an integrated mitigation approach. title: Biodegradable mulch films affecting surface runoff, soil erosion, and film fragment loss from farmland
abstract: The use of conventional plastic mulch films is a common agricultural practice that can lead to persistent plastic film fragments entering soil systems. To prevent the accumulation of these fragments, soil-biodegradable mulch films are marketed as alternatives. Unlike conventional plastic mulch, soil-biodegradable mulch films are ploughed into the soil after use, where they biodegrade over time. title: MARKETING STRATEGIES IN TOURISM-LED REAL ESTATE SALES AND DEVELOPMENT: CASE OF GEORGIA
abstract: This article examines the impact of tourism marketing strategies on real estate sales and development in Georgia. It argues that destina­tion marketing influences property markets indirectly but systematically by producing desti­na­tion awareness, place familiarity, repeat visitation, perceived safety, year-round utility, and confidence in the future attractiveness of a location. title: Conceptual frameworks and learning outcomes for a two-course sequence in energy geographies
abstract: The essay aims to advance the teaching and learning of energy geographies through reflection on 17 years of navigating rapid change in the national and international energy geographies, technologies, economics, and politics. After establishing the institutional and personal research contexts in a large land-grant university, the paper describes a three-part conceptual framework emphasizing energy systems, production of space, and whole-systems approaches. title: Changes in Thermal Growing‐Season Characteristics in Estonia During 1965–2025: Regional Variability and Methodological Sensitivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal growing‐season characteristics in Estonia were analysed for 1965–2025 using daily mean air temperature observations from 15 meteorological stations. Start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and growing‐season length (GSL) were determined using both the traditional Raik–Tarand method and the internationally standardised ETCCDI definition to evaluate their comparability in spatial patterns, annual variability, and long‐term change. title: Assessment of the reproductive biology of largetooth silverside Chirostoma arge (Atherinopsidae) in Lake Chapala, Mexico
abstract: Chirostoma arge (Jordan and Snyder, 1899) is a fish endemic to the central plateau of Mexico important for fishing in natural reservoirs such as Lake Chapala. Unfortunately, little is known about this species of the Atherinopsidae family, which is listed as Data Deficient by the IUCN Red List. This study’s objective was to determine the sex ratio, the stage of gonadal maturity in each sex, the spawning season and to estimate the relative condition factor, the minimum standard length and the standard length at first maturity. title: Evaluating Thermal Resistance in Cryogenic LNG Cargo Containment Systems: A Case Study of The Tangguh–FSRU Jawa Satu Transport Route
abstract: This study evaluated the thermal resistance performance of spherical cryogenic storage tanks on liquefied natural gas carriers operating between the Tangguh refinery and the Jawa Satu Floating Storage Regasification Unit to address the operational challenge of cargo shrinkage. The natural evaporation of cryogenic fluids during maritime transportation represented a physical loss of energy supply and caused a significant financial burden on the national energy supply chain. title: Landscape composition, patch size, and local characteristics shape ant and beetle assemblages in naturally patchy indigenous forests
abstract: Indigenous forests are important reservoirs of terrestrial arthropod biodiversity, but naturally patchy forests are understudied compared to human-fragmented forests. We evaluated the relative influence of landscape composition, patch size, and local characteristics on ants (Formicidae) and beetles (Coleoptera) in Southern Mistbelt Forests in South Africa. These forests exist as small patches within a fire-prone grassland matrix, with the grasslands undergoing modification for forestry, agriculture and rural development. title: Reconstructing Eco-Jurisprudence: Qirā'ah Mu'āṣirah fī al-Aḥkām and Systems Theory in Operationalizing Ecological Maqāṣid
abstract: This research explores the global ecological crisis as a structural failure in the relationship between humans, law, and nature, rooted in the anthropocentric paradigm. Although Indonesia possesses rich theological values regarding nature conservation, the eco-theological response has tended to be ethical-spiritual and lacks legal-formal enforcement. This qualitative research with a juridical-normative approach aims to reconstruct the epistemology of Islamic law through Shofiyullah Muzammil's Qira'ah Mu'āṣirah fī al-Ahkām method, synthesized with Jasser Auda's Systems Theory. title: An internally consistent framework for calculating cascading probabilistic earthquake risk and its application to a case study in New Zealand
abstract: Abstract. Quantifying the combined effects of earthquakes and their cascading hazards is essential for realistic risk assessment, yet such approaches remain limited in practice. Dynamic frameworks that explicitly correlate hazard intensities and their uncertainties across cascading perils provide more consistent and physically plausible impact estimates, offering greater value for resilience planning and risk management. title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of the Seaweed Sensory Space Through Consumer‐Evoked Associations Across Ireland, Norway, Spain, and Turkey
abstract: Understanding the sensory space of a product category is a valuable tool in New Product Development, particularly for emerging food categories such as seaweed, where consumer familiarity remains limited in many markets. The current work explored the sensory associations of consumers willing to try seaweed products across four European countries (Ireland, Norway, Spain, and Turkey) through a cross-cultural online survey. title: Sustainable urban development: An integrated assessment of Kazakhstani cities
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstract Rapid urbanization has increased pressure on urban systems, creating challenges related to resource efficiency, waste management, and environmental protection. These challenges are particularly acute for Kazakhstan, where cities differ substantially in their resource use, environmental conditions, infrastructure, and socioeconomic characteristics. This study aims to conduct a comparative assessment and identify the key characteristics of urban metabolic profiles and sustainable development in Kazakhstani cities. abstract: Mangrove carbon assessments require spatially explicit methods whose assumptions, data support, and verification status remain traceable. This study presents an integrated workflow for operational mangrove mapping, modeled above-ground carbon (AGC) estimation, complementary carbon accounting, parameter sensitivity, and a prototype digital measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) provenance layer for a Sundarbans area bounded by approximately 88.10–89.10°E and 21.50–22.35°N. abstract: The role of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) on the sexual maturity of Prochilodus brevis is unknown. title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
abstract: Abstract Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. title: TECHNOGENIC POLLUTION OF RIVER WATERS IN THE ATYRAU REGION: HYDROCHEMICAL RISK ASSESSMENT FOR RECREATIONAL USE
abstract: River waters in the Atyrau region are utilised intensively for both economic and recreational purposes. The distinctive natural-climatic conditions of the region and ongoing technogenic loading exert a direct influence on the spatial variability of water quality. Consequently, assessing the hydrochemical state of river waters—specifically identifying areas with high pollution risk—is a matter of critical importance. title: Combined effects of heatwaves and pollution on freshwater invertebrates: a scoping review of experimental approaches
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are highly vulnerable to climate change and anthropogenic pollution. Climate change is characterized particularly by an increase in average temperatures, with more intense, longer, and more frequent heatwaves (HWs). While the effects of contaminants are well documented, sometimes in the context of global warming, the impact of HWs, either alone or in combination with pollution, remains poorly studied in freshwater invertebrates. title: Design of Smart Antifouling Surfaces Using Enzyme-Responsive Surface Topographies
abstract: Biofilm accumulation on polymeric surfaces remains a persistent challenge in biomedical, industrial, and environmental systems. Here, we report an enzyme-responsive antifouling surface that integrates particle-generated topography with biologically activated surface renewal. Microparticles of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) and the chitinase-responsive polymer PHEVD were generated by mechanical abrasion and embedded into poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) to create polymer-composite surfaces with three-dimensionally distributed microparticles. title: Long-term changes in extreme precipitation and their non-stationary teleconnections with ENSO and PDO over Vietnam (1981–2024)
abstract: This study investigates long term spatial trends, interannual variability, and evolving teleconnections of total and extreme precipitation across Vietnam using the climate hazards group InfraRed precipitation with station data (CHIRPS) and 11 expert team on climate change detection and indices (ETCCDI) precipitation indices. The results reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity in precipitation extremes. title: Warming vs. browning: a dual mechanism behind net ecosystem production of shallow brown aquatic systems
abstract: Abstract. Northern lakes are warming and browning due to increased cDOM inputs, altering water column C:N:P ratios and temperatures that regulate photoautotrophic and heterotrophic production. Yet the relative importance of warming versus browning, and their combined effects on nutrient stoichiometry and microbial dynamics remain unclear. title: Liquid polymer enhances methanogenesis and restructures prokaryotic communities in freshwater sediments
abstract: Abstract. The widespread use of synthetic hydrophilic polymers, such as polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), has raised concerns about their potential effects on environmental biogeochemical processes, yet their impact on sediment ecosystems remains largely unexplored. We investigated how PVP influences methane (CH4) production and prokaryotic community composition in freshwater sediments over a 56-day anoxic incubation. title: The ‘Great Frost’ of 1708–9 in Britain and the Condescensions of Posterity
abstract: Abstract This article explores the ‘great frost’ of 1709 and its impact on economic life in Britain, challenging a popular view that, based on gross domestic product (GDP) estimates, it was catastrophic. It shows that the annual GDP figures for the period have such wide error margins that they cannot establish the scale of the disruption; that the severe winter was felt in southern but not northern Britain; that there were, in any case, means of partially mitigating such disruptions; and that the economic difficulties that were experienced had various causes, not just those of a bad winter. title: Social inequality among Neolithic fisher-foragers: Statistical analysis of grave goods from three Pitted Ware Culture cemeteries on Gotland, Sweden
abstract: How was burial wealth distributed within a Neolithic fisher-forager society? This paper explores this question by analyzing the distribution of burial goods at three different Middle Neolithic Pitted Ware Culture (PWC) cemeteries located on Gotland, Sweden, dating to c. 3000–2300 BCE. Specifically, our dataset consists of 40 burials from Visby, 51 burials from Ajvide, and 51 burials from Västerbjers. title: Introducing Spiroacetal Units to Tune Thermomechanical Properties and Enhance Chemical Recyclability of Poly(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate)
abstract: Abstract Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is a widely used biodegradable polyester. Still, the range of applications may be further broadened by extending the property range and improving recyclability. To address this issue, we gradually exchanged the adipate and terephthalate units, respectively, of PBAT with rigid spiroacetal units. title: Co-benefits of managing saline cropland for the Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Soil salinization can constrain food production and alter nitrogen (N) losses to air and water, with implications for agricultural and environmental sustainability. These processes are linked to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet their implications for SDG-related outcomes remain poorly quantified. Here, we integrate spatially explicit global N budgets, satellite-derived crop canopy responses, and evidence from a meta-analysis of saline soil management practices to assess salinity-associated changes in SDG proxy indicators and the potential benefits of optimized management. title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale The carbon and oxygen stable isotope ratios (δ 13 C and δ 18 O) of carbonate contained in fish tooth dentin have the potential to offer insights into environmental and ecological conditions, making them promising targets for analysis in fossil specimens. abstract: ABSTRACT While solar‐driven photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting offers a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, sluggish interfacial charge transfer and long‐term instability remain critical bottlenecks. title: Heritage spatial connections and spatial patterns of Huizhou traditional villages
abstract: Conservation and utilization for traditional villages have shifted from individual-village to integrated regional planning. However, insufficient understanding of the spatial heritage connections among traditional villages has resulted in ambiguous cluster delineation and unclear spatial patterns, hindering concentrated and contiguous conservation. Thus, in this work, social network analysis was used to systematically investigate the heritage spatial relationships and spatial patterns of Huizhou traditional villages at the overall, meso, and individual levels. title: Mapping Assessment Tools for Nature-Positive Decision-Making
abstract: Background Efforts to support nature-positive decision-making rely on a growing number of assessment tools for Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and Ecosystem Services (ES), yet the available tool landscape remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. Tools differ widely in scope and purpose, and there is limited evidence on how they are recognised and used in practice. abstract: Timely monitoring of wetland changes is vital for effective conservation and management of the landscape. This study, therefore, examines vegetation dynamics and their climatic, hydrological, and land-use drivers in the Foket floodplain wetland, Upper Blue Nile basin, Ethiopia. The LULC analysis was employed based on 1985, 2002, and 2020 cloud-free Landsat images. The maximum likelihood classification algorithm was applied to classify the images into eight LULC classes. abstract: Abstract Dolomite, a calcium magnesium carbonate mineral, can adversely affect soil properties when present in excessive amounts. The India-Bhutan border region of West Bengal has experienced substantial declines in the quality and yield of fresh tea leaves, potentially associated with dolomite influx from the neighbouring lower Himalayas through recurrent flooding and the use of river water for irrigation. title: Same stimuli, disparate roles and nature across six types of theme parks
abstract: This study investigates how the same experiential attributes play different roles in shaping visitor experience evaluations and emotional responses across six theme park types. Based on 1660 questionnaires, a theme park experience scale was developed for cross-type comparison. The findings show that the psychological characteristics of experience dimensions vary across park types in their functional roles and cognitive–affective nature. title: Effect of an Occupational Health and Safety Educational Intervention on Knowledge, Practices, Musculoskeletal Disorders, and Injuries Among Oilseed Processing Workers
abstract: Occupational hazards, injuries, work-related illnesses, and fatalities remain core public health challenges in industrial settings. Workers in oilseed processing factories are exposed to multiple occupational risks; however, evidence regarding the effectiveness of occupational health and safety educational interventions in these settings remains limited and not explored and examined. title: Compensatory abundance dynamics between an omnivore and a herbivore in agricultural landscapes
abstract: Population ecology grew from a question about how competition governs animal abundance, and its classic models center on intraspecific competition, by which a population is regulated toward its own carrying capacity. But abundance also responds to competition between species. Where two species draw on a shared carrying capacity, density compensation can occur, a decline in one offset by an increase in another. abstract: ABSTRACT Wildlife feeding through intentional or unintentional practices can result in increased human‐wildlife conflict, disease transmission, population growth, and altered behavior. We quantified how spatial and temporal variation in black bear ( Ursus americanus ) bait availability within home ranges influenced black bear diet composition as mediated by sex and age. abstract: Abstract Acidophilic microalgae represent a promising but underexplored source of bioactive metabolites with potential biotechnological applications. Herein, we evaluated the influence of pH and irradiance on the growth performance, photophysiology, and metabolite profiles of a strain of the acidophile Chlamydomonas acidophila . abstract: Abstract The 1976 Seveso disaster prompted a major shift in European industrial safety, leading to the Seveso Directives to prevent major chemical accidents. This review outlines the evolution of the Seveso framework, specifically focusing on the transition to the Seveso III Directive. abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is a low utilization of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in India and lack of a nationwide registry or data. This registry aimed to study the systems of care, functional outcomes, and cost effectiveness of MT treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: Patients were treated with Solitaire™ X and/or React™ catheter as the primary device/s. abstract: Unlike jawed vertebrates relying on Ig-based adaptive immunity, jawless vertebrates utilize variable lymphocyte receptors (VLR) for antigen recognition. abstract: This study investigates the influence of friction stir processing (FSP) on the microstructural evolution, corrosion behaviour and electrochemical performance of Mg–2Gd–2Yb alloy shows potential for further evaluation in short-duration cathodic-protection applications. abstract: Structural and kinematic analyses of the eastern Sulaiman Range, based on focal mechanism solutions reveal systematic spatial variations in faulting style. abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrasound‐assisted extraction (UAE) is promising for recovering seaweed bioactives, but confounding amplitude/power, energy input, and treatment time complicates mechanistic interpretation and cross‐study comparison. abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels hold great promise for flexible electronics, electronic skin, and soft robotics, yet simultaneously achieving high strength, toughness, and conductivity remains challenging. abstract: Abstract. Accurate pluvial flood mapping in ungauged agricultural catchments is often constrained by a lack of calibration data. title: Modelación hidrológica e hidráulica del riesgo de inundación en la quebrada San Francisco, Piura, Perú
abstract: En cuencas con escasa información hidrometeorológica, delimitar zonas inundables exige combinar datos alternativos, evidencia de campo y modelación. Se modeló el comportamiento hidrológico, hidráulico y geoespacial de la quebrada del caserío San Francisco (Tambogrande, Piura, Perú) para identificar zonas inundables y estimar el riesgo. Se usaron precipitaciones máximas de 24 h de PISCO-SENAMHI (1981–2016), ajustadas a distribuciones de probabilidad para períodos de retorno (TR) de 140, 200 y 500 años. title: Identifying knowledge gaps in a biodiversity database and their spatial determinants
abstract: Open-access biodiversity databases are valuable resources in the structuring and accessibility of species occurrence data. By compiling different data sources, they reveal the uneven spatial distribution of knowledge, with certain areas and taxonomic groups being better represented. Understanding the determinants of spatial and taxonomic knowledge gaps helps in informing the use of open-access data. title: Paradigms in Practice: Urban Planning Theories and Governance Dualism in Batam
abstract: Batam was conceived as an ambitious state-led spatial experiment to rival regional industrial centers like Singapore through special economic zone policies, technocratic blueprints, and massive infrastructure investments. However, decades of development have placed the city in an ambiguous position, characterized by persistent socio-spatial inequalities and institutional friction. title: Bioremediation of PET-Contaminated Wastewater Using Shrimp Waste Activated Sludge: A Combined In Silico–Experimental Study
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic pollution is a long-standing environmental problem because it is highly resistant to natural degradation. This study investigates a poorly studied low-cost biocatalytic approach for the degradation of PET-derived wastewater using esterase-producing bacteria isolated from activated sludge of shrimp waste. Theoretical binding affinity and degradation performance were evaluated by the dual-approach strategy of molecular docking simulation (MOE software) and laboratory-scale degradation experiments. title: An overview of the state of biodiversity in Spain: developing a National Red List programme
abstract: Abstract The Spain Species Specialist Group of the IUCN Species Survival Commission, established in 2024, comprises c. 150 specialists in 18 taxonomic working groups. Among its aims is the assessment of the status of Spanish species for the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. We review the Master List of Wild Species in Spain (63,981 species) and analyse taxonomic bias and the low number of these species included in the IUCN Red List (2,687 species) and Spanish legislation (935 species in the List of Wild Species under the Special Protection Regime and the Spanish Catalogue of Threatened Spec

title: A framework to assess trajectories of societal and biological extinction
abstract: Threatened species that are societally extinct, which refers to the loss of a species' presence in human societies, are less likely to receive conservation attention, potentially resulting in their biological extinction going unnoticed. However, little is known about the process and forms of such extinction. Thus, we aimed to quantitatively demonstrate the concept of societal extinction. We hypothesized that societal extinction leads to reduced conservation efforts for the affected species, which may, in turn, be associated with their biological extinction. title: Beyond proximity: Green space visitation patterns and physical health outcomes
abstract: Urban green spaces (GS) are increasingly recognized for mitigating health risks linked to urbanization, yet most research emphasizes proximity rather than actual use in Mediterranean cities. This study examines how GS visitation patterns, demographic characteristics, and physical health outcomes interact in Chania, Crete, addressing gaps in GS exposure and chronic disease prevention. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 718 adult residents between June and August 2024. title: Marina Selection Using Weighted Mixed-Variable Axiomatic Design Framework
abstract: Purpose: Marina selection is a complex multi-criteria decision-making problem characterized by heterogeneous data types, inherent uncertainty, and strong dependence on user preferences. Addressing this complexity requires a decision-support framework that can simultaneously accommodate multiple variable representations while preserving theoretical consistency, transparency, and interpretability. title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa modulates Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance
abstract: Abstract This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. The effects of co-culturing with Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ) on Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) virulence and survival under sub-MIC antibiotic exposure were assessed in vitro using 12 bacterial combinations. These combinations were divided into three groups: standard, co-isolated (from the same patient), and random combinations. title: Expression of a Nitric Oxide Synthase Modifies Arginine Metabolism and Accelerates the Response to Nitrogen Deficiency in Cyanobacteria
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is a signal molecule in organisms of all kingdoms of life, acting as a second messenger during stress responses, growth and developmental processes. Nitric oxide synthases (NOS) are enzymes that produce NO by catalyzing the oxidation of L-arginine to citrulline and NO. The Synechococcus PCC 7335 NOS protein (SyNOS), representative of the cyanobacteria phylum, shows remarkable differences from canonical NOS proteins, with an extra globin domain which has NO dioxygenase activity that can remobilize arginine reserves into nitrate and NO. title: Heatwave‐Resilient Cuticular Microbiota Protect the Leaf Beetle Plagiodera versicolora From Fungal Infection
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves-extreme thermal events characterized by prolonged supra-optimal temperatures-exert profound impacts on global ecosystem stability and species interactions. While the disruptive effects of thermal stress on host physiology and gut microbiota are well documented, the role of cuticular microbiota in host defense under heatwaves remains poorly characterized. title: SEASONAL AND LAND USE INTERACTION ON WATER QUALITY IN THE CAMPO ALEGRE STREAM, GOIANO CERRADO: EVIDENCE OF URBAN IMPACT
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Brazilian Cerrado face escalating degradation from agricultural expansion and urban growth. Understanding the synergistic interaction between land use and seasonal hydrological pulses is critical for water resource management. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal dynamics of water quality and potential ecotoxicological risks in the Campo Alegre Stream basin (Santa Helena de Goiás, Brazil). Water samples were collected across three land-use zones - Conservation Unit, Agricultural Area, and Urban Area - during the Rainy Season and Dry Season of 2023. Twenty-six

title: Condition Matters: Fine-Tuning Ecosystem Service Capacity with Ecosystem Condition
abstract: Ecosystem service (ES) capacity matrices are widely used for ES assessment and mapping due to their operational simplicity. However, standard matrices assign uniform capacity scores to ecosystem types without accounting for local variations in ecosystem condition, leading to systematic assessment errors. We present a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem condition into ES capacity matrices through ecosystem-specific condition thresholds. title: Utilização do método GOD para a avaliação da vulnerabilidade à contaminação dos aquíferos da cidade de Maceió, AL
abstract: As águas subterrâneas são um recurso importante para o abastecimento e o desenvolvimento urbano, o que exige a avaliação de sua vulnerabilidade à contaminação. Este estudo avaliou a vulnerabilidade intrínseca dos aquíferos em Maceió–AL pelo método GOD, com dados do Sistema de Informações de Águas Subterrâneas (SIAGAS). Dos 1.173 poços registrados no município, 44 apresentavam as informações necessárias para os parâmetros G (grau de confinamento), O (ocorrência de estratos de cobertura) e D (distância até o lençol freático). title: Economic and financial assessment of the adoption of best management practices in Mediterranean citrus farming
abstract: Aim of study: To assess the financial and economic feasibility of adopting agricultural Best Management Practices (BMPs) in lemon farming, accounting for environmental externalities and comparing them with conventional and organic production systems. Area of study: Region of Murcia (SE Spain). Material and methods: The study applies a financial and economic investment evaluation framework to lemon farming systems. title: Droughts in Africa: Adult Malnutrition and Occupational Change During Recurring and First‐Time Droughts
abstract: ABSTRACT How costly are droughts to adults' nutrition in Africa? Do people adapt to recurring droughts? We measure severe droughts using detailed satellite‐based index of greening observed bi‐monthly on a relatively high‐resolution 0.083° grid between 1982 and 2015, that captures persistent and severe deficits in soil moisture relative to grid‐cell and time‐of‐year normal moisture. title: Divergent Responses of Fungal Communities to Vegetation Structural Complexity in Degraded Roadside Slopes Across Climatic Gradients
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how climate and vegetation structural complexity jointly shape fungal communities is essential for effective roadside slope restoration. To address this, we examined restoration effects on fungal diversity, community composition, and ecological networks across three climatically distinct regions: dry‐hot valley, subalpine, and subtropical. In climatically stressful regions (i.e., dry‐hot valley and subalpine), plots with complex vegetation (Herb+Shrub, Herb+Shrub+Tree, and natural sites) harbored higher fungal diversity than herbaceous‐only plots. title: Assessment of Pump- Based Drinking Water Quality Compliance with World Health Organization Standards in Central Gondar, Ethiopia.
abstract: Access to quality water is critical for public health; however, Ethiopia is grappling with challenges stemming from inadequate infrastructure and limited resources. This study evaluated the quality of drinking water sourced from large and medium-sized pump-based systems in Central Gondar, comparing the findings against WHO water quality standards. Employing an explanatory mixed methods research design, 415 respondents were selected through systematic sampling. title: A cross-cultural assessment of Indigenous fire impacts on a culturally significant species: A case study from the Laynhapuy Indigenous Protected Area, northern Australia
abstract: Contemporary fire management increasingly calls for the inclusion of Indigenous peoples and knowledge systems, recognising that Indigenous burning has shaped landscapes for millennia. Yet research combining Indigenous and Western knowledge systems to evaluate how Indigenous fire regimes support culturally significant fauna remains rare. Working with the Yolŋu Yirralka Rangers in the Laynhapuy Indigenous Protected Area, northeast Arnhem Land, this study used a ‘both-ways’ Before-After-Control-Impact design to understand short-term responses of waṉ'kurra (northern brown bandicoot, Isoodon macrou

title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
abstract: Phase-transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase-transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction-powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. title: Total phenolic content is associated with antioxidant activity independently of preliminary toxicity in medicinal plants from Sinaloa, Mexico: a multivariate approach
abstract: Abstract The medicinal flora of the state of Sinaloa, Mexico, is widely used by rural and highland communities; however, scientific information regarding its phytochemical profile, antioxidant capacity, and toxicological safety remains scarce and fragmentary. The present study evaluated the relationship among the qualitative phytochemical profile, total phenolic content (Folin–Ciocalteu), in vitro antioxidant capacity (DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP), and preliminary toxicity ( Artemia salina lethality assay) of 20 ethanolic extracts obtained from 15 native medicinal species, using an integrative multiv

title: SIKENDALI AMBON: Data Integration, Early Warning, and Supply Chain Control for Transforming Inflation Control in an Archipelagic Region
abstract: Inflation control in archipelagic regions faces distinct challenges: dependence on inter-island supply, weather and shipping risks, and data fragmented across agencies. This article describes the design of SIKENDALI AMBON, a governance change project that integrates price, production, stock, demand, distribution, and logistics data into a logistics balance, an Early Warning System (EWS), and a Decision Support System (DSS) for Ambon City's Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID). title: Age of weaning impacts the growth performance, intestinal morphology and gene expression of the tambaqui Colossoma macropomum larvae
abstract: Abstract Fish larvae feeding management represents one of the critical points for survival and aquaculture success. The larvae of many fish species require live feeds during early development, typically before being transitioned to formulated feeds through a process known as weaning. Despite the importance of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) , to Brazil’s aquaculture industry, the optimal timing for weaning and its effects on larval development remain unclear. title: Genomes of Argia emma (Odonata: Coenagrionidae) and Epeorus albertae (Ephemeroptera: Heptageniidae) as novel resources for evolution, ecology, and conservation research
abstract: Paleopteran insects (Odonata and Ephemeroptera) occupy a crucial position in insect evolution and are ecologically significant indicators of freshwater ecosystem health. Recent improvement in the number of publicly available genomes and transcriptomes have advanced understanding of genome size evolution, morphological innovation, and ecological responses in these orders. title: Material biography and technical utility of 8th-century wooden garden infrastructure: evidence of timber reuse in Unified Silla, Korea
abstract: Waterlogged wooden structures from royal garden contexts provide rare evidence of ancient landscape management and woodworking practices. This study investigates eleven wooden elements excavated from Wolji Pond, a royal garden of the Unified Silla Kingdom (eighth century CE), to evaluate possible timber reuse within aquatic installations. A multi-analytical workflow combining morphological reassessment, digital radiography, wood anatomical analysis, and micro-XRF was applied. title: The Co-Evolutionary Interface: A Socio-Ecological Framework for Integrating Mineral Extraction and Recreational Development
abstract: The transition from mineral extraction to post-mining land use is conventionally structured as a sequential process where recreational functions are introduced after extraction ceases. This temporal separation limits opportunities to incorporate long-term land-use objectives into active mine design and leaves unresolved questions regarding how industrial, ecological, and institutional functions can be coordinated across the mine life cycle. title: Effects of Dietary β‐Glucan on Growth Performance, Haematobiochemical Responses, and Stress‐Related Gene Expression in Stinging Catfish ( Heteropneustes fossilis )
abstract: ABSTRACT The present study evaluated the consequences of dietary β‐glucan on growth, haematobiochemical parameters, and stress‐related gene expression in stinging catfish, Heteropneustes fossilis . A basal diet was supplemented with 0%, 0.05%, 0.1%, and 0.5% yeast β‐glucan and administered to fish at 7%–4% of body weight per day for 100 days. The experiment was conducted in 12 plastic tanks arranged into four treatments in triplicate, with 30 fingerlings stocked in each tank. title: Subsurface temperature profiles across ten Egyptian cities: mapping low-enthalpy geothermal potential for regional energy adaptation
abstract: Abstract We present comprehensive data of daily subsurface temperature profiles for ten Egyptian cities, derived from Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. While ground temperature is a critical parameter for geothermal energy applications and building thermal performance, long-term measured subsurface temperature data across Egypt remains scarce. The presented data fills this gap by utilizing a heat transfer model to simulate annual thermal variations at depths ranging from 0 to -10 meters. title: Targeting Response Regulator PprB Protein With Natural Compounds to Develop Novel Therapies Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: The pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) is recognized as an international pathogen of significance due to its multidrug resistance and strong ability to create biofilm as the basis of chronic and device-associated infections. The two-component regulatory system PprAB is important in the biofilm network, where the response regulator PprB regulates binding, aggregation, and biofilm production in the extracellular environment. institutions: DY Patil Deemed to be University

title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. title: Experimental study on performance and durability of Guangzhou soft soil solidified by a new slag-fly ash based cementitious material
abstract: The development of sustainable alternatives to Portland cement for soft soil stabilization is of great significance for reducing carbon emissions and enhancing infrastructure longevity. This study investigates a one-part slag-fly ash geopolymer binder containing solid sodium silicate for stabilizing Guangzhou soft clay. The optimal mix proportion was a slag-to-fly ash ratio of 90:10, a solid activator dosage of 14% relative to the precursor mass, and a water-to-binder ratio of 0.6, achieving a 28-day compressive strength of 2.01 MPa, 14.9% higher than the pure slag system. institutions: Guangzhou Urban Planning Survey & Design Institute

title: Real-time quantification of fluid flows around bubbles during directional solidification
abstract: Directional solidification of bubbly liquids plays a critical role in shaping the microstructure and properties of many materials, yet the fluid dynamics governing bubble behavior during solidification remain poorly understood. Using cryo-confocal microscopy and particle image velocimetry, we quantify fluid flows around bubbles during solidification of water containing surfactants and tracers. title: Spatial Patterns and Driving Mechanisms of Coupling Coordination Between Urban Expansion and Urban Resilience: Evidence From Multi‐Source Geospatial Data
abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid acceleration of urbanization, understanding the coordination between urban expansion (UE) and urban resilience (UR) has become critical for achieving sustainable urban development. However, the spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of the coupling coordination between UE and UR remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a multi‐source geospatial analysis framework by integrating remote sensing data and socioeconomic statistics to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, spatial correlation, and influencing factors of UE‐UR coupling coordination in Shandong

title: A double diamond model-based design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds
abstract: This study aims to improve patient experience and healthcare professionals' operational efficiency during patient transfer by proposing an integrated design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds within the Double Diamond framework.First, initial user requirements were identified through User Journey Map (UJM) analysis and multi-stakeholder interviews to explore key challenges and potential design needs during the medical transfer process. title: Protocol for integrated phosphoproteomic and proteomic analysis of the mouse ventral tegmental area with functional and kinase motif enrichment
abstract: We present a protocol for label-free proteomic and phosphoproteomic analysis of the mouse ventral tegmental area (VTA). We describe steps for combining region-specific biopsy-punch collection, parallel proteomic and phosphoproteomic processing, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and downstream enrichment analysis. We detail procedures for SynGO-based synaptic localization, g:Profiler/DAVID pathway enrichment, and iceLogo/pLogo motif analysis. title: Enhancing urban water resilience through green infrastructure in Kathmandu, Nepal
abstract: Rapidly growing cities in developing countries, including Kathmandu, Nepal, are struggling to handle water issues driven by both urban growth and climate change. Conventional grey infrastructure is unable to address the rising problems of flooding, polluted water, and declining groundwater recharge. This work evaluates how Green Infrastructure (GI) might help make Kathmandu Valley more sustainable and enhance ecosystem resilience through better water management. title: Legacy effects of selective coppicing on forest regeneration in Bronze Age Italy
abstract: Unambiguous evidence of sophisticated woodland and land-use management in Bronze Age southern Europe is presented from the Terramare culture in northern Italy. Archaeological layers dated to ~3,600 years ago reveal a society whose economy was structurally dependent on wood, used as both building material and fuel, defining what we term here a 'Wood Age' culture. title: Effect of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on growth, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome in a hybrid fish ( Megalobrama amblycephala ♀ × Culter alburnus ♂)
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of dietary supplementation with Clostridium butyricum on the growth performance, intestinal microbiota, metabolome and transcriptome of a hybrid fish ( Megalobrama amblycephala ♀ × Culter alburnus♂ ). Experimental fish were diet supplemented with C . butyricum at 0 (control group [CG]), 4.02 × 10 8 (L), 1.66 × 10 9 CFU/kg (T), respectively, for 8 weeks feeding. title: Valorization of agar extraction residues from the red algae Gelidium sesquipedale as biosorbents for organic and inorganic pollutants
abstract: Abstract The aim of this research is to study the adsorption capacity of methylene blue and methyl orange by Gelidium sesquipedale (GS), Gelidium sesquipedale residues (GSR) and an equal mixture of algae residues and diatomaceous earth (GRD). To this end, we have carried out a physico-chemical and structural characterization of the three samples (GS, GSR and GRD). Gelidium sesquipedale and its residues are rich in lignin (33.22% and 28.60%, respectively) and cellulose (20.29% and 13.31%, respectively). title: Governance-mediated value in sustainable trail tourism: shared responsibility, legitimacy, and stewardship in a nonprofit network
abstract: Long-distance walking trails support sustainable rural tourism, generating economic, environmental, and social value for host communities. Their viability often depends on governance arrangements involving public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and local tourism businesses that collectively manage environmental resources and visitor infrastructure. Although value co-creation is widely studied in tourism, less attention is given to how value is negotiated within stewardship networks supporting public tourism assets. title: Dietary γ-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA) Improves Growth Performance and Increases Plasma Cortisol During Recovery from Short-Term Acute Thermal Exposure in Juvenile Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
abstract: γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is a functional feed additive that may improve growth and stress resilience. The study evaluated the effects of dietary GABA on growth performance and recovery-phase physiological responses after short-term acute thermal exposure in juvenile rainbow trout. Two hundred twenty-five fish (18.9 ± 0.1 g) were fed five diets for 8 weeks: a control diet containing 68 mg/kg (GABA68) and diets with 108 (GABA108), 149 (GABA149), 183 (GABA183), and 218 (GABA218) mg/kg GABA. title: Deciphering the construction of the ancient city of Palenque and its effects on the landscape
abstract: The ancient city of Palenque, in the Mayan territory, was established in a strategic position between the piedmont of the Sierra de Chiapas and the alluvial plain of the Michol River. The city became prominent during the Classic period (250–900 AD), when landscape modifications were carried out at different scales and with varying degrees of intensity during its construction. In this work, we present a combined study of natural and urban soils together with technogenic materials and geomorphological analysis based on LiDAR survey. title: Ultrashort pulse laser cutting of NiTi in liquids and with pulse bursts
abstract: Shape memory alloys, particularly nickel-titanium, are widely used in medical technology for stent fabrication. Laser cutting of NiTi stents requires minimizing heat input and surface contamination to preserve the superelastic material properties and reduce post-processing effort. Ultrashort pulsed laser processing is well suited for this purpose, although a heat-affected zone remains. This study investigates ultrashort pulse laser cutting of NiTi foils in a liquid environment using a custom flow chamber.
