title: Hierarchical Reaction‐Induced Phase Separation in Epoxy/Oligomeric Poly(phenylene ether) Blends: Multiscale Structural and Mechanical Heterogeneity
abstract: ABSTRACT Epoxy/thermoplastic blends often undergo reaction‐induced phase separation (RIPS) during curing, and introducing a deformable thermoplastic component is generally expected to improve the deformation tolerance of brittle epoxy networks. In this study, hydroxyl‐terminated oligomeric poly(phenylene ether) (oPPE) was introduced into an epoxy/amine system to clarify how an initially optically homogeneous formulation evolves into a hierarchically phase‐separated network and how the resulting oPPE‐rich morphology affects tensile ductility. title: Selective feeding and niche differentiation in adult boreal Odonata revealed by DNA metabarcoding
abstract: Abstract Diet choice plays a key role in shaping species interactions, trophic dynamics and ecosystem function, yet the extent to which insect meso‐predators exhibit dietary specialisation and prey selection remains poorly understood. Understanding how meso‐predators partition resources and respond to prey availability is therefore important for interpreting food web structure and ecosystem dynamics. title: Discovery and validation of a SNP panel to identify hybridization and introgression among three trout species
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic introductions of non-native trout for recreation has had widespread effects on native ecosystems and their inhabitants. The Lahontan Cutthroat Trout (LCT; Oncorhynchus henshawi ) is native to western North America and is simultaneously experiencing population declines and hybridization due to climate change and non-native trout introductions, respectively. title: Overtourism, Consumer Protection, and Destination Authenticity: A Comparative Legal Analysis of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand
abstract: Despite its role in local economic empowerment and broader economic growth in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, tourism activities can also present negative impacts for a tourism destination and tourists as consumers, particularly when the activities threaten the authenticity of the said destination. This phenomenon, often referred to as overtourism, raises legal issues regarding whether existing consumer-protection duties and remedies address losses from changed destination conditions. title: Enzyme-Guided Classification of Fungal Eremophilane Biosynthetic Gene Clusters Provides a Predictive Framework for Structural Diversity
abstract: Abstract Elucidating how oxidative tailoring enzymes generate structural diversity in natural products remains a major challenge, because their functions are difficult to predict directly from sequence information. Fungal eremophilanes (EMPs), which share a conserved bicyclic core yet exhibit extensive oxidative diversification, provide an ideal model system to address this problem. title: Challenges of soil arthropod community assessments: Large site-related variation and hidden species-level diversity
abstract: Arthropods are essential for maintaining soil ecosystem functioning. However, their full diversity remains insufficiently explored due to their taxonomic complexity, the limitations of traditional methods such as morphotaxonomy, and constraints associated with DNA barcoding approaches. In this study, we applied COI-based DNA metabarcoding to survey soil arthropod richness and community composition at a single timepoint across 28 long-term monitoring sites in Switzerland representing three land-use types, i.e., arable land, permanent grassland, and forest. abstract: Research Highlight: Geng, Y., Mammides, C., He, R.-C., Wang, L., Luo, K., Zhang, Z.-Y., Wang, B., & Quan, R.-C. (2026). Human hunters are no substitute for vanishing apex predators. title: Flexible composite steel-FRP strips as shear reinforcement of RC beams
abstract: : Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) stirrups are limited by reduced strength at bent regions and, for thermosetting systems, by the need to define stirrup geometry before curing. This study introduces a flexible composite steel–FRP strip comprising a 20-mm-wide, 1-mm-thick flat steel core cold-formed into stirrup geometry and hybridized with longitudinal CFRP, GFRP, or BFRP sheets. title: The cervical microbiome in hispanic populations in Texas and Puerto Rico with and without cervical dysplasia
abstract: Abstract Within the United States, Hispanic women, especially those in Puerto Rico, face an increased risk of cervical cancer development. The objective of this study was to explore the cervical microbiota of Hispanic women at high risk of developing HPV-induced cervical dysplasia or with cervical dysplasia treated in Texas and Puerto Rico. abstract: Este trabajo describe un modelo analítico pensado para analizar el éxito operativo de algoritmos en procesadores de escala intermedia ruidosa (NISQ) mediante un enfoque probabilístico. abstract: Abstract. Hydrometeorological events have a significant impact on road infrastructure and traffic flow. abstract: Abstract. Anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide and reactive nitrogen in various forms disrupt the functioning of ecosystems around the world. In Europe, many valuable habitats, particularly wetlands and semi-natural dry grasslands, are under threat from ongoing eutrophication. However, due to contrasting water regimes, the uptake of anthropogenic nitrogen by plants in these ecosystems is different and is also interrelated with an increase in trophic level in both habitats. title: Polyketides from a soil -derived Streptomyces sp. CSDX076 and their antimicrobial activities
abstract: A new naturally occurring polyketide, pseurotin A 3 -10,11-acetonide (1), along with two known analogs, pseurotin A (2) and pseurotin A 3 (3), was isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp. CSDX076. The structures of these compounds were determined by extensive 1D and 2D nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), ultraviolet (UV), and high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HRESIMS) spectroscopic analyses. title: Reporting the Fleet: News Writing of British Naval Reviews and the Construction of Imperial Identity Frameworks, 1773–1914
abstract: Framing Analysis theory posits that news writing functions as an ideological practice, jointly steered by power structures and media institutions within specific historical contexts, which systematically shapes collective cognition and directs identity formation. From 1773 to 1914, the news writing of British naval reviews constituted a pivotal site for the dynamic construction of imperial identity ideology. title: Innovaciones didácticas y científicas en la Geografía de los libros de texto de la Educación Secundaria Obligatoria de España: competencias (geo)digitales, Educación para la Sostenibilidad y pensamiento crítico
abstract: Los cambios en los manuales de Geografía e Historia de la Educación Secundaria Obligatoria (ESO) tras la reforma educativa de 2020 exigen un análisis por su relevancia como herramienta en la docencia y la materialización práctica del currículo. title: Does the Conversion of Biogenic Organic Nitrates to Nitric Acid Control the Lifetime of Atmospheric Nitrogen Oxides Over the Eastern U.S.?
abstract: Abstract Airborne measurements over the Southeast US during the summer of 2013 revealed the evolution of nitrogen oxides and nitric acid that was markedly different from that over the Northeast US during the winter of 2015. We can reconcile the observed trends by invoking nitrogen oxide reservoir species formed under elevated NO x environments that then convert to HNO 3 . This process may represent a daytime loss pathway of NO x that is faster by many factors than the oxidation of nitrogen dioxide by hydroxyl radicals. title: Centrifuge investigation of pile base effect on the lateral load capacity for large diameter rigid piles embedded in sand
abstract: Large-diameter drilled shafts show rotational-behavior under lateral loads inducing pressure on pile base, which may affect the lateral load capacity. This study examines the effect of pile base pressure (p base ) to the lateral load capacity of large-diameter drilled shafts in sand. A series of centrifuge tests were conducted on model piles with varying slenderness ratios (L/D) and soil conditions, where p base was directly measured. title: Polyamide 6 Conformation and Swelling Transitions in Formic Acid, Dichloromethane, Chloroform, 1,2‐Dichloroethane, and Water Using All Atom Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports the dissolution and inter and intra‐molecular structural properties of Polyamide 6 (PA6) in formic acid (FA), dichloromethane (DCM), chloroform, 1,2‐dichloroethane (1,2‐DCE), and water. The backbone torsional angle probability shows a significant gauche state in water, chloroform, and 1,2‐DCE, indicating poor solvent behavior. title: Direct α ‐C(sp 3 )─H Alkylation and Arylation of Ethers Enabled by Carbon Nitride/Nickel Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: The direct functionalization of α ‐C(sp 3 )─H bonds offers a powerful strategy for converting abundant feedstocks and complex molecules into value‐added products, yet sustainable catalytic platforms that avoid precious‐metal photocatalysts remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a metallaphotoredox system that combines recyclable carbon nitride nanosheets with nickel catalysis for the direct α ‐C(sp 3 )─H cross‐coupling of ethers, amides, and benzylic substrates under visible light. title: Integrative analysis of climate change drivers using ISM DEMATEL approach for structural decision making
abstract: This study aims to explore and structure the complex interplay of key climate change drivers using an integrated Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) approach. By focusing on 14 variables identified through expert consensus, the study seeks to uncover the hierarchical structure and causal relationships influencing climate change, particularly within the context of developing countries such as Indonesia. title: PCOMMUNITY EDUCATION ON GREEN BELT STRUCTURING AND PARTICIPATORY ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY MONITORING AROUND COAL-FIRED POWER PLANT X
abstract: Coal-fired power plants secure baseload electricity but expose neighbouring settlements to fly ash, stockpile dust, flue gases (SO2, NOx) and noise, while residents are usually treated as passive recipients of these impacts and have no means of checking air quality themselves. This participatory action research designed, implemented and evaluated an education programme on multi-strata green belt structuring and citizen-science environmental monitoring for communities around Coal-Fired Power Plant X. title: Risk Analysis of CD-BIM Integration in Structural Jetty Schematic Design: Time Performance
abstract: The early design stage of jetty infrastructure is crucial for setting the project's budget and time. However, current digital processes often do not fully integrate these tasks. Computational design and Building Information Modeling (BIM) have sped up design cycles through faster iterations and improved coordination. Still, they have also increased the likelihood of mistakes, extra work, and project delays. title: Vertical distribution of magnetic susceptibility in permeable sandy soils
abstract: Magnetic susceptibility represents very useful proxy tool to assess the content of ferrimagnetic forms of iron oxides in soils. However, magnetic susceptibility of highly-permeable, sandy soils is very rarely described. The aim of this study is to report on measurements of magnetic susceptibility on the surface and along shallow vertical profiles of sandy soils distinguished in the Polish classification system as rusty soils, ochrous (ochre) soils and Podzols. title: Spatial metabolic insights of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm treatments using stable isotope labeling with DESI mass spectrometry imaging
abstract: Bacteria form biofilms on diverse substrates, and these communities can cause persistent infections owing to their elevated antibiotic resistance. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of chronic infections because of its ability to form biofilms, which makes it difficult to eradicate with conventional antibiotics. The metabolic response of P. aeruginosa biofilms to antibiotic treatment, however, remains only partially understood. title: Honeycomb monolith-based multichannel reactor for methane bioconversion into ectoine
abstract: A novel gas-liquid multichannel bioreactor based on cordierite honeycomb monoliths was engineered and operated under internal gas and liquid recirculation for methane bioconversion into ectoine. The assessment of the volumetric gas-liquid mass transfer coefficients for O 2 ( k L a O 2 ) in this novel bioreactor showed values up to 1472.7 ± 111.6 h −1 , representing an increase of one order of magnitude over conventional bubble column reactors. title: Recorded storm damage and mortgage servicing complaints in US counties
abstract: Storms push households into contact with mortgage servicers over missed payments, forbearance and insurance. We ask where that contact becomes formal complaints. We assign 228,803 of 280,348 mortgage complaints filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau from 2015 to 2024 to counties and compare 898 isolated county exposures to NOAA tropical-storm and hurricane reports in 18 storm months with unexposed counties. title: The densified city and the powerline right-of-way encroachment in Nigeria: Greening as an important intervention.
abstract: Urban densification is generally promoted as a strategy for sustainable development. However, it may also produce unintended consequences, such as exposure to environmental hazards. This study examines potential electrical hazard exposure in relation to the powerline right-of-way (ROW) encroachment in Port Harcourt Metropolis, a rapidly densifying oil and gas industry hub in southern Nigeria, using a mixed-method approach that combines geospatial datasets and social survey data. title: Reframing Stakeholder Roles in Multistakeholder Partnerships: A Role Theory Approach to Collaborative Action on Food Waste
abstract: ABSTRACT Multistakeholder partnerships (MSPs) are promoted as collaborative arrangements to address food waste, yet most research focuses on core stakeholders directly involved in food production and consumption, leaving the roles of supporting stakeholders underexplored. This study redirects attention to these vital actors, such as governmental bodies, financial institutions, and industry associations, whose engagement can be important to initiating, stabilizing, and sustaining collaboration. abstract: Abstract A library of 1H-pyrrolo[3,2-c]quinolines (PQs) was synthesized, and SAR analysis identified compounds with low-nanomolar potency in CCRF-CEM cells (IC50 = 13−18 nM) and selectivity indices > 1000-fold over BJ fibroblasts. title: Genetic structure and demographic decline in the endangered short-tailed chinchilla (Chinchilla chinchilla) of the Atacama Region
abstract: The short-tailed chinchilla ( Chinchilla chinchilla ) was historically subjected to intense exploitation for the fur trade and currently faces multiple threats, yet knowledge of its genetic structure and demographic history remains limited. Here, we analysed genetic variation in populations from the Atacama Region (Chile) using single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) and microsatellite markers. abstract: Abstract Boron (B) deficiency severely limits tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) productivity and fruit quality, particularly in alkaline or low-organic-matter soils, while conventional foliar boron fertilizers suffer from low uptake efficiency and environmental losses. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel nanoboron (NB) formulation and evaluated its efficacy compared with boric acid using physicochemical characterization, molecular simulations, greenhouse studies, metabolomics, and field validation. abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi bisnis yang diterapkan oleh PT Permodalan Nasional Madani (PNM) Unit Layanan Modal Mikro (ULaMM) Kedaton dalam membangun keunggulan bersaing yang berkelanjutan di tengah ekosistem Holding Ultra Mikro yang terdiri dari PNM, BRI, dan Pegadaian. title: A Basic Matrix Protein Songin Selectively Promotes Aragonite Aggregation and Modulates Calcium Carbonate Crystallization in Hyriopsis cumingii
abstract: Abstract In China, the pearl industry of Hyriopsis cumingii contributes approximately 80% of pearl production. Matrix proteins play crucial roles in shell and pearl biomineralization. However, the functions of basic matrix proteins in H. cumingii remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a novel predicted secreted basic matrix protein, designated Songin, from the freshwater pearl mussel H. cumingii. abstract: This study established a dual-strategy framework for heavy metal mitigation in date palm products by integrating physicochemical washing of whole Zahidi fruit with biosorption by inactivated Lactobacillus biomass in date syrup. A sequential baseline-creation design helped distinguish measured solid-phase metal changes from potential true removal. Phase 1 evaluated tap water washing, chemical soaking (citric acid, deionized water, NaHCO₃), and ultrasonication on Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺, and As partitioning, alongside semi-trained sensory evaluation. title: Multiscale bamboo reconstruction enables adsorption-coupled solar evaporation for contaminated water treatment
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation efficiently separates water from nonvolatile contaminants but provides limited control over pollutants retained at the evaporation interface. Here, we report a bamboo-derived adsorption-coupled solar evaporator (ASE) created by multiscale reconstruction of bamboo. title: A Low-Cost IoT Smart Pill Box with Physical Intake Verification: Design and Evaluation in Real-Life Use
abstract: Medication non-adherence undermines the treatment of chronic diseases, and reminder applications cannot show whether a dose was taken. This paper reports a 52-day field evaluation of a low-cost smart pill box that registers each intake event with an infrared sensor and a reed switch, time-stamps it with a battery-backed clock, queues events locally during network outages and forwards them to a Laravel server that alerts the patient, a caregiver and a physician by staged e-mails. title: Integrated Topological, Physical, and Functional Vulnerability of Road Networks to Compound Seismic-Landslide Hazards in the East African Rift
abstract: Abstract Road networks in tectonically active regions face compound seismic and landslide hazards that can simultaneously disrupt multiple links. However, existing vulnerability assessments typically examine physical, topological, and functional dimensions in isolation and address only single hazard types. title: Experimental investigation of suction flow enhancement in submerged jet pumps via perforated mixing chamber
abstract: Liquid–liquid jet pumps are essential in dredging, slurry transport, and submerged mixing applications, yet their suction performance remains constrained by the limited entrainment area in conventional solid-walled mixing chambers. This study experimentally investigates the geometric modification of using perforated mixing chambers that enable distributed radial suction driven by the hydrostatic pressure differential between the surrounding fluid and the low-pressure core induced by the motive jet. abstract: Global seismographic networks (GSNs) capture fine details of ground motion signals, assisting scientists and governments in detecting and characterizing earthquakes and other seismic events worldwide. Continued improvements in these networks enhance knowledge about Earth structure, atmospheric interaction, and geological hazards. abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade-off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor-acceptor (D-A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge-transfer efficiency-with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. abstract: Nick Joaquin (1917–2004) is a Filipino literary master and national artist whose numerous works include the prize-winning novel The Woman Who Had Two Navels (1961). abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving a simultaneous enhancement of permeability and selectivity remains a central challenge in nanofiltration membrane design. title: Hormonal and metabolic adaptations in Omega-3-supplemented rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) supplementation on endocrine and metabolic profiles of forty-five nulliparous rabbit does during their first reproductive cycle. Animals were randomly assigned to one of three diets: control (CNT), 5% extruded linseed (L), and 5% extruded linseed plus 0.2% Padina pavonica extract (LPP). title: Cosmogenic Selection: How Retained Organization Shapes Future Possibilities
abstract: Cosmogenic Selection (CGS) is proposed as a conceptual framework for examining how organized reality develops across physical, biological and cognitive domains. Its central proposition is that what persists changes what can happen next: differences enter relationships, some consequences are retained, and retained organization reshapes or expands subsequent possibilities. title: Type VI secretion drives reciprocal growth inhibition among symbiotic Vibrio fischeri strains
abstract: Bacterial cells are often in direct contact with one another and compete for nutrients and space. The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a contact-dependent mechanism that enables bacteria to deliver toxic effectors into neighbouring cells. Vibrio fischeri is a bacterial symbiont of the Hawaiian bobtail squid Euprymna scolopes and encodes a T6SS on its second chromosome (T6SS2) that promotes interference competition among strains within the squid light organ. abstract: Understanding species distributions is essential for biogeographical and ecological studies. This study reports the geographical ranges of two large-size octannulate species of the leech genus Orobdella Oka, 1895, O. octonaria Oka, 1895, and O. nakahamai Nakano, 2016, based on newly collected specimens. abstract: ABSTRACT Bio‐based aerogels are a compelling class of sustainable materials, with some of them distinguished by their exceptional thermal superinsulating performance, i.e. conductivity lower than that of air. title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of reservoir storage in the Algarve region (Southern Portugal): implications for regional water security
abstract: ABSTRACT The Algarve region in southern Portugal relies heavily on reservoirs to support domestic water supply, irrigation, tourism, and other economic activities. This study examined the spatio-temporal dynamics of storage in six major reservoirs: Bravura, Arade, Funcho, Odelouca, Odeleite, and Beliche, using monthly and annual storage data from 2012 to 2025. title: Cellulose acetate nanoparticles: impacts of concentration and exposure time on the biochemistry and hematology of juvenile Colossoma macropomum
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the physiological impacts of acute-exposure of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) to different concentrations of cellulose acetate nanoparticles at different sampling times. title: Phytochemical Profiling and Anticancer Potential of Ipomoea hederifolia L. Root Extract: LC–MS Characterization and Molecular Docking Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer remains a major global health burden, with millions of new cases reported annually. Plant‐based products are gaining popularity due to their remarkable biological activity and fewer side effects. The Convolvulaceae family exhibits promising anticancer effects; Ipomoea hederifolia is one of the species rich in bioactive secondary metabolites. title: Integrating Spirulina cultivation as a bioregeneration step in a closed loop CO2 absorption process: Experimental validation
abstract: The integration of microalgal cultivation with CO₂ capture via chemical scrubbing can improve carbon utilization efficiency while reducing operational costs. However, the reciprocal effects between absorption and cultivation units need further investigation. This study evaluated the integration of carbonate-based CO₂ capture with cultivation of the alkaliphilic cyanobacterium Spirulina sp. in a Bicarbonate-based Carbon Capture and Algae Production System (BICCAPS). title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. abstract: Abstract Milk thistle ( Silybum marianum (L.) Gaertn.) is an important medicinal plant, yet limited research has addressed its agronomic performance and genetic diversity under water‐limited conditions. This study evaluated the potential of 28 Iranian ecotypes and one foreign accession to assess variation in agronomic traits, oil concentration, and methanol extractable dry matter under normal irrigation and drought stress during two growing seasons. title: STRENGTHENING LOCAL ECONOMIES THROUGH ECOTOURISM: EVIDENCE FROM BINTANG DISTRICT CENTRAL ACEH PROVINCE, INDONESIA
abstract: This study investigates the role of ecotourism in strengthening local economies in Bintang District, Central Aceh by identifying key potentials within natural and socio-cultural resources. It explores how assets such as Lake Laut Tawar, agrobased livelihoods, and community enterprises can drive sustainable economic development. abstract: Introduction Climate change, rapid urbanization, and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) pose intersecting threats to public health in low- and middle-income countries. While evidence supports integrating health into climate policy, limited attention has been paid to how climate change and urban resilience policies address key NCD-related pathways, particularly diet and physical activity. title: Air quality and noise exposures near an urban freight railyard in Canada
abstract: Growing demand for freight rail alongside trends in residential land use can lead to increased railyard activity near populations. Railyard locomotive and train movements generate air and noise pollution associated with adverse health effects. We sampled gaseous and particulate pollutants and measured sound levels over 15 months in a Toronto (Ontario, Canada) residential neighbourhood surrounding an active freight marshalling railyard. Analyses showed that both air pollutant concentrations and noise levels were higher in the railyard neighbourhood compared to non-railyard-influenced urban loca
journal: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment

title: Impact of the 1 April 2026 Artemis II Rocket Launch on the Upper Atmosphere: TIMED/GUVI Observations
abstract: Abstract The NASA Artemis II rocket was successfully launched at 06:35 p.m. ET (22:35 UTC) on 1 April 2026 from the Kennedy Space Center (28°35′28″N 80°39′03″W). The rocket plume caused enhanced Lyman α emission (up to ∼3 kR) observed by TIMED/GUVI on 2–6 April (5 days). Its peak intensity decreased linearly from April 3 at a rate ∼740 R/day. The half‐maximum width of the zonal Lyman α intensities at 20°–30° latitude (at ∼01:30 p.m. local solar time) increased from ∼3,000 km on April 2–∼9,000 km on April 6. institutions: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

title: Urinary kisspeptin as a non-invasive reproductive biomarker in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does
abstract: Kisspeptin is an upstream regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and plays a critical role in the estrous cycle and pregnancy in domestic animals. The KISS1 gene, also known as the "metastatin" gene, has emerged as a promising diagnostic biomarker in reproductive physiology across livestock species. This study aims to explore the dynamics of urinary/plasma kisspeptin and their creatinine-normalized ratio during the bovine and caprine estrous cycle and pregnancy. Experimental animals comprised two groups (cyclic and pregnant). The cyclic group consisted of 12 cyclic crossbred cows
institutions: National Institute of Animal Nutrition and Physiology

title: Enzymatic Transformation of Soluble Nonreactive Phosphorus Compounds to Improve Phosphorus Removal and Recovery Potential from Wastewater
abstract: Abstract A substantial fraction of total phosphorus (TP) in the environment exists as soluble nonreactive phosphorus (sNRP). These compounds can resist treatment processes and therefore persist in wastewater effluent, posing challenges for meeting stringent TP limits and long-term eutrophication risks. We employed an integrated experimental and chemoinformatics approach to evaluate the chemical diversity of sNRP and its impact on the fate of sNRP during enzymatic treatment. Transformation of selected sNRP compounds was evaluated using E. coli alkaline phosphatase (ALP). The tested compounds th

title: A Self‐Cleaning Solar Evaporator Based on MXene/Aramid Nanofiber Aerogels for Efficient Water Desalination
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its high energy conversion efficiency and broad accessibility to solar energy, interfacial solar steam generation presents a promising, and cost‐effective solution for desalination of saline water. However, salt accumulation on evaporator surfaces remains a major challenge, especially in the case of high‐salinity environments as the blockage it creates significantly hinders the efficiency as well as continuity of the evaporation process. Salt accumulation also significantly degrades the evaporator's surface over time, reducing its performance and efficiency. Researchers have ex

title: Traceable Privacy and Cybersecurity Compliance Control Baseline for Indonesian Academic Information Systems
abstract: Academic information systems process student identities, academic records, library transactions, authentication logs, learning analytics, and third-party service integrations. In Indonesia, privacy and cybersecurity compliance is difficult to operationalize because legal obligations are often separated from system risks, IT governance controls, ownership, and audit evidence. This study develops a traceable privacy and cybersecurity compliance control baseline for Indonesian academic information systems. The method applies structured literature-based conceptual synthesis and design science-insp

title: Geographical Expansion and Native Species Displacement: The Invasion of Cecropia peltata L. (Urticaceae) in Cameroon
abstract: ABSTRACT Plant invasions pose a global ecological concern, yet their study in continental tropical Africa is limited. Cecropia (Urticaceae) is a genus of fast‐growing Neotropical tree species, some of which have been introduced and become invasive in the paleotropics. In this study, we examined the invasion process of the C. peltata introduction in Cameroon, focusing on its geographical distribution, temporal dynamics, and potential impacts on the closely related native species Musanga cecropioides . After surveying 837 km of roads in 2018, we found that C. peltata was widely distributed acros

title: Molecular and Microbial Evidence for Plastic‐Film Transformation in Pig‐Urine‐Derived Media: Distinguishing Aging, Depolymerization, and Biodegradation
abstract: ABSTRACT Pig urine is a chemically active, microbially populated waste stream containing urea, ammoniacal species, salts, minerals, and dissolved organics. This study experimentally evaluates transformations of low‐density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), and commercial poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT)/poly(lactic acid) (PLA)‐based film in controlled pig‐urine‐derived media separating hydration, abiotic chemistry, native biological exposure, nonviable‐biomass effects, and enriched biological activity. title: Effects of a three-year maize-soybean rotation on soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing Fusarium spp. inoculum potential
abstract: Maize-soybean succession dominates grain production in tropical Brazil, and rotation is often recommended to improve soil health. However, few field studies have followed both soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing pathogens over several seasons in tropical no-till systems. We compared continuous maize, continuous soybean and maize-soybean rotation for three seasons (2016-2017 to 2018-2019). In a fourth season (2019-2020), maize was grown in all plots to test legacy effects. Bacterial communities were profiled by 16 S rRNA (V3-V4) amplicon sequencing. The fum1 gene of fumonisin-produ
journal: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology

title: Quantifying urban heat: A spatiotemporal study of climate change and population growth in Ikorodu, Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: Climate change and rapid urban growth are increasingly altering local climatic conditions in cities across the Global South.One important manifestation is the urban heat island (UHI) effect, whereby built-up urban areas experience higher temperatures than surrounding less-developed areas.This study examines the relationship between climate change, urban growth, and rising temperatures in Ikorodu, a rapidly expanding peri-urban area of Lagos State, Nigeria.Using simulated but realistic datasets derived from Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) records, Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Chang
journal: African Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
institutions: Lagos State University of Science and Technology

title: Climate variability and change as an emerging operational challenge to malaria control among district malaria focal persons in Dar es Salaam Tanzania
abstract: Malaria transmission in Tanzania has declined significantly over the past decade, following the scale-up of vector control and case management interventions. However, climate change may threaten these gains through long-term changes in climatic conditions that could influence mosquito breeding patterns and transmission dynamics. Short-term and seasonal fluctuations in rainfall and temperature, may also influence malaria risk and disrupt vector control activities, particularly during heavy rainfall. District malaria focal persons are responsible for implementing and coordinating malaria control
institutions: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences
Mbeya University of Science and Technology

title: Assessing the impacts of projected climate scenarios on irrigation reliability and reservoir sustainability in Sri Lanka’s dry zone
abstract: Abstract Climate change poses major challenges for irrigation water management in Sri Lanka’s dry zone. This study assesses the performance of the Nachchaduwa reservoir under historical and projected climate scenarios using multiple General Circulation Models (GCMs). Eight GCMs were ranked through compromise programming, with the top three models bias-corrected and downscaled to generate climate projections for the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) scenarios: SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, under near-future (2015–2050) and mid-future (2051–2075) conditions. The ensemble GCM data used for HEC-HMS to

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE s

title: New insights on Suretta nappe structure and lithostratigraphy revealed by high-resolution geological survey of Val di Lei (Central Alps, Italy)
abstract: This contribution presents a 1:10.000 scale geological map of the Val di Lei basin (Italian Central Alps), produced within the framework of the Italian National Geological Mapping Project (CARG). The area mainly exposes rocks of the Suretta nappe (Middle Penninic) and minor portions of the Avers nappe (Upper Penninic). The Suretta nappe comprises a polymetamorphic basement, Carboniferous–Permian metaplutonites, and a Permian–Mesozoic metasedimentary cover. The structural framework reflects a polyphase Alpine deformation superimposed on relict pre-Alpine features. New field data refine the lith

title: Determinants of Enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by Product Type: Focus on Fixed-Effects Models
abstract: This study analyzed the effects of paid claims, government subsidy rates, and disaster relief grants, among other factors, on enrollment in Storm, Flood, and Earthquake Insurance by product type. The study employed a fixed-effects model and proposed policy improvements to analyze panel data constructed from the insurance records of 229 local governments from 2013 to 2025. The analysis showed that the previous year's paid claims and government subsidy rates had significant positive associations with driving enrollment; however, the specific operational mechanisms exhibited heterogeneous pattern
institutions: Ministry of the Interior and Safety

title: Charting the Course: Practical Steps for Philippine HEIs to Embark on Internationalization
abstract: In response to a global imperative and local legislative mandates like the Transnational Higher Education Act (RA 11448), this paper provides a practical seven-step roadmap for Philippine Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) to systematically initiate and strengthen their internationalization efforts. By integrating UNESCO’s regional student mobility data with a case study of Panpacific University and comparative insights from University of Santo Tomas (UST) and Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU), this study proposes a Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) -based framework of seven strategic actions th

title: Signals to remember: investigating the retrieval function of colors
abstract: Abstract Learners often rely on visual cues, such as color highlights, to recall important information in instructional texts. Color can serve as an attention-guidance cue but also a memory cue to promote learning. However, research has not yet thoroughly explored how colors can serve both purposes: signaling relevant information within the learning material and serving as memory cues to foster retrieval during testing. Therefore, this study investigated whether different signaling colors in digital learning environments can serve as memory cues to enhance retrieval and improve learning outcom

title: Prospecting for efflux pump and repressor genes in rivers of the Amazon region of Brazil
abstract: BACKGROUND: The spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria in water bodies poses a significant public health concern. Efflux pumps represent critical mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, regulated by genetic repressors that aid bacterial adaptation to environmental stress. This study profiles the diversity of efflux pump genes and genetic repressors in the surface waters of the Cereja (Bragança) and Uraim (Paragominas) rivers in the Amazon region of Brazil. METHODS AND RESULTS: Surface water samples were collected along a gradient of anthropogenic impact, and environmental DNA was sequenced on

title: Food waste to biomass approach: A sustainable strategy for the production of alternative microbial culture media for filamentous fungi growth
abstract: The valorization of organic waste is still one of the challenges in the path towards environmental sustainability and a circular bioeconomy. This research aimed at assessing the ability of three substrates of organic residues (olive pomace, potato peels and the green seaweed Ulva lactuca) to be used as alternative culture media for filamentous fungi. Mycelial growth on these media was compared with the conventional Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Sabouraud media using three fungal species namely Fusarium oxysporum (F1), Fusarium solani (F2) and Alternaria alternata (N2) as biological models. Th
institutions: Université Djilali de Sidi Bel Abbès

title: From sediment pulse to ecological recovery: a nine-year study of benthic macroinvertebrate response to Elwha River dam removal
abstract: Large dam removals are increasingly important river restoration actions, but long-term ecological responses remain poorly understood, especially for removals involving large sediment releases. We evaluated benthic macroinvertebrate (BMI) responses following removal of the Elwha and Glines Canyon dams on the Elwha River, Washington, USA. At the time of removal (2011–2014), these were the largest dams to be dismantled worldwide. institutions: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service Northwest Fisheries Science Center
United States Fish and Wildlife Service

title: Quantum Chemical Insight into Species Competition in Electrochemical Upgrading of Bio-Oil
abstract: Abstract Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents an alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value-added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. In a binary mixture, the presence of FF has been shown to inhibit the reduction

title: Impact of YAQ001 on the Gut Microbiome, Permeability and Markers of Systemic Inflammation in Patients With Cirrhosis
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: YAQ001 is a novel, non-absorbable, gut-restricted, multiporous, carbon bead adsorbent. Pre-clinical studies and a clinical trial suggested its therapeutic potential and safety in patients with cirrhosis. This substudy aimed to explore the effects of YAQ001 on the gut microbiome and their exploratory association with biomarkers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation. METHODS: Twenty-eight-patients with cirrhosis were randomized (double-blind) to receive YAQ001 (4 g once daily) or placebo. Gut microbiome and biomarkers of inflammation and gut permeability were assessed

title: From Monomer to Mesh: The Biochemical Maturation of Gel-Forming Mucin Glycoproteins
abstract: Abstract Secreted mucin glycoproteins, which form the scaffolds of the mucus hydrogels coating tissue epithelia, are among the most complex molecules in nature. Mucin protein backbones are typically more than 5000 amino acids in length, become stapled into domain folds by over 100 disulfide bonds, and contain thousands of potential sites for O-glycosylation. The glycans added to these sites vary in chemical composition, length, and degree of branching, producing mucins with diverse biochemical and biophysical properties. title: Mitigating Weld Defects in AISI 4145 Medium-Carbon Steel During Shielded Metal Arc Welding
abstract: Welding defects pose significant challenges to product quality and productivity in manufacturing industries. Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) is the most widely used welding method in developing countries such as Ethiopia. This thesis identifies and addresses the root causes of welding defects in SMAW of medium carbon steel (AISI 4145) at Akaki Basic Metal Industry (ABMI), and optimizes welding parameters to enhance weld quality and reduce defect rates. Pareto analysis identified porosity and undercut as the most critical defects, together accounting for a 6% rejection rate in production over
journal: International Journal of Mechanical Engineering and Applications

title: Ammonia and methane mitigation from dairy manure using sulfur‐based manure storage additives
abstract: Abstract Dairy manure storage is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and other air pollutants, including methane (CH 4 ) and ammonia (NH 3 ). Easily deployable mitigation strategies, such as manure storage additives, can help reduce the environmental impact of dairy production. Sulfur‐based manure storage additives, specifically gypsum (CaSO 4 ), have been proposed as low‐cost manure amendments that may influence CH 4 emissions; however, their potential to mitigate NH 3 emissions and their effectiveness across sulfur dosages remain unclear. title: DIGITAL HEALTH ADOPTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH BETTER HEALTHCARE PERFORMANCE BUT PERSISTENT INEQUITY IN BANGLADESH: A NATIONWIDE CONVERGENT MIXED-METHODS STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELLING STUDY
abstract: Background: Bangladesh is scaling digital health under its Digital Health Strategy 2023–2027, yet empirical evidence on how adoption relates to health-system performance and equity is fragmented. We examined how governance, change management and implementation barriers shape digitalization adoption, and how adoption relates to performance, patient-reported outcomes and perceived health inequality. Methods: A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in all eight administrative divisions. title: Revealing the Values of Eco-theological Islamic Education in the Blora Manganan Tradition through the Perspective of Scientia Sacra Nasr
abstract: The global environmental crisis stems from the modern desacralization of nature. This study explores the Manganan tradition in Blora, Indonesia, as a living system of Eco-theological Islamic Education through Seyyed Hossein Nasr’s Scientia Sacra. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, this study collected data through participant observation, semi-structured interviews with six informants, and documentation in Panolan Village, Blora, in July 2025. title: The Use of Space in Neanderthal Campsites: Evidence from Spatial and Taphonomic Analyses of Charcoal Remains from Level Ra of Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstract: Abstract This work aims to investigate the formation processes of the charcoal assemblage from level Ra at Abric Romaní, a well-preserved Middle Palaeolithic rock shelter in north-eastern Spain that was occupied by Neanderthals. To this end, we adopted an anthracological approach that combines both taxonomic and taphonomic observations. Spatial patterns and potential formation processes were explored through spatial analysis using Kernel Density Estimation and the Moran’s index across the excavated layer. institutions: Institut Català de Paleoecologia Humana i Evolució Social

title: Vaccinia virus growth factor induces divergent signaling programs and biological outcomes from cellular epidermal growth factor
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling is a major pathway that controls cellular growth, survival, proliferation, and differentiation. Viruses often hijack this pathway to create a favorable environment to support their replication. Vaccinia virus (the prototype member of poxviridae) encodes its own viral growth factor (VGF). VGF is a secreted viral polypeptide with sequence and structural homology to the cellular EGF, which binds to and activates EGFR signaling. title: Financial and economic performance of coconut plantation rejuvenation assisted by engineered wood products: A Fijian case study
abstract: Coconut plantations support the livelihoods of millions of smallholder families globally, including a high proportion who live in poverty. Many growing regions are caught in a ‘senility trap’, with large areas over the age of 60, with nut yields well-below their potential. Presently, senile palm removal incurs high direct costs and opportunity costs associated with foregone nut production before replanted coconuts become commercially productive. title: Regulatory aspects of risks posed by veterinary medicinal products to European necrophagous birds: A case study with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used in human and veterinary medicine to treat pain and inflammatory diseases. However, the uncontrolled treatment of free-roaming and sheltered livestock with NSAIDs, mainly diclofenac, has caused catastrophic impacts on the biodiversity of necrophagous birds. For instance, a decline of up to 95 % in populations of various species of vultures occurred in South Asia from the late 1990 s to the early 2000 s. institutions: National Laboratory of Health, Environment and Food
Arthur Rylah Institute for Environmental Research

title: Challenges and Opportunities Faced by Residents of Informal Settlements in Sustaining Their Livelihoods: Evidence from Karu Urban Area, Nasarawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Informal settlements dominate urban landscapes in developing countries, yet evidence on the specific challenges and opportunities residents face in sustaining livelihoods remains limited, particularly in Nigeria's peri-urban interface. This study identifies these challenges and opportunities in Karu Urban Area, Nasarawa State. title: A DPSIR-based scoping review of land degradation in Borana Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: This study examines land degradation in Ethiopia’s Borana Zone using the Drivers–Pressure–State–Impact–Response (DPSIR) framework. Land degradation poses a growing threat to pastoral livelihoods and ecosystem stability in arid and semi-arid regions. The study aims to synthesize existing evidence on the causes, state, impacts, and responses related to land degradation in the area. A scoping review approach was employed following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature was retrieved from Google Scholar and Web of Science. Forty-four studies, most of them published between 2015 and 2025, were inclu

title: Investigation of carrot powder as a plant‐derived nitrate source in dry sausages: impact on sensory quality, amines formation and microbial community
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Rising demand for clean‐label products is fueling the use of natural curing ingredients in product innovation. This study evaluated carrot powder as a plant‐derived nitrate source for natural curing in dry sausage. Compared with other plant‐based nitrite alternatives, carrot powder may provide additional pigments and phenolic compounds that could benefit color and sensory quality. title: Participatory Mapping of Village Potential to Support Local Development Planning in Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This community service program identified, classified, documented, and mapped the development potential of Puuhialu Village, North Konawe Regency, Southeast Sulawesi, between 1 May and 1 June 2026. We combined a participatory approach with descriptive analysis, treating the village government and residents as partners who checked and corrected our findings rather than as mere respondents. title: Listado de fauna silvestre en categoría de riesgo de conservación en Isla del Carmen y Laguna de Términos, Campeche, México
abstract: Los listados documentales de fauna en riesgo pueden sobreestimar el número de taxones cuando los registros de ocurrencia a nivel de especie se cruzan directamente con categorías normativas asignadas a subespecies. El objetivo de este estudio fue elaborar un listado actualizado de las especies de fauna silvestre registradas en Isla del Carmen y Laguna de Términos, Campeche, México, incluidas en alguna categoría de riesgo de la NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010. title: Development and Validation of Low-Carbon Concrete for Floating Offshore Wind Substructures
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the development, optimisation and preliminary scale-up assessment of low-carbon self-compacting concrete mixes tailored for floating offshore wind substructures, comparing traditional Portland cement (CEM I) with slag-based CEM III/B binder systems. A comprehensive experimental programme was conducted, encompassing multiple laboratory-scale mix designs, fatigue behaviour assessment using the Locati method, and pilot-scale production trials involving one 1.5 m 3 batch of each selected mix. title: One-Step Growth Curve Analysis of a Bacteriophage Infecting Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Background: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic gram-negative bacterium associated with the contamination of edible bird’s nest (EBN) production systems. Pseudomonas aeruginosa may infect swiftlets and produce pigments that cause greenish staining of EBN, thereby decreasing the product's quality and market value. Bacteriophages are promising biocontrol agents owing to their host specificity and environmental safety. journal: Journal of Applied Veterinary Science And Technology

title: Efficacy of raccoon removal in urban and rural sites in northern Illinois
abstract: Abstract Raccoons ( Procyon lotor ) are opportunistic and highly adaptable mesopredators that may negatively impact avian and reptilian species. Although wildlife professionals often utilize predator control techniques to manage raccoons, information to guide management activities is lacking. We analyzed the efficacy of raccoon removal within urban and rural sites in northern Illinois, USA, during 2022–2024. title: Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments
abstract: While organic amendments are promoted for enhancing soil quality, their impacts on the net global warming potential (GWP) and the underlying microbial mechanisms in the maize system remain elusive. By using a long-term field experiment established in 2007 under a winter wheat-summer maize rotation system, a field study was conducted to investigate the effects of different organic-amended treatments (manure application and straw return coupled with conventional or no tillage) on greenhouse gas (i.e., nitrous oxide [N 2 O] and carbon dioxide [CO 2 ]) emissions, soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks a
institutions: Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences

title: Rapid Composting Behavior and Properties of Sustainable PLA /Thermoplastic Corn Starch Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Plastic food packaging extends shelf life but causes environmental pollution. Biopolymers such as poly(lactic acid) (PLA) are gaining interest as sustainable alternatives. However, PLA has limitations including slow biodegradation rate, brittleness, and high production cost. This study aims to address these issues by incorporating thermoplastic starch (TPS), a low‐cost, biodegradable biomass based on corn starch, into PLA to develop fast‐compostable biocomposites. title: Ecology and conservation of subterranean biodiversity of Greater Lisbon, Portugal
abstract: Abstract Subterranean ecosystems harbour fauna moulded by extreme and stable conditions such as absence of light, narrow temperature ranges, high humidity and low availability of organic matter. The adaptations of cave fauna, coupled with the isolation of populations, often lead to a higher incidence of endemics and greater vulnerability to environmental changes. These ecosystems face severe threats caused by pollution and overexploitation, habitat loss and climate change, particularly evident in areas of increased human pressure as capitals of countries. title: Visitors’ perceptions and demand preferences for cultural ecosystem services in urban parks for sustainable tourism management
abstract: Abstract Urban parks serve as vital public spaces for recreational activities. However, key scientific questions remain regarding how, and to what extent, socio-demographic characteristics influence visitors’ perceptions of different types of cultural ecosystem services (CESs). Two further questions concern how park visitor typologies and their characteristics can be systematically identified, and how the demand preferences of different visitor groups for CESs can be understood. abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. title: A system-based abstraction hierarchy framework for seismic risk assessment of urban transportation networks
abstract: Urban transportation networks are critical infrastructure for post-earthquake emergency response, making proactive seismic risk assessment essential. However, existing frameworks often examine transportation components, interdependencies, and cascading effects separately, making it difficult to integrate them into a unified seismic-risk framework for transportation systems. This study introduces the Urban Transportation System Abstraction Hierarchy (UTSAH), a directed graph–based framework integrating abstraction hierarchy theory with network analysis across five hierarchical levels. International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis

title: Farmer and advisor perspectives on soil amendments: motivators, barriers, and insights for scaling
abstract: Soil amendments such as gypsum, structure lime, and pulp and paper mill sludge have multiple localised agronomic and broader environmental benefits, but their uptake by farmers remains limited. This exploratory mixed-methods study examined farmers’ and advisors’ perceptions of factors influencing soil amendment adoption through interviews with 11 farmers and 5 agricultural advisors in Southwest Finland, complemented by a nationwide survey of 20 advisors, which provided supplementary perspectives on advisor perceptions. title: Novelties in Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae) from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Revisiting the Dimerostemma collection in Rio Grande do Sul, the southernmost state of Brazil, one new species of Dimerostemma is described and another is resurrected. Although previously synonymized under Dimerostemma arnottii , Dimerostemma oppositifolium is here resurrected based on its distinct opposite leaves, linear to lanceolate leaf limbs, and specific pappus scale measurements. Additionally, Dimerostemma ramboi is described as a new species endemic to the state of Rio Grande do Sul. Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

title: Additive genetic effects of two large effect loci shaping age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
abstract: Fitness-related traits are shaped by both additive and non-additive genetic effects, resulting in a complex and context-dependent genetic architecture. However, the relative contribution of these components remains poorly understood, particularly for major-effect loci underlying life-history traits. In this study, we investigated the additive genetic contributions and potential epistatic interactions between 2 unlinked major-effect loci, vgll3 and six6, that influence age-at-maturity in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). title: foxQ2 marks fast-acting interneurons including dopaminergic neurons of mushroom bodies and central complex in the beetle Tribolium castaneum
abstract: Abstract The brain is one of the most complex animal organs and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II . This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals while it has been lost from vertebrates. title: Integrating ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 Management Systems with Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction in Niger Delta Oil Operations
abstract: Oil operations in the Niger Delta sit inside the same floodplains, creeks and villages that host millions of residents. Hazards such as spills, fires, floods and pipeline failures rarely stop at the fence line, yet the management systems that govern them usually do. This paper argues that ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) and ISO 14001 (environment), both built on the same high-level structure, can be deliberately extended to include community-based disaster risk reduction (CBDRR). title: Phase engineering of Mo x C regulates electronic structure and interfacial hydrogen-bond networks over Ru sites for pH-universal hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Metallic ruthenium (Ru) represents a promising Pt alternative for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, achieving efficient HER, particularly under pH-universal conditions, remains challenging due to sluggish interfacial water dissociation kinetics. Herein, we report a phase engineering strategy that utilizes well-defined cubic and hexagonal molybdenum carbide (α–MoC/β–Mo2C) supports to regulate Ru–MoxC metal–support interactions and interfacial microenvironments. title: Integration of Landscape Aesthetics and Sustainable Business Models in Kaliaren Village Land Utilization
abstract: This research aims to identify and optimize land use in Kaliaren Village through the integration of landscape aesthetic aspects and the development of sustainable business models. Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach, this study maps the existing conditions of land use, analyzes aesthetic and economic potential, and explores the perception of the community and stakeholders through observation, in-depth interviews, Focus Group Discussions, and spatial analysis. The results of the study show that Kaliaren Village has strong landscape potential in the form of terraced rice fields,

title: Pace-dependent reorganisation of shoulder-hip coordination in front crawl swimming
abstract: Shoulder and hip roll are distinct but coordinated components of body roll during front crawl swimming, yet shoulder-hip coordination has largely been examined using discrete measures. This study applied continuous relative phase (CRP), Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM), and complementary coupling analyses to a previously published kinematic dataset, to examine shoulder-hip coordination during sprint and 400 m pace front crawl. title: Policy Strategy To Reduce Unemployment In Bengkulu Province
abstract: This study examines the structural challenges of unemployment and labour-market development in Bengkulu Province. Despite an open unemployment rate (TPT) of 3.20% in May 2026, the province recorded 37,242 unemployed people, while 65.45% of employed people worked in the informal sector. Using descriptive policy analysis of secondary data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS), particularly the 2025–2026 National Labour Force Survey (Sakernas), this study analyses employment trends and policy alternatives. title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator ( Alligator mississippiensis ) based on fluctuating thermal regimes
abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determines sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. However, existing TSD reaction norms are derived from constant temperature laboratory conditions, leaving open the question of their applicability to natural conditions where incubation temperatures fluctuate. title: Inventarios de atractivos turísticos como instrumento para la gestión territorial
abstract: El inventario de atractivos turísticos constituye una fuente de información para la planificación local, pero su utilidad depende de la vigencia, trazabilidad y localización de los registros. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el valor del inventario histórico de atractivos turísticos del cantón San Francisco de Milagro, Ecuador, como antecedente para la gestión territorial. Se aplicó un enfoque documental, descriptivo y retrospectivo, con revisión de una memoria técnica publicada por CLIRSEN en 2009, basada en información turística de 2007–2008, y contraste normativo con instrumentos na

title: Hierarchically Wrinkled Silver Ink as a Platform for Fully Integrated Stretchable Electronic Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of high‐performance stretchable electronics continues to be limited by the fundamental trade‐off between electrical conductivity, mechanical resilience, and cost‐effective manufacturability. This work introduces a Silver Hierarchical Responsive ink (SHRink), a universal approach for the fabrication of highly stretchable interconnects, wirings, and skin‐interfaced electrodes. title: Computational prioritization of fungal-derived H1 receptor ligand candidates for allergy-related research
abstract: Activation of the G-protein-coupled histamine H1 receptor (H1R) contributes to allergic responses such as bronchoconstriction, vasodilation, and pruritus. This study aimed to computationally prioritize novel fungal-derived compounds for H1R-targeted investigation based on predicted binding characteristics, pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles, and BBB permeability. A comprehensive workflow incorporating SP and XP molecular docking, ADMET, SAR, DFT, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM/GBSA, and Dynamic Cross-Correlation Matrix (DCCM) analyses was employed. title: Assessment of possible interactions between Citrus aurantifolia leaf alkaloid-rich compounds and relevant protein targets in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats
abstract: Aim: This study assessed the neuroprotective effect of lime (Citrus aurantifolia) leaf via the interaction of its inherent alkaloid compounds with specific neuronal protein targets [acetylcholinesterase (AChE), adenosine deaminase (ADA), and monoamine oxidase (MAO)] in scopolamine-induced amnesic rats. Methods: Lime leaf alkaloid-rich extract (LLARE) compounds were characterised using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, and the in silico absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) screening was accomplished on the SwissADME server. title: Identifying Middle Paleolithic Residential Units Through the Spatial Organization of Combustion Structures at Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain)
abstract: Abstract The habitual and controlled use of fire among Neanderthal groups, together with the residential use of caves and rock shelters, represents a major turning point in the emergence of Paleolithic camp bases. In Middle Paleolithic sites, the interrelation between shelter geomorphology, fire-use locations and activity areas has been interpreted as evidence of spatial organization. title: Food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children and parents in southern Peru: A cross-sectional study using projective techniques
abstract: Peru's school feeding program applies largely uniform menus across regions with very different food cultures, yet little is known about how children and parents in these regions represent food. This cross-sectional study compared food perceptions and breakfast choices among school-age children (10-12 years) and their parents in five cities of southern Peru (Arequipa, Cusco, Moquegua, Puno and Tacna). Three projective techniques were applied: free drawing and a sorting task with 600 children from public primary schools (120 per city), and a breakfast composition task with 576 parents. Drawings

title: Integrating high-resolution magnetic surveys and metaheuristic optimization for quantitative characterization of subsurface magnetic sources in a municipal landfill
abstract: Landfill leachate poses a significant environmental risk by transporting toxic metals and organic contaminants into surrounding soil and groundwater. This study establishes a rapid, non-invasive geophysical framework for delineating potential subsurface leachate pathways using high-resolution magnetic surveying integrated with advanced magnetic data processing and metaheuristic optimization. A total of 246 magnetic measurements were acquired across the Benowo landfill, Surabaya, Indonesia, using a proton precession magnetometer. title: Decoupling Sustainability Reporting and Social Media Communication After a Sustainability Scandal: Strategic Silence, Selective Disclosure and Legitimacy Stabilisation
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how corporate sustainability disclosure evolves across a legitimacy‐threatening event by analysing the interaction between formal sustainability reporting and social media communication. Using a qualitative, longitudinal, event‐centred single‐case design, the study investigates a major Italian organic meat producer over the 2021–2024 period through formal sustainability reporting, Facebook content and stakeholder interactions, regulatory and contextual documents and selected economic indicators. Findings reveal a marked divergence across corporate‐controlled disclo

title: Tail movements and prey displacement: A new observation in Erythrolamprus miliaris (Serpentes: Dipsadidae) and a potentially overlooked pattern in xenodontine snakes
abstract: Tail movements associated with prey capture have been reported in snakes under a variety of functional contexts, including caudal luring, caudal distraction, and prey flushing. Herein, we describe an unusual predatory interaction between the semi-aquatic snake Erythrolamprus miliaris and a toad of the genus Rhinella under controlled laboratory conditions. This observation provides new insights into the predatory behaviour of xenodontine snakes. title: கஙக வடடர மரபச சழலயல அறவம வபபத தழவலம வளண தழலளரகளககன தமழவழத தகவல தடரபத தலயடடன மதபபட: Traditional Ecological Knowledge and Heat Adaptation in the Kongu Region: An Evaluation of a Tamil-Language Communication Intervention for Agricultural Workers
abstract: Rising temperatures, water scarcity and variable rainfall affect agriculture and the working conditions of agricultural labourers. This article proposes an approach to heat adaptation that brings together traditional ecological knowledge from the Kongu region and contemporary climate information. It examines representations of nature, heat, rainfall, water and agriculture in Sangam literature, the Tirukkural, Silappathikaram and Periyapuranam through a literary and ecological reading. journal: KALANJIYAM - International Journal of Tamil Studies

title: Antibiofilm Activity of Zinc Sulfate Against Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from Clinical and Retail Meat Sources in Baghdad, Iraq
abstract: Biofilm formation was investigated among 60 Staphylococcus aureus isolates obtained from both retail meat and clinical samples in Baghdad, Iraq. These isolates were divided into 75% (45/60) clinical isolates and 25% (15/60) meat-derived isolates. Biofilm formation among all isolates was evaluated using the microtiter plate assay, while the presence of the biofilm-associated genes icaA, icaB, icaC, and icaD was determined by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). title: Andrographolide Combined With Voriconazole Enhances Antifungal Activity Against Aspergillus Species
abstract: Azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus is increasing globally, necessitating novel combination strategies to restore the efficacy of first-line antifungals such as voriconazole (VCZ). Andrographolide (ADR), a natural diterpene lactone, has shown limited direct antifungal activity but exhibits synergistic effects with amphotericin B and immunomodulatory properties. However, its potential as an adjunct to VCZ against Aspergillus species remains unexplored. title: Estimating the causal effect of extreme flooding on urban property markets: A case study of Porto Alegre, Brazil
abstract: The May 2024 floods in Porto Alegre, Brazil, triggered a pronounced spatial repricing of climate risk in the city’s housing market. Using a Bayesian structural time-series framework, we estimate an average causal impact of a 4.7% increase in sale prices and a 9.1% increase in rental price indices, driven primarily by price appreciation in elevated, flood-resilient neighborhoods. Our econometric approach accounts for nonlinear trends and macroeconomic controls, isolating the causal effect of the disaster. institutions: International Institute for Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation

title: Distribution of Tuberculosis (TB) Cases Based on Patient Characteristics in the Working Area of the Simeulue District Health Office in 2026
abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the public health problems that requires serious attention because it can increase morbidity and mortality rates. The spread of tuberculosis cases is influenced by various patient characteristics such as gender, age, area of residence, treatment status, and occupation. This study aims to determine the distribution of tuberculosis cases based on patient characteristics in the working area of the Simeulue District Health Office in 2026. title: Do herbivorous fish amplify the competitive dominance of floating-leaved plants over submerged plants?
abstract: Growing interest in the relationship between herbivorous fish and aquatic plants has revealed multiple pathways by which fish can influence aquatic plant biomass and coverage. However, the impact of herbivorous fish on species competition and community assembly in aquatic plants remains poorly understood. Here, based on a mesocosm experiment with four aquatic plant species (two floating-leaved and two submerged) and one herbivorous fish, we quantified competition coefficients among plant species and fish effects using a modified Ricker model. title: Genomic and morphological data corroborate Percina crypta (Percidae: Etheostomatinae) as a valid taxon and reveal undescribed diversity in the Percina nigrofasciata complex
abstract: Percina crypta Freeman, Freeman & Burkhead, the Halloween Darter, was described in 2008 as a new species endemic to the Chattahoochee and Flint River systems in the Apalachicola Basin, Georgia and Alabama, USA. The description illustrated phenotypic differences between Percina crypta and sympatric Percina nigrofasciata (Agassiz) sensu lato (s.l.) (the Blackbanded Darter) but lacked genetic data. title: Paving over the source: Land use change and the everyday struggle for water in Mbale town, Kenya (2014-2025)
abstract: Secondary cities are where Africa’s urban future is being decided, yet they remain academically invisible. While Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu are extensively studied, towns like Mbale-Vihiga County’s administrative capital absorb over 60% of Kenya’s urban growth with no commensurate infrastructure. This study seeks to find out what happens when a town urbanizes over its own catchment. institutions: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology

title: Trayectorias de flujo subterráneo asociado a los lagos de Pátzcuaro y Cuitzeo
abstract: This study determines the components of a groundwater flow system associated with Lakes Pátzcuaro and Cuitzeo. The objectives are: a) to delineate flow trajectories and b) to identify the pathways that contribute to lake recharge. The methodology included water sampling, hydrogeochemical, isotopic, and statistical analysis of groundwater and surface water. title: Signal peptides for engineered protein secretion by free and hydrogel-encapsulated cyanobacteria
abstract: Cyanobacteria provide a promising platform for light-driven heterologous protein production. In heterologous production systems, cells are typically lysed for product purification or to facilitate interaction with external substrates, unless the product is secreted. Fusion to molecular “shipping labels” known as signal peptides can target chimeric proteins to native membrane translocation pathways and result in secretion. title: Spatial modeling for the protection of waterways in the Quinsaloma canton, Los Ríos, Ecuador
abstract: This research aims to spatially model the protection of watercourses in Quinsaloma canton (Los Ríos, Ecuador), for the integrated management of water resources. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining quantitative and qualitative techniques, including surveys of 90 residents and interviews with community leaders. title: Aptamer‐Functionalized Pro‐Photosensitizers for Targeted Elimination of Drug‐Resistant Bacterial Biofilm Infection by Sequentially Activated Photodynamic‐Antibiotic Therapy
abstract: Drug-resistant bacterial infections seriously threaten public health, and the formation of a biofilm barrier plays an important role. Drug-resistant biofilms are difficult to remove because the penetration and specificity of traditional antimicrobial drugs are poor, and the microenvironment in the inner layer of biofilms is hypoxic. Herein, we developed activatable aptamer-functionalized pro-photosensitizers (APMB) by modifying the clinical photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) with an aptamer that can specifically bind to drug-resistant bacteria. title: Evolution of aroma-active compounds and precursor-aroma relationships in spiced brine-stewed pork intestine during stewing
abstract: Pork intestines are widely appreciated for their distinctive flavor and texture, yet their dynamic development during spiced brine stewing remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated GC-MS, GC-IMS, GC-O-MS, and eOAV analyses highlighted six major aroma-active compounds, with ethyl maltol and eugenol showing high potential aroma relevance. title: Segmented lithospheric architecture beneath the Middle—Lower Yangtze River metallogenic belt constraints by magnetotelluric array data
abstract: The Middle—Lower Yangtze River Metallogenic Belt (MLYMB) is a major Fe-Cu-Au-Mo polymetallic belt in eastern China. However, the deep geodynamic processes responsible for the contrasting metallogenesis characteristics of its individual ore districts remain under debated. We constructed a three-dimensional (3-D) lithospheric-scale resistivity model using magnetotelluric (MT) data from 160 stations. title: Ion and particle size distribution measurements in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: seasonal insights and challenges in new particle formation event characterization
abstract: Abstract. New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of atmospheric aerosols and cloud condensation nuclei, influencing climate and air quality. In highly polluted regions such as the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP), where precursor concentrations and condensation sinks are among the highest globally, NPF remains poorly constrained due to limited observations of particles and ions in sub–10 nm size range. abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop.
