title: Multi‐Parametric Fluorescence Spectroscopy for the Detection and Characterization of Plant‐Derived Protein Residues on 316L Stainless Steel
abstract: ABSTRACT Adsorption of proteins and other biomolecules on stainless steel and other functional metallic surfaces is a key interfacial phenomenon in food processing environments, leading to progressive surface accumulation of organic residues. Their presence can impair the material performance, promote microbial adhesion, complicate cleaning procedures, and ultimately create significant hygiene challenges. title: Integrated geochemical and spatial analysis of trace element redistribution in salinized arid agro-landscapes: Evidence from the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan)
abstract: Arid agro-landscapes are highly vulnerable to the soil degradation caused by long-term irrigation and climatic constraints.This study investigated the spatial patterns and geochemical characteristics associated with trace element redistribution in salinized irrigated soils of the Turyanchay River basin (Azerbaijan).A geochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling units from representative sampling sites was analyzed for trace element composition using energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (EDXRF).A separate physicochemical dataset comprising 22 depth-specific sampling un

title: Subsurface Modeling Using Gravity Data in Southern Yogyakarta and Its Implications for The May 26th, 2006 Earthquake
abstract: The Yogyakarta region is one of the most seismically vulnerable areas in Indonesia, so detailed subsurface fault characterization is crucial for effective disaster mitigation strategies. Previous studies have recognized the Opak Fault as the main structure controlling seismicity in this area, but the geometry and existence of other fault systems remain less constrained. This study aims to delineate the subsurface density variations associated with fault zones and rock deformation. title: Palaeoproteomic investigation of archaeological sediments associated with ochre use in the Middle Stone Age of southern Africa
abstract: The African Middle Stone Age (MSA) represents the cultural and technological context associated with the emergence of Homo sapiens and the development of complex cognition. In this setting, ochre use is considered a multifaceted proxy for modern behaviour, allowing inferences about technical and symbolic aspects of Homo sapiens. Powdered ochre is reported in multiple southern African ethnographic and archaeological contexts alongside various organic materials, some of which are protein-based. title: Beyond Primary Nucleation: Molecular Basis of Peptide Crystal Secondary Nucleation at Soft Interface
abstract: ABSTRACT The formation of peptide 2D crystals with well‐organized molecular arrays by primary nucleation mechanism have provided an efficient way to incorporate biofunctions into the underlying single layer graphene and MoS 2 , leading to broad applications for biosensing, biomedicine and bioelectronics. Further realizing a high‐level architecture of peptide 3D crystals coupling with the underlying nanomaterials would expand its applications for the next‐generation bionanodevices, while facing a big challenge. title: Proteasome Inhibitor MG132 Facilitates Antiviral Effects by Inhibiting TFEB Degradation and Activating Autophagy
abstract: Abstract The ubiquitin-proteasome system, which serves as one of the most common cellular degradation pathways, plays a critical role in maintaining proteostasis. Yet, the correlation between the ubiquitin-proteasome system and antiviral defense remains to be defined. In this work, pharmacological inhibition of proteasomes via treatment with MG132, which inhibited proteasome activity during viral infection, facilitated antiviral effects in vitro. title: Hollowing Out Nanofibers for Enhanced Visual Brightness and More Effective Solar Heating
abstract: The temperature rise of a solar-heating textile is controlled by both generation and dissipation of heat. However, current designs mainly focus on increasing light absorption to generate more heat, often darkening the material while leaving thermal management largely overlooked. Herein, hollowing the nanofibers in a nonwoven mat produces a counterintuitive "brighter-yet-hotter" advantage over their solid (core-shell) counterparts. abstract: Although heazlewoodite‐type nickel sulfide (Ni 3 S 2 ) exhibits promising hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, its application in overall water splitting remains limited by sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics associated with insufficient water activation. Herein, Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen‐rich spongy carbons are constructed to regulate interfacial electronic properties and unlock Co–Ni catalytic synergy for efficient water electrolysis. title: Las tecnologías educativas para enseñar geografía e historia
abstract: Este artículo analiza el uso de tecnologías educativas en la enseñanza de geografía e historia mediante una revisión bibliográfica narrativa crítica de siete publicaciones de 2021–2026. Se realizaron búsquedas dirigidas y se contrastaron datos bibliográficos en revistas, registros académicos y organismos oficiales. La selección comprendió revisiones, investigaciones sobre enseñanza y un informe institucional. abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aim To address the dual challenges of water scarcity and climate change in rice production, a 2‐year field study was conducted to assess the combined effects of water management practices and γ‐polyglutamic acid (γ‐PGA) application on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water productivity, and economic benefits. title: Coordination‐Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. title: Retrospective evaluation of repeated dose dermal toxicity studies in North American agrochemical risk assessment
abstract: Current North American pesticide regulations mandate route-specific repeated-dose dermal toxicity (RDDT) studies for dermal exposure risk assessment. To evaluate the scientific necessity of this study requirement, a proof-of-concept retrospective analysis was conducted on conventional active pesticide ingredients with Syngenta end use product registered in North America (NA) from 2001 to 2025, examining publicly available risk assessments for 51 pesticides assessed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) and 43 by the Health Canada Pesticides Regulatory Directorate (PRD).

title: A Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assembly and Demographic History Inference of Ostrya rehderiana
abstract: Ostrya rehderiana is a critically endangered plant species with an extremely small population size. However, the absence of high-quality genome assembly has impeded the understanding of the causes and genetic consequences of its endangered status, especially how theses genetic consequences result in the failure of its population regeneration. In this study, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long-read sequencing, Hi-C, Illumina resequencing, and RNA-seq data to generate a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and annotation for this species. title: Discovery and Structure Elucidation of a New Polyketide‐Derived Tetrahydropyran‐Containing Conjugated Fatty Acid Derivative Isolated From Typhonium blumei
abstract: ABSTRACT A chemical investigation of the 95% EtOH extract of Typhonium blumei led to the isolation of a new polyketide‐derived tetrahydropyran‐containing conjugated fatty acid derivative ( 1 ), together with four known compounds ( 2 – 5 ). The structure of compound 1 was elucidated through comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including 1D and 2D NMR spectra ( 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, DEPT, HSQC, HMBC, COSY, and NOESY), as well as HR‐ESI‐MS data. title: Effects of heatwaves and larval host plant on overwinter performance of a generalist herbivore
abstract: Abstract Heatwaves are increasing in frequency and severity due to anthropogenic climate change and may play a role in recent insect declines. Heatwaves can occur during any season, and how insects are affected by heatwaves may depend on an insect's phenology and life stage when the heatwave occurs. Most research investigates summer heatwaves; however, winter heatwaves may have greater negative impacts on insects than summer heatwaves, but further investigation is necessary. title: Estimation of Dietary Microplastic Ingestion: Empirical Analysis for Delhi-NCR
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly detected in food products and may contribute to human exposure through daily dietary consumption. However, information on dietary MP exposure in Delhi-NCR, India, remains limited. This study aimed to investigate MP contamination in commonly consumed food items and assess their potential contribution to dietary exposure among residents of Delhi-NCR. title: Does telehealth narrow the urban-rural gap? A dual assessment of in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility
abstract: Telehealth has been proposed to reduce rural prenatal care barriers, but its equity effects depend on whether predicted accessibility translates into observed utilization. We examine whether predicted and revealed in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility diverge across the urban-rural continuum of South Carolina and whether these measures align with ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA)-level birth-related need, measured as average annual live births by residence. title: Integrated fertilizer management and agrometeorological conditions associated with yield and nutritional quality of Boro rice
abstract: Increasing rice production while improving grain nutritional quality is essential for global food security. We hypothesized that integrated fertilizer management combined with a suitable rice variety would enhance grain yield, nutrient uptake, and nutritional quality compared to conventional fertilizer management, while agrometeorological conditions would help explain variations in crop performance. title: Dual Functionality of Chitosan in Chia Oil-in-Water Emulsions: From Interfacial Behavior to Short-Term Stability
abstract: Physical stability of chitosan (CH)-based emulsions was investigated and compared with emulsions formulated with egg yolk (EY), a conventional food emulsifier. Additionally, a mixture of both components was examined to assess its potential to improve emulsion performance. Emulsion quality was characterized by evaluating interfacial properties, including interfacial tension and interfacial rheological properties, as well as the evolution of droplet size distribution using laser diffraction, optical microscopy, visual inspection, and multiple light scattering in chia-oil-in-water emulsions. title: Monospecific cover crops perpetuate soil biotic homogenization in croplands across diverse soils
abstract: Abstract Croplands are known to support significant soil biotic homogenization. Cover crops are commonly used as a sustainable agriculture practice; however, many times these cover crops are composed of single‐species. Unfortunately, the influence of monospecific cover crops on soil biotic homogenization remains virtually unknown. Here, we performed a common garden experiment including soils from 27 agricultural fields across mainland China and two major cover crops grown separately in monoculture: a legume ( Vicia villosa Roth) and a gramineae ( Lolium multiflorum Lam.). title: A Tension‐Controlled Arthroscopic Technique for Fixation of a Glenolabral Articular Disruption Lesion in an Overhead Athlete
abstract: Glenolabral articular disruption lesions are rare post-traumatic injuries that occur after shoulder instability events particularly in young, high-demand athletes. Managing these injuries can be challenging especially in overhead athletes who require a degree of physiologic laxity to preserve throwing mechanics. Although various treatment methods have previously been described, literature addressing these injuries in overhead throwers remains limited. title: The complete chloroplast genome of diploid Hieracium tomentosum (Asteraceae, Cichorieae)
abstract: Hieracium is a megadiverse genus within the family Asteraceae, in the tribe Cichorieae subtribe Hieraciinae. We report here the complete chloroplast genome of the diploid Hieracium tomentosum L. The assembled plastome measures 153,218 bp in total length with one large single-copy (LSC, 84,604 bp), one small single-copy (SSC, 18,438 bp), and two inverted repeat (IR, 25,088 bp) regions. It comprehends 127 genes, including 83 protein-coding genes, 8 rRNA genes, and 36 tRNA genes. title: Effects of 4R nitrogen management on corn silage production
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) is one of the critical and costliest inputs for corn silage ( Zea mays ) production. Excessive N applications decrease profits for growers via increased cost of production and raise environmental concerns. The four core principles of the 4R nutrient stewardship framework—right source (S), right rate (R), right time (T), and right place (P)—aim to optimize N management. Most previous studies evaluating N management for corn silage only examined one or a few 4R practices. title: Energy efficient data gathering in load balanced clustered wireless sensor networks with compressive sensing
abstract: Rapid energy loss from continuous sensing and data transmission often shortens network lifespan. This work suggests Bernoulli holomorphic swarm optimized Hermite polynomial compressive sensing (BHSO-HPCS), an energy-efficient data collection method, to overcome this difficulty. The suggested approach minimizes energy usage without sacrificing network performance by combining compressive sensing (CS) and load-balanced clustering algorithms. title: A Comprehensive Review on Furcellaran‐Based Food Packaging: Applications, Developments and Horizons
abstract: ABSTRACT Growing concerns regarding the uncontrolled proliferation of plastic materials, which pose significant environmental challenges, have prompted researchers to seek innovative, eco‐friendly alternatives to conventional petroleum‐based packaging. Among various biological sources, seaweed has emerged as a very promising candidate. These seaweeds are rich in polysaccharides that can act as biopolymers in sustainable food packaging formulations. title: Planetary-scale metagenomic analysis reveals CRISPR targeting dynamics across ecosystems
abstract: Interactions between microorganisms and their mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including viruses and plasmids, impact microbiome dynamics. CRISPR-Cas systems are important regulators of these host-MGE interactions, but a global understanding of the diversity, activity and roles of CRISPR spacers across Earth's biomes is still lacking. Here we develop a computational approach to search short-read data and collect 794 million CRISPR spacers across 367,609 public metagenomes, from which we identified 1.18 billion hits between 41 million spacers and 2.5 million viruses and plasmids. title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). title: GSK3 Inhibition During Annelid Head Regeneration Results in a Hyper‐Proliferative Blastema and Impaired Differentiation
abstract: A major goal of regeneration biology is to uncover the molecular mechanisms that allow a wide range of animals to replace body parts through regeneration. Glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK3) is known to have significant regulatory influence on developmental pathways that are integral to successful regeneration in several animal groups. Annelids include some of the most highly regenerative animals known and, although GSK3 has been studied during regeneration in several species, its major roles remain unclear. title: Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Anti‐Melanogenic Activity of a Novel Pectic Polysaccharide From Alhagi camelorum Fisch
abstract: Hyperpigmentation disorders motivate the search for structurally defined and effective natural depigmenting agents from plant-derived polysaccharides. The present study characterized the structural features and evaluated the anti-melanogenic activity of ACP-II-1, a novel pectic polysaccharide isolated from Alhagi camelorum Fisch. ACP-II-1 had a molecular weight of 26.145 kDa and contained GalA, Rha, Gal, Ara, GlcA, and Xyl at respective molar proportions of 0.798, 0.072, 0.053, 0.052, 0.016, and 0.009. title: Financiamiento Popular y Solidario: Percepción y rol en el fortalecimiento emprendedor en Machala, Ecuador
abstract: El fortalecimiento del emprendimiento se ha convertido en un aspecto trascendente para el desarrollo socioeconómico en Ecuador. Este estudio se enfocó en analizar la incidencia del Sistema Financiero Popular y Solidario en la experiencia de crédito de emprendedores del cantón Machala-Ecuador. Se optó por un enfoque cuantitativo de alcance explicativo, recolectando los datos para el modelo logístico ordinal mediante una encuesta aplicada a 300 emprendedores, de este total solo 233 recibieron financiamiento procedente del Sistema. title: Chemical fingerprinting of a furniture waste landfill fire: parent and alkylated PAHs, organophosphates and environmental-health risk assessments
abstract: Abstract Fires at furniture-waste storage sites are an under-researched source of persistent organic contaminants. This study characterized 13 charred furniture-waste samples collected after a landfill fire in Tychy, Poland, using GC–MS to determine parent and alkylated PAHs and organophosphate esters (OPEs), and to perform screening-level environmental and human-health assessments. title: Thermoresponsive PNIPAM Gel-Coated PCL Nanofibers: Characterization, Vapor-Phase Release of Rosemary Essential Oil, and Activity Against Aspergillus flavus
abstract: Rosemary essential oil (REO) was incorporated into electrospun poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) nanofibers, which were subsequently modified with a thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-gel coating using an immersion-based approach. The coated fibers exhibited temperature-dependent surface wetting behavior below and above the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of PNIPAM. title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). title: Role of the nagZ Gene in Antibiotic Resistance and Environmental Stress Tolerance of Yersinia enterocolitica
abstract: NagZ is a glycoside hydrolase that regulates AmpC β-lactamase and biofilm formation in Gram-negative bacteria, and its inhibitors show promise as antibiotic adjuvants. However, the role of nagZ in the important foodborne pathogen Yersinia enterocolitica, which exhibits strong environmental adaptability and increasing rates of antibiotic resistance, remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of NagZ on antibiotic resistance and environmental tolerance in Y. enterocolitica. title: Predicting tree growth using light availability as an indicator of competition
abstract: Tree growth modelling and predictions are essential components of forest planning and ecological research. Airborne laser scanning data can provide detailed information about tree crowns, where primary photosynthesis happens. The aim of this study was to investigate, whether intercepted solar radiation received by tree crowns, modelled using drone-based Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data, can be used as an indicator of competition in individual tree growth models instead of traditional competition variables such as basal area or basal area of larger trees. abstract: Background: Whether the initial clip type selected during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) of the mitral valve—grasping width and arm length—independently influences procedural and echocardiographic outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 138 consecutive patients undergoing mitral TEER. The first implanted clip was classified as narrow standard-length (NT), long narrow-arm (XT), or long wide-arm (XTW). abstract: "Community informant" species serve as critical sources of information. However, interactions between multiple informant species in complex systems remain unclear, including whether they jointly contribute vocalizations and thus public information, eavesdrop on each other, or do not interact, and whether joint contributions provide benefits through complementary or supplementary mechanisms. title: Early Maize Growth In Rhizoboxes Under Ageratum Conyzoides Leaf Extract And Chicken Manure
abstract: Maize requires adequate nutrients during vegetative growth, and organic fertilizers can serve as an alternative nutrient source to inorganic fertilizers. Babadotan (Ageratum conyzoides L.) leaves contain nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium and may therefore be used as a aqueous leaf extract. This study evaluated the effect of babadotan leaf extract and chicken manure on the vegetative growth of maize (Zea mays L.) grown in rhizoboxes. abstract: Plastic waste exhibits a significant environmental challenge as of its resistance to natural degradation, the study aimed to characterize outer layer morphological changes and elemental composition Related to with fungal treatment of plastic plates using imaging electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and basic mapping. A refined isolate of Penicillium notatum, collected from soil, was used for fungal exposure. title: Skeletal Development During Metamorphosis of the Rice Field Frog Hoplobatrachus rugulosus (Wiegmann, 1834) (Anura: Dicroglossidae)
abstract: The rice field frog (Hoplobatrachus rugulosus) is an important native species in Southeast Asian agricultural wetlands and a major commodity in the aquaculture industry. Despite its ecological and economic importance, and its use as an animal model in various studies, detailed data regarding its skeletal ontogeny remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by presenting a comprehensive chronological atlas of osteogenesis for H. rugulosus from Gosner stages 28 to 46. abstract: Abstract Reclamation of saline–alkali land relies on salt leaching and restoring soil fertility. However, the micro‐scale pore‐architectural changes associated with different land‐use systems remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in relation to their potential implications for water transport and fertility retention. This study selected natural land‐use systems (wasteland [WL] and degraded grassland [GL]) and artificial land‐use systems (upland field [UF] and paddy field [PF]) in Jilin, China, and scanned 5–7 mm macroaggregates for computed tomography imaging. title: Integrating tectonically guided fractured-rock groundwater exploration and community based governance for water security in Pakistan
abstract: Pakistan faces a growing water crisis driven by climate change, groundwater depletion, declining water quality, and increasing demand. We propose a hybrid framework that integrates regional structural geology with community-based water governance to improve long-term water security and climate resilience in the Indus River Basin. abstract: This paper examines the role of local gastronomy as a development mechanism for tourism events in Montenegro, with special focus on the perceptions of employees in the tourism sector. Starting from the assumption that gastronomy constitutes an important element of destination identity and competitiveness through the provision of tourism events, the research aims to determine how employees perceive its significance, which dimensions shape their perception, and which factors influence the formation of attitudes toward gastronomy in tourism events as a basis for tourism development. title: Biochar and PGPR co-application mitigates salinity stress in Malabar spinach (Basella alba L.) by modulating growth, stress markers, and antioxidant defense
abstract: Soil salinity is a major problem for agricultural productivity, adversely affecting plant growth, physiology, and biochemical performance. Malabar spinach ( Basella alba L. ), an important leafy vegetable with high nutritional value, is sensitive to salinity stress, leading to reduced yield and market quality. Developing sustainable strategies to mitigate these effects is essential for its cultivation in marginal soils. abstract: Three specimens of Dipluran Japygidae, collected from two widely separated caves – one in the western Mediterranean and the other in Southeast Asia – have revealed the existence of an impressive, distinctive and unusual cercal amour pattern, unlike that of other Japygidae, characterized by two to three pairs of subsymmetrically arranged teeth. abstract: Abstract Mercury removal from aqueous and hydrocarbon media requires sorbents that combine strong binding affinity with sufficient pore accessibility and mass transfer. title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERACTIVE ETHNOMATHEMATICS-BASED E-LKPD ON MAGETAN LOCAL ARCHITECTURE TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF SOLID GEOMETRY CONCEPTS
abstract: Learning flat-sided solid geometry requires students to connect abstract mathematical concepts with visual representations and real-world objects. However, mathematics instruction at the junior high school level may still rely on conventional teaching methods, printed learning materials, and limited integration of local cultural contexts. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of an interactive mathematics electronic student worksheet (E-LKPD) based on the ethnomathematics of Magetan’s local architecture. title: Obsidian sourcing of artifacts from the Late Formative site of La Puntilla in the Southern Nasca Region, Peru
abstract: We report X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) analyses of 88 obsidian artifacts from the Early Horizon (aka Formative Period) site of La Puntilla in the Southern Nasca Region (SNR) of south-central Peru. The sample includes a range of artifact types, including 19 projectile points, 21 bifaces (some likely point fragments), 2 cores, 5 utilized flakes, and 41 unmodified flakes. title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 for reductive photocatalysis
abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. title: Metagenomic evidence for climate-associated variation in microbial methylmercury production across peatlands
abstract: Abstract Peatlands are major global mercury (Hg) reservoirs and are highly sensitive to warming, yet climate effects on microbial controls of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) formation remain unclear. Here, we combined global synthesis with new measurements to assess climate-associated variation in net MeHg production. abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional ABX 3 perovskites place organic species at A ‐sites or as X ‐site linkers, where the B ‐site is reserved for metals. title: Biological Activities of the Endemic Plant Colchicum figlalii: Cytotoxic, Antioxidant, and Antimicrobial Properties
abstract: Throughout history, plants have been used in the treatment of various diseases, forming the foundation of traditional medicine and inspiring modern pharmaceutical research. Notably, Colchicum species, recognized for their therapeutic potential, represent an important group of plants evaluated in both traditional use and modern pharmacology. This study investigates the in vitro cytotoxic, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities of the methanol extract of Colchicum figlalii, an endemic species found in Muğla, Türkiye. title: Formal Total Synthesis of (±)‐Carexane L Enabled by a PPA‐Mediated Fragmentation–Cyclization Cascade and Heck Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a succinct formal total synthesis of the rearranged aromatic sesquiterpene (±)‐carexane L, an indanone‐based natural product derived from the roots of Carex distachya Desf., a species indigenous to the Mediterranean maquis, commencing from benzoic acid. The synthesis strategically employs a combination of one‐pot polyphosphoric acid (PPA)‐mediated cyclization and Heck cross‐coupling as pivotal reactions.

title: The Roman bridges in Jarash (Gerasa), Jordan: a re-examination of their design, chronology and function
abstract: This fresh perspective on the Roman bridges in Jarash investigates previously unexamined aspects of their design, chronology and function. It focuses on the contrasting design elements of two well-attested bridges, both likely built in the 2nd century BCE, together with a third bridge identified during the research. abstract: Purpose: To explain how EPC project owners can align front-end development, contracting strategy, procurement discipline, execution monitoring, cost optimization, and claims prevention into a single governance framework. Methodology: Analysis of the EPC lifecycle and the use of the Kashagan project as a case study to illustrate the impact of technical complexity, immature risk planning, and execution failures. title: Trajectory Planning for Multi-Robot Formation Control with the Artificial Potential Field
abstract: In multi-robot formation control systems, trajectory planning plays a crucial role as it determines the ability of a formation to follow desired paths smoothly and accurately. This study presents a framework for Mecanum-wheeled robot teams, combining quintic-polynomial waypoint generation, a virtual-structure model, an artificial potential field for tracking and obstacle avoidance. abstract: Aquifer recharge is key to the sustainable use of groundwater and to ensuring a global supply of fresh water. Since the 20th century, recharge projects have proliferated along with a variety of concepts such as AR, MAR, ASR, SAT, among others, sparking debate over their definitions. title: Genome and methylome of the root crop table beet (Beta vulgaris)
abstract: Abstract Table beet ( Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris var. vulgaris ), also known as red beet, garden beet, or beetroot, is an important crop with both nutritional and agricultural value, yet high-quality genomic resources for this taxon are limited. We present the chromosome-scale genome assembly RefTab-1 based on PacBio and Hi-C data of the inbred table beet genotype W357B. abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates the location accuracy (LA) of the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID) network by analysing lightning strikes recorded near tall structures located either on flat ground or on elevated terrain, such as mountain ridges, over a 14-year period from 2012 to 2025. title: Modelling future collapse risk of aapa mires across a boreal climate gradient
abstract: Northern peatlands provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration that mitigates climate change. Warming and land use threaten many peatlands, but a unique subclass of peatlands called aapa mires are currently listed as Least Concern in Europe. We aimed to evaluate risk for aapa mires in Finland using newly available datasets. abstract: Introduction Active school commuting (ASC) offers many health benefits yet remains underexplored in regional settings. abstract: ABSTRACT The deep decarbonization of China’s steel sector is critical for achieving national carbon neutrality and global climate goals. Existing studies on China’s steel transition often lack detailed representations of provincial heterogeneity, cross-sectoral interactions, and breakthrough technologies. This study develops an improved steel module within the Global Change Analysis Model-China (GCAM-China) to explore provincial low-carbon transition pathways for China’s steel sector. abstract: Spanning from 1750 to nearly the present day, the Carbon Dioxide Information Analysis Center fossil fuel (CDIAC-FF) dataset quantifies carbon dioxide emissions to the atmosphere by fuel type and economic sector for countries around the world. This paper updates the long-standing CDIAC-FF dataset to 2022 and includes methodological updates. abstract: This study investigates gamma irradiation-induced modification of B 4 C reinforcement and its effect on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and electrochemical corrosion behavior of Al/B 4 C composites. B 4 C micropowders irradiated at 50, 100, and 150 kGy were incorporated into aluminum sheets through accumulative roll bonding. abstract: Polyploidy is a major driver of plant evolution and speciation. Autopolyploidy, in particular, plays a key role in the emergence of cryptic lineages that are morphologically similar yet genetically and ecologically distinct. abstract: Unlike gaseous fuels, which are fully characterized by chemical composition, metal fuels also vary in particle size. This paper investigates the effect of particle size on laminar flame propagation in iron particle suspensions with oxygen–argon and oxygen–helium carrier gases. Using a McGill Bunsen-type metal-fuel burner, pure iron flames are stabilized across a broad range of fuel concentrations. title: Climatic and host‐plant drivers of continental‐scale Miridae diversity: Integrating generalized linear modelling with local spatial association analyses
abstract: Abstract Identifying the mechanisms that structure large‐scale insect diversity is central to ecological theory. Herbivorous insects are expected to respond both to direct climatic constraints and to bottom‐up regulation mediated through host‐plant diversity, yet the relative importance of these pathways at continental scales remains unresolved. This study evaluates drivers of species richness in Miridae (Hemiptera: Heteroptera) across the Nearctic region using negative binomial generalized linear models integrated with global and local spatial autocorrelation analyses. abstract: ABSTRACT Process safety should function as a formative axis of chemical engineering education rather than as an isolated topic reserved for a single elective or a late stage lecture block. abstract: Variations in landscape-scale acorn production have been studied across the Quercus genus to understand its role in ecosystem ecology and forest regeneration. Multiple weather conditions may influence annual acorn production, especially the positive influence of seasonal rainfall. Prior studies have assessed the effects of rainfall measured over monthly and seasonal scales, but have not focused on the potential influence of daily rainfall events (e.g., frequency and volume) on acorn production. abstract: Avicennia marina (Forssk.) Vierh. is an important mangrove plant with high nutritional and medicinal values, featuring saccharides as its primary bioactive compounds. title: The influence of accountability on procurement performance: a case study ministry of blue economy and fisheries Zanzibar
abstract: Accountability is a foundational pillar of procurement governance, yet quantitative evidence on how accountability mechanisms specifically shape procurement outcomes within individual government ministries in Zanzibar remains scarce. This study examined the influence of accountability on procurement performance at the Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries (MoBEF), Zanzibar. title: Eco Comics in Environmental Education: Bibliometric Mapping and Review of Elementary School Studies
abstract: Eco-comics provide visual narratives for environmental learning, but the scope of the literature and the outcomes assessed in elementary schools remain unclear. This review combines bibliometric mapping of the broader literature with a descriptive synthesis of elementary school studies. Scopus records retrieved on 1 September 2026 were screened with reference to PRISMA 2020; 135 articles were mapped bibliometrically, and six empirical elementary school studies were synthesized descriptively. title: Response-surface optimization of high-performance GO-PET-PEG forward osmosis membranes for bentazone removal
abstract: In this work, a single-layer forward osmosis (FO) nanocomposite membrane was developed and tested for bentazone removal from aqueous systems. Unlike conventional dual-layer thin-film composite membranes, this architecture, incorporating graphene oxide (GO) as a nanofiller and polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a pore-forming agent in a recycled PET matrix, eliminates interfacial defects between layers while simplifying fabrication. title: New to Science: Insect Discoveries from Long-Term Monitoring in Terrestrial Protected Areas in Abu Dhabi, UAE
abstract: In 2005, the known insect fauna of the United Arab Emirates comprised approximately 800 species. Through the Invertebrate Inventory Project, initiated by the Environment Agency-Abu Dhabi (EAD), a comprehensive inventory of insect diversity within the Emirate's protected areas has been conducted for more than two decades. title: Fire history and atmospheric drying jointly control forest reburn severity
abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire activity is increasing across western United States forests, leading to more frequent reburns, or areas that burn multiple times within short intervals (approximately two decades). Prior fire can reduce subsequent burn severity through fuel limitation, but this effect is not consistent across landscapes or climate conditions. title: Identification of Chaperonin10 as a gene necessary for tolerance to root heat stress in rice
abstract: Due to global warming, crops are exposed to heat stress more frequently. This may reduce yields, hence heat-tolerant varieties are needed. For this, it is important to identify genes governing heat tolerance. In this study we identified a line that is sensitive to high temperature in roots, and through QTL analysis we identified a gene associated with heat tolerance in rice. title: Determinants of Crop Diversification in Boro Rice‐Based, Wetland Farming Systems in Bangladesh
abstract: The haor landscape of Bangladesh is highly reliant on Boro rice cultivation, making farm households vulnerable to recurring floods and climate-related risks. Crop diversification can intensify agricultural resilience and reduce production risks. This study examined the pattern, extent, and determinants of crop diversification using a cross-sectional field survey performed in 2023 among 240 farm households in three purposively selected upazilas (Itna, Mithamoin, and Nikli) of Kishoreganj district. title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant‐ and fungal‐derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. abstract: The development of promising photocatalysts for hydrogen production is one of the most important areas of research. Enhanced efficiency can be achieved by modifying the composition and creating composite structures, thereby improving the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. title: Chloroplast Genome Characterization and Phylogenetic Implications of Reyesia and Salpiglossis (Salpiglossideae, Solanaceae)
abstract: ABSTRACT Solanaceae represents one of the most economically significant families among flowering plants. abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens apiculture by reducing floral resources, water availability, and colony productivity. Although beekeepers adopt various adaptation measures, barriers to effective adaptation remain poorly understood across different agro ecological settings. abstract: Background. Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of global infectious disease deaths. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. title: A cross-cultural study of harbour scene paintings of the Thirteen Factories in Guangzhou from 1760 to 1860
abstract: During the Canton System, the Thirteen Factories in Guangzhou formed a cross‑cultural visual field in which Harbor Scene Paintings (HSPs) served as both commodities and sites of Sino-Western visual negotiation. Drawing on visual culture studies and the pictorial turn, this study constructs a comparative cross‑cultural visual analysis framework. abstract: Abstract Voucher specimens are central to studying threatened taxa. However, errors in their locality data can distort understandings of these species’ distributions, and in extreme cases may even misguide assessments of species’ conservation statuses. The Perth slider, Lerista lineata , represents an informative exemplar of this situation. abstract: Regulating the spatial charge distribution in donor-acceptor (D-A) porous organic polymers (POPs) to suppress charge recombination remains a formidable challenge in the field of photocatalysis. abstract: The study of the degradation of archaeological objects is essential for guiding their conservation and restoration, alongside understanding possible formal and aesthetic changes that may have occurred since their burial. abstract: Gas drainage boreholes easily suffer hole wall collapse and coal particle blockage under in-situ stress and mining disturbance, drastically lowering gas extraction efficiency. abstract: The disposal of chrysotile asbestos waste poses significant environmental hazards, while heavy oil residues demand costly pretreatment to remove toxic metals and sulfur. abstract: Correlation coefficient is widely used in biomedical and biological literature. title: When seeds change hands: gender, intersectionality, and access to seed in rural Senegal
abstract: Abstract Despite advances in understanding seed circulation in rural communities, little is known about the gendered and intersectional power relations that shape farmers’ access to seed. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host-specific gut microbiota responses. abstract: Renewable energy plays a key role in the energy transition to combat climate change and, more recently, has become an important instrument for enhancing energy security. abstract: Partiendo de una visión ontológico-teológica de la creatio ex nihilo, se aborda la creación en Génesis 1 como la ordenación de un caos que también depende ontológicamente de Dios. Se argumenta que la información es crucial en el proceso creador, con la palabra divina como fuente de información constituyente. abstract: Aspergillus sclerotiorum has been identified as an entomopathogenic fungus with potential as a biological control agent, yet its cellular effects on insect hosts are not well characterized. abstract: Local food in the Mekong Delta is closely connected with the daily life of the region, and it reveals cultural identity and stories of the region. abstract: Purpose This study examines how India is positioned within the changing international trade-politics-development landscape created by geoeconomic fragmentation, energy-market uncertainty and supply-chain realignment. abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the relationship between economic development and the formation of thermal hotspots, defined as areas of geographically concentrated thermal pollution associated with fossil‐fuel use. While these processes are typically studied at the interspecific level, emerging evidence suggests that plant-soil interactions can be genotype-specific, contributing to intraspecific density dependence (iDD). abstract: Crude oil transportation in the Niger Delta requires effective thermal management to maintain flow assurance. Heat loss, wax precipitation, and increasing viscosity can restrict crude-oil flow and increase operational risks. abstract: Pandanus amaryllifolius Roxb (pandan) is a valuable aromatic industrial crop in Southeast Asia. abstract: Abstract Cyanobacterial exopolysaccharides (EPSs) are promising sustainable biopolymers, yet halotolerant strains remain comparatively underexplored and the relationships between EPS composition and functionality are still not well-defined. abstract: This study aimed to identify the underlying perceived significant dimensions of factors linked with livelihood transformation among Flue-Cured Virginia (FCV) tobacco farmers in the Northern Light Soil (NLS) region of Andhra Pradesh. Understanding these latent factors is essential for designing integrated interventions that enhance livelihood resilience. abstract: This paper advances the study of echoic language by demonstrating its greater structural complexity and functional breadth than is commonly recognized. Based on examples found in a naturally occurring exchange of comments on an online blog about the strangler fig, we analyse a text underpinning a multilayered network of echoes. abstract: Many spermicide products currently in use incorporate contraceptive detergents as their active ingredients. These substances have been shown to adversely affect normal microbiota and vaginal epithelial cells, as well as raise the risk of vaginal and cervical infections and ulcers. This study investigated the potential impacts of crude venom from the scorpion species Scorpio maurus palmatus (Smp) on the motility of human spermatozoa in vitro. The potential changes in tree resilience over time in response to the combined changes in fire regime and climate remain unknown. abstract: Abstract Background Households provide an ideal setting to study SARS-CoV-2 transmission modes due to the close proximity and extended exposure among members. abstract: Strawberry tree ( Arbutus andrachne L.) leaves represent a sustainable source of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients with considerable potential for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and functional food applications. abstract: Abstract Restoring xylem water transport function after drought is central to plant drought adaptation. abstract: Lignocellulosic energy crops are promising feedstocks for anaerobic digestion, but their biogas potential depends on biomass productivity, composition and digestibility. abstract: Curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles (Curc-AgNPs) are promising biogenic nanomaterials in medical and environmental applications. title: Land-based search and rescue training: evolution and simplification
abstract: Land-based search and rescue training in Aotearoa New Zealand has undergone substantial change, yet there has been limited examination of how these changes have affected the analytical foundations of search management. This review was undertaken to identify what concepts, tools and competencies have been retained, modified or lost in the Managing Land Search Operations course that evolved into Manage the Initial Response and Extended Search Planning. title: Labor transformation and sustainability risks in smallholder farm households: a scoping review from Indonesia
abstract: Labor transformation in smallholder farming households has become a critical yet underexplored dimension of agricultural sustainability, particularly in developing countries. This scoping review examines global research on labor transformation and its implications for agricultural sustainability, with a particular focus on Indonesia. Using the Arksey and O’Malley framework, the study integrates bibliometric analysis (VOSviewer) and thematic analysis (NVivo) to identify major research patterns and conceptual gaps in the literature. abstract: Abstract Keimeliopteridae n. fam., a new family of stem-group paraneopteran insects containing two species, Keimelioptera solensis n. gen. n. sp. and K. rara n. gen. n. sp., is described from the Upper Triassic (Norian) Cow Branch Formation of the Solite deposit in Virginia and North Carolina, USA. A phylogenetic analysis using 16 terminal taxa and 68 morphological characters recovered Keimeliopteridae outside of crown Paraneoptera (bark lice, true lice, thrips, and hemipterans), as sister to Hypoperlidae + Paraneoptera sensu stricto. abstract: ABSTRACT The production of chemical commodities from biomass via liquefaction, such as fast pyrolysis, is inherently linked to further refining and separation processes. With the latest developments to improve predictive capability of phase equilibria models for fast pyrolysis bio‐oil (FPBO), they are now being applied to describe its fundamental behavior in cases that are relevant today. abstract: Background: Costa Rica introduced universal one-dose varicella vaccination in 2007 using a one-dose schedule administered at 15 months of age through the Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS). A previous national study described epidemiological changes through 2014 by comparing pre- and post-vaccination periods; however, contemporary data on subsequent patterns and residual disease burden are limited. abstract: Earthen dams located in high mountain environments are exposed to intense environmental stresses due to strong freeze-thaw cycles that can affect material integrity. Climate change can further amplify these stresses through the increasing frequency of extreme events and natural hazards. At the same time, their remote locations and hostile environmental conditions may be challenging for monitoring instrumentation. title: Experimental Studies on the Thermal Runaway of Three Lithium-Ion Batteries Used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: Abstract With the glorious progress and applications in the field of unmanned aerial vehicles and low-altitude economy, the safe use of lithium-ion batteries in daily life has become indispensable and pivotal. It is unfortunate that there has not been any evaluation of the risk of LIBs being exposed to thermal abuse in unmanned aerial vehicles. The topic of thermal runaway of LIB used in unmanned aerial vehicles is not well-studied. title: Integrating computational fluid dynamics and field experiments to optimize mixing and irrigation strategies for biogas slurry application in Chinese yam
abstract: Maximizing the agricultural value of biogas slurry while mitigating its environmental risks requires precise blending and irrigation, yet optimized methodologies remain underdeveloped. This study employs Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) numerical simulation to analyze the fluid dynamics of three designed mixed fertilizer pipeline structures. It investigates how mixing sequence affects fertilizer blending efficiency within pipes of identical diameter. abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed shale depositional facies change rapidly and exhibit strong lithological heterogeneity, resulting in unclear controlling factors of reservoir development and hindering the identification of favourable reservoirs. Therefore, this study focuses on the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation (Es 4 ) in the northeast Bohai Bay Basin. title: Modelling leaf heat balance and thermal-neutrality conductance of urban trees for building edge planting in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India: Effects of leaf size and stomatal behaviour in a tropical monsoon climate
abstract: Leaf-to-air temperature difference (ΔT) is often read as an index of the cooling provided by trees planted along building edges. A two-sided, non-linear leaf energy balance was forced with hourly typical-day climates reconstructed from India Meteorological Department normals (1991–2020) for Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India, a hot-humid tropical monsoon (Aw) climate. title: Functional expression of heteromeric insect/human nicotinic acetylcholine receptor chimeras without accessory proteins
abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are primary targets of insecticides. While most mammalian nAChRs form functional channels in heterologous systems, insect nAChRs remain notoriously difficult to reconstitute. Here, we co-expressed insect/human subunit chimeras to enable functional analysis of heteromeric insect nAChR ligand‑binding sites in Xenopus laevis oocytes. title: Mechanics of Polyborosiloxanes across Strain Rates and Strain Amplitudes
abstract: Abstract We report a comprehensive study of the dynamic mechanical properties of polyborosiloxane (PBS) tested using uniaxial compression, shear rheometry, compression DMA, impact loading, and vibrational transmissibility on a commercially available PBS formulation. We report properties for varying orders of magnitude in strain rate and as a function of strain amplitude wherever possible to quantify performance limits of PBS for different loading cases. title: From black plates to backyard animals: Chigger communities associated with wild and domestic hosts and the environment in a rural village setting
abstract: Chigger mites (larval Trombiculidae) are obligate ectoparasites, some species transmit Orientia tsutsugamushi , the causative agent of scrub typhus. Despite their public health significance in rural Southeast Asia, relationships between chiggers infesting wildlife, domestic animals and those present in the surrounding environment remain poorly characterised. title: Study of the N-Soliton Solutions for the (2+1)-Dimensional Generalized Caudrey–Dodd–Gibbon–Kotera–Sawada Equation
abstract: This paper investigates the N-soliton solutions of the (2+1)-dimensional generalized Caudrey-Dodd-Gibbon-Kotera-Sawada equation. title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals. The regulation of biotic-abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. title: Every drop counts: optimizing water use efficiency for sustainable tomato production
abstract: Ensuring food production in the face of increasing water scarcity is one of the main challenges for sustainable agriculture worldwide. As climate change intensifies and water availability becomes increasingly limited, the adoption of strategies that enhance water use efficiency in agriculture is imperative. The objective of this study was to evaluate whether the combination of deficit irrigation and biostimulant application can maintain tomato yield while improving water and energy use efficiency, thereby contributing to more sustainable horticultural production systems. title: Effect of bacterial cellulose nanocrystal and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine incorporation on the mechanical properties of resin-modified glass ionomer cement
abstract: Background and purpose Resin-modified glass ionomer cements (RMGICs) are commonly utilized as restorative materials because of their ability to release fluoride, form chemical bonds with tooth structure, and desirable biocompatibility. Nevertheless, their comparatively low mechanical strength limits their application in regions subjected to high stress. title: Peri-Injury Stearidonic Acid Ethanolamide Modulates Astroglial Reactivity-Associated Markers in a Mouse Model of Mild Traumatic Brain Injury
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) can cause persistent neuroinflammation and astroglial reactivity. This study examined whether peri-injury administration of stearidonic acid ethanolamide (SDEA) was associated with changes in astrocyte-associated responses after mTBI and in primary astroglial cultures. title: Biochemical profile of oxidative and antioxidant changes in sheep with clinical pneumonia
abstract: This study characterized systemic oxidative and antioxidant changes in sheep with clinical pneumonia. Twenty sheep diagnosed with clinical pneumonia were compared with 20 individually matched healthy controls. Total antioxidant status (TAS), total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), paraoxonase-1 (PON1), arylesterase (ARE), total sialic acid (TSA), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) were assessed. title: Integrating land-use and climate connectivity to link protected areas at the country level
abstract: Abstract Context Ecological corridors that are high in biodiversity potential and stable under climate change are central to long-term conservation planning. Yet spatial prioritization frameworks rarely integrate land-use resistance and climate stability into a unified approach, limiting their operational value for landscape management and policy. title: Heterogeneity of child and adolescent asthma determinants across urbanization stages: a 21-year global analysis
abstract: Urbanization reshapes environmental exposures, lifestyle, and health systems, yet global evidence on how child and adolescent asthma risk factors evolve across development stages remains limited. Using panel data from 149 countries (2000–2020), this study applied clustering and coupling coordination analysis to identify stage-specific pathways of urbanization and air quality transitions. Generalized additive models were subsequently employed to explore the heterogeneity of asthma determinants across these stages. title: Multiplexed Ultrahigh-Throughput Evolution for Esterase Selectivity across a Broad Substrate Scope
abstract: Abstract Directed evolution of enzymes is generally performed toward a specific substrate, which predictably improves enzyme activity toward the probe substrate. However, it is difficult to predict whether evolved enzymes will be selective or promiscuous toward other substrates. Multiplexed directed evolution can identify enzyme variants with selectivity/promiscuity across multiple substrates, but is typically performed using plate-based screening assays that are limited to testing a few hundred mutants. title: A Fully Lithography‐Free Fabrication Strategy for Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising bioelectronic devices that leverage volumetric amplification for highly sensitive biosensing, but their fabrication typically relies on complex and costly cleanroom‐based photolithography. Despite recent efforts toward printing‐based lithography‐free OECT fabrication, achieving high operational stability remains challenging. title: Development and characterization of an Eugenol–Shilajit–Chitosan nano-gel composite with anticancer activity against oral squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for over 90% of oral malignancies and remains associated with high morbidity, recurrence, and poor long-term survival rates. To address these clinical challenges, the development of multifunctional nanotherapeutic systems capable of improving active stability and localized anticancer activity has become a vital focus in oral oncology and dental nanomedicine. abstract: Molecular self-assembly offers a powerful route to engineer sophisticated materials that mimic biological compartmentalization. Inspired by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), which drives the formation of cellular membraneless organelles, we rationally designed glycolipid-based coacervates by tuning the attractive and repulsive intermolecular interactions. title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing "impact trajectories"). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. title: Integrating social science into conservation practice: Evidence from environmental non‐governmental organization publications and practitioner perspectives
abstract: Abstract Social science is critical to conservation success, yet has not become mainstream. title: African Economic History
abstract: Abstract African economic history has experienced a revival during the 21 st century through the globalisation of economic history as a field and a growing interest in how history has shaped current economic inequalities. This survey reviews the development of the field since its initial foundations, and illustrates the ways in which more recent work has diverged in its methods and approaches. title: Updating the Coordinates of Itera Geodetic Benchmarks Based on the ITRF2020 Global Reference Frame
abstract: The International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF) is a global reference framework essential for maintaining the consistency and precision of positioning results in response to ongoing geodynamic changes. The adoption of ITRF2020 requires updates to geodetic control point coordinates to ensure compliance with international reference standards. This study aims to update the benchmark coordinates at Itera based on the ITRF2020 global reference frame. abstract: This paper reports a comprehensive physicochemical and electrical investigation of MAPb1−xBixBr3 perovskite powders (nominal x = 0 to 0.16) synthesized by antisolvent (acetone) precipitation. abstract: Rechargeable lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) are central to the clean energy transition, but their production, use, and disposal may introduce contaminants into drinking water systems. Using U.S. EPA Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR5) data, we evaluated whether ZIP codes with LiB waste activity or LiB facilities had higher lithium or per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) burdens in drinking water. abstract: Microbial pesticides are promoted as alternatives to conventional pest-control inputs, yet their use may remain limited in chemically intensive production systems. This study examined chemical-input use, microbial pesticide use, extension exposure, and reported constraints related to the transition to microbial pesticides in geographical indication (GI) pineapple production among Tha Uthen pineapple farmers in Nakhon Phanom Province, Thailand. abstract: Understanding refuelling performance at stopover sites is central to elucidating the migration strategies of passerines, particularly at Mediterranean landfall islands where birds arrive after crossing major ecological barriers. We investigated fuel deposition dynamics and potential flight range in five long‐distance migrant passerines (Great Reed Warbler, Sedge Warbler, Common Nightingale, Wood Warbler and Garden Warbler) using long‐term ringing data (2007–2024) from the Antikythera Bird Observatory, Greece. title: In the House of My Father: Kinship in the Work of Donald Rodney
abstract: Kinship is a fraught topic in the work of British artist Donald Rodney. From his earliest sketchbooks to his final exhibition, Rodney used concepts of relatedness, genealogy, and inheritance to connect his own family history with broader narratives of slavery and empire, Pan-African solidarity, and Black British identity. abstract: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of mosquito-borne viruses and threatens human health globally. To monitor temporal changes in the population genetics of Ae. aegypti in Yunnan Province, we collected specimens from five sites between 2016 and 2018 and analyzed them at nine microsatellite loci and the mitochondrial cox I gene. abstract: Abstract River cooters (Pseudemys concinna) are a novel and compelling system in which to study adaptations and trade-offs in biology teaching labs. title: Processed manures sustain silage corn yield with amendment‐specific soil and forage response
abstract: Abstract In semiarid western US dairy systems, field evidence remains limited on whether processed manure products can sustain silage corn ( Zea mays L.) productivity and improve soil health. title: The impact of resilience on psychological well-being through emotional intelligence among students at Islamic boarding schools in Kendal Regency
abstract: Psychological well-being is essential for students' positive development, particularly in Islamic boarding schools, where adolescents must adapt to academic demands, religious responsibilities, and communal living. This study aimed to examine the relationship between resilience and psychological well-being through the mediating role of emotional intelligence among Islamic boarding school students in Kendal Regency, Indonesia. title: Wood‐MOF Thermoelectrics for Heat and Power Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoelectric materials and devices enable to harvest heat energy from the environment, which offers a promising solution for addressing the critical issue of conventional fossil fuels for energy supply. However, sustainable development of low‐grade heat conversion to electricity is limited by materials and technologies. abstract: Abstract The emergence of drug resistance and the limited availability of effective therapeutics continue to hinder the treatment of protozoal diseases, highlighting the need for new chemotypes with broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. In the present study, a series of nitro and trifluoromethyl-substituted thiochromene carboxamides, previously identified as antileishmanial agents, were further explored for their broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. title: Elements in baby foods from the French market and associate health risks
abstract: Commercially prepared baby foods contribute both to the nutrient intake and dietary exposure to potentially toxic elements during early childhood. This study determined the levels of 28 major and trace elements in 97 commercially available baby foods marketed in France using microwave-assisted acid digestion, followed by ICP-MS. title: Cancer-selective cytotoxicity of a semi-synthetic derivative of oleuropein via proteostasis network impairment
abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, driving continued research for innovative therapies with enhanced specificity and efficacy. Natural products have long been recognised as a valuable source of anticancer agents due to their structural diversity and unique biological activities. Building on the anticancer potential of oleuropein, a major olive tree (Olea europaea) metabolite, we evaluated a newly synthesised semi-synthetic analogue, GS32, for its cytotoxic activity in vitro. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion owing to their well‐defined architectures, tunable porosity, and tailorable coordination environments. However, conventional MOF photocatalysts are predominantly employed as components in composite materials, and direct structural modulation of MOFs themselves to boost photocatalytic performance remains challenging. title: Dietary Supplement Use from Infancy to Adolescence in Croatia: Prevalence, Types and Associated Factors
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Although the use of dietary supplements is increasing worldwide among the pediatric population, comprehensive national data on consumption patterns in Croatia remain limited. abstract: Abstract Gusset end details are usually welded-around with fillet welds leading to high structural and notch stress concentrations. abstract: Abstract The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. abstract: ABSTRACT A pharmacological survey of Argyreia species in Vietnam was conducted to investigate their chemical constituents and biological activities. Here, we report for the first time the essential oil (EO) composition and bioactivity of Argyreia capitiformis and Argyreia nasirii . GC‐MS analysis showed marked interspecific variation. abstract: Broccoli contains abundant bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anticancer properties. title: Material concreto para la enseñanza de la factorización en estudiantes con necesidades educativas específicas no asociadas a la discapacidad
abstract: El aprendizaje de la factorización exige reconocer estructuras algebraicas y relacionar representaciones geométricas y simbólicas. El objetivo fue analizar las diferencias en el rendimiento académico de estudiantes de noveno año de Educación General Básica con necesidades educativas específicas no asociadas a la discapacidad, entre una secuencia concreto-pictórico-abstracta (CPA) con material manipulativo y una enseñanza centrada en fórmulas y procedimientos algebraicos. title: Seismotectonic Controls on the Toba–Samosir Subsurface Environment Revealed by Double-Difference Earthquake Relocation
abstract: North Sumatra is characterized by complex interactions among the Sumatran Fault System, regional subduction, and the volcanotectonic setting of the Toba Caldera, producing heterogeneous shallow crustal seismicity and structurally controlled subsurface environments. This study investigates the seismotectonic and subsurface structural characteristics of North Sumatra using double-difference earthquake relocation, with particular emphasis on the Toba–Samosir region. title: Longitudinal fecal cortisol metabolite concentrations across the transition period in multiparous dairy cows under commercial conditions
abstract: Abstract This longitudinal observational field study characterized fecal cortisol metabolite (FCM) concentrations across the transition period in multiparous Holstein-Friesian dairy cows under commercial conditions. The dataset comprised 38 clinically healthy cows from four farms, with 19 sampled in winter and 19 different cows in summer. Each cow was sampled at 1 month and 1 week before parturition and 1 week and 1 month after parturition, yielding 152 observations. title: Indoor temperature and office work performance in a temperate climate
abstract: The relationship between indoor temperature and office work performance (OWP) remains contested. Previous laboratory studies, including a controlled experiment in Singapore, report limited or no effects within typical office ranges, but replication across climatic contexts is needed to assess generalizability. The present study was conducted in the temperate climate of the San Francisco Bay Area, closely replicating the Singapore protocol with a 30% larger sample: 75 participants completed four 165-min sessions at 21, 23, 25, and 27°C in a controlled environmental chamber. title: The Longitudinal Association Between Students’ Extrinsic–Dynamic Spatial Ability and Achievement in Science Education in Elementary School: A Random‐Intercept Cross‐Lagged Panel Model
abstract: Research has shown that extrinsic-dynamic spatial ability is relevant to achievement in science education. However, the direction of the relationship between extrinsic-dynamic spatial ability and achievement remains unclear; this issue was thus addressed in a longitudinal study. Fourth graders (N = 335) from Hong Kong were assessed on these two constructs three times, at 4-month intervals; control variables were also included during the first assessment. title: Knockdown of Smurf1 Promotes Autophagy‐Dependent Ferroptosis in Acute Liver Failure by Inhibiting Ubiquitin‐Mediated Ulk1 Degradation
abstract: Treating acute liver failure (ALF) relies on rescuing dying hepatocytes and restoring liver regeneration. Ferroptosis contributes to ALF development, so regulating iron homeostasis or lipid peroxide production may be an effective treatment strategy. Ubiquitination can modify ferroptosis and is involved in liver diseases. The study aims to explore the mechanism of E3 ubiquitin ligase Smurf1 regulating ferroptosis in acute liver failure. title: Designing Embodied Citizenship: Paradoxes of Decolonization in the Making of an “Indian” Regime of Clothing Size Standards
abstract: ABSTRACT This article critically examines INDIAsize—an Indian government–funded anthropometric initiative to “decolonize” body size standards used in clothing production. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted in New Delhi between 2020 and 2024, I demonstrate how body size research and design standards–making processes become sites for negotiating ideologies of citizenship and belonging in postcolonial contexts. title: Senior elite swimmers were top-10% youths: A Swedish population cohort study
abstract: We evaluated how well swimming performance at ages 13–15 identified future senior elite status (ages 22–25) in a non-selected national cohort. Using the Swedish federation’s Tempus Open database, we followed 8,965 Swedish-developed swimmers born 1995–2001. Each swimmer’s youth performance was summarized as the maximum within-cohort percentile across ages, events, and pool lengths; the resulting top-10%-in-any-cell filter retained approximately 19% of the cohort. title: Mangrove-Derived Halotolerant Endophytic Bacteria Confer Strain-Specific and Consortium-Mediated Salt Tolerance in Peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.)
abstract: Soil salinity is a major abiotic stress that severely limits crop productivity worldwide. This study evaluated the potential of halotolerant endophytes isolated from mangrove plants to enhance salinity tolerance in the peanut (Arachis hypogaea L. cv. JL24). A two-step approach, including screening and validation methods, was applied. Initially, six mangrove endophytes, ACR52, EAR173, EAR191, EAR195, EAL318, and ACL463, were tested for their capacity to colonize the non-host peanut. title: Drought and Water Stress Analysis in the Kaman Region (Kırşehir, Türkiye) Using Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2A Data
abstract: This study evaluates vegetation dynamics and drought conditions in the semi-arid agricultural landscapes of Kaman (Türkiye) using integrated remote sensing data. NDVI and NDMI derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2, together with land surface temperature (LST) and Sentinel-1 soil moisture, were analyzed to assess vegetation–environment interactions. NDVI time-series analysis revealed a clear seasonal phenological cycle, with peak vegetation growth in spring and a marked decline during summer due to increased temperature and reduced moisture availability. abstract: Seafarer clinics prossess complex data governance characteristics due to the requirement to comply with international maritime organization (IMO) international standards and the obligation to integrate national data with the manistry of health of the republic of Indonesia’s SATUSEHAT platform. title: The Role of ICT in MENA Environmental Sustainability: A Panel GMM Approach
abstract: Climate change poses a major threat to environmental sustainability worldwide, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, which faces rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, and air pollution. The role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in environmental sustainability remains debated, as studies report both positive and negative effects. This study investigates the impact of ICT, education, GDP per capita, and tourism on environmental sustainability in selected MENA countries from 2015 to 2020. Annual data were obtained from the World Development Indicators

title: Evaluation of sustainability of lubricants by life cycle assessment and carbon footprint measurement
abstract: The global increasing awareness of sustainability has greatly affected the traditional lubricant market. The goals to reduce environmental pollution have increased the use of biolubricants rather petroleum based ones significantly due to several harmful impacts of the later including non-biodegradability, higher carbon emissions and bio-toxic wastes. In this review, a comparative analysis of biolubricants (soybean and rapeseed oils lubricants) with mineral and synthetic lubricants was performed with respect to their life cycle assessment (LCA) and carbon footprint (CFP) measurement. title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles.
