title: Open Educational Resources as Enabling Conditions for Student Resilience to Failure and Uncertainty
abstract: As today's scientific challenges become increasingly complex and interdisciplinary, future researchers in the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) need both disciplinary skills and adaptive resilience to persevere and cope productively with failure. We argue that Open Educational Resources (OER) provide the enabling conditions for this resilience. OER are freely accessible and openly licensed materials that can be reused, adapted, and redistributed without cost barriers. title: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells-derived exosomes ameliorate doxorubicin-induced nephrotoxicity via the modulation of pyroptosis-associated signaling
abstract: Abstract Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical application is constrained by nephrotoxicity, with no therapeutic interventions currently available. This study aimed to delineate the ameliorative potential of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) derived exosomes (EXO) in an experimental model of DOX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). Twenty-four rats were divided into 4 groups: Control, DOX intoxicated, DOX + EXO, and EXO only groups. title: Prohibitive Effects of ω‐3 on Pancreatic Damage in an Experimental Diabetes Model: Blood Glucose, Insulin, Lipid Profiles, Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Pancreatic Tissue Morphology, and Apoptotic Pathways
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of Omega-3 (ω-3) against damage to pancreatic tissue in rats with experimentally induced diabetes using streptozotocin. Twenty-eight male Wistar Albino rats were divided into four groups: Control, Diabetes Mellitus (DM), ω-3, and DM + ω-3, with seven rats in each group. STZ was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) into the DM group, and blood glucose levels were measured on the fourth day after injection. title: Investigations on the morphological and thermophysical characteristics of graphene oxide incorporated sodium nitrate for high-temperature thermal energy storage applications
abstract: Abstract Sodium nitrate (SN) is a promising molten salt phase change material with high energy storage capacity and thermal stability for high-temperature latent heat thermal energy storage systems. To address the low thermal conductivity of SN, we have incorporated graphene oxide (GO) (0.5-2 wt%) as a nanoadditive and evaluated the variation of thermophysical properties of SN. The structural and functional characteristics of graphene oxide – sodium nitrate (GO-SN) composites were studied using TEM, XRD, FT-IR, and Raman spectroscopy. title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. title: Measuring circular economy performance in the EU: evidence from an FAHP-weighted composite index
abstract: Assessing circular economy (CE) performance across EU countries remains challenging due to the scarcity of country-level composite measures and uncertainty surrounding indicator importance. This study develops a circular economy index aligned with the EU Circular Economy Monitoring Framework. Expert judgments (n = 7) were collected through pairwise comparisons and translated into pillar and indicator weights using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP). title: Comparative Study of Moses in the Qur’an and the Bible: Narrative Differences, Theological Construction, and Historical Context
abstract: This article compares the narratives of Moses in the Qur'an and the Bible and explores ‘thinking beyond the narratives.’ Existing comparative studies often focus only on identifying similarities and differences. This research aims to address this gap by asking why such variations and similarities exist and what their theological implications are. Using a qualitative, critical-comparative analysis method that combines narratological, comparative theological, and historical-critical approaches, this study examines key episodes, such as the Golden Calf incident and the drowning of Pharaoh. title: Trading the Globe’s Flora from the German Provinces: The Unio Itineraria in Esslingen, 1827-1845
abstract: Abstract In the first half of the nineteenth century, a scientific society called the Unio Itineraria was formed in Esslingen, a small town near Stuttgart in what was then the German states. Operating as a joint-stock company for the collection, sale, and distribution of botanical specimens, it became well-known and well-respected as a mechanism to acquire plants from around the world in Europe. title: Full-scale fatigue and burst testing of girth-welded steel pipe under combined internal pressure and bending has consequences for pressure safety margins
abstract: Abstract The strategic role of hydrocarbon transmission pipelines is unquestionable today. This role can be interpreted within a country, but also between neighbouring countries, or within larger regions, continents and between continents. An incident on such a pipeline can therefore cause disruption both within a country and beyond, in wider regions. The critical elements of high-pressure gas transmission pipelines are often the girth welds. title: Exploring Potential EGFR Inhibitors from Isodon Serra Phytochemicals: Molecular Docking, Dynamics, and ADMET Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), a key oncogenic driver in various cancers, particularly non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), was selected as the molecular target for this investigation. A validated molecular docking protocol was employed using AutoDock Vina, with re‐docking of the co‐crystallized ligand (PDB ID: 1M17) yielding an RMSD of 1.4095 Å, confirming reliability. title: Structural, Mechanical, Thermal, and Preliminary Biological Characterization of Cymbopogon citratus Leaf Fibers for Sustainable Material Applications
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable bio-based materials has increased interest in underutilized plant fibers as environmentally friendly alternatives for engineering applications. In this study, Cymbopogon citratus (lemongrass) leaf fibers were extracted using an eco-friendly water-retting process and characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), tensile testing, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), antibacterial assays, and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). abstract: Microwave plasma is considered a crucial engineering technology and an effective method for preparing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with controllable properties, thereby opening up numerous possibilities for their application in environmental remediation and water treatment technologies.The structural and optical characteristics of the prepared AgNPs, as well as their photocatalytic activity toward methylene blue dye degradation, were investigated.AgNPs were prepared using a microwave plasma system at operating voltages of 150, 160, and 170 V. title: Hydroclimatic variability and threshold responses of cereal production to drought in Somalia, 2001–2025
abstract: Somalia’s drought is conventionally read as a drying and warming trend that erodes food production. This study asks whether the decisive change lies in the variance rather than the mean, and how cereal production responds. Monthly Combined Drought Index values for 73 districts are joined to seasonal production of maize and sorghum, the two staple cereals, for 45 crop growing districts from 2001 to 2025, then analysed with trend and variance tests, panel fixed effects and a threshold regression. title: “I Have Nothing Left in the Tank”: Parental Burnout‐Relevant Experiences Amid Climate Change
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To explore how parents describe climate‐related depletion in the parenting role and how a parental‐burnout framework can inform its interpretation. Background Climate conversations can place emotion‐regulation demands on parents, including managing a child's distress while containing their own and reassuring without credible closure. Yet how parents experience these demands remains underexplored. title: Subsidence inversions – the surface water vapour thief
abstract: Abstract A deep anticyclonic subsidence inversion reached near‐surface levels over southern England on 25 April 2026, resulting in relative humidity levels falling below 15% widely and sub‐10% in the Reading and Wokingham area. Such low levels in lowland England have very few historical precedents within the last century or more. Furthermore, careful analysis of the automatic weather station psychrometer records from the University of Reading Atmospheric Observatory on this occasion suggests that the relative humidity here may have fallen briefly below 6%.

title: Irrigation and microbial fertilizer synergistically improved the substrate health status and water and fertilizer use efficiency of facility Chinese cabbage
abstract: Improper irrigation and fertilization in facility substrate cultivation can lead to substrate degradation and inefficient use of water and fertilizer resources, thereby constraining high-quality and sustainable production of vegetables. This study investigated Chinese cabbage grown in facility substrate cultivation, with three irrigation levels (W 1 : 90% of substrate maximum water holding capacity (WHC), W 2 : 70% WHC, and W 3 : 50% WHC) and microbial fertilizer application levels (F 1 : 3.75 t·ha⁻¹, F 2 : 3.00 t·ha⁻¹, F 3 : 2.25 t·ha⁻¹), to evaluate the effects of different water–fertilizer

title: Charge-Driven Engineering of Titanium Implants with Chitosan and Poly- l -Lysine for Dual Antiadhesive and Anticorrosive Functionality
abstract: Abstract Peri-implant infections remain a major cause of implant failure, motivating the development of multifunctional titanium surfaces capable of preventing bacterial colonization while preserving implant performance. Herein, a chitosan/poly-l-lysine (CH-PLL) bilayer coating was engineered on hydroxyl-rich titanium surfaces generated by hydrothermal treatment (HT) or plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO). title: Development of Contextual-Based Physics Learning Modules Inquiry and Learning Management System to Improve Students' Self-Regulation and Digital Literacy
abstract: This study aims to develop and validate a physics learning module based on a contextual inquiry approach assisted by a Learning Management System (LMS) that is valid, practical, and effective in improving the self-regulation skills and digital literacy of high school students. The research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model which is limited to the Implementation and Evaluation stage. title: Development and validation of a low-cost, wearable near-infrared spectroscopy system for quantifying tissue water fraction in the human brain
abstract: Significance: Cerebral water fraction is physiologically relevant to brain fluid dynamics, glymphatic function, cerebral edema, and dehydration, yet it is not routinely measured in wearable neuroimaging. Aim: We aimed to develop and validate a low-cost, wearable, light-emitting diode (LED)-based continuous-wave near-infrared spectroscopy system capable of concurrently monitoring changes in cerebral hemoglobin concentration and water fraction from the forehead. title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. title: Clonality in European black poplar conservation units using genomics
abstract: Aim of study: We performed a fine scale characterization of two European black poplar (Populus nigra) in situ conservation units, using a large sample of individuals and a comprehensive set of genetic markers. This information is pivotal to understand the population dynamics of the units for implementing conservation and management plans. Area of study: We studied two populations with distinct environments and management practices in Spain and Austria. Material and methods: We genotyped 500 adults and 250 juveniles within each population using 13K single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers.
institutions: Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria

title: Biotechnological potential of aquatic hyphomycetes: a review
abstract: Aquatic hyphomycetes are an ecological group of anamorphic fungi that play an essential role in decomposing plant substrates in lotic environments. This narrative review compiled studies highlighting the biotechnological potential of this group, contributing to the understanding of its applications and perspectives. The analysis emphasizes aquatic hyphomycetes as significant producers of metabolites with applications across various sectors, including industrial, agricultural, environmental, and health sectors. title: A lncRNA–miRNA axis regulates the balance between proliferative and invasive states in melanoma
abstract: Abstract Melanoma is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by significant phenotypic plasticity, allowing tumor cells to transit between different phenotypic states. This process, known as phenotype switching, drives metastasis and therapeutic resistance. While the primary transcriptional markers defining these states are well-established, the non-coding regulatory networks that stabilize these phenotypes remain incompletely understood. title: Network centrality position shapes urban innovation capacities: evidence from China’s interlocking corporate network
abstract: Understanding how cities function as innovation incubators within increasingly interconnected economies is crucial for sustainable development. This study investigates how a city’s centrality within an enterprise-derived network shapes its technological innovation capabilities and underlying mechanisms. We construct an interlocking network model based on extensive corporate linkage data for Chinese cities. institutions: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

title: Seroprevalence, Risk Factors, and Farmer’s Knowledge and Practices on Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia in Morogoro Rural District, Tanzania
abstract: Background: Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP), a highly contagious disease of cattle, is a major constraint to cattle production in Tanzania. Purpose: This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of CBPP, identify animal and herd level risk factors of the disease, and assess the knowledge and practices (KP) of cattle farmers regarding CBPP. Method: Data were collected from August to November 2025 through a cross sectional study involving three cattle production systems; pastoral, agropastoral, and ranching. title: The genetic landscape of RAG deficiency: Novel and founder variants in a large Algerian cohort
abstract: RAG1/RAG2 deficiency causes diverse SCID phenotypes, but large, systematically characterized cohorts from North Africa remain lacking. We retrospectively characterized 128 confirmed RAG1/RAG2-deficient patients diagnosed over 14 years in Algeria, classified per PIDTC 2022 criteria. Consanguinity was high (70.3%), with RAG2 (57.0%) outnumbering RAG1 (43.0%), a reversal of patterns reported elsewhere. Classical SCID (61.0%) and Omenn syndrome (23.4%) predominated. title: Bremachlorin-Based Photodynamic-Therapy-Induced Effects in Low-Oxygenated Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) Tumor Microenvironment
abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a minimally invasive treatment whose efficacy is strongly influenced by tumor oxygenation and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by severe hypoxia, dense stroma, and immune suppression, limiting therapeutic responsiveness. In this study, we investigated how Bremachlorin-based PDT remodels the TME in two murine PDAC models with distinct immune phenotypes (T-cell–high and T-cell–low) and compared them with the immunogenic MC38 colon carcinoma model. abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO 2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. title: Design and performance analysis of reset-based active disturbance rejection control
abstract: To address the inherent trade-off between transient performance and noise robustness of the traditional linear extended state observer (LESO) within the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) framework, a novel reset extended state observer (RESO) scheme is proposed. Its core idea is to introduce a state correction mechanism regulated by the reset gain matrix into the LESO, which can maintain structural simplicity to the greatest extent. title: Performance evaluation of a biomass-fired parallel-flow tray dryer for orthodox black tea processing
abstract: The uniform and efficient drying process is still a big problem in the decentralized orthodox tea industry, especially in the field of using cost-effective and eco-friendly thermal drying equipment. In this study, an experimental evaluation of a biomass-fired parallel-flow tray dryer with 15° inclined airflow-guiding plates was conducted to explore the drying performance, moisture uniformity, and energy-efficiency for the drying system. title: SCIN Overexpression Attenuates LPS-Induced Apoptosis and Differentially Modulates EGFR Abundance and Phosphorylation in Human Oral Keratinocytes
abstract: Background: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory and immune-mediated oral mucosal disease characterized by epithelial damage, basal cell degeneration, and recurrent lesions. However, the molecular mechanisms responsible for keratinocyte injury and apoptosis during OLP progression remain incompletely understood. title: Sound advice: A calibration framework for defining detection space in passive acoustic monitoring
abstract: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a transformative tool for biodiversity assessment in recent years. Despite widespread acceptance and application for conservation-related outcomes, the interactive effects of hardware limitations, signal propagation, and environmental conditions on how far a signal can be reliably detected remain critically understudied. Such studies in regions of high biodiversity such as the Western Ghats of India, can bolster ongoing monitoring of conservation efforts. title: Green synthesis and characterization of Bi₂O₃ nanoparticles using Cuminum cyminum seed for antimicrobial and cytotoxic evaluation
abstract: Green synthesis provides an alternative to traditional chemical processes of nanomaterials preparation, which is cost-effective and environmentally benign. This paper has demonstrated synthesis of bismuth oxide nanoparticles (Bi 2 O 3 NPs) using Cuminum cyminum seed extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent of bismuth nitrate precursor. The formation of nanoparticles was first signaled by a change of color of reaction mixture to be visible and subsequent analysis by physicochemical characterization. title: Design and Analysis of a Bending–Torsion Coupled Bio-Inspired Claw Attachment Mechanism for Variable-Diameter Curved Surfaces
abstract: Reliable aerial perching on variable-diameter curved surfaces requires both sufficient grasping preload and conformal interfacial contact, whereas conventional underactuated bird-claw-inspired mechanisms primarily accommodate in-plane geometric variations and therefore have limited adaptability to surfaces with spatially varying curvature. This study presents a bending-torsion coupled bird-claw-inspired attachment mechanism for variable-diameter curved surfaces. title: Waterborne eDNA metabarcoding of the upper Llano River watershed (Texas, USA) detects regionally unreported green plant taxa
abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) represents a promising tool for documenting biological diversity in locales where intensive field surveys are challenging, as in the case of west-central Texas. Its utility is amplified in lotic systems, which can transport eDNA several kilometers from its source and often contain signals from both aquatic and nearby terrestrial organisms. title: Multi‑omics integration identifies key microbial taxa, metabolites, and genes associated with intramuscular fat deposition in Danzhou chickens
abstract: ABSTRACT Intramuscular fat (IMF) content is a major determinant of meat quality, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying its deposition remain poorly understood, particularly in indigenous chicken breeds. In this study, an extreme phenotype grouping strategy was adopted. The application of biopolymer–surfactant complexes composed of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acids) and cationic lipids as barrier coatings resolves these issues. abstract: Abstract. Aerosol hygroscopicity is a key property governing aerosol water uptake and aerosol–cloud interactions, yet the hygroscopicity of organic aerosol (OA) remains poorly constrained because of its chemical complexity and diverse emission sources. title: Effects of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-d) on the liver and kidney of Tropidurus torquatus (Squamata, Tropiduridae)
abstract: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is widely used in tropical agriculture, yet its effects on non-target ectothermic vertebrates remain poorly understood. This study assessed the subchronic toxicological impact of 2,4-D on the liver and kidneys of Tropidurus torquatus, a neotropical lizard commonly found in agricultural areas. Seventeen adult males were divided into control (n = 9) and treatment (n = 8) groups. abstract: Abstract Context Termites, like other pattern-generating organisms, often create vegetation heterogeneity. The vegetation and nutrient profiles of termite mounds shape local distributions of biodiversity. Yet, little is known about how termite mounds’ effects scale to shape landscape-level biodiversity distributions. Objectives We investigated how termite mounds influence bird distributions at the species and community levels within and across three ecosystems in a human-modified African savanna landscape. abstract: The trophic interactions between plants, insect herbivores and their predators are complex and prone to trophic cascades. Theory predicts that predators increase plant biomass by feeding on herbivores. However, it remains unclear whether different types of predators regulate herbivores to the same degree, and how intraguild predation impacts these trophic interactions. abstract: ABSTRACT The cosmetics industry faces increasing pressure to integrate upcycled agro‐food by‐products, yet consumer adoption remains constrained by contamination concerns that are strongest for products applied directly to the body. Linear attitudinal models offer limited insight into how meaning is constructed around novel “waste‐derived” claims. title: Pressure Gradient Enhanced Air Sparging for VOC ‐Contaminated Soils: Evaluation in a Three‐Dimensional Laboratory Model
abstract: Abstract This study presents a pressure gradient enhanced air sparging (PGEAS) approach that intensifies local pressure gradients and airflow in contaminated soils. Three‐dimensional laboratory model tests evaluated emitted gaseous contaminant concentrations, residual contaminant distributions, total removal efficiency, and effective removal zones in low‐ and high‐permeability soils. abstract: ) represents a rare and critically endangered subspecies endemic to the Afromontane forests of Kenya. This study investigated the seasonal dietary composition of the mountain bongo at the Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy and the Mawingu Mountain Bongo Sanctuary. We conducted a two-year observational study on the reintroduced wild population, employing random focal animal sampling at 30-min intervals during active feeding periods from 06:00 to 11:00 and 16:00 to 19:00. abstract: The flame propagation behaviour of NH 3 /H 2 mixtures at intermediate pressures is still not well understood, despite the growing interest in ammonia (NH 3 ) as a carbon-free energy carrier. abstract: Abstract Diffuse sources and resulting surface water quality impairments are major challenges for achieving advanced environmental goals as formulated in the EU Water Framework Directive or in the Zero Pollution Ambition of the European Green Deal. However, the effectiveness of legal and practical interventions is to date insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract Background Weight regain affects most individuals attempting to treat obesity and its comorbidities, and it is associated with increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. Several strategies have been proposed to induce weight loss, including caloric restriction (CCR), diet replacement (DR) and alternate-day fasting (ADF). abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effect of exposure to direct sunlight and its main components, i.e. visible (VIS) radiation and long-wavelength UV-A (UV-A1; 350–400 nm) radiation, on the photosynthetic performance of two mat-forming epigeic lichens Cetraria aculeata (melanic species with light-absorbing cortex) and Cladonia uncialis (usnic species with light-reflecting cortex). title: Molecular Interactions of Secondary Organic Aerosol With Evolving Convective Clouds
abstract: Abstract Given the complex nature of secondary organic aerosols (SOA), knowledge of their interactions with clouds is highly limited. In this study, we developed a molecular‐level cloud parcel model, CSVA‐cloud. A key feature is its unified microphysical framework for gas‐particle partitioning of water and organic molecules. title: Implications of informal settlement characteristics for household water and sanitation services in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya
abstract: Informal settlements are commonly characterized by concentrated populations, inadequate infrastructure and poor living conditions that may constrain household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. Anchored on Urban Political Ecology (UPE) theory, this study examined the implications of informal settlement characteristics for household WASH services in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya. title: Development of a noninvasive video-oculography setup for determining VOR presence in a severe vestibular impairment mouse model
abstract: The vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), which stabilizes gaze during head movement, serves as a key indicator of vestibular integrity. Conventional systems for VOR measurement in mice often require invasive head fixation, posing risks to animal welfare and experimental reproducibility. In this study, we developed and validated a noninvasive immobilization setup for detecting the presence of VOR responses in a severe vestibular impairment mouse model, offering a welfare-oriented alternative to surgically fixed systems. title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Non-classical monocytes and VCAM-1 + synovial fibroblasts were lower at peak arthritis while pro-resolution MerTK + CD206 + macrophages were increased at resolution onset. abstract: Abstract Insect‑damaged barley seeds typically exhibit poor germination and are often discarded. This study investigated whether dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) cold plasma could improve the germination of partially viable seeds of barley seeds severely damaged by Sitophilus oryzae , to our knowledge, no study has been conducted in this area. title: Environmental risk, natural disasters, and economic growth management in Indonesia: A satellite-based analysis
abstract: This study examines how environmental risk and natural disasters affect economic performance in a disaster-prone emerging economy. It focuses on the short-run and long-run impacts of flood exposure, forest loss, and spatial economic expansion on Indonesia’s economic growth, with implications for investment stability and growth management. The study integrates satellite-based indicators of flood exposure, forest loss, and night-time light intensity with national time-series macroeconomic data for Indonesia over the period 1960–2024. title: Pollen‐Derived Paper for Sustainable Droplet Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Harvesting electricity from raindrops offers a promising route toward distributed self‐powered electronics, but conventional devices rely predominantly on non‐renewable synthetic polymers and metals. Here, we report a pollen‐derived droplet energy harvester (PDEH) fabricated from abundant sunflower pollen. Defatting and mild de‐esterification convert rigid pollen grains into processable microgels that form free‐standing paper. title: Transcriptional and ultrastructural analysis of a pigmentation polymorphism in frog eggs
abstract: Melanin synthesis in gametes is exceptionally rare among vertebrates. Among amphibians, egg pigmentation patterns range from unpigmented or subtly melanic eggs, such as in foam-nesting frogs to the heavily pigmented eggs known from some poison frogs and salamanders. This diversity is hypothesized to improve the survivability of externally developing embryos through camouflage, temperature regulation, or protection from UV-induced DNA damage. title: A Review of Dynamic Stall Mitigation Using Active, Passive, and Bio-inspired Flow Control Techniques
abstract: Abstract Dynamic stall is a highly unsteady aerodynamic problem that restricts the performance of pitching airfoils used in helicopters, wind turbines, and UAVs. Effective suppression of dynamic stall is crucial for improving aerodynamic efficiency, structural stability, and energy output. Several flow techniques have been developed in the past decade to mitigate dynamic stall, but a thorough assessment of their capabilities, limitations and potential remains limited. title: National assessment of trauma care system capacity in Ecuador: Evaluating institutional resources and practitioner KAPS domains
abstract: We evaluated Ecuador's trauma care system capacity by analyzing the discrepancy between hospital infrastructure and the individual dimensions of the Knowledge, Attitudes, Practices, and Safety (KAPS) framework among medical specialists. A nationwide, multicomponent cross-sectional study was conducted (2025-2026), comprising a complete structural audit of 49 eligible public hospitals (Levels II and III) and a KAPS survey of 215 trauma-facing specialists representing 36 institutions (73.5% institutional participation rate). title: Economic lock-in and local environmental justice in plastic-waste-fuelled tofu production in East Java, Indonesia
abstract: Background Plastic-containing waste provides low-cost process energy for small producers but creates environmental-health concerns for workers and nearby communities. Small tofu enterprises may rely on these fuels when cleaner alternatives remain financially or operationally inaccessible. This study examined East Java tofu production through environmental-justice perspectives, focusing on risks, affordability, livelihoods, and local governance.Methods An exploratory mixed-method rapid assessment included 150 tofu workers, three community leaders, and three local authority representatives. abstract: The genus Ferula (Apiaceae) is widely distributed across Central and Southwest Asia and is recognized for its diverse secondary metabolites and traditional medicinal uses. However, the phytochemical composition of Ferula songarica and Ferula foetida from Kazakhstan remains poorly explored. In this study, UHPLC–ESI–MS/MS-based metabolite profiling coupled with in silico annotation was applied to characterize methanolic extracts of F. songarica and F. foetida. title: Analysis of dynamic revenue models in logistics delivery service companies
abstract: Delivery service companies in Indonesia face a decline in the number of shipments due to the large number of competitors and uncompetitive shipping price offers. This condition automatically affects the revenue received by the company. This study aims to analyze the mechanism of the relationship between tariff setting and the revenue performance of courier service companies and evaluate the behavior of revenue and profits in various tariff scenarios and demand conditions. title: Changes in Long‐Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study
abstract: AIM: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk. abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. abstract: Summary In fluctuating environments, the kinetics of stomatal opening and closing influence the balance between carbon gain and water loss. Smaller guard cells may respond faster to fluctuating environmental conditions because of their greater surface area for osmolyte flux relative to cell volume. abstract: El presente artículo desarrolla una herramienta metodológica para evaluar la vulnerabilidad de los bienes patrimoniales y los espacios museográficos ante el riesgo de inundación, aplicada como estudio de caso en el Museo de Antioquia (Medellín, Colombia). title: Effects of B fertilization on biomass production and wood quality of young Corymbia citriodora subsp. variegata plantations
abstract: Boron (B) is a micronutrient closely linked to tree productivity and stem quality in eucalyptus, with important implications for industrial wood utilization. However, the field response of Corymbia citriodora subsp. variegata (CCV) to B fertilization remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of B application rates on wood volume, aboveground biomass, nutritional status, nutrient use efficiency, stem morphology, specific leaf area (SLA), leaf area index (LAI), stem architectural defects, wood basic density, and chemical composition in a young CCV plantation. title: Broken Power-law Distributions of Photospheric Magnetic Concentrations and Implications for Solar Dynamo
abstract: Abstract Photospheric magnetic concentrations (MCs) are a direct manifestation of the solar dynamos that govern the solar magnetic field evolution and solar cycles. abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. title: Design and fabrication of functionally graded 3D polymeric scaffolds for simultaneous cell support and localized MicroRNA delivery
abstract: Scaffolds have proven useful as matrices for cell culture, tissue ingrowth, organ formation, mechanical support, drug screening platforms, and localized delivery systems. Their performance depends on multiple structural and material properties that determine their suitability for specific applications. title: Multi-omics characterization of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum MUM8-1A from Thai fermented beef sausage: Probiotic traits and safety
abstract: Traditional fermented foods are valuable sources of novel probiotic candidates with strain-specific functional properties. In this study, strain MUM8-1A, isolated from mum wua , a traditional Thai fermented beef sausage from Khon Kaen Province, Thailand, was characterized using integrated phenotypic, genome-based, and untargeted metabolomic approaches. title: Evaluating social outcomes of urban bat citizen science: A case study of public knowledge, attitudes, and nature connectedness
abstract: Abstract Citizen science is widely used in biodiversity monitoring, yet its application to bats remains limited, particularly regarding how participation influences public understanding and support for conservation. This study examined short‐term changes in ecological knowledge, attitudes toward bats, and connection to nature following participation in a bat‐focused citizen science program. title: Whole genome sequencing, assembly, and functional annotation of Hyphopichia burtonii Y951 isolated from Vitis vinifera L. cv Cabernet Sauvignon grape must
abstract: Hyphopichia burtonii is a non-conventional yeast present in diverse environments including bread, cured meat, grape must, zebra dove droppings and corn weevil. Strains derived from different environments display different traits. However, limited information exists on the genomic diversity of this species. Here we present the genome of H. burtonii Y951 strain isolated from grape must and proven to have antifungal activity against various grapevine fungal pathogens. abstract: Abstract Springtime haze in the intensive agricultural regions of Northeast China is closely associated with large‐scale open biomass burning (OBB), yet the resulting chemical evolution remains poorly understood. Based on the field campaign utilizing a High‐Resolution Time‐of‐Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer (HR‐ToF‐AMS) in Harbin during 2022, we identified OBB as the primary driver of intense haze episodes, characterized by sharp increases in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) and synergistic surges in associated inorganic species. title: Biomimetic Nanoparticles With Overexpressed Adhesion Proteins for Targeted Delivery of Gambogic Acid in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Cancer cell membrane coating offers a promising strategy for targeted drug delivery, yet its homotypic targeting mechanism and optimization remain insufficiently understood. This study identifies epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM), rather than Galectin-3, as the pivotal mediator of homologous uptake in hepatocellular carcinoma. title: Surgical delay is not associated with increased mortality in Greenlandic hip fracture patients: a 5-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Hip fractures are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Guidelines recommend surgery within 24 h, but Greenland’s vast geography and Arctic weather often delay surgical treatment. Our aims were (1) to describe the time until surgery among hip fracture patients in Greenland and (2) to evaluate its association with 30-day and 1-year mortality. title: Estimating the urban heat island effect with lichens and bryophytes: a citizen science protocol
abstract: The urban heat island effect (UHI), whereby urban areas are warmer than the surrounding rural areas, has become an increasing threat to human health and affects biodiversity. Counteracting this public health concern requires large-scale monitoring of urban heat. One cost-effective way to obtain this data is by using bioindicators, such as lichens and bryophytes. abstract: Upcycling recycled polycarbonate (rPC) into higher-value engineering blends remains challenging because recycling-induced chain scission compromises toughness and melt integrity. abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) is a vital nutrient for plant growth and development, making it essential for sustaining agriculture as human colonies are established in space. However, there is limited knowledge of native P forms and of the interaction between applied P and the lunar or Martian regolith. This highlights the need to examine how this essential nutrient interacts with the regolith for sustainable P management. title: Interactive effects of drug use and social vulnerability on health outcomes among street involved youth in a prospective cohort study from Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Background/objectives Street-involved youth experience overlapping behavioral and structural vulnerabilities that increase the risk of adverse health outcomes. However, longitudinal evidence examining whether social vulnerability modifies the health effects of drug use remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. This study investigated the independent and interactive effects of drug use and social vulnerability on adverse health outcomes among street-involved youth in urban Indonesia. abstract: Summary Atmospheric CO 2 is rising at unprecedented rates. While its physiological effects on plants are well‐documented, the direct evolutionary impact on plant pathogens remains unknown. We investigated how CO 2 interacts with other abiotic factors to shape the evolutionary potential of pathogens. We combined controlled CO 2 gradient experiments with quantitative genetics to assess the interactive effects of CO 2 , temperature and geography on Phytophthora infestans . abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). title: Current Trends in the Application of Monolithic Catalysts in Environmentally Friendly Technologies for Autonomous Heat Supply and Post Combustion Emission Control: A Mini Review
abstract: Several approaches aimed at the development of catalytic packages based on ceramic and metal monolithic materials are reported and discussed in this paper. These approaches are intended for heat-generating devices and exhaust gas purification systems where high efficiency and environmental reliability are required with a wide range of concentrations and chemical natures of ecotoxicants, and where the inlet flows are characterized by high volumetric velocities. title: Topographical Imagination in Marina Cvetaeva’s «Pis'mo», «O Germanii», and «Natal'ja Gončarova»
abstract: In a substantial number of her texts – poetry as well as prose – Marina Ivanovna Cvetaeva (1892–1941) constructs contrasting dimensionalities: one-dimensional lines, two-dimensional planes, and three-dimensional objects are set in contrast to one another. She juxtaposes squares and flat surfaces with open landscapes, towers, and cathedrals. abstract: Conventional excavator bucket designs frequently exhibit over-engineering, which reduces operational efficiency due to excessive structural mass. This study aims to optimize the PC500 bucket with a capacity of 5 m³ to reduce mass and evaluate fatigue. 3D modeling was performed using SolidWorks, while Finite Element Analysis (FEA) testing was simulated through Ansys Workbench. title: The Impact of Purposeful Humor on Student Engagement and Learning in an Elementary Classroom: An Action Research Study
abstract: The purpose of this action research study was to explore how humorous science books can be purposefully integrated into elementary science instruction to enhance student engagement and conceptual understanding. Participants included nineteen second-grade students, ages seven to eight. The study examined the impact of teacher-led, intentional humor embedded in science texts featuring jokes, playful language, and a narrative voice. abstract: ABSTRACT Supercapacitors, renowned for their advantages of low‐cost, high‐power density, excellent cycling stability, environmental benignity, and superior safety have gained widespread application in diverse fields. However, their further development is limited by drawbacks such as low energy density. NiCo‐carbonate layered double hydroxide (NiCo‐Carbonate LDH) is a promising electrode material, but its two‐dimensional (2D) nanostructures tend to agglomerate, reducing capacitance utilization. abstract: Abstract The antibiotic resistance of pathogenic microorganisms due to the irresponsible use in healthcare and agricultural practices is one of the global threats for the human, especially immune-compromised patients. Thus, searching for a novel compounds from fungi with unique affinity to combat the drug-resistant microorganisms was the objective. Talaromyces purpurogenus # PZ292970.1, an endophyte of palm tree Elaeis guineensis , has the highest productivity of azaphilone pigment (25.5 AU410/ml), with a strong activity against E. coli (MIC value 6.8 µg/ml), S. aureus and C. albicans (MIC val

title: An integrated multilayer environmental impact assessment framework for accelerating sustainable energy infrastructure permitting
abstract: The deployment of sustainable energy infrastructure in the European Union is now limited less by technology costs than by the duration and unpredictability of permitting. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), the main authorization instrument for energy projects, evaluates the impacts of a proposal. title: Individual Resilience as Human Capital Stock: Neighborhood Social Capital, Environmental Perceptions, and Dynamic Pathways Across COVID-19 Phases
abstract: Abstract This study, grounded in the social ecological theories, investigates how the pathways linking neighborhood relationships, perceived environmental quality (PEQ), and individual resilience (IR) differed between the COVID-19 pandemic and the post-pandemic period. The empirical focus is on Chinese international students (CIS) in the UK, who experienced a unique form of “double exclusion” during the pandemic. title: Co‐Infection of Aeromonas veronii and Citrobacter braakii in Yellow Catfish ( Tachysurus fulvidraco )
abstract: Recently, a disease outbreak was observed in farmed yellow catfish (Tachysurus fulvidraco) in Tianjin, China. Naturally infected fish exhibited surface haemorrhages, abdominal distension, anal redness, and hemorrhagic ascites. Histopathological examination revealed systemic lesions in the stomach, intestine, liver, and spleen. Two Gram-negative bacterial isolates, designated PFL and PFS, were isolated from the liver and spleen of diseased fish, respectively. abstract: To improve the efficiency of aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) systems, it is desirable to minimize the spreading of the buoyant injectedfluid. One proposed approach is density compensation, whereby asolute like salt is added to the injectate to increase its density andreduce buoyancy-driven spreading. title: Ultra-lightweight mid-IR methane sensor for in-situ UAV-based measurements: Design and demonstration
abstract: Abstract. We developed an ultra-lightweight mid-infrared laser spectroscopic sensor for precise, rapid mobile measurements of atmospheric methane concentrations aboard small uncrewed aerial vehicles. The design is simple and compact, featuring a Herriott-type multi-pass cell in an open-path configuration. A single board computer with two on-chip microprocessor units allows rapid data acquisition and onboard wavelength modulation spectroscopy, making the sensor a stand-alone turnkey instrument. title: Three‐Dimensional Resistivity Imaging Constrains Crustal Heterogeneity Beneath the 2010 Yushu Ms 7.1 Earthquake Rupture
abstract: Abstract The 2010 Yushu (eastern Tibetan Plateau) Ms 7.1 strike‐slip earthquake ruptured unilaterally toward the southeast but left a hypocentral segment without mapped surface rupture, followed by a two‐stage reorganization of aftershocks. title: Multi‐Omics Analyses Identify Candidate Genes Associated With Stage‐Specific Quality Formation in Mulching‐Treated Moso Bamboo Shoots
abstract: Bamboo shoots are nutrient-rich edible resources, and organic mulching promotes earlier shoot emergence and increases yield. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating mulching-treated shoot (MtS) development remain unclear. Field experiments across three Moso bamboo forests, combined with biochemical profiling, metabolomics, and transcriptomics, examine MtS development. abstract: ABSTRACT Genotype × year (G × Y) interactions significantly complicate successful variety selection, especially in dryland (rain‐dependent) ecosystems experiencing intense climate fluctuations. title: Limestone reaction and crop yield in sandy soil of Bahia’s Cerrado, Brazil
abstract: Soil amendment is an essential step toward the introduction or maintenance of intensified agricultural production systems. The aim of the present research is to assess lime’s response to crops rotation and sandy soil yield in Bahia’s Cerrado region, Brazil, under controlled conditions. The experiment was conducted at completely randomized design with four replications. The crops were grown in pots filled with 20 kg of Oxisol (14% of clay). abstract: Endemic rice varieties can create locally abundant lignocellulosic residues. This study evaluates Sigupai rice husk, an Aceh endemic biomass, as a feedstock for cellulose nanocrystal production through alkaline delignification, hypochlorite bleaching and controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis at 1, 2 and 3 mol/L. The work tests how increasing acid concentration affects yield, residual non-cellulosic material, crystallinity, surface chemistry and particle-size distribution. title: A Comparative Study of Component-Provided Reconstruction-Based and Flexible-Linking Concept Mapping Designs in Collaborative Problem Solving
abstract: This study compares two integrated concept mapping designs within a collaborative problem solving (CPS) setting. The first employs a component-provided reconstruction-based (CPRB) concept mapping approach with real-time automated diagnostic feedback (Kit-Build), while the second uses a component-provided flexible-linking (CPFL) approach with delayed human-mediated feedback (Figma). abstract: The purpose of this study was to discover the artistic conceptualizations and priorities of collegiate, faculty, and professional musicians during the moment-to-moment decision-making of a rehearsal. We utilized musicians’ verbalizations during chamber music rehearsals as a vehicle for exploring their thought processes. abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an underrecognized cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide, with growing public health relevance, particularly in settings where routine diagnostic testing is limited. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is another epidemiologically related hepatitis virus, but few studies have directly compared these infections in Brazil. abstract: Endophytic bacteria (EB) associated with medicinal plants contribute to plant growth by enhancing nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and phytohormone production. This study aimed to isolate and characterize potential endophytic bacterial isolates (EBIs) from Echinops kebericho Mesfin and Lepidium sativum L., two traditional Ethiopian medicinal plants, and to evaluate their ability to utilize various growth substrates. abstract: Abstract Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Here, we report that during early acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, hepatocytes exhibit transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. We evaluated edible muscle from open-air and greenhouse paddies (three independent units per system, each pooling 50 snails) for proximate composition, hydrolyzed amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins, elements, and exploratory volatile profiles. abstract: Bacterial cellulose (BC) is a biopolymer with numerous potential applications, although it is associated with considerable production costs of conventional culture media. In this study, BC biosynthesis was investigated using native microorganisms from a mixture of non-centrifugal sugars (NCS) and apple juice as a low-cost alternative substrate. abstract: Salinity is one of the major environmental stress factors limiting agricultural production. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of different NaCl concentrations on seed germination and early seedling development in the Çameli variety of black cumin (Nigella sativa L.). abstract: The usage of high-strength steel sheet metals in crash absorbing structures can favour efficient and lightweight designs. abstract: The occurrence of micropollutants (MP) in wastewater has become an increasing environmental concern due to their persistence and incomplete removal by conventional treatment processes. This study evaluated a fixed-bed photobioreactor containing a polyurethane-supported microalgal-bacterial biofilm inoculated with Chlorella vulgaris for the simultaneous removal of organic matter and environmentally relevant MP. abstract: Abstract Enteric fermentation in ruminants is the largest agricultural source of methane (CH₄) and contributes to global warming. abstract: Abstract Nivicolous myxomycetes fruit at snowmelt in mountains, while their amoeboid trophic stages persist unseen in soil. abstract: ABSTRACT Cotton bollworms are a major constraint to cotton production in Benin despite insecticide use, yet their spatio‐temporal distribution remains poorly characterised. abstract: Abstract Long-term lake monitoring often relies on monthly dissolved oxygen profiles, but the robustness of derived oxygen metrics to this temporal resolution is uncertain. abstract: Reliable foundation design for power-transmission towers in mountainous terrain requires accurate knowledge of shallow weathering and bedrock geometry, yet steep relief, irregular bedrock, and uneven weathering limit point-based drilling and conventional surveys at the approximately 22 m × 22 m tower footprint. abstract: Abstract Understanding the movement and survival of birds of conservation concern during migration is critical for guiding conservation action. Unfortunately, the migratory life stage is understudied in many bird species because of the challenges of following such species over large distances, particularly those with small body sizes. Reflecting on the design and implementation of a multiphase mixed methods project involving over 9,000 participants, we examine how complexity emerged through the phenomenon under investigation, the structure of the research design, and the collaborations through which knowledge was produced. abstract: Abstract Using potential pulses in Cu-catalyzed CO2 electroreduction (CO2RR) has recently shown great promise in steering product selectivity. abstract: OBJECTIVES: Maximum gape and bite force are two key metrics of primate craniodental performance, but without mitigating adaptations, large gapes are associated with reduced bite force. abstract: ABSTRACT In arid and semi‐arid ecosystems, burrows serve as vital sanctuaries providing wildlife shelter, nourishment, and thermal buffering. abstract: Abstract Ammonia is a major contributor to eutrophication, making its reliable monitoring essential for protecting aquatic ecosystems and safeguarding water quality. abstract: We investigated the long-term effects of meadow management regimes (abandonment vs. mowing, and its frequency), plant invasion, and habitat availability on three different meadow ecosystem components. abstract: Allura Red AC (AR) is a synthetic anionic dye commonly used as a coloring agent in food and beverages. The extensive use and subsequent discharge of this dye as an industrial effluent raises significant health and environmental concerns. In this research, oxidized graphene-like carbon nanoparticles (Ox-CNPs) were evaluated for their potential in adsorption of AR. abstract: Abstract Background Cattle ectoparasites are important constraints to livestock production in Ethiopia, causing economic losses through reduced productivity, deterioration of hide and skin quality, disease transmission, and increased treatment costs. title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. abstract: This study examines how Azerbaijan’s dark tourism potential can be transformed into sustainable tourism revenue by identifying key strategic and institutional factors. abstract: Climate variability and environmental stressors, including erratic rainfall, recurrent drought, and soil degradation, increasingly threaten the sustainability of smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia, where rain-fed farming remains the main source of livelihood and food security. abstract: Abstract The spin-orbit correlation (SOC) provides a unique probe into the internal spin structure of hadrons. abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising carbon-free fuel, but its practical application is limited by low reactivity. This study investigates the laminar burning velocities (LBVs) and flame instabilities of DMC/NH 3 /air mixtures at 393 K and 1–4 atm, over equivalence ratios of 0.7–1.5 and NH 3 mole fractions of 0–40%. abstract: Illegal logging has generated recurrent civic mobilization in Romania, but the available evidence is dispersed across semi-structured civic and web archives. We construct a corpus of 278 source records dated between 2007 and 2026 and distinguish source records from unique protest events. abstract: Pickering emulsions are stabilized by coating droplet surfaces with solid particles that provide exceptional stability and suppress coalescence. abstract: Food waste (FW) is generated across multiple phases of food production and consumption. title: Seasonal Variation in Milk Quality and Somatic Cell Count of Friesian Crossbred Cows in Southern Highlands, Tanzania
abstract: Seasonal variations in environmental conditions and forage availability can substantially influence milk composition and udder health, yet information from dairy production systems in the Southern Highlands of Tanzania remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of season on physicochemical milk quality parameters and somatic cell count (SCC) in Friesian crossbred cows managed under a semi-intensive production system at the Tanzania Livestock Research Institute (TALIRI) Uyole Dairy Farm. abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. title: Determination of Genetic Diversity of Common Bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) Genotypes Collected From Central Kızılırmak Valley Using Single Nucleotide Polymorphism
abstract: Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is an important edible legume cultivated worldwide and widely used in human nutrition. Developments in the seed sector have encouraged producers to use certified seeds; however, these advances also threaten the extinction of farmer-maintained genetic resources. Therefore, it is essential to collect, conserve, and genetically characterize these resources, including the evaluation of their agricultural traits. abstract: The P* index has been commonly referred to as the “isolation” index in segregation studies because it isolates (more generally, separates) the distributional pattern of a particular group from other mutually exclusive groups. Since the P* index has been conceived to possess useful mathematical properties for capturing the exposure dimension of residential segregation, its spatial versions have been developed by different researchers. title: iota‐Carrageenan/Psyllium Composite Hydrogel for Cationic and Anionic Dye Removal From Wastewater
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents the in‐air synthesis of a novel hydrogel through chemical crosslinking of iota‐carrageenan (ι‐CG) and psyllium (PSY) using epichlorohydrin (EPH) as the crosslinking agent, aimed at the efficient removal of the dyes Crystal Violet (CV) and Fuchsin Acid (FA). The optimized hydrogel formulation, synthesized at 60°C for 5 h with a 1:1 ι‐CG:PSY ratio, 10 mL solvent volume, 0.6 mL EPH, and an alkaline pH of 9, demonstrated a remarkable swelling ratio of 3851% under the optimized synthesis conditions. title: Characterizing gas diffusivity, air permeability, and extracellular enzyme activity in an early‐stage comparison of conventional and regenerative pasture
abstract: Abstract Regenerative pasture is an emerging agricultural framework characterized by high forage diversity, adaptive grazing, and reduced external inputs. However, early‐stage soil structural transitions and associated microbial activities remain unclear, particularly given the higher spatial variability expected in these systems. title: Contrasting Roles of Geothermal Energy and Fossil Fuels in Indonesia's Carbon Emissions
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy is essential for improving environmental quality and mitigating climate change, particularly in fossil fuel-dependent emerging economies. Indonesia has substantial geothermal energy potential, yet its energy mix remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels, highlighting the importance of assessing geothermal energy's contribution to carbon emission reduction. This study investigates the dynamic impacts of geothermal energy in comparison with coal, oil, and gas on environmental quality in Indonesia, proxied by CO2 emissions from 1990Q1 to 2024Q4. title: Green Synthesis of Multifunctional EA‐CuO Nanoparticles Using Elytraria acaulis (L.f.) Lindau Leaf Extract: Assessment of Antimicrobial, Antioxidant, and Antidiabetic Activities
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for sustainable nanotechnology has encouraged eco‐friendly approaches for nanoparticle synthesis. In this study, copper oxide nanoparticles (EA‐CuO NPs) were synthesized using Elytraria acaulis (L.f.) Lindau leaf extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. The nanoparticles were characterized using UV–Vis, FTIR, SEM, TEM, EDX, XRD, DLS, and zeta‐potential analyses. title: Screening of nearly equivalent component groups and mechanism investigation of Si Miao San for treating rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: ABSTRACT Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic disease involving synovitis, cartilage damage, and bone erosion. Si Miao San (SMS), a traditional Chinese formula, shows anti‑RA potential, but its complex composition and mechanisms remain unclear. We developed a novel systems pharmacology strategy combining node importance scoring and Component Contribution Weight (CCW) modeling to identify the nearly equivalent component group (NECG) from SMS. title: Bacterial sialidases subvert the complement system through desialylation
abstract: Bacterial sialidases (neuraminidases) are widely studied virulence factors, yet their impact on the complement system, a central component of innate immunity, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effects of six sialidases from five human pathogens, including Bacteroides fragilis, Clostridium perfringens, Tannerella forsythia, Treponema denticola, and Vibrio cholerae on complement immunity using an integrated approach combining genetics, biochemistry, glycobiology, mass spectrometry, and structural biology. title: Sustainable Biohydrogen Production from Animal Manure: Review into Processes Optimization, Pretreatment Strategies, and Feedstocks Evaluation
abstract: Transforming animal manure from an environmental liability into a renewable biohydrogen resource represents a promising strategy for simultaneously addressing waste management and clean energy production. A narrative comparative review was conducted based on the critical synthesis of 130 peer-reviewed publications. Comparative evaluation highlighted integrating Dark Fermentation (DF) and Photo Fermentation (PF) effectively exploits their complementary metabolic pathways, resulting in more efficient substrate utilization and enhanced biohydrogen recovery than either process alone. title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries
abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. title: Universal spectral correlations in open Floquet systems with localized leaks
abstract: We show that introducing a localized leak in Floquet systems with time-reversal symmetry leads to universal spectral correlations governed by the non-Hermitian symmetry class $\mathrm{AI}^{\dagger}$, associated with complex-symmetric Ginibre random matrices, rather than by the unconstrained Ginibre ensemble. As a concrete example, we analyze the leaky quantum standard map (L-QSM) of the kicked rotor. title: Cytokine context shapes antigen-presenting and matrix-producing states of cancer-associated fibroblasts
abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs). title: From direct emission factors to inverse and indirect impact factors of road traffic: influence of emerging and unregulated pollutants
abstract: Abstract. Even though emissions regulations have successfully reduced concentrations of some road traffic-originated air pollutants, road traffic is still an important source of many unregulated emerging pollutants such as semi-volatile ultrafine particles, non-exhaust emissions and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in urban areas. In addition, road traffic can have season- and location-dependent inverse and indirect effects on the urban aerosol which are not well understood. title: REGIONAL INCOME DYNAMICS IN TÜRKİYE: CONVERGENCE, SPATIAL SPILLOVERS, AND STRUCTURAL DETERMINANTS
abstract: This study examines income convergence across Turkish provinces over the period 2004-2023 by combining traditional convergence analysis with spatial econometric methods. Both unconditional and conditional convergence models are estimated using provincial data. To account for structural heterogeneity across regions, the empirical framework incorporates net migration rates, trade openness, educational attainment, and digital infrastructure measured by per-capita fiber-optic cable length. title: Spatial polarization of endothelial ICAM-1 governs T-cell exclusion in melanoma
abstract: An immunosuppressive microenvironment limits therapeutic efficacy in melanoma. Beyond T-cell abundance and function, tumor control depends on T-cell access to malignant cells, yet the vascular mechanisms governing T-cell positioning remain poorly defined. Using RNA sequencing of endothelial cells from tumor cores versus peripheries in a mouse melanoma model, we identified intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) as a candidate regulator of T-cell localization. title: Enhanced Positive Temperature Coefficient Behavior of High‐Density Polyethylene/Carbon Black Composites via Waste Rubber Volume Exclusion and Electron‐Beam Irradiation Crosslinking
abstract: ABSTRACT Positive temperature coefficient (PTC) conductive polymer composites are promising for self‐regulating heating and overcurrent protection, yet high‐density polyethylene (HDPE)/carbon black (CB) systems still struggle to combine low room‐temperature resistivity, high PTC intensity, and stable high‐temperature electrical response. Herein, ground tire rubber (GTR)‐induced volume exclusion and electron beam (EB) irradiation crosslinking were combined to regulate the conductive network of HDPE/CB composites. title: Network Governance for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Partnerships to Implement UN SDGs in Anti‐Desertification Projects
abstract: ABSTRACT Contemporary governance is increasingly characterized by coordinated engagement among diverse actors in addressing sustainability challenges under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), where network governance strategies play an important role in developing collaborative capacity. This study investigates the role of network governance strategies in enhancing partnership outcomes for implementing SDGs, with a particular focus on SDG 15.3 combating desertification and restoring degraded land. title: Kinetics and Pathways of Urea Release from Granules Spray-Coated with Biodegradable PHBV/PBAT Blends
abstract: Abstract Synthetic fertilisers play a crucial role in agricultural productivity and global food security, with nitrogen-based fertilisers, particularly urea, being the most widely used. However, the nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) of urea is only ~ 50%, leading to substantial nitrogen losses to the environment, resulting in significant environmental, health, and economic impacts. To mitigate these issues, enhanced efficiency fertilisers (EEFs) have been developed, including polymer-coated controlled-release fertilisers (CRFs). journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment

title: Structural asymmetries in global food price inflation: crisis amplification, regional divergence, and the emergence of a persistent food price premium
abstract: Global food price volatility threatens food security, yet how international shocks amplify differentially across developing regions, and why food prices structurally diverge from general inflation, remain poorly understood. This study examines global food price dynamics and sub-regional transmission patterns using monthly Consumer Price Index data for 24 world regions across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas (2001–2025), with particular attention to African and Asian sub-regions. title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
abstract: Abstract Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ /10 and annular features smaller than λ /60. title: Integrative big Five–Environment model: Analyzing pro-environmental behavior through SEM-PLS and fuzzy multi-criteria
abstract: This study investigates the interplay between the Big Five personality traits, Environmental Factors, and pro-environmental behavior (PEB) using an integrated approach that combines Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) and Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision Making (FMCDM). The primary objective is to examine the statistical associations between personality traits—openness to experience, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism—and pro-environmental behavior, as well as the indirect statistical associations through Environmental Factors. title: Formation of Thermally Stable Vesicles from a Cyclic Tetraether Archaeal Lipid
abstract: Abstract The formation of thermostable vesicles by the archaeal lipid β-l-gulopyranosyl-caldarchaetidyl-glycerol (CaldA) is investigated. This caldarchaeol-based lipid comprises the main polar lipid of the archaeon Thermoplasma acidophilum. Vesicle formation is shown and quantitatively analyzed through a combination of laser scanning confocal microscopy, cryogenic-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells
abstract: Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. title: Assessment of Airborne Spores in Erzincan Province via Volumetric Aeromycological Monitoring and Relationship Correlation with Meteorological Data
abstract: Atmospheric spores pose threats to human, animal and plant health by affecting ecosystems; therefore, their identification and the development of prevention strategies are of great importance. To characterize atmospheric spores in Erzincan, weekly sampling was conducted from 01 January to 31 December 2022 using a Lanzoni VPPS‑2000 volumetric sampler. Based on the annual dataset, spores were identified and the start and end dates of the Main Spore Season (MSS) were determined. title: AN EVALUATION OF COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE LEVEL ON SPATIAL UTILIZATION IN LANDSLIDE PRONE AREAS IN NGARGOYOSO SUB DISTRICT YEAR 2025
abstract: Land-use change in Ngargoyoso District has increased due to tourism expansion. Situated on Mount Lawu's slopes with high landslide susceptibility, improper spatial utilization and low public understanding of Spatial Planning escalate disaster risks. This study aims to analyze public knowledge levels regarding spatial utilization in landslide-prone areas and its influencing factors in 2025. The research employs a descriptive quantitative approach supported by explicit qualitative data. title: Network Indices and Diversity Follow Distinct Patterns for Bee–Plant Networks Along a Neotropical Elevational Gradient
abstract: A critical goal of ecology is to quantify mutualistic network structure across all ecosystems and organisms, as these networks often represent essential ecosystem services and therefore network metrics are often used as conservation targets. Some major gaps still exist, one of which is Neotropical bees, a group expected to contribute exceptional insight to ecological network theory, owing to the extreme diversity of mutualistic interactions characteristic of the Neotropics, as well as the unique global distribution patterns of bees. title: Quantum protocols for time synchronisation and distribution: a critical assessment
abstract: Precise time synchronisation underpins critical infrastructure from telecommunications and financial markets to power grids and scientific metrology. Several families of quantum protocols have been proposed and demonstrated for clock synchronisation and time distribution, exploiting entangled photon pairs, quantum key distribution (QKD) correlations, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and entangled clock networks. title: Analysis of Two Large Earthquakes in the South Pacific Coast of Mexico Using Rényi Entropy
abstract: We present a study on the behavior of Rényi entropy for earthquake magnitudes, focusing on two large-magnitude events in the Pacific coast of Mexico: the M8.2 Tehuantepec earthquake in 2017 and the M7.7 Michoacán earthquake in 2022. Based on the discrete version of Rényi entropy, we show that entropy decreases before the mainshocks occur and subsequently exhibits an abrupt increase before returning to stable values. title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. title: Museums, taxonomic uncertainty and ‘lost species’: a case study of the Critically Endangered Siau Scops Owl
abstract: Of the world's Critically Endangered (CR) and Data Deficient (DD) birds, ~27% are ‘lost species’ (lacking verified documentation for >10 years). Some may await rediscovery, and others are probably already extinct, but a few may prove never to have been valid species. Identifying these latter cases is an urgent conservation priority so as not to waste finite resources on costly and futile searches. title: Effects of Seeding and NPS Fertilizer Rates on Grain Yield, Yield Traits, and Quality of Durum Wheat Varieties in Bale Highlands, Southeastern Oromia
abstract: Despite its numerous benefits and yield potential, the current productivity of durum wheat in the highlands areas of Bale Zones, Southern Eastern Oromia is inhibited by soil fertility depletion and inappropriate plant densities per unit area and other interrelated factors. In this view, a field experiment was conducted in the 2023 and 2024 main cropping seasons at Sinana, Agarfa, and Gololcha districts to determine the optimum seeding and NPS application rates. title: Grip-force modulation during action word reading: An RSVP paradigm with Bayesian temporal analysis
abstract: Abstract Grip force provides a behavioral index of motor engagement during action language processing, but prior studies have relied on auditory presentation and fixed analysis windows. We adapted grip force methodology to Rapid Serial Visual Presentation (RSVP) and used a Time-resolved Bayesian Evidence Display (TBED) to characterize motor resonance without predefined time windows. title: Feasibility Study of Green Hydrogen Production From an Onshore Wind Farm in Campania Region, Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Green hydrogen holds significant potential for ensuring a sustainable energy transition. Italy is advancing its green hydrogen strategy to align with European efforts to expand green hydrogen production. However, for an effective energy transition, the feasibility of green hydrogen needs to be evaluated through techno‐economic assessments backed by real‐world data.
