abstract: Background Air pollution is one of the leading global environmental health risks, associated with millions of premature deaths annually. It represents a substantial share of the global disease burden. Despite well-established epidemiological associations, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain only partially understood. There is a need for systematic approaches toward mechanistic understanding that connect particulate matter exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects. title: Market Reaction to Middle East Geopolitical Shocks: Evidence from Iran Conflict Escalation and Energy Stocks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange
abstract: The escalation of the Iran conflict, which threatens global energy supply through the Strait of Hormuz, raises the question of how energy sector stocks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) respond to such geopolitical risk. The study aims to determine whether the conflict generates significant abnormal returns and cumulative market effects and to assess the speed of investor response to the geopolitical shock. title: Psychological flexibility in the work-caregiving interplay of employed family caregivers of people with dementia (DAILY-FLEX): Protocol of an experience sampling study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Employed family caregivers of people with dementia face competing work and caregiving demands that can negatively affect well-being across both domains. The Work-Home Resources model proposes that demands and resources influence cross-domain functioning through changes in personal resources. Psychological flexibility (PF), the ability to remain open to difficult experiences while acting in line with personal values, may represent a dynamic personal resource in this process. title: Active paper sheets incorporating encapsulated essential oils preserve the volatile profile of melon galia (Cucumis melo L. var. reticulatus) during storage
abstract: Galia melon ( Cucumis melo L. var. reticulatus) is a highly appreciated but perishable fruit whose characteristic aroma, mainly driven by esters, deteriorates rapidly along the cold chain. This work evaluated active paper sheets impregnated with microencapsulated essential oils (EOs) as a tool to preserve the quality of Galia melon during a simulated commercial cold chain. title: Ginsenoside RK3 suppresses osteosarcoma via PRMT5/GPX4-ferroptosis axis and enhances doxorubicin chemosensitivity
abstract: Background Osteosarcoma (OS), the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, commonly develops chemoresistance to conventional apoptosis-dependent therapies (e.g., doxorubicin) in metastatic/recurrent settings, leading to poor prognosis. Ferroptosis—an iron-dependent cell death pathway driven by lipid peroxidation—offers a promising alternative, yet clinical translation of synthetic inducers is limited by poor druggability. title: Microscopia óptica avanzada aplicada al estudio de la retina. Análisis de su posible utilización como herramienta de diagnóstico de patología ocular
abstract: La retina está potencialmente afectada de forma directa, por el paso del tiempo, como de forma indirecta, por el modo en el que ese tiempo pasa y como ha estado protegida o expuesta a noxas. title: A multi-criteria decision framework for evaluating refinery oily sludge valorization in red ceramics
abstract: This study develops a multi-criteria decision framework for the comparative evaluation of refinery oily sludge (ROS) valorization in red ceramics. Laboratory-scale ceramic specimens containing 0, 5, and 10 wt% ROS were fired at 950°C and 1050°C. Water absorption (WA), flexural strength (FS), and thermal conductivity (TC) were integrated with study-specific indicators of clay saving (CS), water saving (WS), and theoretical ROS energy contribution (REC). title: Deconstructing Partitiviridae proteins reveals the evolutionary determinants behind their origin and ecological breadth
abstract: Abstract Viruses represent a primary source of biological diversity, yet the specific mechanisms by which viral proteins shape host range remain unclear. Members of the family Partitiviridae offer a minimalist model to address this question: despite their collectively broad host range, they typically encode only an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) and a capsid protein (CP). title: Standardizing freshwater macroinvertebrate taxonomy: a Lithuanian operational taxa list for ecological quality assessments and biodiversity research
abstract: Taxonomic discrepancies pose a significant barrier to national data synthesis and accurate biomonitoring reporting. We compiled a standardized operational taxa list of freshwater macroinvertebrates known to occur in Lithuania, with the goal of improving comparability and ecological quality assessment reliability of biomonitoring data. A national list of freshwater macroinvertebrates was created by synthesizing literature and biomonitoring data. title: Evaluating Fermented and Non‐Fermented Lettuce‐Based Biostimulants Through a Design of Experiments Approach to Address Agronomic and Microbial Impacts in Strawberry Soilless Cultivation
abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive agriculture relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers, which contribute to green‐house gas emissions and to the degradation of soil quality and microbial biodiversity. In line with circular‐economy principles, the conversion of organic biomass into biostimulants through fermentation has emerged as a sustainable strategy to support plant performance. journal: Journal of Sustainable Agriculture and Environment

title: Wheat straw mulching and compost application effects on lima bean productivity, seed quality, and weed density under arid irrigated conditions
abstract: Abstract In the irrigated arid regions of Iraq, soil degradation and severe evaporative demand constrain legume productivity. Although ecological intensification using organic amendments is widely promoted, the specific mechanisms governing crop–weed–soil interactions remain poorly understood. A field experiment was conducted in Baghdad (spring‐summer 2025) using a split‐plot factorial design (3 × 3 factorial with three replications) to evaluate the individual and combined effects of wheat straw mulch (0, 5, 10 cm) and compost (1, 2, 3 t ha −1 ) on lima bean ( Phaseolus lunatus L.) performance

title: Optimizing intra‑row spacing and seed tuber weight to enhance yield, quality, economic return, and profitability of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) in Nepal
abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is an important food and cash crop in Nepal, but its yield remains below potential partly due to suboptimal plant spacing and seed tuber size management. This study evaluated the effects of three intra-row spacings (70 × 25 cm, 70 × 35 cm, 70 × 45 cm) and three seed tuber weight classes (21-30 g, 31-40 g, 41-50 g) on growth, yield, tuber size distribution, starch yield, and economic performance of potato cv. title: Growth under mild drought: transcriptomics comparison of perennial ryegrass genotypes with differential tolerance to water deficit
abstract: Mild summer droughts rarely threaten perennial ryegrass survival, but sensitive cultivars may halt growth early, reducing yields. This study examined the transcriptomic responses to mild drought (5 days without watering) and rewatering in two genotypes with contrasting leaf growth behaviors. title: Variation in the essential oil composition of wild Artemisia absinthium from Hamadan, Iran, across phenological stages
abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate variations in the essential oil composition of a wild Artemisia absinthium population from Hamadan, Iran, across three phenological stages (pre‐flowering, flowering, and post‐flowering) using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry analysis. The essential oil profile showed variation among developmental stages, with changes in the relative abundance of major constituents and chemical groups. title: Synergistic effects of fibrolytic enzymes and lactic acid bacteria on cassava leaf silage quality and microbial community
abstract: Cassava leaves are a valuable protein-rich feed resource, but their high fiber content and poor fermentation characteristics can reduce silage quality. To address these challenges, this study evaluated the synergistic effects of fiber-degrading enzymes and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the fermentation profiles, nutritional quality, and microbial community of cassava leaf silage. Silage was prepared using five treatments: CK (2% glucose), T1 (Lactobacillus plantarum + 2% glucose), T2 (glucanase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), T3 (cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and T4 (glucanase + cellul
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Flight dynamics and optimal control of unpowered avian landings
abstract: Abstract Most birds can transition from aerial to terrestrial locomotion in complex environments. However, to touchdown at safe speeds is challenging as low speeds result in poor aerodynamic control authority, especially in unpowered flight, and how birds manage this is not well understood. Through exploration of the dynamics, we provide an analytical optimal control strategy that minimizes touchdown speed and show that zero touchdown speed is physically possible in unpowered flight. title: Abundance and species diversity of mosquitoes (Diptera, Culicidae) in endemic areas for arboviruses in the Eastern Amazon, Brazil
abstract: Combating the spread of arboviruses in the Amazon relies on understanding the diversity of Culicidae, particularly potential vectors. Areas with historical records of vector occurrence provide crucial insights into the factors driving epidemic emergence. Furthermore, anthropogenic activities, such as deforestation and demographic pressure on the forest, are considered the primary drivers of new outbreaks, creating a scenario of high ecological receptivity for pathogens of public health concern. title: Multimedia-integrated physics instruction: Impact on student engagement in Tanzanian secondary schools
abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of multimedia integration on student attitudes and engagement in physics education in Tanzanian secondary schools. A convergent mixed-methods case study was conducted in four government schools in Mbeya Region with 96 Form Two students and two physics teachers. Grounded in Mayer’s cognitive theory of multimedia learning and Vygotsky’s social constructivism, the eight-lesson intervention used PhET simulations, videos, and animations on sustainable energy sources. title: Synergistic sintering of red mud, fly ash, and Chinese herbal medicine residues into sintered ceramics: A sustainable design combining industrial and agricultural solid waste
abstract: This study investigated the feasibility of using industrial solid waste (red mud, fly ash) and agricultural solid waste (Chinese herbal medicine residue) to jointly produce sintered ceramic materials. The solid waste ratios were adjusted using a stoneware formulation as a reference. title: Thermophilic Adaptation of a Minimal Hammerhead Ribozyme Comes with a Functional Penalty
abstract: Life has adapted to extreme environments, such as elevated pH, extreme temperatures, and environments with a lack of oxygen. The biomolecules made by organisms that live in extreme environments must adapt to remain folded and functional. Recent computational studies have shown that rRNA, tRNA, and certain mRNAs adapt in thermophilic organisms through an increased GC content. However, few previous studies have assessed the efficiency of adapted thermophilic RNAs. title: Polylactic co-glycolic acid (PLGA)-based nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract: A potential therapeutic strategy against oxidative stress and diabetes in rat model
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. Persea americana seed extract (PSE) has antidiabetic potential but suffers from non-specific distribution and poor bioavailability, thus limiting its clinical application. title: Informalidad laboral, calidad del empleo y vulnerabilidad económica en México: evidencia territorial de las entidades federativas
abstract: Labour informality is a structural constraint preventing high employment levels in Mexico from translating into economic well-being. This study analyses the relationship between labour informality, job quality and economic vulnerability across Mexico’s 32 federal entities. A quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive-comparative design with a longitudinal perspective is used, drawing on the National Survey of Occupation and Employment and INEGI’s labour poverty measurement. title: Analysing resource management outcomes: an actor-centred power approach
abstract: This paper presents an adapted methodological Interest-Power-Outcome (IPO) framework for analysing environmental resource management outcomes by integrating the Actor-Centred Power (ACP) framework with Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA). The framework aims to analyse how actors involved in resource management use their power in pursuit of specific interests, and how their interventions on the ground can either align with or diverge from intended policy outcomes in a resource system. title: Closing the loop: business model and feasibility study for a standalone paper recycling unit in Egyptian universities
abstract: Abstract Universities generate substantial volumes of paper waste, yet much of this valuable resource remains underutilized despite increasing commitments to circular economy and sustainable campus initiatives. Paper recycling within university campuses has the potential to reduce solid waste generation, lowering paper procurement costs, and supporting sustainability-focused education. title: Self-powered neural intervention via piezoelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are electromechanical energy-conversion devices constructed from piezoelectric materials. They convert physiological motion, local tissue deformation, or externally applied mechanical stimuli into localized electrical signals and have attracted considerable interest in self-powered neural interventions. Despite the rapid expansion of research in this field, the systematic understanding needed to guide translational optimization remains limited. title: Emissions variability of greenhouse gases within and between sites during late‐season corn production in Mississippi
abstract: Abstract Variability of greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes and emissions among replicates in a study area can have an impact on results depending on the statistical tools used to assess significant differences among fixed effects. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of site and time (i.e., date) and the variability within and between sites on soil GHG (carbon dioxide [CO 2 ], methane [CH 4 ], and nitrous oxide [N 2 O]) fluxes and emissions from two fields under the same management practices during late‐season corn ( Zea mays ) production in Mississippi. title: Shaping biodiversity from within: How experts' perceptions of values, rules and knowledges influence biodiversity assessment
abstract: Abstract While biodiversity conservation has had its local success, worldwide biodiversity loss continues rapidly. Despite the push towards more inclusive and equitable approaches, conservation practices often reinforce existing conceptualizations of biodiversity, excluding other ways of knowing and valuing nature. This paper explores the process of assessing biodiversity among a group of habitat experts. Our study contributes to the literature with empirical understanding of the tension between objective and more pluralistic, relational understandings of biodiversity among a group of experts.

title: Materials and technological choices in ceramic production of Medieval Almería (al-Andalus): clays, glazes and colorants
abstract: Abstract This article presents the archaeometric characterisation of a collection of medieval pottery (11th–12th centuries) from two documented pottery workshops in the city of Almería. The study focuses on common pottery used for cooking, tableware, water storage, as well as pottery associated with production processes. This type of material is widely represented in the archaeological record, but is rarely characterised from a technological and compositional perspectives. title: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development
abstract: Maternal perceived stress, mental health, and physiological dysregulation during pregnancy can alter the intrauterine environment, shaping infant development through fetal programming processes. Nonetheless, few longitudinal studies in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have jointly examined psychological and biological factors in relation to infant outcomes. This longitudinal study followed 146 Pakistani mother-infant dyads at early to mid-gestation (T1), mid- to late gestation (T2), and postpartum (T3). title: Investigating the effects of dexmedetomidine in cecal ligation and puncture‑induced septic rats
abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality, and ferroptosis has been implicated in sepsis-associated organ injury. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an α2-adrenergic agonist with anti-inflammatory properties, may modulate this process. We examined whether DEX protects against cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)– induced septic lung injury and alters ferroptosis-associated markers in rats. Thirty-two female Wistar rats were randomized to sham, CLP, and CLP pretreated with DEX (30–50 µg/kg, intraperitoneally, 30 min before CLP) groups ( n = 8 each) and euthanized 16 h after surgery. title: Paper waste derived cellulose nanofluids for enhanced oil recovery in high temperature high salinity sandstone reservoirs
abstract: Conventional enhanced oil recovery (EOR) methods often exhibit reduced efficiency under high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) reservoir conditions, necessitating sustainable and high-performance alternatives. This study investigated cellulose nanoparticles (CNPs), defined as nanoscale cellulose particles derived from paper waste, for HTHS EOR applications. High-purity CNPs were synthesized using a deep eutectic solvent (DES) and subsequently surface-modified with (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) to improve dispersion stability and interfacial properties. title: Understanding the uneven geography of Britain’s economic inactivity crisis since Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This paper extends the concept of regional resilience to address economic inactivity as a key economic outcome, and to consider health and demography as sources of regional vulnerability and resilience. Economic inactivity in Great Britain rose sharply following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, but in geographically uneven ways. Results indicate that changes to local economic inactivity are strongly associated with changes to health and ageing of the labour force, but not with changes to immigration linked to Brexit. title: Ecological impact of steeplebush (Spiraea tomentosa L.) invasion on mite communities (Acari, Mesostigmata) in wet meadow ecosystems
abstract: Invasive plants are species introduced outside their natural range and often cause ecological or economic harm. By modifying litter quality, root architecture, and soil chemistry, invasive plants can alter many soil processes, including nutrient cycling and edaphic activity. The main aim of our study was to provide the first assessment in Poland of the ecological impact of Spiraea tomentosa L. invasion on the abundance, diversity, and species richness of soil Mesotigmata (Gamasida; Gamasina and Uropodnia) mite communities in wet meadow ecosystems, thereby offering novel insights into the below

title: Improved use of deep soil water promotes radial growth during drought
abstract: Abstract Increasingly frequent seasonal droughts under rapid climate change threaten the growth stability of subtropical mixed forests across the mid‐subtropical monsoon region. In this study, we combined stable hydrogen and oxygen isotope analyses with high‐precision radial growth monitoring to explore how water source use influences the radial growth of four subtropical tree species. Three contrasting functional strategies were identified based on rooting depth and water uptake plasticity. title: Population structure of the last Tomares nogelii (Lepidoptera, Lycaenidae) population in the European Union—A capture‐mark‐recapture study
abstract: Abstract Effective conservation of highly specialized butterflies in fragmented landscapes requires quantitative estimates of population size, turnover and functional connectivity. Here, we present the first capture–mark–recapture (CMR) survey of the last known metapopulation of Tomares nogelii dobrogensis , a locally monophagous Lycaenid, in northern Dobrogea, Romania. From May to July 2025, six spatially separated colonies were surveyed, recording 832 capture events (638 first captures and 194 recaptures). title: The biological activity of Kedrostis nana plant extracts: Antioxidant, antibacterial and cytotoxic effects
abstract: There has been an increased resurgence of infectious diseases globally which has caused great concern. This is due to the various bacterial species developing resistance to modern synthetic antibiotics. There is a dire need for new treatment or drugs to counteract this concern. Medicinal plants have been the go-to therapeutic treatment as they contain numerous bioactive compounds that have pharmacological activity. title: Identification of Cytoplasmic Male Sterility (CMS) and Maintainer Line through Testcross and Self-Pollination in Chili Peppers (Capsicum annuum L.)
abstract: Hybrid seed production in chili is more efficient when using male-sterile plants. Cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) produces 100% male sterile progeny and eliminates the need for emasculation, making it highly advantageous for hybrid seed production and enhancing the genetic purity of hybrid seeds. Indonesia possesses a wide range of commercial hybrid chili pepper varieties that can serve as alternative sources of CMS genetic resources. title: Hide and Skin Preservation in Ethiopia: Traditional Practices, Improved Techniques, Quality Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Hides and skins are important livestock by-products and the principal raw materials for Ethiopia’s leather and leather-products industries. Their value, however, depends not only on the number of animals slaughtered but also on how promptly and correctly the pelts are removed, preserved, stored and transported before tanning. Fresh hides and skins contain abundant water, nutrients and microorganisms; delays after slaughter can therefore lead to bacterial putrefaction, hair slip, grain damage, unpleasant odour and irreversible losses in leather strength and appearance. title: African Horse Sickness Distribution and Vaccination Coverage in North Shewa Zone, Ethiopia: A 5-Year Retrospective Study (2019–2025)
abstract: African horse sickness (AHS) is a severe, vector-borne viral disease of equids associated with high mortality and substantial socioeconomic losses. However, regional epidemiological evidence from Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to describe the temporal, seasonal, and spatial distribution of reported AHS outbreaks and assess vaccination coverage in North Shewa Zone, Ethiopia. A retrospective descriptive study was conducted using Disease Outbreak and Vaccination Activity Report (DOVAR) records from 23 districts for the period 2019–2025. title: Migration and the Geography of Life Expectancy: Selective Sorting and Spatial Dependence Across 172 Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT International migration has grown rapidly in recent decades, yet its relationship with population health is difficult to disentangle from the economic, structural and geographic characteristics of the places migrants move to. This study examines whether international migration is associated with population‐level life expectancy after accounting for confounding and the data's spatial structure. title: Hierarchical Linear Modeling of BOSP Fund Utilization and Basic Education Quality in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
abstract: Equalizing basic education quality in archipelagic East Nusa Tenggara (NTT), Indonesia, remains a structural challenge because learning outcomes vary widely across regencies under the decentralized School Operational Assistance (BOSP) program. This study examines how school level BOSP spending on books (Component 02) and teacher training (Component 05) predicts school mean scores on the Academic Ability Test (Tes Kemampuan Akademik, TKA), the national Grade 6 assessment of reading literacy and numeracy, and whether regency poverty and the Education Cost Index (IBP) moderate these relationships

abstract: The peak onset of mental disorders occurs during adolescence; therefore, youth mental health conditions have become a major global public health concern, imposing substantial social and economic burdens. Depression and anxiety exhibit distinct developmental and sex-specific patterns, and prior studies indicate that teacher-student relationships and screen time significantly influence school-aged children's mental health conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Thymus willdenowii ( T. willdenowii ) Boiss. is an endemic Moroccan medicinal plant whose bioactive potential remains poorly documented. This study aimed to characterize the hydroethanolic extract of T. willdenowii and evaluate its antioxidant, antimicrobial, antifungal, and insecticidal activities. Aerial parts were extracted and analyzed using qualitative and quantitative phytochemical assays and high‐performance liquid chromatography with ultraviolet detection (HPLC/UV–vis). title: Beyond the ventricle: the atrial contribution to feline hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and implications for diagnosis, prognosis, and emerging therapy
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common heart disease of cats and is conventionally characterised by its ventricular phenotype. The clinical events that determine quality and duration of life in affected cats, however, are atrial in their proximate pathophysiology. Congestive heart failure arises from elevated left atrial pressure transmitted to the pulmonary venous bed, arterial thromboembolism arises from blood stasis in a remodelled and dysfunctional left atrial appendage, and survival tracks left atrial size and function independently of left ventricular wall thickness. title: Molecular mechanisms of boron in animal nutrition: from cellular signalling to systemic metabolic regulation
abstract: Boron is essential for higher plants and biologically active in animals, although its essentiality in mammals remains unproven because no boron-dependent enzyme, cofactor, or consistent deficiency syndrome has been established. This review critically examines the biochemical, cellular, and physiological roles of boron in animal nutrition, emphasizing chemical speciation, dose dependence, and mechanistic uncertainty. title: Epidemic dynamics of wheat stripe rust under climate change and lagging human-led disease management
abstract: Abstract Wheat stripe rust poses substantial challenges to food security in China, and elucidating its epidemic patterns provides a scientific basis for disease management. To investigate the factors underlying its widespread 2020 outbreak and the associated inoculum transmission dynamics, 645 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici samples were collected from 15 provinces across China in this study. title: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome: Potential Role in Magnetoreception
abstract: Abstract Radical-pair-based magnetic compass mechanisms are believed to depend on spin-selective reaction pathways modulated by the Earth’s magnetic field. However, the influence of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) on the magnetic compass function at the molecular level remains largely unknown. title: Development of Interactive Media Learning for Flood Risk Education: Enhancing Flood Knowledge in Tha Than, Eastern Thailand
abstract: This study developed and evaluated interactive digital learning media that translate local flood evidence from Tha Than Subdistrict, Chachoengsao Province, Thailand, into flood risk education. A research and development design were used with two objectives: (1) to design and develop the media from local flood evidence and to evaluate their quality and efficiency (E₁/E₂), and (2) to compare flood knowledge before and after use of the media. title: Demarcating and negotiating borders: Stancetaking and identity construction in Polish online discourse about Russia's war in Ukraine
abstract: This study investigates discursive borderwork in online communication about the war in Ukraine. It examines how borders are drawn through the dynamics of nomination and stancetaking and their relationship to identity construction at both the micro scale of individual references and the macro scale of single comments and interactional exchanges. The analysis draws on user-generated content from Polish internet forums collected between April and September 2022. title: When low bending stiffness challenges the test: Bonded doublers for Mode I and Mode II delamination characterization of micro- and nanoparticle-modified woven GFRP laminates
abstract: This study investigates bonded doubler reinforcement for Mode I and Mode II delamination testing of thin, compliant 0°/90° woven glass-fiber/epoxy laminates with unmodified and particle-modified matrices. Double Cantilever Beam (DCB) and End-Notched Flexure (ENF) tests were performed on laminates modified with SiO 2 nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes, or carbon-filler, with the unmodified laminate serving as reference. title: Genetic diversity of the endangered saproxylic beetle Boros schneideri and preliminary insight into its associated bacterial and fungal communities
abstract: Boros schneideri is a rare and endangered saproxylic beetle associated with old, dead trees. We investigated its genetic diversity in Western Polesie, Poland, and assessed larval microbiota and mycobiota. Mitochondrial COI and 16 S rRNA, and nuclear ITS1 markers of B. schneideri were analyzed using haplotype and nucleotide diversity estimates, Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, and median-joining networks. title: Strain-Dependent Lactic Fermentation Primes Milk Proteins for Gastrointestinal Digestion Under Age-Specific Physiological Conditions
abstract: Lactic fermentation modifies milk proteins through the proteolytic activity of lactic acid bacteria, potentially altering their susceptibility to gastrointestinal digestion. This study evaluated how fermentation by Lactobacillus delbrueckii and Lactobacillus helveticus, individually and in co-culture, affects the structure of bovine milk proteins, their subsequent gastrointestinal digestion, and residual immunoreactivity. title: Vanishing Borders: Ethnicity and Trade Costs at the Origin of the Yugoslav Market
abstract: This article uses the creation of a paradigmatic multi-ethnic state, Yugoslavia, in 1918, and a novel large dataset of grain prices to examine the effect of ethnicity on trade costs when borders changed. Controlling for transport costs and import tariffs, we find a large but transitory border effect. Ethno-religious differences initially significantly increased price gaps, but their negative influence vanished over time as well. abstract: BIFLEX is a flexible underactuated gripper inspired by the human thumb–index pair and designed for distal precision pinch and proximal adaptive holding. Building on a previously developed soft-hybrid Fin-Ray finger, this study combines finger-geometry optimization, four-bar kinematic synthesis, and shared single-motor actuation through a four-bar and tendon–pulley transmission. title: Emirates dreams: factors attracting Sub-Saharan African immigrants to the UAE and the challenges
abstract: This study examines the push and pull factors that brings low-skilled Sub-Saharan African migrants to the UAE, and the challenges encountered in pursuit of their migration goals once there. Through semi-structured interviews with 45 Sub-Saharan African migrants this research employs Push-Pull Theory and Social Network Theory to explore three central questions: the push and pull factors driving migration, the lived experiences and hardships faced by migrants, and the gap between pre-migration expectations and post-migration realities. abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric scaffolds can conform to irregular bone defects and deliver wireless electrical stimulation, yet whether their mechanical and electrical functions persist throughout the months-long course of bone remodeling, as well as whether the regenerated bone ultimately recovers load-bearing function, remains unresolved. abstract: Specific genetic mutations serve as clues to cancer emergence. However, non-genetic cell state shift mechanisms—such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)—drive swift, reversible drug tolerance and metastasis. abstract: Integrated multi-club ownership networks have expanded rapidly in European football, yet empirical research comparing the financial returns of their youth development with traditional single-club structures remains limited. This study compares two non-integrated clubs (Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur) with two integrated networks (Manchester City, Brighton & Hove Albion). abstract: Soil fertility depletion caused by declining organic matter and imbalanced nutrient inputs is a major constraint to barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) production in the Ethiopian highlands. title: Quantitative Fracture Analysis of All‐Polymer Active Layers for Intrinsically Stretchable Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Comprehensive Summary Stretchy organic solar cells require active layers that can not only tolerate large tensile deformation but also resist crack propagation after damage initiation. However, conventional mechanical descriptors such as crack‐onset strain and fracture strain provide limited information on how cracks evolve and dissipate energy in deformable photovoltaic films. Here, we provide a quantitative fracture‐analysis framework for elastomer‐toughened all‐polymer photovoltaic active layers by combining optical crack tracking, crack‐aspect‐ratio analysis, film‐on‐water fracture testing

title: The actual sky of Van Gogh’s Starry Night: a multidisciplinary reconstruction
abstract: The Starry Night : whether its sky represents spontaneous fantasy or a realist depiction has gone unanswered for over a century. Earlier astronomical readings, constrained by the conventional June dating, reached mutually exclusive conclusions, and the painting’s celestial arrangement was never quantitatively tested. In contrast, this study narrows the dates on which the Moon and Venus fall within the painter’s field of view, confirms that selection by Procrustes fitting of the asterism, and cross-checks it against meteorological and bioclimatic records and the original letters. title: Effects of Planting Date on Grain Yield Components and Northern Leaf Blight Severity in Two Contrasting Maize (Zea mays L.) Cultivars Under Rainfed and Irrigated Conditions
abstract: Abstract Adverse meteorological conditions often force farmers to plant maize ( Zea mays L.) outside its optimal planting window. Early or delayed planting can significantly influence crop phenology, yield, and disease severity. This study evaluated two contrasting cultivars, PAN4R-872BR (early-maturing and NLB-susceptible) and DKC75-65BR (medium-maturing and NLB-resistant), across multiple planting dates and assessed the effect of planting date on Northern Leaf Blight (NLB) severity. title: Integrating Camera-Trap Monitoring and Community Surveys to Assess Human–Asian Badger (Meles leucurus) Interactions in Agricultural Landscapes of the Meng Mountains, China
abstract: Human–wildlife interactions can threaten rural livelihoods and complicate wildlife conservation in agricultural landscapes. We combined community surveys and camera-trap monitoring as complementary sources of information to assess human–Asian badger (Meles leucurus) interactions across four sites in the Meng Mountains, China. We surveyed 400 residents and monitored 82 camera-trap stations from April 2024 to August 2026, representing 72,406 trap-nights. title: Contrasting CH 4 flux responses to distinct drought regimes and nitrogen enrichment in a temperate steppe
abstract: Summary Drought and nitrogen (N) deposition alter greenhouse gas fluxes, but how distinct drought scenarios interact with N enrichment to regulate the methane (CH 4 ) sink remains poorly understood. We conducted a 4‐yr field experiment in a temperate steppe to examine CH 4 fluxes under three drought regimes – early‐season intense drought (ID), mid‐season chronic drought (CD), and mid‐season reduced rainfall frequency (RF) – and N addition. title: Perceptions of Local Communities on Plant Diversity and Forest Patches Along the Rural–Urban Gradient in Central Highland of Ethiopia
abstract: ABSTRACT Local community perceptions are crucial for effective biodiversity conservation and sustainable land use management. However, limited attention has been given to how local community perceptions and ethnobotanical knowledge shift along spatial gradients. This study investigated local perceptions of forest patch dynamics and ethnobotanical knowledge shifts across a rural–urban gradient in Central highland of Ethiopia. title: Processing and functional valorisation of Aronia melanocarpa pomace: a critical assessment of extraction technologies and industrial implementation barriers
abstract: Chokeberry ( Aronia melanocarpa ) pomace is a major by-product of juice production and represents a rich source of polyphenols, dietary fibre, and functional compounds. Despite its high nutritional and technological potential, its industrial utilisation remains limited. This study provides a critical and application-oriented review of processing, extraction, and valorisation strategies for chokeberry pomace, with particular emphasis on technological performance, stability of bioactive compounds, and food-related applications. title: Psychiatric Pharmacotherapy and the Problem of Mechanistic Validation: A Critical Review
abstract: Psychiatric pharmacotherapy is among the most widely practiced and epistemically contested domains of contemporary medicine. Antidepressant consumption has risen significantly across OECD countries over the past decade, yet the neurobiological hypotheses used to justify these prescriptions remain unvalidated. This critical review examines the principal psychiatric drug classes, including antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, benzodiazepines and related anxiolytics, and psychostimulants. title: Physical disaster risk and sovereign debt distress
abstract: This paper examines how physical disaster risk affects sovereign debt distress in emerging and developing economies. Using a Generalized Panel Smooth Transition Regression model, I show that the sovereign consequences of storms and earthquakes are strongly state-dependent. Specifically, storm shocks increase default severity when fiscal space is constrained by high interest payment burdens, whereas stronger external conditions–healthier external balances and higher FDI inflows–dampen storm-related distress. title: Physical Properties of Carboxymethyl Cellulose (I): Solubility, Conformation and Supramolecular Aggregation
abstract: Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), commonly used as the sodium salt (NaCMC) and also known as cellulose gum, carmellose or E466, is an ionic cellulose ether widely used in foods, pharmaceuticals, drilling fluids, detergents, paper products and lithium-ion battery slurries. Its physical properties depend strongly on the degree and pattern of substitution, which control crystallinity, water solubility, chain conformation, supramolecular aggregation and rheology. title: Ontologizing (not: describing) language through epistemic practices: a case for critical epistemic pluralism
abstract: This contribution argues that language, as well as individual languages, are not autonomous objects merely described by epistemic practices. Rather, they are social phenomena brought into being – in other words, ontologized – through such practices. In the case of European standard languages, this is reflected in the process Auroux (1994) calls grammatisation, which was driven by professional language ontologizers and speakers alike and has contributed to the perception that languages are internally structured systems with fixed rules. title: The transition towards CSA as a relational model: shaping relational processes between farmers and governments, agri-food corporations and the financial sector
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) can enhance the mitigation and adaptation capacity of the sector. Yet progress towards CSA remains slow. Durable and scalable transformation requires more than technological adoption or changes in farmers’ capabilities; it depends on the relationships through which actors coordinate resources, interests, and institutional conditions. However, these interdependencies remain fragmented across the literature. title: Agent-based simulation of equity-oriented water reallocation under drought: A case study of the Geum River Basin
abstract: Study region : Geum River Basin, South Korea, a structurally heterogeneous watershed with 14 agricultural, 12 domestic/industrial intake, and 3 hydropower stakeholders. The basin has the highest agricultural water demand among South Korea’s six major river basins, with precipitation concentrated in the summer monsoon season, making dam operations critical for balancing competing water demands during irrigation. title: Pyelonephritis in cats and dogs - a scoping review
abstract: There is a lack of consensus regarding the diagnosis and treatment of bacterial pyelonephritis (PN) in dogs and cats. The aim of this scoping review was to increase knowledge by describing published scientific literature on the subject, specifically to collate definitions and diagnostic criteria, antimicrobial regimens, reported outcomes, and to identify knowledge gaps. A structured search was performed of the bibliographic databases Biosis, CAB Abstracts, Medline, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. title: Experimental enhancement of a double-slope solar still using external reflectors and nano-coated absorber plates for solar desalination
abstract: Freshwater scarcity, particularly in arid and off-grid regions, demands efficient and low-cost desalination technologies. While solar stills offer a sustainable solution, their low productivity remains a key limitation. Studies on the combined effect of external reflectors and nanoparticle-coated absorber plates in double-slope solar stills are scarce, and no such investigation has been conducted under the climatic conditions of Gondar, Ethiopia. title: New instantons for matrix models
abstract: The complete, nonperturbative content of random matrix models is described by resurgent-transseries—general solutions to their corresponding string-equations. These transseries include exponentially-suppressed multi-instanton amplitudes obtained by eigenvalue tunneling, but they also contain exponentially-enhanced and mixed instanton-like sectors with no known matrix model interpretation. title: Rubberized Geopolymer Concrete for Sustainable Construction: A Critical Review of Interface Engineering, Performance Trade-Offs, Durability, and Environmental Impacts
abstract: The use of Rubberized Geopolymer Concrete (RGC) represents a sustainable solution that can reduce reliance on Portland cement and make use of the potential uses of waste-tire rubber in construction. This review paper critically evaluates the constituent materials, design parameters, rubber pretreatment, fresh and hardened properties, durability, microstructure, and performance-enhancement measures of RGC. title: Heterogeneous architectures enable a 138x reduction in physical qubit requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing under detailed accounting
abstract: Abstract Quantum computer hardware is predicted to scale over hundreds of thousands of qubits coming online in the next decade. Despite significant theoretical and experimental QEC progress, quantum computer architecture has suffered a significant gap, with bottom-up physical-device-driven challenges largely disconnected from top-down QEC-code-driven considerations. In this work, we unify these two views, presenting a complete heterogeneous quantum computing architecture incorporating task-specific hardware selection and QEC encoding, and agnostic to code selection or physical qubit parameters

title: Immune dysregulation and adaptive resilience in response to air pollution
abstract: Air pollution is increasingly recognized as an important environmental factor associated with immune dysfunction and disease susceptibility. This narrative review critically synthesizes current evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which airborne pollutants may alter immune homeostasis and influence adaptive resilience. Particular attention is given to particulate, gaseous, semi-volatile, and biologically derived pollutants, including particulate matter, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, metals, wildfire smoke, pollen, and microbial aerosols. title: Differences in Serum Cytokine Profiles Between Vegetarians and Omnivores: Exploratory Assessment of Dietary Factors
abstract: Background/Objectives: Evidence suggests that plant-based diets are associated with reduced risk of chronic inflammatory diseases and lower circulating C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. However, associations with other inflammatory biomarkers, including interleukins (ILs), tumor necrosis factors (TNFs), interferons (IFNs), and chemokines, remain limited and inconclusive. This study compared multiple serum cytokine and chemokine levels between healthy vegetarians and omnivores. title: CineEducation: Il mondo del cinema nell'insegnamento delle lingue
abstract: Several contributions explore how film can open up spaces for critical reflection on social, cultural, and scientific issues. Mayer and Schwarz, in Windows and Mirrors: Approaching Diversity with the TV series Heartstopper, revisit the metaphor of films as both “windows” into other lives and “mirrors”. Wengler’s contribution, Feministischer Widerstand in virtueller Realität mit DRAW FOR CHANGE! We exist, we resist, takes this engagement further by examining the use of immersive media. title: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. title: Can You Say This for Me? Speaking Up by Proxy in Co-Located Discussion
abstract: Equal participation in co-located discussion is important for effective collaboration, yet people often hold back when they anticipate negative interpersonal or professional consequences, especially when raising a point requires voicing it themselves. We present SecondVoice, a mixed-reality system that enables people to speak up through an embodied virtual proxy. By separating what is said from who says it, SecondVoice brings hesitant points into the live spoken discussion without putting the speaker on the spot. title: Existence of Minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah Model via Covariance Floors on the Value Distribution
abstract: The Gaussian Mumford-Shah model segments an image into regions by minimizing a continuous multivariate Gaussian negative log-likelihood term plus a perimeter penalty. It is used for scalar- and vector-valued images, in particular hyperspectral images, but the existence of a minimizer in general is not guaranteed. The energy is unbounded below whenever the covariance of a single region degenerates, regardless of the perimeter of the regions. title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
abstract: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM. title: Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses
abstract: Agent harnesses enable large language models to act through tools, observe the results, and iteratively work toward a task goal. Verification checks and revises agents' work to improve output quality. Yet there is limited guidance on how harnesses should organize this effort. We study verification as an axis of test-time scaling by examining when to intervene, who checks the work, and how checking leads to revision. title: Measuring Healthcare Accessibility and Resilience for Smart and Connected Rural Communities: A Florida Panhandle Case Study
abstract: Rural communities in the United States face persistent healthcare disparities, with fewer providers and facilities, longer trips to care, lower health literacy, and weaker transportation and broadband infrastructure than their non-rural counterparts. title: Ferron-driven motion of non-collinear ferroelectric domain walls
abstract: We study the propagation of ferrons, the quanta of electric polarization waves, through a ferroelectric texture. We predict by analytic and numerical calculations that a $90^\circ$ domain wall (DW) operates as a beam splitter of longitudinal ferron and transverse optical phonon modes. An associated momentum-flux imbalance leads to forces that drive DW motion. title: Compass Correlations in a Square-Lattice Magnet
abstract: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. title: Perimeter shell properties of branched polymer adsorbents in various conformational states
abstract: The structural accessibility and perimeter shell properties of branched macromolecules are studied using Monte Carlo simulations on a simple cubic lattice. Constituent polymer chains of these macromolecules are constructed in an algorithmic way as: a set of collinear monomers; a self-avoiding walk (SAW); tigthly packed monomers. title: Towards Systematic Control of the Nucleon Gluon PDF with the Pseudo-PDF Method
abstract: We present updated lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) results for the unpolarized nucleon gluon parton distribution function (PDF) using the pseudo-PDF methodology. The calculation is performed at valence pion masses $M_π\approx 310$ and $690$ MeV on an $a \approx 0.06$ fm ensemble with $2+1+1$ flavors of highly improved staggered quarks (HISQ) generated by the MILC Collaboration. title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. title: Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
abstract: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. title: Enhancing Lunar PNT Performance Through Surface Station Enabled Radiometric Observables
abstract: Future lunar surface missions require reliable positioning for autonomous rover operations. Lunar navigation satellite systems may provide limited vertical positioning accuracy due to satellite availability and observation geometry, particularly during early deployment. This study investigates a radiometric navigation architecture in which a lunar surface station (SS) improves rover positioning through double-differenced satellite observations and additional surface-to-surface ranging. title: Practical Complete Tracking Through Gimbaled Unidirectional Actuation with Application to Multirotor UAVs
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of practical tracking control for robotic vehicles with gimbaled unidirectional actuators, with special application to multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles. A widely recognized obstacle to tracking control for multirotors is the free-fall singularity --- when a multirotor is commanded to free fall, the vehicle's target attitude becomes undefined. title: Dynamical plausibility of triple-assisted interaction in Be-star multiple systems
abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks, but the origin of their angular momentum remains uncertain. We investigate whether observed Be-star multiple systems are dynamically compatible with triple-assisted interaction, in which a tertiary companion drives Kozai-Lidov (KL) eccentricity excitation in an unresolved inner binary. We combine speckle-interferometric detections, reported inner periods, and proper-motion anomalies (PMa) with synthetic populations of hierarchical triples. title: Language Scent: Exploring Cross-Language Information Navigation
abstract: While multilingual users often switch between languages when seeking information, this process remains undersupported by current systems where information is typically siloed by language. Our formative study reveals that users select their search language based on its perceived value for their current information need, a concept we formalize as language scent. title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Relative geometry of nuclear mean fields through differential forms
abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. A pair invariant measures the angle between two density gradients, weighted by their magnitudes, and the coarea formula resolves its contribution over level surfaces. A triple invariant factorizes exactly into a weighted pair term and a directional term that measures the variation of a third field along the level-surface intersections. title: Dramarrator: Object-Based Audio Editing for Audio Drama Production from Books
abstract: Audio dramas weave dialogue, sound effects, and music into immersive stories. Creators often adapt books into audio dramas, but this process remains labor-intensive, requiring them to interpret source material, author scripts, generate audio assets, and assemble them on a timeline. Because story elements like characters and scenes manifest across many interdependent assets, a single change can ripple into manual updates across the entire project. title: Engineering Lightweight Burrows-Wheeler Transform Construction on the GPU via Prefix-Free Parsing
abstract: The Burrows-Wheeler transform (BWT) is the core of many compressed full-text indexes and most read aligners. The fastest BWT constructions on GPUs need about $20$ bytes of device memory per character, which severely limits the texts that can be processed there. For example, on our GPU with 24 GB device memory, this is only about 1200 MiB. Prefix-free parsing (PFP) can be used to reduce the memory requirements of BWT construction algorithms in main memory. title: Beyond urban boundaries: Percolation reveals land-consumptive growth in India
abstract: Cities often extend beyond their administrative boundaries, complicating assessments of urban sustainability. Using Global Human Settlement Layer data for India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975--2025), we develop a percolation-based framework for urban delineation. Within district-based regions, we apply unrestricted DBSCAN to spatial coordinates of 100-m cells with positive population and built-up surface. title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
abstract: Resonance-induced excessive vibrations can degrade performance, reduce reliability, and shorten the service life of engineering structures. To reduce the risk of resonance, structural natural frequencies are generally engineered to be shifted away from excitation frequencies. title: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment
abstract: The simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem arises in multi-robot applications such as perimeter security and environmental monitoring, where robots must survey a region of interest and coordinate to enclose targets once they are detected. Surveillance favors spatial dispersion for coverage, whereas containment requires target-centric cohesion for enclosure. abstract: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. title: The Hosts and Mass Distribution Function of the Most Massive Black Holes: Implications for the nHz Gravitational Wave Background
abstract: We use the core-radius, $r_γ,$ of a galaxy's central core along with a volume-limited sample of brightest cluster galaxies (BCG) to determine the $z=0$ mass distribution function of the most massive super-massive black holes (SMBH). title: Systematic Study of Neutrino-Nucleus Interactions for the DUNE Experiment
abstract: The recent generation of high-precision neutrino oscillation experiments, such as the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), relies on the accurate reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to determine fundamental parameters like Charge-Parity (CP) violation and the neutrino mass hierarchy. title: Size exclusion chromatography as a characterization tool for quality control of marine biopharmaceutical keyhole limpet hemocyanin
abstract: Abstract Keyhole limpet hemocyanin is a large metalloprotein present in hemolymph of the mollusk Megathura crenulata . This protein is highly immunogenic, making it very attractive to the biopharmaceutical industry, where it is used as a carrier protein for haptens, an adjuvant, or as a stand-alone biologic for the treatment of various cancer diseases. title: Seasonal cycle in surface seawater isotopic composition
abstract: Abstract. Data of stable isotopologs of water in the quality-controlled CISE-LOCEAN database provide an unprecedented sampling of the surface Atlantic Ocean and the southwest Indian Ocean. title: Updated Estimates of Radiocarbon‐Based Deep Ocean Circulation Age
abstract: Abstract The deep ocean circulation age based on radiocarbon was last determined almost 20 years ago, when digital archiving was not standard practice. This work updates the circulation age while making two improvements by using new nutrient data and modifying the calculation. The newly calculated circulation age is spatially more coherent and older in the deep North Pacific than before. The basin‐averaged circulation age for the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and Southern Ocean is respectively 256, 930, 689, and 326 years. The study confirms the centennial timescale of the world oceans.

title: Assessing biodiversity responses to climate change in South Africa using National Living Planet Index
abstract: South Africa’s biodiversity is increasingly threatened by climate change, yet system-specific impacts across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems remain under-quantified. This study examined whether rising surface air temperatures are statistically associated with vertebrate population trends, using a reweighted National Living Planet Index (LPI) to represent ecological change. The study aimed to test temperature–biodiversity relationships across the three ecological systems to inform alignment with the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) and the National Climate C

title: Pulses as a candidate crops for doubling farmers' income
abstract: In presence of newer and continuous challenges such as growing population with high demand for protein, shrinking agricultural land, unfavorable climate change coupled with increasing incidence of biotic and abiotic stresses, pulses as a candidate crop could contribute immensely towards doubling farmers income through effective efforts oriented towards diminishing cost of production through efficient technological options, site specific management of agro-inputs, quality assurances of these and employing resource saving measures. title: An update on hatchery success of olive ridley turtles ( Lepidochelys olivacea ) at Playa San Miguel, Costa Rica
abstract: Abstract Reducing threats to sea turtle eggs and hatchlings is critical for increasing hatching survival and recruitment, which supports the recovery of sea turtle populations. However, changes in temperature and rainfall from climate change have been identified as emergent risks to the nesting success of sea turtles globally. To reduce both of these threats and increase the nesting success of the beach, eggs are relocated to a protected area and covered in mesh (e.g., hatchery). title: Career Opportunities in Agriculture and Allied Sciences
abstract: The opportunities are available to work as research scientist, teacher, Marketing Manager, science writer, Quality Control Officer orproduction in-charge in the food, chemical and pharmaceutical industry, Analyst (Venture-Capitalist) Environmental /Safety Specialist.Biotechnology companies require corporate executives with business/ management degrees. A graduate in biotechnology can get a job in government sector such as universities and colleges, research institutes or at private centers as research scientist/assistant.

title: The Indonesia Education Report Card as a Catalyst for Data-Based Planning and School Quality Improvement
abstract: This systematic literature review examines the implementation and impact of the Indonesia Education Report Card (Rapor Pendidikan) within the Merdeka Belajar (Freedom to Learn) framework. The review synthesizes evidence from 33 studies focusing on Data-Based Planning (Perencanaan Berbasis Data, PBD), managerial applications, and implementation challenges. abstract: In this research, the validity of promises of strong employment perspectives for graduates of Turkish universities in transportation and logistics programs is investigated on the basis of the factual evidence. There are some differences among twelve programs in terms of employment percentage, time-to-first-job, and income level. title: New surfing: twenty-first century representations
abstract: In the late twentieth century, academic analyses increasingly challenged longstanding grand narratives of surfing pointing to smoothed evidence, tidied complexities and limited conceptualization, context and detail. Today, at the beginning of the second quarter of twenty-first century, academic analyses are highly alert to evidence and diverse surfing discourses and practices that in the identification of cultural heterogeneity expose tensions and contradictions as surfers of different ages, social classes, genders, sexualities, races and ethnicities compete for access to, and use of, surf bre

title: River Plastic Retention and Export across Europe
abstract: Rivers play a central role in the global distribution of plastic pollution. Despite recent research showing that the majority of plastic is not transported to the sea, most plastic transport models have not explicitly included plastic retention in rivers. We propose a new model to quantify micro- and macroplastic retention on land and in rivers, and export toward the sea. Of the 3.55 Mt year-1 of plastics emitted to the environment, only 0.1% of microplastics and 0.5% of macroplastics are exported from the river outlet. title: Diurnal Microclimate and Air Pollutant Patterns in Two Urban Parks in Dili
abstract: Urban parks can modify local thermal conditions and pollutant concentrations, yet field evidence from tropical coastal cities such as Dili, Timor-Leste, remains limited. This study compared microclimate and atmospheric pollutant patterns at 5 de Maio City Park and Lecidere City Park, focusing on air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, CO₂, PM₂.₅, and PM₁₀, alongside vegetation structure. Field observations used portable sensors to measure microclimate variables and pollutant concentrations, while canopy characteristics and leaf morphology were recorded. title: Integrated Hydraulic and Biological Monitoring Reveals Stage-Specific Passage Performance in a Vertical-Slot Fishway in the Upper Yangtze River
abstract: Dams fragment river networks, but post-construction evaluations of fishways often treat hydraulic suitability and biological performance separately. We assessed a 1486-m-long vertical-slot fishway comprising 326 pools at the Jinsha Hydropower Station in the upper Yangtze River during its first operating season. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Hydraulics and Mountain River Engineering

title: Ideological Divisions and Politicization of Foreign and Security Policy: Polish Political Parties’ Responses to the War in Ukraine
abstract: The article examines Polish political parties’ reactions to the war in Ukraine. The statements of Polish decision-makers and opposition demonstrate that, contrary to expectations derived from literature, the ‘rally round the flag’ effect was short and the war became quickly politicized. The analysis indicates that region-specific ideological divisions between Polish liberals and conservatives and parties’ different understanding of national interest led to politicization of foreign and security policy. The article strives to answer broader questions about domestic constraints on foreign and se

title: Phenotypic Selection, Genetic Variation, and Genome-Wide SNP Fingerprinting of Typhoon-Surviving Candidate Individuals in Casuarina equisetifolia
abstract: Casuarina equisetifolia L. is a key pioneer tree species for coastal shelterbelt plantations in tropical and subtropical regions. However, long-term reliance on a limited number of superior clones has narrowed its genetic base and reduced stress resistance, which necessitates the selection of elite individuals and the construction of molecular identities to support precise germplasm identification. title: DISTRIBUTION TREND OF HEAVY METALS AND PAHS IN SEDIMENT, POREWATER, AND WEST AFRICAN MUD CREEPER (Tympanotomy falcatus var. radula) FROM THE NIGER DELTA
abstract: Background: Petroleum-impacted Niger Delta creeks remain under-monitored, with few studies integrating sediment, porewater, and biota over time. Methods: Heavy metals (Fe, Zn, Ni, Cd, Cr), total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) and the 16 US EPA priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (ΣPAH₁₆) were measured monthly from March to August 2026 at three stations along Bille Creek, Rivers State, Nigeria. Samples comprised surface sediment, interstitial water and soft tissue of Tympanotonus fuscatus var. radula. Porewater physicochemical parameters were also measured. Analyses used ICP-OES, ICP-MS, GC
journal: Magna Scientia Advanced Biology and Pharmacy

title: An integrated chemical and biomarker approach using Ucides cordatus (Crustacea; Decapoda) to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two Amazonian estuaries
abstract: In this study, an integrated chemical and biomarker approach was applied using the mangrove crab Ucides cordatus to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two distinct Amazonian estuaries. Crabs were collected from São José Bay (A1-minimally impacted) and São Marcos Bay (A2-impacted by port activities) on the Amazon coast of Brazil. Simultaneously with crab sampling, physicochemical parameters and trace element levels in sediment and water samples were assessed. title: Sheep Industry Pivot Project: Global Comparative Review. Diversifying Market Pathways to Enhance Demand for Australian Sheep Products
abstract: This report forms the first stage of a two-year project led by Edith Cowan University to identify and commercialise new market pathways for Australian sheep products and by-products. The project responds to a period of significant structural change within the industry, most notably the legislated phase-out of live sheep exports by sea by May 2028, which is reshaping market dynamics and supply chain configurations. As an initial global benchmark and review, this report examines international best practice and emerging opportunities to inform industry transition, with the broader project focused

title: Cross-Sensor Comparison of SWOT Level-2 Pixel Cloud and ICESat-2 ATL13 Water-Surface Elevations over Tibetan Plateau Lakes
abstract: High-altitude lakes on the Tibetan Plateau (TP) are important components of regional water-cycle regulation and climate responses, yet their long-term monitoring remains challenging due to limited in situ observations and sparse spatial sampling of conventional satellite altimetry. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides two-dimensional observations of inland water-surface elevation (WSE), offering new opportunities for lake monitoring in remote regions. title: Evaluation of the Conformity of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) in the Processing of Frozen Scad at a Fish Processing Unit in Pati Regency
abstract: The implementation of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) is a fundamental requirement for maintaining the quality and safety of fishery products, including frozen scad. This study aimed to evaluate compliance with GMP requirements in frozen scad processing at a fish processing unit in Pati Regency, Central Java. The study was conducted from April to August 2025 using a descriptive observational method. title: Plakaty propagandowe Ligi Obrony Powietrznej i Przeciwgazowej oraz Ligi Morskiej i Kolonialnej z lat 20. i 30. XX wieku
abstract: PROPAGANDIST POSTERS OF THE AIRBORNE AND ANTIGAS DEFENCE LEAGUE AND THE MARITIME AND COLONIAL LEAGUE IN THE 1920S AND 1930S The poster – a genre of functional graphic design which appeared in Poland at the end of the 19th century – grew increasingly popular in the interwar period, becoming a significant element not only of Polish art, but also of Poland’s political, economic and social life. By performing numerous functions (including the spread of propaganda), it influenced the public opinion, shaping the views shared by Polish society. journal: Krzysztofory Zeszyty Naukowe Muzeum Historycznego Miasta Krakowa

title: Selected Trace Metals in Four Major Surface-Water Reservoirs of the Houston Metropolitan Area
abstract: This technical note reports selected trace metals in four major surface-water reservoirs associated with the Houston metropolitan region. Shoreline surface-water samples from Lake Houston, Lake Livingston, Lake Conroe, and Clear Lake were analyzed for As, Cd, Cu, Pb, Ni, and Zn by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) following U.S. EPA Method 200.8 quality-control procedures. Copper was the dominant analyte in all reservoirs, with mean concentrations of 9.82-15.5 µg L⁻¹. Measured concentrations were low, and arsenic and lead were below relevant federal drinking-water benchmark
journal: Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology

title: MICROPLASTICS AND THEIR EFFECTS: ENVIRONMENTAL DISTRIBUTION, ANALYTICAL CHARACTERIZATION, AND ECOLOGICAL AND HUMAN HEALTH IMPLICATIONS
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become a widespread environmental concern due to the extensive use of plastic materials and their persistence in environment and possible interaction with biota. Microplastics are generally considered to be small pieces of plastic particles with a size less than 5 mm and they can originate either from fragmentation of larger plastic debris or from direct emissions from industrial, waste and consumer products. journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology

title: Gender‐Based Violence in Pacific Fisheries
abstract: Coastal and offshore fisheries play a vital role in the Pacific Island economies, food security and cultural heritage. While the past two decades has seen increased recognition of gender dimensions of fisheries, managers, practitioners and industry partners have not yet tackled the problem of gender‐based violence (GBV) in the sector. Empirical research of GBV across Pacific fisheries is necessary to prevent the sector from inadvertently exacerbating violence, as well as to actively combat it. We conducted a scoping review to synthesise the evidence of GBV within formal and informal fisheries,
journal: New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research

title: Strong Relationship Between Betio precipitation on Tarawa Atoll (Kiribati) and Niño 3 SST Anomalies: Evidence from 1949 to 2025 Observations
abstract: Abstract Although the influence of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) on central Pacific rainfall is well recognized, quantitative assessments of contemporaneous and lagged relationships using official multi-decadal station observations remain scarce. We analyze monthly precipitation at Betio on Tarawa atoll for 1949–2025 provided by the Kiribati Meteorological Service, in relation to Niño 3 sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies. institutions: Japanese Red Cross College of Nursing

title: O transporte marítimo internacional no contraste entre estados desenvolvidos e em desenvolvimento e o princípio das responsabilidades comuns, porém diferenciadas e respectivas capacidades
abstract: International maritime transport plays a central role in the global economy while significantly contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, thus positioning itself within the contemporary debate on climate change. title: Public Administration of Seafarers' Labour Mobility under Martial Law: Toward a Model of Managed Mobility
abstract: Ukraine has long been one of the leading suppliers of qualified seafarers to the world merchant fleet. Most Ukrainian seafarers serve on foreign-flagged vessels, and their earnings are a significant source of foreign currency for the national economy. The introduction of martial law in 2022 created a governance dilemma for the state. Men of military age face restrictions on leaving the country, and the state has mobilization needs. title: Splice seeding as an alternative to conventional twine-wrapping for Saccharina latissima cultivation: biomass yield, substrate efficiency, and commercial implications
abstract: Abstract As the emerging temperate kelp industry seeks to scale in the west, established seeding methodologies, principally twine and direct seeding, present persistent bottlenecks in hatchery costs, space requirements, and operational reliability. This study evaluates splice seeding, a precision-spacing technique common in East Asian kelp aquaculture, as an alternative approach for Saccharina latissima cultivation. Seeded twine was cut into 3 cm sections and manually inserted into 12 mm twisted cultivation ropes at 5, 10, and 20 cm intervals; conventional twine-wrapping served as the control.

title: Strategic Priorities for Destination Management in Bali, Malang, and Yogyakarta: Tripadvisor Evidence
abstract: Destination management organizations need attraction-level evidence, but open records at that level are scarce and rarely tested for representativeness. This study audits a public dataset of 52,930 TripAdvisor review records, written by 33,530 users about 30 popular attractions across Bali, Malang, and Yogyakarta with reported visit years from 2013 to 2022, and asks which strategic priorities such records can responsibly support. publisher: Universitas Hindu Negeri I Gusti Bagus Sugriwa Denpasar

title: Mismanagement of Persistent Organic Pollutants: Policies and Implementation Challenges in Bangladesh
abstract: Despite the grave and escalating threat posed by persistent organic pollutants to human health, biodiversity, and marine ecosystems, Bangladesh has failed to establish effective mechanisms and public awareness for controlling their use. In recognition of the profound risks associated with Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), the international community adopted the Stockholm Convention in 2001, to which Bangladesh became a signatory by formulating its National Implementation Plan (NIP) in 2007.
