title: Arthropods communities in organic orchards and adjacent hedgerows on Terceira Island (Azores, Portugal): a dataset supporting biological control research
abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. title: Compound-Specific Carbon and Hydrogen Isotope Fingerprinting Resolves Dominant PAH Sources in Sediments from a Major Shipyard Harbor
abstract: Abstract Accurate source discrimination of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in industrialized coastal sediments remains challenging because multiple pyrogenic sources often exhibit overlapping molecular signatures. Despite frequent elevated PAH contamination in sediments near shipyards, the dominant sources remain poorly constrained. In this study, compound-specific dual isotope analysis (δ13C and δ2H) was applied to surface sediments from Okpo Harbor, a major shipbuilding center in South Korea. title: Evaluation of SWOT HR PIXC version D water level time series of small lakes
abstract: Abstract. Satellite altimetry has successfully monitored inland waters for more than 30 years and is increasingly important as the demand for freshwater grows and climate change accelerates. Launched in December 2022, the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite is the first to provide 2D spatially distributed elevation measurements, with a 21-day revisit time and better coverage depending on latitude and a nominal requirement to detect lakes as small as 0.06 km2. title: Constructing Local Identity Through the Cultural Wisdom of Phi Boong Tao Masks in Lat Khang, Phu Ruea District, Loei Province
abstract: This research article aimed to achieve the following objectives: 1) to investigate the historical background of Phi Boong Tao masks, 2) to explore the process of constructing local identity through Phi Boong Tao masks, and 3) to study conservation approaches for preserving the local wisdom of Phi Boong Tao mask-making in Ban Hai Tak, Lat Khang Sub-district, Phu Ruea District, Loei Province. title: RRBF-KMA: high-resolution radar–gauge merged precipitation dataset for South Korea (2016–2024)
abstract: Abstract. This study presents a long-term, high-resolution precipitation dataset over South Korea generated by merging nationwide composite radar reflectivity with dense rain gauge observations from the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). The dataset provides precipitation at 10-minute temporal resolution and 0.5 km spatial resolution on a regular grid of 2305 × 2881 pixels, covering the period from 2016 to 2024. title: Molecular detection of Rickettsia spp. in ticks (Ixodida: Argasidae and Ixodidae) and mites (Trombiculoidae) from a Brazilian taxonomic collection
abstract: Rickettsia species are arthropod-hosted endosymbionts classified into phylogenetic and serological groups, heterogeneous concerning their ecologies. This study aims to screen ticks and mites deposited in the Acarological Collection at Center of Taxonomical Collections at Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais, Brazil, for rickettsial occurrences, making available genetic data on hosts and bacteria. Endogenous mitochondrial markers for ticks and mitochondrial and nuclear genes for chiggers were sequenced for sample quality control and species identification. title: Unlocking delafloxacin fluorescence with 9-fluorenyl methyl chloroformate: A sensitive spectrofluorimetric method for pharmaceutical and plasma analysis with greenness and whiteness assessment
abstract: BACKGROUND: A highly sensitive spectrofluorimetric method was developed for the determination of delafloxacin based on fluorescence derivatization with 9-fluorenyl methyl chloroformate (FMOC-Cl). The derivatization reaction was performed at room temperature in borate buffer (pH 8.0), producing a strongly fluorescent derivative suitable for sensitive quantitative analysis. RESULTS: The formed fluorescent derivative exhibited maximum excitation and emission wavelengths at 264 and 314 nm, respectively. title: Comparative Assessment of Climate Change Impacts and Farmers’ Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices in Tropical Crops Production Systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens tropical crop production through erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and more frequent extreme weather events that reduce crop productivity and disrupt farm management. This study assessed climate change impacts and farmers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) across banana, cassava, and mixed-cropping systems in Davao Oriental, Philippines. A total of 450 farmers were surveyed using a structured questionnaire, and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). title: Not everywhere, not always: 30 targeted PFAS in ambient surface waters of Queensland, Australia
abstract: Abstract This study provides a summary of ambient concentrations of 30 commonly analysed perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) at 54 sites adjacent to various land use types across the east coast of Queensland, Australia. Sites were sampled for surface water every 2 months for a year (2019–2020). The results showed higher concentrations of PFAS in surface waters adjacent to major city areas (e.g. urban, industrial, residential land use types), and the lowest in surface waters adjacent to remote and regional areas (e.g. national parks, agriculture land use types). title: Improved Constraints on the Surface of LHS 3844 b from Its Mid-infrared Spectrum
abstract: Abstract The thermal emission spectra of terrestrial exoplanets provide a window into their surface compositions and corresponding geological processes. Close-in rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs are ideal targets for these studies, as observations have shown that most have little to no atmosphere. LHS 3844 b is an ultrashort-period super-Earth orbiting a nearby M dwarf, and is the most favorable target that does not have a dayside magma ocean. title: The Maya Preclassic in the mid‐elevations of tropical Mexico
abstract: ABSTRACT The Mesoamerican Preclassic period offers a laboratory for understanding how interactions between climate and early human occupation have shaped tropical ecosystems. Although the environmental history of the Maya lowlands during this period is relatively well known, mid‐elevation regions remain poorly understood. Here, we present a multiproxy sedimentary analysis from Lake Nahá, tropical mountains of southeastern Mexico, to elucidate climate–human interactions. title: Time-Series modeling of supply chain disruption drivers in ASEAN agri-food logistics networks
abstract: Disruptions in agri-food supply chains pose logistical and operational challenges for ASEAN member economies, whose agricultural sectors are simultaneously exposed to fluctuations in freight costs and climate-related production shocks. Prior time-series applications in shipping markets, agricultural commodity co-movement, and supply chain performance have generally examined these channels separately, and the joint transmission of these channels into ASEAN agri-food commodity logistics outcomes remains largely unexamined. title: Microbial contamination and risk assessment of lip care products
abstract: Cosmetic lip products have been used widely for aesthetic and therapeutic purposes, but repeated applications on the lips andenvironmental exposure could pose health risk to consumers. The aim of this study was to assess the microbial and heavy metalcontamination potential human health risk assessments of lip care cosmetic products sourced from different retail outlets. Cosmetic lip products which comprised of lip sticks, lip glosses, lip oils and lip balms were sourced from three retail outlets. title: Redescription of Uranoscopus bicinctus Temminck and Schlegel 1843 (Teleostei: Uranoscopidae): an integrative approach resolves taxonomic uncertainty related to variation in body colouration and oral luring organ
abstract: Abstract The highest diversity of the family Uranoscopidae (commonly known as stargazers) is in the Indo-Pacific. Many guidebooks and studies from the region have found the number and identification of species to be difficult to determine, especially in the genus Uranoscopus . Herein we redescribe Uranoscopus bicinctus Temminck and Schlegel 1843 to address new information on the morphological variation across the species’ range that has contributed to taxonomic confusion. title: EVI ‐Derived Spectral Stability of Central Chilean Sclerophyll Forests During the 2010–2025 Megadrought and a Nested 2019–2021 Hyperdrought
abstract: Abstract Climate change is increasing the frequency, severity and persistence of droughts, particularly in Mediterranean‐type ecosystems, where seasonal water limitation strongly constrains forest canopy condition and ecosystem functioning. Satellite‐derived vegetation indices provide a valuable approach for assessing canopy‐level responses to drought over broad spatial and temporal scales. title: Isopycnal Pathway for Small‐Particle Export in a Decaying Cyclonic Eddy Revealed by a BGC‐Argo Float
abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies influence carbon export through production, subduction, mixing, and particle redistribution. In this study, a BGC‐Argo float observed a deep particle layer in the twilight zone during the decay of a cyclonic eddy in the Northwest Pacific. The layer contained pigment‐depleted particles, remained confined to a narrow density range near 26 kg m −3 , and often exhibited particulate backscattering comparable to or greater than that of the overlying subsurface biomass maximum. title: Authentic Deeds And Notarial Accountability In Fisheries Vessel Transactions
abstract: Illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing is commonly addressed through patrols, vessel monitoring, licensing controls, and criminal enforcement. These measures remain incomplete when the legal identity and ownership history of a vessel cannot be verified. This article examines the legal function of authentic deeds in fisheries-vessel transactions and clarifies the accountability of Indonesian notaries within an ownership-transparency framework. journal: Pena Justisia Media Komunikasi dan Kajian Hukum

title: Microplastic contamination in surface water and sediments of Lake Canaçari, Central Amazon, during the dry season
abstract: Abstract Contamination by microplastics is an emerging environmental problem that is widely distributed across continental aquatic environments and may cause ecological impacts. This study evaluated the occurrence, concentration, and chemical and morphological characteristics of microplastics in surface waters and sediments from Lake Canaçari, comparing two areas with different land-use patterns within a floodplain system in the Central Amazon. title: Against the tide: law, illegality and the everyday in Corrubedo
abstract: Abstract ‘Corrubedo’ is one of many stories Ben Judah tells in This is Europe: The Way We Live Now . It follows Graña, a fisherman from the titular Galician town who, faced with the erosion of his community, is forced to answer what Martha Nussbaum terms a ‘tragic question’ and joins the crew of Kunlun , a vessel sailing to Antarctica to poach Patagonian toothfish. Given the ubiquity of European law, in this article we interrogate its role in shaping the choices available to him and his everyday. title: Comparative assessment of phytoplankton community using different filtration methods based on environmental DNA metabarcoding—a case study of Caohai Wetland
abstract: In environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, the choice of filter membrane material and pore size governs DNA enrichment, detection sensitivity, and taxonomic representativeness of aquatic communities. This study employed eDNA metabarcoding to evaluate the influence of various filter membranes on the phytoplankton community within Caohai Wetland. Four membrane materials with a pore size of 0.22 μm were tested: mixed cellulose esters (MCE), polyethersulfone (PES), nylon (NY), and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and three pore sizes were tested with the MCE membranes: 0.22 μm, 0.45 μm, and 0.8 μm.

title: Blue injustice: competing claims for freshwater forage fisheries
abstract: Abstract This paper draws on blue justice scholarship to examine how inequalities are intensified as small forage fish move between “fish as food” and “fish as feed,” highlighting distributional justice as a key lens for understanding pressures on fisheries-based households. Forage fish, which can be consumed in diverse forms or diverted into aquafeed (including direct feed and fishmeal), are contested resources among artisanal fishers, fish processors, and small producer fish farmers in Cambodia’s Tonlé Sap region. title: DRY FISH MARKETS IN INDIA: TRADE PERFORMANCE, PRICE TRENDS AND MARKET CHALLENGES
abstract: The paper mainly centered upon dryfish outlets in India. It has found that dried fish market in India is a key part of the fisheries industry providing income to producers traders manufacturers and consumers. It is marked by limited production, price differences across regions, several ways of taking goods to markets, and the increase of both domestic demand and exports. Primary hurdles relate to the lack of storage, poor sanitation, difficult transportation, changing prices, and underdeveloped markets. journal: International Journal of Management Public Policy and Research

title: Paralytic shellfish toxin production in Alexandrium minutum (Dinophyceae): Insights from omics integration using toxigenic and nontoxigenic recombinant progeny
abstract: Paralytic shellfish toxins (PSTs) are produced by certain species of cyanobacteria and dinoflagellates. Part of the PST biosynthetic pathway has been elucidated in cyanobacteria, and the implication of some sxt genes has been confirmed by experimental studies. Contrary to cyanobacteria, knowledge about PST biosynthesis in dinoflagellates is more limited and generally restricted to comparative studies with the cyanobacterial pathway. title: Comparative Danio rerio (Hamilton, 1822) embryo toxicity of three sunscreen products: mortality, coagulation, and morphological outcomes
abstract: Three commercial sunscreen formulations, organic (A), mineral (B), and hybrid (C), containing UV filters and cosmetic additives, were evaluated for developmental toxicity in zebrafish, Danio rerio (Hamilton, 1822) embryos. title: Sovereignty and meteorology: China, France, and the 1932 Xisha Islands dispute
abstract: An intense debate broke out between China and France over the sovereignty of the Xisha Islands in the early 1930s, in which meteorology played a key role. abstract: Disaster outcomes in rural Indonesia are shaped not only by the intensity of hazards but also by the social relationships through which communities communicate, cooperate, and access resources. This integrative review examined how community social capital contributes to disaster resilience in rural Indonesia and under what conditions it fails to do so. Founded in 1600 as a joint-stock corporation under a royal charter, the Company’s objectives were progressively converted from trade monopoly into the de facto domination of South Asia over the following two centuries. abstract: Pakistan consumes an estimated 500 million disposable pens annually, generating roughly 2,300 tonnes of unrecovered plastic waste. No domestic manufacturer currently produces a pen made from zero virgin plastic. Resource development, such as mining, and climate change-impacted natural phenomena like permafrost thaw can introduce contaminants into aquatic systems. abstract: Forward-deployed tripwire forces are one tool used to enhance the credibility of security guarantees. Conventional wisdom holds that these vulnerable deployments improve deterrence by increasing the credibility of the sending state’s commitment to fight to defend the host, but recent scholarship has questioned their effectiveness. Critics argue that because tripwires lack capability, and publics do not punish leaders who back down, they do not deter. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how encounters with ruins and spectres in the field inform (post)colonial trajectories of exploration and research. abstract: India’s agricultural trade remained in surplus during 2003-25, showing stronger stability than total merchandise trade and resilience in the face of global downturns and the pandemic. title: The Establishment of Christian Hegemony through the Doctrine of Discovery
abstract: This essay examines the establishment of Christian hegemony through the theological and legal framework of the Doctrine of Christian Discovery (DoCD), tracing its roots from medieval Europe to its application in the Americas. Drawing on postcolonial and decolonial theorists, the work interrogates how Christian identity was formed in opposition to the “proximal” and “distal” other—Jews, Muslims, pagans, and later Indigenous peoples—through a dominion theology that fused religious exclusivity with political supremacy. abstract: Abstract Remediation of mercury (Hg)-contaminated sediments seeks to reduce Hg and methylmercury (MeHg) transport and exposure. title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles.

abstract: Abstract Legumes are increasingly promoted as a diversification strategy to mitigate externalities in low‐diverse cropping systems. title: The perceived reasons for participation in private tutoring in the Sultanate of Oman
abstract: Private tutoring (PT) is becoming increasingly widespread around the globe, and the Sultanate of Oman is no exception. Even though the Omani educational system witnesses continuous development, PT is gaining popularity. The present research paper aims to explore the reasons that drive the need for private tutoring lessons as perceived by the students, parents, and teachers. Three distinct questionnaires were developed based on a review of pertinent literature to collect data for this descriptive analytical study. Participants in the study included 261 students, 214 parents, and 87 teachers, an
journal: International Journal of Education and Practice

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
abstract: Abstract Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. title: Impact of Acetate, Formate, and Lactate Background Electrolytes on Nitrate and Nitrite Separation by Capillary Electrophoresis
abstract: This study comparatively evaluated acetate, formate and lactate background electrolytes (30 mM, pH 4.0) for the determination of nitrate and nitrite by capillary electrophoresis. Standard solutions (5, 25 and 50 µg mL-1) were used to investigate the effects of electrolytes on migration time, theoretical plate number, peak symmetry and resolution. Acetate generated the highest electroosmotic flow mobility but resulted in the longest migration, the lowest theoretical plate numbers and pronounced peak fronting. journal: International Journal of Chemistry and Technology

title: Influence of vetch– Brachiaria intercropping and phosphorus fertilisation on soil nutrient dynamics and forage mineral composition of Brachiaria varieties under a Mediterranean climate
abstract: A field experiment consisted of a 4 × 4 × 2 factorial layout in a randomised complete block design with four replicates at the Mariendahl and Welgevallen sites, Western Cape province, South Africa. Treatments comprised four phosphorus (P) levels (0, 20, 40 and 60 kg P ha-1), four Brachiaria (syn. Urochloa) varieties and two cropping systems (grass monoculture and vetch intercropping). title: Stable Isotope-Assisted Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometry Reveals Uptake, Metabolism, and Resolvin Biosynthesis from Docosapentaenoic Acid in Atlantic Salmon ( Salmo Salar L.) Hepatocytes
abstract: Abstract Docosapentaenoic acid (DPA, 22:5n-3) is an intermediate omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid with emerging biological significance, yet its metabolic fate in fish remains poorly defined. Stable isotope-assisted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) was applied to trace the uptake, intracellular retention, and bioconversion of deuterium-labeled DPA (DPA-d5) in primary hepatocytes from Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar L.). title: Competencias investigativas del docente universitario y su impacto en el acompañamiento de tesis
abstract: La elaboración de una tesis constituye una etapa compleja de la formación universitaria donde el estudiante articula decisiones teóricas y metodológicas con la orientación de un docente asesor. El estudio tuvo como objetivo determinar el impacto de las competencias investigativas del docente universitario en el acompañamiento de tesis de pregrado en educación. Se realizó una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, retrospectiva y documental con 32 díadas asesor–tesis de cuatro universidades privadas peruanas. La trayectoria investigativa de cada asesor se reconstruyó mediante una ventana

title: Let's talk data archiving: practical insights into FAIR and long-term data management from early-career perspectives
abstract: Research data provide the basis for scientific discovery, yet their long-term value depends on careful curation and documentation. Data archiving is often treated as a final administrative task rather than an integral part of research. This report summarizes key insights from an interactive seminar organized by the Association of Polar Early Career Scientists (APECS) Germany, which explored practical approaches to making data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) from early-career perspectives. Speakers from PANGAEA, the Arctic Data Center, and the (AC) 3 project highlighted
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

title: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR LIFECYCLE SAFETY MANAGEMENT AND ASSURANCE OF RECHARGEABLE LITHIUM BATTERIES FOR MILITARY APPLICATIONS: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF INDUSTRIAL, MILITARY, AND SPACE SAFETY DOCUMENTS
abstract: Rechargeable lithium batteries are used across diverse military platforms, where safety management must address not only battery design and testing but also operational conditions, handling, incident response, and end - of - use management. This study conducted a structured comparative document analysis of 14 industrial, military, space, and operational safety documents to develop an integrated lifecycle safety management and assurance framework for military battery applications. Safety requirements were organized into seven lifecycle safety management domains comprising 23 detailed elements.

title: Persian Literature and Cultural Life in Central Asia: From Civilizational Roots to the Reform Movements in Bukhara (Late Nineteenth Century – Early Twentieth Century)
abstract: This study examines the transformation of Persian literary and cultural life in Bukhara and its wider Central Asian environment from the nineteenth century to the early twentieth century, with particular attention to the relationship between literature, education, literacy, journalism, and cultural identity. Rather than treating literary modernization as an exclusively aesthetic development, the study approaches it as part of a wider transformation in the production, circulation, and social function of knowledge. journal: Emirati Journal of Education and Literature

title: RTMB: An R Package for Fitting Latent Variable Models With Template Model Builder
abstract: Hierarchical and latent variable models are fundamental in ecology, fisheries science, and epidemiology, but fitting them efficiently relies on automatic differentiation (AD) combined with approximations such as the Laplace approximation. Template Model Builder (TMB) has become a standard tool for this kind of inference in R, but it requires users to write the objective function in C++, which is a potential obstacle for those unfamiliar with it, slows model iteration through compilation, and complicates debugging and simulation. title: Institutional Management Capacities of Supply Chain of the Essential Household Commodity: Validated Capacity Building Framework
abstract: The study assessed the management for supply chain of the essential household commodity–cooking fuel at Palo, Leyte during CY 2025. Cooking fuel stands as an essential household commodity directly linked to food security, public health, and livelihood stability. Yet in disaster-prone municipalities such as Palo, Leyte, supply chains remain vulnerable to typhoons, price volatility, transport disruptions, and institutional fragmentation. This study assessed cooking fuel supply chain management and institutional resilience capacities in Palo, Leyte, with the ultimate goal of developing a context-

title: Reconstructing the dietary history of Japanese black bears through stable isotope analysis of hair
abstract: Abstract The population of Japanese Asiatic black bears ( Ursus thibetanus japonicus ) has been increasing in Japan, leading to more human–bear conflicts, including crop damage and an increase in the lethal removal of bears. However, it remains difficult to verify whether captured bears were directly involved in such damage. This study focused on the carbon and nitrogen stable isotope ratios in guard hair, based on the premise that growing hair records dietary intake, to develop a method for reconstructing the dietary histories of captured individuals. title: Tripartite Arrangement in Human Resource Capability and Collaborative Competence Based: Enhance Action Plan in Public Service and Governance
abstract: Based on the findings, personnel from DPWH, PNP and DepEd demonstrate a strong human resource capability and collaborative competence, confirming that personnel possess the necessary skills and attitudes to work across agencies. The strongly agree rating on the level of collaborative competence of the personnel proves that better individual and organizational capacities directly lead to more effective inter-agency cooperation. title: Asymmetric Migration Shapes Genetic Structure of the Invasive Avian Vampire Fly ( Philornis downsi ) Across the Galápagos Islands
abstract: Biological invasions on islands provide a natural framework to study how dispersal and connectivity influence evolutionary and ecological processes. The avian nest parasitic fly, Philornis downsi-first recorded in Darwin's finch nests in 1997-causes high mortality in endemic land birds, yet its inter-island and sex-specific patterns of dispersal and genetic structure remain poorly understood. title: Diferencias de género y edad en la competencia Aprender a Aprender en la universidad
abstract: Aprender a aprender es una competencia para organizar y regular el propio aprendizaje en función de las necesidades, del contexto y principalmente de los objetivos trazados. El artículo expone los resultados de un estudio que tuvo como objetivo comparar las diferencias de la competencia aprender a aprender en función del género y edad de un grupo de 436 estudiantes universitarios de Lima-Perú. El diseño fue comparativo transversal y para la recolección de datos se utilizó el cuestionario de evaluación de la competencia Aprender a Aprender, de Gargallo-López et al. (2021). title: Advances in Coordination Chemistry–Based Sensors for Monitoring Toxic Metal Pollutants in Aquatic Environments
abstract: Toxic metal contamination of surface water, groundwater and wastewater threatens ecosystems and the communities that depend on them. Conventional methods such as atomic absorption spectrometry and inductively coupled plasma-based techniques are reliable but need laboratory facilities, which restricts routine monitoring in remote and resource-limited settings. Coordination chemistry links metal-ion recognition to measurable optical or electrochemical responses. journal: Journal of Ethnobiology and Environmental Research

title: Cross-national validation of the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale for Youth (DASS-Y) in Lebanese and Chinese adolescents
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale for Youth (DASS-Y) has been validated in several countries, but its measurement equivalence between Middle Eastern and East Asian adolescents remains untested, and prior validations primarily relied on single analytic approaches without examining complex factor structures or brief screening forms. This study evaluated the DASS-Y in Lebanese adolescents enduring sociopolitical strain and Chinese adolescents under comparatively stable conditions. title: Unilateral cross-feeding constrains adaptive evolution, even in the producer without direct fitness effects
abstract: Cross-feeding interactions are pervasive in microbial communities and profoundly shape community structure, stability, and function. While previous studies have explored how cross-feeding affects evolvability, this work has predominantly focused on bidirectional mutualistic interactions in engineered auxotrophic systems where both partners reciprocally exchange essential metabolites. However, most metabolic interactions in natural microbial communities are unidirectional, with organisms feeding on the metabolic waste products of other species. title: The wellbeing triad: modelling the interdependent pathways of healthcare workers' happiness, motivation, and health in a rural setting in Kenya
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study evaluated the relationships and recursive pathways among healthcare workers linking happiness, work motivation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in a rural setting in Kenya. METHODS: The author used a cross-sectional dataset collected across all hospitals (n=24) at the secondary and tertiary healthcare levels in the rural county of Meru. Using STATA v15.1, a three-stage least squares (3SLS) regression model was applied to assess the bidirectionality of the topic under study. title: Bebeklerde Ve Çocuklarda Memeli Dalış Refleksi (MDR): Fizyolojik Temeller, Gelişimsel Özellikler Ve Meta-Analiz

title: Cultivating ISI: Shaping the Future of Idiomatics in Language Education and Research
abstract: This article advances the evolving field of Idiomatics, devoted to the rigorous study of idiomatic and figurative language. It is organized into five main sections, framed by a preamble and a prologue that establish the conceptual stage, and concluded by an epilogue and a coda that reflect on the work’s implications and future directions. Positioned between inherited nomenclatures and emergent inquiry, the article confronts a labyrinth of competing terms that have long obscured conceptual clarity. title: Polyphonic Resistance: Countering Erasure in Palestinian Poetry
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how contemporary Palestinian poetry articulates and potentially disrupts the exclusion of experiences of harm from dominant frameworks of representation. Against the background of erasure, we examine how poems address epistemic injustice and intervene in the politics of visibility and voice, notably in the context of the annihilation of Gaza. Situating Gaza within historic harm that extends back to the Nakba, our analysis foregrounds the longue durée of harm. title: Understanding socio-economic valuation in UK urban development through the lens of power
abstract: Improving social and environmental outcomes, especially health outcomes, is a central priority in the development of urban areas, and there have been many attempts in the UK and internationally to model and measure these outcomes in order to improve quality of life. Quantitative methods often appear to carry more weight than qualitative methods, though what weight they are afforded by different actors and stakeholders across the many systems of urban development is not well understood. title: In silico-guided discovery and experimental validation of VPW from Nannochloropsis oceanica as an antioxidant cytoprotective peptide and a protectant against H₂O₂-induced C3G degradation
abstract: Although Nannochloropsis oceanica (N. oceanica) is widely exploited for feed and oil production, its protein fraction remains underutilized. Here, we developed a virtual-to-experimental workflow to discover antioxidant peptides from N. oceanica protein hydrolysates. Sequential in silico screening of 356 peptides yielded six candidates, which were docked against six antioxidant-related core targets; among them, VPW showed favorable binding, with a best binding energy of −7.61 kcal/mol. title: New findings on the occurrence and removal of seven key pollutants in secondary battery wastewater treatment plants
abstract: This study provides the first comprehensive characterization of seven key pollutants [lithium (Li), cobalt (Co), aluminum (Al), manganese (Mn), nickel (Ni), copper (Cu), and sulfate (SO 4 )] in production-process wastewater from five major secondary battery-related industrial sectors and in 26 full-scale secondary battery wastewater treatment plants (SBWTPs) treating wastewater from nine sectors. title: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
abstract: BACKGROUND: Urbanisation imposes pervasive environmental change, yet it remains unclear whether evolutionary responses to cities are largely idiosyncratic or whether similar selective pressures across cities repeatedly generate predictable genomic outcomes. RESULTS: Here, we analyse whole-genome data from 524 individuals of three widespread bumble bee species sampled across nine independent urban-rural pairs in Central Europe to test whether urban environments drive parallel evolutionary responses across cities and species. title: Hedonic Analysis of Cassava Product Attributes' Influence on Observed Market Prices. A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Kilifi County, Kenya
abstract: Cassava commercialisation is increasing in Kenya, mainly due to recent emphasis on its role in enhancing food security and income generation. However, smallholder cassava farmers still receive low prices for their products, constraining their ability to maximise returns. There is limited empirical evidence on how cassava product attributes influence market prices. Understanding the product attribute-price relationship will enable farmers to orient their production, marketing and value addition to attract better prices. journal: East African Journal of Agriculture and Biotechnology

title: Language and the Environment: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Flood Narratives in South-Eastern Nigeria
abstract: Flood has become one of the most destructive environmental hazards in South-Eastern Nigeria. It displaces communities, destroys farmland, and reshapes public discourse on climate vulnerability. While hydrological and policy studies have examined its physical and administrative dimensions, little attention has been paid to how language constructs, naturalizes, or contests the disaster's meaning. title: Long-term land-atmosphere carbon monoxide exchange from a tall tower in a rural Central European region
abstract: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric trace gas, significantly influencing the atmosphere's oxidative capacity and indirectly affecting climate. However, the net land-atmosphere exchange of CO remains highly uncertain due to the scarcity of long-term monitoring. This study presents and analyses a 10-year-long CO flux data series from a tall-tower eddy covariance (EC) system operated in a rural Central European region. title: Functional Food Innovation of Mekai Leaf (Albertisia Papuana Becc.) Catfish Sticks Based on Community Empowerment in Tuwung Village
abstract: The community service program in Tuwung Village, Central Kalimantan, aims to address overproduction and fluctuations in catfish prices through downstreaming and food diversification. The solution offered is the transfer of technology for producing catfish sticks seasoned with natural Mekai leaf (Albertisia papuana Becc.) as an organic, non MSG flavor enhancer. title: Investigating emerging contaminants in dams from the Vhembe District in Limpopo and, for the first time, in the Orlando Dam, Gauteng Province, South Africa
abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including certain organophosphate pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, and metals, as well as pharmaceuticals such as antiretroviral drugs (ARVs), are contaminants of increasing concern in freshwater sources in South Africa (SA). One surface water sample from each site was collected from dams in an urban area, Gauteng Province, and from a rural area, the Vhembe District in the Limpopo Province in SA. title: A Study on Impact of Incoterms on Freight Cost and End-To-End Documentation
abstract: International trade rests on a quiet but consequential piece of legal shorthand: the Incoterm. A three-letter code decides who pays for freight, who insures the cargo, who clears customs at either end, and who absorbs the cost when something goes wrong along the way. For a freight forwarder sitting between exporter and importer, that code is not background detail — it is the operating instruction for every shipment that crosses the desk. title: The Aesthetics of Control, The Step of the Masses - The Processing of Folk Dances and Its Social Impact in Communist Albania (1945–1990)
abstract: Purpose: This paper aims to analyze the profound transformation of Albanian folk dances during the communist regime (1945–1990), focusing on artistic-aesthetic changes and the social impact of this phenomenon. title: Phenolic Diglycoside Biomarkers: Assessing 2020 Wildfire Smoke Impacts on Oregon Pinot noir Wines Alongside Sensory and Marketplace Data
abstract: Abstract This study presents the first AVA-resolved retrospective assessment of wildfire smoke impacts on 2020 Oregon Willamette Valley Pinot noir by merging phenolic diglycoside (PDG) biomarker concentrations with sensory appraisals and marketplace performance. Analysis of 90 commercial wines representing all 12 Willamette Valley AVAs revealed that most lots lacked molecular evidence of substantial wildfire smoke exposure. title: Im/mobilities and the Occupying Gaze
abstract: This article considers how the occupying gaze transforms bodies and objects into suspended sites of gendered and political violence. While in peacetime waiting suggests ennui and stasis, the im/mobility that occurs at Israeli checkpoints is entangled with power, including who decides how time is valued, and how and whose bodies move (and where to). Against this backdrop, the gaze transforms bodies and objects into political and gendered sites of violence. title: Haematology and biochemistry parameters for koalas ( Phascolarctos cinereus ) on Raymond Island, Victoria : use of point‐of‐care analysers
abstract: Biochemistry and haematology analytes can provide information on the health status of individual animals or populations in direct comparison to expected values or reference intervals developed using the same analysis methodology from a healthy reference population of the target species. Point-of-care analysers are increasingly used in the assessment of wildlife health; however, their effective use in wildlife species requires establishment of appropriate expected values from clinically healthy animals. title: Legitimizing war: continuity and change in US just war discourse on Iraq (2003) and Iran (2026)
abstract: This article examines the continuity and transformation of US just war discourse by comparing George W. Bush’s 2003 Iraq address and Donald Trump’s 2026 Iran remarks. It investigates whether the 2003 pattern of just war legitimation persists in 2026 and how its discursive realization has shifted. Using Critical Discourse Analysis and the Discourse-Historical Approach, the study reconstructs a five-element pattern of just war discourse: conflict management, negative other-presentation, positive self-presentation, historical contextualization, and a call to action. title: Comparative Analytical Characterization and Chromatographic Profiling of Virgin and Recycled Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and its copolymeric variants represent a critical class of thermoplastic polymers widely deployed in packaging, industrial textiles, and consumer products due to their tensile strength, dimensional stability, and chemical resistance. PET materials are broadly categorized into virgin polyester (vPET), derived directly from petrochemical feedstocks, and recycled polyester (rPET), produced via the mechanical or chemical reprocessing of postconsumer polymer waste. title: First record of Youngia japonica (L.) DC. (Asteraceae: Tribe Cichorieae) in Aotearoa / New Zealand
abstract: We report the first verified records of Youngia japonica subsp. japonica (Asteraceae: Tribe Cichorieae) in northern Aotearoa / New Zealand. Five populations have been discovered across Tāmaki Makaurau / Auckland and Te Tai Tokerau / Northland. Specimens were identified using morphological characteristics consistent with flora descriptions, and verified through sequencing using nrDNA ITS (ITS1 and ITS2 spacer regions) and the chloroplast trnH-psbA intergenic spacer. title: Evaluation of Wheat Genotypes for Combined Heat and Drought Stress Tolerance
abstract: A field experiment was carried out from November 2021 to April 2022 to assess the tolerance of five wheat genotypes to combined heat and drought stress. The study followed a split plot design with three replications. The main plot treatment consisted of two growing conditions (normal condition and combined heat and drought condition) and the sub-plot treatments consisted of five wheat genotypes (BARI Gom 29, BARI Gom 30, BARI Gom 31, BWMRI Gom 3 and BAW 1290). title: Sustaining Life under Extraction: Environmental Justice and Community Capabilities in Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap
abstract: Extractive pressures threaten collective life despite economic gains. This study examines how environmental injustice reshapes substantive opportunities to sustain livelihoods and pursue valued collective futures. Environmental justice and community capabilities frame readings of Anindita S. Thayf’s Tanah Tabu [Taboo Land] and Korrie Layun Rampan’s Api Awan Asap [Fire, Clouds, and Smoke]. journal: East Asian Journal of Multidisciplinary Research

title: Gap Analysis of Good Manufacturing Practice Compliance in Fruit Crunch Production: A Case Study of CV Sahabat Pangan
abstract: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) serve as a fundamental prerequisite for ensuring food safety and quality by controlling potential hazards throughout the production process. This study aimed to evaluate the level of GMP compliance at CV Sahabat Pangan based on the Regulation of the Minister of Industry of the Republic of Indonesia No. 75/M-IND/PER/7/2010 using Gap Analysis, identify existing nonconformities, and propose corrective actions. title: Mixing intensity and spatial strength variability in laboratory deep-mixed columns
abstract: Deep mixing method (DMM) column quality is commonly characterised by the coefficient of variation (COV) of unconfined compressive strength, which cannot distinguish depth-wise variability from local horizontal heterogeneity. Internal strength variability was characterised for laboratory deep-mixed columns prepared at four blade revolution counts, T2, T4, T6 and T8 (2000, 4000, 6000 and 8000 rev/m), using a miniature DMM apparatus on kaolin clay. title: Human in vitro airway models to assess point-of-contact respiratory toxicity of surfactants: development and evaluation of a repeated-exposure study design
abstract: Repeated-dose exposure studies can provide insights into the toxicity of test substances, including dose-response relationships, cumulative effects, delayed responses, and reversibility of effects. A limited number of in vitro studies have assessed the effects of repeated exposure of respiratory cells to chemicals applied as liquids (via direct pipetting). title: Transforming Canadian Federal Governance in a Polycrisis
abstract: Abstract Since 1995, scientific consensus has linked human activity to climate change, yet the political and financial power of the carbon economy remains entrenched. Under conditions of polycrisis, many states continue to miss emissions targets and, in some cases, retreat from climate commitments. Transformative political will is therefore urgently needed to achieve carbon neutrality. abstract: Introducción: La identidad es un fenómeno que, por su naturaleza social y psicológica, no puede definirse de manera estática. Presentamos aquí una revisión bibliográfica narrativa con el objetivo de proveer un panorama de conocimiento en torno a los mecanismos de conceptualización, para estructurar una tipología de las identidades identificadas en el corpus. abstract: Background: Extreme heat presents a growing challenge for nursing education in tropical regions. However, there is limited qualitative evidence regarding students’ experiences across commuting, campus, and learning environments. Aim: This study explores nursing students’ experiences of heat, its perceived impact on academic functioning, and both personal and institutional responses. abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive legal audit investigating the systemic water shortage in Bengaluru and its direct implications on fundamental rights, particularly the right to life, dignity, and livelihood under the Constitution of India. With a population exceeding 13 million heavily reliant on distant river supplies and rapidly depleting groundwater, Bengaluru faces a recurring structural deficit, marked by a documented official shortfall of over 500 million liters per day and widespread drying of borewells. title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
abstract: Abstract Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. Philosophical concepts of value, truth and memory are linked to the theory and practice of conservation and architecture in order to shed light on the current crisis of environmental values, resulting from the deterioration of the national conservation system, loss of authenticity, damage to integral value – the memory of the environment and architectural erosion. abstract: The European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages recently broke new ground by supporting two languages that had previously died; and not just under its fairly tokenistic, unburdensome Part II, but the much more extensive (and expensive) Part III. Manx Gaelic, having been recognised by the United Kingdom under Part II in 2003, went on to Part III status in 2020, followed by Cornish in 2025 (CoE, 2021; 2025a, 2026). abstract: Genre fiction often turns to librarians, archivists, and knowledge institutions when information becomes unstable and ethically charged. Drawing on a curated corpus of fiction across fantasy, science fiction, horror, dystopian, and historical traditions, this thematic critical review uses close reading and interpretive synthesis to show how knowledge-keepers stage conflicts over access, censorship, preservation, authority, and collective memory. title: Photometric variability of blue supergiants: Constraints on stellar masses and evolutionary stages
abstract: Blue supergiants are crucial to understanding the evolution of massive stars. However, their formation, mass loss, and pulsational properties remain poorly understood. Although distinguishing between pre- and post-red supergiant (RSG) phases is challenging, stellar pulsations provide valuable constraints on their masses and evolutionary status. This study analyzes TESS light curves of six blue supergiants with high luminosity-to-mass ratios to identify periodicities. abstract: Excessive smoke from diesel locomotives signals incomplete combustion and degrades engine performance and air quality. This exploratory mixed-methods study examined factors associated with smoke level in CC206 locomotives running B40 biodiesel at a depot in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, using records from January to June 2026, and ranked maintenance risks. abstract: Nigeria's dependence on imported goods, foreign expertise, and external technologies across critical sectors of its economy has significantly constrained domestic industrialization, employment generation, technology acquisition, and sustainable national development. title: A Practical Formulation for Seismic Damage Accumulation on Multiple Mainshock‐Aftershock Sequences Based on Disaggregation of the Mainshock Hazard
abstract: ABSTRACT Earthquakes often occur in clusters (foreshocks, mainshocks, and aftershocks) and can lead to cumulative structural damage. Many studies have extended traditional performance‐based earthquake engineering (PBEE) to account for damage accumulation in multiple mainshock‐aftershock (MS‐AS) sequences using Markov chain processes and state‐dependent fragilities. title: Toward a Psychology of Science: A Dynamic Cognitive Model of the Evolution of Scientific Theories
abstract: Responding to a recent call for the development of a psychology of science, we examine how scientists manage empirical anomalies, a routine yet consequential challenge in scientific practice, and how their responses shape theory development. We argue that defensive anomaly-reduction strategies, which allow researchers to preserve an initial theoretical claim, can generate important secondary benefits. title: Evolutionary decoupling of morphological and behavioural antipredator responses and their hormonal basis across anuran species
abstract: Adaptive plasticity allows organisms to adjust their phenotypes to environmental heterogeneity. Defensive responses to predation risk exemplify such plasticity, which, in the case of amphibian larvae, can involve changes in morphology, behaviour, physiology and life histories. These defences are hypothesized to be mediated by the glucocorticoid hormone corticosterone (CORT), but empirical support across species is inconsistent. title: Effect of Pyrolysis Temperature on Chemical Characteristics and Toxicity of Liquid Smoke from Teak Sawdust
abstract: Liquid smoke derived from lignocellulosic biomass has attracted increasing attention as a natural preservative due to its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. The chemical composition and toxicity of liquid smoke are strongly influenced by pyrolysis temperature. This study investigated the effect of pyrolysis temperature (320–400 °C) on the chemical characteristics and toxicity of liquid smoke produced from teak (Tectona grandis) sawdust. abstract: Squalene-based oil-in-water emulsions underpin established vaccine-adjuvant platforms, while palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) provides a potentially recoverable non-animal source of squalene. This qualitative literature review critically integrates research on PFAD separation, pharmaceutical impurities, squalene-emulsion mechanisms, formulation stability, clinical vaccine evidence, and sustainable manufacturing. title: Implementation of Green Marketing in SMEs as an Effort to Enter the Market
abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of green marketing among silk SMEs in Makassar as an effort to expand their market reach. The research employed a descriptive qualitative method with a case study approach, using interviews, observation, and documentation. Findings reveal that enviromentally friendly production practices, such as the use o natural dyes and manual weaving, have begun to be adopted by some medium-scale SMEs. title: School Meal Programs and Student Learning Motivation: A Qualitative Case Study in Indonesia
abstract: Although school meal programs are widely associated with nutritional and health benefits, their relationship with students’ learning motivation remains underexplored across diverse educational contexts. This study examines how Indonesia's Free Nutritious Meals (Free Nutritious Meals/MBG) program relates to students' learning motivation at SMA Gama Yogyakarta. title: Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in English as a subject in basic education (ESBE) in ASEAN
abstract: Abstract This study employs a multiple case study design to examine diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in English as a subject in basic education (ESBE) in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). The study shows that DEI in ESBE in ASEAN has shown some progress, and yet challenges abound. title: Digital Transformation in Vietnam: Opportunities, Barriers, and Policy Implications for Sustainable Development
abstract: This structured narrative review examines the opportunities, barriers, and policy implications of digital transformation in Vietnam during 2020–2026. It integrates peer-reviewed studies of organizational change and digital strategy with Vietnamese policy instruments, official economic statistics, the United Nations E-Government Survey, and regional digital-market reports. abstract: Background: In a dense neighbourhood of Ojo, Lagos, household waste is collected mixed, drains are blocked by plastic, and the private sector participation (PSP) operator often arrives late, so residents burn refuse or tip it into open spaces. Young people who pick and sell recyclables earn irregular income and are treated as a nuisance, not as part of the waste system. title: Balancing the Rights of Insurers and Policyholders in the Cancellation of Insurance Agreements Following Constitutional Court Decision Number 83/PUU-XXII/2024
abstract: Ideally, an insurance contract should place the insurer and the insured in a balanced legal relationship grounded in freedom of contract, good faith, and legal certainty. In practice, however, Article 251 of the Indonesian Commercial Code has enabled insurers to unilaterally cancel coverage on the grounds of inaccurate statements, misrepresentation, or the insured’s concealment of material facts. abstract: Upconversion nanoparticles absorb near-infrared light and re-emit it at shorter wavelengths, which allows conventional photosensitizers to be activated deep inside tissue, beyond the reach of their own absorption bands. Such systems have been built from many combinations of host lattice, dopant, shell architecture, surface coating and photosensitizer attachment chemistry, and applied to tumors, to drug-resistant bacteria and to biofilms. abstract: Abstract Objectives The 2025 Paediatric Rheumatology Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) National Report highlighted variation in service provision across England. Understanding current care pathways is essential to support equitable access and optimise outcomes for children and young people (CYP) with rheumatic conditions. abstract: Growing environmental concerns regarding petroleum-based plastics have accelerated the search for sustainable food-packaging alternatives. Muscle protein-based edible films and coatings have emerged as promising biodegradable materials because of their film-forming ability, oxygen barrier performance, biocompatibility, and nutritional value. abstract: Abstract We investigate whether observers on rocky habitable-zone (HZ) planets in known multi-planet systems could recognise the apparent retrograde motion of neighbouring planets. abstract: The understanding of changes of rainfall patterns and climate extremes are crucial factors for addressing agricultural risks and sustaining water resources in Ethiopia. This study aims to investigate baseline rainfall climatology (1991-2020) and long-term spatiotemporal changes (1981-2022) of Kiremt seasonal rainfall totals (PRCPTOT) and selected ETCCDI-based rainfall indices across Ethiopia. title: Pauta. Soporte nutricional en el paciente crítico
abstract: La malnutrición es frecuente en niños críticamente enfermos y se asocia con mayor morbimortalidad, infecciones, ventilación mecánica prolongada y mayor estadía hospitalaria. El soporte nutricional constituye, por tanto, un componente esencial del tratamiento integral en cuidados intensivos pediátricos. Esta pauta propone estandarizar la evaluación, indicación, implementación y monitorización del soporte nutricional del niño crítico, integrando recomendaciones internacionales y herramientas aplicables a la práctica clínica.

abstract: The Gaorang lithium (Li) deposit is a newly discovered pegmatite deposit in the northeastern Ke’eryin ore field within the Songpan-Garzê Orogenic Belt. abstract: Malaysia hosts millions of migrants: willing and coerced, with legal status and without. Despite relying on migrant workers, Malaysian policies do little to alleviate exploitation. Malaysia has signed the UN and The Association of Southeast Asian Nations anti-trafficking protocols, but has not signed the UN refugee or statelessness conventions. title: Causal effects between gut microbiology and hyperlipidemia
abstract: Recent studies have confirmed the connection between gut microbiota (GM) and hyperlipidemia. This study used the Mendelian randomization (MR) technique to explore the association between GM and hyperlipidemia. MR was used to examine data derived from a genome-wide association study that combined data from 211 intestinal microbiota and hyperlipidemia. abstract: Microbial biophotovoltaics (BPVs) are an emerging renewable energy technology that harnesses photosynthetic microorganisms to generate electric current. Despite the rapid growth of the field, the lack of standardized testing and reporting methods currently prevents the benchmarking of devices, slowing technological progress. abstract: Abstract This study examines how initial water content influences the strength and microstructural response of a low-plasticity clay stabilized with unsaturated polyester resin (UPR). abstract: BACKGROUND: Schistosomiasis is one of the most prevalent neglected tropical diseases in sub-Saharan Africa, causing substantial morbidity and millions of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Although the WHO aims to eliminate schistosomiasis as a public health problem in several countries by 2030, current epidemiological data on schistosomiasis in Zambia are insufficient to adequately characterize transmission patterns, identify priority intervention areas, and inform the planning and evaluation of control programmes. abstract: Between 2021 and 2023, the State of Florida enacted numerous bills and took administrative actions interfering with university autonomy and academic freedom amid a combative political discourse vilifying universities as too “woke.” Defenders of these interventions have argued that academic teaching and research content have not been censored. abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores multifunctional epoxy‐based nanocomposite coatings incorporating PDA‐functionalized laser‐generated MoS 2 /ZnO nanofillers for carbon steel protection. abstract: Este artículo analiza la viabilidad de establecer un parque temático de Disney en Punta Cana, bajo el concepto de “Disney Caribe”. A través de un enfoque cualitativo con revisión documental y análisis contextual, se exploran los factores económicos, sociales, turísticos y medioambientales que influyen en la ejecución del proyecto. title: Conservation status of New York's pollinators
abstract: Abstract The global decline of insect pollinators is now well documented and recognized publicly from all over the Earth in a wide variety of ecosystems. Because a great deal of pollinator‐relevant environmental regulation (e.g., pesticide limitation, invasive species control) happens at the subnational level, an understanding of the subnational conservation status of these organisms is needed for targeting actions and monitoring their efficacy. We selected focal taxa from each of the four major insect groups known to be important pollinators: Hymenoptera, Diptera, Coleoptera and Lepidoptera.

abstract: BACKGROUND: In the context of museum and cultural heritage protection, rapid and accurate identification of Coleopteran pests is crucial for museum and cultural heritage protection. abstract: Smallholder farmers in southwestern Ethiopia face overlapping challenges that trap them in cycles of poverty and land degradation, yet the feedback mechanisms sustaining these traps remain poorly understood. title: Magnetic Lineaments and their Relationships with Geological Structures in the Tanganyika Graben
abstract: This study investigates the distribution of magnetic lineaments in the Congolese sector of the Tanganyika Graben and their relationships with geological structures and rift architecture. Magnetic maps were generated and processed using digitized data from the aeromagnetic survey conducted by Kenting Surveys Ltd. (1983). The resulting maps were interpreted to delineate lineaments and assess their geometry, orientation, and spatial distribution.

abstract: An Export Processing Zone also known as Free Trade Zone is a designated geographical area established by a government for businesses to operate. Several of such zones are usually established in different parts of a country. Mostly, the businesses that operate in the zones are private sector driven and are mainly aimed to promote export-oriented industrialization, facilitate technology transfer and attract foreign direct investments. abstract: This study seeks to analyze how the role of sarong Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) is done to encourage economic growth in the area in Gresik City. abstract: Dalbergia ruddae wood is highly valued in Mexico for the manufacture of musical instruments. However, the lack of information on its anatomical structure makes its identification difficult. The identification of Dalbergia woods is highly complex due to the similarity between species. Some Dalbergia species are in danger of extinction. abstract: Growing pressure for corporate sustainability highlights the critical need to understand how governance structures drive corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. abstract: Turkey is one of the countries where water resources exhibit high regional and seasonal variability; it is becoming increasingly vulnerable to drought risks due to population growth, urbanization, climate change, and the impact of agricultural water demand. abstract: Abstract I argue that questions can be transmitted through asking just as beliefs are transmitted through testimony. Just as we rely on testifiers to assert only when their epistemic position is good enough, so (I argue) we rely on queriers to ask questions only if they are in a position to know that the question is sound, which guarantees that the asked question has an answer. title: Colonial logics in contemporary governance: The role of outsourcing in Indigenous affairs
abstract: Abstract This paper explores the ways in which Indigenous Peoples’ right to self‐determination is undermined through government outsourcing processes in Indigenous affairs in Australia. These processes, which are themselves based on settler colonial interpretations of ‘independence’ and ‘efficiency’ that are naturalised within the state, work to deny First Peoples’ governance of their own futures. abstract: High pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) poses a serious threat to captive rare birds. Because effective countermeasures are limited, the use of human antiviral drugs to treat HPAIV infections in captive rare birds has been considered. Although the human antiviral drug, baloxavir marboxil (BXM), is not approved for the treatment of influenza virus infection in birds, previous studies demonstrated the antiviral efficacy of BXM in experimental avian models. abstract: Digital transformation is a vital part of a state’s political agenda, aiming not only to accelerate economic growth and promote sustainable social development but also to change the image of a state in the context of soft power enhancement. abstract: The gladiolus (Gladiolus grandiflorus) is a cut flower of great economic, social, and cultural importance that is widely appreciated for its striking colors and morphology. Thrips are one of the main pests for production, increasing management costs and decreasing flower quality. abstract: Abstract Temperate alley-cropping agroforestry with short-rotation coppice is gaining interest due to its multifunctionality in agroecosystems; however, yield uncertainties from potential tree-crop competition and unknown wood production limit its adoption. To our knowledge, this is the first study to compare crop yields between agroforestry and open cropland while quantifying wood production across tree ages and rotations. abstract: Abstract Exposure to organophosphate esters (OPEs) has been implicated in reproductive toxicity; however, evidence linking OPE exposure to diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) and the underlying mechanism remains limited. abstract: Indonesia has issued sovereign green ṣukūk since 2018, yet project financing regulations do not link environmental and social safeguards to eligibility. abstract: To maximize the benefits of compost derived from food, garden and agricultural waste on production systems, it is essential to understand its effects on soil properties. abstract: There remains considerable debate about the exact relationships between climate, conflict, and migration. This article draws on appeal applications to the Administrative Review Tribunal in Australia from asylum seekers from Sudan and South Sudan to trace links between climate-related conflict and asylum migration to Australia. abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. abstract: As urban temperatures rise from climate change, the burden of heat exposure is likely to be unequally distributed across neighborhoods. Prior research shows that heat varies based on neighborhood racial/ethnic composition, with people of color experiencing higher temperatures relative to Whites. abstract: Abstract Deficit irrigation (DI) is a sustainable approach to optimize water use while maintaining yield and quality of potato tubers, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions like the Mediterranean. title: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss
abstract: The Persona Selection Model (PSM) posits that post-training selects a persona the model learned during pre-training. Work on subliminal learning has shown that models can impart covert signals (like "love of owls") into semantically unrelated outputs like strings of numbers, and that students trained on these outputs inherit those traits. In this work I show that by evaluating the likelihood of such outputs under the base pre-trained model with an appropriate header, a method I call persona-header likelihood evaluation (PHLE), one can decode these subliminal signals and classify between them.

title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
abstract: Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution. We present RiseHarness, a framework for iteratively improving agent harnesses with model weights fixed. It focuses on flipping tasks with both successful and failed runs under the same configuration, using successful runs as references for failure analysis. title: The Impact of Orbital Data Centers on the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
abstract: As the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory begins its Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), satellite operators are racing to launch Orbital Data Center (ODC) satellites into low-Earth orbit. We present an impact assessment of a simulated $\sim$1 million ODC satellite constellation, arranged per recent filings across two low-Earth and two Sun-synchronous orbit regimes, on one year of Rubin Observatory LSST observations. title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
abstract: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. Cross-language correspondence was greater for sociocultural meanings than for meanings concerning nature and motion, a contrast recurring across models and classification

title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
abstract: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

title: A design concept for the High Resolution Imager on the Habitable Worlds Observatory
abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will be NASA's next flagship astrophysics mission, designed to search for signs of life on planets around nearby stars and conduct transformational science across astrophysics. Its High Resolution Imager (HRI) is not only the observatory's main imaging camera, but also provides grism spectroscopy and sub-microarcsecond astrometry, as well as the observatory's fine guidance, wavefront sensing and pupil imaging. title: Enhancing coarse bathymetric grids using a generative model: An arctic case study
abstract: Bathymetric mapping of ice-covered polar seas remains a major challenge. Persistent sea ice restricts systematic surveys, while icebreaking operations degrade multibeam echosounder (MBES) data quality through noise, hull vibrations, and ice interference. As a result, digital terrain models (DTMs) from bathymetric surveys in ice-covered regions are often fragmented, coarse, and incomplete, limiting interpretation of seafloor morphology, including glacial landforms used to infer former glacier extent and ice-sheet dynamics. title: Level 4 autonomous ship situational awareness system architecture and sensor trust management protocol
abstract: The relevance of this study is determined by the fact that, for Level 4 autonomous ships, traditional situational awareness architectures do not comply with Rule 5 of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea concerning continuous lookout by all available means, since such ships do not distinguish between random noise, sensor degradation, and cyberattacks. This paper proposes a Level 1 situational awareness architecture consistent with the Endsley model. title: Imminent Emergence of Permanent Surface Marine Heatwave States Across Global Oceans
abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) can devastate ocean ecosystems, yet the timing at which anthropogenic changes in MHW characteristics permanently emerge from natural variability at the global scale remains poorly quantified. Here, we present the first global time of emergence analysis of MHW characteristics of the ocean surface using simulations from 21 Earth system models from the sixth Coupled Model Intercomparison Project under moderate (SSP2‐4.5) and high (SSP5‐8.5) greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. Thaliacean Community Dominance Shift in the Northern South China Sea
abstract: Abstract Thaliaceans are pivotal gelatinous zooplankton that accelerate carbon export and structure pelagic food webs through rapid filtration and production of dense fecal pellets and carcasses. While taxon‐specific contributions to the biological pump are recognized, their ecological niches and drivers of distribution remain poorly resolved. Here, we analyzed a 5‐year data set (2007–2011) from annual surveys in the northern South China Sea, spanning contrasting hydrographic regimes shaped by the Pearl River plume, Yuedong upwelling, and Taiwan Bank upwelling. Differentiating Westerly and Asian monsoon dust fluxes to the tropical Pacific Ocean since the late Pliocene
abstract: Asian dust flux is a fundamental regulator of global climate and marine biogeochemical cycles, yet it is difficult to separate the dust fractions delivered to the tropical Pacific Ocean by the Westerlies and East Asian Winter Monsoon (EAWM). We present a 4-million-year record of eolian evolution from the Philippine Sea to deconvolve these two distinct transport systems on the basis of grain-size modeling and geochemical fingerprinting. title: Crevice Corrosion of Mild Steel Assemblages in Quiescent Seawater Under Extended Exposure Periods
abstract: ABSTRACT Crevice corrosion is a known issue for high chromium steels exposed to seawaters. However, it occurs also for mild and low alloy steels. Herein observations are reported for initiation and corrosion progression of mild steel. Crevices 30 to 200 µm in size, with outstands up to 100 mm, were considered, all exposed for up to 4 years in quiescent Pacific Ocean seawater. Both corrosion losses and pit depths on surfaces exterior to crevices increased with nitrate dosing but decreased for filtered UV‐treated seawater. title: Hydrological Regulation Disrupts Estuarine Spawning Grounds via Salinity Front Displacement but Preserves Nursery Habitats: Evidence From the Yellow River
abstract: Abstract Global rivers are increasingly threatened by fragmentation and sediment accumulation in reservoirs and dams. The Water‐Sediment Regulation Scheme (WSRS) has been widely implemented to mitigate these challenges, yet its ecological impacts on estuarine fisheries remain poorly quantified. Critically, WSRS operations often coincide with the spawning season of many marine fish species, raising concerns about disruptions to reproductive success and juvenile recruitment. title: Controls on reservoir quality and fracture distribution in the Old Red Sandstone of the Buchan field, UK central North Sea
abstract: The Buchan field, located in blocks 20/05a and 21/01a of the UK Continental Shelf, produced 148 MMstb of oil between 1981 and 2017 before production ceased for facility integrity reasons. A redevelopment is being considered and requires renewed reservoir models to estimate remaining potential. Reliable predictive modelling has historically been hindered by the complex behaviour of the Devono-Carboniferous Upper Old Red Sandstone reservoir, where low-permeability matrix sandstone is variably enhanced by natural fractures and localised high-permeability matrix streaks. title: Potential and Limitations of ICESat-2 Photon-Level Bathymetry for Dam Reservoirs in South Korea
abstract: Reliable bathymetric information is essential for reservoir management, yet conventional surveys are difficult to repeat consistently across large numbers of reservoirs.This study evaluated the potential and limitations of the Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) photon-level observations for reservoir bathymetry using surveyed reference bathymetry from eight major dam reservoirs in South Korea.A fixed analysis set of 33 ICESat-2 track-reservoir cases and 66 water-body intervals was established through screening of ATL03 photon distributions, and bottom-associated ATL03 return

title: Improved recovery of sub-ice shelf bathymetry from gravity data using an isostatic correction: a case study from the Dotson and Crosson ice shelves, West Antarctica
abstract: Abstract. Bathymetry beneath ice shelves is challenging to observe yet is vitally important for modelling how ice sheets will evolve into the future. An alternative to direct observation of bathymetry is to invert airborne gravity data for the bathymetric signal. Appropriate gravity data can be collected via remote sensing above the ice shelf and be used to provide an initial estimate of sub-ice-shelf bathymetry, typically at wavelengths of ~5 km and above. title: A Scene-Adaptive Trajectory Association Method for UAV Vision–AIS Applications in Airborne Maritime Perception
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data provide high-frequency visual observations and low-frequency identity/location messages, respectively. However, these two types of sensor data differ in spatiotemporal dimensions and pose engineering challenges for association and matching. This paper proposes a scene-adaptive trajectory association framework for airborne maritime perception. title: Enhanced Melt Supply Promotes Near‐Symmetric Oceanic Crustal Accretion at the Ultraslow Eastern Gakkel Ridge
abstract: Abstract Variations in melt supply can shift slow and ultraslow ridges between magmatic and tectonic accretion modes, but whether this effect persists at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge remains unclear. The eastern Gakkel Ridge provides a critical test because it spreads at only ∼6–10 mm/yr yet shows anomalously strong magmatism. title: Particle Size Distribution and Mean Diameter Characterization of Beach Sand from Haffa, Salalah, Oman
abstract: Particle size distribution is an important physical characteristic of coastal sediments, influencing sediment transport, depositional behavior, permeability, packing characteristics, and particle–fluid interactions. The present study investigates the particle size characteristics of beach sand collected from Haffa Beach, Salalah, Sultanate of Oman, using sieve analysis and moment-based particle diameter calculations.
