title: Feasibility of Wearable Heart Rate Variability Monitoring During a Military Closed-Circuit Rebreather Dive: An Exploratory Case Report
abstract: Background: Heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring during real-world closed-circuit rebreather (CCR) diving remains methodologically challenging. This exploratory case report describes phase-related HRV variations obtained from a wearable device during a military CCR dive. Methods: A trained male military diver underwent continuous monitoring with a RootiRx® single-lead wearable device placed in a custom waterproof enclosure. title: Arbitraje de emergencia: bases teóricas y diseño procedimental en los reglamentos arbitrales peruanos
abstract: Emergency arbitration is consolidated in international commercial arbitration practice. In the Peruvian legal system, given the absence of comprehensive legislative development, arbitral institutions have driven the development of this mechanism through special provisions in their rules. This article analyzes its theoretical foundations and procedural framework based on a representative sample of Peruvian institutional arbitration rules. title: Isolation of ecdysterone from a sea anemone (Cnidaria, Actiniaria) collected off Dakar (Senegal) and in vitro cytotoxic evaluation against head-and-neck and renal carcinoma cell lines
abstract: Sea anemones (Cnidaria, Anthozoa, Actiniaria) are still poorly explored as a source of secondary metabolites, although some of them have shown cytotoxic and antitumour activity. A specimen collected off Soumbédioum (Dakar, Senegal) was extracted with ethanol and then with dichloromethane/methanol (1:1). title: Rainfall Trends in Northern Algeria (1901–2024): Spatial Heterogeneity, Temporal Asynchrony, and Implications for Cereal Production
abstract: Abstract Northern Algeria is a transitional zone between the Mediterranean and the Sahara, yet the spatiotemporal structure of its long-term precipitation trends remains poorly studied. This study analyses 124 years of monthly precipitation data (1901-2024) extracted from the CRU-TS4.09 gridded dataset (0.5°×0.5°) at 50 stations distributed across the region. title: Direction-Specific Nonlinear Hysteresis Modeling and Parameter Identification of a Composite Metal Rubber Vibration Isolator
abstract: Metal rubber (MR) exhibits excellent environmental adaptability and nonlinear damping characteristics, making it a promising material for multi-directional vibration isolation in aerospace and marine applications. However, the hysteresis behavior of MR-based isolators strongly depends on loading direction due to different structural layouts and load paths. title: The Effect of Adding Papain Enzyme and TCR Calcium to Commercial Feed on The Growth of Giant Freshwater Prawns (Macrobrachium rosenbergii)
abstract: Giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii) is one of the freshwater commodities in Indonesia with high market demand. In order to increase the growth rate of these prawns, their feed is supplemented with papain enzyme and calcium. The former is a proteolytic enzyme that plays a role in breaking down proteins into simpler compounds of amino acids, allowing it to be more easily absorbed into the prawn’s body. title: Boron-doped mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles as a dual-delivery platform for tetracycline and phytochemicals: A synergistic strategy against multidrug-resistant bacteria
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and biofilm-associated tolerance substantially limit the effectiveness of conventional antibiotic therapy. This study investigated boron-doped mesoporous bioactive glass (B-MBG) nanoparticles as a dual-payload delivery system for the combined administration of tetracycline and selected hydrophobic phytochemical adjuvants, including berberine, curcumin, and resveratrol. journal: Frontiers in Life Sciences and Related Technologies

title: Isobaric Crystallization of Aqueous Magnesium Chloride Solutions at Icy Moon Conditions
abstract: Abstract Subsurface oceans inside icy moons are expected to contain dissolved salts whose crystallization controls the mineralogy of their hydrospheres and potentially their surfaces. Here, we use in situ neutron diffraction to investigate the isobaric crystallization of a nearly saturated MgCl2/D2O solution between ambient pressure and 0.4 GPa. title: Gen-EBM: An energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that strongly depend on the underlying climate feedbacks. We present the Geneva energy balance model (Gen-EBM), a new 1D latitudinal EBM designed for the rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. title: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse
abstract: Abstract Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes undergo gravothermal evolution whose late-time behaviour is central to predictions for dense substructure and black-hole seed formation. We revisit the calibration of this evolution using a new spherical Direct Simulation Monte Carlo code, SphDSMC, which follows spherically symmetric SIDM systems without force softening and to substantially higher central densities than standard N-body simulations. title: Species–area relationships in honeycomb worm bioconstructions
abstract: Abstract The increase of species richness with the available or sampled area is a fundamental principle in ecology, but explanatory models of this relationship have never been tested in worm reefs representing priority systems as biodiversity hotspots and habitats of conservation concern. Alternative models based on the ‘random placement hypothesis’ versus the occurrence of processes operating at different scales were experimentally tested in patches of the tubeworm Sabellaria alveolata . title: Metocean-Dependent Blade-Pitch Control of Floating Wind Turbines: Balancing Regulation and Pitch Activity
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbines operate under continuously varying atmospheric and ocean conditions, whose influence is not explicitly accounted for in conventional blade-pitch controller scheduling. As a result, control strategies designed to provide strong rotor-speed regulation may introduce unnecessary blade-pitch activity under certain environmental conditions. This work proposes a metocean-dependent control methodology that adapts the regulation authority to the prevailing wind and wave excitation, balancing power regulation and actuator demand. title: More Frequent, Faster, and Seasonally Reorganized Drought‐to‐Pluvial Transitions in U.S. Cities
abstract: Abstract Hydroclimatic variability is projected to intensify under continued warming, yet the evolving likelihood, rapidness, and seasonal timing of drought‐to‐pluvial transitions remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a probabilistic framework that integrates a severity‐resolved Markov formulation to estimate conditional drought‐to‐pluvial transition probabilities, Event Coincidence Analysis to quantify Relief Time (TR; the interval between drought amelioration and subsequent pluvial onset), and circular statistics to characterize the seasonal timing of post‐drought pluvial occurrence. title: Study of rainfall dynamics in Juína, Mato Grosso: monthly precipitation deviations and their influence on agricultural activities
abstract: Rainfall variability is a determining factor in climate risk and agricultural performance in tropical regions, as it conditions soil water availability. The objective of this study is to characterize annual and monthly precipitation in the municipality of Juína-MT, from 1985 to 2024, using descriptive statistics and anomalies, relating the observed patterns to ENSO (ONI) and discussing implications for agricultural planning according to ZARC. abstract: Abstract. In carbonate U–Pb geochronology, unknown initial 234U/238U disequilibria can be debilitating for the accuracy of 206Pb/238U dates. title: Campo de Dalías and the “Almeria miracle”: a cautionary tale of the value of water in agriculture
abstract: Abstract Renowned for having one of the highest concentrations of greenhouses in the world, Campo de Dalías, located in the southeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in the southwest of the province of Almeria in Spain, offers a compelling case for understanding the evolution of how water has been valued and managed in agriculture. The region’s trajectory, from the discovery of groundwater in the 1940s, through its subsequent overexploitation, degradation, and eventual depletion, ultimately led to the adoption of water-efficient practices and the use of desalinated water for irrigation today. title: Orbital-scale precipitation variations in the western Qaidam Basin during the Late Pliocene: evidence from magnetic parameters and median grain-size
abstract: A recent study suggests that the precipitation records of the western Qaidam Basin during the middle Piacenzian warm period (mPWP, 3.264–3.025 Ma) are broadly consistent with those of the monsoon-influenced regions, and are highly sensitive to 20 kyr precessional cycles, implying that the East Asian summer monsoon (EASM) precipitation intensified and penetrated farther westward into the Asian interior during this warm interval. title: Electrical resistivity technique for assessing groundwater tables in an unconfined aquifer system and the importance of Dar-Zarrouk parameters in aquifer investigation: a case study from Walajabad block, Tamil Nadu, India
abstract: Groundwater occurrence in Walajabad block, Tamil Nadu, is influenced by variations in geological formations and subsurface conditions, making detailed characterization important for groundwater exploration and management. This research explores the groundwater characteristics and subsurface resistivity patterns for this block. In this study, 110 vertical electrical sounding (VES) points were conducted using the Schlumberger electrode array to investigate the subsurface resistivity distribution and groundwater conditions. title: Scale-aware emergent constraints on Tibetan Plateau warming: contrasting global and regional predictors
abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are increasingly used to reduce uncertainty in regional climate projections by exploiting relationships across models between observable historical predictors and projected changes. However, the choice of historical window and predictor scale can strongly affect constraint performance. Using the Tibetan Plateau (TP), a region of complex terrain, as a testbed, we compare two widely used predictors for constraining future TP warming: large-scale global mean surface air temperature (GSAT) and regional Tibetan Plateau surface air temperature (TPSAT). title: Airborne performance assessment of the DLR MIRO MGA 3 quantum cascade laser spectrometer for fast N 2 O measurements
abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the most dominant precursor of ozone-depleting substances and the third most important anthropogenic greenhouse gas, with agriculture contributing the largest share of emissions (56 %). Over the past two decades, airborne in-situ measurements have become increasingly important for studying emission and transport of N2O in the atmosphere, also driven by the development of more precise and simultaneously faster Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL)-based spectrometers. title: Sgr A* as a galactic PeVatron: Multimessenger signatures of the magnetic Penrose process
abstract: The magnetic Penrose process (MPP) is one of the most efficient mechanisms for extracting rotational energy from a magnetized Kerr black hole (BH), enabling charged particles to reach very-high energies. We investigate this process in Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), the supermassive BH at the Galactic center (GC), focusing on its ultra-high-efficiency regime, in which neutrons undergo beta decay inside the BH ergosphere. title: National Monitoring of Mangroves has Outpaced their Integration into Climate Policy
abstract: Purpose of Review Ambitious global targets for mangrove conservation have advanced rapidly in recent years, yet little is known about whether systems are in place to effectively track progress towards these targets. In particular, we lack understanding of national capacities for monitoring changes in mangrove extent and condition and how they interact with national climate policy. title: A hierarchical knowledge- and data-learning Bayesian network model – Application of dynamic risk assessment for oil and gas pipelines subjected to cascading disaster chains
abstract: This study explored a knowledge- and data-driven dynamic risk assessment method for oil and gas pipelines subjected to cascading disaster chains. Firstly, a hierarchical disaster causation model (HDCM) was constructed to describe causal disaster relationships and cascading transmission paths of oil and gas pipeline disasters within a unified framework. title: A Ridge-Penalised Fourier Autoregressive Framework for High-Dimensional Periodic Time Series Dataset
abstract: Time series associated with the seasonal climate are highly persistent with strong periodic behaviour making reliable statistical forecasting a challenge. Integrated autoregressive models on a conventional framework may fail to represent multifrequency seasonality. Fourier Autoregressive (FAR) models offer flexibility but may experience instability when the model complexity escalates in nature. title: Addressing seablindness: defense diplomacy and NATO-GCC cooperation in countering naval hybrid threats
abstract: This article examines the strategic potential of defense diplomacy in enhancing cooperation against maritime hybrid threats between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). Hybrid threats, marked by ambiguity, deniability, and cross-domain tactics, pose acute risks to the Gulf’s dependence on maritime trade, energy exports, and subsea digital infrastructure. abstract: This paper presents a finite element strength assessment of a ship double bottom structure. A detailed three-dimensional finite element model is developed to describe the structural arrangement and complexity of the double bottom, including plating and longitudinal and transverse stiffening. title: Towards the real diamond formation conditions: insights and perspective
abstract: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. title: Intense rainstorms as drivers of lacustrine turbidity currents: implications for paleoflood records
abstract: Flood turbidites in lake sediments are widely used to reconstruct past flood activity, yet the physical link between flood hydrology, sediment transport, and the resulting deposit remains incompletely constrained. In this study, we investigate the mechanisms controlling turbidity-current initiation in the subaquatic delta of the Muota River (Switzerland) and how they are reflected in the sedimentary record of Lake Lucerne. title: Integrating a global glacier model into local hydrological modeling: Impacts on melt contributions
abstract: Abstract. Snow and glacier meltwater are critical water resources for mountain regions, yet their accurate representation in hydrological models remains challenging. As climate change alters the timing and magnitude of melt contributions, accurate partitioning between snow and glacier sources becomes increasingly important. abstract: Abstract Plastic debris accumulation in natural ecosystems is a major environmental challenge. Yet production continues to grow because plastics often deliver lower life-cycle impacts than available alternatives. Due to severe material- and application-specific constraints, neither mechanical nor chemical recycling can presently be deployed at sufficient scale to prevent substantial environmental leakage. abstract: Declining amphibian and reptile populations in Costa Rica, particularly at mid-elevations, underscore theurgent need for updated herpetofaunal inventories in vulnerable, anthropogenically disturbed areas like the CentralValley. title: Early disaster response to extreme heat in modern Shanghai, 1873–1949: limited preparedness and unequal protection
abstract: As extreme heat has become one of the most deadly climate risks in cities today, a fundamental question is rarely asked: where does a city’s heat-disaster response capacity actually come from? Taking Shanghai from 1873 to 1949 as a case study, this study reconstructs summer extreme heat events by integrating Xujiahui Observatory temperature observations with modern newspapers and municipal archives. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the influence of disulfide bonds, associated with covalent adaptable network behavior, on the thermal stability of aromatic epoxy-amine networks. To this end, a network synthesized by curing aromatic epoxy (DGEBA) with a disulfide-containing aromatic diamine (AFD) was aged at 160°C, and its performance was compared to a reference network composed of DGEBA cured with methylene dianiline (DDM). title: Efficient Degradation and Recycling of Waste Formaldehyde Polymers to Value‐Added Diindolylmethane Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT The effective degradation of formaldehyde polymers catalyzed by Y(OTf) 3 with indole derivatives in water has been achieved, yielding a series of diindolylmethane compounds with added value. It provides a new route with additional potential for the upcycling of waste paraformaldehyde and polyoxymethylene plastic as a green alternative C1 synthon.

Traditionally, planting densities were often chosen with the assumption that at least one mid-rotation thinning operation would provide intermediate cash flow(s) while also accelerating the growth of residual trees to more quickly provide solid wood products at future thinnings and final harvest. abstract: Nuclear cogeneration is increasingly proposed to support decarbonisation, partly via hydrogen (H2) production through electrolysis, thermolysis, or a combination of these, but wide-scale adoption is limited by process inefficiencies, high costs, and concerns around nuclear wastes. Recent work demonstrated that gamma radiation, sourced from 137Cs, splits water into H2 at high yields with a TiO2 photocatalyst, extrapolating that world spent nuclear fuel (SNF) stockpiles could generate ~60% of world hydrogen demand, worth ~90 billion USD/y. abstract: There are over 80 structures of the manna discourse in John 6 proposed in scholarly literature. title: Temperature decouples friction, wear and residual fatigue in lubricated wire ropes under acidic exposure
abstract: Crossed wire-rope contacts in deep-mine hoisting combine acidic exposure, sliding and subsequent bending fatigue. Low friction, however, does not necessarily indicate surface protection. We examined sulfate-containing acidic unlubricated (S) and lubricated (SY) contacts at 30 and 60 °C. The study combined bulk rheology, crossed-contact testing, wear profilometry, SEM/EDS and residual bending-fatigue testing. title: VPP-Driven Sail and Foil Trim Optimization for the Olympic NACRA 17 Foiling Catamaran
abstract: Abstract The Nacra-17 is the current Olympic catamaran sailed in the Olympic Games since 2016 by a mixed crew. Over the years, the boat has undergone some changes. The initial design of the boat featured a set of appendages that only rarely allowed the boat to foil. Today, Nacra-17 features semi-L-shaped daggerboards and T-rudders, all of them independently trimmable. This allows the boat to foil at wind speeds of 9 kn and below on an upwind tack and even earlier on a downwind tack. abstract: Abstract. Winter carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) fluxes from soils under seasonal snowpacks make non-negligible, yet poorly constrained contributions to annual carbon budgets across Arctic regions. Quantifying these fluxes and their spatial variance will better constrain uncertainties in simulations of winter carbon fluxes from terrestrial biosphere models. title: A global overview of pigeon–fruit interactions
abstract: Pigeons are widespread worldwide. These relatively large‐bodied birds can significantly influence ecosystem structure and function through their feeding habits, especially on islands where large mammals and a few avian taxa are scarce or absent. However, their dietary guilds as frugivores and granivores, and their ecological roles as seed dispersers and predators are poorly understood. abstract: The textile industry, which plays a vital role in countries’ economic development, contributes to numerous environmental, economic, and social problems because of its extensive use of chemicals and high consumption of water and energy during production. abstract: Green banking is the process of operating banking and using technology or physical banking infrastructure efficiently and effectively. As much as possible, green banking is expected to provide zero effect or minimal negative impact on the environment and society. abstract: ABSTRACT As the most abundant renewable aromatic biopolymer, lignin holds great promise for sustainable photothermal composites. However, its practical application is constrained by inefficient photothermal conversion, mainly due to strong aggregation and inherent structural features. To improve its photothermal efficiency and compatibility with polymer matrices, chemical modification is often required. title: Comparative evaluation of four wind tunnel blockage correction methods for propeller testing
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates classical and contemporary wind tunnel blockage correction methods for propeller testing, with a focus on slipstream effects in closed section tunnels. Four methods: Glauert, Barnsley and Wellicome (1992), Mikkelsen and Sørensen (2002), and Werle (2011) were selected as representative of distinct theoretical approaches and time evolution, were implemented and compared using experimental data from three commercial propellers (APC 10×5E, 12×6E, 13×6.5E) tested in both open (unblocked) and closed (blocked) wind tunnel configurations. title: Selection of the Parameter of the Synchrony Estimator for the Correlation Between Time Series Sampled at Different Time Points
abstract: Abstract The synchrony estimator with parameter $$\beta $$ β for the correlation between two time series observed at different time points is defined as the standard Pearson correlation coefficient computed using a fraction $$\beta $$ β of the pairs of the two series corresponding to the smallest time differences. Two problems limit the use of the estimator in applications. First, no rule is available for selecting $$\beta $$ β . Second, it has been argued in the literature that the estimator only partially exploits the information in the data, since it does not use all available observations.

title: Heat stress and urban economic growth in China: Dynamic effects, channels, and evidence from functional data analysis
abstract: Against the background of global climate warming, the impact of high-temperature variation on urban economic growth has become an increasingly important issue in climate economics and urban sustainability research. Using daily maximum-temperature observations and city-level economic data for 247 prefecture-level and higher-level cities in China from 1992 to 2023, this study constructs a long-term functional representation of daily temperature for each city. abstract: Abstract Cacay (Caryodendron orinocense) is a native tree species increasingly cultivated in commercial plantations in the Colombian Orinoquía for its high-value nuts and oil, but the effects of this emerging tree crop on biodiversity remain poorly understood. We evaluated how cacay plantations influence bird taxonomic and functional diversity by comparing them with adjacent natural forests in the Colombian Orinoquía. title: Ion Transport Enhancement in Charge-Regulating Hydrogels
abstract: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. title: Temperature-dependent swelling and compressibility behavior of microfiber-reinforced bentonite
abstract: Abstract Bentonite is widely used as a buffer material in deep geological repositories because its low hydraulic conductivity and swelling pressure help limit advective radionuclide transport. Elevated temperature, however, can cause drying and shrinkage, which may alter swelling behavior and reduce mechanical integrity. Fiber reinforcement has been proposed to mitigate these effects, but the behavior of fiber-reinforced bentonite at elevated temperature remains poorly understood. abstract: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia () presents a sustainable pathway to valorize nitrate‐contaminated wastewater while enabling decentralized ammonia production. title: Effect of RANDALLfoils on the fluid dynamics of rowing
abstract: Abstract Rowing-blade attachments have the potential to modify blade-fluid interactions during the rowing stroke, however these effects remain difficult to isolate in on-water rowing. This study experimentally investigates the RANDALLfoil, a blade attachment designed to alter the flow around a rowing blade, using 1:4 scaled rowing motions. abstract: Abstract This paper takes the 1-meter off-axis primary mirror of the AIMS solar telescope as the research object, and adopts the finite element method to analyze its gravity-thermal coupling deformation characteristics under seven elevation angles and three temperature conditions. abstract: Species of the genus Zygaena exhibit remarkable morphological diversity in Iran, which historically led to the description of numerous species and subspecies in the region. One of these lineages, the fraxini-group, currently comprises nine species and 36 subspecies, largely delimited based on external morphology, biology and distributional data. abstract: Abstract Understanding the coupled influence of nanoscale interfacial effects and pore structure is essential for clarifying water-transport mechanisms in nanofiltration (NF) membranes. Previous studies have mainly examined either nanoscale transport effects, such as wall slip and interfacial viscosity variation, or membrane structural parameters independently, while their combined effects on membrane permeability remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract The Mediterranean region is emerging as a strategic area for energy transition, where cross-border electricity interconnections can play a key role in integrating renewable energy resources and strengthening Euro-Mediterranean cooperation. In this context, the ELMED interconnection between Italy and Tunisia serves as a significant case study for analyzing how cross-border electricity exchanges can facilitate the integration of renewable energy surpluses between power systems with different demand profiles and resource availability. title: Induced Volatile Chemistry and Arthropod Predation Across a Tree Diversity Gradient
abstract: Plant volatile organic compounds (VOCs) play a key role in defence against herbivores and in mediating multitrophic interactions. Yet, how surrounding plant diversity modulates these responses in forest trees remains poorly understood. We examined the effects of tree species richness on induced VOC emissions and arthropod predation in Quercus petraea in a biodiversity-ecosystem functioning experiment. abstract: Maize production in smallholder farming systems is increasingly constrained by declining soil fertility, reduced crop productivity, and the high cost of inorganic fertilizers. Recycling crop residues and utilizing residual fertilizer nutrients may provide a sustainable approach to improving nutrient-use efficiency and maintaining crop productivity. This study evaluated the effects of maize root biomass and diammonium phosphate (DAP), applied individually and in combination, on maize growth, yield, selected soil properties, and economic performance over two successive cropping seasons. abstract: Abstract Understanding how habitat structure and spatial configuration jointly influence species abundance is critical for conserving grassland birds in fragmented landscapes. We evaluated the effects of within-patch habitat structure and patch- and landscape-scale attributes on bird abundance in wet grassland patches ranging from 3,350 to 160,207 m², embedded within natural rangelands managed under extensive livestock grazing in southern Brazil. abstract: Conventional garment design typically relies on static anthropometric measurements, which may not adequately account for changes in body dimensions and posture during highly dynamic activities such as rock climbing. This study investigates how climbing-specific movement analysis and dynamic anthropometry can inform ergonomic design of rock-climbing clothing. abstract: Anthropogenic carbon emissions remain closely linked to the structure and short-run adjustment of financial and industrial systems. abstract: The article revisits the discussion about the potential influence of Jewish traditions concerning the image of Jacob engraved on the Throne of Glory on Jacob’s vision in the Slavonic Ladder of Jacob. abstract: Abstract Context Home-ranging is common among animal species, as site fidelity facilitates cognitive map development and promotes efficient habitat use. The adaptive value of site fidelity, however, should decline as environmental conditions change, yet empirical evidence remains limited. abstract: Bromide in source waters promotes the formation of toxic brominated disinfection byproducts during chlorination and ozonation, necessitating efficient, affordable pretreatment materials. abstract: Abstract Observations and cosmological simulations indicate that the early Universe hosted numerous compact, high-density stellar systems, where close encounters and physical collisions between stars were likely common. abstract: Two important indicators of climate change are the decline in Arctic sea ice area and the increase in average temperatures globally. abstract: Stowage planning for Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) vessels can be represented with different mathematical formulations for efficient stowage plans: hybrid-slot, grid-based, and lane-based representations. abstract: We present refined predictions of the geoneutrino flux for the 500-tonne Jinping Neutrino Experiment (JNE). abstract: In the autumn of 2026, mathematics is facing what may be the deepest crisis in its history. The entire ecosystem through which mathematical knowledge is produced, validated, communicated, and assessed is beginning to break down. Mathematics departments, those usually quiet and civilized places, are suddenly in turmoil -- the unlikely theaters of a new Battle of the Ancients and the Moderns. abstract: Coherent distributed radar architectures enhance the detectability of low-reflectivity targets. abstract: We study the shift equivalence testing problem for high-degree sparse multivariate polynomials. title: Topographically Forced Stationary Waves Can Explain the Near-Surface Zonal Winds Observed by Huygens on Titan
abstract: Titan's equatorial superrotation is associated with climatological retrograde (westward) near-surface winds at low latitudes, as consistently simulated by Titan general circulation models. However, the Huygens probe measured prograde (eastward) near-surface winds, contrary to the expected circulation. We investigate whether these observations reflect localized forcing by large-scale topography, using paired three-dimensional dry simulations with and without topography in the Titan Atmospheric Model. title: Chebyshev-expanded covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory
abstract: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component $U_V$ is incorporated at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $σ$, $ω$, $δ$, and $ρ$ channels. title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension.

abstract: Structures with large global contributions to a flow field are not necessarily those that are most closely associated with a specified engineering observable. abstract: In the case of the totally degenerate split degenerations given by fibered powers of Tate curves over $\mathbf{Z}[[q^{1/w}]]$, this article proves a Fourier expansion principle that applies to higher coherent (equivariant) cohomology classes of rigidified line bundles on the $\mathbf{Z}((q^{1/w}))$-fiber. We do not require any ampleness hypotheses. abstract: Abstract. We present TERRA-NG, a portable, GPU-accelerated, matrix-free mantle-convection code. A single Kokkos C++ implementation runs at scale on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPU supercomputers. abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. abstract: Efficient simulation of wave propagation in high-contrast media is challenging because standard explicit schemes are subject to severe time-step restrictions induced by fine spatial scales and fast multiscale modes, whereas fully implicit schemes require costly globally coupled solves. abstract: The paper concerns the orbital stability of positive standing waves for the logarithmic Choquard equation with a small local nonlinear perturbation. abstract: In this paper, the Space Electric and Magnetic Sensor (SEAMS), a space based mission dedicated to very low frequency (below 16 MHz) observations of the radio sky is proposed. abstract: In real-time autonomous field applications, GNSS is often unreliable and inaccurate. abstract: We prove unconditional lower bounds on the number of recursive calls made by the two algorithms of Fredman and Khachiyan (1996) for monotone Boolean duality testing, as a function of the explicit input size $N$. abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. abstract: This paper examines how many policies promoted in democracies to tackle climate change place additional burdens on particularly vulnerable individuals and communities. abstract: Background: Smallholder farmers on the coastal chars of Patuakhali in southern Bangladesh lose part of their aman rice crop to tidal flooding in most years, and dry season salinity reaches fields that were once safe for boro rice. abstract: Abstract. title: Indigenous Peoples and the Rights of Nature: A comparative analysis of environmental justice from the Philippines to the global stage
abstract: Abstract The Rights of Nature (RoN) framework provides that nature has inherent rights independent from economic and environmental rights of humans. To realise this, nature's own legal standing in court needs to be recognised. This article discusses the interconnection of the RoN framework and the rights of Indigenous Peoples, emphasising the need to fully integrate the RoN framework into State‐based legal systems to protect the rights of Indigenous Peoples and the environment. title: Adaptation-Based Climate Litigation and Climate Justice: A Comparative Legal Analysis with Special Reference to Bangladesh
abstract: The increasing impacts of climate change have exposed significant gaps in adaptation responses at both the global and national levels. International climate law has historically placed greater emphasis on mitigation than adaptation. This imbalance is particularly significant for highly vulnerable countries such as Bangladesh. The objective of this article is to examine what constitutes Adaptation-Based Climate Litigation (ABCL). How does ABCL differ from mitigation-based climate litigation? title: The Alternative to “Harm” in the ESA “Take” Claims
abstract: Wildlife agencies recently finalized major changes to regulations interpreting the Endangered Species Act (ESA). These regulations remove longstanding habitat protections for endangered and threatened species. To better protect wildlife and to solidify habitat protection’s role in Section 9 ESA litigation, conservation groups should bring more claims arguing that proposed projects “harass” wildlife by changing or destroying their habitat. This Note explores the potential effectiveness of “take” claims that allege “harass,” rather than “harm,” in the habitat modification context.

abstract: Abstract Riparian terrestrial insects face floods or accidental water exposure; however, their ability to fly off the water surface is unclear. abstract: Offshore wind power (OWP) and offshore energy hubs (OEHs) have recently become stable components of decarbonisation efforts across the EU. abstract: Abstract Rights of Nature initiatives have been met with considerable scepticism within European legal landscapes. Often termed a ‘legal transplant’, a rights‐based approach to nature is criticised as offering little added value beyond the safeguards provided by traditional environmental law. title: Climate justice: Is there an individual right of citizen to climate neutrality?
abstract: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural standing (legitimación activa) remains strictly constrained. Both CJEU and Spanish jurisprudence require proof of direct, individualized harm, preventing citizens from challenging public or corporate inaction on an individual basis. Currently, regulatory mechanisms reduce citizens to submitting administrative complaints or claiming post-damage civil compensation.

abstract: The article examines Ukraine’s port-sector regulatory framework for establishing public-private partnerships (PPPs), the risks to private investment in strategic maritime infrastructure, and how pre-war contracts cannot address military threats, destruction, operational disruption, and prolonged force majeure. abstract: Bamboo-Based Headwater Conservation and Its Utilization as Alternative Energy in Facing Energy Crises and Military Threats. Bamboo management may connect headwater protection with local energy diversification, provided that biomass extraction does not undermine soil cover and ecological functions. This article examines the evidence supporting this connection through a focused narrative review of eleven journal articles published between 2020 and 2026. title: Chasing Bubbles: Toward a Standardized Approach for Quantifying Methane Ebullition Using Bubble Traps in Streams and Rivers
abstract: Abstract Ebullition transports large quantities of the potent greenhouse gas methane (CH4) from stream sediments into the atmosphere. However, the use of different sampling designs complicates comparisons of CH4 emissions estimates between studies. Here, we present the first systematic review of sampling designs used in the past for assessing fluvial CH4 ebullition rates. In addition, we conducted field experiments to estimate the optimal number of bubble traps and the length of the sampling period, and to assess uncertainties in determining CH4 content in the emitted bubbles. title: Exploring the impact of corporate governance and external audit quality on creative accounting practices
abstract: The current study adopts a multivariate model to investigate the impact of board size, board independence, managerial ownership, audit committee independence, and external audit quality (proxied by audit fees) on creative accounting practices. Data for the study were obtained from commercial banks’ annual reports published on the Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) during the period from 2017 to 2021. title: Enhancing Risk Knowledge in Civil Society Organization Leadership: Case‐Based Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT The escalating complexity of China's disaster risk landscape demands a new strategic leadership from civil society organizations (CSOs) to navigate systemic and cascading risks. While the national policies increasingly formalize the role of CSOs in disaster risk reduction (DRR), existing training provisions do not adequately develop the risk‐informed competencies required in practice. title: Climate Justice for Small States: Loss and Damage, and the Limits of International Law A Case Study of Timor-Leste
abstract: This article examines the structural inadequacies of international climate law in addressing loss and damage experienced by small, climate-vulnerable states, with particular reference to Timor-Leste. Grounding its analysis in Article 2 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Article 3 of the Paris Agreement, the article interrogates the tension between the aspirational language of climate justice and the operational constraints embedded within existing legal frameworks. title: The Operational Politics of "Untitled"
abstract: “Untitled” is ubiquitous in modern and contemporary art, yet scholarship has treated it as a homogeneous category signifying openness or resistance. This article argues that “Untitled” functions not as the absence of naming but as an active operational strategy that redistributes naming authority across the art world. Drawing on case studies of four modern and contemporary artists, the analysis identifies three interlocking mechanisms: semantic resistance, perceptual intensification, and institutional recoding. journal: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual

abstract: Krisis iklim yang ditandai kenaikan suhu global, cuaca ekstrem, dan degradasi ekosistem menuntut perubahan perilaku yang berakar pada nilai, bukan sekadar pengetahuan. title: Paris as a Sporting City: Reframing the Past in the 2024 Olympic Games
abstract: The long history of French sport and tourism played an integral role in the Paris Olympics 2024’s planning. The Paris games transported spectators around the city and country to sporting facilities from different eras of France’s sporting development, each reflecting the desires and needs of governments and sports stakeholders working both in concert and in opposition. Olympic organizers showed how Paris as a sporting city centred on world class facilities, such as the Stade de France, but they also included atypical temporary spaces including the Chateau de Versailles. title: From Farm to Table Measuring Host Communities’ Relationship with the Plant World in Instagram Tourism Reels
abstract: Regenerative tourism claims to move beyond sustainability by restoring ecosystems and communities, but whether its communication enacts that claim has not been measured. The article annotates ten Instagram reels and captions from five regenerative, sustainable and neoliberal accounts, across 34 nodes and 261 values, yielding 1,737 multimodal and 565 linguistic annotations. Regenerative reels foreground producers, production settings and food as living matter; neoliberal reels foreground tourists, dining and prepared food and show no producers, a pattern the sustainable account shares. title: A review of country ambition in targeting important areas for biodiversity under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
abstract: Targets 1 and 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) require actions to focus on areas of importance for biodiversity-a prerequisite for reversing biodiversity loss and halting human-induced extinctions as set out in the Mission and Goals of the KMGBF. There is a need to review progress on how countries are aiming to identify and conserve such areas of importance. title: Urban Exodus After COVID-19? Internal Migration Trends Pre- and Post-pandemic in Germany
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been linked to increased net migration gains in suburban, peri-urban, and rural areas, at the expense of larger cities, contributing to suburbanization in many Western countries. Post-pandemic trends are less understood, but recent evidence indicates a return to pre-pandemic levels of internal migration intensity. This study examines internal migration trends in Germany in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, drawing on comprehensive flow data from 1991 to 2024. title: La prevención del delito en la República Popular China: fundamentos normativos y proyección criminológica
abstract: This article offers a legal-criminological analysis of the Chinese public security system. It examines the normative, institutional, and technological foundations underpinning crime prevention in China, highlighting the integration of criminal law with broader policies and mechanisms of social supervision. The study explores how this framework enables early intervention against criminal behaviour while prioritising the collective interest. title: Revisiting Prime Minister John Curtin’s house as an intimate Australian domicile
abstract: John Curtin was the Prime Minister of Australia during WWII and died in office in 1945. In the early-1920s he designed a modest family home in Western Australia with a wide verandah so he could rehearse speeches and recite poetry while perambulating its perimeter. It was a seaside respite far away from the slings and arrows of political and public life in the capital of Canberra. This study reexamines a seemingly ordinary house with extraordinary historical associations to unpick how national narratives and personal domestic materialities collide in the domicile. abstract: The aim of this study is to compare football agent activities in Türkiye and England within financial, administrative, and legal contexts. The study employs a qualitative research design, utilizing document analysis, purposive sampling for data collection, and content analysis methods. The documents collected as raw data include football agent regulations, lists of licensed football agents, agent payments, and agent payment reports publicly shared by the Turkish Football Federation and the English Football Association. title: Islamic Environmental Ethics and Green Banking Adoption in Bangladesh: A Maqasid al-Shariah Perspective
abstract: This research investigates the interplay of Islamic environmental ethics, environmental awareness, and the practice of green banking services in Bangladesh from a moral perspective of Maqasid al-Shariah. title: Operational Accountability in U.S. Museum Collections: A Risk-Based Framework for Documentation, Inventory Verification, and Location and Movement Control
abstract: Catalogue records alone do not guarantee that a museum can account for its collections. Inventories, storage moves, audits, and reconciliation projects have exposed cases in which objects remained in institutional custody while their identity, legal status, location, or associated information had become uncertain. This structured narrative review draws on 23 sources, including 12 peer-reviewed publications, together with museum standards, audit findings, and institutional collections work. abstract: Despite rapid growth in electric vehicle (EV) adoption, few studies have systematically quantified how national income, urbanization, and income inequality are jointly associated with EV charging infrastructure worldwide.To address this gap, this study analyzed cross-sectional data from 100 countries spanning all world regions and income groups.Results show that GDP per capita is the strongest correlate of charger density (beta = +0.49,p < 0.001), with high-income countries reporting an average of 81 chargers per 100,000 people, compared to fewer than 1 in low-income countries.Urbanization als

title: Anaerobic Speed Reserve and Critical Speed as Predictors of 200 m Front Crawl Performance: A Practical Alternative to Physiological Testing in Trained Swimmers
abstract: ABSTRACT Anaerobic speed reserve (ASR) and critical speed (CS) offer practical, performance‐based estimates of physiological tolerances, and can be derived from maximal aerobic speed (MAS) and maximal sprint speed (MSS) in swimming. We evaluated the predictive capabilities of ASR and CS for 200 m front crawl performance in trained swimmers, and whether the addition of physiological markers could improve model accuracy. title: Across North America: Reginald Arthur Lorrain and the Making of a Missionary
abstract: This article examines the North American years (1899–1902) of Reginald Arthur Lorrain, an Englishman who subsequently served for several decades as a Christian missionary among the Maras of the Indo-Burma borderland. Drawing on Lorrain’s unpublished personal diary, the study traces his passage through the agricultural, industrial, and itinerant-labour economies of Manitoba, Ontario, and the southern United States, and argues that the hardship, physical risk, and social marginality he encountered there constituted a formative, if unintended, preparation for his later missionary vocation. title: Climate Justice in Sub‐Saharan Africa: Unequal Burdens and Pathways to Socially Just Adaptation
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change in Sub‐Saharan Africa is often framed through vulnerability, resilience, and adaptation, yet these concepts alone do not fully explain the unequal social, economic, and political conditions shaping climate harm. This review examines climate change through a climate justice lens, focusing on unequal burdens, household welfare losses, fiscal constraints, adaptation finance, gendered inequalities, and pathways to socially just adaptation. abstract: Techniques of formalization are widely used in philosophy and other disciplines as tools for analysis and research. While epistemological and methodological aspects of formalization have received quite some attention in the meta-philosophical literature, the politics of formalization—the entanglements of formalization with power relations, and in particular the impact of formalization for projects of liberation or oppression—has received comparatively little attention. title: Reproducing Historic Inorganic Compounds: Reference Materials for Identifying Compounds in the Clemens‐Winkler Collection (Part 3)
abstract: The Clemens‐Winkler collection is a significant 19 th ‐century archive of inorganic chemical specimens, offering insights into the scientific practices of its era. As part of a digitization project, this study uses nondestructive analytical techniques—synchrotron‐based X‐ray diffraction (XRD) and X‐ray fluorescence (XRF) at the P21.2 beamline of PETRA III, as well as laboratory Raman spectroscopy and handheld XRF—to characterize historical samples without opening or damaging their sealed containers. title: Looking back, looking ahead: Local perspectives on landscape changes and native‐tree restoration in Madagascar
abstract: Abstract Across sub‐Saharan Africa, tree‐based restoration efforts are dominated by exotic tree species due to their rapid biomass accumulation and short‐term economic returns. However, their limited contribution to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning has renewed interest in native‐tree restoration as a more sustainable strategy. Madagascar represents a pivotal case study given its high‐level commitment to counter accelerating deforestation rates and preserve its exceptional endemic biodiversity. abstract: The Algerian economy remains highly exposed to external shocks owing to its persistent reliance on hydrocarbon exports. This study assesses the contribution of the date-palm industry to economic diversification and external competitiveness. title: The Many Routes to the Ubiquitous Bradley–Terry Model
abstract: The rating of items based on pairwise comparisons has been a topic of statistical investigation for many decades. Numerous approaches have been proposed. One of the best known is the Bradley–Terry model. This paper seeks to assemble and explain a variety of motivations for its use. Some are based on principles or on maximizing an objective function; others are derived from well-known statistical models, or stylized game scenarios. They include both examples well-known in the literature as well as what are believed to be novel presentations.

abstract: This article is a result of the first year of the educational project under the National Program "Education with Science", implemented at the Faculty of Biology at Sofia University "St. Kliment Ohridski". The project aims to create a sustainable connection between the academic community, school teachers and students, introducing modern scientific achievements and research approaches into school education. title: Determinants of Retail Consumers’ Purchasing Decisions for Basic Foodstuffs in Mahakam Ulu Regency: A Study of Price Volatility, Service, and Store Loyalty
abstract: This study examines perceived price volatility, service quality, and store loyalty in relation to grocery-store choice in Mahakam Ulu. Questionnaire data from 102 purposively selected consumers were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Service quality (β = 0.368; p = 0.002) and store loyalty (β = 0.572; p < 0.001) showed positive associations; price volatility did not (β = 0.005; p = 0.937). title: Exploring patterns for social‐ecological success of ecosystem restoration worldwide
abstract: Abstract Ecosystem restoration is a crucial response to human‐induced land degradation, which threatens biodiversity and ecosystem functions, poses food and water insecurity and undermines livelihoods, cultural values and human–nature relationships. For restoration to be effective and equitable, it is essential to understand how social and ecological factors interact to shape restoration processes and outcomes. title: Access to and control over water security: The perspective of gender equality in Lao PDR
abstract: Climate change and water-related disasters significantly affect water security and livelihoods, particularly in vulnerable communities. In Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), women often bear the burden of domestic water collection, yet their role in water governance remains limited. The objective of this study was to examine gendered dimensions of access to water security and participation in water-related decision-making across household, community, and institutional levels in Lao PDR. title: Extension Demonstrations and Field Days for Promoting Climate-Resilient Alley Cropping: A Case of Glen Arm, Maryland
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an extension field day in increasing participants’ knowledge, perception of sustainability, and willingness to adopt climate-resilient alley cropping (CRAC) in Glen Arm, Maryland. The field day included a tour to the demonstration site along with a classroom participatory discussion on key CRAC practices, including vegetables, fruit trees, cover cropping, water harvesting, composting, mulching, and integrated pest management. abstract: The study evaluated the perceived effects of implementing single-use plastic regulations on micro fish vendors in the Island Garden City of Samal. It used a quantitative descriptive-comparative study design to examine the vendors' demographic characteristics and their perceptions of the regulation's impact on their business operations. The study also found no differences in perceived impact among vendors when divided into groups by age, gender, and educational attainment. title: Refugee Presence and Perceived Changes in Local Social Norms: A Study of Communities Hosting Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh
abstract: Population visibility, daily interactions, institutional responses, material constraints and community solidarity all need to be taken into consideration in understanding perceptions of social change in refugee hosting contexts. This study analyzes the primary survey data of 460 respondents from villages supporting Rohingya refugees and villages adjacent to Rohingya refugee camps in Bangladesh. title: Smart Local Legislation: Comparative Lessons from Madrid, Taiwan, and Estonia for Indonesia’s Regional Regulation-Making
abstract: This article examines the need to transform Indonesia’s regional regulation-making from a predominantly formal and documentary process into a smart, participatory, data-driven, and accountable model of local law-making. The problem addressed is the gap between the normative promise of public participation in regional legislation and the institutional reality in which legal information systems, particularly JDIH, remain focused on documenting enacted regulations rather than facilitating public access to the process of norm formation. title: Adapt or Perish? Local stakeholders’ responses to climate change in Ghana’s cocoa-growing regions
abstract: Climatic pressure on cocoa production in Ghana is well documented, and adaptation research in the sector has concentrated almost entirely on smallholder farmers. Little is known about how other actors along the cocoa supply chain perceive climate change and their own capacity to support adaptation. This study explored how local stakeholders in cocoa-growing communities perceive climate change impacts, adaptation measures and adaptive capacities. A descriptive phenomenological design was used. title: Taxpayers’ View of the Tax Concept: A Metaphorical Analysis
abstract: This study examines taxpayers' perceptions of the tax concept through metaphors. Metaphor analysis is an effective tool for revealing how taxpayers make sense of the tax concept. This research used qualitative data collection techniques to compile and thematically classify metaphors produced by taxpayers from different sociodemographic groups about taxation. title: Is Global Cognition Associated with Sociodemographic and Lifestyle Factors, and with Mental Health in Older Adults Living in Rural Ecuador? Insights from the EcuAging Study
abstract: Little is known about the cognitive health of older adults living in rural Ecuador, where more than 70% of the rural population experiences multidimensional poverty. Using cross-sectional data from the EcuAging study, we examined the associations of sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and anxiety and depressive symptoms with global cognition, measured with a modified Spanish version of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), among 238 adults aged 55 years and older living in rural communities of Loja province. title: A review of the governance challenges in the regional integration of the ASEAN Single Aviation Market
abstract: Purpose This article aims to critically examine the governance challenges in the ASEAN Single Aviation Market (ASAM) at policy and operational levels. Design/methodology/approach An integrative review framework was adopted to synthesise diverse sources, including academic literature and policy documents. The data were examined through qualitative document analysis with content analysis and thematic coding to identify obstacles in implementing ASAM. title: Selective Innovation: Conditions for Cultural Continuity in Janger Banyuwangi
abstract: Visible innovation does not establish the continuity of living performance traditions. This article examines how selective change relates to continuing practice in Janger Banyuwangi, Indonesia. A critical integrative review synthesizes published Janger research and institutional documentation, drawing on heritage and organizational resilience scholarship to interpret relationships between change and continuity. title: Towards an Epicurean Pragmatic Model of Sustainable Capitalism. A Philosophical Framework for Values-Driven Business
abstract: Abstract This paper reinterprets Epicurean ethics as a strategic lens for sustainable capitalism, emphasizing its relevance beyond traditional philosophical discourse. By focusing on the concepts of ataraxia (tranquility) and aponia (absence of bodily pain), the article proposes a pragmatic ethical framework for business leaders navigating ecological and social challenges. abstract: Summary Approximated by a geocentric axial dipole oscillating between two states of polarity, the main geomagnetic field experiences directional fluctuations during stable periods termed palaeosecular variation (PSV). Although employers often include equality principles in internal policies, such commitments are largely declaratory and reflect a narrow understanding of equal treatment, often reducing it to the gender pay gap. title: Sustainable fashion trade-offs: material innovation, circularity, and systemic change
abstract: The fashion industry is widely recognized as one of the most environmentally harmful industries, prompting increasing attention to technological and circular solutions promoted as pathways toward sustainability. This review paper critically examines whether these approaches can deliver meaningful sustainability outcomes by focusing on the trade-offs they entail. abstract: Abstract Parliamentary committees are critical venues of legislative work. Yet women, already underrepresented in most legislatures, are often further marginalized within these powerful substructures. This note examines women’s representation in the Canadian House of Commons’ 24 standing committees, 2006–2025, using an original dataset capturing committee membership and leadership across six Parliaments and four major parties. This study examined the factors influencing language shift and dialect drift in the survival of the Eastern Subanen dialect in Purok 4, Lampasan, Don Victoriano, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. title: Libertad procedimental y las buenas prácticas arbitrales del soft law
abstract: This article analyzes one of the most relevant topics in Arbitration, which is procedural and evidentiary freedom and its direct relationship with Soft Law (Best Practices). It is a particularly significant issue in Peru, since the vast majority of local ‘arbitration experts’ resort to the Civil Procedure Code, which significantly undermines the practice of arbitration.

At the same time, member states were perfectly ready to help each other fight the devastating bushfires that raged around the Mediterranean. abstract: Contemporary public transportation systems ubiquitously employ audio-visual advertising platforms. abstract: ABSTRACT Global leadership in phasing out fossil fuels is an important new frontier in climate governance, yet remains undertheorised within existing scholarly accounts of climate leadership. title: Wild Bird Nutrition in a Changing World: Dietary Ecology, Seasonal Nutrient Demands and Conservation Implications
abstract: Nutrition is a central link between wild birds and the habitats on which their survival, reproduction, moult and migration depend. Bird species exploit diverse foods—including seeds, fruits, nectar, invertebrates, fish and vertebrate prey—and differ in how they acquire and process nutrients. title: There is no outside: on the impossibility of non-Eurocentrism
abstract: Abstract This article argues that there is no fully non-Eurocentric standpoint available after colonialism. The Western symbolic order – institutional, epistemic, juridical, and political-economic – has become globally hegemonic, structuring not only liberal international institutions but also the grammar of their critique. title: LEGAL REMEDIES FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE MINORITY IN COMPANIES IN NIGERIA
abstract: The principle of majority rule is fundamental to corporate governance and the administration of companies. However, the exercise of majority power often creates the risk of oppression, discrimination, and unfair prejudice against minority shareholders. This article examines the legal remedies available for the protection of minority shareholders in companies in Nigeria. It explores the historical development of the rule in Foss v Harbottle and its impact on minority rights within corporate entities. title: Material meanings of ‘transformative learning’ among sustainability educators in universities
abstract: Prominent calls have been made to radically shift current teaching provision in higher education towards critically ‘transformative’ pedagogies that align with the pressing imperatives of sustainability. Yet much uncertainty remains over how educators envision the notion of ‘transformative learning’ and their possible role in supporting it. In this study, 21 interviews were conducted with specialist UK-based academics in which they were asked to bring a physical object to represent what ‘transformative learning’ might look like in the context of their sustainable development-focused curricula.

abstract: Social commerce has grown rapidly and become a major platform for public transactions, including in rural areas. Here we evaluate the use of metabarcoding of airborne environmental DNA (eDNA) as a non-invasive method for surveying cave vertebrates. abstract: Oral traditions, including folk songs, myths, legends, and folktales, are integral aspects of every society, encapsulating collective beliefs, customs, religious practices, cultural heritage, and everyday lifestyles. abstract: Soil-transmitted helminths (STH) are parasitic intestinal worms infecting humans through contact with, or ingestion of, soil contaminated with eggs shed by infected individuals. abstract: This article analyzes criminal law enforcement against illegal nickel mining in Kolaka, Southeast Sulawesi, and evaluates whether the applicable sanctions serve deterrent, preventive, and ecological-restoration objectives. abstract: This study examines brand equity, sales promotion, purchase decisions, and customer loyalty among Purbasari body scrub consumers on TikTok Shop in Yogyakarta City. abstract: This research assessed the wellness strategies and employee productivity in the Local Government Unit of Lapu-Lapu City during Calendar Year 2026 as basis for the development of a Strategic Wellness Plan. abstract: Floodplains are of great ecological and agricultural importance worldwide. abstract: This article evaluates how a key missionary society negotiated the evangelistic impulse to introduce the Bible through the vernacular with huge societal pressures, across the British Empire, to promote English literacy among indigenous peoples. abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic ecological transformations are challenging conventional environmental management paradigms, as maintaining historical ecological structures and functions becomes increasingly untenable. abstract: In this article, we examine the U.S. H-2A and H-2B guest worker programmes to show how discretionary power is embedded in state labour migration governance, with implications for the expansion of liminal citizenship among immigrant workers. abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance is shaped by biosocial and microbiological processes, yet sex and gender have not been systematically framed across the three domains (infection, antibiotic selection and transmission) that lead to drug-resistant infection. Synthesising available evidence, we find no consistent sex or gender bias in resistance prevalence; where differences are reported, prevalence is more often higher in men. title: OPTIMIZATION OF TOURIST ROUTES IN BATAM CITY USING INTEGER LINEAR PROGRAMMING WITH DESTINATION CATEGORY CONSTRAINTS
abstract: Tourist route planning plays an important role in improving travel efficiency and visitor experience in urban tourism areas. Batam City offers numerous tourist destinations with diverse characteristics, making route planning under realistic constraints a challenging task. Classical Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) models assume that all destinations must be visited, which is often impractical in real-world tourism scenarios. Therefore, this study proposes an optimization model for tourist route planning in Batam City using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) with destination category constraints.

abstract: A partir de uma abordagem qualitativa, método de pesquisa memorial, observação participante e análise documental, este artigo faz uma análise crítica sobre a relação entre os estudantes africanos e a esquerda acadêmica brasileira. abstract: In recent decades, growing numbers of educated youths across the Global South have embraced geographical relocation to escape blocked social mobility at home. abstract: Este artículo propone una cartografía conceptual de los modos de posicionamiento teórico ante la violencia. abstract: Hunter‐based monitoring programs offer a cost‐effective approach to large‐scale wildlife monitoring, but their performance depends on sufficient observation effort and robust assessment of estimate precision. abstract: This paper discusses the interplay of climate-induced mobility, border dynamics, and politics of humanitarian-refugee diplomacy in the modern international system. It states that climate change has become one of the key factors leading to displacement, transforming the migration patterns and imposing more and more pressure on the existing system of governance. title: Moral Injury and Resilience in Military Personnel: An Integrative Review
abstract: Military service exposes personnel not only to life threat but also to events that violate deeply held moral beliefs, such as killing, failing to prevent harm, or being betrayed by trusted leaders. The psychological aftermath of such events has been termed moral injury, a construct that overlaps with, but is distinct from, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). abstract: This paper presents twelve AMS radiocarbon analyses for Ongamira and Characato (Southern Pampean Hills, Argentina) using a problem-oriented strategy. title: Policy adaptation frequency: central interventions and local policy outcomes in China’s governance system
abstract: Policy adaptations by central governments are often viewed as essential for institutional agility. However, little is known about how often such adaptations should be implemented to improve policy outcomes at the local level, particularly in hierarchical governance settings. To address this gap, we considered policy adaptation frequency as a structural driver of local outcomes, using China’s Business Environment Optimization reform as a case study. abstract: La participación de las mujeres en la caficultura familiar comprende actividades productivas que, particularmente en el beneficio poscosecha, pueden articularse con las tareas domésticas y ser interpretadas como una forma de “ayuda” familiar. Esta situación puede dificultar el reconocimiento de su aporte a la producción de calidad y a las decisiones sobre los recursos derivados del café. abstract: El principio de publicidad de los juicios es un principio constitucional dinámico, adapta su modo de realización cuando cambian los medios de acceso, las tecnologías de difusión y la forma en que se construye la opinión pública. abstract: This article explores the ways in which the use of regulation, through the use of law, ethics, policies and standards, raises complex and deeply important questions about the ways in which our systems enable health (in)justice. title: Can Lithium Production Drive the Green Economy? Panel Evidence from Five Leading Producers, 2010–2023
abstract: This study examines the relationship between lithium and green economic performance in Australia, Chile, Argentina, China, and the United States over the period 2010–2023. Using balanced panel data and econometric methods, including Pooled Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Fixed Effects (FE), Random Effects (RE), and the Hausman test, the study assesses the effects of lithium production (LP), lithium utilization (LU), lithium-related investment in renewable energy (LIR), and innovation and technological development (ITI) on the Green Economy Index (GE). title: CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY INDUSTRY IN MALAYSIA
abstract: The purpose of this study is to highlight the challenges faced by the Renewable Energy (RE) industry in Malaysia. This conceptual review examines previous research and articles on renewable energy in Malaysia and internationally, including current statistics, developments, and the status of renewable energy worldwide. The review covers key areas related to renewable energy, including its definitions, purposes, barriers, problems, challenges, principles, policies, strategies, and recommendations. title: Managerial Perception of the Application of the Circular Economy in the Hotel Sector
abstract: Despite growing interest in the circular economy (CE) in the hotel sector and extensive research identifying the conditions associated with its implementation, evidence remains insufficient on the organisational processes through which CE implementation takes shape. This research gap is the focus of the present study, which, recognising managers as agents of organisational change, addresses the following research question: How do managerial interpretations shape CE implementation? title: Closing the loop locally: transition barriers to nontoxic circularity in the built environment in a Swedish municipality
abstract: Circular economy is promoted globally as a framework for tackling resource scarcity, pollution, and climate change by enabling the reuse of products, materials, and energy rather than discarding them. An important yet often overlooked aspect of circular economy concerns the presence of hazardous chemicals in recycled materials. Since these chemicals are present in everyday products, they will inevitably enter the recycling loop and end up in new products. title: The Changing Electoral Politics of Pursuing Climate Action in the UK
abstract: Abstract Action on climate policy in the UK has been at a crossroads since 2021. The UK's previously world‐leading performance in emissions reduction was derived largely from eliminating coal from electricity supply and relied on a broad political consensus regarding the issue's importance. The next stage of emissions reduction is more contentious, however, and at the same time, the underlying consensus across political parties has collapsed. title: The effective use of delivery partners to enhance client capability in megaprojects
abstract: A capable client is crucial in managing the complexities of megaprojects, requiring a wide range of organizational capabilities. However, client organizations are often temporary and rely on delivery partners to build capability. This research explores how delivery partners can enhance client capability, using the case of High Speed Two (HS2), the UK’s largest infrastructure megaproject. title: Markets, Power and Social Order: Rethinking the Political Economy of Pre-colonial Igbo Land
abstract: The political economy of pre-colonial African societies cannot be understood apart from the institutions through which production, exchange, authority and social relationships were organized. Pre-colonial Igbo Land has long been characterized as a "stateless" or decentralized society, and existing interpretations of its political economy have often emphasized dispersed political organization, subsistence production, long-distance trade and the absence of centralized state structures. title: Transforming Social Media: A Prophetic Model for Moral and Digital Responsibility
abstract: Social media has emerged as one of the most powerful tools of the modern age, capable of serving both constructive and destructive purposes. In today’s interconnected world, it shapes public opinion, influences perceptions, and drives social trends. However, its misuse has become widespread, with talented individuals spending excessive time on unproductive online activities and entire societies increasingly influenced by its addictive nature. title: Regional Development and Economic Co-operation Dynamics: The Case of Azerbaijan and the Caspian Countries
abstract: This study investigates the trade intensity relationships between Azerbaijan and the Caspian littoral countries—Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Russia—during the period 2006–2024. The main purpose of the study is to present a descriptive analysis of the historical trends in the bilateral trade relations of countries in the Caspian region. title: Lionardo Salviati, Tacitism and the People of Florence
abstract: This article explores Lionardo Salviati’s Discorso sopra le prime parole di Cornelio Tacito, a brief commentary on the beginning of Tacitus’ Annales published in 1582. While it is widely recognised as one of the first examples of political commentary on the Roman historian, its content has only received scant attention. abstract: The study provides an econometric basis for the employment effects of diversified agritourism services in Uzbekistan and tests whether a target of 40,000 jobs – 24,000 newly created and 16,000 brought out of the shadow economy – is attainable through the development of agritourism destinations. title: Animals in Behavior Analysis: Considerations for Effective and Ethical Research, Teaching, and Practice
abstract: Abstract Behavior analysis has a long history of using nonhuman animals in basic research, classroom teaching, and applied practice, yet discipline-specific guidance for competent and ethical animal work remains limited. This paper reviews historical and contemporary trends in animal use within behavior analysis, including the decline of traditional animal laboratories, growing interest in invertebrate models, and expansion of behavior-analytic work into homes, shelters, zoos, and other applied settings. title: Mental Health, Nature, and Poetry in Ranu Uniyal's The Day We Went Strawberry-Picking in Scarborough
abstract: Ranu Uniyal is one of the most prominent contemporary Indian poets whose work engages with questions of identity, ecology, and gender. This article analyses her collection The Day We Went Strawberry-Picking in Scarborough (2018) through the lenses of ecocriticism and ecofeminism. title: Building capacity in evidence-based healthcare: a mixed-methods evaluation of training activities in South Africa
abstract: Objectives Cochrane South Africa (CSA) is a Cochrane geographic group established in 1997, aiming to advance the skills and awareness of evidence-based healthcare (EBHC) nationally and regionally through a comprehensive training programme. This project aimed to evaluate the training delivered by CSA from 2021 to 2022. abstract: Intangible cultural heritage represents the collective memory, cultural identity, and traditional knowledge of local communities, while its sustainable inheritance increasingly faces challenges arising from modernization, migration, and lifestyle transformation.
