title: Wood and seagrass fibre-based materials including TPSea on hot sounding rocket structures
abstract: Abstract In order to assess the applicability of wood- and seagrass-based materials as thermal protection system materials in space, a test with fin leading edges made of two solid woods (oak and mahogany) in the arc-heated wind tunnel L2K was conducted. The requirement analysis enabled the selection of three untreated, native solid woods (birch, oak and larch), and four wood-fibre materials (TPSea-0, -1, -C and I-WBM) for further tests. title: The critical foundations of truly sustainable environmental auditing
abstract: This essay addresses the urgent need for transformative action in environmental governance and examines how environmental auditing can support diagnostic and transformative agency within social-ecological systems. This requires a radical conceptual reconfiguration of environmental audit. To this end, the essay advances five conceptual foundations for a more impactful and sustainable approach. title: Odesa-teksten
abstract: This article examines the transformation of the Odesa Text in independent Ukraine. It traces three coexisting modalities: a post-Soviet nostalgic vision rooted in Odesa’s Russophone and Soviet past; a reinterpretation that challenges the old Odesa myth and foregrounds Ukrainian history and new urban spaces; and a wartime Odesa Text shaped by Russia’s invasion and the importance of testimony. The article demonstrates how different types of the Odesa Text reflect different versions of “selective cosmopolitanism” and forms of self-identification.

title: Resource Rents And Institutional Quality: Exploring Global Corruption's Paradox
abstract: This study explores the complex relationship between natural resource rents, institutional quality, and corruption, stemming from the "natural resource curse" paradox. Employing a fixed-effects methodology with data from 175 countries, the research reveals that the interaction between natural resource rents and institutional quality significantly escalates corruption. abstract: The tin mining scandal in Indonesia reveals the complexities of corporate crime, which inflicts massive financial and economic losses upon the state. This normative legal study analyzes the dynamics of corporate criminal liability and the effectiveness of the "follow the money" approach in tracing and recovering assets derived from mining-related crimes. abstract: Abstract There is a long history of integrating games in classical pedagogy, although most of these studies have focused on history teaching or Latin and Greek language acquisition. In this article, I extend prior research on antiquity game-based learning to illustrate how video games can also be used for mythology education, or the familiarity with particular stories and characters which have inspired artworks, political movements, and other cultural phenomena throughout history. abstract: Global society faces the critical challenges of eradicating poverty, ensuring food security, and addressing environmental degradation. In this context, agricultural microbusinesses emerge as essential actors in productive dynamics, contributing significantly to food sovereignty and economic transformation. In Latin America, family farming supplies 53% of global food demand, accounts for 7.92% of GDP, and employs one-fifth of the economically active population. title: Law after empire
abstract: This paper examines how legal knowledge circulates in post-colonial contexts, arguing that the authority of law after empire is produced through the movement of people, institutions, and epistemic practices along old and new imperial routes. Drawing on comparative research on three regional courts, the Caribbean Court of Justice, the now-defunct Central American Court of Justice, and the East African Court of Justice, it reframes post-colonial legality not as a story of transplantation or dependency, but as a process of circulation and translation. title: Termitomyces striatus : A Novel Mycofood With a Rational Pharmacological Approach
abstract: The folk population of India has a mycophilic inclination, and wild mushrooms may help sustain their livelihood. One such wild mushroom has been reported from India and is traditionally consumed as a myco‐food by ethnic communities. abstract: La obra Uncle Tom’s Cabin de Harriet Beecher Stowe es un clásico de la literatura publicado en 1852 que denuncia la situación racista que vivían las personas de color estadounidenses, quienes, por su etnia, estaban sometidas al esclavismo de la época. abstract: Acknowledging the benefit of Rainfall Simulators (RS) is continuously growing among researcher, mainly for laboratory-scale models where natural rainfall is either unavailable or inconsistent. abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication errors are a persistent threat to patient safety in psychiatric settings, where complex pharmacotherapy and ethical conscience heighten nurses' stress of conscience. AIM: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a structured educational program on knowledge about medication errors and stress of conscience among psychiatric nurses. abstract: Mining activities in Boyolali Regency provide economic benefits but also generate socio-environmental and governance challenges. This study examines sand and rock mining governance through the perspective of Siyasah Dusturiyah and proposes a governance model based on prophetic values. abstract: This paper explores the ideal regime in Homeric epics from the perspective of political philosophy, challenging both the "pre-political" taxonomies of political anthropology and the exclusionary Platonic-Aristotelian legacy. abstract: Over recent decades, criminological research has paid increasing attention to citizens’ perceptions of the police. However, studies on young people’s perceptions remain limited, particularly among underrepresented groups. This article examines the perceptions of a group of girls with histories of offending, drawing on their experiences of police contact. abstract: American jails and prisons are ripe for analysis by medical humanities scholars. Carceral institutions have been an especially salient feature of American history since the late-twentieth century, when U.S. incarceration rates began surging and culminated in what has come to be known as "mass incarceration." abstract: Abstract Two-finger test refers to the physical examination of female genitalia for the purpose of determining virginity. This colonial-era test is invasive and degrading, has no scientific basis, and can neither prove nor disprove allegations of rape. abstract: This paper measures welfare using social welfare functions that weight income growth and its distribution differently. abstract: Digital technology has spread unevenly through South Africa’s public technical and vocational education and training (TVET) colleges. abstract: The origin and evolution of land plants precipitated fundamental changes to the Earth system and enabled the diversification of life on land. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the effectiveness of human resource management (HRM) practices in reducing turnover intentions and strengthening organizational commitment among public healthcare workers in Saudi Arabia during crises. Using survey data from public healthcare employees across three regions, the findings reveal that comprehensive training and organizational support for work‐life balance significantly reduce turnover intentions, while financial incentives have limited effects. title: Blue-eyed bargains: Nazi-era acquisitions at the museum of far eastern antiquities in Sweden
abstract: This article examines the provenance of cultural objects acquired by the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities in Stockholm during the National Socialist era. Taking the 1937 acquisition of two Chinese bronze tripods from Josef Plaut as its point of departure, the study investigates the circumstances of the sale in relation to the Washington Principles and the Terezín Declaration. The analysis subsequently expands to the museum’s acquisition practices between 1933 and 1938. This process identifies a further case involving the 1934 acquisition of books and journals from the scholar Alfred Salmony.

title: Decolonial IR, Indo identity, and epistemic marginalisation in International Relations
abstract: Abstract Recently, a major concern of International Relations (IR) has been the need to ‘decolonise’ the discipline as a remedy for ‘Eurocentrism.’ This article argues that Decolonial IR is at risk of developing and perpetuating notable blind spots and making mistakes similar to those that it rightly berates Eurocentric IR for. First, while pointing at problematic binaries that undergird Eurocentric IR, Decolonial IR fails to escape the use of identity-based binaries of its own when justifying its project. title: Human dimensions of Asiatic black bear presence in Akita City, Japan
abstract: Human-bear interactions with Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus) are increasing in Japan. Examining public perceptions towards bears and bear management is timely with shifting lethal control legislation and rapid spread of negative human-bear interactions throughout Japan. Akita City is one site of recent upsurge in social conflict triggered by increasing human-bear conflict. abstract: The circulation of illegal cigarettes is an excise crime that threatens state revenue and can distort competition in the tobacco industry. This study examines how the Medan Customs and Excise Supervision and Service Office of Intermediate Customs Type B (KPPBC TMP B Medan) handles the circulation of illegal cigarettes through preventive and repressive law enforcement. title: Incorporación del informe respaldatorio del instructor en el reglamento de disciplina para los centros de formación policial ante la impugnación de sanciones por faltas leves y medias del aspirante a servidor policial
abstract: La normativa sancionatoria de los centros de formación policial es un mecanismo fundamental para cimentar la disciplina de una institución jerarquizada; aplicada de manera objetiva, proporcional y conforme al debido proceso, ayuda a que el aspirante a servidor policial comprenda las normas y asuma la responsabilidad de sus actos, por lo que ninguna norma disciplinaria debe aplicarse de modo que vulnere los derechos humanos. title: Bringing social cohesion into forest landscape restoration: Identifying future pathways toward more integrated social‐ecological restoration
abstract: Abstract Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) is increasingly recognized as a key strategy to address land degradation, biodiversity loss and climate change. However, its long‐term success depends not only on ecological outcomes but also on social processes that shape restoration implementation and sustainability. This study explores the relationship between social cohesion and FLR in central Togo, examining how social cohesion influences FLR implementation and how participation in restoration activities can, in turn, shape social cohesion. abstract: Článek se zabývá finančními příjmy českých dezinformačních webů a otázkou, zda tyto weby dodržují relevantní právní regulaci. abstract: Abstract This paper examines the relationship between criminal governance and the internationalization of organized crime, using the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) expansion towards Europe as a case study. It argues that governance can facilitate the transnational expansion of criminal organizations by fostering internal cohesion, regulating illicit markets, and enabling civilian control. title: Peran Keputusan Pembelian Dalam Membentuk Kepuasan Pelanggan Pada E-Commerce Fashion Di Kota Depok
abstract: Perkembangan e-commerce telah meningkatkan persaingan pada industri fashion sehingga pelaku usaha perlu memperhatikan kualitas produk, kualitas layanan, dan promosi penjualan untuk mendorong keputusan pembelian dan meningkatkan kepuasan pelanggan. abstract: This study analyzes the influence of geopolitical risk, oil prices, and gold prices on the performance of Islamic stock indices and examines the role of exchange rates and inflation as moderating variables. Monthly data from the Dow Jones Islamic Market (DJIM) during the conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East between February 2022 and October 2024 were analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with STATA. abstract: The ethics of learning constitute an essential aspect of Islamic education—particularly within pesantren (Islamic boarding schools)—which demands a balance between the mastery of knowledge and the cultivation of character. The narrative of Prophet Moses and al-Khiḍr in Q.S. Al-Kahf [18]: 65–82 provides a Qur’anic basis for examining these dimensions of learning. abstract: The production of cultured meat is gaining regulatory approval in countries worldwide, with the global market being estimated to grow substantially over the next few years. However, its recognition as an effective technology in tackling issues concerning human health, the environment, and animal welfare has been received with mixed feelings across different countries. title: Un émulo de La Fontaine en Inglaterra: John Gay, el primer escritor inglés de fábulas en verso
abstract: El presente artículo versa sobre el escritor inglés John Gay, considerado en su país como uno de los mejores poetas burlescos y satíricos de su época; más concretamente de su obra The Fables, que consta de sesenta y ocho fábulas: cincuenta publicadas en 1727, a las que se añadieron dieciocho en 1738. title: Linking serious game decisions to real-world farmer land use: a case study from the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: Abstract Tropical landscapes are largely shaped by the daily decisions of smallholder farmers. Public institutions and private companies increasingly aim to shape agricultural landscapes by influencing farmer decisions. Farmer land-use decision-making is complex and highly dynamic, especially in tropical smallholder systems. The use of serious games has been proposed as a promising research approach to understand these processes. abstract: This essay discusses the interplay of epistemological-methodological approaches and research practices developed within a global health study that aims to understand and strengthen community actions and organizing by - and preserve the memories of - made-marginalized places and people during the COVID-19 pandemic. abstract: In early 1946, working in the United Kingdom, George Orwell, Arthur Koestler, and Bertrand Russell proposed a manifesto for a new League for the Rights of Man. Their intervention took place alongside the contemporaneous drafting, in the United States, of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). Eighty years later, the UDHR still stands as an enduring monument to the postwar human rights moment, while the 1946 manifesto for a new League for the Rights of Man is remembered only by a handful of scholars. 1 Why did one take off as spectacularly as the other failed? title: The Functions of Discretion in Extradition Treaties
abstract: Abstract Extradition treaties grant the parties considerable discretion: why? What are the functions of this treaty design? Discretion can help bridge differences between treaty parties that might otherwise not agree to cooperate in criminal matters. Factors such as the level of trust at the time the treaty was concluded and the political relationship between the parties therefore affect the degree of discretion in extradition treaties. title: Triangulated brokers: imams, securitisation, and the performance of moderation in Belgium, Germany, Spain, and Italy
abstract: Imams in Europe are cast simultaneously as counter-terrorism assets, carriers of communal authority, and problems to be governed. Drawing on PROTONE project interviews with eleven imams and four Muslim community representatives in Brussels, Berlin, Madrid, and Rome, plus four focus groups, this article develops the concept of triangulated brokerage to explain how imams produce religious authority under asymmetric scrutiny. abstract: Abstract Research on Palaeolithic bone tools has increasingly emphasised methodological refinement and interdisciplinary approaches, yet systematic quantitative assessments of scholarly attention and bias remain limited. This study presents a quantitative synthesis of 137 publications aimed at analysing patterns in tool-type focus, geographic coverage, and methodological change in European Palaeolithic bone-tool research. title: Logic, sense and universes of discourse: On the occasion of a letter from Y. Bar-Hillel to E. Coseriu
abstract: In a letter addressed to Eugenio Coseriu (1921–2002), dated November 10, 1957, the logician and philosopher of science Yehoshua Bar-Hillel (1915–1975) takes issue with the concept of “universe of discourse”, which Coseriu had briefly illustrated in his study “Determinación y entorno” (1955-1956). title: Determinants of Market Access Among Smallholder Onion and Carrot Farmers in Wanale Sub-County, Mbale Distrct, Uganda
abstract: This study examined the determinants of market access among smallholder onion and carrot farmers in Wanale Sub-county, Mbale District, Uganda. The study used a descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods design. Quantitative data were collected from 250 smallholder farmers who completed and returned questionnaires out of a target sample of 285 farmers, representing an 87.7% response rate. title: Modeling Climate Change Impact on Variety-Specific Wheat Sowing and Adaptation Using DSSAT-CERES Simulation in Nepal’s Central Terai
abstract: Wheat is a major source of food and income in Nepal’s Terai region, but its production is threatened by rising temperature and erratic rainfall. However, reliable, site-specific estimates of climate change impacts and practical adaptation options remain limited for the Central Terai region. This study evaluated the impacts of climate change on yields of wheat and tested practical adaptation strategies using the DSSAT-CERES simulation. abstract: Abstract India has shaped its future energy mix towards solar energy due to ambitious renewable energy targets and strong volatility in fossil fuel prices. title: Archaeological Osmosis or How Is Archaeology Seen by Those Who Share Our Lives?
abstract: Archaeologists are always concerned about bringing archaeology into public spheres to create narratives accessible to those who do not use our meta-language. These books, narratives, exhibitions, and other forms of communication are prepared to attract people who do not have permanent contact with archaeology. However, we often overlook a specific group who, while not archaeologists themselves, live with archaeology every day: our spouses, parents, children, and close friends. title: LATINAS: the visual politics of Latinidad in London
abstract: This paper theorises how Latin American women in London reinterpret and reappropriate narratives of Latinidad through grassroots and creative initiatives. It examines Latinidad as a mythological narrative that binds communities of women together and enables the construction of diasporic identities grounded in belonging, resistance, and care. title: A low-cost earthquake simulator for early-years science education: A hands-on approach to teaching seismic concepts in kindergarten and primary school
abstract: Children growing up in seismically active regions such as Greece are routinely exposed to earthquakes from an early age, yet age-appropriate, classroom-ready resources for introducing seismological concepts in kindergarten and early primary years remain scarce. This paper describes the design, construction and classroom use of a simple, low-cost experimental earthquake simulator intended for children aged approximately four to eight years. title: Towards a transformative and territorial leadership: The case of organic farming development in Occitanie
abstract: Cet article a pour objectif de caractériser les modalités d’un leadership transformatif au service d’une action publique locale. Il fait la double hypothèse que cette transformation s’appuie sur les dimensions démocratiques et distribuées de leadership et se manifeste concrètement dans le territoire concerné. title: Humility, non-judgment and frugality in the Orthodox Christian tradition: Theoretical background for the development of positive psychology interventions
abstract: This study explores the conceptual and methodological integration of three fundamental Christian virtues—humility, non-judgment, and frugality—into the framework of positive psychology. While positive psychology has developed evidence-based interventions that cultivate character strengths and promote wellbeing, it often remains disconnected from religious and spiritual traditions that historically shaped corresponding virtues. abstract: Abstract From 2020 to 2024, the European Centre for Law and Justice (ECLJ), a conservative NGO backed by US evangelical Christians, secured certain procedural reforms to the practices of the European Court of Human Rights. The rules and guidance governing the recusal of judges were elaborated, and third-party intervention was made more transparent. abstract: This article highlights the importance of analytical frameworks in enhancing the resilience of local communities to crisis-related threats, as they enable the identification and systematic organization of key factors influencing a community’s capacity to cope with crises. It emphasizes that effective resilience management should be grounded in a proactive approach that conceptualizes resilience as a dynamic property emerging from the interactions among social, technical, and environmental factors. title: Recent Progress in Fe₂O₃–Graphene/TiO₂ Nanocomposite Photoanodes for Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) remain a promising third-generation photovoltaic technology because of their low production cost, mechanical flexibility and good low-light performance. However, the efficiency of conventional TiO₂ photoanodes is limited by the wide band gap (≈3.2 eV), low electron mobility and charge trapping. title: Comparing the role of ‘security’ in EU energy and agri‐food law
abstract: Abstract In EU energy and agri‐food law, ‘security’ is constantly invoked to justify legal action and to guide the adoption and interpretation of law. This article compares the concepts of energy security and food security, focusing on their relationship to sustainability, and asks whether invoking security enables or obstructs each sector's environmental transformation. title: The 2023 New Zealand coalition government: a mandate for change?
abstract: Mandate theories of responsible party government require that parties are programmatic, with elections determining policy direction. In contrast, elitist theories argue that the ability to vote out poorly performing parties is the main means of democratic control. Content analysis of policy documents shows clear differences between parties at New Zealand’s 2023 general election, while voters believed the parties offered different policy directions. title: A history of self-interest and opportunities? The international woodscrew cartel and GKN’s acquisition of the Swedish woodscrew industry in the late 1920s and early 1930s
abstract: Being an outsider in a cartelized context is often preferable, especially if you are well established and possess structural comparative advantages. Such was the position of the Swedish woodscrew manufacturers that provided effective price competition worldwide for a decade. This article analyzes how the international woodscrew cartel, and specifically its leading member, dealt with this during the interwar period. title: Beyond the European Courts: Alternative Case Law on Non-Refoulement at Embassies and Consulates
abstract: Abstract Contemporary asylum systems continue largely to condition access to international protection on physical entry into State territory, exposing asylum-seekers to significant risks along migratory routes. Against this background, this article examines whether the principle of non-refoulement may apply beyond territorial borders when individuals seek protection at embassies and consulates. abstract: While prior research shows that pressure from corporate constituents can improve board gender diversity, it often treats external pressures as equivalent and offers limited explanation of when female board appointments represent substantive governance change rather than symbolic compliance. title: Effect of Boko-Haram Insurgency on Economic Development of Nigeria: A Study of North-Eastern Nigeria
abstract: Boko Haram Insurgency has constituted a serious predicament to the Nigerian state since its emergence in 2002. The sophistication and fluidity of the insurgent group within the North east geopolitical zone of Nigeria has made the group one of the greatest challenge to Nigerian socio economic and political landscape. title: Loneliness and non-loneliness in long-term marriage: Continuous transformation through meaningful life events
abstract: Objective: This qualitative phenomenological study examines how loneliness and non-loneliness are experienced within long-term marriages in Israel, where marriage is the most common relationship status among adults in the third age. Background: Previous research on loneliness within long-term marriage has focused on quality of life, relationship quality, security, belonging, and intimacy, typically examining the presence or absence of these dimensions at specific points in time. abstract: Abstract Global deforestation, primarily driven by agricultural expansion, exacerbates climate change and biodiversity decline, prompting concerted international efforts to combat it. abstract: In this paper, we introduce braided cuckoo hashing, an open-addressed hash table that supports load factor up to $1 - \varepsilon$ (for some parameter $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$), while supporting queries, insertions, and deletions in worst-case time $O(\log \varepsilon^{-1})$, with high probability. abstract: Magmas degas volatiles and metals into submarine arc-related hydrothermal systems, but the nature of this process and its role in seafloor massive sulfide (SMS) mineralisation are poorly understood, particularly in submarine arcs hosting Cu–Au-rich deposits. To address this, we studied glassy melt inclusions (MIs) and matrix glasses from Brothers submarine volcano in the Kermadec arc, where there is strong evidence for magmatic involvement in hydrothermal processes and Cu-Au-rich mineralisation. title: Biofouling communities on idle petroleum transfer hoses and their potential dispersal role at a platform in the Brazilian Campos Basin
abstract: Idle petroleum transfer hoses provide surfaces for attached marine organisms and may subsequently be relocated. This study describes biofouling and visible surface condition at one platform in the Campos Basin, Brazil, after a reported approximately six-month idle period. The dataset comprises 14 reconstructed section records, with approximate total cover estimated visually by one observer from one or two selected monocular ROV stills per record. title: Who Owns the Waterfront? Urban Transformation and Collective Struggles for the Urban Coastal Commons in Barcelona
abstract: Barcelona has undergone continuous transformations along its waterfront since the 1992 Olympic Games, which marked the city’s symbolic “opening to the sea” by turning marginalized coastal areas into accessible public spaces. In recent decades, however, tensions have grown between tourism and urban-development-driven economic interests and citizens’ demands for equitable access and participation. title: Immense but not immutable: A sudden and sustained decline in deep-pelagic life in a large oceanic ecosystem
abstract: The deep-pelagic habitat of the Gulf of Mexico comprises 90.4% of its volume and houses an exceptionally diverse deep-pelagic animal community that provides numerous ecosystem services, including carbon cycling and prey provisioning for oceanic predators. Here, we report sudden, severe, and persistent declines in the abundance of deep-pelagic fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods that have persisted for over a decade. title: Functional Groups of Summer Copepod Assemblage in the Central Barents Sea
abstract: The functional trait structure of copepod assemblages inhabiting Arctic seas remains poorly investigated. In the present study, we aimed to reveal the spatial pattern of copepod functional groups in the central Barents Sea. One type of water mass (the Barents Sea Water) was identified based on an analysis of water properties. Environmental gradients in oceanographic factors, nutrients, and food conditions were relatively stable. Total abundance ranged from 434 to 1168 ind. m−3, with Oithona similis dominated numerically. title: TRAJECTORY OF THE INDIAN OCEAN TRADE FROM 1400 CE TO 1600 CE: A SHIFT FROM PEACEFUL COMMERCE TO NAVAL HEGEMONY
abstract: This study examines the trading system and its evolution in the Indian Ocean between 1400 CE and 1600 CE. It discusses the pre-existing maritime order, Chinese maritime expeditions under Zheng He, the rise of regional powers such as Malacca, and the arrival of the Portuguese in the Indian Ocean. This study throws a light on the aspects that were held before European intervention. The Indian Ocean was a connected and commercially vibrant world, based largely on peaceful trade and multicultural interaction. title: Performance of Acropora species on the Great Barrier Reef's first coral tree nursery
abstract: Abstract Introduction The worldwide decline of coral reefs has led to the proliferation of local‐scale coral restoration projects. Active restoration using in‐water coral tree nurseries and outplanting of coral fragments is relatively new on the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) and complements traditional, passive approaches to reef protection. However, given the infancy of these methods, few studies have measured the effectiveness of coral restoration techniques, including coral nursery systems. title: Scaling laws link conserved gene-abundance distributions to adaptive expression in diatom communities worldwide
abstract: Marine microbes sustain Earth's major biogeochemical cycles, yet how they maintain stable ecosystem functions across diverse environments remains unclear. We analyzed metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data from diatom communities sampled during the Tara Oceans global expedition. While gene abundance distributions remain statistically similar across sample, gene expression varies systematically across geographical locations, a global pattern we show reflects predictable scaling laws. abstract: This study investigates cetacean occurrence and stranding records along the Romanian Black Sea coast between 2021 and 2025, focusing on the three resident subspecies: Tursiops truncatus ponticus, Delphinus delphis ponticus, and Phocoena phocoena relicta. A total of 1392 live individuals were documented across 188 sighting events, with T. t. ponticus and D. d. ponticus together representing 88.3% of all recorded individuals. abstract: Abstract Underwater Wireless Optical Communication (UWOC) is a promising technology for high-data-rate underwater communication due to its high bandwidth and low latency, with potential applications in Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) systems. However, UWOC performance is significantly affected by underwater channel impairments such as turbulence, optical attenuation, and transmitter–receiver pointing errors. title: Onshore Power Supply Readiness in Adriatic–Ionian Ports: A Multiple-Case Assessment and Typology for Marine Spatial Planning and Port Governance
abstract: The onshore power supply (OPS) eliminates ship emissions at berth, yet feasibility is site-specific, and most evidence concerns large Northern European and Asian ports. This multiple-case study assesses OPS readiness at six ports of the Adriatic–Ionian macro-region (Ancona, Ploče, Durrës, Volos, the river port of Belgrade, and the lake port of Ohrid) covering ferry, cruise, cargo, and tourism in the European Union (EU) and non-EU jurisdictions. title: CURRICULUM GAPS IN HOSPITALITY EDUCATION AND CRUISE SHIP INDUSTRY COMPETENCY STANDARDS
abstract: The global cruise industry has experienced remarkable post-COVID-19 growth, generating strong demand for skilled Indonesian workers. Yet a persistent structural gap exists between the learning outcomes of hospitality degree programs and the competency standards required by the hotel departments of international cruise ships. This study identifies and analyses the dimensions of that gap, examines the structural factors that sustain it, explores how alumni adapt once onboard, and formulates evidence-based policy recommendations. abstract: Metapenaeus stebbingi Nobili, 1904 is an Indo-Pacific shrimp species. Larvae of M. stebbingi were obtained from eggs that hatched four days after spawning from gravid females captured from incidental fishery. title: Japan’s Changing Arctic Policy in a New Geopolitical Landscape
abstract: On 29 June 2026, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed the Headquarters for Ocean Policy to begin revising Japan’s Arctic Policy, Japan’s first comprehensive Arctic policy document (2015). Drawing on official documents and scholarly literature, this article traces the evolution of Japan’s Arctic policy since it obtained observer status in the Arctic Council in 2013, focusing on security, and asks why the revision was launched in 2026 and how the changing geopolitics of the Arctic have shaped it. title: Species of the genus Gibberula Swainson, 1840 (Gastropoda: Cystiscidae) from Namibia
abstract: The marine gastropod fauna off Namibia (SW Africa) has hardly been explored. The current study on species of the genus Gibberula Swainson, 1840 is part of an inventory of marine gastropods from Namibia. Four species are described as new, all endemic to Namibia: Gibberula oshishani sp. nov., G. evukule sp. nov., G. ehodhi sp. nov., and G. heyali sp. nov. One additional species was also known from South Africa: G. cf. bensoni (Reeve, 1865). None of the species known from Angola was found in Namibia. title: Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years
abstract: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. abstract: This paper presents abattery module design for a marine hybrid traction system that must satisfy both high‑power (HP) and high‑energy (HE) demands. title: Bioprospecting perchlorate-reducing bacteria: report of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter isolated in Cierva Point, Antarctica, and its contribution to SDG 3
abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) is a global contaminant that has been detected in various environmental matrices. ClO 4 − is considered an emerging pollutant because of its potent endocrine-disrupting effects, which impairs iodine uptake in the thyroid gland, and its high toxicity and persistence. Therefore, the development of technologies for its reduction in ecosystems is imperative; bioremediation is a promising technology for ClO 4 − reduction. title: Stone to Lead: The Anchor from the Dor L2 Cargo and the Chronology of Composite Anchors from the 7th‒4th Centuries BCE
abstract: Abstract A wood and lead anchor stock found in underwater excavations at the Dor Lagoon belongs to a cargo of amphorae and iron blooms, designated as the Dor L2 site, dated to the late 7th‒early 6th centuries Before Current Era (BCE). This anchor is contemporary with the earliest composite wooden anchors found in the Mediterranean, such as those from Mazarrón 2 and Karaburun. abstract: Abstract This article recentres East Africa in the global history of cowrie shells by tracing the trajectories of Monetaria annulus —the East African cowrie species—across interconnected monetary arenas in the nineteenth century. Situating African monetary history within transoceanic processes, it argues that the ‘great cowrie inflation’ in West Africa was closely tied to the reorganization of procurement networks, labour regimes, and commercial infrastructures in the Western Indian Ocean. title: Effect of Microwave Activation on the Activity of Multiphase Heterogeneous CuO/CuFe2O4 Mixed Catalysts for NH3–SCR of NO
abstract: Abstract Marine main engines commonly operate at low speed and low load to achieve economical cruising, which lowers the exhaust temperature. Developing catalysts for the selective catalytic reduction of NO with ammonia (NH3–SCR) that are active at low temperature and over a wide temperature window is therefore essential. In this work, multiphase heterojunction CuO/CuFe2O4 spinel catalysts were synthesized by a microwave-assisted hydrothermal method. title: Unveiling a new species of Cyrtodactylus Gray, 1827 (Squamata: Gekkonidae) hidden in the highlands of Dima Hasao District, Assam, India
abstract: We describe a new species of karst-associated Cyrtodactylus Gray, 1827 (Gekkonidae) of the khasiensis species group within the Indo-Burma clade from Umrangso, Dima Hasao District, Assam, northeast India, based on integrative analysis with morphological and molecular data. abstract: Abstract Seaweeds are said to be ecosystem engineers, supporting biodiversity with habitat creation. This study assessed how large-scale seaweed cultivation by the company in the Faroe Islands using three-year cultivation cycle and partial harvesting affects local marine biodiversity. This study designs and theoretically assesses a carbon dioxide (R-744) refrigeration system for a fishing vessel, integrating the phase change material (PCM) HS23N as a thermal store. abstract: Safety incidents during shore excursions can disrupt cruise itineraries and threaten tourist well-being. This study examines incident-related factors and tour guide preparedness at Company A, a destination management company operating in Bali. A qualitative descriptive design combined content analysis of 45 incident reports from 2025 with semi-structured interviews with 12 purposively selected guides who had handled or witnessed incidents. abstract: The Grand Canal of China is a giant linear cultural heritage. abstract: In the autumn of 1803, William and Catherine Blake returned to London from their three-year sojourn in a cottage in the coastal village of Felpham, Sussex. abstract: Abstract Biological particles are an important but poorly understood component of Amazonian aerosols, having impacts on ecosystems, climate and human health. Here, we show that African dust plumes transport microbial communities across the Atlantic into the Amazon rainforest. We characterize the bacterial, fungal, and archaeal communities at 42 and 323 m above ground at the Amazon Tall Tower Observatory, both during background conditions and a five-day North African dust intrusion. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution poses a growing threat to mangrove ecosystems, particularly in tropical regions where ecological and socioeconomic dependencies are high. abstract: With the increasing need to decarbonize maritime transport, green ammonia (NH₃), produced from renewable energy sources, has emerged as a promising alternative marine fuel. abstract: ABSTRACT Pigeon snaring was an élite sport in the traditional Tongan chiefdom, undertaken on purpose‐built mounds known as sia heu lupe . LiDAR imagery combined with field survey and mound documentation on the island of Tongatapu has identified a comprehensive corpus of these sites. This includes Vaolahi, an elaborate complex of sia heu lupe and other features associated with the Tu‘i Tonga paramount, as well as other mounds and mound clusters across the island. title: European Exploration Innovations: The Role of Afro-Asian Technology and Ideas in European Exploration, 1400–1700
abstract: This paper revisits the formation of the European Age of Exploration by re-examining the claim of an “independent Western breakthrough.” Taking European overseas expansion from 1400 to 1700 as its main thread, the paper argues that Europe’s maritime capabilities did not emerge out of nowhere, but gradually developed through the absorption of mathematical knowledge, astronomical observations, navigational instruments, shipbuilding experience, and gunpowder technologies from Asia and Africa. abstract: Aim of the study Extending the biomedical model, increasing attention has been directed toward the psychological determinants of seasickness. The present study examined whether, among sailors, threat appraisal is associated with an increased frequency of seasickness symptoms and lower self-efficacy. Furthermore, the study investigated whether self-efficacy mediates the relationship between threat appraisal and symptom frequency. title: Geoinformación marítima para la decisión antártica de Chile
abstract: La creciente variabilidad ambiental y la intensificación del uso marítimo de la Antártica elevan las exigencias de planificación, coordinación y apoyo a la decisión. Este artículo plantea que, para Chile, la geoinformación marítima antártica constituye una capacidad estratégica más que un soporte técnico especializado. Sobre la base de antecedentes recientes de hielo marino, turismo y articulación institucional, se propone avanzar hacia un nodo geoespacial interoperable que fortalezca la proyección nacional, la seguridad operacional y el resguardo ambiental.

Its growing use in tourism creates opportunities to communicate maritime knowledge and support livelihoods, while also raising questions about cultural authenticity, community participation, and the continuity of traditional skills. This qualitative case study examines how Phinisi is maintained as living heritage and how its use in tourism intersects with cultural preservation and sustainable tourism in Tana Beru. title: Aircraft for Dispersal of Calcite Plumes for Heat Mitigation
abstract: Aircraft are evaluated as an alternative to towers for distribution of calcite particle plumes. Airplanes and airships are compared. The proposed plumes will block solar radiation and offset warming from global climate change regionally. Using aircraft is much more cost-effective than towers because the capital costs are much lower. One airport needs to be constructed for a small fleet of aircraft versus many tall towers and many sets of redundant equipment. The operational costs are higher. Even though labor costs are lower for airplane operation, the energy costs are higher than for towers.

title: From Colonial to Educational: Dialogic Imagination of Matthew 28:19-20 and the Story of Apapuhang in Sangihe
abstract: This article addresses the issue of how the Christian mission in Indonesia is understood, specifically, the tendency to equate the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20) with "Christianization". This perception is linked to a colonial legacy that has shaped biblical interpretation and potentially hinders religious moderation and interfaith peace. The study aims to reinterpret Matthew 28:19-20 from the perspective of the Sangihe people by engaging in a dialogue with the “Apapuhang” folktale. abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable management of shark fisheries is challenging because sharks are highly vulnerable to fishing mortality. By analysing data from three independent scientific surveys between the early 1970s and late 2000s across three fishing regions in southern Australia, we show that conservative fisheries management following severe depletion facilitated full stock recovery of the gummy shark ( Mustelus antarcticus ), a species of moderate biological productivity. abstract: One transformative, inexpensive (~$0.5-1/kg), and low-carbon energy source is natural hydrogen produced by serpentinization and other geochemical processes. Global data on its accumulation, migration, and geological mechanisms have been collected in the present study. Temperature, pressure, and mineralogy all affect the rate at which hydrogen is generated. title: Human Plunder: Slaving Raids, Economic Warfare, and Mercantilism in the French Caribbean, 1665-1713
abstract: Abstract Between 1665 and 1713, at a time of almost perpetual warfare in Europe, privateers frequently assaulted and seized enslaved people from rival colonies all over the Caribbean. Following mercantilistic principles, the French in particular sought to increase the labour force in their colonies while undermining their enemies’ plantation economies. Of the about 14,000 to 16,000 slaves captured in inter-colonial raids, more than 10,000 were forcibly taken to French colonies. These raids not only came at a high human cost but also led to shifting economic fortunes in the Caribbean.

abstract: Body morphing is widely used in nature for agile locomotion; yet, despite significant interest in morphing wings, aerial robotics has not explored a morphing fuselage to control flight. title: Rediscovery of Sphagnum perichaetiale and S. trinitense (Sphagnaceae) in Puerto Rico
abstract: Two Sphagnum species thought to be extinct in Puerto Rico were rediscovered. The current distribution range of these species is substantially reduced compared to the historical distribution based on herbarium records. We contribute notes on S. perichaetiale and S. trinitense distribution, habitat, and a checklist of associated plant species. A key to the three extant Sphagnum species found in Puerto Rico is presented along with suggestions for conservation efforts to preserve S. perichaetiale and S. trinitense. abstract: This article narrates the decision-making and processes behind the return of a parcel of land in New South Wales, Australia, to a Local Aboriginal Land Council. abstract: This study examines how dependence on natural resources and ecosystem services shapes the strategic behaviour of nature-based tourism firms operating in changing environments alongside competing land uses. abstract: With its unique ''anti-form'' aesthetic style, Moby-Dick constructs ''the world of action.'' abstract: This article focuses on the social outcomes of archaeological fieldwork. title: When Alexander Did Not Visit Jerusalem in 332-331 BCE
abstract: The famous legend of Alexander the Great’s respectful visit to Jerusalem represents the positive relationship between Hellenistic kings and the Jewish people. We can prove that this event never happened. The question becomes how and why the story developed. The tale concludes with the invitation to the Jews to enlist in his army, and their acceptance illustrates the loyalty of Jewish soldiers in Alexander’s armies and those of his successors, the Seleukids and the Ptolemies, for over a century and a half.

abstract: Abstract This study investigates a low-carbon, waste-integrated concrete mixture for fabricating artificial coral units using three-dimensional concrete printing (3DCP). abstract: Diarrheal disease remains a leading cause of childhood illness and death in South and Southeast Asia, yet region-wide syntheses of its prevalence are sparse. abstract: Purpose This paper examines human trafficking in Southeast Asia as a structural feature of labour regimes and mobility governance, rather than an isolated criminal phenomenon. abstract: Abstract Marine plastic litter is a major environmental problem across all oceans, including remote regions. abstract: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. abstract: Globally, intertidal molluscs are integral to the subsistence, commercial, and cultural identities of coastal and inland communities dependent on marine resources for survival. Despite their importance, the knowledge of intertidal zones in South Africa remains fragmented across ecological, socio-economic, and biotechnological disciplines. abstract: This paper demystifies the popular perception that Kerala’s coastal communities have retained their traditional fishing culture (Kerala Tourism Citation2022), often romanticised in digital archives, using Vypeen Island as a case study. While digital archival narratives present harmonious images of cultural continuity, they disregard ecological and socio-economic issues that contour the coastal life. abstract: The mismatch between the scale of ecological processes and management decisions represents a significant challenge in marine conservation. This misalignment can result in ineffective conservation measures and compromise the sustainability of marine ecosystems. However, the ecological consequences of the organic matter released following bloom collapse via viral infection are poorly understood. abstract: This article contributes to and expands the environmental history of recreational fishing through examining the development of recreational fishing in late colonial Luanda, Angola, 1945–1975. It draws on colonial archives, newspapers, tourism magazines, specialised fishing periodicals and oral testimonies to argue that recreational fishing developed through processes of dwelling in different coastal environments as practitioners and practices took shape in relation to their ecological conditions and possibilities. abstract: The Echigo Plain in central Japan is an actively subsiding sedimentary basin influenced by tectonic subsidence and anthropogenic activity. title: From Diving Sites Toward Sustainable Underwater Trails: Formal and Informal Routes, Underwater Attractions, and Nature Conservation Considerations in Selected Polish Case Studies
abstract: Inland diving sites may contain routes, attractions, and infrastructure, but these elements do not determine how a future underwater tourist trail should be organized. This study applies an emerging pre-implementation framework using an 85-record database of Polish inland diving sites compiled from specialist diving sources, operator and institutional materials, maps, and scientific publications. All records were screened; thirty-seven identifiable arrangements in 31 records were assessed using three route-confirmation criteria (T1–T3): spatial identification, reproducibility, and current use.

abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based facial recognition system that utilizes a police photo archive for real-time suspect identification at maritime seaports. The system processes real-time images captured by UAVs and compares them against a curated database of 669 known suspects. abstract: In 1972, as Toronto’s cultural landscape was being reshaped by postwar immigration and countercultural movements, poet Gwendolyn MacEwen and musician Nikos Tsingos opened the Trojan Horse at 179 Danforth Avenue. abstract: The postglacial evolution of High Arctic coastal environments is recorded in the rich fossiliferous archives of raised marine terraces. This study employs a multi‐proxy approach combining molluscan community analysis, taphonomy and sedimentology to reconstruct the Early to Mid‐Holocene environmental dynamics of the Mimerdalen embayment in the Billefjorden area of central Svalbard. abstract: Nigeria combines a large burden of mismanaged plastic waste with strong dietary reliance on fish, which makes the contamination of fish by microplastics a question of ecological and public-health relevance. abstract: Women in Jorong Pasia Tiku, a coastal village in West Sumatra, run small enterprises but rarely try to grow them. This study asks why, and what that choice reveals about how Minangkabau women act within their gender relations and coastal livelihoods. Research on women’s entrepreneurship usually tracks income, growth, and digital adoption. abstract: Despite the ecological and economic importance of Ria de Aveiro, Portugal, little is known about the diversity and seasonal dynamics of fungal communities. The scalloped hammerhead shark (Sphyrna lewini) is a cosmopolitan species known to undergo ontogenetic habitat shifts. abstract: This article reconceptualizes the Atrato River as a living pedagogical archive that participates in the formation of Black education in Chocó, Colombia. abstract: This article examines how idiomatic and figurative language constructs environmental meaning in the works of the American writer Ernest Hemingway and the Uzbek novelist Tog'ay Murod. Currently, this is the smallest and possibly the most ancient island population of canids on Earth. Among the endemics of island faunas, carnivores are generally very rare, and among the canids only the California island fox (Urocyon littoralis) is listed in taxonomic and conservation databases. title: Political Ecology of Agrarian Change in Social Forestry among the Tana Ai Community in Sikka Regency, East Nusa Tenggara
abstract: This paper examines how the dynamics of Social Forestry, which serves as a means of establishing new spaces/territories, trigger agrarian, social, economic, and ecological changes in communities, and even give rise to socio-territorial conflicts between the state and local communities. Building on the political ecology perspective, this article addresses two interrelated questions. title: Between Helsinki and Brussels: The 1995 EU Commission Strategy for the South Caucasus and the Emergence of an EU Strategy on Russia
abstract: This article examines the European Union’s (EU) unsuccessful effort to develop a common strategy toward the South Caucasus and argues that the process nevertheless played a significant role in the evolution of the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) and emerging debates on a common strategy toward Russia. title: Thinking With Care About Animals in Medicine and Veterinary Medicine: Gender and the Politics of Care in Scotland, 1910–30
abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, we ‘think with care’ about gender in Scotland in the early twentieth century, undertaking an ethnographic approach to the archive of OneKind, formerly the Scottish Society for the Prevention of Vivisection (SSPV), which has only recently been catalogued. In exploring the development of the SSPV from its beginnings in 1911 to 1930, we draw on Joan Tronto's definition of care and Puig de la Bellacasa's three dimensions of care: labour/work, affect/affections and ethics/politics. title: Setting time of alkali-activated materials: Mechanisms, controlling factors, and retardation strategies
abstract: Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are emerging sustainable binders with low carbon emissions and promising performance, but their practical application is limited by highly variable and system-dependent setting behaviour. abstract: Roadsides represent one of the most extensive anthropogenic networks globally, yet no integrative framework currently supports their systemic ecological characterisation and condition assessment. These areas can mitigate the environmental impacts of roads; yet this potential requires a clearer understanding of their functioning. abstract: ABSTRACT This qualitative case study examined how the Center for Science and the Schools (CSATS), a university‐based intermediary organization, sustained partnerships between STEM researchers and K‐12 educators over 20 years (2004–2024). Data were collected through surveys of 21 STEM research faculty across 16 disciplines, 11 current and former CSATS personnel, evaluations from 477 teachers, and eight archival documents spanning CSATS' history. title: “Don’t Throw Money Away”: Reynolds, Alcoa, and Aluminum Beverage Can Recycling in the United States, 1958–1990
abstract: This article uses oral histories and archival evidence from two major aluminum firms, Alcoa and Reynolds, to reevaluate the interlinked histories of the aluminum beverage can and recycling in the United States. Aluminum firms introduced cans alongside salvage programs that paid consumers for discarded cans, responding to material incentives as well as to growing environmental criticism of disposable containers. title: Vulnerability assessment of non-target species in Rastrineobola argentea (Pellegrin, 1904) artisanal capture fisheries in Lake Victoria, Uganda
abstract: The study assessed the vulnerability of non-target species in Rastrineobola argentea fishery in Uganda’s artisanal capture fisheries in Lake Victoria. A cross-sectional survey of 270 fishers at Katosi and Kiyindi (July 2024) was conducted, supplemented by secondary data on non-target species’ biology. We reviewed literature, interviewed fishers, and used physical observation to identify non-target species. title: Sweetening the Empire: Sugar and Western-Style Confectionery in Modern Japan and Taiwan
abstract: This dissertation examines how Western-style confectionery such as caramel, chocolate, chewing gum, and other sweets became intertwined with Japan’s empire-building from the Meiji period (1868–1912) to the early postwar years. While there have been extensive studies on sugar labor, empire, and capitalism, this dissertation focuses on what happened after the sugar was harvested until it was manufactured into delicious confectionery goods. title: Plasma-Enhanced Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) with Self-Cleaning Electrode for Scalable Remediation of Particulate Matter in Large Diesel Engines
abstract: Abstract We have demonstrated a fundamentally new pollution control device that integrates a plasma-enhanced electrostatic precipitator (PE-ESP) with a self-cleaning electrode. In the PE-ESP, high-voltage (20 kV) nanosecond (20 ns) pulses generate a transient plasma that produces ion densities approximately 6 orders of magnitude higher than those created by a conventional DC corona. This plasma enhancement increases the particle charging efficiency and allows electrostatic precipitators to be designed much more compactly, making them suitable for mobile sources. title: Mobilizing the seafood industry for climate action
abstract: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies providing no climate-related disclosures. Reporting, which can be an indicator of action and priorities, has focused primarily on mitigation, with little attention to adaptation. We consider these gaps and propose four priorities to support capacity and pathways for climate-resilient seafood operations.

Objective: Analyze the scientific production related to the development of emotional intelligence in nursing students. title: Magnetotactic Bacteria at the Earth-Life-Materials Interface
abstract: Conspectus Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) are prokaryotes that biomineralize membrane-bound intracellular magnetite (Fe3O4) or greigite (Fe3S4) nanocrystals, termed magnetosomes. These crystals commonly form chains that function as nanoscale compass needles. As naturally evolved living magnetic nanomaterial systems, MTB connect intracellular biomineralization, magnetic-field-guided behavior, microbial ecology, geological recording, and biomimetic materials design. title: Encoding Environmental Information into Linguistic Forms: A Study of Medicinal Plant Names in Mankon and Moghamo Languages of Cameroon
abstract: This paper investigates the world views that underpin the naming of medicinal plants in Mankon and Moghamo, both Bamenda Grassfields languages of Cameroon. It investigates how environmental information is encoded in the linguistic forms used to name medicinal plants in Mankon and Moghamo, two Grassfields Bantu languages spoken in Cameroon. The study focuses on the relationship between plant nomenclature, morphological structure, semantic interpretation and the speakers’ knowledge of their natural environment. title: Distribution, Levels and Characteristics of Petrogenic Plastics Particles in the Sediments of River Ngadda
abstract: Plastics can fragment into micro and nano size particles by the action of environmental drivers in the ecosystem. The study was aimed at assessing the occurrence, composition, and environmental drivers of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) in the sediments of River Ngadda, Borno State, Nigeria. title: Convergence and divergence of Holocene fire regimes and vegetation dynamics on hills and in the Clay Belt of northwestern Quebec
abstract: The role of topography in long-term climate–fire–vegetation nexuses remains understudied, particularly in the boreal mixedwood lowlands of eastern Canada due to limited accessibility and scarcity of lake-sediment archives on hills. Yet, reconstructing paleoenvironmental conditions on hills is essential to understand long-term boreal landscape dynamics along the entire elevation gradient. We reconstructed fire activity and vegetation dynamics during the Holocene on hills in northwestern Quebec (Canada). title: Influence of Foraging Effort and Diet on Maternal Energy Stores and Offspring Weaning Mass in Gray Seals ( Halichoerus grypus )
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how foraging behavior and diet influence individual reproductive success is a key interest in evolutionary ecology. This is particularly true for capital breeding species where the accumulation and storage of energy to support offspring is critical, often following the “bigger‐is‐better” hypothesis. title: Estimating absolute DNA abundance from replicated metabarcoding
abstract: Abstract Datasets derived from mixed‐template DNA amplification and sequencing (‘metabarcoding’) are common in environmental DNA (eDNA), microbiome or microbial ecology analyses. Such metabarcoding data have been broadly used to inform estimates of biodiversity, distribution and abundance across a wide range of species and habitats. Generally, data from metabarcoding consist of a table of read‐counts assigned to each of a set of taxa or sequence variants. Methodology: A systematic review of a qualitative and descriptive design was conducted using content analysis applied to twenty scientific articles selected from the Scopus, SciELO, Dialnet, Redalyc, and Latindex databases, following the PRISMA guidelines. abstract: Abstract This study has been conducted to understand the patterns of greenhouse gas emissions in the industrial sectors of Bangladesh and to analyse the driving forces behind these patterns. Environmentally extended input−output tables of Bangladesh for the period from 1991 − 2021 from the EORA database and Asian Development Bank have been used in this paper. title: Recombinant expression of single eukaryotic-like proteins changes bacteria-sponge interactions
abstract: Abstract Eukaryotic-like proteins (ELP) are often found in intracellular symbionts of insects, plants and evolutionary early-branching sponges, however their functions remain largely uncharacterised. Here we show that the recombinant expression of single genes of various ELP classes can confer on free-living cyanobacteria the capacity to escape phagocytosis by sponges and thus enable intracellular survival. The findings establish ELPs as molecular factors that can control sponge-microbe interactions, which has implications for the evolution of microbial symbiosis.

title: Advancing pyrolysis–gas chromatography mass spectrometry for tire wear particle mass quantification: effects of elastomer type, microstructure, and sample preparation
abstract: Tire and road wear particles (TRWPs) are a major source of microplastic pollution, yet their accurate quantification by pyrolysis gas chromatography mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) remains challenging due to variability in tire tread composition and pyrolysis marker performance. To better understand the sources of this variability, this study systematically investigates how elastomer type, microstructure, sample preparation, and calibration material influence pyrolysis marker formation and quantification accuracy. title: Community Assembly Processes in Tropical Intertidal Rockpool Fishes
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the drivers of community assembly in extreme and dynamic environments, such as intertidal rockpools, requires the integrated assessment of environmental filtering, species traits, phylogeny, and species interactions. This study aimed to quantify the multi‐faceted drivers of rockpool fish assemblage structure by examining: (a) the association with physical and structural pool attributes, (b) the influence of species functional traits and phylogenetic relatedness, (c) residual co‐occurrence patterns suggestive of species interactions, and (d) temporal and spatial dynamics.

title: Exploring essential oils and propolis as adjuncts or alternatives to azole antifungals for Candida infections: Laboratory experimental study
abstract: Background. Fungal infections caused by Candida species represent a significant and growing threat to human health, particularly among immunocompromised individuals, such as those undergoing chemotherapy, organ transplant recipients, and patients in intensive care units. These opportunistic pathogens are responsible for a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, ranging from superficial mucosal infections to life-threatening invasive candidiasis. title: Floristic diversity and vascular plant contributions of Wari-La trans Himalaya Ladakh India
abstract: Ladakh, a high-altitude cold desert in the Indian, Trans-Himalayan region, is home to diverse and ecologically significant plant species, many of which possess high medicinal properties. However, due to its harsh climatic conditions, rugged terrain and geopolitical constraints, floristic research in this region remains incomplete. The Present study focuses on the documentation of the Wari-La region, a high-altitude pass between the Indus and Nubra Valleys, which has been largely overlooked in previous botanical explorations. title: Performance evolution in Olympic swimming over the last 100 years: A retrospective stroke-based analysis
abstract: This retrospective study examined the historical progression of Olympic swimming performance across 24 Olympic Games from Paris 1924 to Paris 2024. Finalist race data for 1553 women and 1641 men were extracted from the official World Aquatics database, including final times, reaction times, and calculated swimming speeds across all strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly) and Olympic distances (50-1500 m). title: Isolation and selection of phosphate-solubilizing bacteria from lotus (Nelumbo nucifera Gaernt.) soil
abstract: This study aimed to isolate and select bacterial strains with phosphate-solubilizing ability from lotus soil. From lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) soil samples collected at eight sites in the city of Can Tho, 40 phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strains were isolated. These strains were cultured in liquid National Botanical Research Institute Phosphate (NBRIP) medium, and the molybdenum blue method was used over 9 days to assess their phosphate solubilization. abstract: This article proposes an interpretative framework for inclusion in global higher education, with the aim of conducting a critical analysis of the international academic literature published between 2021 and 2025. By applying the Reflective Thematic Analysis method developed by Braun and Clarke, a corpus of 34 articles indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was systematised. These articles address inclusion through the categories of disability, gender and first-generation students (FGS). title: A Sustainable Ecotourism Model: Integrating Forest Conservation, Environmental Protection, and Local Economic Well-Being
abstract: Ecotourism is widely promoted as a development pathway that can simultaneously finance forest conservation, reduce environmental pressure, and raise local incomes. In practice, these three goals are usually pursued through separate policy instruments, and the literature remains fragmented across case studies that rarely explain how the goals reinforce or undermine one another. This study develops an integrative model that specifies the mechanisms linking forest conservation, environmental protection, and local economic well-being in ecotourism settings. abstract: This article presents the results derived from a bibliometric review of scientific production on the tourism-education binomial. The research aimed to analyze the perspectives from which this relationship is approached, based on the literature published between 2014 and 2024, in order to identify the predominant approaches, quantify scientific production, recognize who publishes, determine which journals disseminate the knowledge, and identify which countries conduct the research. However, adherence to IST consumption remains suboptimal, requiring a more comprehensive analysis of its determinants. This study aimed to examine the effects of predisposing, enabling, and reinforcing factors on adherence to IST consumption among adolescent girls based on the PRECEDE–PROCEED model through a systematic review and meta-analysis. abstract: Cachexia and sarcopenia are frequent conditions in cancer patients, associated with loss of muscle mass, functional impairment, poorer tolerance to treatments, and reduced quality of life. In this context, nutritional care plays a fundamental role in the prevention and management of these alterations, particularly through the optimization of dietary intake and the use of nutritional supplements. title: Emerging disease patterns among migrant workers in India: a scoping review
abstract: Internal migrants consist of a socially disadvantaged community who work under informal and labour-intensive sectors. Due to poor working conditions, lack of health care services, and negative social determinants of health, many health-related issues can occur. This scoping review is going to examine the existing literature regarding the health of internal migrants in India. A scoping review was conducted using the PRISMA-ScR checklist. abstract: Environmental crisis is currently one of the biggest worldwide challenges, and to address it, there is a pressing need to move beyond the scientific contexts to cultural forms such as literature, religion, arts, and folklore that transcend rational understanding. Amitav Ghosh, in his fictional work Gun Island, engages with it by establishing an intersection between the changing ecological scenario and the Bengali folktale of the Gun Merchant and the snake goddess Manasa Devi. abstract: Construct your Porphyrian tree! Science does not begin with a frantic raid on databases, but in "phase zero": the mental laboratory where the axe is sharpened before the first strike. This work proposes abandoning "scientific piracy"—that hollow act of copying others' variables and overlaying empty data—and instead becoming architects of knowledge, possessing true intellectual sovereignty.This summons proposes a return to the Porphyrian tree: a logical compass from the third century designed to clear the mire of blurred concepts. title: New insights into the potential introduction pathways of Callinectes sapidus Rathbun, 1896 (Decapoda, Portunidae) in European waters
abstract: Two new COI haplotypes of the invasive Callinectes sapidus were reported for the first time in the western Iberian Peninsula and one of them in Europe, providing new insights into the origin of this species' invasion in European waters. The new haplotypes were recorded at very low frequencies (< 1%) in the Guadalquivir Estuary during 2021 and 2022 and correspond to those reported in the Gulf of Mexico and Brazil, respectively. title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. Together, these processes provide a framework for understanding long-term climate evolution over the past 540 million years.

abstract: Childhood obesity is an important public health problem of multifactorial origin, associated with unhealthy eating habits, physical inactivity, and family, social, and environmental factors. In this context, nurses play a relevant role in health promotion and the prevention of excess weight. Objective: To analyze the role of nurses in the prevention of childhood obesity, identifying strategies, interventions, and barriers related to care. abstract: Introduction: Beta vulgaris, commonly known as beet, comprises three main groups that differ in their macro- and micronutrient composition, particularly in their sugar content. The altissima subspecies, known as sugar beet, has the highest sugar concentration, ranging from 16% to 20%. Objective: To highlight the characteristics of sugar beet and its clinical applications. title: Automation at the gate: can internal security volunteer applications be pre-screened?
abstract: Abstract This article examines the legality of introducing a databased pre-screening stage in the application procedure for internal security volunteers in Estonia. It asks under what conditions automated pre-screening at the outset of administrative procedures can be considered lawful. title: Incidencia de la gestión educativa institucional en la atención inclusiva de estudiantes con necesidades educativas especiales.
abstract: The article titled “The Impact of Institutional Educational Management on the Inclusive Support of Students with Special Educational Needs (SEN)” addresses the need to recognize that educational inclusion encompasses access, participation, and, fundamentally, the curricular accommodations necessary to ensure these students’ continued enrollment in the regular education system. The overall objective was to analyze the impact of institutional educational management on the inclusive support of students with special educational needs. title: An assessment of microplastic contamination in freshwater fish from the Upper Doce River basin (Minas Gerais, Brazil): a 2003 baseline study
abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs)—plastic particles smaller than 5 mm—have become a growing environmental concern due to their pervasive presence in aquatic ecosystems. This study investigates the presence of MPs in freshwater fish specimens collected in 2003 in a small urban pond (Upper Doce River basin, Brazil). From the 744 fragments detected, 258 were registered in Australoheros facetus , 260 in Geophagus brasiliensis , and 226 in Oreochromis niloticus , one of the most consumed freshwater fish species in Brazil. The results revealed MPs distributed in the gills, digestive tracts, and ovaries.

title: Spatial opportunity, rather than conserved traits, is associated with encroachment among African Vachellia species
abstract: Abstract Woody plant encroachment is transforming savanna ecosystems, but the factors determining why some woody species proliferate while others remain at low densities remain poorly understood. We tested whether documented encroachment among African Vachellia species is associated with geographic range size, available functional traits, or phylogenetic structure. abstract: Context: Heuristic strategies enable students to approach mathematical problems through flexible and diverse procedures, fostering conceptual understanding and the development of problem-solving skills. Their incorporation into basic education represents an alternative for strengthening cognitive processes and positive attitudes toward mathematics learning. Objective: To analyze the development and application of heuristic strategies aimed at mathematical problem solving among students in Regular Basic Education. title: Performance of a new regression equation for predicting energy expenditure and its potential for identifying dietary reference values for energy
abstract: The performance of a prediction equation for total energy expenditure (TEE), derived from a large database of doubly labelled water (DLW) measurements of TEE held at the International Atomic Energy Agency, which has been proposed for estimating population energy requirements (ER) from basic anthropometric data as a replacement for the factorial method, is tested against a dataset of 450 DLW-derived measures of TEE in randomly selected urban US adults aged 40-69 years, and its bias is evaluated. title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), in landfill leachate under mesophilic conditions by quantifying carbon conversion to biogas. title: Species Distribution, Species Characterization, and Antifungal Susceptibility of Clinical Dermatophyte Isolates
abstract: The global epidemiology of dermatophytosis is rapidly changing due to the emergence of antifungal-resistant dermatophytes. Epidemiological surveillance has highlighted the need for accurate species-level identification and interaction between clinical microbiology laboratories and clinicians for treatment decisions and early detection of resistant strains. title: Scaling of dimensions and concentrations of plastics in two Dutch rivers
abstract: Plastic pollution raised great environmental concerns due to its persistence and widespread presence. To model ecological impacts, such as ingestion by wildlife, information on the abundance and dimensions of plastic particles is fundamental. Our study examined the relationships between size dimensions (length, area, circumference) of individual particles and the length of particles, their concentration, and cumulative surface area. title: La psicología humanista en las drogodependencias: una visión comprensiva del fenómeno
abstract: Drug dependence has traditionally been recognized as a disease, and there is a growing trend toward evidence-based treatments. At the same time, humanistic psychology has made significant contributions to the conceptualization of this phenomenon, therapeutic intervention, and the adaptation of techniques to individuals' specific needs. These contributions can be understood within the transition from nonprofessional to professional treatments, grounded in research and practical experience, and shaped by contemporary nuances associated with postmodernity. title: Cigarrillos electrónicos en jóvenes: ¿Cuáles son los verdaderos efectos en la salud?
abstract: Electronic cigarettes emerged as an alternative for conventional cigarette consumers, given that smoking accounts for 9% of deaths worldwide. Their initial goal was to facilitate smoking cessation through a progressive reduction in nicotine intake. However, electronic cigarettes have fostered nicotine addiction in young people without prior exposure to tobacco. This situation is a public health concern, as it compromises the respiratory and systemic health of users.
