title: From DPSIR to Cultural Feedback: An Ecocritical Four-Pillar Framework for Reading Anthropocene Crises
abstract: Scholarship on the Anthropocene remains divided between Earth-system analyses of material change and environmental-humanities readings of crisis narrative, a split that leaves each side under-equipped to explain how industrial power, ecological rupture, and cultural meaning shape one another. Integrative models already exist. The most established is the Driver-Pressure-State-Impact-Response (DPSIR) framework, adopted by the European Environment Agency to organise environmental indicators for policy. title: Adaptations of mitochondrial complexes in aquatic mites: A comparative study of Eupodides and Anystides
abstract: Aquatic mites have successfully colonized freshwater habitats, providing an excellent model for investigating the molecular basis of adaptive evolution. Because mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is essential for cellular energy production, adaptive changes in mitochondrial protein-coding genes may reflect evolutionary responses to environmental pressures. title: Genetic Diversity of Hepatitis B Virus and Drug Resistance among Pregnant Women in Tharaka-Nithi County, Kenya: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: With an estimated 360 million people chronically infected, hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has become one of the major global public health concerns, yet little is known about the genetic diversity and drug resistance among pregnant women in Kenya. Therefore, this study investigated the genetic diversity and drug resistance of hepatitis B virus among pregnant women in Tharaka-Nithi County, Kenya. abstract: Accredited social health activists (ASHAs) are an important component of community-based health service delivery in India. abstract: The aquatic biome is exposed to a significant threat of persistent contamination by polyethylene (PE) in the ecosystem. A critical research gap exists in PE-induced tissue-specific bioaccumulation, associated immune and stress responses in fish, followed by potential bioremediation solutions. The present study investigated the bioaccumulation of PE particles and subsequent oxidative stress in Labeo rohita induced by two different doses (0.1 and 0.5 mg/L) over 2 weeks. abstract: Methods from complexity science can help us better understand the development of socioecological systems. Here we investigate how human relationships with diverse species were structured through ecological and cultural networks in the Society Islands and the Gambier Islands, two archipelagoes of Central Eastern Polynesia. abstract: The phylum Rotifera has many species complexes that require integrative analyses to resolve their taxonomic identity. Brachionus angularis comprises different morphotypes. In Aguascalientes, Mexico, we observed two of these morphotypes coexisting. To explore their species identity, we applied an integrative approach that combined taxonomical, ecological, and molecular data. title: 24-hour movement behaviour composition associated with desired social-emotional functioning in the early years
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Movement behaviours (sleep, sedentary behaviour, and physical activity) influence numerous health outcomes in children, including their social-emotional development. title: Integrated geothermal applications in Türkiye for energy carbon management and resource recovery
abstract: Abstract Türkiye is important for geothermal energy not only because it produces electricity from high-temperature fields, but also because it uses geothermal resources for other innovative direct-use applications. A large part of the resource value comes from direct heat use, chemically complex fluids, separated gases, and the way these systems are operated at the surface. abstract: ABSTRACT We use offshore seismic reflection data combined with published geologic and geodetic studies to examine the timings and styles of deformation around the South Caspian Basin, an enigmatic aseismic ‘block’ within the Arabia‐Eurasia collision that moves relative to its surroundings. abstract: Protected Area (PA) management faces multiple challenges, making Protected Area management effectiveness (PAME) assessment essential for promoting continuous improvements in biodiversity conservation. In this context, this study aims to map the global distribution of PAME assessment tools developed in Brazil and internationally, and to analyze how their indicators address society-nature interactions. abstract: Abstract Deforestation and monoculture expansion in tropical watersheds represent important pressures on aquatic ecosystems, yet their associations with zooplankton communities in Neotropical reservoirs remain poorly understood. We evaluated how land use and land cover are associated with the distribution, diversity, composition, and structure of zooplankton communities in six tropical reservoirs with contrasting landscape configurations and trophic conditions. abstract: El pueblo aymara forma parte de los territorios y comunidades andinas del norte de Chile, y su lengua, perteneciente a la familia lingüística jaqi, se ha sostenido a través de generaciones en el ámbito escolar y comunitario. abstract: Symbiosis is a fundamental biological strategy that enables metabolic complementation between distinct organisms. The amoeba Mayorella viridis establishes a photosymbiotic relationship with the green alga Chlorella, yet the physiological basis of this association remains poorly understood. abstract: Freshwater copepods are an important component of aquatic biodiversity in Thailand, but information on their diversity and distribution is still scattered across taxonomic and ecological studies. abstract: Abstract Surfactant‐containing organic‐inorganic mixed aerosols can exhibit diverse mixing states following liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS), ranging from core‐shell to partial engulfing and inverse core‐shell structures, thereby altering their chemical, physical, and optical properties, as well as associated geochemical processes. title: Morphological variation in Middle-Late Pleistocene stone points: a pan-African perspective
abstract: Stone points are central to defining the African Middle Stone Age (MSA), yet their morphological variability has rarely been quantitatively examined at a continental scale. Longstanding distinctions between ‘specific’ industries (e.g., Aterian, Still Bay, Howiesons Poort) and more geographically widespread ‘generic’ MSA assemblages remain unresolved, in part because typological definitions of these cultural entities were historically based on qualitative assessments of limited samples. title: Evidence of Spatial Redistribution Without Detectable Genetic Change in the Greater Caribbean Manatee ( Trichechus manatus manatus ) Population of Puerto Rico
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the genetic diversity and spatial dynamics of small, isolated populations is essential for species conservation. The Greater Caribbean manatee ( Trichechus manatus manatus ) population in Puerto Rico is classified as endangered and has previously shown limited mitochondrial haplotype diversity. In this study, we analysed mitochondrial DNA control region sequences from 36 samples collected between 2010 and 2021 and compared them to 115 previously published sequences. title: New larval host plants for a few Indian butterflies (Lepidoptera: Rhopalocera)
abstract: The present communication reports new larval host plants for four Indian Butterflies. Based on field surveys and rearing experiments, Crateva adansonii DC., Lepidium didymum L., and Barleria cristata L. were established as larval host plants of Belenois aurota (Fabricius, 1793), Pieris canidia (Linnaeus, 1768), and Junonia orithya (Linnaeus, 1758) respectively; and Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre. and Bauhinia racemosa Lam. as larval host plants for Leptotes plinius (Fabricius, 1793).

abstract: Geopolymer concrete (GPC) and glass-fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars are of interest for structural applications in which corrosion resistance and reduced reliance on Portland cement are desirable. This study examined nine rectangular beams under monotonic four-point bending: one ordinary-Portland-cement (OPC) beam with steel reinforcement, one OPC beam with GFRP reinforcement, and seven GPC–GFRP beams. title: Pengarusutamaan Ekowisata Ujung Tamiang dalam Mendukung Konservasi Tuntong Laut (Batagur borneoensis)
abstract: Tuntong laut (Batagur borneoensis) merupakan spesies kura-kura berstatus sangat terancam punah (Critically Endangered) akibat degradasi ekosistem dan aktivitas manusia. Upaya pengarusutamaan pelestarian spesies ini telah dikembangkan di Desa Pusung Kapal melalui pendekatan ekowisata yang melibatkan masyarakat lokal dan wisatawan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi peran Ekowisata Ujung Tamiang dalam mendukung konservasi alam melalui edukasi interaktif, pelindungan lanskap pesisir, dan perluasan partisipasi publik. abstract: Penggunaan pewarna pada produk pangan seperti kue, olahan perikanan, dan makanan penutup bertujuan untuk meningkatkan daya tarik visual serta minat konsumen. Namun, pemahaman masyarakat terkait sumber dan keamanan pewarna pangan, khususnya pewarna sintetik yang tidak peruntukkan bagi makanan, masih perlu untuk ditingkatkan. title: The geology, geochronology and S isotopes of the Binghu Au deposit, Wulansai’er district: Implications for ore genesis and regional gold metallogenesis in the Chinese segment of South Tianshan
abstract: The timing, tectonic setting, and genetic characteristics of gold mineralization in the Chinese segment of South Tianshan remain poorly constrained, limiting our understanding of regional gold metallogenesis. The recently discovered Binghu Au deposit (approximately 40 t) in the Wulansai’er district provides an important opportunity to address these uncertainties. title: Between transgressive intervention and transboundary coordination: quasi-meta-governance in China’s environmental public interest litigation for sustainable development
abstract: In China’s procuratorate-led Environmental Public Interest Litigation (EPIL) system, the procuratorate has to navigate the dilemma between transboundary coordination and transgressive intervention to achieve effective collaborative governance. To conceptualize this distinctive role, this paper extends meta-governance theory by introducing the concept of the “quasi-meta-governor” to explain how a judicially embedded actor can coordinate fragmented governance networks without possessing fully transcendent authority. abstract: Kartpostallar; kişiler arası haberleşmeyi görsel temsille birleştiren ve yayımlandıkları dönemin toplumsal, kültürel ve kentsel yaşamına ilişkin veriler taşıyan iletişim araçlarıdır. title: Reuse of ESR-irradiated tooth enamel for amino acid geochronology: assessing the impact of gamma irradiation
abstract: Abstract Hominin and faunal fossil collections are valuable scientific resources for investigating past populations, making it critically important to preserve these rare materials and prioritise minimally destructive methods. Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating of tooth enamel typically requires laboratory irradiation of powdered subsamples; however, the effects of this treatment on organic biomolecules, and therefore their potential reuse for amino acid geochronology (AAG), remain largely unknown. title: Microstructure and corrosion behaviors of Ni and Ti cold spray coatings for spent nuclear fuel storage canisters
abstract: The microstructural characteristics and pitting corrosion behaviors of Ni and Ti coatings deposited on sensitized austenitic stainless steel 304 (SS304) using cold spray technology were investigated for potential application in dry cask storage systems (DCSSs) for spent nuclear fuel. Microstructural evolution from the feedstock powders to the respective coatings was characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). title: Phylogenetic evidence for the Taxon Cycle: contemporary tests across island and continental systems
abstract: Abstract Modern phylogenetic evidence offers novel opportunities to test classic models in island biogeography. One of the earliest, E. O. Wilson’s Taxon Cycle, proposed that insular lineages progress through sequential and predictable phases, beginning with geographic expansion, followed by ecological specialization, and ultimately range contraction (and even extinction), shaped by dispersal and interspecific competition. title: Legal System Challenges in Environmental Governance in the Case of Benoa Bay Reclamation
abstract: The controversy over the reclamation of Benoa Bay demonstrates that environmental governance depends not only on the existence of regulations but also on legal structure, legal substance, and legal culture. This study aims to analyze environmental governance in Benoa Bay using Lawrence M. Friedman’s Legal System Theory. abstract: El artículo examina la transición de Groenlandia de una periferia insular hacia su consolidación como el “Heartland Marítimo” del siglo XXI. El sistema internacional actual dibuja un escenario de saturación de las rutas ecuatoriales y una crisis del modelo logístico tradicional. title: Trolls, Giants, and ‘Other Folks’ in Finnish Folklore, Archaeology, and Landscape
abstract: Finnish folklore involves numerous stories, tales, and legends that describe human encounters with non-human beings, such as giants, trolls, and earth-dwellers. While this folklore has sometimes been interpreted as reflections of historical events, the consensus today is that such an approach is inapplicable. This article proposes, however, that folklore can provide clues about the dynamics of certain long-term historical cultural processes and how they were anchored on ancient sites and other landscape elements. title: Seismogenic Consequences of COH‐Fluid Rock Interactions in Ultramafic Fault Zones Insights From Carbonation‐Decarbonation Friction Experiments
abstract: Abstract Fluid‐rock interactions have major implications on the frictional behavior of fault rocks. Infiltration of CO 2 ‐bearing fluids in ultramafic fault zones causes the progressive formation of serpentinite, talc‐magnesite (soapstone) and quartz‐magnesite (listvenite) assemblages. Reversed reactions occur when CO 2 ‐poor fluids interact with carbonated fault zones. title: Quantum biogenesis driven by methylated colloidal sulfur within diamagnetic metal matrices and proto-cell self-assembly
abstract: Abstract The transition from prebiotic chemistry to functional, self-replicating cellular architectures remains an unresolved milestone in origin-of-life research. While conventional paradigms focus heavily on transition-metal ferromagnetism, the role of quantum spin states and localized diamagnetic gradients in macromolecular organization is largely unexamined. title: Mechanical Damping Performance of Polymer Composites Reinforced by Self‐Welded Fiber Scaffolds
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the performance trade‐off between high stiffness and high damping in polymer materials, this study proposes a novel method for fabricating damping composites based on self‐welded fiber scaffolds. The approach involves selectively welding polymeric welding phase (PA6) at fiber's intersection points to form a three‐dimensional fiber scaffold, followed by in situ polymerization of acrylates within the pores of the fiber scaffold to generate the damping matrix. title: Checklist of threatened plants of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
abstract: Covering approximately 10% of Borneo’s land area, Sabah is one of the global hotspots for plant biodiversity, yet it faces increasing threats to its flora due to habitat loss and exploitation. This paper aims to compile a comprehensive checklist of threatened plant species in Sabah based on assessments published in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. A total of 660 vascular plant species from 73 families and 199 genera are classified as threatened and compiled in this checklist. title: Roost site characteristics and habitat associations of bats (Mammalia: Chiroptera) in Kamrup District, Assam, India
abstract: Chiroptera play vital ecological roles as pollinators, seed dispersers, and insect population regulators; however, information on their roost site requirements remains limited in many parts of northeastern India. The present study examined roost site characteristics and habitat associations of Chiroptera in Kamrup District, Assam, India. Field surveys conducted from November 2019 to March 2025 documented 16 roosts across nine locations, including natural substrates (trees, leaves, tree cavities and bamboo internodes) and artificial structures (houses and building crevices). title: Ecological Preaching Communication Strategy as a Response to Social Change in the Digital Era: A Comparative Study of Al-Ittifaq Ciwidey Islamic Boarding School and Fish Bank Indonesia
abstract: The global ecological crisis and contemporary social problems compel Islamic institutions to respond through concrete action rather than verbal preaching alone. This study analyzes ecological da'wah communication strategies in responding to social change through a comparative study of Pesantren Al-Ittifaq Ciwidey and Fish Bank Indonesia. Both institutions demonstrate how Islamic theological values are operationalized through action-based programs in distinct institutional contexts. title: Cue for dominance? Visuo-chemical communication in males of Sambar Rusa unicolor in subtropical forests of India
abstract: Olfactory signalling among mammals remains understudied, particularly in ungulates. This study documents “preaching,” an olfactory communication behaviour exhibited by male Sambar Deer Rusa unicolor, that involves an upright posture, rubbing of the pre-orbital gland, and sniffing tree bases. Observations were made using camera traps in the Haridwar Range of Rajaji Tiger Reserve, Uttarakhand, India. Six bucks over three years old were observed preaching from February 2024 to March 2024. title: Cabinets of curiosities: collecting, displaying, consuming
abstract: The cabinet of curiosities (Wunderkammer), a pan-European practice of collecting, displaying, and consuming from the Renaissance to the nineteenth century, has in the past attracted museum scholars and cultural historians rather than literary critics. This special issue of EJES argues for its relevance to literary criticism and theory. title: Professionalism: the Australian Emergency Management Uniform Minimum Dataset
abstract: The professionalisation of emergency management in Australia is ongoing. Supporting that process is the development of a body of knowledge to support the new profession. The body of knowledge for emergency management requires that emergency events are recorded in a manner and format that supports ongoing learning and research. There is currently no agreed format or standard for the recording of emergency events in Australia. title: Biocontrol potential of a rhizosphere-associated Bacillus amyloliquefaciens F2 isolate against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4 in Pakistan
abstract: Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense is a serious fungal, soil-borne disease. It is also known as PANAMA disease, considered a major threat to the yield and quality of Banana worldwide. In this study, endophytic bacteria were isolated from soil, roots, and leaves of healthy banana plants growing in Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) tropical race 4 (TR4) infested soil. title: Bansa at Kapuluan: Notes on the Archipelagic Nuance of Bienvenido Lumbera’s discourse of the Region and Nationhood
abstract: This paper explores a re-reading of the ‘region’ that appears in National Artist Bienvenido Lumbera’s advocacy for valuing regional literature as a foundation of a strong national literature. His discourse against the othering of the regional literature as ‘vernacular’ is encapsuled in the philosophy of his works: that the region represents a precise, immediate worldview, while the national offers a wider, encompassing perspective of the Filipinos (Lumbera 156). title: “To a cupped hand’s size”: Reading Poetics of Scale in Edith Tiempo’s Poetry
abstract: Edith Cutaran Lopez-Tiempo’s body of work, alongside her stature as Philippine National Artist for Literature, has generated substantial scholarship on the fertile imaginaries and intersections of formalist poetics, the institutionalization of the writing workshop, and Philippine poetry in English. Building on these contributions, I turn instead to Tiempo’s negotiation of self-fashioning, memory work, and imaginative practice as a way of articulating questions of scale in her oeuvre. title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks
abstract: Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. Here, we used simulations to test the efficiency of monitoring species interactions within Biodiversity Observations Networks (BONs). title: The Nexus Between Agriculture, Cattle Breeding and Climate Change in The Island of Crete, Greece
abstract: Climate change threatens human prosperity as it affects many economic sectors including food production. Agriculture, cattle breeding and climate change are interrelated and interconnected affecting each other. Agriculture in Crete was in the past an important pillar in the local economy while nowadays its role has been decreased. title: Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: 2026 Expert Consensus
abstract: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Spasticity is one of the most frequent and highly disabling features of MS, often accompanied by cramps, pain, bladder dysfunction, sleep disturbances, fatigue, and tremor. Recently, the concept of ‘spasticity-plus syndrome’ (SPS) has emerged to reflect the interplay among these symptoms. title: Iberian copper and Bronze Age Europe: Late Bronze Age mining and supply at Las Minillas (Badajoz, Spain)
abstract: Despite abundant copper deposits, the deep history of copper mining in Iberia has not been as extensively studied as in other European ore-rich areas. Here, the authors present new radiocarbon dates that demonstrate Late Bronze Age copper mining at Las Minillas, near Granja de Torrehermosa (southern Spain). Extensive mining infrastructure and abundant stone tools further identify Las Minillas as one of the largest Late Bronze Age copper-mining complex securely dated in Spain. title: Precipitation Probability Distribution, Percent Runoff, and Trend Analysis for 25 Reservoir Basins in Texas from 1980–2019
abstract: This study analyzed precipitation probability distributions, percent runoff, and trends in precipitation from 1980 to 2019 in the Brazos, Colorado, Guadalupe, Neches, Red, and Trinity river basins in Texas for 25 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers reservoirs and 15 other reservoirs for the purpose of flood risk and water-resource management. title: Regionalized greenhouse gas emissions and infrastructure requirements for future global iron and steel production
abstract: Abstract The steel industry accounts for approximately 7–9% of global greenhouse gas emissions, making it a key sector for decarbonization. Here, we quantify current and prospective greenhouse gas emissions from crude steel production facilities worldwide. Based on life cycle assessment, current greenhouse gas emissions of global crude steel production are around 3.7 gigatonnes carbon dioxide equivalent per year, highly concentrated in Asia. title: Coupling of sedimentary environment and hazardous trace element enrichment in lacustrine oil shale: evidence from the Lunpola Basin, Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: The Lunpola Basin, developed during the Cenozoic era on the Tibetan Plateau, serves not only as a sedimentary record of plateau uplift but also as a significant reservoir of oil shale. This study focuses on the sedimentary environment of the oil shales in the Lunpola Basin and the enrichment mechanisms of trace elements, particularly hazardous elements, within them. title: UVC-LED Disinfection Technology: Mainstream Waveband Characteristics, Applications and Challenges
abstract: Driven by the global demand for public health security, ultraviolet C light-emitting diode (UVC-LED) disinfection technology has emerged as a promising mercury-free alternative to conventional methods. Adopting a wavelength-based comparative framework, this review systematically synthesizes the disinfection characteristics of four mainstream UVC-LED wavelength bands (233 nm, 254 nm, 260–270 nm, and 270–280 nm), facilitating direct cross-band comparison of inactivation mechanisms, biosafety profiles, and practical applicability. title: Combined toxicity of cyanotoxins and anthropogenic contaminants on Chlorella vulgaris: insights from single and binary mixture exposures
abstract: Aquatic organisms in eutrophic brackish and freshwater systems are chronically exposed to natural and anthropogenic contaminants, including cyanotoxins, metals and pesticides, mainly driven by cyanobacterial blooms and human activities. However, the environmental risks posed by their combinations to the aquatic environment remain poorly understood. title: Quantifying Carbon Storage in Black Ash Wetlands Following Emerald Ash Borer and Forest Management
abstract: Abstract The impacts of non-native Emerald Ash Borer (EAB) are likely to be most severe in black ash wetlands, possibly requiring preemptive forest management to maintain ecosystem functions such as carbon storage. We used a silvicultural experiment in northern Minnesota to evaluate how EAB-induced mortality and preemptive management affect total ecosystem carbon storage and the distribution of carbon among ecosystem pools. title: Plant taxonomic diversity of Barunei Hill, Eastern Ghats, India
abstract: The present study on Barunei Hill documented 149 plant species. Out of 149, native species and non-native species are 125 and 24, respectively. Native species account for 4.58% of the 2,727 species recorded in the flora of Odisha. Native species belong to 112 genera and 50 families at the same time non-native species represent 23 genera and 15 families. Of the 125 native species, 43 are trees, 37 herbs, 29 shrubs, and 16 lianas/twiners/climbers. title: New elevational limits of Himalayan mammals in eastern Sikkim, India
abstract: The eastern Himalaya is recognised as one of the most important biodiversity hotspots in the world. There is a limited understanding on the mammalian distributions in its high-altitude landscapes. To address the knowledge gap, we conducted extensive camera-trap surveys across protected and adjoining non-protected landscapes of eastern Sikkim, India, a part of this eastern Himalayan biodiversity hotspot between February 2023 and May 2026. abstract: A new species of the genus Neoterpnosia (Neoterpnosia mawphlangensis sp. nov.) is described from the semi-evergreen forests of Mawphlang Hills, Meghalaya, northeastern India, using morphological and bioacoustics analyses. title: Patronage and Accounting Between the Philippines and China, 1733–1797
abstract: Abstract Missionary efforts followed the expansion of the Old World’s frontiers, often entwined with trade. This article reviews the accounts of the Franciscan mission in China and of the obras pías of Manila during the eighteenth century to analyse how local conditions and empire-wide structures translated into specific actions on the ground. abstract: A escassez de rotas marítimas diretas entre o Norte do Brasil e a Região das Guianas limita o aproveitamento do potencial comercial da fronteira amazônica, diante do crescimento econômico de Guiana, Suriname e Guiana Francesa. abstract: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. title: Multi‐Scale Growth of an Mw 7.0 Earthquake via Hierarchical Cascading Rupture From an Mw 3.8 Repeating Event
abstract: Abstract To understand what governs earthquake size, we investigated the 2021 Mw 7.0 Japan Trench earthquake, which began near a nest of repeating earthquakes. High‐precision hypocenter relocation and P‐waveform correlation show that the mainshock initiated nearly identically to Mw 3.8 repeaters. Waveform deconvolution reveals that, after breaking the Mw 3.8 patch within 0.1 s, the mainshock rupture cascaded through Mw 5–6 patches within 2 s and into the main slip area at 3–6 s. title: Interacting Effects of Climate and Land Use on Biodiversity: A Guide to What They Are and Why They Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT Problem Climate and land‐use change are two key drivers of biodiversity change. Their widespread effects on species and communities have prompted fears that interactions between the two drivers could cause severe biodiversity loss. abstract: Cholera remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, where limited water and sanitation, population displacement, conflict and weak health systems sustain recurrent epidemics. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the social history of enslaved wet nurses in the eighteenth‐century Cape Colony, arguing that the romanticised depiction of these women within settler households was not a softening of the system of slavery but an integral part of how it functioned. title: Temporal trends in age at menarche among Sri Lankan girls: A review of published evidence (1950–2009)
abstract: Mean age at menarche (MAM) is a sensitive biological indicator of childhood nutrition and broader socio-economic conditions of a population, and its decline over time is well documented in developed countries. Several studies have been conducted in Sri Lanka since 1950 to estimate the MAM in different regions, ethnic groups and socio-economic strata, but the published evidence has not previously been collated. PubMed, Google Scholar, ResearchGate and the Sri Lanka Journals Online platform were searched and primary Sri Lankan publications reporting MAM were retrieved for the period 1950 to 2009

title: Infrastructures of differential inclusion: accommodation access for displaced persons in Italy
abstract: This article examines how Italian migration policies are translated in accommodation infrastructures at a local level. Applying the perspective of differential inclusion, it compares institutional reception pathways for people displaced from Ukraine under the Temporary Protection Directive (TPD) with ordinary asylum procedures. abstract: This study examined sustainability-oriented school leadership, environmental management practices, and climate resilience among selected school heads in Sapa-Sapa I District, Tawi-Tawi, as a basis for developing a Sustainable School Governance Framework. Anchored in the Whole-Institution Approach to Education for Sustainable Development, Sustainable Educational Leadership, and Organizational Climate Resilience, the study employed a descriptive-correlational design using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. title: Improved Estimates of Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity From Non‐Equilibrated Climate Simulations
abstract: Abstract Calculating equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) requires simulations of a thousand years or more for the climate to re‐establish equilibrium, but most ECS estimates are derived from shorter model integrations. The widely used “Gregory method” for such estimates systematically underestimates ECS, a bias previously attributed to the time‐dependence of climate feedbacks. Here we demonstrate this underestimate instead arises primarily from an underestimate of radiative forcing. abstract: Boron recovery from natural brines is of increasing industrial interest, yet the factors controlling its extraction efficiency remain insufficiently understood. In this work, the kinetics and equilibrium behaviour of boron extraction from synthetic brines mimicking the Salar de Hombre Muerto were investigated using 2-ethylhexan-1-ol and 2-butyloctan-1-ol diluted in kerosene. abstract: This study investigated the impact of electronic permit-to-work (e-PTW) systems on operational efficiency in the Nigerian oil and gas industry. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, and a questionnaire survey was used as the instrument for data collection. Collaboration, productivity, communication and error reduction were constructs used to capture operational efficiency. title: Economic Value of Bukittinggi City Regional Public Library: Travel Cost Approach and Contingency Valuation
abstract: Regional public libraries deliver services without charging admission, making their benefits difficult to observe in local budget accounts. This study estimated the economic value of the Bukittinggi City Regional Public Library and examined correlates of annual visit frequency and willingness to pay (WTP) for voluntary contributions. title: Automatic astrometric calibration of low-cost all-sky cameras
abstract: All-sky cameras support weather monitoring, amateur astronomy, fireball and space-debris detection, and measurements of light pollution. These applications require reliable astrometric calibration despite imperfect camera alignment and variable observing conditions. We present an open-source procedure that combines a compact fisheye model, an exact rotation to account for camera tilt, and automatic star matching. title: Climate Change, Migration, and National Security in Pakistan: Assessing The Emerging Nexus and Its Policy Implications
abstract: Climate change is increasingly affecting Pakistan’s livelihoods, human mobility, economic stability, and national security. This study examines the relationship between climate change, migration, and national security in Pakistan, focusing on how climate hazards disrupt livelihoods, generate displacement, and create wider security pressures. abstract: The Siegerland (W-Germany) exhibits distinct phases of intensive metallurgy during the Iron Age (2nd – 1st centuries BC) and Middle Ages (9th – 16th centuries AD) that coincide with landscape transformations and shifts in local subsistence economies. Multi-proxy analyses of alluvial sediments – pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, coprophilous fungal spores, and lipid biomarkers – provide insights into these land use changes. abstract: Background: Midwifery laboratories are essential for developing clinical competencies, yet service quality and resource adequacy are frequently assessed separately. Objectives: This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an integrated instrument for assessing midwifery laboratory quality. title: Animal Bones from Danish Single Grave Contexts
abstract: Since the 1890s, the Danish Single Grave Culture (SGC; c. 2850-2350 BCE) has been recognised as a distinct cultural complex with its core area centred on the sandy regions in Mid and Western Jutland, often associated with a pastoral-based economy. However, the absence of animal bone material from this area seriously constrains interpretations of prehistoric subsistence strategies and human-animal relations. abstract: Abstract Objective The implications of climate change are unfolding in riverine systems, carrying consequences for fish populations and further challenging fisheries management. In the Pacific Northwest, United States, significant expansions of nonnative bass (family Centrarchidae) habitat are projected, fueling concern for the recovery of imperiled Pacific salmon Oncorhynchus spp. due to known predation impacts. abstract: Haberlea rhodopensis Friv. (Gesneriaceae) is a Tertiary glacial relict endemic to the Balkan Peninsula and belongs to the rare group of vascular resurrection plants capable of successfully withstanding long periods of almost complete drought. In addition, the species is valued for its multiple applications as a rich source of various biologically active compounds and as an ornamental plant in rock gardens. abstract: Helminths induce regulatory T cells (Tregs) to establish chronic infections, promoting long-term persistence of both parasites and hosts. TGF-β1 is essential for Treg induction by initiating Foxp3 expression. title: Primary and secondary invasion pathways: why the distinction matters
abstract: Abstract The pathways by which non-native species are introduced and spread shape the rate and geographic patterns of biological invasions. They can be classified as primary, where species cross jurisdictional or biogeographic boundaries, or secondary, where they move within those boundaries after introduction. Despite economic, political, social, and ecological differences between these pathway types, most classification schemes and regulatory frameworks do not explicitly distinguish between them. title: Ultraviolet Fluorescence of a Black Horse Fly (Tabanus atratus) Larva
abstract: Many insects fluoresce when exposed to ultraviolet light, and it is becoming a useful tool for surveys. The availability of low-cost ultraviolet flashlights and their ease of use is providing an opportunity for researchers and citizen scientists to explore fluorescence in insects. This note reports the ultraviolet fluorescence of a Tabanus atratus (Black Horse Fly) larva.

abstract: Abstract Balinese temple restoration is commonly interpreted through symbolism, belief, and architectural tradition, yet such readings leave how ritual regulates material action insufficiently examined. This article reconceptualises ritual as a regulatory technology: a procedural infrastructure that authorises intervention, defines thresholds of acceptable change, and structures material circulation within living heritage. abstract: Abstract This paper identifies and traces a persistent yet largely unrecognized literary motif that I call “late-life worldbuilding.” Alongside the familiar portrayal of old age as a condition of physical decline and retrospective wisdom, the western literary tradition repeatedly imagines elderly protagonists embarking on visionary journeys toward the creation of new worlds and new forms of life. title: Facing far forward: Mental health in large-scale combat operations
abstract: Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCO) present unprecedented challenges to the provision of medical and mental health care on the battlefield. Characterized by restricted mobility, contested logistics, disrupted communication, drone attacks, subterranean environments and the necessity for prolonged field care, the LSCO environment will severely disrupt traditional models of combat and operational stress control (COSC) that rely on far-forward specialty providers and fixed facilities. abstract: Loloan Malay, a minority language spoken in Bali, lacks a standardized orthographic system, resulting in inconsistent spelling practices. This study provides a phonological description of Loloan Malay and examines orthographic challenges arising from phonological variation and language contact, with the aim of proposing a practical orthographic framework combining both phonemic and morphophonemic principles informed by community preferences. abstract: O diagnóstico da sífilis congênita (SC) precoce é frequentemente dificultado pela ausência de sinais clínicos ao nascimento e pelas limitações da sorologia neonatal, o que confere relevância à investigação do comprometimento ósseo, uma de suas manifestações mais frequentes. abstract: Abstract This paper examines how embodied, situated and relational experiences outside‐the‐classroom can open space for epistemic dislocations in Management Education under conditions of ecological crisis. abstract: Unscripted dialogic campaign programs remain underexplored as integrated political marketing strategies for candidate positioning and youth engagement. abstract: Türkiye produces roughly 70% of the world's hazelnuts, yet little is known about how price changes pass from producers to consumers in this market. abstract: Drymarchon corais is a generalist species, with a diet that includes amphibians, lizards, amphisbaenians, other snakes, eggs, birds, and small mammals. abstract: E-commerce has become a major force driving industrial upgrading, urban expansion, and urban–rural integration. abstract: Abstract Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. abstract: An interview with Peggy Mohan, which focuses mainly on her first book, Jahajin. It covers her perspectives on literary historiography, faction, and related topics.

abstract: The Inner Mongolia Pilot Free Trade Zone has created strong demand for graduates who combine English proficiency, practical cross-border e-commerce skills and local trade knowledge. abstract: The First Opium War is both a conventional starting point for modern Chinese history and an event readily reduced to political slogans. Mao Haijian’s The Qing Empire and the Opium War reconstructs the Qing military, intelligence, and decision-making processes behind the defeat; Julia Lovell’s The Opium War places the conflict within British imperial commerce and the politics of public memory. Reading the two books comparatively, this essay examines responsibility for defeat, the origins of the conflict, and the subsequent making and forgetting of war memory. abstract: Landslides are complex natural hazards resulting from interactions among geological, geomorphological, hydrological, climatic and anthropogenic processes. This study extends multi-analytical characterization by quantifying compressive strength and mass-based binder-to-aggregate ratio of four archeological mortar groups from Aden Cisterns, Harawa Pool, Seera Fort, and Salama Pool. title: Decoding Doctor Departure Decisions in Regional Queensland
abstract: Background: Medical workforce shortages are a pervasive issue across Australia, with rural and regional hospitals facing particular challenges in maintaining a stable workforce. Frequent turnover of prevocational doctors in these areas can adversely impact service delivery and healthcare outcomes. The primary aim of this study is to investigate the reasons why prevocational doctors leave regional hospitals, and whether these reasons vary across different regional settings. abstract: Abstract Dutch dietary patterns are high in animal-based foods, contributing to non-communicable diseases and environmental pressures, but may vary across generations due to social and cultural factors. Penelitian observasional dengan desain potong lintang dilaksanakan pada Januari–April 2026 dengan melibatkan 126 pasien yang memiliki data variabel lengkap dan kondisi klinis stabil. abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes (T2D) affects up to 18.3% of Mexicans, surpassing the global prevalence of 11.1%. Among Amerindian groups, Mayan ancestry has been linked to a higher risk of T2D. We examined associations of KCNJ11 (rs5215, rs5219) and TCF7L2 (rs7901695, rs11196205) genetic variants with T2D in 232 individuals, including 99 participants diagnosed with T2D and 132 metabolically healthy individuals. abstract: The objective of this study was to analyze the scientific production indexed in Scopus between 2020 and 2025 on the development of soft skills in teacher strengthening. title: Which treatment is most effective at reducing the damage caused by the pest box tree moth? A case in a Mediterranean mountain
abstract: Boxwood ( Buxus sempervirens ) is an important element of the European plant landscape. Currently, this species is seriously threatened due to the high impact of the pest box tree moth ( Cydalima perspectalis ). This lepidopteran is an invasive species of Asian origin that feeds exclusively on the genus Buxus . Management of this pest is necessary, but field trials are lacking. title: The litter decomposition dynamics under land-type conversion by microbial communities in the Yellow River floodplain
abstract: Land-type conversion contributes significantly to litter decomposition, yet microbial feedback mechanisms remain unclear in river-floodplain areas. abstract: Abstract Fungal infections have emerged as a significant concern in healthcare, due to the development of antifungal resistance and the limited availability of diagnostic and therapeutic options. The Candida species represent a category of particular importance with regard to fungi. Therefore, the implementation of infection prevention and control measures, such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) disinfection, is imperative in healthcare settings. title: Bondage, Dominación, Sumisión, Sadismo y Masoquismo (BDSM), consentimiento y derecho penal en España: Dilemas bioéticos y propuestas de regulación
abstract: Aquest article examina la tensió entre autonomia sexual, dignitat i tutela penal en el context del BDSM consentit a Espanya. title: Breathing at the Border: PM₂.₅ Exposure, Immigration, and COPD Across Census Tracts Close to Ports-of-Entry
abstract: The North American Free Trade Agreement, now the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, has increased semi-truck and vehicular traffic at international ports-of-entry, raising air pollution concerns in the US-Mexico border region. Studying the border county of El Paso, Texas, a central hub for Mexican imports, we extend the literature by examining the prevalence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) across census tracts with varying proximities to the port-of-entry, PM 2.5 exposure, and percent immigrant. title: Multidimensional Poverty Reduction Under the National Target Programme on Sustainable Poverty Reduction in Viet Nam: Evidence from the 2021-2025 Cycle and Implications for 2026-2030
abstract: The National Target Programme on Sustainable Poverty Reduction for 2021-2025 closed at a moment of fundamental institutional change: Viet Nam’s national target programmes were consolidated from 2026, and the multidimensional poverty standard will be raised from 2027. This study evaluates the full implementation cycle of the programme, measures the degree of disparity across regions, and identifies the bottlenecks facing the new period. title: Heat‐responsive genes in Bemisia tabaci : roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance
abstract: BACKGROUND: Temperature strongly influences insect physiology and can affect responses to chemical stress. However, the molecular basis underlying the relationship between thermal responses and insecticide resistance in the whitefly Bemisia tabaci remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify conserved temperature-responsive genes and determine their functional roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance. title: Thermal Performance and Cooling Mechanisms of Thatch Roofs in Nigerian Traditional Architecture
abstract: Contemporary architecture in Nigeria has largely abandoned indigenous building typologies in favor of Western-derived, energy-intensive designs reliant on reinforced concrete and corrugated metal sheets. This shift has resulted in severe indoor thermal discomfort, necessitating massive energy consumption for mechanical cooling. This paper provides a comprehensive thermodynamic and architectural analysis of the cooling efficacy of thatch roofs combined with mud walls in Nigerian traditional architecture. abstract: Fungal endophytes considered one of the major sources of promising bioactive compounds. This study aimed to isolate endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa for the first time, and to evaluate their biological activities. Results illustrated that, two fungal endophytes isolates were isolated, identified as Alternaria sp. and Alternaria alternata morphologically and genetically. title: Imported chikungunya in French travelers returning from outbreak-affected regions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks-whether officially notified or not-can cause to travelers. abstract: Groundwater is the main source of domestic water supply in Moundou, the second-largest city in Chad, located in the Western Logone basin and within the Chari-Logone hydrological system. The literature published specifically on groundwater quality in Moundou remains sparse, originating from a small number of research teams and often based on one-off sampling campaigns. abstract: Las enfermedades alérgicas (por ejemplo, asma y rinitis) son muy propensas a variar con las modificaciones del ambiente; de hecho, el cambio climático que hoy observamos, producto de la contaminación atmosférica, ha incrementado la frecuencia y la gravedad de estas enfermedades. title: Functional systems integration: a framework for reconciling livestock production and wild herbivore conservation in nature-positive rangelands
abstract: Reconciling livestock production, wild herbivore conservation and human well-being remains a persistent challenge in rangeland management. Conventional approaches have largely pursued these objectives through separate production and conservation strategies, reinforcing a production–conservation trade-off while overlooking the ecological and institutional processes linking them. abstract: This study aims to develop a framework for the Carbon Credit Market. Assessment of credit risk in financing environmental performance and the voluntary market. A total of 5,432 peer-reviewed journal articles published during the years 2001 to 2026 were reviewed to map out the academic structure and evolution of this field. title: The Fragmentation of War and Peace: Rethinking Peace Processes in a Polycentric World
abstract: This Special Issue argues that fragmentation is a structuring condition of contemporary conflict, operating within domestic conflict systems and across the international order. Domestically, authority is dispersed among elites, armed groups, and civic actors; internationally, peacebuilding frameworks have given way to parallel mediation, regionalised intervention, and competing geopolitical projects. abstract: Abstract In the US Midwest, liquid manure is most commonly applied on bare soil after fall crop harvest, increasing the risk of nutrient loss during winter and early spring. Applying manure as a side‐dress into standing corn ( Zea mays L.) using tankers or soft drag hose systems can better match seasonal plant N uptake, but producers need evidence that this practice maintains crop yields and reduces excess nitrogen (N) in the soil after harvest. abstract: BACKGROUND: The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) includes a large workforce with a diverse spectrum of military occupations and potentially related exposures. The objective was to examine associations between service in distinct military occupations and the subsequent development of cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used CAF administrative data linked to national cancer registry data. abstract: Heatwaves are increasing in intensity, frequency, and duration and may drive the responses of organisms to climate change more strongly than gradual increases in mean temperature. The effects of heatwave events on wildlife remain poorly understood because the magnitude of these effects often depends on environmental the context: additional environmental stressors can exacerbate the impact of extreme temperatures. abstract: The 2015/16 El Niño-driven drought is the most severe South Africa has experienced in decades, causing widespread nationwide welfare losses. While drought affects all households, understanding how its impacts manifest across male- and female-headed households (MHHs and FHHs) is critical, as heterogeneity in household composition could shape the magnitude and distribution of the welfare losses. abstract: The placenta is a transient organ mainly derived from fetal tissue that is essential for establishing metabolic and immune interactions that support healthy pregnancies in eutherian mammals. Across mammals, placentas show high morphological diversity in both the degree of tissue invasiveness and in the complexity of tissue integration between maternal and fetal tissues. abstract: Este artículo analiza la serie fotográfica Ravens (1986) del fotógrafo japonés Fukase Masahisa, centrándose en la construcción de la escena fantasmática y su capacidad para generar conexiones emocionales profundas con el espectador. abstract: Economic growth and income inequality are two important indicators of a country's economic development. China and India have experienced substantial economic transformation since 2000. China has become a major manufacturing and export centre, while India has expanded in services, information technology, manufacturing and domestic consumption. abstract: BACKGROUND: Older Asian immigrants encounter challenges that limit access to healthcare services and experience physical inactivity that can exacerbate psychological distress. Virtual reality offers a promising technology for delivering mindfulness and physical activity interventions that promote body awareness and physical fitness. abstract: Abstract Plastic waste, particularly from microplastics (MPs), has become a pervasive pollutant in aquatic environments, while conventional wastewater treatment plants remain largely ineffective at removing these persistent contaminants. abstract: Abstract This article explores the interplay between the informal economy, adaptive capacity to natural hazard-related disasters, and disaster impact, drawing on annual data from 1993 to 2020 for a sample of 39 disaster-prone countries. abstract: Abstract Thermal cracking, rutting, and moisture damage are common pavement distresses caused by heavy traffic growth, construction deficiencies, and environmental effects, reducing service life and performance. abstract: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.) are hidden enemies of crops and often-overlooked pests that cause severe yield losses in diverse crops. title: El asentimiento informado en la niñez y la discapacidad: una reflexión bioética desde la autonomía progresiva y las necesidades de comunicación en Chile
abstract: L'assentiment informat de nens, nenes i adolescents (NNA) constitueix un desafiament bioètic major en contextos on la discapacitat i les necessitats de comunicació dificulten processos tradicionals d'informació i decisió. A Xile, malgrat els avanços normatius basats en l'autonomia progressiva, l'accessibilitat universal i l'educació inclusiva, persisteix una bretxa entre les exigències legals i la pràctica clínica i educativa. Aquest article analitza críticament l'evolució del marc jurídic nacional i les tensions ètiques derivades del model tutelar, la representació parental i l'omissió sistem

title: Metodologías activas y narrativas digitales para fortalecer la comprensión lectora, la producción escrita y el pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de Educación Básica y Bachillerato
abstract: Las metodologías activas y las narrativas digitales (digital storytelling, DST) ofrecen posibilidades para fortalecer competencias vinculadas con la lectura, la escritura y el pensamiento crítico; sin embargo, la evidencia sobre su integración explícita en contextos escolares permanece limitada. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar sistemáticamente la evidencia empírica sobre los efectos y aportes de las metodologías activas, el DST y su integración en la comprensión lectora, la producción escrita y el pensamiento crítico de estudiantes de Educación Básica y Bachillerato o niveles equivale

abstract: Os mapeamentos geoquímicos vêm sendo utilizados em diferentes países e para diferentes objetivos, sendo uma ferramenta de extrema importância para a identificação das características geoquímicas do ambiente. title: Effects of virtual reality and music intervention on pain relief in outpatient hysteroscopy
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Outpatient hysteroscopy is an essential gynaecological procedure used to evaluate and treat any intrauterine pathologies. However, the most common reason for procedure failure is pain. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) and music for pain management during outpatient hysteroscopy. METHODS: This was a non-blinded randomised controlled trial conducted at a single tertiary hospital in Hong Kong. title: Insights from archaeobotanical investigations at Shuqayra al-Gharbiyya: one thousand years of agriculture, biodiversity, and food processing at an Early Islamic Qasr
abstract: This article presents the results of the archaeobotanical study of the site Shuqayra al-Gharbiyya, which was founded as an Umayyad palace or qasr during the Early Islamic period and was continually occupied until the Late Ottoman period. Within the study the major crop taxa cultivated at or nearby the site, including a range of cereals, pulses, and fruit and nut trees, were identified. title: Long‐Term Legacy of Exotic Pioneers: Over Two Decades of Biodiversity Monitoring Reveals Constrained Succession in a Restored Sanitary Landfill
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term ecological studies are critical for evaluating restoration strategies on challenging sites, such as closed landfills. This study presents a 23‐year biodiversity monitoring program (2000–2023) at the restored Southeast New Territories sanitary landfill in Hong Kong. We tracked the succession of woody trees and shrubs and of soil and litter invertebrates to assess the impact of initial revegetation with exotic pioneer species, particularly nitrogen‐fixing legumes. title: Non-operative treatment of idiopathic scoliosis using physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE): a state-of-the-art-review on behalf of scoliosis research society (SRS) comprehensive care committee
abstract: PURPOSE: Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) are widely used in the nonoperative management of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Although recommended in international guidelines, uncertainty remains regarding their effectiveness, indications, and long-term clinical relevance. This state-of-the-art review aimed to critically synthesize current evidence on PSSE, identify areas of agreement and controversy, and clarify their role in contemporary conservative scoliosis care. title: Un montaje: una manera de relacionar arte, imaginación, creatividad y posición política en la psicología cultural
abstract: Para establecer la relación a la que se refiere el título se hizo uso de reflexiones conjuntas entre autores en torno a la imaginación y creatividad de Julio Cortázar, al tropo de las ruinas, especialmente de la Biblioteca de Sarajevo y el performance de Kounellis. El escrito es un diálogo a dos voces entre los autores que fue desbrozando el camino para tratar la imaginación y creatividad en el arte y en la psicología cultural. Se establecen argumentos y al final se asume una postura política en torno al intervencionismo del Imperialismo.

title: Visual Scene Memory Predicts Route‐Retracing Performance in an Age‐Diverse Adult Sample
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial navigation ability varies substantially across individuals, yet the cognitive mechanisms driving these differences remain partially understood. Self‐report measures show limited correspondence with objective performance. This study examined whether visual scene memory predicts navigation performance in an age‐diverse adult sample beyond demographic factors and self‐reported sense of direction. abstract: The increasing incidence of attacks on medical professionals, including doctors, by patients and their relatives has emerged as a serious concern in healthcare workplaces, with consequences for employee safety, psychological well-being, job satisfaction, performance, retention, and organisational effectiveness. title: Understanding the International and National Legal Instruments in the Management of Eswatini Irredentism in the Post-Colony
abstract: This article examines how international and domestic legal instruments, particularly the 1964 Cairo Declaration and Eswatini’s 1968 independence Constitution, have shaped the management of Eswatini’s irredentist project in the postcolonial period. It argues that, rather than pursuing territorial revision through overt confrontation, the Eswatini monarchy has strategically navigated the normative frameworks of international law and domestic constitutional order to advance claims to territories lost under colonial rule. title: From Innocence to Endurance: Revisioning the American Adam in The Revenant
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper argues that Alejandro González's film, The Revenant, reconfigures the tradition of the American Adam by presenting Hugh Glass as a postlapsarian Adam whose moral authority derives from endurance rather than innocence. R. W. B. Lewis defines the Adamic hero as a figure of “heroic innocence,” ahistorical and situated at the beginning of experience. Glass, however, is “the first man” only after the Fall: marked by violence and loss, yet morally centered. title: Trap-based detection of citrus longhorned beetle ( Anoplophora chinensis ) in forest demarcated areas of Croatia
abstract: Citrus longhorned beetle (CLB), Anoplophora chinensis , is an EU quarantine pest whose concealed life stages complicate early detection in forests. Traps are not a standard component of CLB surveillance: the immature stages develop hidden in trunks and roots, adults fly infrequently and disperse over short distances, and the large, conspicuous adults are often reported by the public rather than found by formal surveillance, so visual inspection has remained the standard method. title: Directions for Circular Economy Development in Thanh Hoa Province: Potential, Challenges, and Policy Implications
abstract: A circular economy seeks to retain the value of products, materials, and resources within the economy while reducing waste generation and pressure on virgin-resource extraction. In Thanh Hoa Province, this transition is closely associated with the industrial concentration of Nghi Son Economic Zone, municipal solid waste management, agricultural value chains, and tourism. This article uses document analysis, policy analysis, and descriptive synthesis of secondary data published up to 25 October 2026. title: Industrial Solid Wastes Recycling from Steel and Power Sectors Delivers Climate and Net Societal Benefits
abstract: Abstract Sectoral decarbonization can substantially reshape the quantity and composition of industrial solid waste and its associated resource recovery potential, yet how these changes evolve along decarbonization pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a sectoral transition framework linking future waste generation, recycling technologies, life cycle environmental impacts, and societal benefits. abstract: Tetrafluoroethylated motifs are increasingly widespread in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, efficient and sustainable methods for their incorporation into complex polycyclic frameworks remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a visible‐light‐promoted radical cascade cyclization of N ‐alkenyl indoles using readily available 1,2‐dibromotetrafluoroethane (BrCF 2 CF 2 Br) as a tetrafluoroethyl radical source. abstract: This study presents a literature review on the relationship between diabetes mellitus and periodontal disease, highlighting the bidirectional interaction between these conditions and the underlying inflammatory mechanisms. The presence of periodontal disease can contribute to increased systemic inflammation, adversely affecting glycemic control and complicating the management of diabetes mellitus. Conversely, diabetes mellitus can alter the immune response and prolong the inflammatory process, thereby promoting the progression and worsening of periodontal disease. title: Visions of the Future and the Problem of the Cold War Past
abstract: Using Mike Davis’ City of Quartz , Leslie Marmon Silko's Almanac of the Dead , and Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower as an entry point, this article reconstructs the career of the concept of the Cold War, tracing the decline of its paradigm in favor of a shift to the more capacious category of imperialism.

title: Droplet-Mediated Size Control of Stober Silica Particles in Surfactant- and Organic Solvent-Free Emulsions
abstract: The aqueous Stöber synthesis is a promising organic solvent-free variant of the conventional Stöber synthesis. However, particle formation under aqueous, phase-separated conditions remains underexplored. Here, we develop a method for tuning the particle diameter from 80 to 350 nm by varying the stirring energy introduced into the two-phase system from 70 to 1050 mW/kg. title: Comparative effects of endemic plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria on morphological and nutritional characteristics of Hordeum vulgare and Avena sativa forages
abstract: Plant–microbe interactions play a fundamental role in regulating plant growth and nutrient accumulation, thereby influencing forage yield and chemical composition. This study evaluated the effects of three PGPR strains on the growth and nutritional composition of two forage cereals, Hordeum vulgare and Avena sativa, cultivated under non-controlled field conditions. title: Internationalisation by appropriation: Expertise, empire, and nineteenth-century health governance
abstract: Abstract How did health governance get internationalised, and with what effects? In the early nineteenth century, a range of transregional sanitary councils were responsible for mitigating the pandemic spread of diseases such as cholera. The International Sanitary Conferences, first convened in 1851, centralised this arrangement but also discriminated against non-European public health expertise. This article argues that this was a case neither of imperial power politics alone nor simply of functional problem-solving, but of the appropriation of pre-existing governance structures. abstract: The article aims to analyze the epistemological construction and consolidation of the concept of the historic center as a fundamental category within cultural heritage studies and urban planning. A documentary-analytical study was conducted, based on a systematic review of specialized literature, documents issued by international organizations, and heritage charters. title: Resistance to Gastrocolonialism: Resilience and Culinary Innovation Among Multiethnic Communities in Indonesian School Canteens
abstract: Abstract Short Background Gastro-colonialism is the globalization of fast foods that are replacing local indigenous foods as part of people’s daily diet and even in school canteens. In West Kalimantan, the complexity of such a situation is further due to the ethnic diversity giving way to culinary tradition rich in variation but at risk to marginalization. Objective: This study aims to identify forms of resilience and innovation in multiethnic traditional foods in response to the dominance of gastro-colonialism in school cafeterias in West Kalimantan. title: Radiocarbon-based models of earliest Iron Age village community (Køge Bay region, East Zealand)
abstract: This paper explores the dynamics of village community formation and change during the earliest Iron Age (c. 500–1 BC) using radiocarbon-based models. A dataset of more than 5000 radiocarbon dates from a study area within the Køge Bay region (East Zealand, Denmark) is compiled to approach multiple scales of analysis. title: Climatology and trends of observed daily and hourly extreme precipitation in the French Alps
abstract: Abstract. The French Alps are characterized by complex topography, which influences precipitation regimes and associated risks in various ways. Extreme precipitation, especially when it happens on very short timescales, can lead to flash floods and landslides with important social and economic impacts. Local stakeholders, working on prevention and protection from such events, report a perceived recent increase in sub-daily extreme precipitation intensities in the French Alps. abstract: Using a double-voiced narration as self-ethnography, the paper draws on our individual practices across the fields of performance, craft, and ethnology, as well as on territories where they overlap: on one side, mask-making, and on the other, mask-wearing. We reflect on how masks (face-masks and mask-costumes) have found their way into our work as the duo behind “Plastic Art Performance collective”, an (eco)art group that emerged in 2020 within the Bucharest performance art scene which works to connect body practices to ecological consciousness. title: Proxy warfare and regional instability: The role of non-state actors in the Pakistan-India-Afghanistan triangle (2015-2025)
abstract: Proxy warfare has become a prominent feature of modern warfare and conflicts as both large and small states alike are pursuing these tactics to attain greater strategic leverage with minimal financial and political costs. South Asia has long been suffering from regional rivalries and disputes marked by tacit pitching of non-state actors or proxies having ramifications for the region and beyond. abstract: Background: Bajakah Tampala (Spatholobus littoralis Hassk.) has previously been investigated for its secondary metabolites and potential antioxidant activity; however, studies integrating its liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) profile with antioxidant evaluation using the 2,2′-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) assay remain scarce. title: Research culture methods detect more anaerobes compared to conventional clinical workflows in periprosthetic joint infection: a pilot study of 14 cases
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. This pilot study aimed to compare the microbial detection capabilities of standard clinical culture methods with enhanced research laboratory techniques, and to explore whether additional microbial findings might have the potential to influence antibiotic treatment planning. abstract: Abstract Amid growing calls for Australian universities to engage meaningfully with Indigenous knowledges, this article examines how Indigenous-led, place-based inquiry can reorient academic practice toward culturally regenerative possibilities. Drawing on a Cooperative Inquiry conducted with Whadjuk Noongar Boodjar, we follow six Noongar-led experiences involving Country, language, ceremony, deep time, embodiment and more-than-human relations. abstract: The intraspecific variation in elytral maculation of Cylindera (Cylindera) sauteri (Horn, 1912) and Cylindera (Cylindera) pseudocylindriformis (Horn, 1913) (Coleoptera: Cicindelidae) has not previously been studied in detail. title: Logística e innovación bajo fuego: Acelerar la experiencia militar
abstract: El empirismo de Clausewitz sostiene que el conocimiento práctico del campo de batalla supera cualquier modelo teórico, no existen fórmulas universales y el mando debe adaptarse a las circunstancias reales. El conflicto en Ucrania ha redefinido el diseño de la guerra, obligando a los ejércitos a innovar en terreno y fortalecer el apoyo logístico. Ante futuros escenarios volátiles y complejos, se vuelve urgente agilizar la toma de decisiones en el frente, donde la adaptación táctica es decisiva para la supervivencia.

title: Untold mourning: The epistemology of naming and grieving the loss of identities
abstract: This paper explores the epistemology of mourning through the lens of two Asian American scholars pursuing doctoral degrees at a Midwestern university. We examine how racialization in Midwestern educational institutions reflects a broader historical and cultural distancing from Vietnamese immigrants and refugees, despite a shared geopolitical past. title: The use of conspiracy theories and mis/disinformation in the operations of ‘new religions’ in Japan: Kōfuku-no-Kagaku and the responses to the COVID-19 pandemic (2020–2024)
abstract: The article illuminates the use of conspiracy theories and mis/disinformation in the communications of a prominent ‘new religion’ in Japan, Kōfuku-no-Kagaku (‘Happy Science’), during the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on scholarship on religion and conspiracy theories, including the conspirituality approach, this article explores Kōfuku-no-Kagaku’s conspiratorial explanations of the origins of pandemic, and its anti-vaccination stance. title: Performance Evaluation and Late Blight Reaction of Advanced Potato Genotypes for Yield and Quality Traits in Bekoji, Southeastern Ethiopia
abstract: The research aimed to assess potato genotypes that possess high yield and tuber quality characteristics and yield traits. abstract: While empathy training has long been considered a cornerstone of clinical interventions for intimate partner violence (IPV), emerging evidence on the link between empathy and IPV perpetration suggests an inconsistent association. abstract: Baseball arrived on Prince Edward Island through the same networks of travel, trade, and migration that connected the Island to the wider world. First introduced through visiting fishermen and strengthened by growing ties between Island communities, the game gradually moved from informal contests in fields and public spaces into organized clubs, interprovincial competition, and established leagues. abstract: Este trabajo analiza la percepción y el nivel de conocimiento de la población mexicana respecto al uso de la biomasa como fuente de energía, un recurso considerado por la comunidad académica como la segunda alternativa de energía renovable más prometedora y con mayor potencial en el país. abstract: Summary The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt is a biogeographical province, and its eastern sub-province faces intense pressures from land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). abstract: Abstract Children's interactions with animals shape their understanding of the biological world and humans' place in it. Understanding where children report they encounter and gain their knowledge of animals can provide insight into the early experiences that help shape human attitudes and connections to nature. title: Powering the vertical city: Electricity supply uncertainty in the high‐rise housing market
abstract: Abstract A stable electricity supply is critical to high‐rise cities. This article studies how electricity supply uncertainty, triggered by Taiwan's 2017 power crisis, affects housing prices and migration in a densely populated, high‐rise urban area. The crisis involved 2 weeks of electricity rationing followed by the August 15 large‐scale blackout that affected nearly six million households. Using within‐building comparisons across floors, we find that the power crisis led to a persistent decline in the relative value of upper floor housing units. title: Measurements and modeling of urban secondary organic aerosol formation potential as a function of precursor volatility class in the Los Angeles area during summer 2022
abstract: Abstract. Urban secondary organic aerosol (SOA) contributes to degraded air quality which can affect human health. Improvements in Los Angeles (LA), CA air quality have mainly plateaued since 2010. In summer 2022, measurements were made to quantify the SOA formation potential (SOA-FP) in ambient LA air. Two oxidation flow reactors (OFRs) ingested ambient air: one was equipped with an electrically conductive polymer inlet that denuded lower volatility species, and the other was run without an inlet. This allowed the separate quantification of SOA-FP from higher vs. lower volatility precursors.

abstract: Parent–child early interaction is crucial for promoting children’s development. This study explored associations of self-reported and observed parental playfulness with young children’s social, emotional, and behavioral development. This paper treats China's new round of county-to-city upgrading (CCU policy) as a quasi-natural experiment and uses county-level panel data from 2000 to 2022 to examine its effect on total grain production through a staggered difference-in-differences approach. title: Deforestation and resource disputes in Papua New Guinea
abstract: Abstract Disputes over land and other resources are common in poor areas of Asia and the Pacific, where common pool resources matter for livelihoods, property rights are poorly defined, and state capacity for dispute resolution is low. title: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: T-Cell Dysregulation and Regulatory T-Cell Dysfunction
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated innate and adaptive immune responses. abstract: Abstract Drought stress severely constrains the growth and productivity of woody perennials. While elevated CO2 (ECO2) can mitigate drought stress, the systemic mechanisms underlying this synergy remain largely unexplored in horticultural species. Here, we integrated physiological assays with transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses to investigate how ECO2 (710 ppm/760 ppm) enhances drought resistance in mulberry (Morus alba L.), an economically important tree crop. abstract: Justification: Student persistence remains a major challenge for public higher education in Ecuador. For many students, gaining access to university does not necessarily mean completing their studies, particularly when economic hardship threatens academic continuity. Objectives: To examine the relationship between perceptions of institutional financial aid, knowledge of the regulations governing it, socioeconomic conditions, and perceived student persistence. title: Certezas fragmentadas. La procelosa vida del “comandante Morales”
abstract: Hidden among inaccuracies, the life of Commander Morales allows for debate about the use of document as providers of certainty. Sources are always partial in several senses and their fragmentary contribution requires conceiving them as imperfect pieces of a puzzle in permanent construction, ultimately incomplete and distorted, where there is no room for shortcuts. Several interesting lives come together in a village near the front to compose a portrait of the Republican rearguard that calls into question the usual narrative and leads us to reflect on the limits of historical knowledge.

abstract: In Ireland, weather has long shaped people’s understandings of place and numerous myths and folktales highlight embodied experiences of the land.
