abstract: This paper examines the pseudo-restoration of Hebrew and its status in modern Israel as a case study in how an ‘ancient’ language is mobilised for national identity and political myth-making. Originally a regional variant of Canaanite, Hebrew was superseded as a vernacular by Aramaic and ceased to be spoken in late antiquity. abstract: For much of their existence, the International League Toronto Maple Leafs adhered to the same segregationist colour barrier that was in place across all of white organized baseball. abstract: La prevención del sedentarismo durante la infancia y la adolescencia requiere diferenciar el tiempo sedentario, la actividad física insuficiente y el uso recreativo de pantallas. abstract: Land-use changes among production–living–ecological (PLE) spaces are critical drivers of regional carbon metabolism. Although these changes have been extensively examined in urban agglomerations and plains, their carbon metabolic mechanisms in mountainous areas remain inadequately explored. abstract: ABSTRACT The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) senses environmental and physiological cues by responding to a wide range of chemicals, thereby mediating diverse physiological functions. abstract: The UAE is one of the world's hottest countries and imports more than 90% of the food consumed by its population. abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive and life-threatening disease, with rupture-related mortality reaching up to 80% in Mexico. abstract: The article analyzes the distinctive features of the book publishing activities of the Union for the Liberation of Ukraine (ULU) during the First World War. abstract: Homestead agroforestry is a cornerstone of traditional farming systems in Ethiopia, significantly contributing to both livelihoods and biodiversity. While similar practices have been studied elsewhere, findings are often context-dependent. abstract: Protected areas are cornerstones of avian conservation, yet forest-associated bird communities continue to decline even within protected lands. The capacity of a protected area to sustain bird populations depends on both internal habitat quality and the surrounding landscape context, yet the relative importance of these scales remains poorly understood. abstract: Climate change has manifested as a primary catalyst of extreme weather patterns in Karachi. The rise in temperature has disturbed the conventional climate cycle, leading to extended periods of drought, heat waves, and erratic rainfalls. title: Traumatismo craneoencefálico en motociclistas: Síntesis de la evidencia con contextualización para Paraguay
abstract: Introducción: en Paraguay, los motociclistas fueron el 58 % de las muertes viales en 2024; en una serie hospitalaria de motociclistas fallecidos, el 86,9 % presentaba lesión craneoencefálica. abstract: Durante la hospitalización pediátrica se realizan procedimientos invasivos y dolorosos que pueden generar ansiedad y miedo, especialmente en niños que, debido a su edad, pueden no comprender completamente la situación. abstract: El artículo analiza el papel transformador de las redes sociales en la participación política de las mujeres. The central aim is to demonstrate how Kahlo’s artistic practice transcends mere expressions of suffering, serving as an intentional and powerful mechanism for self-care, resilience, and the restoration of individuality. abstract: Résumé En 2026, dans les provinces et états d’Amérique du Nord où les relations de travail sont fondées sur le modèle du Wagner Act de 1935, la grève politique ou sociale est, la plupart du temps, interdite. title: Gender matters in seed system assessments: evidence from smallholder farms in Morocco, Senegal, and Madagascar
abstract: Despite growing recognition of the importance of involving smallholder farmers in seed systems governance, gender remains a critical but overlooked dimension. Women’s seed practices are often misunderstood, underdocumented, and excluded from policy and research, leading to governance frameworks that fail to address their needs or even exacerbate inequalities. This calls for collecting gender-disaggregated data and developing more inclusive methodologies in seed system assessments. This study evaluated syringe labelling practices, standards alignment and educational needs among anaesthesia trainees and technicians in India. Methods: A multicentre online cross-sectional survey was conducted across India from February to May 2025. abstract: Abstract This article examines secondary pausal phenomena in modern oral recitation traditions of Biblical Hebrew, focusing on final nasalization and diphthongization. Its primary aim is to document and present the empirical basis for analysis, drawing on recordings from the Hebrew University Language Traditions Project. abstract: The protection of the natural environment during armed conflict has become an increasingly significant concern in international humanitarian law (IHL), given the devastating environmental consequences of contemporary warfare. Armed conflicts frequently result in the destruction of forests, contamination of water resources, degradation of agricultural land, pollution of the atmosphere, and damage to ecosystems essential for human survival. title: Naming the nameless: a preliminary study of bynames for the deceased from an onomastic perspective
abstract: The article proposes a new term, postmortonyms, denoting names assigned to unidentified deceased individuals. Drawing on an exemplary semantic onomastic analysis of 220 postmortonyms from multiple cultures, the study explores the motivations, structures, and functions of these bynames, distinct from posthumous names, deadnames, and necronyms. title: Transdisciplinarity in the crosshairs: political threats to inclusive research
abstract: Transdisciplinary research (TDR) promises to address society’s most complex challenges by integrating expertise across disciplines and sectors. However, as political polarization intensifies, TDR’s commitments to collaborate across differences, engage lived experience, and generate social impact can become points of contention and vulnerability. title: Human trafficking and the mental health burden of forced migrants in Germany
abstract: PURPOSE: Forced migration increases vulnerability to exploitation. Globally, around 50 million people are affected by human trafficking, which often involves trauma with negative mental health effects. Forced migrants already face elevated risks of PTSD, depression, and anxiety, yet the specific association of trafficking on their mental health remains unclear. abstract: Las cooperativas de ahorro y crédito cumplen una función relevante en los territorios donde operan, pues facilitan el acceso a servicios financieros y, al mismo tiempo, impulsan iniciativas vinculadas con el bienestar de sus socios. abstract: Population health is a central input into social welfare, but health itself is complex and multidimensional. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how urban spatial structure affects the earnings gap between high‐ and low‐skilled workers in China. We combine individual‐level panel data with satellite‐derived measures of urban form. We find that less compact cities have a wider skill earnings gap. abstract: Anaemia is a common haematological complication among those who have human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and is linked to a reduced quality of life, faster disease progression and higher mortality rates. This review looks at the extent of the problem, the mechanisms involved, the risk factors, the significance and the management of anaemia in people with HIV/AIDS, using evidence from sub-Saharan African areas, including Nigeria. abstract: Soil aggregate stability (AS) is a critical indicator of soil physical quality, yet its long-term drivers in vulnerable silty soils remain inadequately quantified. This study analyzed the determinants of AS over 25 years (1999–2023) in a long-term field experiment on a temperate silty Luvisol, comparing four cropping systems: conventional (CON), low-input (LI), organic (ORG), and conservation agriculture (CA). title: An Argument for Minimalism about Action
abstract: Abstract Minimalism is the view that the mark of action is object‐causation, rather than intentionality, voluntariness or goal‐directedness. Actions, on this view, are instances of objects causing change. Despite a recent surge of interest in the view, it is still seldom regarded as a serious alternative to orthodox theories of action, according to which action is, by its nature, intentional, voluntary, or, more broadly, a psychological phenomenon. This paper argues that it should. It provides a simple argument for regarding minimalism as the default view of the nature of action.

title: Estimating the Kinetic Energy Spectrum from the Second-Order Velocity Structure Function using a Regularized Fitting Approach
abstract: Abstract Ocean turbulence plays a key role in shaping large-scale circulation, heat uptake, and biogeochemical processes. The kinetic energy (KE) wavenumber spectrum is a fundamental diagnostic, quantifying how KE is distributed across spatial scales. The second-order structure function—computed from velocity differences between spatially separated observations—provides a complementary measure, but unlike the KE spectrum, it reflects a non-local, weighted integral of KE over all scales. title: Dilution drives deep degassing of sulfur in hydrous basaltic magmas
abstract: Abstract Sulfur (S) is thought to degas at higher pressures from hydrous magmas (e.g., arc and some ocean island basalts) relative to water-poor magmas, from which S degasses at lower pressures (e.g., Kīlauea, mid-ocean ridge basalts). Our modelling of degassing shows this occurs for magmas that are either reduced (i.e., S is present predominantly as H2S in the vapor and dissolved sulfide in the melt) or oxidised (i.e., dominantly SO2 in the vapor and dissolved sulfate in the melt). abstract: While Alnus nitida (Spach) Endl. is a vital multipurpose tree in the Western Himalayas, combined evaluations of phenotypic traits and fodder quality across wide elevation gradients are lacking. To address this gap, 15 natural populations in Himachal Pradesh (1000–2466 m above mean sea level) were evaluated during 2021–22 to establish a multi-trait baseline for tree improvement and elite genotype selection. abstract: Abstract. This study conducts LES respectively with lake-only, mountain-only, and combined lake-mountain configurations. title: Drivers of productivity in a tidal marsh specialist bird species ( Rallus crepitans )
abstract: Abstract Effective conservation efforts are contingent on understanding the underlying demographic processes that regulate wildlife populations. Productivity is a key driver of population growth, and in avian taxa, nest survival and clutch size dictate the number of chicks successfully hatched. Patterns in productivity can vary spatially and temporally, shaping populations and their evolutionary trajectories. abstract: Human-driven climate change has amplified the magnitude and reduced the predictability of natural environmental fluctuations. Temperature, a major physiological stressor, is rising in both its mean and the frequency of extremes. Understanding how organisms adapt to shifts in both thermal mean and variability is therefore critical for predicting their performance under future climates. abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable spat supply remains a key constraint for Mabé pearl farmers in the Pacific island nation of Tonga. This study evaluated the effect of deployment depth on Pteria penguin (Röding, 1798) spat recruitment and final shell size across seven sites in Vava'u, Kingdom of Tonga. Spat collectors were deployed at depths of 6 and 12 m for 12 months between October 2023 and October 2024, and all spat recruited were counted and measured. abstract: Pollen and nutrient analyses of the faeces of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) were made to understand its preferred dietary plants and ecology. Pollen preserved in the faeces accurately reflected its diet as a mixed feeder including Artemisia, Caryophyllaceae, Asteroideae, and Ephedra, characteristic plants of the Alpine steppe vegetation under a cold and arid climate in the higher Himalaya. The role of landscape composition and configuration in biological invasions is widely considered while its interplay with landscape connectivity is less understood. title: Carbon recycling, energy flux, and mercury dynamics along a river affected by multiple disturbances
abstract: Abstract Small hydroelectric power plants, such as run‐of‐river dams (RORs), are increasingly promoted as low‐impact renewable energy sources, yet their disturbance on mercury (Hg) cycling remains poorly evaluated in impact assessments. abstract: Summary Polarization observables have long been used to infer properties of the Earth, but the geophysical literature has not explicitly addressed the problem of a general metric for comparing arbitrary polarization states (independently of specific application contexts). title: Resource waves across snowpacks and alpine vegetation extend seasonal resource availability in alpine ecosystems
abstract: Alpine ecosystems are energy-limited and highly seasonal. Consumers in the alpine zone must track rapidly shifting windows of prey availability during the short growing season. Prolonged snowmelt creates a mosaic of persistent snowfields, scrubs and alpine tundra. In addition to vegetation-dwelling arthropods, wind-transported arthropods deposited on snowpacks, known as arthropod fallout, provide an allochthonous subsidy from lower elevations to alpine environments. abstract: La2Zr2O7 (LZO) pyrochlore is a thermally and chemically stable host for luminescent lanthanide ions, but most studies on Eu3+-doped LZO concern nanoparticles prepared by chemical routes. title: Arboreal life supports slow and steady pace of life in the Pacific dry forest of Ecuador
abstract: Abstract Age and growth-related data provide key insights into life-history strategies, yet remain scarce for neotropical amphibians, particularly arboreal species inhabiting highly seasonal environments. We used skeletochronology to conduct the first empirical assessment of sex-specific aging and somatic growth patterns of an arboreal frog from the Pacific dry forest of Ecuador. abstract: PURPOSE: Dry Eye Disease (DED) is highly prevalent among university students and may be influenced by modifiable factors such as psychological stress and sleep disturbance. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations of sleep disturbance and perceived stress with DED, while the secondary objective was to evaluate their potential interaction. abstract: The erosion of fine sediments from an immobile coarse-grained bed depends on the degree of exposure of the coarse grains. In an earlier study (Trevisson & Eiff, Water Resour. abstract: Mission Genesis of the European Space Agency has been approved for launch in 2028. Its primary goal is the enhancement of the terrestrial reference frame by establishing a space tie on the Genesis satellite between all space geodetic techniques used for the determination of the frame. abstract: The use of laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) for mapping analysis can provide geochemical and geochronological data in conjunction with crucial spatial information. title: Trilobite biofacies reveal a ‘dual-slope’ paleogeographic pattern of South China during the Early–Middle Ordovician
abstract: Trilobite biofacies are often indicative of particular paleoecological settings and can reveal spatial paleogeographic changes. Multivariate analyses (CA, PCoA and NMDS) were performed using the Raup-Crick coefficient on a dataset of 62 trilobite genera and subgenera from 15 localities across South China during the Early–Middle Ordovician (Floian–Dapingian). abstract: Background: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first recognized during pregnancy.it is one of the most common metabolic disorders complicating pregnancy. there is an increased burden of GDM and its significant consequences for maternal and child health. This study aimed to identify the risk factors associated with GDM among pregnant women at a tertiary care centre and determine their strength of association. abstract: ABSTRACT Gendered systems of power in agriculture underpin a heteropatriarchy that disempowers women's participation. To interrogate how imagery may function as both a reflective and perpetuating force in maintaining heteropatriarchy across the agricultural sector we analyzed 357 images on 36 Australian agriculture organization websites, coding them for key attributes. abstract: Soil nematode communities under invasion by Heracleum sosnowskyi Manden. (Sosnowsky’s hogweed) were studied in habitats of different latitudinal locations. abstract: ABSTRACT To synergistically enhance the strength‐ductility trade‑off and achieve uniform degradation in Fe‐Zn alloys, heterostructured alloy microtubes were fabricated via layer‑by‑layer electrodeposition on a rotating soluble aluminum mandrel. title: Analysis of options for building an orbital constellation of a multifunctional personal satellite communication system
abstract: A comprehensive analysis of the construction of a promising orbital constellation is presented, as a result of which it was found that the existing four-by-seven structure, corresponding to four orbital planes with seven spacecraft in each, with an orbit height of one and a half thousand kilometers and an inclination of eighty-two and a half degrees, is initial for further optimization. Analysis of the instantaneous position of the orbital constellation four by seven, taking into account the radio visibility zone at an angle of ten degrees, demonstrates a coverage close to one hundred percent.

abstract: Seasonal variation can strongly influence species interactions, yet its effects on interaction networks remain poorly understood in tropical and subtropical systems. We surveyed mixed-species bird flocks (MSFs) across 20 2 × 2 km grid cells in a subtropical forest in southern China during breeding and non-breeding seasons, quantified seasonal changes in flock composition and network structure, and examined how species traits and environmental factors drive these changes. abstract: Se documenta la fabricación y puesta a punto de un prototipo de mesa vibratoria uniaxial de bajo costo para el laboratorio del TESVB, como continuación del diseño esquemático previo. abstract: This essay examines error management culture as a higher-order dynamic capability that fosters organizational learning, innovation, psychological safety, and strategic renewal. Drawing upon the rationalist deductive method of René Descartes and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, a rationalist paradigm, and an objectivist critical realist perspective, it argues that error should not be understood as an accidental deviation from organizational functioning, but rather as a constitutive mechanism of knowledge creation, adaptation, and the evolution of social systems. title: A microwave-based system for hydrogen production by using CNT/rGO catalyst
abstract: Due to strict environmental requirements and problems related to fuel use and shortages, hydrogen energy has emerged as a pivotal clean energy carrier. However, conventional production methods are often energy- and carbon-intensive. In the present work, a novel approach for hydrogen production was investigated using a microwave-assisted pyrolysis system. abstract: When conducting studies on animal production, data must be analyzed with appropriate statistical methods. abstract: Martian landslide inventories remain concentrated near the equator, particularly in Valles Marineris. abstract: Persistent rural insecurity in South-South Nigeria has continued to undermine community safety despite the expansion of formal policing and state-led security interventions. Incidences of communal violence, land disputes, theft, cult-related activities, and other localized conflicts have exposed the limitations of conventional security approaches, thereby reviving interest in indigenous conflict management mechanisms. abstract: Every year, thousands of people flee war, persecution, and poverty in their home countries and make the dangerous journey across the Mediterranean in search of a safer future. abstract: The degradation of arable lands is becoming widespread and leads to significant loss of soil organic matter (SOM), expressed both in quantitative losses and in qualitative changes in the molecular and elemental composition of SOM. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how infection‐related traits vary across parasite populations and host stages is key to predicting host–parasite dynamics in complex life cycles. title: Revision of Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier (Asparagaceae) from Madagascar, with the description of five new species and two new varieties
abstract: Asparagus L. sect. Myrsiphyllum (Willd.) Baker ex H.Perrier, which includes the members of the genus with phylloclades, is defined and revised for Madagascar and the Comoro Islands based primarily on morphological evidence. This builds on earlier treatments of the group, taking into account the wealth of new material now available. title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding
abstract: Marine video understanding is crucial for a wide range of real-world applications. However, existing marine video datasets suffer from limitations, including the limited number of data samples, fine-grained text descriptions, and detailed visual attributes. To address these limitations, we introduce a large-scale, video-text dataset featuring rich, in-the-wild visual attributes tailored for complex marine environments. title: Stockmayer Fluid with a Shifted Dipole. III. Ion Solvation
abstract: Though ion solvation is well understood for the standard Stockmayer fluid, the effect of displacing the point dipole of a Stockmayer particle, a simple geometric modification, on ion-solvent structuring and solvation thermodynamics remains less understood. We use molecular dynamics simulations to describe how a dipole shift affects radial and orientational solvent structure around centered ions, how strongly the solvent distinguishes cations and anions, and how the solvent mediates ion-ion pairing. title: Propulsion Systems for a Starshade Rendezvous Mission with the Habitable World Observatory
abstract: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints affect exo-Earth characterization with a starshade rendezvous mission for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)-like telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with EXOSIMS, we model a 60 m starshade for visible-band spectroscopy (500-1000 nm) and a 35 m starshade for near-ultraviolet characterization (250-550 nm). title: X-Dubbing: Speech-to-Speech Translation under Temporal and Visual Constraints
abstract: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video.
